articles.title: Perceptions, knowledge, and attitudes of pharmacists toward pharmacist prescribing of contraceptives in Brazil.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.authors: de Vasconcelos JPT, Melo TAR, Tiguman GMB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2024, Brazil authorized pharmacists to prescribe hormonal contraceptives (HC) for pregnancy prevention through Federal Pharmacy Council no. 12/2024-an important step toward expanding reproductive health access.
OBJECTIVE: To explore the perceptions, knowledge, and attitudes of Brazilian pharmacists regarding pharmacist prescribing of HC, and to identify factors associated with greater knowledge about HC.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between February and March 2025 among Brazilian pharmacists who prescribed or were interested in prescribing HC. A 35-item questionnaire assessed sociodemographic characteristics, professional training, and perceptions, knowledge, and attitudes toward HC prescribing. Descriptive analyses and multiple linear regression were performed to identify factors associated with higher knowledge levels.
RESULTS: In total, 97 pharmacists participated in the study. Most respondents were women (76.3%), aged 30-39 years (35.0%), worked in community pharmacies (45.4%), and graduated from private universities (54.6%). The majority had completed a postgraduate degree (41.2%) and reported attending classes on HC during their undergraduate studies (69.1%), yet only a minority participated in any courses on HC after graduation (33.0%). The mean knowledge score was 4.13±1.79 out of 8 points. Pharmacists from the North region had lower scores compared to those from the Southeast (β=-1.86; 95%CI -3.16; -0.55; std. coeff.=-0.39). The most frequently reported barriers to prescribing HC were lack of time (42.3%) and insufficient training (40.2%). Most respondents (84.5%) agreed that the national regulation enabling pharmacist prescribing of HC represented a professional milestone, although 75.3% believed additional postgraduate training was necessary.
CONCLUSION: Brazilian pharmacists showed moderate knowledge regarding HC, with higher knowledge independently associated with region of practice. Educational reforms and continuing professional development are needed to ensure evidence-based prescribing and reduce disparities. Strengthening pharmacists' skills could improve contraceptive access and promote reproductive health equity in Brazil.

articles.title: Children and Families Affected by Parental Substance Use: Clinical Report.
articles.authors: Schiff DM, Farst KJ, Kellogg ND et al.
articles.abstract: Children and adolescents whose parents have an alcohol or substance use disorder are at increased risk of short- and long-term sequelae, ranging from medical conditions to psychosocial, safety, and behavioral challenges. In the course of providing health care services to children, pediatricians and other pediatric clinicians are likely to encounter families affected by parental substance use and are in a unique position to support the well-being of both the child and family. The purpose of this clinical report is to briefly discuss the epidemiology of substance use during pregnancy and while parenting in the United States; highlight the influence of bias, racism, and other structural inequities on families affected by substance use; describe the known risks associated with prenatal and postnatal parental substance use; discuss use and interpretation of toxicology testing as part of a substance exposure evaluation; review approaches to screening for prenatal and parental substance use; propose key topics for anticipatory guidance in the pediatric clinic; identify and address concerning parental and child presentations related to parental substance use leading to concern for child abuse or neglect; and provide recommendations for pediatric clinicians involved in the care of children from families affected by substance use.

articles.title: Puberty, not age, marks the start of adolescent brain structural remodeling.
articles.authors: Chad JA, Klukas OC, Ghasoub M et al.
articles.abstract: Many studies have shown that pubertal changes are associated with brain changes, but there lacks a clear understanding of what happens to the brain at puberty, and whether it opens the brain structural remodeling that characterizes adolescence. In this study, we used three longitudinal waves of structural MRI data from thousands of participants of the ABCD study aged 9-14 years to compare brain changes between age-matched children who had either reached or not reached a major pubertal milestone: menarche in females and fonarche (voice drop) in males. We found that only the children who had reached the milestone exhibited widespread contraction of cortical surface area and subcortical volume. The contraction was more pronounced in females, in line with previous evidence of how gonadal hormones regulate neuronal fine-tuning. Our findings suggest that reaching puberty, rather than reaching a particular age, begins the adolescent phase of structural brain development.

articles.title: The Role of Self-Collection in Optimising Cervical Screening for People With Intellectual Disability: A Multi Perspective Qualitative Study.
articles.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
articles.authors: Winkler L, Power R, Allison KR et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on whether self-collection addresses inequities in cervical screening participation for people with intellectual disability is limited. This study explored how self-collection is understood by people with intellectual disability and those in their support and healthcare networks and factors that support or hinder access.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were undertaken with four participant groups in New South Wales. This analysis reports on participants who discussed self-collection (n = 59) within a broader interview study (N = 66): people with intellectual disability (n = 9); family members and support people (n = 12); managers/leaders in disability organisations and private disability services (n = 19) and healthcare professionals (n = 19). Interviews used trauma-informed and accessible methods and were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis within a co-production framework.
RESULTS: Three themes captured participants' perspectives: (1) Reclaiming bodily autonomy: self-collection restored decision-making power by allowing people to collect their own vaginal sample or choose and guide a trusted healthcare professional to assist (2) Safety, trust, and freedom from harm: Self-collection was perceived as less invasive than a speculum examination and supported safer participation for those with healthcare anxiety or trauma (3) Structural inequities and ableist gatekeeping: Limited confidence with self-sampling, ableist assumptions, clinician-centred pathways, and uncertainty around support roles constrained access.
CONCLUSIONS: Self-collection offers important opportunities to improve cervical screening participation for people with intellectual disability but requires multisectoral reforms including accessible sexual and reproductive health education and screening information informed by lived experience, trauma-informed and rights-based training across health and disability workforces and alternative screening models for safer home-based self-collection. These changes are essential to realise the reproductive autonomy and safety of people with intellectual disability and ensure meaningful progress towards equitable cervical cancer elimination.

articles.title: Targeted HK2 Silencing via Folate-Decorated Core-Shell Tecto-Dendrimers Modulates Glycolysis-Associated Metabolic Processes in Ovarian Cancer Cells.
articles.authors: Wang X, Yuan C, Wei J et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer exhibits profound metabolic dependence on aerobic glycolysis, rendering hexokinase 2 (HK2), the rate-limiting enzyme of this pathway, a key therapeutic vulnerability. However, therapeutic exploitation of HK2 silencing remains hindered by the intrinsic instability and inefficient intracellular delivery of siRNA. To overcome these limitations, we developed a folate-functionalized core-shell tecto-dendrimer (FA-G5/G3) capable of selectively targeting HK2 through folate receptor-mediated uptake and intracellular delivery of HK2 siRNA. The engineered nanocomplex exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including stable architecture, appropriate particle size, and excellent biocompatibility. Following cellular internalization, FA-G5/G3 facilitated intracellular delivery of HK2 siRNA, resulting in effective post-transcriptional silencing of HK2 expression. This intervention disrupted glycolytic metabolism, reduced downstream LDHA expression, and markedly decreased extracellular lactate production. By suppressing a central glycolytic regulator, the FA-G5/G3-mediated HK2 silencing strategy reduced glycolytic activity and provided a potential approach for exploiting metabolic vulnerabilities in ovarian cancer. Collectively, this study establishes a targeted CSTD-based siRNA delivery platform for glycolysis-associated metabolic changes and provides a promising therapeutic strategy for overcoming metabolic vulnerabilities in ovarian cancer.

articles.title: 150 years after Hertwig: how the discovery of fertilisation transformed reproductive medicine.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Viville S
articles.abstract: The year 2026 marks the 150th anniversary of Oscar Hertwig's demonstration that fertilisation results from the fusion of sperm and oocyte, a discovery that fundamentally transformed biology and medicine. This historical review retraces the intellectual journey from ancient philosophical and theological interpretations of conception through the theories of spontaneous generation, preformationism, and the discovery of spermatozoa, culminating in Hertwig's experimental demonstration of gamete fusion in 1876. It examines how successive advances in embryology, reproductive physiology, genetics, and molecular biology progressively replaced speculation with experimental evidence, establishing the scientific basis of human reproduction. The review further describes how these discoveries enabled the development of assisted reproductive technologies, including artificial insemination, in vitro fertilisation, intracytoplasmic sperm injection, gamete cryopreservation, and gamete donation, profoundly changing the management of infertility. By linking historical milestones with their clinical consequences, this article highlights how fundamental biological discoveries have continuously driven therapeutic innovation and illustrates the enduring impact of Hertwig's work on modern reproductive medicine and the lives of millions of patients worldwide. One hundred and sixteen years separate Oscar Hertwig's demonstration of fertilisation in 1876 from the introduction of intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) in 1992. Between these two landmarks lies one of the most remarkable scientific and clinical journeys in reproductive medicine.

articles.title: Analysis the ovotoxicity and ovarian cancer stem-like progenitors generation in benzo[a]pyrene-treated Mice.
articles.authors: Bhardwaj N, Singh A, Babu R
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Benzo(a)pyrene (BaP), a member of the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) family, is a potent carcinogen and causes cancer in multiple organs. The present research investigates the toxicity of BaP in the reproductive tract of female Swiss mice.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A standardised dose of BaP (50 mg/kg body weight twice a week for one month) was administered to induce systemic oxidative stress in murine models. After 4 months, BaP administration reduces the numbers of primordial and primary ovarian follicles and induces stromal cell hyperplasia and inflammation inside the ovary. The thickness of uterine layers decreases, while the diameter of the uterine lumen and number of uterine glands rise. Atrophied uterine linings, as well as endometrial hyperplasia (EH) with abnormal glandular development are apparent. Using flow cytometry, three different ovarian cancer stem-like progenitors (CSLP) were identified based on the expression of CD44 and CD133 receptors: CD44⁺CD133⁻, CD44⁺CD133⁺, and CD44-CD133+. BaP treatment increases CD44+CD133-(7.3-fold, p < 0.005) and CD44+CD133+ cells (2.53-fold, p < 0.0005), while decreasing CD44-CD133+ cells (52% reduction, p < 0.0005). BaP administration also increases the CD44 (4-fold, P < 0.0005) and CD133 surface expression (47% increase, p < 0.005) as well as ROS production (2-fold increment, p < 0.005) in ovarian cells. The RT-qPCR data suggests a marked reduction in the relative expressions of antioxidant genes (SOD1, SOD2, catalase, GPX1, and FOXO3) in ovarian cells.
CONCLUSIONS: BaPadministration disrupts folliculogenesis, reduces ovarian follicle size, and causes epithelial hyperplasia, lymphocytic infiltration, increased vascularisation, atrophied uterine lining, and abnormal glandular growth in the uterus. It induces CSLPs and CD44 and CD133 expression in ovaries. The BaP administration also increases ROS and decreases antioxidant gene expression in the ovaries.

articles.title: Evaluation of FGFR2, VEGFA, and MMP1 gene variants for ovarian cancer susceptibility among South Indian women: a hospital-based case-control study.
articles.authors: Canchi Sistla H, Seshachalam A, Rathnam KK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a genetically heterogeneous malignancy characterized by marked molecular and histologic heterogeneity. Genetic variation in pathways involved in angiogenesis and extracellular matrix remodeling may contribute to OC susceptibility. The present study evaluated VEGFA rs833061, FGFR2 rs1219648, and MMP1 rs1799750 polymorphisms in a South Indian cohort and investigated their individual and combined associations with OC risk.
METHODS: This hospital-based pilot case-control study included 240 histopathologically confirmed OC cases and 254 cancer-free controls. Genotyping was performed using PCR-RFLP and allele-specific PCR. Associations with OC susceptibility were assessed using logistic regression with adjustment for age and menopausal status, with the codominant model as the primary genetic model and alternative models as secondary analyses. Exploratory clinicopathological and multifactor dimensionality reduction (MDR) analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: MMP1 rs1799750 was associated with increased OC susceptibility, with the 2G/2G genotype showing higher odds of OC (aOR = 2.10, 95% CI = 1.12-3.94; p = 0.0179). Similarly, VEGFA rs833061 was also associated with increased susceptibility, with T/C and C/C genotypes showing higher odds (aOR = 2.51, 95% CI = 1.55-4.06; p = < 0.001 and aOR = 1.87, 95% CI = 1.04-3.35; p = 0.021, respectively). However, FGFR2 rs1219648 was not associated with overall OC susceptibility but showed exploratory associations with selected clinicopathological characteristics. The two-locus VEGFA-MMP1 MDR model showed the highest testing balanced accuracy among evaluated models (TBA = 0.5853; CVC = 10/10).
CONCLUSION: VEGFA and MMP1 variants showed associations with OC susceptibility in this South Indian cohort. Combined-genotype and MDR findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, independent cohorts.

articles.title: Preparation and characterization of Kaempferol-loaded Niosomes and their effects on apoptosis and cell migration in SKOV3 ovarian cancer cells.
articles.authors: Farahmandpour S, Kavousi M, Jamshidian F
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian cancer remains one of the most lethal gynecological malignancies worldwide, underscoring the urgent need for more effective therapeutic strategies. Kaempferol, a naturally occurring flavonoid with well-documented anticancer properties, has attracted considerable attention because of its antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic activities. However, its therapeutic application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, and limited cellular availability, which restrict its clinical potential.
METHODS: Kaempferol-loaded niosomes (KMF Niosomes) were prepared using the thin-film hydration method and characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and dynamic light scattering (DLS). SKOV3 ovarian cancer cells were treated with free kaempferol (free KMF) or KMF Niosomes (0.00625-0.8 mg/mL) for 24, 48, and 72 h. Cell viability was evaluated using the MTT assay, whereas apoptosis and cell-cycle distribution were assessed by flow cytometry. The relative expression levels of BAX, TP53, BCL2, and MMP2 were determined by quantitative real-time PCR.
RESULTS: Compared with free KMF, the niosomal formulation exhibited significantly greater cytotoxic activity, resulting in lower IC₅₀ values at all evaluated time points. It also produced greater modulation of apoptosis-related gene expression, characterized by increased expression of BAX and TP53 together with reduced expression of BCL2. In addition, treatment with the niosomal formulation was associated with reduced expression of the migration-associated gene MMP2 at the mRNA level. Flow cytometric analysis further demonstrated an increased proportion of cells in the G0/G1 phase and a higher proportion of apoptotic cells in cells treated with KMF Niosomes than in those treated with free KMF.
CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these findings suggest that niosomal encapsulation enhances the in vitro anticancer activity of kaempferol against SKOV3 ovarian cancer cells and is associated with transcriptional modulation of apoptosis-related genes, cell-cycle progression, and migration-associated cellular responses. However, because drug-release kinetics, formulation stability, intracellular uptake, protein-level validation, and in vivo therapeutic efficacy were not evaluated, the mechanisms underlying the enhanced biological activity cannot be conclusively established. Therefore, further mechanistic and in vivo studies are warranted to…

articles.title: The effect of metabolic syndrome on bone mineral density in men and women: a systematic review & meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.authors: Ramzan I, Agcaoili N, Ardavani A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is associated with alterations in body composition and metabolic health, however its impact on bone mineral density (BMD) remains unclear, with potential sex- and site-specific differences.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, MEDLINE and Google Scholar for cross-sectional studies published within the last 10 years to investigate the impact of MetS on BMD. Lumbar spine (LS), femoral neck (FN) and total hip (TH) BMD were utilised as outcomes of interest. The included studies encompassed populations from East Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Europe and Latin America. Meta-analysis utilising a random-effects model, compared BMD between participants with and without MetS, subgroup analyses by sex and menopausal status and timeframe-stratified sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Twelve studies reached the synthesis stage, with overall quality found to be low to moderate risk of bias. Men with MetS had significantly higher BMD at the LS (p = 0.03) and FN (p = 0.003), with a significant pooled effect across skeletal sites (Z = 5.57, p < 0.00001). In women, no significant association between MetS and overall BMD was observed. However, subgroup analyses demonstrated that postmenopausal women without MetS had significantly higher FN and LS BMD compared with those with MetS (FN: Z = 2.14, p = 0.03; LS: Z = 2.02, p = 0.04). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a larger pooled effect for LS BMD in woman in studies with assessment periods of one year or less.
CONCLUSION: MetS is tentatively associated with sex- and site-specific differences in BMD based on observational studies, with potential effect-size differentials according to assessment chronology. Further research is warranted to clarify these associations and their potential clinical implications using higher-quality trial data.

articles.title: Association of quantitative vascularization of the anterior fornix/cervix region with placenta accreta spectrum and associated intraoperative hemorrhage.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Kassir E, Hernandez-Andrade E, Gerulewicz-Vannini D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate a quantitative method for analyzing vascularization in the anterior fornix/cervix (AFC) region in women at risk of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). The primary aim was to evaluate the association between quantitative vascularization (QV) and severity of PAS (determined by histopathology) and to estimate the optimal QV cut-off value to predict PAS. A secondary aim was to evaluate the association of QV with severe intraoperative blood loss (IOBL).
METHODS: This was a prospective study including patients with anterior placenta previa referred for suspected PAS at the University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston, TX, USA, between December 2021 and June 2025. Transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler (with standardized settings) was performed to visualize the cervix and the lower uterine segment in the midsagittal plane. The prenatal diagnosis of high risk for PAS was based on ultrasound features including loss of the uteroplacental interface, the presence of placental lacunae, increased vascularization and abnormal bladder wall. For QV assessment, a videoclip was acquired, in which the AFC region was defined and post-processing analysis was used to estimate the percentage of color pixels within the AFC region in each frame. The mean value across all frames was defined as the QV value. QV values were not provided to clinicians and were not used for clinical decisions. Associations between QV and PAS, depth of implantation, IOBL and units of blood products transfused were evaluated, as well as the ability of QV to discriminate between patients with and those without PAS.
RESULTS: A total of 117 patients were included. PAS was confirmed histopathologically in 89 (76.1%) patients (placenta accreta, n = 11; placenta increta, n = 55; placenta percreta, n = 23). A reliable estimation of IOBL was obtained in 109 patients and severe IOBL (> 1500 mL) occurred in 53 (48.6%) of these cases. The area under the receiver-operating-characteristics curve, demonstrating the ability of QV to discriminate between cases with and those without confirmed PAS, was 0.821 (95% CI, 0.739-0.886). The optimal QV cut-off value was 8.5%, yielding a sensitivity of 70.5% (95% CI, 59.8-79.7%), specificity of 89.7% (95% CI, 68.3-96.1%), positive predictive value of 93.9% (95% CI, 86.1-97.5%) and negative predictive value of 50.0% (95% CI, 40.3-57.8%). QV ≥ 8.5% was associated with increased odds of PAS (odds ratio (OR), 14.9 (95% CI, 4.7-47.0);…

articles.title: Mapping developmental and targeted secretory signatures of euploid and aneuploid human embryos using an advanced endometrial model.
articles.authors: Yagüe-Serrano R, Piñeiro-Silva C, Morales-Álvarez S et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Do euploid (EU), trisomy 21 (T21), and monosomy 21 (M21) human embryos exhibit different patterns of secreted proteins and morphometric changes during extended in vitro culture, either with or without endometrial cell support?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Secreted protein profiles and morphometric parameters discriminate between euploid and aneuploid embryos during post-implantation in vitro culture with endometrial cell support.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Extended in vitro culture systems with and without endometrial cells have enabled the study of early human post-implantation development and highlighted the importance of embryo-endometrial crosstalk during implantation. However, how embryo chromosomal status influences implantation dynamics and embryo-endometrial interactions remain poorly understood.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: Laboratory-based study. Sixty-nine supernumerary human embryos donated for research at blastocyst stage (5 days post-fertilization, d.p.f.) (EU, n = 24; T21, n = 21; M21, n = 24) were used.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Extended in vitro culture until 14 d.p.f. was performed using two systems: a cell-free culture medium optimized for post-implantation development, and a 3D culture based on cell-engineered receptive endometrial scaffold technology (CREST), providing epithelial and stromal cell support. Secreted levels of CALR (calreticulin), β-hCG, human placental lactogen (hPL), pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A), and placental growth factor (PlGF) were quantified at different developmental time points corresponding to 7, 10, 12, and 14 d.p.f. Embryo morphometric parameters, including area, degree of expansion, axis ratio, and circularity were also measured.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Embryos cultured without endometrial support showed compromised viability beyond 10 d.p.f., with significantly reduced secretion of β-hCG, hPL, PAPP-A, PlGF, and CALR. The area of post-implanted EU and T21 embryos cultured in cell-free medium progressively increased up to 9 d.p.f., unlike M21 embryos. However, all showed no changes in blastocoel expansion and maintained a rounded morphology throughout all post-implantation culture. CREST systems extended viability up to 14 d.p.f. and enhanced secretion levels of all evaluated protein markers compared with embryos cultured in cell-free conditions. Among embryos cultured in CREST systems, M21 embryos exhibited diminished hPL, CALR, and PlGF secretion as early as 7…

articles.title: HBV-Associated Immune Remodeling of TNFSF10+ Monocytes Through the LPAR3-GALNT4 Axis During Pregnancy.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.authors: Zhang J, Wen Y, Wu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection can lead to adverse pregnancy outcomes, and monocytes may contribute to immune dysregulation associated with HBV-related pregnancy complications. However, the underlying mechanisms by which HBV influences monocyte function during pregnancy complications remain poorly understood.
METHODS: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from HBV-infected and uninfected pregnant women were analyzed using flow cytometry. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) was performed in anti-TNFSF10 antibody-blocked PBMCs and LPAR3-overexpressing THP-1 cells. LPAR3 was overexpressed in THP-1 cells, followed by cell adhesion, migration, flow cytometry, and immunofluorescence.
RESULTS: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from HBV-infected pregnant women revealed a significant reduction in TNFSF10+ monocytes compared with uninfected controls. Transcriptomic analysis of anti-TNFSF10 antibody-incubated PBMCs showed that LPAR3 was significantly upregulated in TNFSF10+ cells, with enrichment of pathways related to immune regulation and pregnancy-associated biological processes and innate immune responses. Hepatitis B virus X (HBx) overexpression impaired THP-1 cell adhesion and migration, and reduced TNFSF10+ monocyte-like characteristics, which were partially restored by LPAR3 overexpression. RNA-seq of LPAR3 overexpressing THP-1 cells revealed significant activation of immune and inflammatory signaling pathways. Furthermore, LPAR3 overexpression increased the expression of the glycosylation-related gene GALNT4, and GALNT4 restoration partially rescued HBx-induced impairment of monocyte adhesion and migration.
CONCLUSION: LPAR3 may contribute to the regulation of monocyte functional states and TNFSF10+ monocyte-like characteristics, potentially contributing to immune dysregulation, highlighting LPAR3 as a potential target for immune monitoring and mechanistic exploration during HBV-associated pregnancy.
KEY MESSAGES: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, and monocytes play a critical role in maternal immune regulation. However, the mechanisms by which HBV alters monocyte function and contributes to pregnancy complications remain unclear. This study identifies LPAR3 as a regulator of monocyte functional states and TNFSF10+ monocyte-like characteristics. HBV infection impairs monocyte adhesion and migration, which can be partially rescued by LPAR3 overexpression. LPAR3 may serve as a potential target for immune…

articles.title: Grief, adjustment, and acceptance: A qualitative study of mental health, coping, and identity in people with Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser Syndrome (MRKH).
articles.authors: Marshall N, Hunker KE, Rajesh Z et al.
articles.abstract: Receiving a diagnosis of Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser Syndrome (MRKH) presents unique challenges. Little is known about MRKH-related mental health, coping, and identity across the lifespan or the role of positive adaptation in individuals' experiences of MRKH. Participants completed interviews on mental health, family planning, sexual well-being, relationships, and healthcare experiences. A reflexive thematic analysis approach was used to analyze the data. Three themes represented experiences of living with MRKH: grief, adjustment, and acceptance. Our analysis reconstructed a common pattern across participants' retrospective accounts, in which experiences of grief were often described in relation to the period following diagnosis, while adjustment and acceptance were frequently reflected in participants' narratives of living with MRKH. Participants' experiences of mental health, coping, and identity differed across the three themes. The results suggest that many people with MRKH demonstrate psychological resilience and describe enhanced well-being alongside experiences of grieving, adjustment, and acceptance.

articles.title: A multi-dataset associative analysis of single-cell and bulk transcriptomic profiles in preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Liu B, Cui X, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Preeclampsia is a multifactorial disease involving diverse pathological mechanisms and signaling pathways. However, the specific mechanism of PE is not yet completely elucidated.
METHODS: The scRNA-seq dataset GSE173193 and the bulk transcriptomic dataset GSE74341 were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus and analyzed separately as complementary datasets. The single-cell dataset was used to explore cellular heterogeneity, inferred intercellular communication, pathway activity, candidate regulons, and transcriptional-state trajectories. The bulk dataset was analyzed using CIBERSORT, GSEA, and GSVA to estimate immune-cell fractions and assess their associations with candidate regulators. Cross-dataset findings were interpreted as complementary association-level evidence rather than direct validation.
RESULTS: Within the analyzed datasets, macrophages/monocytes exhibited relatively high inferred communication activity. FOLR2+ macrophages and APOBEC3A+ monocytes were identified as candidate subpopulations of interest, while EVX1 and KLF9 were identified as computationally predicted candidate regulators associated with immune and metabolic pathways. In the bulk transcriptomic dataset, CIBERSORT using the blood-derived LM22 reference matrix estimated higher fractions of dendritic cells and resting mast cells and a lower fraction of activated CD4+ memory T cells in the preeclampsia samples. These estimates may not fully represent specialized placental or decidual immune-cell populations and should not be interpreted as directly measured changes in placental immune-cell abundance. Given the limited number of biological samples and the lack of detailed clinical metadata, these observations should be regarded as exploratory dataset-level associations that may be influenced by inter-individual, gestational, or other clinical heterogeneity.
CONCLUSIONS: This study employed complementary analyses of independent single-cell and bulk transcriptomic datasets to identify exploratory immune-cell and transcriptional associations in preeclampsia. The identified cell populations and candidate regulators provide hypotheses for future investigation but require confirmation in independent cohorts and experimental studies.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Antenatal Interventions in Preventing Pregnancy-Related Complications: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Priyanka U, Upadhayay P, Majumder B et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus, preeclampsia, and other adverse pregnancy outcomes continue to contribute substantially to maternal and neonatal morbidity worldwide. The increasing burden of metabolic and hypertensive complications during pregnancy has strengthened the need for effective, targeted preventive strategies. Although pharmacological, lifestyle, dietary, and healthcare system interventions have been widely studied, their effects vary according to the clinical outcome, population risk profile, intervention intensity, timing, adherence, and healthcare setting. Gaps therefore remain in identifying which approaches provide consistent benefit across different maternal and neonatal outcomes. This review synthesized evidence from randomized controlled trials evaluating interventions intended to improve pregnancy-related outcomes. A structured systematic search and study-selection process was undertaken, and eligible trials included pharmacological, lifestyle, dietary, behavioral, and healthcare system interventions. Data were synthesized qualitatively, and methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using established criteria. The findings indicate that pharmacological interventions, including aspirin, calcium supplementation, and antenatal corticosteroids, showed benefits for selected outcomes in appropriately defined clinical populations and settings. Lifestyle and dietary interventions showed heterogeneous findings, with structured and intensive approaches demonstrating favorable outcomes in some populations, whereas lower-intensity interventions produced less consistent effects on major clinical endpoints. Behavioral and healthcare system interventions improved selected aspects of care delivery and patient-centered outcomes, although effects on major maternal and neonatal clinical outcomes were less consistent. Overall, the evidence supports targeted, context-specific use of preventive interventions rather than direct ranking of intervention categories, while recognizing substantial heterogeneity across populations, interventions, and outcomes.

articles.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Rora-Associated Aberrant Granulosa Cell Differentiation in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
articles.authors: Ji P, Sun S, Xu X et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by follicular developmental arrest, yet the molecular basis underlying impaired granulosa cell (GC) differentiation remains incompletely understood.
METHODS: We constructed a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of ovaries from DHEA-induced PCOS-like mice and matched vehicle controls, and leveraged spatial transcriptomics as an orthogonal reference for major cell-type annotation, followed by in-depth profiling of GC heterogeneity. Pseudotime inference, co-expression networks, and regulon activity analysis were integrated, and findings were validated in independent human GC datasets. In silico Rora perturbation, cell-cell communication analysis, and drug repositioning were additionally performed.
RESULTS: We identified a subset of luteinized mural GCs with robust Rora regulon activation, termed Rora-regulon-active GCs. This subset was markedly enriched in PCOS and was reproducibly observed in independent human GC datasets. Rora-regulon-active GCs exhibited an incomplete luteinization phenotype coupled with lipid-metabolic reprogramming. In silico Rora knockdown partially reconfigured GC differentiation trajectories and shifted the PCOS-skewed subset composition toward control, with concordant changes in metabolic transcriptional programs. Cell-cell communication analyses implicated stromal-derived Mdk-Sdc1 signaling and suggested additional crosstalk with macrophages potentially mediated by ligands such as Vegfa. In silico drug repositioning prioritized betaine hydrochloride and bempedoic acid as candidate therapeutics.
DISCUSSION: Our study delineates a Rora-associated aberrant GC differentiation program linked to PCOS, nominating this aberrant program as a potential cellular basis of PCOS-associated follicular arrest and providing mechanistic and translational leads for precision-targeted therapy.

articles.title: A COLLABORATIVE, DATA-DRIVEN APPROACH TO ADVANCING HEALTH EQUITY ACROSS AN ACADEMIC HEALTH SYSTEM.
articles.journal: Transactions of the American Clinical and Climatological Association
articles.authors: Suntha M, Wiggins TM, He LI et al.
articles.abstract: Recognizing equity as a pillar of health care quality, University of Maryland Medical System (UMMS)-a statewide, integrated academic health system-embarked on a purposeful journey to advance high-quality care for all. Combining organizational change frameworks with principles of high reliability, we established equity as a cornerstone of system transformation in 2021. We have since disaggregated data to identify gaps in nine key patient outcomes: severe maternal morbidity, pediatric asthma-related ED visits, diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, congestive heart failure, opioid prescribing, unplanned readmissions, and patient experience. Through a systemwide "Health Equity Challenge," interdisciplinary teams explored hospital-specific data, analyzed root causes, and selected evidence-based strategies to close identified gaps in outcomes. Efforts over the last five years have yielded 12 unique action plans, with more than 20 strategies tied to defined performance measures. Our health system's collaborative, data-driven approach to advance health equity is facilitating transformative organizational change with measurable impact.

articles.title: Factor H polymorphism elevates granzyme B and impairs complement inhibition in human and mouse models.
articles.authors: Chakravarthy H, Xi J, Yoo HS et al.
articles.abstract: The complement factor H (CFH) Y402H polymorphism is a leading genetic risk factor for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Here, we identify extracellular granzyme B (GzmB) as a crucial mediator connecting complement dysregulation to structural pathology. In non-AMD human donor eyes, the high-risk CFH genotype was associated with increased GzmB-positive choroidal mast cells, membrane attack complex deposition, and distinct vitronectin redistribution. Using in vitro human retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells, we demonstrate that complement fragment C5a triggers GzmB secretion and zonula occludens-1 disruption. RNA sequencing of GzmB-stimulated RPE cells confirmed transcriptomic signatures of barrier dysfunction and cellular stress. Furthermore, GzmB-deficient mice displayed preserved choroidal vitronectin compared with wild-type controls, supporting a role for GzmB in cleaving this terminal complement inhibitor. These findings delineate a pathogenic C5a-GzmB pathway compromising extracellular matrix integrity, implicating extracellular GzmB as a critical downstream mediator linking genetic risk to early AMD onset.

articles.title: Disparities in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and severe maternal morbidity: Evidence from a statewide birth cohort.
articles.authors: Solberg A, Hoppe K, Gangnon R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) complicate 15% of pregnancies nationally and are a major contributor to severe maternal morbidity (SMM). We aimed to characterize temporal trends and demographic disparities in HDP incidence and evaluate the association between HDP and SMM in a statewide cohort.
METHODS: This study is a descriptive and regression-based analysis of a retrospective cohort of Wisconsin births from 2017 to 2023. Data were obtained from the Wisconsin Hospital Association (WHA). Subtypes of HDP were identified using ICD-10 codes. Incidence rates of HDP per 10,000 births and average annual percent changes (AAPC) were estimated using Poisson regression and examined across demographic variables. Outcomes measured included SMM incidence, AAPCs, and SMM indicators by HDP.
RESULTS: Among 388,250 pregnancies, the incidence of nearly all HDP subtypes rose from 2017 to 2023. Severe pre-eclampsia had the highest AAPC (11.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 10.6%-13.0%). HDP incidence was highest in urban areas, though the AAPC in preeclampsia was greater in rural areas (8.7%; 95% CI, 7.1%-10.3%; p = 0.004). Black patients experienced higher incidences of HDP, with significant differences in AAPC for HDP overall, chronic hypertension, and severe preeclampsia (p < 0.001). Patients with HDP had higher SMM rates compared to those without, though the AAPC in SMM did not differ by HDP status.
CONCLUSION: These findings highlight a growing burden of HDP in Wisconsin, with an increase in severe preeclampsia incidence and disparities by geography and race. Targeted interventions in rural areas and for Black patients are needed to improve disparities in HDP incidence and reduce SMM across Wisconsin.

articles.title: Antenatal diagnosis and classification for placenta accreta (adherence) spectrum: Clinical practice guideline and recommendations by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine and the Perinatal Medicine Foundation.
articles.authors: Dall'Asta A, Sen C, Aryananda R et al.
articles.abstract: This practical guidance was developed by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine in collaboration with the Perinatal Medicine Foundation to support antenatal diagnosis and clinical management in pregnancies at risk for placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). It provides an evidence-informed approach to screening, diagnosis, referral, and peripartum planning across healthcare settings with different resources. PAS is increasingly encountered alongside rising cesarean delivery rates, use of in vitro fertilization, and a history of uterine surgery. It remains associated with severe maternal morbidity, including massive hemorrhage, large-volume transfusion, uterine rupture, peripartum hysterectomy, pelvic organ injury, intensive care admission, and maternal death. Early recognition and multidisciplinary care are therefore central to management. Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is considered a potential precursor of PAS. Women with a low implantation site and a previous cesarean delivery are at increased risk. Early transvaginal ultrasound is advised in women with a previous cesarean delivery to establish the implantation site, identify CSP, and support counseling and timely consideration of uterine-preserving treatment. In the second and third trimesters, combined transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound assesses placental location, myometrial thickness and contour, and the uterovesical interface. Sonographic markers include placental lacunae, placental bulge, uterovesical hypervascularity, and bridging vessels, which may occur individually or in combination. Two-dimensional grayscale ultrasound is the mainstay of antenatal assessment, supported by color Doppler; three-dimensional imaging may provide additional information in selected specialist settings. Magnetic resonance imaging has a complementary role when ultrasound is inconclusive, placental location is non-anterior or non-previa, or technical factors limit visualization. Suspected CSP or PAS should prompt referral to a perinatal center with multidisciplinary expertise, blood product support, adult and neonatal intensive care, and access to complex pelvic surgery. Delivery timing and surgical preparation should be individualized.

articles.title: Mode of conception and pregnancy outcomes at term among low-risk nulliparous patients.
articles.authors: Cozzi-Glaser GD, Blanchard CT, Pace LA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Available data suggest that assisted reproductive technology (ART) is associated with adverse perinatal outcomes; however, prior studies have been confounded by multifetal gestations, preterm birth, and patient medical comorbidities. There are limited data on pregnancy outcomes among ART-conceived low-risk singleton pregnancies delivering at term. Thus, we aimed to measure the association between mode of conception and mode of delivery among low-risk nulliparous patients delivering singleton gestations at term.
METHODS: Secondary analysis of the ARRIVE trial (NCT01990612), a multicenter randomized, controlled, unmasked, parallel-group trial of nulliparous patients delivering at term, March 2014-August 2017. Pregnancies were categorized by mode of conception as either ART or spontaneous. The primary outcome was cesarean delivery. Secondary outcomes included a composite of perinatal death and severe neonatal complications, and select maternal and neonatal adverse outcomes. Bivariate analyses compared baseline characteristics and outcomes by mode of conception. Primary and secondary outcomes were compared using multivariable logistic regression to generate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity analyses by type of ART (in vitro fertilization [IVF] vs. ovulation induction [OI] with or without artificial insemination [AI]) and by embryo age were planned.
RESULTS: Of the 6106 participants in the original trial, 6084 met eligibility criteria: 157 (2.6%) conceived with ART and 5927 (97.4%) did not. Among those with ART, 103 (65.6%) underwent IVF and 54 (34.4%) conceived with OI or AI. Patients undergoing ART were noted to have an older age, differing race/ethnicity, lower body mass index (BMI), more likely to be married, employed full-time, privately insured, and less likely to smoke cigarettes. Cesarean occurred more frequently in those with ART than those spontaneously conceived (29.9% vs. 20.2%; OR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.20-2.40). This remained significant after adjusting for confounders (aOR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.15-2.45) and was significant in subgroup analysis comparing IVF conception to spontaneous (31.1% vs. 20.2%; aOR, 1.78; 95% CI, 1.12-2.82). Additionally, there was no difference in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (aOR, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.00-2.73), other maternal morbidities, and adverse perinatal composite (aOR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.49-1.67).
CONCLUSIONS: Nulliparas delivering a singleton fetus at term conceived by ART had an…

articles.title: SCML1 overexpression promotes DNA damage and improves the therapeutic efficacy of cisplatin for ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Zhang P, Zhang Y, Wang M
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OVCA) is one of the most common gynecological tumor and is the eighth most common cause of cancer death in women. Sex comb on midleg-like 1 (SCML1) plays an important role in the regulation of embryonic development, but its role in OVCA has not been detected. SCML1 was identified to be associated with cisplatin resistance in OVCA. The expression of SCML1 in OVCA tissues was verified by testing clinical samples. The effect of SCML1 on the proliferation and drug resistance of OVCA cells was investigated in vivo and in vitro. The expression of SCML1 is significantly lower in OVCA cisplatin-resistant tissues. After SCML1 knockdown, the proliferation ability and cisplatin resistance of OVCA cells were significantly enhanced. The overexpression of SCML1 can inhibit the expression of E2F transcription factor 1 (E2F1) and promote the expression of O-linked N-acetylglucosamine transferase (OGT).

articles.title: Hyperglycemia induces endothelial mitochondrial dysfunction and myeloperoxidase dysregulation in PCOS iPSCs.
articles.authors: Wu CE, Huang CC, Chen TH et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with increased risks of cardiovascular disease (CVD), driven in part by endothelial dysfunction. Using patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), we established an endothelial model to examine cellular responses to metabolic stress independent of the complex systemic environment. We demonstrate that PCOS iPSC-derived endothelial cells (PCOS iPSC-ECs) exhibit a disease-specific susceptibility to hyperglycemia, resulting in impaired angiogenesis, mitochondrial fragmentation, and bioenergetic impairment. This stress-induced injury is accompanied by aberrant intracellular myeloperoxidase (MPO) expression. Consistent with these findings, clinical data revealed elevated systemic MPO levels in women with PCOS that correlate with diastolic blood pressure (DBP), glucose levels, and low-density lipoproteins (LDLs). Our results identify an intrinsic metabolic-oxidative defect, a latent mitochondrial vulnerability triggered by hyperglycemic stress, in the PCOS endothelium. These findings position MPO as a potential biomarker and putative mediator for cardiovascular risk stratification in PCOS.

articles.title: The smooth muscle titin filament system regulates uterus contractility and implantation.
articles.authors: Sur VJ, Fink C, Bergmann N et al.
articles.abstract: Coordinated uterine peristalsis positions embryos for implantation, but the mechanotransduction pathways controlling uterine wave coordination are not well defined. We combined smooth-muscle-specific deletion of titin M-band exons 1 and 2 with vertical agarose gel electrophoresis, mass spectrometry, uterine ring myography, imaging, transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, and targeted immunoblotting. We show that the myometrium expresses smooth-muscle titin and low-abundance full-length titin including the M-band kinase region. Conditional M-band deletion increased oxytocin-evoked force and area-under-the-curve while reducing coordinated wall motion, yielding fewer as well as crowded/mislocalized implantation sites and heavier placentas. Proteomics and immunoblotting identified disruption of an NBR1/p62 autophagy hub with downstream remodeling of excitability, metabolism, and wall mechanics. Reduced telokin and MLCK levels are consistent with impaired relaxation and increased Ca2+-sensitization. Together, these findings establish the titin M-band as a mechanotransductive signaling hub regulating peri-implantation motility with potential clinical relevance for optimizing implantation after in vitro fertilization and preventing ectopic pregnancy.

articles.title: A bioinformatic approach to investigate placental and fetal gene expression during diabetic stress in pregnancy.
articles.authors: Larson E, Ullah A
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Maternal diabetes disturbs the intrauterine environment and poses significant risk to fetal development, yet the molecular responses of placental and fetal tissues to diabetic stress remain incompletely characterized. We applied a comparative bioinformatic framework to two publicly available microarray datasets representing placental/decidua and fetal tissue collected at embryonic day 10.5. Both datasets were processed using RMA normalization, differential gene expression analysis, principal component analysis, functional enrichment analysis, and Pathview pathway visualization in R. Placental/decidual exhibited a comparatively constrained differential-expression profile with only two probes reaching BH-adjusted p < 0.05 and one probe meeting both BH-adjusted p < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1. Rank-based GSEA across the complete gene-ranking distribution was used to identify coordinated pathway-level changes. This analysis identified enrichment of gene programs involving ribosome biogenesis, RNA processing and splicing, cell-cycle and DNA-replication processes, and oxidative phosphorylation. In contrast, fetal tissue exhibited substantially broader differential expression with 2,306 probes meeting both BH-adjusted p < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1. KEGG over-representation analysis identified 62 significantly enriched pathways, including pathways associated with axon guidance, Wnt signaling, focal adhesion, MAPK signaling, and PI3K-AKT signaling. Pathview mapping further demonstrated a broader distribution of transcript-level alterations across fetal signaling components compared with the comparatively localized changes observed in placental/decidual tissue. These findings demonstrate distinct transcriptional responses between placental/decidual and fetal tissue under diabetic stress. The comparatively constrained placental/decidual differential-expression profile together with broader fetal transcriptional alterations is consistent with a model in which the maternal-fetal interface may modulate responses to diabetic stress. Collectively, this comparative analysis identified coordinated molecular processes associated with diabetic pregnancy and provides a framework for early biomarker development in diabetic pregnancies.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40203-026-00778-2.

articles.title: Analysis of Cases Under the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act at a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Retrospective Descriptive Study From Chennai.
articles.authors: V V, S S, J J et al.
articles.abstract: Background and aim Child sexual abuse is a significant public health crisis globally. Despite mandatory reporting requirements under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, systematic hospital-based data on the clinical and obstetric profiles of POCSO victims from individual tertiary care centers in Chennai remain limited. This study aimed to describe the clinico-socioeconomic profile, mode of communication, violence, pregnancy outcome, and medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) in POCSO cases, with a specific focus on victims aged under 18 years presenting with a continuing pregnancy. Materials and methods A hospital-based retrospective descriptive study was conducted at Government Kilpauk Medical College and Hospital, Chennai. Data were extracted from the accident register or AR book for all POCSO cases recorded from January 2025 to June 2026 (18 months). No patient consent was required as this was a record-based retrospective study. A total of 250 cases were analyzed. Results The mean victim age was 15.2 years, and 60.0% were aged 16-17 years. Based on socioeconomic classification, 80.8% belonged to the lower middle class. Social media was the predominant grooming channel (57.6%), with Instagram (27.6%) and WhatsApp (23.6%) (Menlo Park, CA: Meta Platforms, Inc.) leading. Elopement was documented in 45.6%. Juvenile alleged offenders constituted 23.2%. Violence was present in 9.2%; physical injuries in 5.2%. Pregnancy was detected in 27.6% (n=69). Among pregnant victims, 56.5% (n=39) initially expressed willingness to continue the pregnancy, all aged 14-18 years, predominantly from the 16-17 year group (71.8%), 87.2% from the lower middle class, with 89.7% having no contraception awareness. Overall, MTP was subsequently performed in 88.4% (n=61) of pregnant victims, with 85.2% of terminations occurring between 12 and 20 weeks of gestation. Willingness to continue pregnancy was recorded at the time of initial assessment and represented the patient's stated preference at presentation; it did not necessarily correspond to the subsequent pregnancy outcome. Conclusion The subgroup of pregnant victims who wished to continue the pregnancy constituted a distinct medico-legal group requiring multidisciplinary co-management. Digital literacy, reproductive health education, and child marriage prevention are essential priorities.

articles.title: Circulating tumor DNA in body fluids for molecular characterization of cancers beyond tissue and blood.
articles.authors: Shreenivas A, Limaye S, Cristofanilli M et al.
articles.abstract: Liquid biopsy using circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is increasingly used for cancer profiling and monitoring, but blood-based analysis may not capture tumor heterogeneity across anatomical compartments. We evaluated cell-free DNA from cerebrospinal (n = 7), pleural (n = 11), pericardial (n = 1), and ascitic (n = 26) fluids from 45 patients with advanced cancer, comparing molecular findings with matched tissue, blood, and cytology where available. Oncogenic alterations were detected in 87% of body fluid samples, with a median variant allele frequency of 3.15%. TP53 (49%), EGFR (18%), and KRAS (18%) were the most frequently altered genes, and ESCAT tier IA alterations occurred in 31.1% of patients. In six patients (13.3%), potentially targetable alterations were detected in body fluids but not in blood and/or tissue. Among five cytology-negative samples, four were ctDNA positive. These findings support body fluid ctDNA profiling as a complementary approach to tissue, plasma, and cytology, thereby warranting prospective validation.

articles.title: Regional one-step and two-step gestational diabetes screening recommendations and birthweight outcomes in Belgium: A population-based controlled before-after study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics & gynecology and reproductive biology: X
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol X
articles.authors: Costa E, de Meester C, Vercoutere A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) screening practices remain debated. One-step strategies identify more women with GDM, but their population-level benefits remain uncertain. Belgium provides a natural experiment: Wallonia recommended screening with the one-step strategy based on IADPSG criteria in 2012, whereas Flanders continued to recommend a two-step approach.
OBJECTIVE: To compare changes in birthweight-related outcomes and recorded hyperglycaemia in pregnancy (HiP) between these regions after their screening recommendations diverged.
METHODS: We conducted a population-based study including all singleton live births in Wallonia and Flanders during 2010-2011, before the adoption of one-step screening recommendations in Wallonia (n = 211,774), and during 2015-2018 (n = 399,376)., after a transitional implementation period ( between 2012 and 2014). HiP was defined as recorded gestational or pre-existing diabetes. Crude prevalences were calculated by region and period. Logistic and multinomial logistic models estimated changes in HiP, small-for-gestational-age (SGA), large-for-gestational-age (LGA), and macrosomia. Adjusted ratios of odds ratios (aRORs) compared post-versus-pre changes in Wallonia with those in Flanders, accounting for maternal sociodemographic characteristics, body mass index, and parity.
RESULTS: HiP prevalence increased from 2.74% to 4.29% in Flanders and from 5.95% to 8.52% in Wallonia. However, the relative increase was smaller in Wallonia than in Flanders (aROR 0.92, 95% CI 0.87-0.97). The prevalence of SGA decreased from 6.54% to 5.72% in Flanders and from 8.60% to 8.09% in Wallonia, with a smaller relative decrease in Wallonia (aROR 1.11, 95% CI 1.05-1.15). No differential change between regions was observed for LGA (aROR 1.00, 95% CI 0.97-1.04). Macrosomia remained broadly stable in both regions (9.29-9.16% in Flanders and 6.19-6.51% in Wallonia), although a trivial differential change was observed (aROR 1.05, 95% CI 1.00-1.09).
CONCLUSIONS: Although the absolute increase in HiP prevalence was greater in Wallonia, the relative increase in the odds of HiP was smaller than in Flanders, where two-step screening recommendations were maintained. No consistent improvement in birthweight-related outcomes was observed. These findings suggest that changes in screening recommendations may not translate into clinically meaningful population-level changes, although we cannot exclude challenges in their implementation and uptake…

articles.title: Preliminary efficacy of intravitreal faricimab for type 1 retinopathy of prematurity: A pilot case series.
articles.journal: Advances in ophthalmology practice and research
articles.authors: Ma H, Liu H, Zhang W et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSES: This study aimed to first present the preliminary efficacy, reactivation rate, and safety of intravitreal faricimab (IVF) in patients with type 1 retinopathy of prematurity (ROP).
METHODS: This was a single-center, consecutive pilot case series. Infants with type 1 ROP treated with IVF monotherapy (3 mg/0.025 mL) between December 2024 and May 2025 were included. The primary outcomes were treatment response, the reactivation rate, and the interval to reactivation. Secondary outcomes included the absence of ocular complications and significant systemic adverse events.
RESULTS: A total of 10 eyes from 5 infants were included, all of whom completed at least 6 months of follow-up. The mean gestational age was 27.17 ± 0.60 weeks (range, 26.29-28.00 weeks), and the mean birth weight was 1132 ± 344 g (range, 910-1760 g). All eyes (100%) demonstrated complete regression of ROP after initial IVF, with continued peripheral vascularization. Two eyes (20%) from one patient experienced reactivation at 15 weeks after treatment and underwent repeat IVF injection. At the last follow-up, all eyes achieved complete vascularization or reached zone III, with no unfavorable anatomical outcomes, ocular complications, or systemic adverse events.
CONCLUSIONS: IVF monotherapy demonstrated favorable preliminary efficacy and safety in type 1 ROP. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm reactivation rates and durability.

articles.title: Continuous thoracic epidural analgesia as a bridge to delivery for refractory pregnancy-associated anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment syndrome.
articles.authors: Ishii Y, Hosokawa Y, Mori S
articles.abstract: Anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment syndrome (ACNES) is an underrecognized cause of abdominal wall pain. Pregnancy-associated ACNES is uncommon, and its optimal management remains uncertain. A 38-year-old woman in her first pregnancy at 37 weeks and 2 days of gestation presented with severe localized abdominal pain and a positive Carnett's sign. Repeated local anesthetic injections provided insufficient relief. Continuous thoracic epidural analgesia at the T8-T9 level achieved sustained pain control and served as a bridge to cesarean delivery. No recurrence was observed during the first postpartum week. This case suggests that continuous thoracic epidural analgesia may be considered for refractory pregnancy-associated ACNES when less invasive treatments are ineffective.

articles.title: Performance and Safety of a Continuous Glucose Monitoring System in Pregnant Women With Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Multicenter, Open-Label Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.authors: Shen J, Shang H, Zhu W et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is increasingly important in pregnancies complicated by diabetes, where strict glycemic control is essential to prevent adverse outcomes such as fetal macrosomia and preterm birth. In gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)-which accounts for most of the diabetes in pregnancy-maternal hyperglycemia is the primary clinical concern. This study evaluated the accuracy and safety of a factory-calibrated CGM system over 15 days in pregnant women with diabetes, with most having GDM.
METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, open-label trial enrolled 60 pregnant women (95% GDM, 3.3% type 1 diabetes, 1.7% type 2 diabetes). Each participant wore 2 sensors simultaneously, 1 on each upper arm, for up to 15 days. Venous blood glucose reference values were obtained using a Biosen C-line GP+ analyzer. Accuracy was assessed by 20/20% agreement rate, Diabetes Technology Society (DTS) error grid analysis, and mean absolute relative difference (MARD). Safety and usability were also evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 2901 matched CGM-reference pairs were analyzed (1451 from left-arm sensors, 1450 from right-arm sensors). The 20/20% agreement rate was 96.6% (95% CI, 95.6%-97.5%) for the left arm and 96.8% (95% CI, 95.8%-97.7%) for the right arm. The overall MARD was 7.72% (95% CI, 7.33%-8.11%) for the left arm and 7.66% (95% CI, 7.27%-8.05%) for the right arm.
CONCLUSION: The CGM system demonstrated accurate, stable, and safe glucose monitoring over 15 days in pregnant women with predominantly GDM. Its strong performance supports its utility as a reliable tool for glucose monitoring during pregnancy.

articles.title: Creatine supplementation effects on cognition, sleep, and menopause symptoms in response to six weeks of high-intensity resistance training in perimenopausal females.
articles.authors: Baker PA, DelBiondo GM, Kelly CG et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Perimenopause (PERI) women experience cognitive dysfunction, sleep disturbances, and menopause-related symptoms, yet few accessible and time-efficient interventions have been evaluated. The purpose of the current study was to determine the impact of creatine monohydrate (CM) during six weeks of high-intensity resistance training (HIRT) on cognition, sleep, and menopause symptoms in PERI females.
METHODS: PERI females (n = 51; Age: 46 ± 5 yrs) were randomized to CM (n = 18), placebo (PLA) (n = 20), or a non-training control (CON) group (n = 13). CM and PLA groups completed a 5-day loading phase (20 g·day⁻¹) followed by six weeks of maintenance (~ 4.5 g·day⁻¹) combined with twice-weekly progressive HIRT. Cognitive performance (Stroop, Rey 15-item memory test) and prefrontal oxygenation via functional near-infrared spectroscopy were assessed at baseline (BASE), pre- (PRE), and post-training (POST). Sleep and self-reported menopause symptoms (temperature sensitivity, fatigue, soreness, brain fog, and bloating) were monitored daily using a WHOOP wearable wristband.
RESULTS: Stroop reaction time improved over time (congruent: p < 0.001; incongruent: p = 0.004) with no group differences. Prefrontal oxygenation during the Stroop test increased with CM at POST (+ 0.32 ± 2.01%) compared to a decrease with PLA (- 1.62 ± 2.01%; p = 0.003). Sleep consistency showed a time × treatment interaction (p < 0.001), with higher consistency in CM than PLA at week 6 (baseline-adjusted mean difference: +7.4% points, p = 0.015).
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory analysis, CM combined with HIRT was associated with greater prefrontal oxygenation, higher sleep consistency, and fewer self-reported temperature sensitivity days relative to PLA in PERI females.

articles.title: Contraceptive method choice by type of intimate partner violence: findings from the 2015 Colombian demographic and health survey.
articles.authors: du Marchie Sarvaas ES, Svallfors S, Salazar M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major global health issue and limits women's reproductive autonomy. Despite high IPV and contraception prevalences in Colombia, the link between specific types of IPV and contraceptive methods remains understudied. This study aimed to examine associations between IPV and the type of contraceptive method used by Colombian women.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the 2015 Colombian Demographic and Health Surveys. The sample included 13,896 ever-partnered women aged 15-49 who were not pregnant, infecund, or used permanent methods. Contraceptive method was categorised as: no contraception, traditional/fertility awareness methods (FAM), intrauterine devices (IUDs)/implants, oral/injectables, and external condoms. Exposure variables included any IPV, physical, sexual and emotional violence, and controlling behaviour in the past 12 months. Adjusted multinomial logistic regressions were conducted, with a significance level of p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Physical and emotional IPV were associated with higher relative risks of using traditional/FAMs and IUDs/implants, and lower probabilities of using oral/injectables or external condoms. Sexual IPV was associated with higher relative risk and controlling behaviour with lower relative risk of using all contraceptive methods.
CONCLUSIONS: IPV-exposed women were more likely to use long-acting methods that can be used covertly, are less susceptible to partner interference, and require fewer healthcare visits, which may reflect increased contraceptive vigilance. Understanding the impact of IPV on contraceptive methods is necessary to improve women's reproductive autonomy. Integrating IPV screening into family planning services and further research into contraceptive decision-making in abusive relationships is recommended.

articles.title: Maternal mid-pregnancy metabolic profiles and growth trajectories across the first 36 months of life in a UK multi-ethnic birth cohort.
articles.authors: Zielinska-Pukos MA, Zulyniak MA
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the influence of maternal mid-pregnancy metabolomic profiles on offspring anthropometric growth trajectories (weight, length/height, and BMI) across the first 36 months of life in a multi-ethnic birth cohort.
METHODS: This longitudinal study analyzed 1423 mother-child pairs from the Born in Bradford cohort. Using NMR, 147 metabolites were quantified in maternal fasting blood samples collected at 26-28 weeks of gestation. Children's growth trajectories for weight, length/height, and BMI across 0-36 months of life were modeled using latent class growth mixture models. Partial least squares discriminant analysis identified key maternal metabolites distinguishing growth trajectories, followed by linear mixed-effects regression examining associations with WHO growth z-scores adjusted for a minimal set of covariates (ethnicity and gestational diabetes mellitus, GDM).
RESULTS: Three distinct growth trajectories were identified for each anthropometric measure: normative, intermediate, and non-uniform (accelerated for weight and BMI or faltered for length/height). For each growth trajectory, between 30 and 41 metabolites were required to differentiate between trajectories within each anthropometric measure. Fourteen lipoprotein subclasses were required across weight, length/height, and BMI, with an additional 16 to 31 metabolites required in one or two trajectories. Numerous associations between metabolite levels and change in z-score anrthropometric measures were observed and validated within each growth trajectory (-0.47 to 1.5 for weight; -0.87 to 2.2 for height/length; and -0.85 to 1.8 for BMI; P < 0.05) per unit change in metabolite. South Asian ethnicity and GDM were associated with lower z-scores (-0.214 to -0.212 and -0.044 to -0.041 for weight; -0.061 to -0.045 and -0.104 to -0.101 for length/height; and -0.157 to -0.182 and -0.083 to -0.071 for BMI, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Metabolomic profiles in mid-pregnancy, especially lipoproteins, characterize observed offspring growth in different directions and/or strengths in various growth trajectories from birth to 36 months of age.

articles.title: Prevalence of multi-nuclear and multi-ovular follicles within paediatric ovarian tissue: recommendations for systematic subclassification.
articles.authors: Jayasingam M, Assis M, Gook DA et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Do premenarcheal girls have a high proportion of morphologically abnormal ovarian follicles?
SUMMARY ANSWER: A higher prevalence of follicles with an abnormal number of oocytes and nuclei was found in premenarcheal ovarian tissue compared with postmenarcheal tissue.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Morphological aberrations of ovarian follicles, including multi-nuclear oocytes and multi-ovular follicles, have been documented across species, including humans. These specific morphological aberrations, together with other types of abnormal follicles, are more prevalent in the ovaries of children and decline in number with age. However, detailed studies of the prevalence of multi-nuclear and multi-ovular follicles in paediatric ovarian tissue are limited.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: This was an observational study of the ovaries of children and adolescents who underwent ovarian cryopreservation prior to chemotherapy.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: The study recruited participants aged 0-18 years who underwent ovarian tissue cryopreservation at a single centre. Haematoxylin and eosin-stained slides of ovarian biopsies were scanned and analysed to determine follicle number and aberrations in morphology and the cortical area was measured. Abnormal follicles were defined as those with an abnormal number of oocytes or oocyte nuclei. Relationships with menarcheal status (premenarcheal; postmenarcheal) and age were assessed.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: A total of 149 participants' ovarian samples were evaluated in the study, of whom 67 (45%) had follicles with abnormal numbers of oocytes or oocyte nuclei. Amongst 117 participants who had adequate follicle numbers, these abnormal follicle types accounted for 3.8% (902/23 891) of the total number of follicles and were significantly more common in premenarcheal girls (52/80; 65.0%) compared with postmenarcheal girls (15/37; 40.5%; P = 0.013). Ovular abnormalities (in 76.7% of abnormal follicles) were more common than nuclear abnormalities (in 23.3% of abnormal follicles; P < 0.001). Bi-ovular primordial follicles were the most common abnormality, comprising 54% of the total abnormal follicle population and were present in 41.9% of participants.
LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: Small ovarian biopsies were analysed, which may not fully represent the whole ovary. There is also a limited number of participants in each menarcheal group.

articles.title: Endometrial compaction and ongoing pregnancy in modified natural cycle frozen euploid embryo transfer: a prospective multicentre cohort study with standardized transvaginal ultrasound assessment.
articles.authors: De la Torre Pérez E, Castillo-Farfán JC, Carratalá-Munuera MC et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Does endometrial compaction, assessed by transvaginal ultrasound at two measurement time points, predict ongoing pregnancy in patients undergoing single euploid blastocyst transfer in a modified natural cycle frozen embryo transfer (mNC-FET)?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Endometrial compaction of ≥5% between the day of ovulation triggering and the day of embryo transfer was not associated with ongoing pregnancy rate or any secondary reproductive outcome in this prospective multicentre cohort.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Endometrial compaction-a reduction in endometrial thickness (EMT) following progesterone-induced secretory transformation-has been proposed as a potential marker of endometrial receptivity in FET cycles. However, existing evidence is conflicting. Retrospective studies have reported positive associations between compaction and ongoing pregnancy in programmed cycles, while prospective data, including the only prior study restricted to euploid single FET, have not confirmed this relationship. Crucially, most studies have used transabdominal ultrasound for the transfer-day measurement, a recognized source of measurement error. No prospective study has examined compaction exclusively in mNC-FET using transvaginal ultrasound at both time points.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: Prospective multicentre observational cohort study conducted between March 2023 and March 2025 across six assisted reproduction units of Instituto Bernabeu group (Spain). A total of 207 patients who met all inclusion criteria and completed the full protocol were analysed.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Women aged 18-50 years undergoing mNC-FET with a single euploid blastocyst (confirmed by preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy via next-generation sequencing) were included. EMT was measured transvaginally at T1 (day of hCG trigger) and T2 (day of embryo transfer). Compaction was defined as a ≥5% reduction in EMT from T1 to T2. Additional thresholds of ≥10% and ≥15% were evaluated as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was ongoing pregnancy, defined as foetal cardiac activity at 10 weeks of gestation. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, adjusting for age, previous live births, previous miscarriages, BMI, and oocyte origin.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Of 207 patients, 58 (28.0%) met the compaction criterion (≥5%). The compaction group had a significantly greater T1 EMT (9.55 ± 1.54 mm vs 8.39 ± 1.14 mm, P < 0.001) and a lower T2 EMT…

articles.title: Hybrid human-digital motivational incentive intervention protocol for smoking cessation among perinatal Medicaid patients.
articles.authors: Bayrakdarian ND, Tomlinson DC, Bonar EE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cigarette smoking is a top cause of preventable morbidity and mortality that disproportionately impacts those covered by Medicaid. For pregnant individuals, tobacco exposure can lead to health concerns, including increased likelihood of preterm birth and low birth weight. Prior motivational incentive interventions have shown that pregnant individuals are more likely to achieve smoking abstinence, which improves infant health, when provided incentives. However, many interventions are limited by the burden of frequent in-person office visits. Hybrid human-digital interventions can balance the benefits of human-touch with the scalability and reach of digital health.
METHODS: This paper outlines the protocol of a single-arm Perinatal Incentives2Quit program, herein Incentives2Quit-Peri, a hybrid human-digital motivational incentive intervention for smoking cessation. Incentives2Quit-Peri recruits patients through community-partnered clinical sites. Patients are paired with a coach who guides them through enrolling in the Incentives2Quit-Peri mobile app with an integrated carbon monoxide monitor, and in the Michigan Tobacco Quitlink phone program. Patients receive rewards (i.e., virtual or physical gift cards), for intervention engagement and smoking cessation. Building on promising pilot findings, and developed through community-centered design, Incentives2Quit-Peri aims to evaluate technical feasibility and program acceptability, and exploratory outcomes focused on smoking reduction, birthweight, and optimizing intervention engagement and cessation.
CONCLUSION: The Incentives2Quit-Peri program is a key step towards scalable, personalized motivational incentive programs to assist pregnant individuals in pursuing smoking cessation. Furthermore, this program serves as the basis for future programs tailored to varied populations facing tobacco-related health disparities.

articles.title: Phytochemical and biological investigation of Galium sinaicum: Cytotoxic constituents with in vitro PARP-1 inhibitory activity.
articles.authors: Elbermawi A, Zulfiqar F, Khan IA et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical carcinoma remains one of the greatest women's health challenges at a global level, usually constrained by chemoresistance and systemic toxicity despite advances in diagnostic screening and treatment strategies. In this light, screening for new safe plant-derived phytochemicals is an essential oncological investigation strategy. In this study, a phytochemical profiling of Galium sinaicum aerial parts collected from Sinai led to the isolation and identification of 19 different secondary metabolites, including flavonoids and iridoid glycosides, lignans, phenolic acids, and anthraquinones.
