Among the isolated compounds, myricetin-3-O-rhamnoside (12) was the most cytotoxic compound against cervical cancer HeLa cells, with an IC50 value of 14.92 μM that was comparable to sorafenib. Furthermore, isolariciresinol (4) and rutin (15) showed significant cytotoxic activity (IC50 26.41 and 22.06 μM, respectively). Regarding the molecular target, these three lead constituents inhibited in vitro the activity of PARP-1 activity (IC50 109.6, 122.4, and 153.4 nM) compared to Olaparib (IC50 80.4 nM), indicating that their anti-tumor effect may arise by a combination of direct cytotoxicity and interference with DNA damage repair. Consistent with experimental results, molecular docking of these compounds into the active site of PARP-1 (PDB: 7AAD) resulted in strong binding energies (-8.63 to -9.87 Kcal/mol) and similar binding dispositions to Olaparib. When combined with the favorable ADME prediction, these data prove that G. sinaicum compounds are promising lead scaffolds for preclinical validation, especially in vivo cervical cancer models.

articles.title: In vitro fertilization vs surgery for infertility in women with deep and ovarian endometriosis: a partially randomized patient preference trial.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Benaglia Md L, Vignali Md M, Reschini MSc M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis-associated infertility can be managed either surgically or through assisted reproductive technologies. Given the recent substantial improvement in the accuracy of ultrasound diagnosis of ovarian endometriomas and deep infiltrating endometriosis, surgery is no longer required to detect these disease forms.
OBJECTIVE: Infertile women with ultrasound-diagnosed endometriosis face 2 alternatives; they can be either operated or straight embark in in vitro fertilization. In this study, we aimed to compare these 2 options, as no randomized clinical trial has yet addressed this clinical scenario.
STUDY DESIGN: A multicenter, pragmatic, partially randomized patient preference trial was conducted at 3 Italian tertiary referral centers with expertise in both endometriosis surgery and in vitro fertilization. The trial was designed to compare reproductive outcomes between in vitro fertilization and surgery in infertile women with ultrasound-diagnosed ovarian and deep infiltrating endometriosis. Women with a history of previous surgery for endometriosis or prior in vitro fertilization were excluded. Additional key eligibility criteria were age <40 years, regular menstrual cycles, endometriomas <4 cm, absence of hydrosalpinx, ureteral stenosis or subocclusive bowel symptoms, and normal semen analysis. Women who had a strong preference and declined randomization could be enrolled in a parallel patient preference cohort. Women allocated to in vitro fertilization were scheduled for up to 3 complete in vitro fertilization cycles, whereas those allocated to surgery attempted natural conception. The primary outcome was conception leading to live birth within 12 months of randomization. Analyses were performed according to the intention-to-treat principle. Considering a 20% absolute increase in live birth rate in the in vitro fertilization group as clinically relevant, the preplanned sample size was 206 women (103 per group), at the usual level of α=5% and β=20%. The trial was registered on February 8, 2021 (NCT04743167).
RESULTS: Recruitment began in March 2021 and was discontinued in September 2024 in accordance with the Ethics Committees after the enrollment of 130 women (55 in the randomized cohort and 75 in the preference cohort), owing to investigators' increasing awareness of a markedly higher likelihood of success in women allocated to in vitro fertilization. In the randomized cohort, the number of live births observed in the surgical and in…

articles.title: Assessing the safety of estro-progestin and progestin-only drugs: a signal detection study of meningioma reports in EudraVigilance.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Manuzzi A, Fazio E, Nikitina V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exogenous hormonal therapies are used for contraception and for several gynecologic and menopausal indications, frequently for prolonged periods. Previous epidemiological studies have reported an increased risk of meningioma with some progestins, particularly following prolonged exposure and high cumulative doses. It is a common intracranial tumor with marked female predominance, suggesting a potential role of hormones in its pathogenesis and growth. Most meningiomas are located in the anterior or middle skull base, where a higher prevalence of progesterone receptors has been observed. This evidence further underlines the relationship between hormonal factors and this type of intracranial tumor. Moreover, rapid and spontaneous tumor regression has been reported after cessation of treatment with exogenous hormones or when serum progestogen levels decrease due to physiological factors.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the presence of a safety signal for meningioma among users of estro-progestin and progestin-only therapies using pharmacovigilance data.
STUDY DESIGN: Data from the EudraVigilance database were analyzed using both descriptive and statistical approaches. Three complementary disproportionality methods were applied to strengthen signal detection: reporting odds ratio, information component, and empirical Bayes geometric mean. The study period covered the last 10 years, from January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2025. The drugs analyzed included: drospirenone-ethinylestradiol combination, dienogest-ethinylestradiol combination, drospirenone-only, desogestrel and levonorgestrel. We included all reports in which these drugs were recorded as suspected, excluding those in which they were reported only as concomitant drugs.
RESULTS: A total of 21,091 reports, corresponding to 70,476 drug-adverse drug reaction pairs, were identified. As expected, most reports concerned female patients, consistent with both the indication of these therapies and the known higher prevalence of meningioma in women. Disproportionality signals were identified for drospirenone and desogestrel-only formulations, suggesting a potential association with meningioma: A disproportionality signal was identified for desogestrel-only pills (110 reports; reporting odds ratio 11.11, 95% confidence interval 8.79-14.06; lower limit of the 95% credible interval of the IC 2.64; lower limit of the 95% confidence interval of the EBGM 5.79). A novel exploratory signal also…

articles.title: A collaborative model for bladder exstrophy care: A retrospective review of surgical outcomes, urinary continence, and renal function.
articles.authors: Kamran H, Foroutan H, Azh O et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We report the surgical outcomes of a nine-year collaborative model for managing a predominantly previously operated cohort of patients with bladder exstrophy (BE).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with classic BE managed between 2016 and 2024 during annual collaborative surgical missions. Patients with ≥1 year follow-up were included. Surgical management was individualized and included bladder closure (BC), bladder neck reconstruction (BNR), bladder neck injection (BNI), bladder neck closure (BNC), bladder augmentation (BA), and continent urinary diversion (CUD). Follow-up combined in-person care with telemedicine. Outcomes included continence (volitional voiding ≥3 h), dryness (≥3 h with clean intermittent catheterization), complications, and renal function.
RESULTS: Fifty-five patients were included, 80% of whom had undergone previous reconstruction. Initial procedures included primary BC (n = 11), redo BC (n = 11), BNR without CUD (n = 15), BNR with CUD with/without BA (n = 6), BNC with CUD and BA (n = 7), and BNI (n = 5). At last follow-up, 11 patients (20%) had undergone additional continence surgeries. All primary BCs performed by our team were successful. Following the last major continence procedure, BNR without CUD achieved 36.4% continence and 3% dryness, BNR with CUD (±BA) achieved 66.7% dryness, and BNC with CUD and BA achieved 90% dryness. Overall, 47.3% of patients achieved continence or dryness. Postoperative complications occurred in 30.9% of patients, and no patient developed renal failure.
CONCLUSIONS: A structured collaborative model can deliver outcomes comparable to high-income settings, even in complex, previously operated patients. Individualized surgical planning combined with hybrid follow-up provides a practical and potentially scalable model for delivering specialized BE care.

articles.title: mRNA alternative splicing dysregulation in oocytes causes premature ovarian failure.
articles.journal: Journal of genetics and genomics = Yi chuan xue bao
articles.authors: Yue W, Li YX, Gao D et al.
articles.abstract: Primordial follicle survival determines female reproductive lifespan, yet the post-transcriptional mechanisms governing this process remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that the splicing regulator SRSF2 is required for maintaining the ovarian follicle reserve through the regulation of RNA processing in oocytes. Oocyte-specific ablation of Srsf2 using Gdf9-Cre causes complete female infertility, progressive follicular depletion, and increased follicular apoptosis. Linear amplification of complementary DNA ends and sequencing (LACE-seq) identifies 1609 SRSF2-bound transcripts enriched in RNA-regulatory and cellular homeostasis-related processes. Subsequent RNA-seq analysis reveals broad transcriptomic and alternative-splicing dysregulation after Srsf2 loss, including prominent exon 7 skipping of the oocyte-specific transcription factor Nobox and a marked reduction in full-length NOBOX protein. Supplementation with correctly spliced Nobox mRNA partially rescues follicular developmental defects in vitro, supporting Nobox as a functionally important downstream target rather than the sole mediator of the Srsf2-deficient phenotype. Together, these findings identify SRSF2-dependent RNA processing as an important regulator of oocyte and follicle homeostasis and suggest that disruption of SRSF2-regulated splicing may contribute to ovarian insufficiency.

articles.title: Robot-assisted laparoscopic fertility-sparing resection of accessory cavitated uterine malformation.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Msika A, Rousset P, Robelin L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a fertility sparing robot-assisted laparoscopic resection of accessory cavitated uterine malformation (ACUM) SETTING: A referral center specialising in minimally invasive gynaecological surgery.
PARTICIPANT: A 28 years old G0P0 woman, with a history of a laparoscopic exploration for abdominal pain and appendicectomy was performed. Pathological analysis did not formally diagnose appendicitis. Pelvic symptoms began at the age of 13 with dysmenorrhea, pelvic pain, and later deep dyspareunia. Pelvic MRI was performed in the late adult age and revealed a mass on the side of the uterus, measuring 30 × 30 × 24 mm, classified as FIGO VI from Munro et al.'s leiomyoma subclassification system [1], with a central haemorrhagic component and a peripheral muscular component consistent with the diagnosis of an ACUM.
INTERVENTIONS: A robot-assisted laparoscopic procedure was performed. ACUM was suspected during the procedure. A vertical myometrial incision was created. Careful dissection was then carried out using monopolar energy. The vascular structures were identified and preserved during the dissection. The accessory uterine malformation was removed without uterine cavity perforation. The myometrial layer was then closed using three interrupted 0 polyglactin 910 sutures (Vicryl 0) sutures.
CONCLUSION: ACUM is a rare condition. A diagnostic odyssey is common for young patients with chronic pelvic pain. Vaginal ultrasound and/or pelvic MRI remain the most important complementary imaging tests for making a diagnosis. However, the final diagnosis is histopathological. A FIGO-based classification [1] may be useful for categorizing the location of accessory cavitated uterine malformations and guiding surgical management. In a retrospective cohort study, approximately 70% of lesions were classified as FIGO-type 7 or 8 [2]. Thus, for most patients, fertility-sparing surgery with no uterine cavity effraction is possible and offers complete resolution of pelvic pain. Robotic assistance enables precise dissection with stability and magnification; particularly useful for these lesions, which sometimes do not display a clear dissection plan.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced colposcopy training improves diagnostic reasoning and communication competencies: A randomized controlled study.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Yan C, Li X, Chen X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer remains a major global health issue, and colposcopy training struggles with standardization and scalability. AI has potential to improve medical education, but its effectiveness in colposcopy training remains underexplored.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven virtual patient platform for colposcopy training among resident physicians.
METHODS: In this randomized, assessor-blinded, wait-list-controlled trial, 60 obstetrics and gynecology residents (PGY-2/3) from two affiliated teaching hospitals were enrolled (May 2023-September 2025). Participants were randomly assigned to either the Immediate AI Intervention group (traditional teaching plus an AI platform throughout) or the Wait-List Control group (traditional teaching only during Month 1, followed by the AI platform). The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the Case Analysis score at 1 month. Secondary outcomes included theoretical knowledge, communication performance, diagnostic justification, and operative competence assessed via OSCE.
RESULTS: At 1 month, the Immediate AI group showed superior performance in Case Analysis (78.57 ± 3.72 vs 71.03 ± 5.82, mean difference = 7.54, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 1.54), Diagnostic Justification (81.63 ± 6.21 vs 74.13 ± 6.77, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 1.15), Communication Performance (80.97 ± 3.90 vs 75.77 ± 6.08, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 1.02), and Theoretical Knowledge (84.67 ± 6.27 vs 80.43 ± 5.07, p = 0.006, Cohen's d = 0.74). Operative competence showed no significant difference (p = 0.113). Both groups achieved high proficiency (over 85 points) within 3 months. Satisfaction was high (90.0% participants, 91.7% supervisors).
CONCLUSION: An AI-driven virtual patient platform significantly accelerates the acquisition of diagnostic reasoning and communication skills in colposcopy training, demonstrating high educational efficacy and acceptance for scalable, standardized education.

articles.title: Evaluating the feasibility and impact of a remote, algorithm-based blood pressure titration program in postpartum women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: the postpartum algorithm for text-based hypertension management (PATH) randomized clinical trial.
articles.authors: Vullikanti M, Del Cueto P, Vivaldi M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Optimal postpartum management of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) remains unknown. This pilot randomized control trial explored feasibility and safety of an algorithmic, text-based intervention targeting a blood pressure (BP) < 130/80 mmHg (in accordance with American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association recommendations - ACC/AHA) on hypertension management at 6 weeks postpartum as compared with routine care.
STUDY DESIGN: 200 postpartum patients with HDP (excluding chronic hypertension) were randomized at hospital discharge for delivery or postpartum HDP admission from a tertiary care center in a 1:1 fashion to the intervention (targeting a blood pressure < 130/ 80 mmHg) or routine care. Patients and clinicians were blinded with respect to randomization.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the proportion of patients who achieved normotension as defined by the ACC/AHA (systolic blood pressure < 130 mmHg). Secondary outcomes were frequency of medication titration, outpatient visits, and non-billable healthcare encounters.
RESULTS: The virtual intervention did not differ from routine care with respect to the primary outcome using office- ascertained BPs (72% intervention vs 74% routine care, p = 0.83). At 6 weeks postpartum, clinic systolic BP did not differ by group (121 mmHg vs 119 mmHg, p = 0.3), though home-reported SBPs during the same period were lower among those randomized to the intervention (119 mmHg vs 125 mmHg, p < 0.001). No adverse events occurred in either group.
CONCLUSIONS: As compared to routine care delivered at a tertiary care center, no differences were observed with respect to systolic BP at 6 weeks postpartum using a virtual, algorithm-based intervention. A high proportion of patients in both randomized groups achieving normotension by ACC/AHA targets without adverse events.

articles.title: Context-dependent effects of prenatal low-dose aspirin and low-molecular-weight heparin exposure on placental glucocorticoid barrier function and fetal development.
articles.authors: Chen L, Li M, Xu D et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Placental 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (11β-HSD2) is a key enzyme that protects the fetus by limiting exposure to maternal glucocorticoids and is closely linked to fetal growth restriction (FGR). This study investigated the effects of combined low-dose aspirin (LDA) and low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) on placental 11β-HSD2 and underlying mechanisms.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational cohort study involving 115 pregnant women, including controls, clinically diagnosed FGR pregnancies, and women with autoimmune disease (AID) who received prenatal LDA and LMWH exposure (PAHE). A caffeine-induced FGR mouse model was established, and PAHE effects were evaluated under normal and FGR conditions on fetal growth, organ development, placental 11β-HSD2 expression, and cAMP/PKA signaling.
RESULTS: In the clinical cohort, birth weight was higher in the AID + PAHE group than in the clinically diagnosed FGR group, and cord cortisol levels were lower. In mice, PAHE reduced FGR incidence and increased male fetal growth under FGR conditions, while effects under normal pregnancy conditions were also evaluated. PAHE increased placental cAMP/PKA levels and 11β-HSD2 expression, reduced fetal corticosterone levels, and partially restored selected hepatic, placental, and gonadal alterations under FGR conditions. Under normal and FGR conditions, PAHE was associated with reduced hippocampal markers.
DISCUSSION: The human findings provide hypothesis-generating evidence, whereas the mouse study provides controlled preclinical evidence. PAHE may influence fetal growth through the cAMP/PKA-11β-HSD2 axis, with organ- and pregnancy-context-dependent effects. The hippocampal findings represent a potential developmental safety signal requiring further validation.

articles.title: Ellagic acid mitigates follicular atresia in laying chickens via GPX4 upregulation to block ferroptosis and p53 suppression to attenuate DNA damage.
articles.authors: Yuan Q, Tang X, Yang Z et al.
articles.abstract: Follicular atresia is a critical factor limiting the reproductive lifespan of laying chickens, a process primarily driven by the progressive death of granulosa cells. This study investigates the precise redox mechanisms underlying chicken follicular atresia and evaluates the cytoprotective efficacy of Ellagic Acid (EA). In vivo and in vitro analyses revealed that this atretic process is executed by a lethal synergy between lipid peroxidation-driven ferroptosis (characterized by mitochondrial collapse and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) depletion) and DNA damage response-triggered apoptosis (characterized by the activation of the p53 signaling axis). EA intervention successfully mitigated this structural and cellular degeneration. Mechanistically, molecular dynamics simulations and cellular thermal shift assays provided compelling biophysical evidence that EA physically binds and structurally stabilizes the active pockets of both GPX4 and p53. The indispensability of this dual-targeting paradigm was validated through siRNA-mediated gene silencing: GPX4 knockdown abrogated EA's ability to restore intracellular glutathione and suppress ferroptosis, while p53 knockdown blunted its anti-apoptotic rescue effects. A double knockdown neutralized EA's protective pleiotropy. In conclusion, chicken follicular atresia is structurally governed by a GPX4/p53-mediated interplay between ferroptosis and apoptosis. EA functions beyond a generic antioxidant as a specific, dual-target pharmacological agent, highlighting targeted redox interventions as a highly viable strategy for preserving the ovarian reserve in laying chickens.

articles.title: Schaftoside from galgeuntang as a multi-target class I histone deacetylase inhibitor: Integrated molecular docking, dynamics, and systems pharmacology analysis.
articles.authors: Shah FH, Cho JS, Lee SH et al.
articles.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are enzymes that remove acetyl groups from lysine residues of histone proteins, playing a critical role in gene expression regulation. Particularly, Class I HDACs (HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC8) are implicated in cancer development and have attracted significant interest as therapeutic targets. However, developing isoform-selective HDAC inhibitors remains challenging. We screened 1625 phytocompounds from the Korean herbal formulation Galgeuntang using the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology database. After applying drug-likeness filtering, 235 compounds underwent molecular docking against HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC8. Schaftoside emerged as the sole candidate engaging all three isoforms, with binding energies of -115.1, -103.8, and -135.5 kcal/mol, respectively. ADMET profiling, quantitative cytotoxicity predictions across multiple cancer cell lines, and in silico gene expression analysis were then performed. One hundred nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable complex formation and PCA-based free energy landscape analysis revealed well-defined conformational minima for each complex. Schaftoside exhibited potent predicted cytotoxicity against hematological and gastrointestinal malignancies (selectivity Index: 8.7-18.6), including the cisplatin-resistant A2780cisR ovarian carcinoma line. In silico transcriptomic profiling predicted downregulation of oncogenic drivers (MYC, STAT3, AKT1) with concurrent upregulation of tumor suppressors (TP53, CDKN1A) and suppression of the HDAC machinery itself. ADMET profiling revealed high aqueous solubility but limited membrane permeability, indicating that structural optimization will be required. Schaftoside therefore constitutes a promising multi-target Class I HDAC inhibitor scaffold, warranting experimental validation through enzymatic assays, histone acetylation analysis, and cell-based cytotoxicity testing.

articles.title: Mortality after ventriculoperitoneal shunting for idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus and its clinical predictors.
articles.authors: Hamouda AM, Kumar R, Pennington Z et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) often have comorbid conditions that may adversely impact survival, but long-term mortality risk in this population remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: Patients who underwent VPS placement for iNPH at a single tertiary care center between 2017 and 2025 were identified. Comorbidities, demographic characteristics, and perioperative complications were evaluated using univariable Cox regression analyses to identify factors associated with mortality at the last follow-up. Comorbidities were quantified with the modified Frailty Index-5 (mFI-5) and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI).
RESULTS: 452 patients were included (median age, 75.3 years; 61.9% male). Forty-four (9.7%) died during follow-up (median 39.1 months), with a median postoperative survival of 19.8 months and a median age at death of 78.4 years. Median mFI-5 was 1.0 and median CCI was 2.0. Baseline comorbidities in total cohort included prior myocardial infarction (MI) in 5.8% of patients, congestive heart failure (CHF) in 6.9%, cerebrovascular accident (CVA) in 14.4%, dementia in 27.1%, and functional dependence in 54.9%. At presentation, 96.0% had gait impairment, 84.5% had cognitive deficits, and 81.6% had urinary incontinence. Regarding perioperative outcomes, 57 patients (12.6%) were hospitalized more than one day and 30 (6.7%) required non-home discharge. Postoperative subdural fluid collections occurred in 13.6% of patients, while 6.9% underwent shunt revision. On multivariable Cox regression analysis, higher CCI (HR 1.27, p = 0.005) and hospitalization >1 day (HR 3.20, p = 0.001) were independently associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSION: Nontrivial rates of mortality are seen following VPS in iNPH - approximately estimated at 10% over four years in the present study. Increased mortality appears correlated with more extensive comorbidities and poorer functional status, highlighting the importance of careful patient selection in this frail population. Notably, this mortality rate closely approximates the mortality expected on an actuarial basis for an age- and sex-matched general population and is substantially lower than mortality previously reported for patients with mild cognitive impairment, suggesting that VPS may mitigate the excess mortality otherwise anticipated in this population.

articles.title: Ex vivo γ-globulin treatment of oocytes in women with anticentromere antibody-related infertility: An exploratory phase I/II study.
articles.authors: Teramoto S, Ueno T, Aono F et al.
articles.abstract: Anticentromere antibodies (ACAs) impair chromosome segregation of oocytes and embryos, contributing to repeated in vitro fertilization failure. We evaluated whether ex vivo γ-globulin supplementation of oocyte culture medium could improve reproductive outcomes without systemic administration of high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin. This prospective study enrolled women aged 30-46 years with infertility and ACA titres ≥ 1:640 undergoing intracytoplasmic sperm injection. In Phase I, 40 oocytes underwent parallel dose-ranging at 0%, 1.0%, 1.5%, and 2.0% γ-globulin. No concentration met the prespecified criterion for an unacceptable reduction in fertilization with ≥ 1 pronucleus, and 2.0% was selected for Phase II. The γ-globulin-treated cohort (n = 16) was compared with historical controls (n = 28) and age-matched ACA-negative controls. In the primary oocyte-based analysis, normal fertilization rates were similar between treatment and historical control groups, whereas treatment was associated with higher good-quality blastocyst (9.6% vs. 4.2%; risk ratio [RR], 2.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-4.93) and live birth rates (4.0% vs. 0.4%; RR, 11.40; 95% CI, 1.35-96.58). A patient-based analysis similarly showed a higher cumulative live birth rate than in historical controls (31.3% vs. 3.6%; P = 0.018). A supplementary age-adjusted mixed-effects analysis accounting for clustering within patients and retrievals yielded a consistent but imprecise association with higher odds of live birth (adjusted OR, 12.02; 95% CI, 1.38-104.45; P = 0.024). Several oocyte-based developmental outcomes remained lower than in ACA-negative controls. These findings provide preliminary proof of concept, with potential benefit observed in isolated oocytes without immune cells. Further studies are required.

articles.title: Sex- and gender-related differences in narcolepsy and idiopathic hypersomnia: a narrative review.
articles.authors: Chung JS, Tao G, Lin A et al.
articles.abstract: Sex- and gender-related differences are increasingly recognised across central disorders of hypersomnolence, although evidence varies between narcolepsy type 1, narcolepsy type 2 and idiopathic hypersomnia. Literature suggests females experience longer diagnostic delays in narcolepsy and are more frequently diagnosed with idiopathic hypersomnia. Females also report greater subjective sleepiness, poorer quality of life and higher rates of psychiatric comorbidity, whereas males may experience greater impacts on personal relationships and higher rates of suicidality. Preclinical studies demonstrate sex-specific differences in the orexin system, stress responses, energy metabolism and neuroendocrine regulation, providing plausible mechanisms for clinical heterogeneity; however, human evidence remains limited and inconsistent. Sex-related differences in objective sleep testing and treatment response have been reported, although few studies were designed to evaluate these outcomes. Women face additional management challenges related to pregnancy, contraception and medication safety as reproductive safety data remain limited for many wake-promoting and anti-cataplectic therapies. Overall, substantial evidence gaps remain, particularly for narcolepsy type 2 and idiopathic hypersomnia. Future prospective, sex-stratified studies and objective biomarkers capable of identifying biologically meaningful disease subtypes are needed to improve diagnosis, refine disease classification and support personalised management.

articles.title: Dihydrotanshinone I suppresses ovarian cancer by targeting splicing factor SRSF1 to regulate the long non-coding RNA SLC8A1-AS1/FOXO1 axis.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.authors: Tu X, Yang R, Miao C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a lethal malignancy with limited therapies. The natural compound dihydrotanshinone I (DHT) exhibits broad antitumor activity, yet its precise molecular targets and mechanistic interplay with oncogenic lncRNAs in OC remain largely unexplored.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the molecular targets and underlying mechanisms of DHT‑regulated lncRNAs in OC.
STUDY DESIGN: DHT efficacy was evaluated in vitro and in vivo. Mechanisms were investigated via lncRNA profiling, transcriptomic analysis, functional assays, and protein‑binding experiments.
METHODS: The antitumor efficacy of DHT was assessed in OC cells and xenograft models. LncRNA candidates were screened using microarray and validated by clinical cohort analysis. The regulatory role of SLC8A1-AS1 was further verified through functional assays. RNA pull-down/MS and RIP were performed to identify proteins binding to SLC8A1-AS1. Rescue experiments were conducted to evaluate whether SRSF1 influences SLC8A1-AS1 stability. The DHT-SRSF1 interaction and binding sites were examined through SPR, CETSA, DARTS, MS, and molecular docking. Transcriptomics and western blot were conducted to analyze downstream signaling cascades.
RESULTS: DHT significantly suppressed OC growth. SLC8A1-AS1 was highly expressed and associated with poor prognosis in OC. Mechanistically, SRSF1 bound to SLC8A1-AS1 and enhanced its stability, activating the PI3K/AKT/FOXO1 pathway. DHT directly bound to SRSF1 and induced its degradation, downregulating SLC8A1-AS1 expression and inactivating the pathway, ultimately suppressing proliferation in OC.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies SLC8A1-AS1 as a novel prognostic biomarker in OC and provides the first evidence that DHT exerts its antitumor effects by targeting the SRSF1/SLC8A1-AS1/FOXO1 axis. These findings unveil the role of SLC8A1-AS1 in OC progression and elucidate the mechanistic basis for the therapeutic potential of DHT.

articles.title: Family planning in multiple sclerosis: An Australian perspective.
articles.authors: Lechner-Scott J, McCombe P, Buckland A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop evidence-based, Australia-specific recommendations for managing multiple sclerosis (MS) before conception, during pregnancy and after birth, balancing maternal health, disease control, and fetal safety.
METHODS: A panel of seven Australian MS specialists, from academic and clinical backgrounds, convened (April-October 2025) via virtual meetings and email correspondence. A targeted literature review covered MS, pregnancy, postpartum relapse, breastfeeding, vaccination and disease-modifying therapy safety. Guidance from the Therapeutic Goods Administration, international clinical guidelines, and safety data were examined to inform interpretation.
RESULTS: Evidence indicates that MS does not increase adverse pregnancy outcomes, although a higher risk of small-for-gestational-age birth may occur. Treatment selection should account for teratogenicity and rebound risk. Teriflunomide, fingolimod, siponimod and cladribine require cessation well before conception and are contraindicated during breastfeeding. Natalizumab can be continued until conception and through the first and second trimesters using extended-interval dosing; postpartum resumption is advised to minimise rebound relapses. Ofatumumab and ocrelizumab should be stopped if pregnancy is confirmed. Treatment decisions should be individualised through shared decision-making. European Union guidance supports use of ocrelizumab during breastfeeding, consistent with evidence of minimal monoclonal antibody transfer into breastmilk. As breastfeeding does not prevent relapse, early postpartum DMT resumption is recommended to reduce relapse risk. Contraceptive use remains low despite requirements for many therapies.
CONCLUSION: With proactive planning, women with MS can achieve optimal pregnancy outcomes. This consensus integrates evidence, regulatory considerations and Australian guidance to support a practical framework for family planning in MS.

articles.title: Circulating tumor DNA in gynecologic oncology: moving from the present into the future.
articles.authors: Chang YE, Lin YG
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The use of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) offers a promising, minimally invasive alternative to tissue biopsies for real-time surveillance in gynecologic cancers. This review provides an overview of ctDNA technology, its clinical interpretation and foundational applications in oncology, as well as its current uses in gynecologic cancers.
RECENT FINDINGS: Selecting the appropriate ctDNA assay is critically important, as current platforms address distinct clinical questions by offering either deep genomic sequencing data (i.e. ultra-sensitive and deeply sequenced) or broad genomic information (i.e. thousands of biologically relevant genomic variants). Robust prospective data in other solid tumors are now emerging and may inform how ctDNA can be utilized in gynecologic cancers to inform tumor burden or track evolving tumor biology.
SUMMARY: Thoroughly understanding the strengths and limitations of ctDNA usage in gynecologic cancer is imperative for accurate patient counseling and well-informed real-time therapeutic decision-making.

articles.title: Semen parameters on the day of fertilization and PGT-A outcomes in couples with idiopathic early recurrent pregnancy loss.
articles.authors: Zhu S, Hou X, Liu W et al.
articles.abstract: The association between semen parameters on the day of fertilization and preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) outcomes in couples with idiopathic early recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) remains uncertain. This retrospective cohort study included 998 couples with idiopathic early RPL who underwent their first next-generation sequencing-based PGT-A cycle between January 2017 and December 2022, yielding 4352 biopsied blastocysts. Semen volume, sperm concentration, and total motility were assessed on the day of intracytoplasmic sperm injection according to World Health Organization sixth-edition thresholds. Embryo-level associations were analyzed using generalized estimating equations, and clinical outcomes after single euploid frozen-thawed embryo transfer were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Lower sperm concentration (<16 × 106/mL) was not significantly associated with embryo aneuploidy but was associated with increased odds of embryo mosaicism in the adjusted model (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.437, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.108-1.864; p = 0.006). This association remained significant in the multivariable model (OR 1.432, 95% CI 1.084-1.892; p = 0.012). Semen volume <1.4 mL and total motility <42% were not significantly associated with embryo aneuploidy or mosaicism. In analyses of reproductive outcomes after single euploid embryo transfer, semen volume, sperm concentration, and total motility were not significantly associated with live birth or total pregnancy loss. These findings suggest that reduced sperm concentration on the day of fertilization may be associated with embryo mosaicism in couples with idiopathic early RPL undergoing PGT-A, whereas conventional semen parameters do not appear to compromise live birth or pregnancy loss outcomes once a euploid embryo is transferred.

articles.title: Changes in management of FETO-treated infants with severe CDH.
articles.authors: Jeffreys E, Jenkinson A, Kronfli R et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aims to evaluate changes in outcomes and management of infants with severe congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) undergoing fetoscopic endoluminal tracheal occlusion (FETO) across two eras, and to compare outcomes by side of defect over the last decade. Retrospective review of liveborn infants with severe CDH (observed to expected lung to head ratio [O/E LHR] < 0.25 left-sided; < 0.45 right-sided) who underwent FETO at King's College Hospital, London, UK, and survived to delivery. Fifty-eight infants were included across two 5-year periods (2002-2007 and 2020-2025). Survival improved from 44.1% to 70.8% (p = 0.044). Right-sided defects were more common in the second epoch (9% versus 54%, p < 0.001). All infants in the second era had echocardiography-guided inotropic and ventilatory management, which was not universally available earlier. In the second epoch surgical repair occurred later (4.0 versus 6.5 days, p = 0.018), repair by two-stage abdominal closure (laparostomy) increased from 0% to 77.8% (p < 0.001) and recurrence fell from 33 to 0% (p = 0.042). Mechanical ventilation, oxygen therapy and admission were longer latterly. In thirty-one infants delivered between 2015 and 2025, preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) occurred in 67% of left-versus 92% of right-sided CDH, but at an earlier gestational age in left (p = 0.032). Left CDH infants had longer duration of mechanical ventilation (p = 0.04) and hospital stay (p = 0.006) with no mortality difference (exploratory).
CONCLUSION: Survival of FETO-treated severe CDH infants improved from 44 to 71% alongside later repair, staged abdominal closure and echocardiography-guided management. Left-sided defects had greater respiratory morbidity and longer admission than right-sided defects without changing survival.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • FETO improves survival in severe left-sided CDH, but postnatal management has changed substantially since its introduction.
WHAT IS NEW: • Survival of FETO-treated severe CDH rose from 44 to 71% over two decades despite more right-sided defects. Repair occurred later, following haemodynamic and respiratory stabilisation (as guided by echocardiography) with staged abdominal closure in 77.8% of recent repairs; recurrence decreased from 33 to 0%. • Left-sided CDH infants had greater respiratory morbidity and length of stay than right-sided CDH infants, without a significant difference in mortality.

articles.title: Association between voiding dysfunction symptoms and health-related quality of life in primary school children: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Yoğurtcu H, Ozbicakci FS
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Voiding dysfunction is a common pediatric problem and accounts for roughly one-fifth of visits to pediatric urology clinics. We examined whether voiding dysfunction symptoms were related to health-related quality of life in primary school children. We conducted a cross-sectional correlational study with 498 children aged 8-12 years and their parents from three primary schools in İzmir. Parents completed the Voiding Dysfunction Symptom Score (VDSS), whereas the children completed the Kid-KINDL Health-Related Quality of Life Questionnaire. Sixty children (12%) screened positive on the VDSS. Urgency was the most frequently reported symptom (34.9%), followed by voiding more than seven times per day (18.7%) and daytime incontinence (15.3%). Total VDSS and Kid-KINDL scores showed a weak inverse correlation (r = -0.112, p = 0.012; r2 = 0.013, indicating a small effect size). Before covariate adjustment, children who screened positive on the VDSS had lower total quality-of-life scores than those who screened negative on the VDSS (74.3 ± 12.1; 77.9 ± 12.3). The largest unadjusted difference was in the Family Relationships subdimension (p < 0.05). Neither this difference nor the total-score difference remained significant after Bonferroni correction or adjustment for demographic covariates.
CONCLUSION: The unadjusted findings suggested lower health-related quality of life among children who screened positive on the VDSS, with the clearest difference in Family Relationships. These associations were no longer significant after demographic adjustment.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Among school-aged children, voiding dysfunction is relatively common and has been linked to poorer psychosocial functioning and lower quality of life.
WHAT IS NEW: • VDSS-positive screening was associated with lower unadjusted quality-of-life scores, especially in Family Relationships, but this association did not persist after covariate adjustment.

articles.title: Sex differences in exercise-induced pro-inflammatory cytokine responses relevant to Alzheimer's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Lee H, Noh KW, Sung JY et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundChronic inflammation contributes to the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD), and physical exercise is a promising nonpharmacological strategy for modulating systemic inflammatory responses. However, evidence regarding sex- and exercise type-specific effects on AD-related pro-inflammatory cytokines remains fragmented.ObjectiveTo quantitatively synthesize evidence on sex differences in inflammatory cytokine responses relevant to AD according to exercise type, focusing on tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-1β (IL-1β).MethodsA systematic search identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of aerobic exercise (AE), resistance exercise (RE), and combined exercise (CE) on circulating cytokines in adult men and women. Percentage changes from pre- to post-intervention were extracted and pooled using random-effects meta-analyses. Subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, exercise type, cytokine, and menopausal status.ResultsThirty-two RCTs involving approximately 1200 participants were included. TNF-α showed the most consistent response, with significant reductions after AE and CE in both sexes, whereas RE reduced TNF-α primarily in women. IL-6 decreased across exercise type-dependent modalities, with the largest reductions following AE and no consistent sex-specific differences. Effects on IL-1β were limited and largely nonsignificant across exercise types.ConclusionsExercise-induced modulation of inflammatory cytokines relevant to AD is cytokine-specific and exercise type-dependent, with additional influence from biological sex. TNF-α appears most responsive to exercise, supporting AE and CE as potential strategies to mitigate systemic inflammation associated with AD risk. Further trials are needed to clarify sex-specific mechanisms and the clinical relevance of exercise-induced inflammatory modulation across the AD continuum.

articles.title: Second-trimester Maternal Serum Insulin-like Growth Factor Binding Protein 4 to Sex Hormone-binding Globulin Ratio as a Predictor of Spontaneous Preterm Birth: A Prospective Observation Study from North India.
articles.authors: Sachan R, Sharma S, Shyam R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The ratio of maternal serum insulin-like growth factor binding protein 4 (IGFBP-4) to sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) has emerged as a promising proteomic predictor, but validation in high-burden settings including India is limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the predictive value of the second-trimester IGFBP-4/SHBG ratio for spontaneous preterm birth (PTB) and association with fetomaternal outcome.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was carried out over a period of 1 year. A total of 190 singleton pregnant women between 16 and 21 weeks of gestation were enrolled. Maternal serum IGFBP-4 and SHBG levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) technique using an ELISA kit as per the producer protocol. Participants were followed till delivery and categorized into Group A preterm (delivery <37 weeks, n = 54) and Group B term (delivery ≥37 weeks, n = 136). Predictive accuracy (AUROC) of the ratio for PTB was assessed. Fetomaternal outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: The PTB rate was 28.4%, and the second-trimester IGFBP-4/SHBG ratio was significantly higher in Group A than Group B (0.619 ± 0.399 vs. 0.191 ± 0.242; P < 0.001). ROC analysis for the ratio at enrollment yielded an AUC of 0.906 (95% confidence interval: 0.859-0.952). At a cutoff >0.188, the ratio showed 94.4% sensitivity and 79.4% specificity for predicting PTB. A raised baseline ratio was significantly associated with spontaneous preterm delivery (86.1% preterm vs. 37.8% term, P < 0.001), similarly low birth weight (74.7% vs. 36.0%, P < 0.001), low 5-min Apgar (10.1% vs. 0.0%, P = 0.001), and increased neonatal intensive care unit admission (P = 0.031).
CONCLUSION: The second-trimester maternal serum IGFBP-4/SHBG ratio is a highly sensitive and specific predictor for spontaneous PTB. It also correlates strongly with adverse neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Ovine follicular fluid extracellular vesicles improve oocyte maturation and exhibit ribosome-related cargo signatures†.
articles.authors: Tang Y, Liu J, Liu L et al.
articles.abstract: Oocyte developmental competence is critical for efficient assisted reproduction in livestock. In vitro maturation (IVM) is often the first step in in vitro embryo production, making improvements in oocyte quality an important goal. We supplemented IVM medium with ovine follicular fluid-derived extracellular vesicles (oFF-EVs), evaluated oocyte maturation and subsequent embryonic development, and characterized vesicle cargo. The isolated oFF-EVs exhibited typical small extracellular vesicle features. Among the concentrations examined, 30 μg/mL yielded the highest mean maturation rate and greatest cumulus expansion. PKH67 tracing revealed time-dependent uptake by cumulus cells. Supplementation reduced reactive oxygen species levels, increased glutathione content, and maintained mitochondrial membrane potential. It also improved cortical F-actin organization, cortical granule distribution, chromosome distribution, and spindle morphology, accompanied by increased total AKT abundance. Following in vitro fertilization, the cleavage rate and blastocyst total and inner cell mass cell numbers increased, whereas the blastocyst rate was not significantly altered. Small RNA sequencing identified 84 microRNAs dominated by the let-7 family, while proteomics identified 4,730 proteins enriched in RNA processing, ribonucleoprotein complexes, intracellular transport, and protein homeostasis. Integrated analyses revealed a ribosomal protein module centered on FAU ubiquitin-like and ribosomal protein S30 fusion (FAU), suggesting ribosome-related cargo signatures. These findings support oFF-EV supplementation as a strategy to improve sheep oocyte maturation and subsequent developmental competence and identify cargo features for further functional investigation.

articles.title: Placental Interdigitation Is Associated with Reproductive Pace across Mammals.
articles.authors: Parmeggiani C, Pan T, Boyd M et al.
articles.abstract: The placenta is a transient organ mainly derived from fetal tissue that is essential for establishing metabolic and immune interactions that support healthy pregnancies in eutherian mammals. Across mammals, placentas show high morphological diversity in both the degree of tissue invasiveness and in the complexity of tissue integration between maternal and fetal tissues. This variation is thought to reflect strong selective pressures on reproductive strategies, balancing maternal investment, offspring development, resource transfer, and reproductive pace. Previous studies have explored the relationship between placental morphology and mammalian life history focusing mainly on placental invasiveness and giving less attention to placental interdigitation. Here, we expand the scope of previous comparative work by analyzing 509 mammalian species to examine how three life history traits (gestation length, interbirth intervals, and relative litter mass) are associated with placental morphology. We also test whether placental morphology covaries with broader multivariate life history structure using phylogenetic principal component analyses (pPCA). We found that, relative to invasiveness, placental interdigitation was more strongly associated with reproductive timing. Labyrinthine placentas were associated with shorter gestation lengths than villous and trabecular placentas, and species with villous placentas were associated with the longest interbirth intervals. Placental invasiveness showed no association with life history variation. Neither invasiveness nor interdigitation was associated with relative litter mass. Our results suggest that, although diverse census timing may have limited the extent of our interpretation, placental interdigitation is associated with reproductive timing (gestation length and interbirth intervals), whereas neither interdigitation nor invasiveness is associated with relative litter mass, an approximate measure of offspring mass produced per reproductive event relative to adult body mass.

articles.title: Dioscin Promotes Ferroptosis in Cervical Cancer Cells via the TIGAR-ROS Axis.
articles.authors: Liu Y, Xi H, Min S et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer seriously threatens women's life and health, highlighting the urgent need for targeted therapies. TP53-induced glycolysis regulatory phosphatase (TIGAR), upregulated in cervical cancer and regulated by HPV E6, may be involved in cervical cancer progression, making its inhibition a potential therapeutic strategy. This study aims to investigate the role and mechanism of TIGAR in cervical cancer ferroptosis resistance and identify a TIGAR-targeting drug to suppress cervical cancer advancement. Through RNA-seq, transmission electron microscopy, and western blotting, we found that TIGAR knockdown significantly promoted ferroptosis by increasing intracellular lipid reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels. Furthermore, through molecular docking, CETSA, and SPR analysis, we identified Dioscin as a compound that binds to TIGAR. Dioscin treatment effectively inhibited cervical tumors via TIGAR both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, Dioscin interacted with TIGAR and promoted ferroptosis, at least in part, through the TIGAR-ROS axis. Collectively, these findings indicate that TIGAR suppresses ferroptosis via lipid ROS reduction, while Dioscin counteracts this process, at least in part, through the TIGAR-ROS axis. Thus, Dioscin holds promise as a potential targeted therapeutic agent for cervical cancer.

articles.title: Menopause Literacy Gaps Across Individual, Healthcare and Societal Levels: A Qualitative Study of Women's Experiences and Healthcare Providers' Perspectives.
articles.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
articles.authors: Pourshahrokhi N, Farokhzadian J, Hunter MS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause is a major life transition that can affect women's physical, psychological, cognitive, sexual and social well-being. Despite the availability of evidence-based interventions, many women remain insufficiently informed and experience difficulties accessing reliable information and appropriate support.
OBJECTIVES: To explore menopause-related information needs and challenges from the perspectives of menopausal women and healthcare professionals and to identify individual, healthcare-related and societal factors influencing menopause literacy.
DESIGN: A qualitative study informed by a constructivist paradigm was conducted using semi-structured interviews and conventional qualitative content analysis.
METHODS: Twenty-two peri- and postmenopausal women and 10 healthcare professionals were purposively recruited from healthcare settings in Southern Iran. Data were collected until data saturation was achieved, defined as the point at which no new codes or categories emerged from successive interviews. Interview transcripts were analysed using conventional qualitative content analysis following the approach of Graneheim and Lundman. Trustworthiness was enhanced through prolonged engagement, member checking, peer debriefing and established criteria for qualitative research.
RESULTS: Three interrelated themes were identified: understanding and accepting menopause, menopause management, and challenges of transition. Women described menopause as an unexpected and multidimensional transition affecting physical, psychological, cognitive, sexual, social and occupational well-being. Both women and healthcare professionals identified substantial gaps in menopause literacy and emphasised the need for timely education, evidence-based information and supportive healthcare. Symptom management strategies, lifestyle modification, family and peer support, and access to reliable information were perceived as important facilitators, whereas limited awareness, menopause-related stigma, insufficient provider engagement and difficulty identifying trustworthy information were reported as major barriers.
CONCLUSIONS: Menopause literacy is shaped by interacting individual, healthcare and societal factors. Strengthening evidence-based menopause education, improving healthcare support and developing accessible, person-centred information resources may enhance women's ability to navigate the menopausal transition and inform the design of future educational and digital…

articles.title: Development and validation of a nomogram for predicting overall survival in FIGO IB3-IIA2 cervical adenocarcinoma: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Huang Y, Gao X, Li Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The prevalence of cervical adenocarcinoma has risen significantly, complicating management strategies for locally advanced stages. To address insufficient prognostic data for International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage IB3-IIA2 cervical adenocarcinoma after radical hysterectomy, this study developed a model to evaluate overall survival (OS).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled patients with FIGO stage IB3-IIA2 cervical adenocarcinoma who underwent radical hysterectomy and platinum-based chemotherapy between March 2016 and December 2020. Baseline data were retrospectively collected from medical records, and follow-up outcomes were prospectively gathered. A Cox proportional hazards regression model was employed to identify the potential factors. A nomogram was developed to assess the probability of OS. The predictive accuracy was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration curve, and decision curve analysis. The Kaplan-Meier methodology was applied to generate the OS curve.
RESULTS: A total of 365 patients were enrolled, including 228 with FIGO stage IB3 and 137 with stage IIA2 disease. The median OS time was 57.8 months. The 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year OS rates were 97.2%, 90.1%, and 83.8%, respectively. Lymphovascular space invasion (hazard ratio [HR] 6.601; 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.012-14.468), surgical margin (HR 24.340; 95% CI 8.342-71.047), lymphocyte count (HR 3.937; 95% CI 2.499-6.202) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (HR 1.224; 95% CI 1.111-1.348) were independently associated with OS. These significant variables were then integrated to formulate a nomogram for predicting 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year OS. The nomogram exhibited excellent and robust discrimination in both the training and validation sets, with area under the curve values of 0.788-0.980 across 1-5 years in both cohorts. Calibration curves indicated a high consistency between predicted probabilities and actual frequencies, whereas decision curve analysis curves confirmed significant clinical net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities.
CONCLUSION: Patients with FIGO stage IB3-IIA2 cervical adenocarcinoma who exhibited lymphovascular space invasion, positive surgical margin, higher lymphocyte count, and higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were at a higher risk of mortality. The nomogram-based prognostic model effectively predicted survival probabilities, serving as a tool for individualized…

articles.title: Impact of real-time digital dashboard on birth outcomes in high-volume tertiary center: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Attali E, Greenberg G, Gabbai D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the impact of implementing a real-time intrapartum digital monitoring dashboard on labor progression and birth outcomes in a high-resource high-volume tertiary care delivery ward.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a university-affiliated medical center. We included all women admitted for an attempted vaginal delivery between January 2012 and December 2022. The intervention group included deliveries from January 2021 to December 2022, after full implementation of the dashboard. The control group included deliveries between January 2012 and May 2019, prior to implementation. Deliveries during the system's rollout phase (June 2019 to December 2020) and elective cesarean sections were excluded. The dashboard displayed real-time maternal and fetal data for all delivery rooms simultaneously. The primary outcome was labor duration, measured from admission to the delivery room until delivery. Secondary outcomes included prolonged second stage of labor, intrapartum fever, perineal lacerations (including obstetric anal sphincter injury), vacuum deliveries, and 5-min Apgar score < 7. Multivariable logistic regression and trend analyses were performed to adjust for potential confounders.
RESULTS: A total of 90 530 women were included in the study (70 922 pre-implementation and 19 608 post-implementation). After adjusting for maternal and clinical characteristics, dashboard implementation was associated with lower risk of labor >6 h (adjusted relative risk [aRR] 0.67, 95% CI 0.6-0.7) and prolonged second stage (aRR 0.64, 95% CI 0.5-0.7) and with fewer perineal lacerations (aRR 0.80, 95% CI 0.7-0.9). There were no significant differences in vacuum delivery rates or adverse neonatal outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Implementation of a real-time digital dashboard for intrapartum monitoring was associated with shorter labor and fewer perineal injuries without compromising neonatal safety, supporting a potential role for ward-wide digital monitoring in intrapartum care.

articles.title: Physical activity during pregnancy and gestational weight gain among nulliparous women: Secondary analysis of the Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-To-Be.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Hsu T, Chen TS, Yu T
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examines the longitudinal association between leisure-time physical activity during pregnancy and gestational weight gain (GWG) among nulliparous women.
METHODS: We analyzed data from 8146 nulliparous women enrolled in the Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-To-Be (nuMoM2b). Physical activity was assessed at three visits using questionnaires and categorized by weekly metabolic equivalent (MET)-hours and adherence to guidelines. GWG was evaluated as the rate of weight gain during successive gestational periods and as gain at or above the 75th percentile. Multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic, lifestyle, dietary, and pregnancy-related factors were used to examine overall and time-dependent associations.
RESULTS: Women with consistently higher physical activity levels experienced a faster rate of GWG during early pregnancy but a slower rate during later pregnancy. Compared with women reporting <7.5 MET hours/week, those reporting ≥21 MET hours/week had a greater early pregnancy rate of GWG (adjusted mean difference 0.032 kg/week, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.009 to 0.056) but a slower later pregnancy rate (-0.026 kg/week, -0.053 to 0.000). Women who consistently met physical activity guidelines were less likely to have GWG at or above the 75th percentile before delivery (adjusted risk ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.98). Time-updated analyses further showed that higher physical activity during mid-pregnancy was associated with a slower subsequent rate of GWG.
CONCLUSION: Leisure-time physical activity was associated with GWG in a stage-specific manner. These findings highlight the importance of considering gestational timing when evaluating the effects of physical activity on maternal weight gain and support continued promotion of physical activity throughout pregnancy.

articles.title: When Menstrual Pain Becomes Care-Worthy: A Qualitative Study of Delayed Care-Seeking Among Young Women With Function-Limiting Dysmenorrhoea in Southwest China.
articles.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
articles.authors: Zhu Q, Jia B, Yu Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysmenorrhoea can disrupt education, work, sleep, mobility and other daily activities, yet recurrent pain that limits daily functioning does not always prompt timely formal care-seeking.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to explore how young women in Southwest China interpret recurrent function-limiting dysmenorrhoea and decide whether to seek formal care.
METHODS: This qualitative study was based in Guiyang, Guizhou Province, Southwest China. Seventeen women aged 18-31 years with recurrent dysmenorrhoea affecting daily functioning took part in semi-structured interviews. Interviews were conducted face-to-face or online, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Five themes were developed: making pain ordinary across family, peers and clinics; keeping pain within the logic of warmth and regulation; when pain becomes care-worthy: functional disruption as a threshold; reproductive expectations and delayed medicalisation; and normal tests, uncertain explanations and delayed re-entry into care. Care-seeking was often delayed as participants normalised menstrual pain, relied on culturally familiar warming or body-regulating practices, had concerns about analgesics or expected pain to improve after childbirth. Non-specific clinical explanations could also temporarily reassure participants and contribute to delay. Participants described seeking formal care when pain disrupted study, work, sleep, mobility or daily activities, when medication or self-management no longer worked, or when reproductive or gynaecological concerns emerged.
CONCLUSIONS: Delayed care-seeking was shaped by whether menstrual pain became recognised as a legitimate reason for formal care. Menstrual health education and clinical communication should validate function-limiting pain, clarify when assessment is needed and provide clear follow-up guidance.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Four women with lived experience of function-limiting dysmenorrhoea helped develop parts of the interview guide. Their feedback during pilot interviews led to additional questions about healthcare access and practical barriers to seeking care. They also supported recruitment and contributed to discussions of interview accounts and developing themes.

articles.title: Rat sarcoma inhibitors in and beyond gynecologic malignancies.
articles.authors: Dwabe S, Samaeekia R, Cristea M
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recent advances in direct rat sarcoma (RAS) inhibition and downstream pathway targeting have created novel therapeutic strategies which can be utilized in gynecologic oncology. This review examines RAS biology, lessons learned from other malignancies, and emerging strategies for gynecological malignancies.
RECENT FINDINGS: KRAS G12C inhibitors in lung cancer established the clinical feasibility of direct RAS targeting, while colorectal cancer studies demonstrated the importance of lineage-specific combinations. KRAS G12D inhibitors, targeted protein degraders, and multiselective RAS(ON) inhibitors represent the next frontier in RAS inhibition, expanding therapeutic options across both gynecologic and nongynecologic tumors. In recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer, therapeutic advances have centered on inhibiting the downstream RAS-mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)-extracellular signal-regulated kinase signaling pathway using MEK or combined RAF/MEK and focal adhesion kinase inhibitors, rather than direct RAS inhibition, demonstrating encouraging clinical responses, leading to accelerated approval for KRAS-mutant disease.
SUMMARY: RAS-pathway directed therapy requires consideration of tumor lineage, specific alleles, and functional pathway dependence. Although clinical progress in gynecologic oncology is most relevant in low-grade serous ovarian cancer, emerging non-G12C therapies warrant further evaluation across gynecologic malignancies. Novel combinations and integrated biomarkers will be necessary to improve patient selection and overcome therapeutic resistance.

articles.title: Spermidine-mediated AMPK signaling pathway drives M2 macrophage polarization to promote the growth of vaginal cancer.
articles.authors: Hu P, Gao Y, Xu J et al.
articles.abstract: Vaginal cancer represents a rare and malignant tumor in the reproductive tract, with its mechanisms of onset and progression still uncharted. Spermidine (SPD), with its anti-inflammatory biological properties, has been connected to metabolic irregularities in a range of diseases. However, the specific molecular pathways through which SPD may impact the growth of vaginal cancer are not well understood. Consequently, this study delved into the biological effects of SPD within the context of vaginal cancer. Vaginal swabs from healthy individuals and vaginal cancer patients were acquired to quantify SPD levels with an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The effects of supplemental exogenous SPD on vaginal cancer cell viability were examined by the cell counting kit-8 test. The impact of SPD treatment on macrophage polarization was appraised via qRT-PCR and flow cytometry. The expression of AMPK and mTOR, proteins within the AMPK/mTOR signaling pathway, was analyzed in macrophages using the western blot. Elevated levels of SPD were found in vaginal cancer patient samples. The treatment with SPD led to increased phosphorylation levels of AMPK and mTOR proteins within macrophages, thereby activating the AMPK/mTOR signaling pathway. Such treatment also promoted the expression of markers associated with M2 polarization and inhibited those related to M1 polarization. The introduction of an AMPK pathway inhibitor counteracted these results. SPD, which is present at higher levels in vaginal cancer patients, can activate the AMPK/mTOR signaling pathway and induce macrophage M2 polarization that promotes the growth of vaginal cancer cells.

articles.title: Fertility Treatment and Risk of Melanoma: A Certainty-Rated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 3,733,499 Women.
articles.authors: Stylianakis D, Solinas C, Petrelli F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer safety after fertility treatment is well studied for breast and gynaecological tumours, but melanoma risk remains poorly characterized. We synthesized internally controlled evidence on this association.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov (2000-2025) were searched for comparative observational studies of melanoma incidence. The primary outcome was incident melanoma; treatment-pathway/SIR analyses were secondary. Hazard ratios and case-cohort relative risks (rare-disease approximation) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis (REML, Hartung-Knapp) in R; SIRs were synthesized separately. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-E and certainty graded using GRADE.
RESULTS: Twelve observational studies (3,733,499 women; 219,357 exposed) were included. ROBINS-E rated no study overall low risk of bias (83% some concerns, 17% high risk), reflecting incomplete ultraviolet-exposure adjustment. Melanoma risk was modestly elevated (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.02-1.50; I2 = 0%; prediction interval 0.97-1.58); drug-only ovulation induction showed a stronger association (HR 1.39, 95% CI 1.01-1.92), while ART/IVF was near-null (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.81-1.48). Corresponding absolute increases were approximately 3-8, 5-13, and 1-3 per 10,000 women over 10 years (baseline 13.3-33.1/100,000/year). Certainty was very low for any fertility treatment and drug-only treatment, and low for ART/IVF. SIR-based analyses were non-significant and highly heterogeneous (SIR 1.25, 95% CI 0.66-2.38; I2 = 80%).
CONCLUSIONS: Observed associations are small and of very low to low certainty, reflecting incomplete ultraviolet-exposure and risk-factor adjustment; causality cannot be established. Current evidence does not justify changes in fertility-treatment practice. Future studies require cycle-level exposure data and rigorous ultraviolet-exposure control.

articles.title: Testosterone, Testosterone Replacement Therapy, and Cardiovascular Disease: A Contemporary Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.authors: Maligireddy AR, Barua ST, Barua RS
articles.abstract: Whether low endogenous testosterone is causal for cardiovascular disease, and how the cardiovascular risk of testosterone replacement therapy should now be classified, remain contested, while US labeling has moved in 2 opposing directions within 16 months. We conducted a targeted narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles, searching MEDLINE and primary regulatory documents from January 2000 through July 2026. Evidence was graded with a prespecified 3-tier structured author-consensus rating separating established randomized findings, unresolved secondary signals, and evidentiary absence. Low endogenous testosterone is consistently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality but most plausibly marks multimorbidity rather than causation. TRAVERSE established that physiologic transdermal testosterone replacement therapy was noninferior to placebo for 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events over ∼3 years, within a permissive margin and against a 61% discontinuation rate. Observational analyses linking normalization to lower mortality were not reproduced under randomization. Atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, fracture, and noncalcified plaque progression remain unresolved. Blood pressure rises across the class; on ambulatory monitoring the magnitude differs by individual product rather than by route. Long-term exposure and nontransdermal formulations remain untested, and the age-related-hypogonadism limitation of use is now proposed for removal. Noninferiority over 3 years should not be read as long-term clinical equivalence. Safe use of testosterone replacement therapy requires appropriate patient selection, distinction between pathologic hypogonadism and functional or age-associated low testosterone, mapping of each recommendation to its evidentiary tier, and close multidisciplinary collaboration.

articles.title: Assessment of Persistent Postpartum Hypertension Following Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.authors: Daneshmand M, Dasari H, Hales L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying individuals with persistent postpartum hypertension (ppHTN) after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy is an important strategy to mitigate associated long-term cardiovascular risks. Accordingly, we aimed to review the literature surrounding the assessment of ppHTN after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
METHODS: We conducted a scoping review using Arksey and O'Malley's methodological framework. We developed and pilot-tested a data extraction tool to collect information on ppHTN assessment methods, including timing and setting, blood pressure (BP) thresholds used, and inclusion of patient preferences. Data were synthesized into tables and narrative summaries. Barriers and facilitators to BP assessment protocols, remote BP monitoring, and follow-up attendance were mapped using the Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation - Behavior (COM-B) framework.
RESULTS: Of 14 593 records, 96 papers met inclusion criteria. BP measured in the hospital alone was most common (n=41), followed by the hospital/home combination (n=18), and the outpatient/home combination (n=9). Monitoring typically began within 0 to 7 days postpartum (n=28), ending at 1 to 6 weeks (n=20) or 6 to 12 months (n=20) postpartum. ppHTN was defined using elevated BP thresholds (n=28), most commonly ≥140/90 mm Hg (n=18), medication initiation (n=8), lack of BP normalization over time (n=4), or referral to a specialist (n=2). Only 7 studies assessed patient preferences. Facilitators to home BP assessment included the use of educational material, while barriers involved digital access limitations.
CONCLUSIONS: ppHTN assessment methods varied in timing, setting, and BP thresholds. Findings underscore the need for standardized, patient-centered guidelines that account for BP assessment methods across settings.

articles.title: Sleep and the Gut-Brain Axis: Bidirectional, Converging Mechanisms Linking Brain Health, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration.
articles.journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology
articles.authors: Bowler B, Nasir AR, Szewczyk A et al.
articles.abstract: Sleep and the gastrointestinal (GI) tract interact in a complex and reciprocal relationship, although the molecular and physiological pathways underlying this interaction remain only partially defined. Communication between the central (CNS) and enteric nervous systems (ENS) spans neural, immune, endocrine, and metabolic pathways, including vagal nerve signaling, the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, gut-resident microbiota, and circulating microbial metabolites, such as bile acids with neuroinflammatory or neurotransmitter activity. In this narrative review, we synthesize evidence from animal models, observational cohorts, and intervention trials to map this bidirectional axis, focusing on several underexamined modulatory mechanisms including the interaction between the gut microbiome and the glymphatic system, the brain's perivascular waste-clearance network, which is implicated in the removal of amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau in Alzheimer's disease; neuroendocrine regulation and sex-related differences in gut microbiome composition and sleep patterns, which may help explain the divergent neurodegenerative disease risks between men and women; and age-related parallel trajectories of microbiome senescence and sleep fragmentation in older adults. We discuss melatonin, cortisol, estrogen, and ghrelin as endocrine mediators linking circadian biology to gut physiology, and we consider how environmental and lifestyle factors further perturb this system. These mechanisms form an integrative framework of the gut-brain-sleep axis and highlight priority directions for mechanistic and translational research, including significant nodes in this pathway where targeted interventions may help cognitive resilience and slow the neurodegenerative disease progression. More research clarifying these mechanisms may help identify the most promising targets, potentially leading to personalized, precision-medicine-based therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Intravenous Leiomyomatosis-A Single Centre Experience and Literature Review.
articles.authors: Smiljkovic OD, Markovic VM, Lalic K et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Intravenous leiomyomatosis (IVL) is a rare, histologically benign proliferation of uterine smooth-muscle cells that extend intravascularly. The clinical significance of IVL lies in the potential for mechanical obstruction of the major veins and heart, as well as possible thromboembolic complications. Methods: A retrospective case series included four patients with confirmed IVL, treated at the Clinic for Gynaecology and Obstetrics "Narodni front" between 1 January 2020 and 31 December 2025. The following were recorded: medical history, imaging diagnostics (ultrasound, MRI), operative findings, histopathology, and follow-up data. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee, and written informed consent for participation in the study was obtained from all the patients. Results: The series included four patients aged 40 to 73 with histologically confirmed IVL who were treated surgically. In one patient, an intraoperative complication occurred in the form of sigmoid colon lesion and consequential resection, requiring surgical reconstruction, while the remaining procedures were completed without major complications. Histopathological findings in all cases indicated benign smooth-muscle differentiation with the presence of intravascular nodules of smooth-muscle cells (IVL). Residual disease and recurrence were documented in one patient. Conclusions: Our cases reflect a diverse spectrum of clinical presentations of IVL indicating the heterogeneity of the disease and the importance of a multimodal, multidisciplinary approach to the optimal management of this rare entity. The absence of further disease progression in our patients following bilateral oophorectomy, i.e., iatrogenic menopause, suggests the possible hormonal dependence of IVL.

articles.title: Risk factors for endometrial cancer incidence and regional and ethnic disparities in the USA.
articles.authors: Adekanmbi V, Guo F, Wang J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial cancer (EC) is the most common gynaecologic cancer in the USA and a major cause of cancer-associated mortality among women. We aimed to identify the independent contributions of individual- and contextual-level factors to EC incidence.
