METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal retrospective cohort study using anonymised data from women aged 18 years and above without EC included in the All of Us Research database before 1 January 2017. We followed participants from study entry until October 2023 (median follow-up = 6.6 years). We used mixed-effects Cox regression models to examine data from individuals nested within ZIP-code areas and states, analysing individual-level risk factors and neighbourhood-level socioeconomic predictors in addition to adjusting for area-level clustering.
RESULTS: Of 81,171 eligible women followed for 496,709 person-years, 778 (0.96%) developed EC. The risk of EC risk approximately thrice as high among women aged 50-59 years (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) = 2.92; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 2.20-3.88), 60-69 years (aHR = 2.97; 95% CI = 2.21-4.00), and ≥70 years (aHR = 2.86; 95% CI = 2.02-4.06) than among women under 40 years of age. Non-Hispanic White women had a 44% higher risk than non-Hispanic Black women (aHR = 1.44; 95% CI = 1.15-1.80). Obesity was associated with more than twice the risk of EC (aHR = 2.16; 95% CI = 1.85-2.52), while diabetes was associated with a 27% higher risk (aHR = 1.27; 95% CI = 1.06-1.51).
CONCLUSION: Individual-level factors, particularly age and obesity, were the main predictors of EC incidence. Prevention efforts should prioritise obesity reduction, age-specific screening awareness, and lifestyle modifications.

articles.title: Reappraising the safety of menopausal hormone therapy for women-implications for the clinic.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Hirschberg AL
articles.abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is currently the most effective treatment for vasomotor and other estrogen deficiency-related symptoms. Despite its proven efficacy, concerns regarding long-term safety, particularly breast cancer, venous thromboembolism, and cardiovascular disease, have influenced clinical practice and patterns of MHT use over the past decades. This review summarizes the evolution of evidence regarding the safety of systemic MHT, from the introduction of conjugated equine estrogens in the 1940s through landmark randomized clinical trials to contemporary evidence and international guideline recommendations. Early concerns regarding endometrial safety with estrogen-only treatment were largely resolved by the addition of progestogens for women with an intact uterus. The Women's Health Initiative trial fundamentally changed perceptions of MHT cardiovascular safety, but subsequent analyses established the "timing hypothesis," demonstrating that the benefit-risk profile depends on age and time since menopause at treatment initiation. More recent evidence has highlighted clinically relevant differences between estrogen formulations, routes of administration, and type of progestogen. Transdermal estradiol is associated with a lower risk of venous thromboembolism than oral estrogen, while micronized progesterone and dydrogesterone may offer a more favorable breast safety profile than some synthetic progestins, although randomized evidence is lacking. Current evidence supports an individualized approach to MHT, with treatment decisions based on symptom burden, age, time since menopause, route of estrogen administration, type of progestogen, and individual risk factors. For healthy women initiating therapy before age 60 years or within 10 years of menopause, the overall benefit-risk profile is favorable. Future research should focus on optimizing formulation-specific safety, generating comparative randomized evidence, and further refining personalized treatment strategies to maximize benefits while minimizing risks.

articles.title: Inter-arm blood pressure differences and blood pressure variability in early pregnancy: limited associations with pre-eclampsia.
articles.authors: Skov HL, Riishede I, Rode L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate an association of inter-arm blood pressure differences (IAD) and within-visit variability of blood pressure in early pregnancy with pre-eclampsia.
METHODS: Blood pressure information was available on 8117 participants from the prospective PREeclampsia Screening In DEnmark (PRESIDE) study. Three consecutive blood pressure (BP) measurements were taken on both arms simultaneously in participants attending the first-trimester ultrasound. Maternal characteristics, medical history, and pregnancy outcome were collected. Outcomes were pre-eclampsia overall, further stratified into preterm (delivery < 37 weeks of gestation) and term cases (delivery ≥ 37 weeks of gestation).
RESULTS: Women developing pre-eclampsia had a higher diastolic IAD (2.67 mmHg vs 2.33 mmHg) and pulse pressure IAD (4.67 mmHg vs 4.33 mmHg OR 1.04 (95% CI: 1.01; 1.07)). Pulse pressure IAD was associated with pre-eclampsia (adjusted OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01, 1.07) and term pre-eclampsia (OR 1.05, 95 % CI 1.02, 1.08), but not with preterm pre-eclampsia (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.9, 1.06). There were no associations between systolic IAD, within-visit BP variability and pre-eclampsia.
CONCLUSION: Diastolic IAD and pulse pressure IAD in early pregnancy were higher in women developing pre-eclampsia. No association was found between systolic IAD or within-visit BP variability and pre-eclampsia.

articles.title: Interconnections between the immune system and infertility in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a scoping review.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Dos Santos LSDS, Rocha GR, Santos GLC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To map the existing evidence on the influence of the immune system on infertility in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
METHODS: This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were were conducted in January 2025 in PubMed, Embase, Virtual Health Library, LILACS, Web of Science, and Scopus for studies published between 2010 and 2024 in English, Portuguese, and Spanish. Study selection and data extraction were conducted independently by two reviewers. Data were analyzed descriptively and synthesized narratively, supported by charts and figures. This review considered primary studies published between 2010 and 2024 in English, Portuguese, or Spanish involving women of reproductive age with polycystic ovary syndrome, addressing the interplay between immune dysfunction and infertility. Gray literature, duplicate records, animal or in vitro studies, reviews, meta-analyses, and articles not aligned with the review objective were excluded.
RESULTS: A total of 19 studies were included, most of them observational and conducted predominantly in China and Middle Eastern countries. The main markers investigated were inflammatory cytokines, immune cells, and proteins related to oxidative stress. Increased levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines were observed, along with reduced levels of regulatory cytokines, consistently associated with anovulation and reproductive dysfunction. The evidence also demonstrated interactions between chronic low-grade inflammation, hormonal imbalance, and metabolic disturbances, which collectively contribute to impaired ovulatory function and reduced fertility.
CONCLUSION: Infertility in PCOS is driven by a complex interplay between immune imbalance and endocrine-metabolic dysfunction, with chronic inflammation playing a central role in ovulatory and endometrial impairment. Despite these advances, the predominance of observational evidence and regional concentration of studies restrict broader applicability. These results underscore the need for well-designed research integrating immunological and reproductive pathways to inform more precise therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Association between triglyceride-glucose index (TyG) as a surrogate marker of insulin resistance and risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM): updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Vásquez-Tirado GA, Moncada-Gutiérrez DA, Farfán-Castillo A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether the first-trimester triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index predicts subsequent gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).
METHODS: MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 12, 2025. Eligible studies were prospective or retrospective cohorts including adult women with singleton pregnancies, first-trimester TyG assessment, and later GDM ascertainment; non-original studies, case reports/series, and duplicates were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects models with REML and Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Sensitivity, subgroup, diagnostic accuracy, publication-bias, and GRADE certainty analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Fourteen observational cohorts comprising 462,233 pregnant women were included; 30,875 (7%) developed GDM. Twelve studies contributed adjusted association estimates. Elevated first-trimester TyG was associated with higher odds of GDM (OR 2.35, 95% CI 1.88-2.94; I2=92%). The association persisted after excluding influential studies (OR 2.36, 95% CI 1.91-2.90; I2=30.6%) and was consistent in Asian populations and low-risk-of-bias studies. Diagnostic performance was moderate, with pooled sensitivity of 0.62 (95% CI 0.54-0.69), specificity of 0.64 (95% CI 0.60-0.69), and AUC of 0.67. Limitations included substantial heterogeneity, variable TyG thresholds, observational designs, and limited non-Asian evidence.
CONCLUSIONS: First-trimester TyG is associated with increased GDM risk and may support early risk stratification, but its moderate diagnostic performance precludes use as a standalone screening test.PROSPERO registry: # CRD420251125511.

articles.title: Telehealth usefulness during postpartum hemorrhage management: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Nieto-Calvache AJ, Maya J, D'Antonio F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This literature systematic review aims to evaluate tele-medicine's effect in managing postpartum hemorrhage.
DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase (Ovid), and the Cochrane Library were consulted from inception to March 27, 2024.
STUDY SELECTION: Studies evaluating tele-medicine interventions (including tele-education, tele-consultation, virtual interventions for improving hospital processes) in the management of postpartum hemorrhage were included, without restrictions on study design.
DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Data extraction and quality assessment were performed. Due to substantial heterogeneity across studies, a meta-analysis was not conducted, and results were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies.
RESULTS: Nineteen studies were included. Most were conducted in low and middle-income countries (n=17/19) and used observational or quasi-experimental design (n=15/19). Four cluster randomized controlled trials evaluated the effectiveness of virtual training strategies, although only in one of them clinical variables were incorporated. Most studies reported improvements in process-related or clinical outcomes following telemedicine interventions. Reported barriers included limited funding, challenges in implementing recommendations at local hospitals, and lack of incentives for sustained use.
LIMITATIONS: The included studies were heterogeneous in design, interventions, and outcomes, and most had observational designs, limiting the strength of the evidence.
CONCLUSION: Developing and maintaining resilient health systems to address postpartum hemorrhage in low-resource settings requires innovative approaches that adapt technology to the context to enhance health outcomes. One such innovation could be tele-medicine, but further research is needed on barriers to implementation and translating the potential benefits of education and timely interaction between patients and expert groups into improved clinical outcomes.PROSPERO: #CRD42023448275.

articles.title: Preeclampsia Risk in Obese Pregnant Women without Diabetes Mellitus: a Meta-Analysis Comparing Metformin versus Control Group.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Lopes BC, de Oliveira NML, Araújo VDC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of metformin on reducing the risk of pre-eclampsia in obese pregnant women without diabetes.
SOURCES OF DATA: Following PRISMA guidelines, Scopus, Embase, PubMed (MEDLINE), Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, LILACS, SciElo, and Web of Science were searched for articles published between 2014 and April 2024. Search terms: ("Metformin" OR "Biguanide" OR "Glucophage" OR "dimethylbiguanide") AND ("pre-eclampsia" OR "preeclampsia") AND ("obese pregnant women" OR "obesity in pregnancy" OR "maternal obesity" OR "pregnancy" OR "obesity").
STUDY SELECTION: From 2022 studies identified, three randomized controlled trials comparing metformin with placebo or standard care in obese pregnant women without diabetes were included. Primary outcomes were pre-eclampsia incidence; secondary outcomes included gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, cesarean delivery, postpartum hemorrhage, and NICU admission.
DATA COLLECTION: Data were extracted, and odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Metformin did not significantly reduce PE risk (OR: 0.42; 95% CI: 0.10-1.68; p=0.22; I2=81%). Secondary outcomes showed no significant differences. Subgroup analysis excluding a methodological outlier suggested potential benefit (OR: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.10-0.38; p<0.00001; I2=0%). Metformin alone may not effectively prevent PE in these women, but efficacy could improve with lifestyle modifications. Study heterogeneity highlights the need for larger, rigorous trials.
CONCLUSIONS: Metformin should not be routinely recommended for pre-eclampsia prevention in obese pregnant women without diabetes until robust evidence from further research supports its efficacy.Prospero registry: CRD42024611538.

articles.title: Fibromyalgia in pregnancy and postpartum period: effects on quality of life, obstetric outcomes, delivery decisions, and breastfeeding: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Pereira BMDS, Alencar VB, Azi LMTA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the impact of fibromyalgia (FM) during pregnancy and the postpartum period on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), obstetric outcomes, and breastfeeding practices.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, and SciELO were searched for studies published between January 2010 and May 2024. The review followed Cochrane Collaboration standards and PRISMA 2020 recommendations.
STUDY SELECTION: Randomized and observational studies assessing FM during pregnancy or postpartum were eligible. Titles, abstracts, and full texts were independently screened by two reviewers according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria.
DATA COLLECTION: Data were extracted on maternal HRQoL, psychological well-being, obstetric complications, and breastfeeding outcomes. Methodological quality was appraised using ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies.
DATA SYNTHESIS: From 152 records identified, five studies met inclusion criteria, encompassing 8,182 women with FM. FM was associated with greater pain intensity, reduced functional capacity, lower HRQoL, and higher rates of depressive and anxiety symptoms. A population-based cohort showed modestly increased risks of gestational diabetes, preterm birth, and cesarean delivery, while reproductive capacity and breastfeeding duration appeared unaffected. Most studies presented moderate risk of bias due to confounding and reliance on self-reported data.
CONCLUSION: FM during pregnancy appears to be associated with reduced maternal HRQoL and impaired psychological well-being and may be associated with a modest increase in obstetric risk.PROSPERO registry: #CRD42024572007.

articles.title: Effect of the 'Ready-to-Use Vitrification and Warming Kit' on Pregnancy Rates Following Vitrification-warmed Blastocyst Transfer: A Retrospective Study.
articles.authors: Mizobe Y, Orita Y, Takeuchi K
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A newly developed ready-to-use (RtU) vitrification-warming kit enables vitrification in 12-13 min and thawing in 6 min, thereby simplifying culture operations by reducing overall handling time, but its effects on operability and clinical pregnancy rates following frozen-thawed embryo transfer need to be assessed.
AIM: This study aimed to compare clinical pregnancy rates between RtU kit and conventional CryoTip method used for vitrification in women undergoing single blastocyst frozen embryo transfer.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: A retrospective cohort study performed in a random sample of patients who underwent frozen embryo transfer between October 2023 and December 2024.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Blastocyst vitrification was performed using the CryoTip and RtU kit. Only single blastocyst transfers during a cycle of hormone replacement therapy were performed.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Kruskal-Wallis and Chi-squared tests were used with continuity correction.
RESULTS: The RtU kit demonstrated a higher warming rate than the CryoTip system while maintaining comparable cooling characteristics. No significant differences were observed between groups in pregnancy positivity (68.2 vs. 71.6%), clinical pregnancy (56.2 vs. 65.5%) and miscarriage rates (11.5 vs. 13.9%). Higher live birth rates were observed in the RtU group (54.1% vs. 42.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: The RtU vitrification-warming kit shortened the warming procedure and showed higher live birth rates compared with the CryoTip method. However, the favourable association with live birth did not remain statistically significant after adjustment for confounding factors. Further prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: Performance of HPV testing and liquid-based cytology after negative colposcopy in women with ASC-H, HSIL or AGC cytology.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Campos CS, Bovo AC, Fonseca B et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the performance of HPV testing and liquid-based cytology (LBC) in detecting HSIL+ (CIN2, CIN3, AIS, or cancer) after negative colposcopy in women screened with ASC-H, HSIL or AGC cytology.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter clinical trial (NCT05120167) involving 600 women referred for colposcopy due to ASC-H or worse cytology between October-2021 and October-2022. After excluding positive colposcopy cases, 257 women with negative colposcopy underwent HPV DNA testing and LBC. Histopathological diagnosis after excision of the transformation zone or 18-month negative follow-up served as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values (PV), and accuracy were calculated for each test individually and combination.
RESULTS: A total of 227 women completed the study. HSIL+ was diagnosed in 15.4% (35/227), including two superficially invasive carcinomas. HPV testing alone demonstrated the highest sensitivity (94.3%) and negative PV (98.6%), but lower specificity (73.4%) and positive PV (39.3%). When restricted to HPV16 and/or 18, specificity increased to 94.8% and PPV to 57%. LBC showed balanced performance, with sensitivity of 80%, specificity of 84.9%, and PPV of 49.1%. Combining HPV and LBC using an "OR" rule yielded the highest sensitivity (97.1%) and NPV (99.2%), whereas the "AND" rule provided the highest specificity (91.7%), PPV (62.8%), and overall accuracy (89.4%).
CONCLUSION: A substantial proportion of HSIL+ lesions persist despite negative colposcopy. HPV testing effectively rules out disease, and combining with LBC enhances diagnostic safety and accuracy. This dual-test approach offers a practical strategy to guide management and reduce diagnostic failures in women with ASC-H or worse cytology.

articles.title: Pulse wave velocity as a non-invasive discriminative marker of bone health in postmenopausal women.
articles.authors: Avramovska M, Nikleski Z, Avramovski P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Increased arterial stiffness has been linked to osteoporosis. This study evaluates Pulse Wave Velocity (PWV) as a discriminator of osteopenia and osteoporosis at the lumbar spine and femoral neck in postmenopausal women.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, arterial stiffness and bone mineral density (BMD) at the spine and femoral neck were assessed using carotid-to-femoral Pulse PWV and dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Eighteen premenopausal women (mean age 41.30±4.30 years) and forty-eight postmenopausal women (mean age 59.40±9.10 years) participated in the study. Osteoporosis (T-score ≤-2.5) and osteopenia (-2.5< T-score ≤-1) were defined by T-score criteria.
RESULTS: Pearson's correlation results showed: PWV and femoral neck BMD (r = -0.439, P = 0.002), PWV and spine BMD (r =-0.358, P = 0.012), and PWV and menopausal duration (r = 0.381, P = 0.008). PWV demonstrated significant discriminative ability for femoral neck osteopenia [b = 0.6472, Wald = 5.717, Odds ratio (OR) = 1.910, P = 0.017, Area Under Curve (AUC) = 0.704], femoral neck osteoporosis (b = 0.7206, Wald = 5.838, OR = 2.056, P = 0.016, AUC = 0.758), spine osteopenia (b = 0.8489, Wald = 5.639, OR = 2.337, P = 0.018, AUC = 0.677), and spine osteoporosis (b = 1.0829, Wald = 8.269, OR = 2.953, P = 0.004, AUC = 0.804).
CONCLUSION: PWV was inversely correlated with femoral neck and spine BMD, and positively correlated with menopausal duration. It serves as a significant discriminator of bone health, indicating increased odds of osteopenia and osteoporosis.

articles.title: Pharmacological preeclampsia prophylaxis: Are high-risk patients being left behind? A cross-sectional study at a Brazilian hospital.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Marques HFF, Lourenço I, Leal CRV et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate low-dose aspirin and calcium prescription rates among high-risk preeclampsia (PE) patients at a Brazilian tertiary hospital and identify predictors of prophylaxis failure.
METHODS: Cross-sectional study conducted at a Brazilian maternity hospital, in 2025, under guidelines recommending calcium for PE prevention. We included 100 high-risk pregnant/postpartum women who initiated prenatal care before the 12th gestational week. Prescription was adequate if initiated before the 16th week. Separate multivariable logistic regressions identified independent predictors of adequacy (p<0.05).
RESULTS: Among 100 women, 87% had at least one major risk factor; 13% had only multiple moderate factors. Adequate prescription before the 16th week was 54% for aspirin and 77% for calcium. Patients with only moderate factors had the lowest rates (23.1%). In multivariable analyses, chronic hypertension was independently associated with adequate prescription for aspirin (AOR 3.07; 95% CI 1.21-7.80; p=0.018) and calcium (AOR 4.11; 95% CI 1.26-13.46; p=0.019). Initial care at our center predicted adequate aspirin prescription (AOR 5.21; 95% CI 1.95-13.91; p<0.001) and showed a trend for calcium (AOR 3.24; 95% CI 0.98-10.79; p=0.054). Intervention omissions overlapped: 95.7% of patients without calcium also lacked aspirin.
CONCLUSION: Pharmacological PE prophylaxis is driven by high-visibility clinical comorbidities and the structural setting of initial care. While prominent maternal risks trigger provider adherence, moderate risk factors face structural bottlenecks at lower-level facilities, rendering optimal aspirin initiation dependent on tertiary insertion. Although recent guidelines withdrew routine calcium recommendations, this study highlights that real-world adherence within the referral network was sub-optimal due to early prenatal screening bottlenecks.

articles.title: Effectiveness and safety of adjunct interventions for external cephalic version in breech presentation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Bortoli AC, Fortunato VCR
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of adjunct and implementation-related strategies associated with external cephalic version (ECV) in pregnant women with breech presentation.
METHODS: Randomized controlled trials comparing adjunct or protocol-based strategies related to ECV (including pharmacological tocolysis, neuraxial anesthesia or analgesia, systemic analgesia, or timing/procedural approaches) with standard care, placebo, or expectant management were included.
SEARCH STRATEGY: MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and LILACS were searched from inception to February 2026.
DATA SELECTION AND EXTRACTION: Data extraction and risk of bias assessment using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Dichotomous outcomes were pooled using risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) under random-effects models.
RESULTS: Ten randomized controlled trials comprising 2,745 randomized women were included; 2,722 contributed complete outcome data to the primary meta-analysis. Adjunct and implementation-related strategies were associated with higher ECV success rates (RR 1.53; 95% CI 1.15-2.04; I² = 87%). Pharmacological tocolysis demonstrated the largest effect (RR 2.39; 95% CI 1.39-4.11), followed by neuraxial anesthesia (RR 1.75; 95% CI 1.07-2.85) and systemic analgesia (RR 1.39; 95% CI 1.15-1.69). Protocol-based strategies did not significantly improve success rates. No statistically significant reduction in cesarean delivery was observed (RR 0.88; 95% CI 0.76-1.02). Serious maternal and neonatal complications were uncommon.
CONCLUSIONS: Adjunct and implementation-related strategies, particularly pharmacological tocolysis and neuraxial anesthesia, increase the likelihood of successful ECV. Although the effect on cesarean delivery remains inconclusive, ECV appears safe when performed in appropriate clinical settings.

articles.title: Comparison of 25 µg Vaginal Misoprostol Versus Dinoprostone Gel for Induction of Labor in Term Prelabor Rupture of Membranes: A Retrospective Record-Based Observational Study.
articles.authors: Jinger S, Songara P, Dabi K
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM) at term occurs in 8-10% of pregnancies, and a long latency period is associated with infection in both the mother and the newborn. In women with an unfavorable cervix, cervical ripening and induction of labor are widely used with prostaglandin analogs. However, the preferred agent in women with term PROM remains unclear. This study compared the efficacy and safety of 25 µg vaginal misoprostol (prostaglandin E1) and dinoprostone (prostaglandin E2) gel in women with term PROM.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a record-based, comparative, observational study with a retrospective design conducted at a tertiary care teaching hospital in West India over 12 months. Records of 200 women with term PROM (≥37 weeks), singleton cephalic pregnancy, and an unfavorable cervix (Bishop's score ≤6) were reviewed. The primary outcome was the induction-to-delivery interval and the proportion of vaginal deliveries within 24 hours. Secondary outcomes included change in Bishop score at six hours, oxytocin dose, interval from induction to active labor, need for oxytocin augmentation, mode of delivery, and maternal and neonatal safety outcomes. An independent-samples t-test was employed for continuous variables, and chi-square or Fisher's exact test was used for categorical variables; p < 0.05 was considered significant.
RESULTS: The two groups did not differ in maternal age, parity, PROM duration, or baseline Bishop score. The mean Bishop score at six hours was significantly higher in the misoprostol group (5.68 ± 1.31 vs 4.78 ± 1.26; p < 0.001). The mean induction-to-active-labor interval (6.80 ± 1.58 vs 8.19 ± 2.06 hours; p < 0.001) and the induction-to-delivery interval (11.81 ± 3.06 vs 13.78 ± 3.99 hours; p < 0.001) were significantly shorter with misoprostol, which also required fewer doses (1.62 ± 0.63 vs 1.91 ± 0.67; p = 0.002) and less oxytocin augmentation (16 (16.0%) vs 46 (46.0%); p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in the proportion of vaginal deliveries within 24 hours (92 (92.0%) vs 94 (94.0%); p = 0.780) or cesarean deliveries (8 (8.0%) vs 6 (6.0%); p = 0.780). The groups did not differ in uterine hyperstimulation (5% vs 2%), abnormal fetal heart rate (8% vs 6%), postpartum hemorrhage (4% vs 5%), mean birth weight, or NICU admission (4% vs 0%).
CONCLUSIONS: 25 µg vaginal misoprostol was associated with more effective cervical ripening and shorter time to delivery than dinoprostone gel,…

articles.title: School, community, family, clinic, and technology-based approaches to adolescent pregnancy prevention: a comprehensive systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
articles.authors: Mahmud PE, Wakano M, Makatita S et al.
articles.abstract: Adolescent pregnancy remains a global public health issue associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, educational disruption, and long-term socioeconomic consequences. This systematic review synthesised evidence on school, community, family, clinic, and technology-based interventions for adolescent pregnancy. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in Embase, ProQuest, Scopus, and PubMed to identify relevant articles published between 2018 and 2023 The screened articles were full-text, and the selected articles were open access. The search strategy combined MeSH terms and keywords using the Boolean operators Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, 1352 records were identified, and 25 studies (randomised controlled trials [RCTs], mixed-methods, quasi-experimental) were included. Study quality and risk of bias were assessed using structured appraisal tools: the Joanna Briggs Institute Guidelines Tools for RCTs and quasi-experimental studies, and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tools for mixed-methods studies. The findings were analysed through a design-stratified narrative synthesis to account for methodological heterogeneity. A meta-analysis was not conducted because the included studies were methodologically and clinically heterogeneous, thereby limiting the validity of pooling effect sizes. School- and technology-based interventions improved sexual health knowledge and attitudes but showed limited behavioural change. Community programs demonstrated moderate improvements in contraceptive use and delayed sexual initiation at 6-12 months. Clinic-based models increased communication and service utilisation but rarely measured pregnancy incidence. Only intensive family-based interventions with structured reinforcement reduced pregnancy rates at ≥12 months. Knowledge improvement does not guarantee a reduction in pregnancy. Sustained impact depends on intervention intensity, reinforcement, and long-term follow-up, supporting integrated multicomponent strategies with standardised pregnancy indicators.

articles.title: Maladaptive Cognitive Emotion Regulation: Risk Factor for Fertility Quality of Life among Infertile Women: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.authors: Anupriya, Siddiqui A, Lata S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infertility poses considerable emotional and social challenges and is associated with reduced quality of life among women. The experience of infertility can evoke a range of emotional responses, including stress, anxiety and feelings of loss, which leads to psychological distress, making cognitive-emotion regulation a crucial factor to assess and substantiate its interwoven nature.
AIM: This study aims to explore this intricate display of cognitive emotion regulation (CER) with fertility quality of life (FQoL) among women suffering from infertility.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: The present study employed a cross-sectional, correlational research design. Purposive sampling recruited 103 women aged 20-40 years from two different fertility clinics.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Participants were assessed with a sociodemographic sheet, the CER Questionnaire and the Hindi FertiQoL Scale.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: The relationships between the variables were explored using descriptive statistics, correlational analysis and hierarchical regression.
RESULTS: The findings indicate that FQoL is significantly negatively associated with self-blame and overall maladaptive CER (M-CER) and positively associated with refocus on planning. In hierarchical regression, refocus on planning was added as an adaptive strategy and showed a positive trend in predicting FQoL (β =0.194, P = 0.052), whereas self-blame (β = -0.351, P < 0.01) and M-CER (β = -0.075, P < 0.05) emerged as significant negative predictors.
CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the necessity for focused psychological interventions that assist infertile women in recognising and reducing M-CER strategies while promoting adaptive regulation.

articles.title: Soluble E-selectin and QRISK3-based Cardiovascular Risk Assessment in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Prospective Case-control Study from India.
articles.authors: Singh N, Dandapath I, Gupta A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with metabolic abnormalities and increased long-term cardiovascular risk. Endothelial dysfunction is considered an early event in atherogenesis, and soluble E-selectin has been proposed as a marker of endothelial activation. However, its role in cardiovascular risk assessment in PCOS remains uncertain.
AIM: The study aimed to compare circulating soluble E-selectin levels between women with PCOS and healthy controls and evaluate their association with metabolic parameters and QRISK3-based cardiovascular risk scores.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: Prospective hospital-based case-control study.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two hundred women with PCOS diagnosed according to the Rotterdam criteria and 50 age-matched healthy controls aged 18-40 years were enrolled. Clinical assessment, anthropometry, fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, C-reactive protein and soluble E-selectin levels were evaluated. Estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk was calculated using the QRISK3 algorithm.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Group comparisons, correlation analyses and multivariable linear regression were performed.
RESULTS: Mean soluble E-selectin levels were comparable between women with PCOS and controls (0.61 ± 0.33 vs. 0.61 ± 0.29 ng/mL, P = 0.935). Within the PCOS group, soluble E-selectin correlated positively with HbA1c (r = 0.326, P = 0.001) and fasting blood glucose (r = 0.271, P = 0.001), while no significant associations were observed with anthropometric measures, lipid parameters, blood pressure or QRISK3 scores. In multivariable analysis, fasting blood glucose remained independently associated with soluble E-selectin.
CONCLUSION: Soluble E-selectin levels did not differ between women with PCOS and controls and showed limited associations with cardiovascular risk factors. These findings do not support a major role for soluble E-selectin in cardiovascular risk assessment among young women with PCOS.

articles.title: Screening for maternal infection in pregnancy to prevent preterm birth: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Azzahra Z, Ibrahim F, Ocviyanti D
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze whether screening for maternal infections during pregnancy to prevent premature birth is associated with a reduction in premature birth.
DATA SOURCES: A systematic review was conducted. PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library and ProQuest databases were screened for original studies carried out on pregnant women and used Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) terms and free-text keywords related to pregnancy, infection screening, and preterm birth.
SELECTION OF STUDIES: Randomized and observational studies that evaluated antenatal screening for maternal genital or urinary infections, compared screened populations with usual care without additional targeted infection screening, and reported preterm birth (<37 weeks) or related obstetric outcomes were included.
DATA COLLECTION: Study selection and extraction were performed independently by two reviewers.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Out of 858 records obtained, 10 studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies screened for various genital and urinary infections. The effect estimates for the unselected antenatal populations were mostly not significant. Nevertheless, maternal infection screening in selected or high-risk populations and subgroup analyses among nulliparous women screened for bacterial vaginosis (BV) or Chlamydia trachomatis/Neisseria gonorrhoeae (CT/NG) was associated with reduction in preterm birth. Marked heterogeneity in populations, settings, target infections, and screening protocols limited direct comparison across studies.
CONCLUSION: Antenatal infection screening in unselected pregnant populations did not show a significant reduction in preterm birth. However, more favourable findings were observed in selected or high-risk populations, although overall effects are heterogeneous. Further well-designed studies in clearly defined target populations are needed to define optimal screening strategies for routine practice.PROSPERO registration number: CRD420251244205.

articles.title: Trends, collaboration, and impact of scientific research on the Mediterranean diet during pregnancy.
articles.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
articles.authors: Barja-Ore J, Liñan-Bermudez A, Guillen-Calle BE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Mediterranean diet (MED) is well recognized for its general health benefits and, specifically, during pregnancy, where it may reduce risks such as gestational diabetes, intrauterine growth restriction, preterm birth, and low birth weight. It is also associated with improved maternal metabolic, psychological, and immune outcomes. This study analyzes the scientific production on MED during pregnancy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: descriptive bibliometric study was conducted on original articles addressing MED in pregnant women, published in Scopus (2015-2024). Predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria were applied, selecting 211 documents. We used SciVal and Bibliometrix (RStudio) to estimate production, bibliometric impact, and collaboration network indicators; Bradford's law to identify core journals; and MS Excel for trend analysis.
RESULTS: Scientific output has shown sustained growth over the last decade, concentrated in Q1 journals such as Nutrients, American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, and Frontiers in Nutrition. Spain led in volume and impact, with consolidated networks involving institutions such as Harvard University. National co-authorship showed higher average impact than international collaborations. Latin America, Africa, and much of Asia were underrepresented, limiting the global applicability of findings.
CONCLUSION: Research on the Mediterranean diet during pregnancy has shown consolidation in both volume and impact, driven by scientific advances and the inclusion of this dietary pattern in clinical guidelines. However, geographic, and thematic gaps remain, requiring more inclusive, multicenter, and population-diverse research agendas to maximize global relevance and applicability.

articles.title: Investigating the relationship between dental caries, microbial plaque, and unknown infertility in men and women: A case-control study.
articles.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
articles.authors: Haghighi Morad A, Taheri S, Shirinzad M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tooth decay is one of the most common chronic diseases worldwide. Very few studies were conducted on the relationship between dental caries and infertility, and the results of those conducted on this topic are contradictory. The present study investigated the relationship among dental caries, microbial plaque, and unknown infertility in men and women in Hamadan City.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This case-control study was conducted on 332 fertile and infertile women and men in 2022. Interviews and tests were used as part of the data-collecting process, and a three-part questionnaire served as the data collection instrument. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS software version 20.
RESULTS: The mean decayed, missing, and filled teeth of the male case and control group was 11.36 and 9.6, respectively. This figure for the female case and control groups was 11.33 and 8.96, respectively (P < 0.001). In the male case and control groups, the average number of decaying teeth was 5.71 and 3.71; in the female case and control groups, they were 6.3 and 3.36, respectively (P < 0.001). The average plaque index in the male and control groups was 34.97 and 28.8, respectively, and in the female case and control groups was 28.84 and 24.81, respectively (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Based on the results, it is necessary to educate the general public, especially couples of childbearing age, to observe oral and dental hygiene and seek the detect dental caries on time by midwives and dentists in health centers.

articles.title: Are women cryopreserving enough oocytes for fertility preservation? A probabilistic model integrating AI-based oocyte morphology and age-dependent euploidy.
articles.authors: Braga DPAF, Setti AS, Del Collado M et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: How many mature oocytes are biologically required to achieve at least three euploid blastocysts, by maternal age and AI-derived oocyte quality, and how does this estimate compare with real-world oocyte yields in elective fertility preservation?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Required oocyte numbers rise steeply with advancing maternal age and decreasing AI-derived oocyte quality, and the median number cryopreserved per fertility preservation cycle falls progressively below estimated requirements, by 12- to 30-fold in women older than 40 years.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Elective oocyte cryopreservation is increasingly used to preserve future reproductive potential, but counselling typically relies on uniform age-based oocyte targets that do not account for inter-individual variability in oocyte biological competence. Although AI-based oocyte assessment has shown promise as an objective adjunct to morphological evaluation, no biologically integrated framework has been used to translate AI-derived oocyte quality into a quantitative requirement-versus-yield comparison in fertility preservation.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: Retrospective cohort study with probabilistic modelling of blastulation and euploidy, using three datasets from a single private university-affiliated IVF centre. Model development used 13 782 mature oocytes from 1625 autologous ICSI cycles (1020 patients, 2021-2024) and 3325 biopsied embryos with conclusive PGT-A results (857 patients). External validation was performed in 1948 oocytes from 333 ovum donation cycles in 271 donors (2020-2024). Real-world application used 1647 elective fertility preservation cycles in 1100 patients between 2012 and 2024.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Each oocyte was scored using a commercially available artificial-intelligence image-analysis system that assigns a 0-10 oocyte quality score. Blastulation and euploidy were modelled by logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors. The integrated probabilistic framework computed the minimum number of mature oocytes required to obtain at least three euploid blastocysts at a probability of 90% or greater, by maternal age category and tertile of AI-derived oocyte quality score. Model-derived requirements were compared with the median number of oocytes actually cryopreserved per fertility preservation cycle.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Blastulation increased with higher AI-derived oocyte quality score (OR 1.19 per point, 95% CI 1.18-1.21;…

articles.title: Three and Two Dimensional Saline Infusion Sonohysterography in Diagnosing Uterine Cavity Lesions.
articles.authors: Jafarabadi M, Alizadeh M, Rezayof E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Given the invasive and costly nature of reference diagnostic methods like hysteroscopy , this study aimed to compare the diagnostic accuracy and the dimensional measurement agreement of uterine cavity lesions between two-dimensional saline infusion sonography (2D SIS) and three-dimensional saline infusion sonography (3D SIS) against the gold standard of hysteroscopy and histopathology.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted on 283 female patients who were candidates for hysteroscopy. Prior to surgery, all patients underwent blinded evaluations via 2D SIS and 3D SIS performed by experienced radiologists, and the type, number, location, and size of the lesions were recorded. Subsequently, all patients underwent diagnostic hysteroscopy and tissue sampling for pathological evaluation as the gold standard. Diagnostic performance metrics were calculated, and the dimensional agreement of the lesions between the modalities was statistically evaluated using the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis.
RESULTS: The mean age of the patients was 35.9 ± 8.1 years. Histopathological examination confirmed endometrial polyps in 20.5% and leiomyomas in 17.3% of the patients. Compared to 2D SIS, 3D SIS demonstrated higher sensitivity (83.15% vs. 78.65%), higher specificity (93.30% vs. 91.75%), and higher overall diagnostic accuracy (90.11% vs. 87.63%). In the dimensional agreement analysis, 3D SIS showed an excellent correlation (ICC = 0.927) and a negligible mean systematic error (mean bias: -0.26 mm; 95% limits of agreement: -7.77 to 7.25 mm) compared to hysteroscopy. In contrast, 2D SIS systematically overestimated lesion dimensions compared to hysteroscopy (mean bias: 2.21 mm) and exhibited the widest limits of agreement when compared with 3D SIS (-8.76 to 13.70 mm).
CONCLUSION: 3D SIS is an accurate, non-invasive tool that lacks systematic bias in measuring uterine tumors, offering superior performance compared to the 2D SIS method. Given its high overall accuracy, 3D SIS can be utilized as a reliable first-line diagnostic tool, significantly reducing the necessity for unnecessary diagnostic hysteroscopies and the associated financial burdens on the healthcare system.

articles.title: Liquid Biopsy as a Screening Tool in Recurrent Implantation Failure During IVF: A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Saeedinia R, Hemmat A, Heidary Z
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) remains a multifaceted challenge in assisted reproductive technology (ART), affecting a subset of in vitro fertilization (IVF) patients despite transfer of high-quality embryos. Conventional diagnostics often require invasive procedures that may disturb endometrial receptivity. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence on liquid-biopsy strategies for RIF screening, emphasizing biofluids such as uterine fluid (UF), spent embryo culture medium (SCM), peripheral blood, cervicovaginal fluid (CVF), and seminal plasma.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Literature searches covered PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science through August 2025, with inclusion of pivotal pre-2022 studies. Eligible works included observational studies, clinical trials, multi-omics analyses, and systematic reviews reporting molecular biomarkers relevant to endometrial receptivity or embryo competence.
RESULTS: UF-derived microRNAs (miRNAs) and extracellular vesicle (EV) cargo during the window of implantation (WOI) consistently differentiate receptive from nonreceptive endometrium, with predictive accuracies (AUC 0.75-0.90) in small validation studies. SCM-based noninvasive PGT-A (niPGT-A) shows moderate concordance (~65%) with trophectoderm biopsy PGT-A, constrained by contamination and low cfDNA yield; recent advances include blastocoel fluid integration and methylation-based decontamination. Peripheral blood, CVF, and seminal plasma biomarkers remain exploratory due to lower specificity. Pre-analytical standardization and harmonized outcome definitions are critical for translation.
CONCLUSION: UF-miRNA/EV profiling holds the strongest promise for noninvasive RIF screening, whereas niPGT-A may serve as an adjunct for embryo competence assessment when biopsy is not feasible. Both approaches require multicenter validation and prospective trials demonstrating improved live-birth rates before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: Cerebrotendinous Xanthomatosis: Clinical Features of Affected Individuals From Latin America.
articles.authors: Martínez-Hernández HR, Villa-Villegas L, Piña-Avilés CE et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis (CTX) is an autosomal recessive disorder that may be underdiagnosed in Latin America (LatAm).
METHODS: We describe 6 Mexican individuals with CTX from 2 unrelated families and review published LatAm cases. MEDLINE was searched (1966-October 2025) for CTX cases reported in LatAm in English, Portuguese, or Spanish. Twenty studies including 28 patients from 23 families were identified, and international CTX cohorts were selected for comparison.
RESULTS: Individuals from one Mexican family carried compound heterozygous CYP27A1 variants (c.562C>T and c.1016C>T), whereas those from the other family harbored homozygous c.944_948del. Parkinsonism and dystonia were prominent among Mexican patients. Most LatAm cases were male, with childhood onset and a mean diagnostic age of 41.7 ± 16.17 years. Xanthomas, cataracts, diarrhea, and movement disorders were frequent. Elevated cholestanol levels were detected in 14 of 34 individuals. Genetic testing was performed in 24 of 34 individuals; all tested individuals had pathogenic CYP27A1 variants. Dentate nuclei abnormalities were the main brain MRI findings. Chenodeoxycholic acid was used in 13 of 34 cases.
DISCUSSION: Besides classic CTX features, brownish dental enamel, hyperlordosis, and urinary incontinence were identified among some LatAm patients. Symptom onset was earlier in LatAm than in other regions. Diarrhea and neurologic symptoms with early-onset cataracts or xanthomas should prompt genetic testing for CTX.

articles.title: Laparoscopic Endometriosis Phenotypes and Preoperative Non-suspicion of Endometriosis in Women With Superficial Disease: A Retrospective Study in Kinshasa.
articles.authors: Monzango Sibo GLM, Itewa Monka L
articles.abstract: Background Superficial peritoneal endometriosis (SPE) is difficult to identify before surgery, especially without concomitant ovarian or deep disease. We described laparoscopic phenotypes and examined factors associated with the absence of documented preoperative suspicion of any endometriosis among women subsequently found to have SPE. Methods We retrospectively analyzed gynecologic laparoscopies performed at three Kinshasa sites between January 2019 and June 2026 by one surgeon. Superficial, ovarian, and deep phenotypes were recorded as non-mutually exclusive. The analytical outcome was absence of documented preoperative suspicion of endometriosis of any phenotype among women with laparoscopically identified SPE and classifiable preoperative records. Modified Poisson models with robust variance estimated exploratory adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs). Results Of 1,743 gynecologic laparoscopies, 216 (12.4%; 95% CI, 10.9%-14.0%) showed endometriosis and 1,527 (87.6%) did not. SPE occurred in 139/216 (64.4%), ovarian disease in 137/216 (63.4%), and deep disease in 68/216 (31.5%); 104/216 (48.1%) had overlapping phenotypes. Among 135 women with SPE whose preoperative records were classifiable, 83 (61.5%; 95% CI, 53.1%-69.3%) lacked documented suspicion of endometriosis; this proportion was 46/56 (82.1%) in isolated SPE. In the clinical model, infertility was associated with higher non-suspicion (aPR 1.59; 95% CI, 1.07-2.35), while deep dyspareunia was associated with lower non-suspicion (aPR 0.65; 95% CI, 0.45-0.94). With additional adjustment for coexisting operative phenotypes, the infertility association weakened (aPR 1.39; 95% CI, 0.95-2.04) and the dyspareunia estimate remained borderline (aPR 0.70; 95% CI, 0.49-1.00). Conclusions SPE and ovarian disease were the most common laparoscopic phenotypes in this selected surgical cohort. An absence of documented suspicion of any endometriosis was frequent among women with SPE, especially isolated SPE. Associations with infertility and deep dyspareunia are exploratory and may reflect clinical documentation, surgical referral pathways, and coexisting disease. Prospective standardized assessments are needed.

articles.title: Development and Preliminary Validation of the SHUDE Scoring System for Chronic Endometritis in Women With Previous Reproductive Failure Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization Treatment.
articles.authors: Jain S, Shrivastava D, Vagha S
articles.abstract: Background Chronic endometritis (CE) has been increasingly recognized in women with infertility and previous reproductive failure, but its diagnosis remains challenging because clinical, hysteroscopic, and histopathological findings may vary between individuals. Hysteroscopy provides direct visualization of the endometrial cavity; however, individual hysteroscopic findings may have limited diagnostic value when considered in isolation. The present study aimed to develop and pilot-test the SHUDE scoring system, a standardized multidomain scoring framework for the structured assessment of CE in women with previous reproductive failure undergoing in vitro fertilization. Methods Following approval from the Institutional Ethics Committee, this methodological study was conducted at a tertiary care center. Thirty eligible women with infertility and a history of reproductive failure were included for the pilot assessment of the scoring system. The SHUDE scoring system comprised six domains: demographic characteristics, reproductive history, clinical history, clinical examination, hysteroscopic findings, and evidence of endometrial tuberculosis. Content validity was assessed using a four-point relevance scale by a multidisciplinary panel of six experts comprising reproductive medicine specialists, obstetricians and gynecologists, and clinicians experienced in diagnostic hysteroscopy. The item-level content validity index (I-CVI) and scale-level content validity index based on the average method (S-CVI/Ave) were calculated. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha. Results The six domains demonstrated acceptable content validity, with I-CVI values ranging from 0.83 to 1.00 and an overall S-CVI/Ave of 0.94. Pilot testing among 30 eligible women yielded a Cronbach's alpha of 0.84, indicating good internal consistency across the six domains. Conclusion The SHUDE scoring system demonstrated high content validity and good internal consistency in this preliminary evaluation. These findings provide initial support for the relevance and coherence of the scoring framework but do not establish its diagnostic accuracy or an optimal diagnostic threshold. Further evaluation in larger, independent populations is required to determine its diagnostic performance, reproducibility, and potential clinical applicability.

articles.title: Conservative surgery vs hysterectomy for placenta accreta spectrum disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Lino GM, Galvão PVM, Luna VLM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Resection and reconstruction of the uterus may be an alternative to hysterectomy in placenta accreta spectrum disorders. We aimed to review whether surgical and maternal outcomes were comparable between these techniques.
METHODS: Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library databases were searched until 1 January 2025. We included randomized controlled trials (RCT) and nonrandomized studies (NRSI) comparing conservative surgery, involving resection and reconstruction of the myometrium without placental removal, to hysterectomy in patients with placenta accreta, increta, or percreta. Two authors were responsible for independently screening the title and abstract, and the full texts of all identified records. We assessed the risk of bias with ROB-2 or ROBINS-I, and the quality of evidence with GRADE. The main analysis only included studies without a high risk of bias. A secondary non-inferiority Bayesian analysis was reported alongside the results.
RESULTS: We included one RCT and eleven nonrandomized studies (1586 women). Most women had FIGO PAS Grade 2 and 3a and with upper uterine segment involvement. Compared to hysterectomy, conservative surgery may result in a similar number of transfused packs of red blood cells (MD -0.70 packs, 95% CI -1.28 to -0.12; 1 RCT and 4 NRSI, 649 women; I2= 0%; low-certainty evidence), and a similar risk of bladder injury (RR 0.36, 95% CI 0.12 to 1.07; 1 RCT and 4 NRSI, 649 women; I2= 0%; low-certainty evidence). Excluding rare outcomes, the probability that conservative surgery is non-inferior to hysterectomy was greater than 90.0%.
CONCLUSION: On the basis of low evidence, conservative surgery may not increase the risk of clinically important harm compared to hysterectomy, with the benefit of uterus preservation. Further RCTs are needed to reach definitive conclusions.

articles.title: Atosiban versus nifedipine for the management of preterm labor: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Pascon A, Fumes AJ, Rüdinger NH et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy, maternal safety, and neonatal outcomes of atosiban versus nifedipine in the management of preterm labor, with particular attention to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission rates.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, EBSCOHost, ClinicalTrials.gov and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were systematically searched up to May 25, 2025. No language restrictions were applied.
STUDY SELECTION: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing atosiban and nifedipine in women with clinically diagnosed preterm labor were included, provided they reported at least one outcome related to pregnancy prolongation. Six RCTs comprising 1,070 patients met inclusion criteria.
DATA COLLECTION: Two reviewers independently extracted data on efficacy, maternal adverse effects, and neonatal outcomes using a standardized form. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Pooled analyses showed no significant difference between atosiban and nifedipine in delaying delivery for 48 hours (risk ratio [RR] 1.09; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.97-1.23) or 7 days (RR 1.04; 95% CI 0.89-1.22). Atosiban was associated with a significantly lower risk of maternal headache, hypotension, and tachycardia. Atosiban was associated with a non-statistically significant trend toward higher NICU admission (RR 1.36; 95% CI 0.97-1.94; p=0.079), an estimate derived from only two RCTs with substantial heterogeneity (I2=69.8%) and warranting cautious interpretation. No significant differences were observed for neonatal death, sepsis, or hemorrhagic disease.
CONCLUSION: Atosiban and nifedipine offer comparable tocolytic efficacy. Atosiban carries a more favorable maternal safety profile but shows a non-significant trend toward higher NICU admission warranting confirmation in larger trials. Tocolytic selection should therefore be individualized, weighing maternal tolerability against this uncertain neonatal signal.Systematic Review Registration: PROSPERO CRD420251065426.

articles.title: Successful vaginal birth after two or more cesareans versus failed trial of labor: A systematic review and meta-analysis of maternal and fetal outcomes.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Spaleta BNM, Oliveira JA, Queiroz LF et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess maternal and neonatal outcomes associated with a failed versus successful (VBAC-2).
DATA SOURCES: A systematic search across Pubmed, Embase and Cochrane was conducted up to October 2025, supplemented by backward snowballing.
STUDY SELECTION: Studies with pregnant women with a two or more previous cesarean deliveries undergoing a trial of labor were included. No restrictions were applied.
DATA COLLECTION: Data on maternal and neonatal outcomes and risk and protective factors were extracted. The DerSimonian and Laird random effects model was applied, reporting Odds Ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was evaluated using I2 statistics and the Cochran Q test. Methodological quality was appraised using the Cochrane Risk-of-bias tool for non-randomized trials (ROBINS-I).
DATA SYNTHESIS: Out of 4065 studies screened, 12 studies (n= 3429) were included. We observed higher odds of postpartum hemorrhage (OR 1.98), maternal transfusion (OR 3.29), uterine rupture (OR 6.47), and neonatal intensive care unit admission (OR 6.44) in the VBAC-2 failure group. Epidural anesthesia (OR 0.56) and a history of previous vaginal birth (OR 0.27) were identified as protective factors, while a higher Body Mass Index was a risk factor for VBAC- 2 failure.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the critical need for comprehensive patient counseling, risk assessment, and heightened clinical vigilance to optimize care strategies in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Opportunistic salpingectomy for ovarian cancer prevention Number 12 - 2026.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: da Silva AL, Cândido EB, Carvalho JP et al.
articles.abstract: •Opportunistic salpingectomy (OS) is a biologically sound strategy for ovarian cancer prevention, as most high-grade serous carcinomas (HGSC) originate in the fimbrial epithelium of the fallopian tube. •Epidemiological data and meta-analyses consistently show a substantial risk reduction (approximately 40-80%) in tubo-ovarian carcinoma following salpingectomy. •The procedure is safe when performed during hysterectomy or benign gynecologic surgery, adding minimal operative time (10-16 minutes) without increasing perioperative complications. •Evidence shows that it is reliable to perform OS instead of tubal ligation or fimbrectomy for permanent contraception. •Current evidence confirms that OS does not impair short-term ovarian reserve or accelerate the onset of menopause. •Implementation requires structured counseling on the irreversible nature of the procedure and shared decision-making.

articles.title: The burden of medically indicated preterm birth due to preeclampsia and its association to the fullpiers score in a high-risk maternity setting.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Tondello GC, Ramos JSC, Dacaz ECS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Describe the prevalence of medically indicated preterm birth due to preeclampsia (PE), maternal and perinatal outcomes, and the use of the fullPIERS calculator for risk assessment.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at a high-risk maternity center through a review of women records with medically indicated preterm birth due to PE between January 2020 and December 2023. Sociodemographic data, maternal and perinatal outcomes were evaluated. The fullPIERS calculator was applied using a cutoff value ≥2.15%, proposed as a predictor of adverse outcomes.
RESULTS: During the study period, 24,507 births were recorded, which 2,523 were preterm (10.2%). Preterm birth attributed to PE occurred in 9.75% of cases (n=246), with 2.4% (n=6) progressing to eclampsia. The mean maternal age was 31.7 years and mean systolic/diastolic blood pressures were 157.3 mmHg and 100.9 mmHg, respectively. Thrombocytopenia was observed in 25.6% of women, and elevated transaminases occurred in 14%. The mean gestational age at delivery was 34.06 weeks, and 68.8% of deliveries were indicated due to worsening blood pressure control. The stillbirth rate was 2.45% (n=6). Women with fullPIERS scores ≥2.15% (n=53) presented greater disease severity, including higher rates of thrombocytopenia, elevated creatinine (15%), lower gestational age at delivery (mean 32.8±3.2 weeks), and increased prevalence of HELLP syndrome (9.3%) and perinatal mortality (2.45%).
CONCLUSION: Preeclampsia is an important cause of medically indicated preterm birth and is associated with adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes. The fullPIERS model may represent a useful adjunct tool for assessing disease severity and supporting clinical decision-making in this context.

articles.title: Use of dental prostheses and negative self-perception of oral health in climacteric women: prevalence and associated factors.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Santos VCS, Fonseca AA, Macedo MTS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the prevalence and factors associated with the use of dental prostheses and negative Self-Perception of Oral Health (SPOH) with sociodemographic, behavioral, and clinical factors in climacteric women.
METHODS: An epidemiological, cross-sectional, and analytical study was conducted with 757 climacteric women. The use of dental prostheses was assessed by self-report, and negative SPOH by the Oral Health Impact Profile (OHIP-14). Independent variables included sociodemographic, behavioral, and clinical factors. Associations were investigated using crude and adjusted Poisson regression.
RESULTS: Seven hundred fifty-seven climacteric women were evaluated, of which 43.9% reported negative SPOH and 48.7% used dental prostheses. The use of prostheses was associated with postmenopause (PR: 2.77; 95% CI: 2.12-3.68; p<0.001), marital status (PR: 1.16; 95% CI: 1.15-1.42; p=0.019), polypharmacy (PR: 1.24; 95% CI: 1.18-1.54; p=0.003), tobacco use (PR: 1.34; 95% CI: 1.09-1.65; p<0.001), hypertension (PR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.11-1.69; p<0.001), osteoarticular diseases (PR: 1.29; 95% CI: 1.03-1.61; p<0.001), osteoporosis (PR: 1.33; 95% CI: 1.05-1.68; p<0.001), and sarcopenia (PR: 1.21; 95% CI: 1.18-1.50; p=0.004). Negative SPOH was associated with polypharmacy (PR: 1.33; 95% CI: 1.00-1.74; p=0.008), tobacco use (PR: 1.28; 95% CI: 0.99-1.66; p=0.017), osteoarticular diseases (PR: 1.25; 95% CI: 1.16-1.63; p=0.042), depression (PR: 1.69; 95% CI: 1.13-2.52; p=0.001), anxiety (PR: 1.99; 95% CI: 1.30-3.04; p<0.001), and intense climacteric symptoms (PR: 3.73; 95% CI: 2.36-6.30; p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: A high prevalence of dental prosthesis use and negative SPOH was found among climacteric women, associated with sociodemographic, behavioral, and clinical factors. Health strategies should prioritize targeted interventions based on these determinants.

articles.title: Fetal arrhythmia and heart disease during COVID-19 pandemic in patients who underwent echocardiography.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Mattos FA, Tavares GMP, Callado GY et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the characteristics and the occurrence of fetal heart diseases and arrhythmias in pregnancies that underwent fetal echocardiography examination during COVID-19 pandemic.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data extracted from the Fetal Ultrasound and Fetal Medicine Departments of Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein, a tertiary hospital in São Paulo, Brazil, from January to December 2021. The sample was analyzed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and Student's t-test or the Mann-Whitney test. Logistic regression was performed to assess the risk of fetal arrhythmia and/or heart disease.
RESULTS: A total of 148 fetuses were included in the analysis. The prevalence of fetal heart disease/arrhythmia was higher among patients with maternal comorbidities (73.3% vs. 39.1%), fetal defects (14.3% vs. 0.8%), and functional abnormalities (26.7% vs. 4.5%). Maternal COVID-19 showed no significant association with fetal cardiac outcomes. Maternal comorbidity, fetal malformation, and the presence of functional abnormalities were identified as independent risk factors.
CONCLUSION: Maternal comorbidities were associated with fetal arrhythmia and/or heart disease, but no causal relationship was found between COVID-19 and adverse fetal cardiac outcome.

articles.title: Emerging mechanism-driven therapies for endometriosis: From GnRH antagonists to microbiome and device-based strategies (Review).
articles.authors: Thomas KS, Lekshmi SS, Gurrala H et al.
articles.abstract: Millions of women of reproductive age suffer from endometriosis, a chronic, estrogen-driven condition that causes pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea and infertility. Conventional therapy focuses on symptom suppression with hormone medications or the surgical excision of lesions; however, it is not curative. Recent developments in the understanding of the pathophysiology of endometriosis have revealed novel immunological and molecular mechanisms that are being used in experimental therapies. The present review outlines developing techniques, including targeted endocrine modulators, epigenetic treatments, anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory drugs, antioxidants, anti-angiogenic medicines, and microbiome-based therapy. Prominent examples are new oral gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor antagonists, selective progesterone receptor modulators and aromatase inhibitors that aim to overcome progesterone resistance. Alternative methods, such nutraceuticals and biologic and small-molecule inhibitors (such as metabolic drugs and anti-cytokine therapies) are being explored. Novel supplemental options are provided by device-based neuromodulation and improved surgical techniques (such as advanced laparoscopy, robotic excision, image-guided surgery, nerve-sparing techniques and adhesion barriers). While many of these innovations are promising, current evidence is limited by small studies and disease heterogeneity. Future directions emphasize rigorous trials with standardized outcomes, including fertility measures and combinations of therapies to achieve personalized, long-term relief.

articles.title: Trends in tubal sterilization and territorial disparities in Brazil: a nationwide time series study from 2013-2022.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Sampaio ALN, de Oliveira AV, Amaral JAT et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyse the trends in tubal sterilization in Brazil, regions and Federative Units by age group, race/skin colour and type of procedure from 2013 to 2022.
METHODS: Time series study with data from the Hospital Information System with females aged 20-59 years who underwent tubal sterilization procedures from 2013 to 2022 and defined by the standardized code utilized in the Brazilian Unified Health System for gathering data. Trends in tubal sterilization rates by region, age group, race/skin colour and procedure type were assessed. We estimated the average annual percent change (AAPC) and the 95% confidence interval (CI) of the tubal sterilization rates by Joinpoint regression. We compared the trends by coincidence test.
RESULTS: There were 719,426 tubal sterilizations in Brazil, with an overall upward trend (AAPC: 4.3; CI: 1.0-7.8). However, trends remained stationary in the Southeast (AAPC: 2.6; CI: -0.2-5.5) and South (AAPC: 0.4; CI: -3.5-4.4). All age groups had upward trends, except those aged 50-54 (AAPC: 6.2; CI: -7.5-22.0) and 55-59 years (AAPC: 7.4; CI: -4.9-21.4), which showed stationary trends. The analysis by race/skin colour predominantly indicated upward trends with greater AAPC amongst Browns. There were upward trends for procedures performed non-postpartum (AAPC: 8.5; CI: 7.5-9.4) and stationary trends for those performed postpartum (AAPC: 1.0; CI: -5.2-7.7).
CONCLUSIONS: While Brazil as a whole exhibited upward trend over the period, significant disparities were observed across regions and populations, reflecting structural inequalities in access and choice of contraception methods.

articles.title: Amniotic fluid embolism Number 11 - 2026.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Alves ÁLL, Nozaki AM, da Silva LB
articles.abstract: •Amniotic fluid embolism is a rare condition with high maternal mortality. It typically occurs during labor or delivery, and the pathogenesis has not yet been fully elucidated. •Survival of parturients with amniotic fluid embolism requires early recognition, rapid initiation of treatment, and access to skilled care based on the management of critically ill obstetric patients. •The classic clinical presentation of amniotic fluid embolism involves sudden hypoxia and hypotension or cardiopulmonary arrest, accompanied or immediately followed by non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and hemorrhage secondary to disseminated intravascular coagulation. •In cases of amniotic fluid embolism occurring during labor, bleeding typically originates at invasive interventions sites (intravascular lines and urinary catheterization). Following vaginal or cesarean delivery, bleeding arises primarily from the uterus, birth canal lacerations, and incision sites (abdominal wall and episiotomies). •Key laboratory abnormalities observed in amniotic fluid embolism include decreased fibrinogen levels, thrombocytopenia, and elevated D-dimer levels. The latter has limited diagnostic value, as levels are typically elevated during pregnancy and the postpartum period. •Arterial blood gas analysis in amniotic fluid embolism indicates the presence of hypoxemia and metabolic acidosis. Although chest radiography is initially unremarkable, if pulmonary edema and respiratory distress syndrome are present, dense bilateral pulmonary infiltrates may be observed. •The identification of amniotic fluid debris in pulmonary artery catheters or histopathological samples of lung tissue should not be considered diagnostic of amniotic fluid embolism. •The primary goals in managing amniotic fluid embolism are cardiopulmonary resuscitation, hemorrhage control, reversal of coagulopathy, and when indicated, fetal delivery. •In cases of amniotic fluid embolism accompanied by coagulopathy, massive transfusion is a necessary measure for effective, definitive treatment. The infusion of uterotonics, non-surgical invasive interventions (intrauterine balloons and intrauterine suction systems), and surgical procedures (vascular ligation, uterine compression sutures, and hysterectomy) may be used as adjuncts to control hemorrhage but are not considered definitive treatments. •The main differential diagnoses for amniotic fluid embolism include complications of neuraxial anesthesia; hemorrhage due to uterine atony, retained…

articles.title: Invasive and Non-invasive Biomarkers to Study the Genetic Instability among Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome Women of South Indian Cohort.
articles.authors: Mukherjee AG, Abilash VG, Hariprasath L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder associated with reproductive and metabolic abnormalities. Emerging evidence suggests that genomic instability may contribute to its pathophysiology and long-term health consequences.
AIM: The aim of this study was to evaluate genomic instability in women with PCOS using invasive and non-invasive cytogenetic biomarkers.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: A case-control study was conducted among women with PCOS and age-matched healthy controls from a South Indian cohort.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Buccal epithelial cells and peripheral blood samples were collected from 200 women with PCOS and 100 healthy controls. Genomic instability was assessed using the buccal micronucleus cytome (BMCyt) assay, cytokinesis-block micronucleus (CBMN) assay and chromosomal aberration analysis.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Data were analysed using GraphPad Prism 6.0. Group comparisons were performed using Student's unpaired t-test or Mann-Whitney U test as appropriate, with P < 0.05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Women with PCOS exhibited increased frequencies of nucleoplasmic bridges, nuclear buds, micronucleated binucleated cells and chromosomal aberrations compared with controls. Higher frequencies of chromosomal breaks, chromatid breaks and dicentric chromosomes were also observed, indicating increased genomic instability in the PCOS group.
CONCLUSION: Women with PCOS demonstrated increased cytogenetic abnormalities suggestive of elevated genomic instability. The combined application of BMCyt, CBMN and chromosomal aberration analyses provides complementary information regarding deoxyribonucleic acid damage and chromosomal instability in PCOS and may be useful for genomic instability assessment in future studies.

articles.title: Genitourinary syndrome: pelvic examination contributes to optimal management in postmenopausal women.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Buhl CN, Nunes CC, Ferreira AB et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the correlation between self-reported symptoms, clinical assessment and vaginal hormonal cytology in diagnosing genital atrophy in postmenopausal women attending a tertiary menopause clinic.
METHODS: A convenience sample of postmenopausal women aged 30 years and older, experiencing a broad spectrum of climacteric symptoms and without prior treatment or debilitating conditions, was included in the study.
