The study protocol encompassed: 1) Menopause Rating Scale (MRS), 2) pelvic examination using the Vaginal Health Index (VHI), and 3) assessment of vaginal hormonal cytology through the Meisels Index (MI). Univariate and bivariate descriptive analyses, as well as simple and multiple linear regression analyses, were conducted to identify factors associated with MI, with a significance level set at 5%.
RESULTS: One hundred and fifty-four women were studied, with a mean age of 50 years (±9) and mean age at menopause onset of 44.3 years (±6). The mean body mass index (BMI) was 28.7 (±5.4). The average MI was 47.8 (±23.8), MRS urogenital domain score was 6.1 (±3.7), and VHI score was 16.7 (±3.8). Multiple regression analysis showed significant associations between MI and total VHI (p < 0.001), BMI (p = 0.0263), and age (p = 0.0004). Women with higher MI tended to have higher VHI scores, higher BMI, and were younger.
CONCLUSION: The study suggests that pelvic examination contributes to optimal management of all postmenopausal women, including those who do not report symptoms.

articles.title: Progestin-Only contraceptive and clinical complications in women with sickle cell disease: a prospective study.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: da Silva FAC, Pedrosa EN, Hazin-Costa MF et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the influence of progestin-only contraceptives use on the occurrence of clinical complications in women with sickle cell disease.
METHODS: A prospective, non-randomized, comparative study was conducted involving 54 women with sickle cell disease between March 2018 and August 2020. Were excluded the women that were pregnant or wanted to become pregnant, were over 40 years old, and were not sexually active at the time of recruitment. Following contraceptive counseling, participants were monitored at 3, 6, and 12 months. They were classified into three groups: progestogen only, combined hormonal, and non-hormonal contraceptives users. Clinical complications were assessed throughout the follow-up. Data analysis was performed using logistic regression models for repeated binary outcomes, applying the generalized estimating equation method with robust variance. The value of p<0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: All participants experienced pain crises during their lives. No significant differences were observed between the groups regarding the frequency of pain crises. However, the progestogen only group presented a significantly lower frequency of headaches at 3, 6, and 12 months (p=0.012, p=0.016, and p=0.021, respectively) compared to the combined hormonal group.
CONCLUSION: Contraceptives containing progestogen only were not associated with a reduction in pain episodes in women with sickle cell disease but were associated with a lower frequency of headaches compared to combined hormonal contraception.

articles.title: Tubal Recanalization Following Tubal Sterilization- A 15-year Retrospective Cohort Study at a Tertiary Care Center in South India.
articles.authors: Daka SR, Chaturvedula L, Syed H
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tubal sterilization is a common contraceptive method in resource-limited settings like India. Reversal via recanalization is often sought following child loss. Success rates vary, with pregnancy achievable in over half of the cases. Identifying prognostic factors is essential for optimal patient selection and counseling.
AIM: The aim of this study was to assess pregnancy rates following tubal recanalization after sterilization and identify key prognostic factors.
SETTING AND DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary care teaching hospital in South India.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data from 409 women undergoing tubal recanalization between 2003 and 2017 were analyzed.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data. Categorical variables were compared using the Chi-square test. P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Out of 551 women, 409 whose details were available were included in the study. Most women were ≤30 years old (73.9%), sought reversal primarily due to loss of child (68.4%), and had puerperal sterilization (62.9%). The overall pregnancy rate was 57.0% (233/409). Among conceptions, live births accounted for 64.8%, miscarriages 14.6%, and ectopic pregnancies 20.6%. Over 94.8% of conceptions occurred within 4 years postrecanalization. Significantly higher pregnancy rates were observed in women ≤30 years old, with prior vaginal deliveries (60.8%; P < 0.001), interval sterilization (78.2%; P < 0.001), isthmo-isthmic anastomosis (85.7%; P < 0.001), recanalization within 4 years of sterilization, residual tubal length >6 cm (85.9%; P < 0.001), and absence of tubal adhesions (60.4%; P = 0.009).
CONCLUSION: Tubal recanalization is a reasonable option for fertility restoration after sterilization in appropriately selected women, with key prognostic factors identified for better patient selection and counseling, though the high ectopic pregnancy rate warrants close monitoring and informed consent.

articles.title: Effect of Anti-thyroid Peroxidase Antibodies on Assisted Reproductive Technologies Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Stølan NN, Svendsen PF, Klajnbard A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies (TPOAbs) are common among women of reproductive age, especially in assisted reproductive technologies (ART). Their impact on early embryological outcomes remains unclear. Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) has been proposed to overcome possible adverse effects of TPOAbs in the follicular fluid.
AIM: The aim of the study was to evaluate the effect of TPOAbs on fertilisation in women undergoing in vitro fertilisation (IVF) and to compare fertilisation between IVF and ICSI in TPOAb-positive women.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: The study design was a retrospective cohort study.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data were retrieved from institutional records. 779 women undergoing their first IVF or split cycle at Herlev Hospital between December 2019 and November 2024 were included.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Logistic regression was used to assess fertilisation and blastocyst outcomes. All models were adjusted for age, body mass index, sperm type, sperm quality and smoking status.
RESULTS: No significant differences were observed in fertilisation or blastocyst development between TPOAb-positive and negative women undergoing IVF. In the split group, TPOAb-positive women had higher fertilisation with ICSI than IVF; however, this difference was not significant (odds ratio [OR]: 1.66, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.96-2.90). Among TPOAb-negative women, ICSI was associated with a significantly higher fertilisation rate (OR: 1.50, 95% CI: 1.20-1.87), whereas the increase in blastocyst formation was not significant.
CONCLUSION: Fertilisation did not differ between TPOAb-positive and TPOAb-negative women undergoing ART. Although ICSI was associated with higher fertilisation rates, this effect was observed irrespective of TPOAb status. The benefit of ICSI likely reflects technique-related advantages rather than modulation by thyroid autoimmunity. Prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: Relationship between pregnancy risk factors and ABG umbilical cord of the infant after birth.
articles.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
articles.authors: Amjadi N, Omidi Kermanshahaninezhad S, Talayeh M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Newborn assessment using Umbilical arterial blood gas (UABG) analysis is more objective than other methods for predicting neonatal outcome. Acidic neonates may be at risk of adverse consequences after birth. This study was conducted to determine the risk factors during pregnancy and their effect on the arterial blood gas (ABG) of the neonates after birth.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted on 1794 mothers hospitalized for termination of pregnancy who were referred to Imam Hossein Medical Training Center in Tehran during the years 2021-2023. Information was collected through a checklist before and after delivery. Also, to perform ABG and VBG, a blood sample was taken from the neonate's umbilical cord and extracted from the file. Data analysis was done using SPSS version 25 statistical software.
RESULTS: In this study, between different ABG levels and maternal characteristics, BMI, oligohydramnios, placental abruption, IUGR, acreta, PPROM, delivery mode, and labor with induction, COVID-19, HTN, heart disease, anemia, diabetes, gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia and addiction statistically significant difference was observed (P < 0.05). A significant difference was observed between preterm infants, weighing less than 2500 grams, Apgar score lower than 7 in the first and fifth minutes, and hospitalization in NICU with different levels of ABG PH (P < 0.05). In the multivariable model, fetal distress (OR: 3.51, 95% CI: 1.91-6.44), GDM (Insulin, OR = 5.08; 95% CI: 2.60-9.95), Gestational age at birth (<37, OR = 2.25; 95% CI: 1.23-4.12) were associated with an increased odds of ABG acid level. Also, in the multivariable model, fetal distress (OR: 2.30, 95% CI: 1.70-3.12), GDM (Insulin, OR = 2.48; 95% CI: 1.70-3.64 and diet, OR = 2.42; 95% CI: 1.46-4.02), Labor (Induction, OR = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.10-2), Gestational age at birth (<37, OR = 1.43; 95% CI: 1.06-1.92) were associated with an increased odds of ABG hypoxia level.
CONCLUSION: It can be concluded that umbilical cord blood gas is closely related to neonatal prognosis and is a useful tool for screening newborns at risk. ABG should be considered for all deliveries, as it is an accurate screening test for hypoxia and neonatal asphyxia.

articles.title: The Association of Protein Supplements and Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids with Seminal Parameters and Fertility in Men: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.authors: Mutha AS, Bavlecha AM, Kulkarni VR et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of protein supplements (PSs) and anabolic-androgenic steroids (AASs) has increased globally, particularly among recreational gym users. While the reproductive effects of AAS are well established, data regarding PS and seminal parameters remain limited, especially in South Asian populations.
AIM: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association of PS and AAS use with seminal parameters in men.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: This was a cross-sectional observational study conducted at an private Sexual Medicine Clinic in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male participants aged 21-50 years with self-reported PS use, AAS use or both were enrolled and classified into PS users, AAS users and combined PS + AAS users. Healthy volunteers without known sexual complaints or PS/AAS use served as controls. Semen samples were analysed according to the World Health Organization 2010 guidelines.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Data were analysed using analysis of variance or Kruskal-Wallis tests with appropriate post hoc analysis. P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: A total of 170 participants were analysed, including 58 controls, 62 PS users, 18 AAS users and 32 combined users. Significant differences were observed in seminal volume, liquefaction time, sperm concentration, sperm motility and testicular volume (P < 0.05), while seminal pH remained comparable. Abnormal sperm concentration was observed in 50.0% of PS users, 72.2% of AAS users and 78.1% of combined users.
CONCLUSION: PS and AAS exposure were associated with impaired seminal parameters, with the most pronounced abnormalities observed in combined users. Larger prospective multicentre studies are required to validate these findings.

articles.title: AI-assisted IVF company websites: a content analysis of marketing claims, information quality, legal and ethical issues.
articles.authors: Du L, Zhang Y
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: How do providers of AI-assisted IVF products and services present their AI systems, characterize their products and services, and address patient privacy and data protection concerns on their websites?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Websites of AI-assisted IVF providers predominantly emphasize benefits while failing to disclose risks, provide insufficient information about AI systems and data sources, and inadequately address privacy protection, with none of them including AI-specific provisions in their privacy policies.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Websites promoting AI-assisted products and services for IVF treatments are a key information source for patients, can shape perceptions about this advanced technology, and have an impact on patients' treatment decisions. However, the way providers present such services on their websites has not been previously studied.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: Using online searches and a review of research abstracts presented at the 2022 ESHRE annual meeting, we identified 21 companies offering AI-assisted IVF products or services. Website content was captured between 15 and 22 August 2023, and content analysis was done between 25 August and 15 September 2023. In response to an external reviewer's recommendation, we did a follow-up review on 30 June 2026.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Twenty-one companies (7 IVF equipment producers, 14 exclusively developing AI-assisted IVF products) based in Europe (n = 9), Israel (n = 4), Canada/USA (n = 5), and China (n = 3) were evaluated in this study. The companies collectively offered 30 AI tools including embryo quality assessment, oocyte quality assessment, sperm analysis, endometrial receptivity analysis, and ovarian stimulation optimization. A subset of 10 companies' websites was used for thematic content analysis and the resulting themes were used to develop a coding book with 22 questions examining (i) benefit and risk descriptions; (ii) AI system explanations and performance; (iii) data protection and privacy issues; and (iv) portrayal of products/services. The coding book was finalized and subsequently applied by one of the authors to complete an analysis of the entire dataset. Based on an external reviewer's suggestion, we also analyzed the AI models on providers' websites. Independent coding of 60% of samples achieved almost perfect inter-coder agreement (Cohen's Kappa: 0.831-1.000).
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: All 21 websites (100%) mentioned benefits of…

articles.title: The impact of group prenatal care on breastfeeding: A planned secondary analysis of the CRADLE randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Campbell AIK, DuBose M, Britt J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite providing both maternal and neonatal benefits, breastfeeding rates remain lower than goal targets. Prior observational studies suggest group prenatal care (GPNC) increases breastfeeding initiation compared to individual prenatal care (IPNC), but few randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have examined how GPNC impacts breastfeeding knowledge and self-efficacy. We aimed to determine if participating in GPNC impacts breastfeeding knowledge, breastfeeding self-efficacy, and breastfeeding prevalence postpartum.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This is a planned secondary analysis of the Centering and Racial Disparities (CRADLE) RCT comparing the impact of GPNC versus IPNC on preterm birth. The CRADLE trial enrolled 2350 participants and randomized them to GPNC or IPNC. Eligibility requirements included age of 14-45 years, singleton pregnancy, entering prenatal care before 21 weeks' gestation, and low-risk pregnancy by institutional standards. Questionnaires assessed breastfeeding knowledge (adapted from the Infant Feeding Practices II Survey) and self-efficacy (adapted from Wells' 20-item Prenatal Breast-feeding Self-Efficacy Scale). A per-compliance approach was used, including participants who attended at least five sessions in their assigned group. The primary outcome was breastfeeding at hospital discharge. Secondary outcomes were breastfeeding knowledge, breastfeeding self-efficacy, and breastfeeding prevalence at the postpartum visit. Chi-square, Students' t-test, and multivariable logistic regression were applied. Additionally, a sensitivity analysis was conducted among nulliparous participants.
RESULTS: Of the 2350 participants in the CRADLE study, 1561 were included in this secondary analysis. Participants self-identified as Black (38.3%), Hispanic (24.2%), White (36.2%), or another race and ethnicity (1.3%), and the majority were multiparous. GPNC participants reported higher rates of breastfeeding at hospital discharge compared to IPNC (72.8% IPNC vs. 78.2% GPNC; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02-1.72). GPNC participants also had greater breastfeeding knowledge, scoring higher on the composite knowledge questionnaire (score 18.5, standard deviation [SD] 4.3) compared to IPNC participants (score 17.5, SD 4.4; p < 0.001). No differences were observed in self-efficacy scores or postpartum breastfeeding rates between GPNC and IPNC participants. These findings were generally consistent for nulliparous…

articles.title: A Rare Case of Multiple Recurrent Parasitic Leiomyomas Managed Surgically Without Additional Chemical Estrogen Suppression.
articles.authors: Baptiste C, Everett EN, Rehman HT et al.
articles.abstract: Parasitic leiomyomas (PMs) are rare extrauterine benign smooth muscle tumors that can arise spontaneously or develop iatrogenically following prior uterine surgery, particularly with morcellation of uterine tissue. We present a case of a 49-year-old woman who developed multiple recurrent PMs involving the abdominal cavity, appendix, and abdominal wall over several years following laparoscopic myomectomy with morcellation and subsequent hysterectomy. At her most recent intra-abdominal recurrence, she underwent a bilateral oophorectomy at the time of tumor resection. This case highlights the potential for delayed recurrence of parasitic myomas even years after hysterectomy and supports the importance of clinical vigilance and imaging in symptomatic patients with prior morcellation. It also supports consideration of and further study of the role of estrogen suppression in preventing recurrence.

articles.title: Safety and tolerability of elinzanetant: a pooled analysis from four randomized clinical trials.
articles.authors: Pinkerton JV, Francuski M, Nappi RE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elinzanetant is a dual neurokinin (NK)-1 and NK-3 receptor antagonist approved for the treatment of moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms (VMS) associated with menopause, or those caused by adjuvant endocrine therapy for breast cancer treatment.
METHODS: In this pooled safety analysis, safety data were pooled from four randomized, placebo-controlled studies: the phase IIb SWITCH-1 trial (2018-2019) and phase III OASIS-1-3 trials (2021-2024). All four studies were multicentre, multinational, double-blind trials that included postmenopausal women aged 40-65 years experiencing moderate-to-severe VMS due to natural or surgical menopause. Data were analysed exploratively. Assessments included frequency of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) over 12 and 52 weeks, and exposure-adjusted incidence rates (EAIRs, with 95% confidence intervals [CIs]) over 52 weeks. EAIRs were calculated by weighting event counts against total exposure time (person-years) across studies. Additionally, liver safety and incidence of neoplasms were evaluated.
FINDINGS: The 12-week pooled safety analysis set included 1519 participants: 765 participants in the elinzanetant 120 mg group and 754 participants in the placebo group. The 52-week pooled safety analysis set included 1113 participants in the elinzanetant 120 mg group and 754 participants in the placebo group. TEAEs occurred in 50·8% and 43·2% of participants in the elinzanetant 120 mg and the placebo groups, respectively, over 12 weeks; EAIRs were 196·61 (95% CI 181·33-213·18) and 209·00 (95% CI: 188·96-231·15) in the elinzanetant and placebo groups, respectively, over 52 weeks. The most common TEAEs reported with elinzanetant were headache, fatigue, and somnolence. Treatment discontinuation was low with elinzanetant (7·8%) but higher than placebo (3·6%) over 12 weeks; EAIRs were 14·95 (95% CI 11·99-18·62) and 10·96 (95% CI 7·87-15·27), respectively, over 52 weeks. There were no Hy's Law cases or indication of cholestatic injury. EAIRs of malignant tumors had overlapping CIs between treatment groups. No endometrial hyperplasia/malignancy was reported in either group.
INTERPRETATION: The overall safety profile of elinzanetant appeared favorable in 1113 women based on this exploratory pooled safety analysis. Future time-to-event analyses of TEAEs and real-world post-marketing data are warranted to better characterize the long-term safety profile of elinzanetant.
FUNDING: Bayer.

articles.title: Immunohistochemical Expression of Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen in Invasive Breast Carcinoma: Associations With Histological Grade and Ki-67 Expression.
articles.authors: Kumar V, Kumar A, Singh N et al.
articles.abstract: Background Proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) is a nuclear protein involved in DNA replication and repair. Although PCNA is widely used experimentally as a proliferation-related marker, its clinicopathological relevance in breast carcinoma is less clearly established than that of Ki-67. This study evaluated whether increasing ordinal PCNA immunoexpression was associated with increasing histological grade. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study identified 409 breast carcinoma cases evaluated at the Department of Pathology, Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College, Aligarh Muslim University, Aligarh, India, from October 2018 to December 2020. The sample size was estimated to detect a correlation of 0.38 between PCNA and Ki-67, with 80% power at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05. Eligible complete-data cases were sampled using proportionate stratified random sampling according to menopausal status; computer-generated random selection without replacement yielded 26 premenopausal and 26 postmenopausal women. PCNA and Ki-67 immunoexpression were recorded as negative, mild (1+), moderate (2+), or intense (3+). The primary PCNA-grade association was evaluated using Fisher-Freeman-Halton Monte Carlo inference, Spearman correlation, the Jonckheere-Terpstra ordered-trend test, and Cramer's V; Ki-67 was a secondary comparator. Results The mean age was 49.90 ± 9.85 years, and all 52 patients were women. Grades 1, 2, and 3 comprised six (11.5%), 32 (61.5%), and 14 (26.9%) tumors, respectively. The final PCNA immunoexpression category was mild (1+) in six cases (11.5%), moderate (2+) in six cases (11.5%), and intense (3+) in 40 cases (76.9%). The 3+ PCNA immunoexpression category occurred in one of six grade 1 tumors, 25 of 32 grade 2 tumors, and all 14 grade 3 tumors. PCNA was significantly associated with grade (Fisher-Freeman-Halton Monte Carlo p<0.001; Cramer's V=0.483), with a positive monotonic relationship (Spearman rho=0.476, p<0.001) and ordered trend (Jonckheere-Terpstra Z=3.340, two-sided Monte Carlo p<0.001). PCNA also correlated with Ki-67 category (rho=0.387, p=0.005). Conclusions Increasing PCNA immunoexpression was associated with higher histological grade and showed a moderate positive ordinal association with Ki-67 in this cohort. These findings support a clinicopathological relationship between PCNA expression and proliferative morphology but do not establish independent prognostic or treatment-predictive utility. Larger prospectively assembled…

articles.title: Research progress and clinical translation prospects of multiple urinary biomarkers in non-invasive diagnosis of urothelial carcinoma.
articles.authors: Li S, Wang L, Gao B
articles.abstract: Urothelial carcinoma is a common urinary malignancy with high incidence, recurrence, and mortality. Early diagnosis is pivotal for improving patient outcomes. Current standards have important limitations: cystoscopy, although the cornerstone of diagnosis and surveillance, is invasive and costly, while cytology has limited sensitivity for low-grade or early-stage lesions. Urine, as a liquid biopsy, offers a non-invasive and repeatable approach for sampling urogenital pathology, with the potential for longitudinal monitoring through serial collection. The review covers urinary multi-omics biomarkers, including cfDNA/methylation, miRNAs, extracellular vesicles (EVs), and proteomic/metabolomic signatures. We summarize their performance in early detection, staging, and postoperative monitoring. Integrated multi-analyte models, including true multi-omics assays and multiplex single-omics panels, generally outperform single biomarkers, with some panels achieving >90% sensitivity and >95% specificity in prospective cohorts. Despite progress, several challenges remain: standardization, large-scale prospective validation, and regulatory/reimbursement barriers. We conclude that urinary multi-omics diagnostics are promising complementary tools that may optimize surveillance and risk stratification. Still, limited prospective validation, lack of standardization, and the persistent risk of false-negative results constrain adoption. On current evidence, they are not positioned to replace cystoscopy, which remains the cornerstone of diagnosis and surveillance, particularly in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). However, their most realistic and immediate clinical role is as a triage tool to optimize the selective use of cystoscopy-particularly for risk-stratifying patients with hematuria, adjudicating equivocal cytology, and potentially reducing the frequency of invasive surveillance in low-risk NMIBC patients.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of explainable machine learning models for predicting failure of first ambulation within 12 h after cesarean delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Xiong L, Jin Y, Li W et al.
articles.abstract: Early ambulation is a notable component of postoperative recovery after cesarean delivery, but some women fail to complete first ambulation within the early postoperative period because of pain, dizziness, orthostatic discomfort, residual lower limb numbness, nausea or vomiting, hypotension or poor activity tolerance. Early identification of women at high risk of ambulation failure may support timely and individualized nursing interventions. The present study aimed to develop and internally validate explainable machine learning models for predicting failure of first ambulation within 12 h after cesarean delivery using routinely collected obstetric perioperative nursing assessment data. The present single-center retrospective cohort study included relatively stable women who underwent cesarean delivery between January 2022 and December 2025 and were considered clinically eligible for early mobilization. The primary outcome was failure of first ambulation within 12 h after surgery, defined as no documented successful ambulation within 12 h or discontinuation of an ambulation attempt because of nursing-documented intolerance. Candidate predictors included demographic, obstetric, pregnancy-related, laboratory, anesthetic, surgical and early postoperative nursing assessment variables. Postoperative symptoms and vital signs were assessed within predefined early postoperative intervals, whereas first turning time was treated as a dynamically updated indicator that became available when the first spontaneous or assisted turning event was documented. The model was therefore interpreted as a dynamic early postoperative risk-assessment approach rather than a prediction model applied exclusively at a fixed 4-h time point. The final analytic dataset contained no item-level missing values; therefore, no imputation was performed. The cohort was randomly divided into training and internal validation cohorts at a ratio of 7:3. Logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and LightGBM models were developed and compared. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, classification metrics, calibration, Brier score and decision curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret the final model. A total of 1,486 women were included, and 326 women experienced failure of first ambulation within 12 h, with an incidence of 21.9%. The training and validation cohorts included 1,040 and 446…

articles.title: Diagnostic value of transvaginal three-dimensional ultrasonography combined with superb microvascular imaging for endometrial polyps.
articles.authors: Dong J, Sun Q, Xiao T et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the diagnostic value of transvaginal three-dimensional ultrasonography combined with superb microvascular imaging (SMI) for the preoperative detection of endometrial polyps, and to determine whether multimodal integration improves detection yield, diagnostic confidence, or recognition of diagnostically challenging lesions compared to morphology-based imaging alone.
METHODS: In this retrospective observational study, we reviewed 203 consecutive patients with suspected endometrial polyps who underwent evaluation at the Central Hospital of China Railway 17th Bureau Group Co., Ltd. between July 2025 and January 2026. All patients underwent conventional ultrasonography, transvaginal three-dimensional ultrasonography (3D-TVS), and SMI before hysteroscopic pathologic confirmation, which was used as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was compared among different imaging strategies, including 3D-TVS alone, SMI alone, conventional ultrasonography combined with SMI, and 3D-TVS combined with SMI. The primary endpoint was preoperative detection yield of endometrial polyps.
RESULTS: Compared to conventional ultrasonography, 3D-TVS alone did not significantly improve the overall preoperative detection rate of endometrial polyps, whereas SMI alone significantly increased detection rate (P<0.05). The addition of SMI significantly improved detection when combined with conventional ultrasonography or 3D-TVS (both P<0.001), with 3D-TVS + SMI showing the highest overall diagnostic performance. Conventional ultrasonography and 3D-TVS more readily detected larger, solitary, pedunculated lesions with well-defined margins, whereas missed lesions were more frequently characterized by small size, multiplicity, sessile morphology, lower uterine segment location, intrauterine device use/history, heterogeneous endometrium, or acoustic artifacts (all P<0.05). SMI-based recognition was strongly associated with the presence of intralesional blood flow, central feeding vessels, branching vascular patterns, continuous vascular pedicles, and higher microvascular indices (all P<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified lesion size <15 mm, sessile morphology, acoustic artifact, absence of vascular pedicles, low microvascular density, and failure of coronal plane reconstruction as independent predictors of missed diagnosis (all P<0.05).
CONCLUSION: Transvaginal 3D ultrasonography combined with SMI significantly improves the preoperative detection of endometrial…

articles.title: Association between early gestational weight gain and the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Duan M, Xu F
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the correlation between excessive weight gain during early pregnancy and the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and to provide evidence for early clinical intervention.
METHODS: The clinical data of 152 women with singleton pregnancies who were admitted to the Department of Obstetrics, PLA General Hospital Hainan Branch, from January 2022 to December 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. According to weight gain during early pregnancy (before 14 weeks of gestation), the pregnant women were divided into an excessive weight gain group (> 2.0 kg/week, 68 cases) and a normal weight gain group (0.5-2.0 kg/week, 84 cases). Baseline clinical characteristics, including maternal age, pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI), obstetric history, and family history, were collected. An oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) was performed at 24-28 weeks of gestation to screen for GDM. Univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression analysis were performed to evaluate the relationship between early pregnancy weight gain and the risk of GDM.
RESULTS: Among 152 pregnant women, 35 were diagnosed with GDM, with an incidence of 23.0%. The incidence of GDM in the excessive weight gain group was 32.4% (22/68), significantly higher than 15.5% (13/84) in the normal weight gain group (χ2=6.214, P=0.013). No significant differences were observed in baseline characteristics, including maternal age, pre-pregnancy BMI, and gravidity, between the two groups (P > 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that, after adjusting for potential confounding factors such as maternal age and pre-pregnancy BMI, excessive weight gain during early pregnancy remained an independent risk factor for GDM (OR=2.876, 95% CI: 1.543-5.362, P=0.001).
CONCLUSION: Excessive weight gain during early pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of GDM. Therefore, clinical monitoring and management of weight gain during early pregnancy should be strengthened, and early intervention should be implemented for pregnant women with excessive weight gain to reduce the risk of GDM.

articles.title: Hydroxyurea treatment is not significantly associated with reduced spermatogonial numbers in patients with sickle cell disease.
articles.authors: De Beer E, Delgouffe E, Mazilier P et al.
articles.abstract: Hydroxyurea (HU) is considered a first-line therapy for patients with sickle cell disease (SCD). In cases of inadequate response to HU therapy, patients may receive conditioning therapy prior to haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, which can lead to depletion of the number of spermatogonia. Therefore, in pre-pubertal boys, fertility is preserved through cryopreservation of testicular tissue, although this is an experimental method. Analysis of this tissue showed a considerable loss of spermatogonia, leading to the hypothesis that HU therapy may reduce the spermatogonial number. However, evidence remains limited and conflicting. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the relationship between HU exposure and the spermatogonial number in boys with SCD. The number of spermatogonia per round seminiferous tubule (S/T) and the percentage of tubules containing spermatogonia were determined in cryopreserved testicular tissue from 27 HU-treated patients with SCD. Linear regression analyses were performed to assess their association with HU exposure. Spermatogonia were present in most boys with SCD, although in severely reduced numbers. S/T Z-scores and the percentage of tubules containing spermatogonia were not significantly associated with age at HU initiation, duration of HU exposure, or HU dose. In conclusion, in this cohort, no statistically significant association was observed between HU treatment and reduced spermatogonial numbers in patients with SCD.

articles.title: Cellular senescence in ovarian cancer: a proposed geroncogenic shift linking aging, plasticity, and therapy resistance.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Han Y, Hou P et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer develops within a biological environment that changes substantially with age. Beyond chronological aging, progressive alterations in genome maintenance, telomere integrity, epigenetic regulation, mitochondrial function, metabolism, inflammation, and immune surveillance can reshape the cellular and tissue context in which tumor evolution occurs. Cellular senescence represents a critical point of convergence within this process. Although senescence can restrict the proliferation of damaged or oncogenically stressed cells, persistent senescent cells remain metabolically active and can alter their surroundings through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Here, we propose the concept of a geroncogenic shift to describe how age-associated changes in tissue homeostasis may create stress-response states that are subsequently exploited by malignant and stromal cells. We distinguish two named, complementary components of the framework: systemic decline, referring to the progressive deterioration of cellular and tissue homeostasis during aging, and pathway-specific hijacking, referring to the selective co-option of altered stress-response pathways under oncogenic or therapeutic pressure. Cellular senescence provides a functional interface between these processes because the same stress responses that constrain damaged cells can, when persistent or incompletely resolved, contribute to tumor adaptation. In ovarian cancer, senescence is not a uniform cellular endpoint. Its consequences vary according to the initiating stress, cellular compartment, molecular program, duration, and capacity for recovery or escape. Tumor-cell senescence may suppress proliferation yet also be associated with stem-like adaptation and therapeutic persistence. Senescence-associated changes in fibroblasts and other stromal populations can reshape inflammatory signaling and treatment response, while polyploid and senescence-like states illustrate the extent of cellular plasticity that can exist after therapeutic stress. The SASP further extends the effects of senescence beyond individual cells by influencing neighboring tumor and stromal populations, extracellular-matrix remodeling, inflammation, and dissemination. This perspective has important therapeutic implications. Rather than treating senescence as either a uniformly protective or pathogenic state, therapeutic strategies should distinguish between senescent-cell elimination, SASP modulation, metabolic…

articles.title: Epigenetic adaptations and vulnerabilities in ovarian cancer drug-tolerant persister cells.
articles.authors: Dumbrava MG, Hamernick SJ, Harrington SP et al.
articles.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) recurs in most patients despite initial responses to chemotherapy and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibition. A leading explanation for the high rates of recurrence is the presence of minimal residual disease (MRD) comprised of drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cells that survive therapy through reversible epigenetic reprogramming. DTPs have various adaptations that enable them to tolerate therapy and eventually develop into resistant clones, including quiescence, metabolic and hypoxic stress responses, epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, and immune evasion. Here, we discuss evidence from ovarian cancer of epigenetic mechanisms that coordinate DTP phenotypes, including DNA methylation, histone post-translational modifications, enhancer rewiring, and transcription factor gene-regulatory networks. Based on therapeutic vulnerabilities identified from increased resolution of DTPs, we highlight epigenetic therapies that are currently in clinical trials aimed at depleting MRD to delay or prevent relapse in HGSOC. Finally, we outline emerging technologies that have the potential to detect and monitor persister states in patients, including single-cell transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling, long-read sequencing, and spatial mapping of tumor biopsies.

articles.title: Maternal mortality in the context of COVID-19: an ecological study comparing maternal mortality ratios before and during the pandemic, Minas Gerais, Brazil, 2010-2021.
articles.journal: Epidemiologia e servicos de saude : revista do Sistema Unico de Saude do Brasil
articles.authors: Lopes LMG, de Souza JB, Malta DC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate changes in maternal mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic according to sociodemographic, regional and obstetric care characteristics in Minas Gerais state, and the correlation of the Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) with socioeconomic indicators of macro-region of residence.
METHODS: The study compared Mortality Information System data between 2010-2019 and 2020-2021. The MMR and its percentage change were calculated according to age, schooling, race/skin color, number of prenatal consultations/trimester of prenatal care initiation and health macro-region. We assessed the correlation between the MMR and macro-region socioeconomic variables (Gross Domestic Product [GDP] per capita, Brazilian Deprivation Index and Schooling).
RESULTS: 1,488 deaths were recorded. The MMR increased by 62.5% during the pandemic, especially among women aged 20 to 34 (64.5%), White women (77.7%), women with lower education levels (134.9%), fewer prenatal visits (102.2%), those who started prenatal care in the 1st trimester (58.1%), and those living in the Northwest macro-region (241%). However, the highest MMRs were found in women aged 35 or older (125.1/100,000 live births), Black women (90.5/100,000 live births), women with lower education levels (151.5/100,000 live births), women with fewer prenatal visits (181.2/100,000 live births), women who started prenatal care in the 1st trimester (61.8/100,000 live births), and women living in the Northeast macro-region (122.3/100,000 live births). We found no correlation between socioeconomic indicators and the MMR during the pandemic.
CONCLUSION: The percentage increase in the ratio during the pandemic was greater in groups and regions with historically lower MMRs. Timely recognition of pregnant/postpartum women as a risk group in health crises can reduce preventable maternal deaths.

articles.title: Metabolic rewiring at the obesity-estrogen-polyamine axis in endometrial cancer: emerging mechanisms and translational opportunities.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Simancas-Racines D, Jima Gavilanes D, Matos A et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial cancer is one of the gynecologic malignancies most strongly associated with obesity, yet the biological basis of this association extends beyond excess adiposity as a risk factor. Obesity reshapes the endometrial ecosystem through peripheral estrogen excess, progesterone imbalance, insulin resistance, adipokine dysregulation, chronic inflammation, and activation of anabolic signaling pathways. These mechanisms converge on metabolic programs that support proliferation, invasion, immune remodeling, and treatment resistance. Polyamine metabolism is emerging as a potentially relevant but still incompletely validated layer of this biology. Ornithine decarboxylase 1, the rate-limiting enzyme in polyamine biosynthesis, is overexpressed in aggressive endometrial cancers and has been associated with recurrence and poor survival. Recent evidence further suggests that metabolic syndrome-associated oleic acid may stabilize homeobox B9, protect ornithine decarboxylase 1 from degradation, increase polyamine accumulation, and promote tumor progression. This Mini Review critically examines the obesity-estrogen-polyamine axis as an integrative framework linking endocrine dysfunction, inflammatory remodeling, lipid signaling, and proliferative metabolic rewiring in endometrial cancer. It also discusses biomarker opportunities, therapeutic vulnerabilities, and the translational gaps that must be addressed before this axis can inform precision oncology.

articles.title: Differential sparse attention framework for accurate ovarian cancer subtype classification using DenseNet121.
articles.authors: Saleem MS, Rashid J, Althobaiti T et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ovarian cancer is the most fatal gynecologic cancer, contributing to approximately 207,000 deaths per year worldwide, largely due to late-stage diagnosis and considerable histopathological diversity across subtypes. Accurate subtype classification is clinically important for prognosis and treatment planning, but remains challenging due to high inter-class morphological similarity and the scarcity of adequately labeled histopathological datasets.
METHODS: This study presents a novel attention module, Deep Differential Sparse Attention (DDSA), designed for multi-class classification of ovarian cancer subtypes in histopathology images. The module selectively amplifies discriminative tumor regions while suppressing irrelevant background features, thereby improving both feature representation and model interpretability. A dataset of 3,082 images spanning five subtypes i.e., Clear Cell Carcinoma, Endometrioid Carcinoma, High-Grade Serous Carcinoma, Low-Grade Serous Carcinoma, and Mucinous Carcinoma--was obtained from Kaggle. The training set was balanced to 5,940 images (1,188 per subtype) using RandomOverSampler, with on-the-fly data augmentation applied during training. DDSA was integrated into a DenseNet-based architecture, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using standard classification metrics, including precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, and ROC curves.
RESULTS: The proposed model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 92.53%, with a macro-average recall of 91.54% and a macro-average F1-score of 0.90. AUC values ranged from 0.92 to 0.99 across all five subtypes, indicating strong and consistent classification performance on the test set.
DISCUSSION: These results suggest that attention-guided DenseNet architectures can enhance discriminative feature extraction and improve diagnostic accuracy for ovarian cancer subtype classification. The DDSA module's ability to highlight tumor-relevant regions also supports improved model interpretability, an important consideration for clinical adoption. While these findings are promising, further validation on larger, multi-institutional datasets is needed to confirm robustness and generalizability, and to assess the framework's readiness for clinical deployment.

articles.title: Maternal gestational weight gain and offspring vitamin D level: a multicentre retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Zhao Y, Li Q, Zhu H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study examined the association between maternal gestational weight gain (GWG) and offspring vitamin D levels.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 0-5-year-old children attending routine health checks at 12 centres across 10 cities in Jiangsu Province (April 2014-March 2015) were enrolled via stratified random cluster sampling. Serum 25(OH)D was measured by ELISA.
RESULTS: Among 1,984 mother-offspring pairs, GWG ≤10 kg was associated with an increased risk of vitamin D deficiency (<50 nmol/L) in the unadjusted model (OR = 1.550, 95% CI: 1.196-2.008), and this association remained significant in Model 1 (OR = 1.820, 95% CI: 1.357-2.441), Model 2 (OR = 1.545, 95% CI: 1.060-2.253), and Model 3 (OR = 1.882, 95% CI: 1.228-2.883). For vitamin D insufficiency (50-<75 nmol/L), GWG >19 kg was associated with an increased risk in the unadjusted model (OR = 1.309, 95% CI: 1.026-1.670) and in Model 1 (OR = 1.312, 95% CI: 1.021-1.685), Model 2 (OR = 1.872, 95% CI: 1.305-2.684), and Model 3 (OR = 1.609, 95% CI: 1.054-2.456). This association was statistically significant in Model 3 but was no longer significant after FDR correction.
CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first multicentre study to report an association between GWG ≤10 kg and an increased risk of vitamin D deficiency in offspring, and between GWG >19 kg and an increased risk of vitamin D insufficiency. However, the latter association did not remain significant after FDR correction in sensitivity analyses based on Model 3 and requires confirmation in further studies.

articles.title: Syphilis in pregnancy detection rate: time series study associated with descriptive analysis by periods, Campo Grande, 2015-2023.
articles.journal: Epidemiologia e servicos de saude : revista do Sistema Unico de Saude do Brasil
articles.authors: Reis COF, Borges LADC, Santos-Pinto CDB et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the time series and trend of the syphilis in pregnancy detection rate over nine years and the variations in clinical and epidemiological characteristics across four periods according to relevant public health events in Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul.
METHODS: Time series study with descriptive analysis by periods, using data from the Notifiable Diseases Information System (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação, SINAN) and the Live Birth Information System (Sistema Nacional de Nascidos Vivos, SINASC). Segmented linear regression was used to analyze the temporal trend of the syphilis in pregnancy detection rate, and the Kruskal-Wallis test was employed to analyze clinical and epidemiological variables across the evaluated periods: penicillin shortage (2015-2016); supply normalization and pre-pandemic period (2017-2019); pandemic (2020-2021); and post-COVID-19 pandemic (2022-2023).
RESULTS: A total of 2,802 cases were analyzed. An increase of 170.4% in the detection rate was observed, with a rising trend until 2018 (annual percentage change, APC 31.18%; 95% confidence interval, 95%CI 4.79; 118.80; p-value 0.017) and subsequent stabilization (APC 1.16%; 95%CI -27.24; 15.83; p-value 0.936). Regarding clinical-epidemiological characteristics, there was an increase in the frequency of latent phase, reactive treponemal tests, adequate treatment, and maternal education, and a reduction in partner treatment. During 2017-2019, there was a reduction in the use of non-treponemal tests; in 2020-2021, a decrease in Brown (Brazilian mixed race)/Black/Asian/Indigenous women; and in 2022-2023, an increase in prenatal care visits and late diagnoses.
CONCLUSION: The syphilis in pregnancy detection rate increased until 2018 and remained stable thereafter. Changes in clinical and epidemiological characteristics reflect variations in the care context, with advances in prenatal care, but persistence of weaknesses in the timely diagnosis and treatment of partners.

articles.title: Serological Evidence of Schmallenberg Virus Exposure in Ruminant Abortion Cases from Selected Regions of Iran: A Virus Neutralization Test-Based Study.
articles.authors: Kiani M, Moghaddam AA, Lotfi M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Schmallenberg virus (SBV), an emerging Orthobunyavirus, is associated with reproductive disorders in ruminants. Although SBV has spread from Europe into parts of Asia, epidemiological data from Iran remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate SBV exposure among ruminants from selected regions of Iran using the virus neutralization test (VNT).
METHODS: Serum samples from 92 ruminants (37 sheep and 55 cattle) with a history of abortion or SBV-compatible clinical signs were collected from three provinces in eastern (Sistan and Baluchestan), central (Qazvin), and western (East Azerbaijan) Iran. Sera were inactivated, serially diluted (1:5-1:640), and tested in quadruplicate by VNT on BHK-21 cells with a back-titrated SBV inoculum (125 TCID50/well).
RESULTS: Seventy of 92 samples (76.1%) were positive for SBV-neutralizing antibodies (≥1:10). Seropositivity was 87.5% (14/16), 64.1% (25/39), and 83.8% (31/37) in the eastern, central, and western regions, respectively. Mean VN50 titres varied descriptively, with the highest mean titre observed in the western region (60.47 ± 57.65), followed by the central (43.30 ± 56.65) and eastern (22.73 ± 13.72) regions. Although the Kruskal-Wallis test indicated an overall difference in antibody titres (p = 0.022), post hoc pairwise comparisons with Bonferroni correction did not identify statistically significant differences between any pair of regions. Therefore, regional variation should be considered exploratory and not be interpreted as evidence of confirmed geographical differences in SBV exposure.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides serological evidence of prior SBV exposure among ruminants. Seropositivity indicates prior exposure to SBV and does not establish a causal relationship between SBV infection and abortion. Although regional differences in mean antibody titres were observed descriptively, these patterns should be regarded as exploratory, as pairwise regional comparisons did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. Larger, population-based studies with balanced sample sizes are required to clarify the geographical patterns of SBV in Iran.

articles.title: Hyperoxia exposure disrupts alveolar development and cardiopulmonary transition in preterm pigs.
articles.authors: Doughty R, Offersen S, Thymann T et al.
articles.abstract: Aim Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) remains a major cause of chronic lung disease following preterm birth. We aimed to establish a normobaric hyperoxia-induced preterm pig model that reflects respiratory and cardiovascular consequences of BPD. Methods Preterm piglets (n=18) were delivered by caesarean section at gestational day 106 and exposed either to sustained hyperoxia (85% O₂) or ambient air for 94 hours. Data on echocardiography, pulmonary arterial pressure, and detailed lung and heart histopathology were collected. Results There was clear structural lung injury in hyperoxia-exposed piglets, with increased septal thickness, reduced alveolar density, higher mean linear intercepts and more alveolar necrosis (all p<0.05). Echocardiography revealed a higher prevalence of persistent ductus arteriosus (55.6% in BPD vs. 12.5% in controls; p=0.091). Histology showed right ventricular cardiomyocyte hyperplasia and hypertrophy in hyperoxia-exposed pigs, yet pulmonary arterial pressure was unaffected. Conclusion The preterm pig model recapitulates key physiological and structural hallmarks of "new BPD" and the broader chronic lung disease of prematurity. This model represents a promising platform for investigating mechanisms and interventions in preterm infants at risk of BPD.

articles.title: Second-line MRI after expert transvaginal ultrasound in selected patients with suspected complex deep endometriosis: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Rehal M, Brunes M, Suzuki C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The objective of this study was to evaluate the added diagnostic yield of second-line magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) after expert transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) for preoperative mapping of deep endometriosis (DE).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this prospective observational cohort study, women with suspected DE scheduled for surgery after expert ultrasound were included. TVS was performed according to the International Deep Endometriosis Analysis (IDEA) protocol. MRI was selectively performed as a second-line investigation in patients with suspected advanced disease, inconclusive TVS, or advanced symptoms despite negative TVS findings. Surgical visualization served as the primary reference standard, with histopathology used as a secondary reference standard when available. Diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, and Cohen's κ) was assessed for TVS, MRI, and their combination, and stratified by prior surgical status. For the combined approach, a positive result was defined as a positive finding on either modality (TVS or MRI), representing a rule-out strategy.
RESULTS: Among 221 women with suspected deep endometriosis, 189 underwent surgery, of whom 112 had both TVS and MRI; 55 had previous abdominal surgery. Combined imaging improved sensitivity for rectosigmoid DE (+10.3%; +6 true positives (TP), +3 false positives (FP)) and uterosacral ligament involvement (+29.2%; +14 TP, +12 FP) but reduced specificity for endometriomas (-19.0%; true negatives (TN) 18 to 14), obliteration of the pouch of Douglas (-13.3%; TN 14 to 8), and uterosacral ligaments (-20.3%; TN 35 to 23). Most lesions missed by TVS were in the mid or upper rectum. Accuracy for the urinary bladder and ureters decreased with the addition of MRI (82.2% to 75.7%). Sensitivity for rectosigmoid lesions was higher with the combined method (TVS + MRI) in women with prior surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Among selected complex patients undergoing second-line MRI after expert TVS, combined imaging increased detection of rectosigmoid and uterosacral ligament lesions, but at the cost of reduced specificity. The sensitivity for rectosigmoid disease was greatest among patients with prior abdominal surgery, although this subgroup finding should be considered exploratory. These findings are consistent with a selective rather than routine role for MRI after expert TVS.

articles.title: Non-cancer causes of death following cervical cancer diagnosis: a SEER database study.
articles.authors: Wang S, Ding J, Chen X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify non-cancer mortality after cervical cancer diagnosis and examine how these risks vary over time, by disease stage, race, and registry-recorded treatment patterns.
METHODS: We analyzed 65,852 women diagnosed with cervical cancer in Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-17 (2000-2021). Standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) compared observed deaths with age-, race-, sex-, and calendar-period-specific mortality in the U.S. general population. Fine-Gray models retained every death other than the target cause as a competing event.
RESULTS: Of 24,857 deaths, 19,975 (80.4%) were cancer-related and 4,882 (19.6%) were non-cancer-related. The overall non-cancer SMR was 1.65 (95% confidence interval [CI]=1.60-1.70). After International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage- and race-exact propensity score matching (4,506 pairs; maximum absolute standardized mean difference, 0.079), registry-inferred combined radiotherapy plus chemotherapy without surgery was not associated with overall non-cancer death (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR]=1.01; 95% CI=0.88-1.16); the infectious-disease (sHR=1.72; 95% CI=0.75-3.95) and septicemia estimates (sHR=1.60; 95% CI=0.69-3.72; 23 events) were imprecise. Among 31,617 patients surviving beyond 5 years, the conditional non-cancer SMR remained elevated (1.44; 95% CI=1.38-1.49).
CONCLUSION: Non-cancer mortality remains elevated among cervical cancer survivors, including beyond the 5-year landmark. Treatment-group contrasts are strongly affected by disease stage, treatment-selection mechanisms, and unmeasured clinical factors; they should therefore be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than causal. Survivorship care should integrate cardiovascular, infectious, renal, respiratory, and metabolic risk management.

articles.title: Impact of platinum-free interval on the efficacy of lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.
articles.authors: Hamada R, Seki T, Kono M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Following platinum-based therapy, recurrent endometrial cancer (EC) is treated with lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab (LP). The platinum re-administration response is predicted by the platinum-free interval (PFI), but the PFI and LP efficacy relationship remains unclear. We investigated the association between PFI and LP efficacy in patients receiving LP for recurrent EC.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 96 patients with recurrent EC treated with LP between December 2021 and March 2025 at our institutions. A PFI ≥6 months was defined as a longer PFI. The primary outcomes were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). PFI, mismatch repair (MMR) status, p53 status, International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) 2023 stage (I/II vs. III/IV), histological type (endometrioid vs. non-endometrioid), and number of prior treatment regimens (1 vs. ≥2) underwent multivariable Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: Of the 96 patients, 65 and 31 had PFI <6 months and ≥6 months, respectively. Molecular profiling identified 10 MMR-deficient tumors and 86 MMR-proficient tumors. Endometrioid histology, advanced FIGO stage (III/IV), and ≥2 previous treatment regimen proportions were 38.5% vs. 71.0%, 64.6% vs. 58.1%, and 24.6% vs. 32.3%, respectively, in the patients with shorter vs. longer PFI. Longer-PFI patients had significantly longer median PFS (7.5 vs. 14.2 months; p=0.025) and OS (21.7 vs. 32.9 months; p=0.003). Multivariable analysis determined that a longer PFI was independently associated with improved PFS (hazard ratio [HR]=0.54; 95% confidence interval [CI]=0.31-0.94; p=0.029) and OS (HR=0.37; 95% CI=0.17-0.81; p=0.012).
CONCLUSION: LP therapy following platinum-based chemotherapy was more effective in longer-PFI patients.

articles.title: Radical versus simple trachelectomy for fertility preservation in early-stage cervical cancer: a retrospective cohort study based on propensity score inverse probability of treatment weighting.
articles.authors: Wang W, Lin Z, Liu J
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare oncologic, perioperative, and reproductive outcomes between simple trachelectomy (ST) and radical trachelectomy (RT) in patients with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) 2018 stage IB1-IB2 cervical cancer.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study including FIGO 2018 stage IB1-IB2 cervical cancer patients with negative lymph nodes and margins who underwent RT or ST between January 2010 and December 2023. Propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to balance baseline covariates. Primary outcome was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary outcomes included operative time, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative hospitalization, antibiotic-therapy days, and postoperative laboratory changes, and pregnancy/obstetric outcomes among patients who intended to conceive.
RESULTS: Among 45 patients (RT, n=23; ST, n=22), measured covariate balance was substantially improved after weighting. Median follow-up was 47 months, with two recurrences in the ST group. No statistically significant difference in PFS was detected between groups after weighting (p=0.148). ST was associated with shorter operative time (p<0.001), less intraoperative blood loss (p<0.001), fewer antibiotic-therapy days (p<0.001), smaller increases in white blood cell count (p=0.036) and C-reactive protein (p<0.001), and less albumin decline (p=0.018). Among 15 patients with pregnancy intention, successful pregnancies were observed in 1/6 (16.7%) in the RT group and 3/9 (33.3%) in the ST group.
CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in PFS was detected between ST and RT in this limited cohort. ST was associated with lower perioperative burden, while reproductive findings were descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Larger prospective or multicenter studies with standardized selection criteria and fertility follow-up are needed, particularly for IB2 disease.

articles.title: From Dysbiosis to Malignancy: The Female Genital Tract Microbiome in Endometrial Cancer; Insights from a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Selim AMF, Ibrahim MMLG, Elbrolosy MSM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Emerging evidence suggests that alterations in the female genital tract microbiome may be associated with the development and progression of endometrial cancer (EC). Microbial dysbiosis may contribute to chronic inflammation, immune dysregulation, and metabolic disturbances within the endometrial microenvironment. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate alterations in the female genital tract microbiome in women with EC and to identify microbial patterns associated with benign, premalignant, and malignant endometrial conditions.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and Meta-analysis of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) recommendations. Ten eligible observational studies published between 2016 and 2026 were included, comprising 775 women: 329 with benign conditions, 121 with endometrial hyperplasia, and 325 with EC. Demographic, histopathological, anatomical sampling, and microbiological data were extracted and analyzed using Review Manager, SPSS version 23, and EPI-INFO. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Collaboration tool.
RESULTS: Women with EC were older than those with benign conditions (59.2 ± 5.3 vs. 52.7 ± 4.4 years) and had a higher mean body mass index (33.8 ± 3.8 vs. 27.5 ± 2.0 kg/m²). Endometrioid carcinoma was the predominant histological subtype, and most malignant cases were low-grade and early-stage tumors. EC was associated with significant alterations in the genital tract microbiome. Several commensal taxa, including Lactobacillus, Bacteroides, Prevotella, Staphylococcus, and Enterococcus, were decreased in malignant cases, whereas potentially pathogenic or infection-associated genera, particularly Stenotrophomonas, Streptococcus, and Porphyromonas, were increased (p < 0.001). The pooled analysis demonstrated a significant association between genital tract microbial dysbiosis and EC.
CONCLUSIONS: Female genital tract microbial dysbiosis is associated with EC, characterized particularly by depletion of potentially protective microorganisms and enrichment of potentially pathogenic or infection-associated taxa. These microbial alterations may have potential as adjunctive biomarkers for EC risk stratification and early detection. However, the available observational evidence does not establish a causal role of microbial dysbiosis or infection in…

articles.title: Clinical Utility of Doppler Ultrasonography in Preoperative Risk Stratification of Ovarian Masses: A Retrospective Multi-Centric Analysis.
articles.authors: Fahmy Selim AM, Habal AHAE, Badr AAM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiating benign from malignant ovarian lesions before surgery remains a significant clinical challenge. Reliable preoperative assessment is crucial for appropriate treatment planning and improving patient prognosis. Color Doppler ultrasonography, particularly through evaluation of the resistance index (RI), has gained attention as a non-invasive method for assessing tumor vascularity associated with malignancy.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the diagnostic performance of the resistance index measured by preoperative Doppler ultrasonography in distinguishing benign from malignant ovarian masses.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective study including 470 patients who underwent surgical exploration for adnexal masses at Al-Azhar University, Ain Shams University, Badya University and Zagazig University Hospitals between May 2020 and May 2025. Clinical parameters, sonographic findings, and final histopathological diagnoses were reviewed. Statistical analysis included logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis to determine the predictive accuracy of RI.
RESULTS: Malignant tumors exhibited significantly lower RI values compared to benign masses (mean 0.48±0.07). An optimal cutoff value of ≤0.54 yielded excellent discriminative ability, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.966. At this threshold, sensitivity reached 85.2% and specificity 91.6%, with an overall accuracy of 90.2%. Additional sonographic features, including the presence of papillary projections and septations, were strongly linked to malignancy, whereas simple cystic appearance with thin walls was associated with benign pathology.
CONCLUSIONS: The resistance index derived from Doppler ultrasonography represents a valuable and reliable parameter for preoperative characterization of ovarian masses. Its integration into routine imaging protocols may enhance early detection of malignancy and support more informed surgical decision-making.

articles.title: Cord blood betatrophin and insulin levels in term neonates born to mothers with gestational diabetes: A comparative cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Bharathi U, Kamath SP, Holla R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with altered fetal metabolic adaptation. Betatrophin has been implicated in glucose metabolism, but its role in pregnancies complicated by GDM remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate cord blood betatrophin and insulin levels and examine their relationship in term neonates born to mothers with and without GDM.
METHODS: This hospital-based comparative cross-sectional study was conducted over 18 months at a tertiary care maternity and neonatal hospital. Cord blood betatrophin and insulin levels were measured by ELISA in 150 term neonates born to mothers with GDM (n = 75) and normal glucose tolerance (n = 75). Biomarker levels were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test, and their association was assessed using Spearman's correlation. Univariate and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with betatrophin and insulin levels.
RESULTS: A total of 150 neonates (75 each in the GDM and non-GDM groups) were included. Median cord blood betatrophin levels (ng/mL) were significantly higher in neonates born to mothers with GDM than in those born to normoglycemic mothers [0.810 (IQR 0.583-1.005) vs. 0.526 (IQR 0.331-0.745) ng/mL, p < 0.001]. Similarly, median cord blood insulin levels (µIU/mL) were significantly higher in the GDM group than in the non-GDM group [12.8 (IQR 9.45-17.83) vs. 4.6 (IQR 3.66-7.10) µIU/mL, p < 0.001]. Cord blood betatrophin and insulin levels were positively correlated (r = 0.291, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, GDM remained independently associated with higher cord blood betatrophin (β = 0.35, 95% CI: 0.18-0.53, p = 0.045) and insulin levels (β = 10.21, 95% CI: 6.66-13.76, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Cord blood betatrophin and insulin levels were significantly elevated in neonates born to mothers with GDM. A modest but significant positive correlation between betatrophin and insulin levels suggests an association between betatrophin and fetal insulin metabolism.

articles.title: Pelvic insufficiency fractures after chemoradiotherapy for cervical cancer: incidence, long-term outcomes, and survivorship management.
articles.authors: Saad A, Goldstein J, Atamneh R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic insufficiency fractures, a late complication of chemoradiotherapy for cervical cancer, can cause pain and functional impairment. Although most studies have reported incidence rates and risk factors, few have examined clinical presentation, long-term symptom burden, or the impact on survivorship.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of patients with cervical cancer treated with chemoradiotherapy from 2018 to 2024. We extracted clinical characteristics, treatment details, dosimetric parameters, imaging studies documenting pelvic insufficiency fractures, and clinical outcomes from the electronic medical record. We used the Kaplan-Meier method to estimate the probability of pelvic insufficiency fractures and univariate Cox regression to assess clinical and dosimetric factors associated with their development.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 153 patients (median follow-up: 41.4 months). After chemoradiotherapy, 18 patients (11.8%) developed radiologically confirmed pelvic insufficiency fractures (median time to diagnosis: 9.5 months; probability of pelvic insufficiency fracture at 24 months: 11.4%). PET-CT and/or MRI showed that most pelvic insufficiency fractures involved the sacrum. No statistically significant clinical or dosimetric predictors of pelvic insufficiency fractures were identified. All symptomatic patients (n = 15, 83%) required referral to pain management services (median observed duration of symptoms: 37 months). No symptomatic patient achieved documented complete symptom resolution during the available follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Most pelvic insufficiency fractures presented with new-onset pelvic or sacral pain within 2 years of completing chemoradiotherapy. The lack of clinical or dosimetric predictors suggests a multifactorial etiology of fracture risk. Persistent pain, despite multimodal supportive care, led to long-term morbidity. These findings underscore the need for prospective studies to develop evidence-based preventive strategies, survivorship assessments, and management pathways.

articles.title: RNA-binding proteins in spermatogenesis: functional mechanisms, clinical potential, and future perspectives.
articles.authors: Xu DJ, Yang B, Xu WC et al.
articles.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) govern RNA splicing, stability, translation, and localization through RNA-recognition motifs, K-homology domains, and related structures, orchestrating spermatogonial stem cell (SSC) self-renewal, meiosis, and spermiogenesis. We present the stage-specific roles of key RBPs, such as deleted in azoospermia protein/deleted in azoospermia-like protein (DAZ/DAZL), nanos C2HC-type zinc finger 2 (NANOS2), P-element-induced wimpy testis protein (PIWI) family members, and tudor domain-containing 6 (TDRD6), and illustrate their molecular mechanisms in SSC maintenance, meiotic progression, and sperm morphogenesis. The review assesses RBP expression and modifications as diagnostic biomarkers for male infertility, evaluates RBP-targeted therapies, and notes translational obstacles. Emerging interdisciplinary approaches promise to decode spatiotemporal RBP networks and advance precision diagnosis and treatment of male reproductive disorders.

articles.title: Validation of the WID-CIN Methylation Test for Detection of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia Grade 3 or Worse in an Independent Cohort.
articles.authors: Ellis LB, Bowden SJ, Tighe J et al.
articles.abstract: Many cervical screening programmes rely on cytology for triage of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) positive women. However, cytological triage has variable and often limited sensitivity, and its availability can be restricted in resource-poor settings. The Women's cancer risk IDentification cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (WID-CIN) test is a DNA methylation test shown to have promising diagnostic accuracy as an alternative triage test. In this case-control study, women were recruited from colposcopy clinics in the UK and Greece. Cases were defined as women with histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia Grade 3 or cancer (CIN3+) (n = 128) and controls (n = 119) had histological and/or cytological evidence of normal cervix. The WID-CIN index's accuracy was assessed, and the quality of the index was appraised using a validated biomarker toolkit. The WID-CIN index achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.898 (95%: CI 0.860-0.936) for diagnosis of CIN3+ in all women (irrespective of hrHPV status). In hrHPV positive women only (N = 108), the AUC was 0.875 (95% CI: 0.793-0.956). In contrast to previous work, the WID-CIN maintained high levels of accuracy in women under 30 (N = 57), reporting an AUC of 0.857 (95% CI: 0.762-0.952). Consequently, the WID-CIN index appears to be a highly promising translational biomarker and may provide effective triage to colposcopy clinics. Further validation in large, prospective studies including screening populations and comparison to currently available methods including cytology remain essential next steps.

articles.title: Pre-Existing and Post-Cancer Major Cardiovascular Disease and Their Association With Mortality Outcomes Among Cancer Survivors in Australia.
articles.authors: Rahman MM, Bell K, Joshy G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As cancer survival improves, cardiovascular disease (CVD) has emerged as a major competing cause of death. However, population-level evidence on the burden of pre-existing and post-cancer CVD remains limited. This study aims to quantify pre-existing and post-cancer newly documented major CVD and their association with mortality outcomes among people with cancer.
METHODS: Major CVD was identified using linked hospital records among 344,336 adults registered with primary invasive cancer in the New South Wales Cancer Registry from 2006 to 2016. The cohort was followed up until 31 December 2021. Fine-Grey modelling estimated sub-distributional hazard ratios (sHR) for cancer and cardiovascular mortality, and Cox proportional hazard modelling estimated hazard ratio for mortality from any cause across 20 common cancers.
RESULTS: Overall, 18% (n = 62,675) of participants had pre-existing CVD within 5 years before cancer diagnosis, varying by age (3% for age < 50 vs. 40% for ≥ 80). Of those without pre-existing CVD (n = 281,661), 27% (n = 76,924) had post-cancer newly documented CVD, with the highest age-standardised incidence rates in pancreatic cancer (716 per 10,000 person-years), followed by lung (657). The median follow-up period was 6.8 years with an interquartile range: 2.1-10.3 The sHR of pre-existing CVD for cancer mortality ranged from 0.99 (95% CI: 0.85-1.13) in cancer of kidney to 1.81 (95% CI = 1.71-1.91) in lymphoma, and for cardiovascular mortality, 1.98 (1.78-2.18) in lymphoma to 4.74 (4.39-5.09) in pancreatic cancer. The sHR of post-cancer newly documented CVD for cancer mortality, ranging from 0.87 (95% CI: 0.69-1.05) in liver cancer to 2.33 (95% CI = 2.04-2.62) in cervical cancer and cardiovascular mortality, ranging from 1.45 (95% CI: 1.18-1.72) in myeloma to 3.39 (95% CI = 2.90-3.88) in liver cancer.
CONCLUSION: CVD is prevalent both before and after cancer diagnosis, with strong relations to increased cancer, cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Population-based strategies to strengthen holistic survivorship care and address key risk factors are essential to improve both cancer and cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Fetal Echocardiography After a Normal Anatomy Assessment: A Retrospective Cohort of In Vitro Fertilization Pregnancies.
articles.authors: Dickson B, Maher H, Maynard S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the detection rate of congenital heart disease (CHD) on fetal echocardiogram after a normal and complete detailed fetal ultrasound among pregnancies conceived by in vitro fertilization (IVF).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study examined singleton IVF pregnancies that underwent a detailed fetal anatomic survey without any identified abnormalities, followed by fetal echocardiogram. The primary outcome was the rate of CHD diagnosis after normal and complete anatomic ultrasound. Patients with multifetal gestation, pre-gestational diabetes, a known family history of CHD, fetal abnormalities on anatomy ultrasound, or patients who had an incomplete initial anatomy ultrasound were excluded. Prenatal CHD was confirmed with neonatal imaging and infants were followed after birth.
RESULTS: 300 pregnancies were included, and of these 266 had a normal and complete anatomy ultrasound. 1.5% (n = 4) of pregnancies had minor CHD identified on fetal echocardiography which was not identified on the anatomy ultrasound. None of the infants required cardiac-related interventions in the first year of life.
CONCLUSION: No major CHD was identified at fetal echocardiography after a normal and complete anatomic survey. Our results support the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine guidelines that state a dedicated fetal echocardiogram may be considered, but is not recommended, for singleton IVF pregnancies.

articles.title: Timing of Dexamethasone Administration for Gynecological Laparoscopy Under Enhanced Recovery After Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Tang J, Yuan J, Wang X
articles.abstract: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) remains a major barrier to implementing Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways in gynecological laparoscopy, while perioperative inflammation may delay postoperative recovery.
