The optimal timing of dexamethasone administration for PONV prophylaxis and attenuation of inflammatory responses remains uncertain. This retrospective cohort study enrolled 180 patients undergoing elective gynecological laparoscopy under standardized ERAS protocols who received 8 mg intravenous dexamethasone either 30 min before anesthesia induction or immediately after abdominal incision closure. The primary outcome was the 48-h incidence of PONV. Secondary outcomes included inflammatory biomarkers, namely C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), ERAS recovery indicators, and safety outcomes. Preoperative dexamethasone administration was associated with a significantly lower 48-h PONV incidence than postoperative administration (16.7% vs. 40.0%, P < 0.001), accompanied by reduced symptom severity and shorter episode duration. Patients receiving preoperative dexamethasone also demonstrated lower inflammatory biomarker levels at 24 and 48 h, faster achievement of postoperative recovery milestones, and a shorter hospital length of stay (2.1 vs. 3.2 days, P < 0.001), while safety outcomes were comparable between groups. These findings suggest that preoperative dexamethasone administration is associated with improved PONV control, attenuated perioperative inflammatory responses, and accelerated recovery in patients undergoing ERAS gynecological laparoscopy and may represent a useful strategy for optimizing perioperative care in this population.

articles.title: Genetic engineering in the Post Implantation Uterus using a 4-hydorxytamofen Regulated Cre Recombination.
articles.authors: Li S, DeMayo FJ
articles.abstract: The tamoxifen-inducible PgriCreERT2 mouse model enables temporal Cre recombination in progesterone receptor (Pgr)-expressing reproductive tissues. However, it remains unclear whether the PgriCreERT2 model can be safely activated during pregnancy, as tamoxifen exposure in pregnant mice can adversely affect pregnancy outcomes. Here, we established a 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT) dosing strategy for inducing Cre recombination after implantation using the PgriCreERT2 model. Pregnant females carrying PgriCreERT2 and a Cre-dependent Rosa26Sun1 reporter were administered a single dose of 4-OHT at gestational day (GD) 8.5. Dose-dependent effects on pregnancy and reporter recombination were evaluated using gross morphology, immunofluorescence, histology, placental and fetal measurements, gestation length, litter size, and resorption rate. A dose of 37.5 mg/kg produced robust SUN1 reporter activation in post-implantation uterine tissues while avoiding the overt adverse effects observed at the higher dose tested. Reporter-positive cells were detected predominantly in the uterus. Placental morphology, steroid hormone receptor (PGR and estrogen receptor alpha (ERα/ESR1)), placental development, and vascularization were preserved following treatment. These findings establish a practical 4-OHT induction regimen for temporally controlled recombination in the PgriCreERT2 model during post-implantation pregnancy and provide a methodological framework for studying uterine cell function during decidualization, placentation, and maternal-fetal development while reducing pregnancy-related confounding effects.

articles.title: Pelvic Ultrasonography for Idiopathic Central Precocious Puberty in Girls: A Retrospective Diagnostic and Temporal Validation Study.
articles.authors: Li R, Mei Q, Guo Y
articles.abstract: Idiopathic central precocious puberty (ICPP) and premature thelarche (PT) may initially present with similar breast development. We evaluated pelvic ultrasonography as an adjunctive discriminator and reassessed a multivariable prediction model. This retrospective, single-center study included a development cohort of 175 girls evaluated from August 2022 to December 2024 (90 ICPP and 85 PT) and a temporal validation cohort of 90 girls evaluated from January to December 2025 (48 ICPP and 42 PT). Diagnostic classification was based on clinical assessment and the gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulation test. Distribution-appropriate group tests were used, with Holm adjustment within prespecified families. In the development cohort, all uterine and ovarian measurements differed between groups after adjustment (all adjusted P<0.001). Uterine transverse diameter (UTD) and uterine volume (UV) had areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.830 and 0.829, respectively. At the Youden-derived UTD cutoff of 18.5-19.0 mm, sensitivity was 73.3%, and specificity was 78.8%. A model combining UTD and UV had an apparent AUC of 0.913 and a 10-fold cross-validated AUC of 0.910. The final logistic model included height, bone age, UV, and ovarian volume; its apparent development-cohort AUC was 0.951, and its bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC was 0.944. Applied without coefficient updating to the temporal cohort, the model yielded an AUC of 0.914, a Brier score of 0.121, a calibration intercept of 0.699, and a calibration slope of 0.754. Pelvic ultrasonography can complement, but not replace, auxologic, hormonal, and stimulation-test assessment. The thresholds and model require prospective multicenter external validation before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Clinician recommendations for effectively incorporating digital information into person-centered contraceptive counseling with adolescents.
articles.authors: Smith C, Pleasants E, Rebbeor S et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAdolescents frequently encounter contraceptive information of varying quality online, and many struggle to discern trustworthy claims given limited knowledge and prevalent misinformation. Clinicians often lack strategies to communicate effectively about online information-or patients' digital infospheres-in clinical encounters, impeding person-centered contraceptive counseling.ObjectiveSynthesize recommendations from adolescent-serving clinicians about how to effectively communicate about online information during contraceptive counseling.DesignSecondary analysis of qualitative data.MethodsWe conducted a hybrid inductive-deductive descriptive analysis of semi-structured interview data organized using the 3 Cs Framework for Addressing Health Misinformation and additional inductive codes.ResultsParticipating clinician experts in adolescent sexual and reproductive health (N=24) shared recommendations and suggested scripted language to promote the additional step of Curiosity as precursor to the existing 3 Cs of Compassionate understanding, Connection, and Collaboration.ConclusionThis guidance from expert clinicians can be used to improve person-centered counseling for adolescents in the digital age.

articles.title: Preconception paternal PFAS exposure in mice reprograms the placental epigenome.
articles.authors: Maxwell DL, Maxwell A, Nowak K et al.
articles.abstract: The placenta plays a vital role in supporting fetal growth and development by facilitating nutrient exchange, hormone signaling, and immune regulation. Environmental toxicants such as perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) can disrupt placental homeostasis, leading to increased risk of disease later in life. Paternal environmental exposures may influence offspring health by inducing epigenetic changes in sperm, which may affect sex-dependent placental programming. Here, male mice were exposed to a PFAS mixture (PFOS, PFOA, PFNA, PFHxS, GenX; 20 μg/l each) for 10 weeks and mated with unexposed females. We identified 6656 and 3242 differentially methylated regions (DMRs) in E12.5 placentas of female and male offspring, respectively. Female placentas showed predominantly hypermethylation (78.5%), whereas male placentas were mostly hypomethylated (62%). Gene ontology analyses linked female placental DMRs to cell and embryonic morphogenesis, and male DMRs to anatomical size regulation and hemostasis. Bulk RNA sequencing revealed 168 and 148 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in female and male placentas, respectively. Female DEGs were related to immune regulation, while male DEGs were involved in muscle and mesenchyme development. Sex-by-PFAS interaction models identified distinct methylation and transcription biological pathways. Overlap analysis between F0 sperm and F1 placentas identified 265 shared genes, including 289 female-specific and 124 male-specific genes. Paternal exposure to the PFAS mixture increased glycogen concentrations in male, but not female, placentas. No effects were observed at imprinted loci. These findings demonstrate that paternal preconception exposure to a PFAS mixture alter placental epigenomic and transcriptomic landscapes, which may contribute to sex-dependent trajectories of fetal health and development and offspring phenotypes.

articles.title: Mid-gestation aspirin withdrawal and its effects on maternal hemodynamics and uteroplacental Doppler: A post hoc analysis of the StopPRE trial.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Temprado J, Armengol-Alsina M, Garcia-Manau P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study assesses the effect of aspirin discontinuation at 24-28 weeks of gestation on longitudinal trajectories of mean arterial pressure (MAP) and uterine artery pulsatility index (UtAPI) in pregnant women at high risk of preterm preeclampsia with a normal angiogenic profile.
METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the multicenter StopPRE randomized trial including 936 women identified as high risk for preterm preeclampsia in the first trimester and treated with aspirin. At 24-28 weeks, participants with a normal soluble fms-like tyrosine-kinase 1/placental growth factor ratio (≤38) were randomized to either continue aspirin until 36 weeks (n = 463) or discontinue treatment (n = 473). Serial measurements of MAP and UtAPI were obtained until delivery. Longitudinal trajectories were compared between groups using linear mixed-effects models, including an interaction term between gestational age and treatment group.
RESULTS: A total of 2977 MAP and 2939 UtAPI measurements were analyzed. MAP increased and UtAPI decreased with advancing gestational age in both groups. There were no significant differences between continuation and discontinuation groups in the trajectories of MAP or UtAPI (group-time interaction P = 0.623 and P = 0.498, respectively). Results were consistent when values were expressed as multiples of the median and in sensitivity analyses restricted to women with ≥90% treatment adherence. No differences were observed when analyses were stratified by the development of preterm preeclampsia. A significant reduction in UtAPI percentiles was observed from the first trimester to mid-pregnancy.
CONCLUSION: Discontinuation of aspirin at 24-28 weeks of gestation in high-risk pregnancies with a normal angiogenic profile does not affect longitudinal trajectories of MAP or UtAPI. These findings provide indirect supportive evidence regarding the pharmacodynamic effects of aspirin withdrawal at mid-gestation and suggest that its beneficial effects on uteroplacental perfusion might occur earlier in pregnancy.

articles.title: Perinatal death and mode of delivery among term singleton breech births: A retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital in Ghana.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Ken-Amoah S, Ashong J, Anane-Fenin B et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify the burden of perinatal death and identify factors associated with perinatal death and with cesarean delivery among term singleton breech births at Cape Coast Teaching Hospital, Ghana.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included term singleton breech births with documented fetal cardiac activity at admission from 2015 to 2021; antepartum stillbirths were excluded. Multivariable logistic regression examined factors associated with perinatal death. Mixed-effects logistic regression, with a random intercept for delivery year, examined factors associated with cesarean delivery. Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) are reported.
RESULTS: Among 695 eligible births, 542 (78.0%) were by cesarean delivery. There were 41 perinatal deaths (5.9%; 59.0 per 1000 births), comprising 25 intrapartum stillbirths and 16 early neonatal deaths. Perinatal death occurred in 32 of 153 vaginal breech births (20.9%) and in nine of 542 cesarean deliveries (1.7%). These figures describe outcomes according to actual rather than intended mode of delivery and should not be interpreted causally or as a comparison of planned delivery strategies. Higher parity was associated with increased odds of perinatal death (aOR = 1.32, 95% CI = 1.04-1.68). Older maternal age was associated with higher odds of cesarean delivery (aOR = 1.04, 95% CI = 1.005-1.09), whereas higher parity was associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery (aOR = 0.72, 95% CI = 0.63-0.83).
CONCLUSION: The burden of perinatal death was substantial among term singleton breech births at this Ghanaian tertiary hospital. Most deaths were intrapartum stillbirths. Strengthening antenatal detection, timely referral, intrapartum care, operative readiness, neonatal care, and proficiency in emergency vaginal breech birth may improve outcomes.

articles.title: Intersecting pathways of postpartum depressive symptoms and recurrent binge eating after gestational diabetes: Findings from the LINDA-Brazil cohort.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Silvani J, Zajdenverg L, Appolinario JC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence and correlates of recurrent binge eating (RBE) and postpartum depression (PPD), and examine their association among women with prior gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).
METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis included 699 women with prior GDM who participated in the postpartum baseline assessment of the LINDA-Brazil study. RBE was defined as self-reported recurrent episodes of consuming large quantities of food within a discrete period, accompanied by a sense of lack of control during these episodes. PPD was measured using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), with a cutoff score ≥13. Sociodemographic, obstetric, behavioral, and nutritional characteristics were obtained by interview. Associations were examined using Poisson regression models with robust variance.
RESULTS: Among the 699 participants, 272 (38.9%) presented RBE, and 184 (26.3%) had PPD. At least one of the two outcomes was identified in 49.4% of participants, and 15.9% presented both. RBE was more prevalent among younger women and those with postpartum weight retention greater than 5 kg. PPD was associated with lower household income, current smoking, parity, weight-related factors, and poor sleep quality, whereas current breastfeeding was associated with a lower prevalence. In the primary analysis, women with RBE had a higher prevalence of PPD than women without RBE (prevalence ratio [PR], 2.17; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.63-2.88).
CONCLUSION: RBE and PPD were common and frequently co-occurred among women with recent GDM. Women with RBE had approximately twice the prevalence of PPD compared with those without RBE. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between these conditions.

articles.title: PDE8B rs4704397 Modifies the Association Between Iodine Status and Serum TSH in Pregnant Women.
articles.journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association
articles.authors: Yao C, Li Y, Li C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal thyroid function is essential for a healthy pregnancy, and elevated thyrotropin (TSH) is the hallmark of subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH). Previous studies have shown that both genetic factors, particularly the PDE8B rs4704397 polymorphism, and iodine intake influence TSH levels. However, whether iodine-related changes in TSH vary by genetic background remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between iodine status and TSH levels across different genetic backgrounds in early pregnancy.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the subclinical hypothyroid in early pregnancy (SHEP) prospective cohort, using a nested case-control design. The analysis included 728 pregnant women with SCH and 968 age- and body mass index-matched euthyroid controls. Participants were genotyped for PDE8B rs4704397 using matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time-of-flight mass spectrometry. The urinary iodine-to-creatinine ratio (UIC/Cr) was used to assess iodine status. Restricted cubic spline (RCS), linear, and logistic regression models were applied to evaluate the associations of UIC/Cr with TSH, free thyroxine (fT4), and SCH, stratified by PDE8B genotype.
RESULTS: The distribution of the AA genotype did not differ between case and control groups. In the overall population, the AA genotype accounted for 70% of participants. RCS analyses showed a positive linear association between UIC/Cr and serum TSH concentrations in both the overall population and individuals with the AA genotype, but not in those with the GA + GG genotypes. A nonlinear inverse association between UIC/Cr and fT4 levels was observed across all genotypes. Among individuals with the AA genotype, each standard deviation increase in UIC/Cr was associated with higher serum TSH levels (adjusted β = 0.16, confidence interval [CI]: 0.08-0.24) and an increased risk of SCH (OR = 1.22, CI: 1.08-1.39), but not among those with the GA + GG genotypes (p for genotype × UIC/Cr interaction = 0.09 for both outcomes). In contrast, fT4 levels decreased with increasing UIC/Cr across all genotypes (p for genotype × UIC/Cr interaction = 0.48).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher iodine status was associated with higher TSH levels and an increased risk of SCH only among pregnant women with the PDE8B rs4704397 AA genotype, suggesting that the effect of iodine on thyroid function is modified by genotype.

articles.title: Clinical Care Gaps in the Management of Multiple Sclerosis Among Obstetric and Gynecologic Clinicians.
articles.authors: Budge KL, Oladipo AF, Pandey K
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comprehensive management of multiple sclerosis (MS) requires a multispecialty approach. Routine health care must not be neglected but maintained in consideration of the complexity and variety of consequences of the disease process. This study assesses the confidence of obstetric and gynecological providers (OBGYNs) when caring for people with MS.
METHODS: OBGYNs, including doctors, physician assistants, and advanced nurse practitioners within Hackensack Meridian Health, completed a survey assessing their comfort level with and knowledge of how to care for patients with MS.
RESULTS: The survey was completed by 29.2% of eligible providers. Most reported that people with MS tend to have sexual and bladder dysfunction; contraceptive management does not change; and pregnancy influences the disease process. They were split regarding the risk of infertility in and the impact of menopause on people with MS. There were no statistically significant differences in the recommendations of providers of varying levels of experience on any topic.
CONCLUSIONS: Provider recommendations, regardless of their level of experience, highlight the gaps in the available literature, indicating a need for further research to guide clinical management. Dedicated education on existing guidelines for OBGYN care for people with MS is necessary to improve provider comfort.

articles.title: Correlation between BRCA mutational status and lymph node metastasis in advanced epithelial ovarian cancer: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Guan M, Wang X, Ma Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To clarify the association between breast cancer (BRCA) mutations and clinically relevant factors, with a particular focus on lymph node metastasis (LNM), in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC).
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included patients with histologically confirmed advanced EOC and known BRCA status. Comprehensive clinical, surgical, and pathological data were collected, and survival outcomes were obtained through follow-up. Associations between BRCA mutations and clinicopathological variables were analyzed using univariate and multivariate models. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression.
RESULTS: A total of 106 patients were included, of whom 34 (32.1%) harbored BRCA mutations. Univariate analysis demonstrated that BRCA-mutated patients had significantly higher rates of abdominopelvic LNM, distant LNM, cardiophrenic LNM, and distant metastasis, as well as more advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stages and higher baseline CA153 levels (≥ 100 U/ml). Multivariate analysis identified abdominopelvic LNM, distant LNM, and baseline CA153 ≥ 100 U/ml as independent correlates of BRCA mutation status (all P < 0.05). Furthermore, for OS, BRCA gene status and achievement of R0 resection were independent prognostic predictors for advanced EOC (both P < 0.05); for PFS, elevated HE4 (≥ 500 U/ml) was identified as an independent adverse prognostic factor (HR = 2.292, 95% CI [1.202-4.371], P = 0.012).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that patients with advanced EOC harboring BRCA mutations are more likely to develop both regional and distant LNM. Nevertheless, BRCA mutation status and complete cytoreductive surgery (R0 resection) are associated with favorable prognosis and prolonged survival. Therefore, routine BRCA genetic testing is strongly recommended for all patients with advanced EOC, particularly those presenting with LNM, to facilitate individualized treatment strategies and prognostic assessment.

articles.title: Sexual and Reproductive Health Knowledge, Attitudes, Practices and Associated Factors Among School-Going Adolescents in Conflict-Affected Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Ngaboyeka GA, Mugisho Snr A, Neven A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescents living in conflict-affected settings face major barriers to accessing sexual and reproductive health (SRH) information and services. Evidence on SRH knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) among adolescents in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains limited. This study assessed SRH KAP and identified factors associated with good SRH knowledge among school-going adolescents in North and South Kivu.
METHODS: A school-based cross-sectional study was conducted from April to July 2023 among 559 school-going adolescents from 28 secondary schools in seven health zones of North and South Kivu. Data were collected using a pre-tested structured questionnaire. Good SRH knowledge was defined as an overall knowledge score of ≥75%. Factors associated with good SRH knowledge were assessed using Poisson regression with robust variance, and adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) were estimated.
RESULTS: Overall, 559 participants were included and 50.5% were girls. After age recoding, mean age was 17.2 ± 1.3 years. Overall, 29.7% had ever had sexual intercourse, while 8.1% had ever used SRH services. High domain knowledge was recorded for 32.7% of the 379 participants with general genital-organ categories, 30.2% for HIV transmission, and 26.8% for contraceptive methods. In the adjusted analysis (n=550), high overall SRH knowledge was associated with South Kivu residence (aPR=6.94; 95% CI: 3.84-12.56; p<0.001), Internet information (aPR=1.53; 95% CI: 1.22-1.93; p<0.001), information from another doctor (aPR=1.64; 95% CI: 1.26-2.15; p<0.001), and information from the mother (aPR=1.56; 95% CI: 1.08-2.24; p=0.017). Household size was inversely associated with high knowledge (aPR=0.957 per additional person; 95% CI: 0.917-0.999; p=0.046). Age and school year were not significant after adjustment.
CONCLUSION: Adolescents in North and South Kivu showed substantial gaps in SRH knowledge, low utilization of SRH services, and several indicators of sexual vulnerability. Important differences in SRH knowledge were observed between the two provinces, with higher prevalence of good knowledge among adolescents in South Kivu. Strengthening comprehensive sexuality education and improving access to reliable, adolescent-friendly SRH information through schools, families, healthcare providers, digital platforms, and other appropriate communication channels may help address these gaps. Interventions should also consider…

articles.title: Maternal Mortality in Somalia: A Narrative Review of Burden, and Health System Challenges.
articles.authors: Dirie SA, Fiidow OA, Dirie AM et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal mortality remains a major public health challenge in Somalia and is among the highest globally despite recent progress. This narrative review aimed to synthesize evidence on the burden of maternal mortality and the health system challenges contributing to its persistence. A literature search was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, and relevant grey literature, including national surveys, policy documents, and reports from international organizations. The review found that maternal mortality in Somalia remains alarmingly high, accompanied by low utilization of antenatal care, skilled birth attendance, facility-based delivery, and postnatal care services. Financial constraints, geographic inequalities, insecurity, and socioeconomic disparities continue to limit access to maternal healthcare, particularly among rural and nomadic populations. Key health system challenges include inadequate healthcare financing, weak infrastructure, shortages of skilled health workers, limited implementation of the Essential Package of Health Services, and dependence on donor-supported services. Direct obstetric complications, including postpartum hemorrhage, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, sepsis, obstructed labor, and unsafe abortion, remain major contributors to maternal deaths. Maternal mortality in Somalia is driven by a combination of limited maternal healthcare utilization and persistent health system weaknesses. Strengthening primary healthcare, expanding access to skilled birth attendance and emergency obstetric care, improving referral systems, and addressing socioeconomic barriers are essential to reducing preventable maternal deaths and improving maternal health outcomes.

articles.title: Discrete time survival analysis machine learning models for IVF prognosis across multiple cycles.
articles.authors: Shao T, Ghinis A, Dancet E et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Can discrete time survival analysis machine learning (ML) methods provide reliable and accurate predictions of cumulative live birth rate (CLBR) for patients both at diagnosis (pre-treatment) and after the first cycle of treatment (post-treatment)?
SUMMARY ANSWER: We developed discrete time survival analysis ML models that provide personalized CLBR estimates of up to six complete IVF cycles with good discriminative performance, especially at the post-treatment phase.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: The first relevant prognostic models to estimate IVF cumulative success rate across multiple cycles have moderate performance, with C-statistics ranging from 0.7 to 0.73 for both pre-treatment and post-treatment models.
STUDY DESIGN SIZE DURATION: This retrospective, single-center study included a cohort of 1429 couples who started their IVF treatment at a tertiary center between January 2014 and April 2021 as the development dataset. An additional 613 couples who started treatment at the same center between April 2021 and December 2023 were used as the temporal validation dataset.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS SETTING METHODS: Predictive performance was assessed using the following metrics: prediction error (Brier score, scaled Brier score), time-dependent AUC (cumulative/dynamic AUC, mean AUC, and time-dependent precision-recall AUC), and calibration (mean calibration, calibration plot, and calibration slope). Both pre-treatment and post-treatment models predicted the cumulative live birth success rates of up to six complete IVF cycles. Various discrete time survival analysis methods were trained, evaluated, and compared with the baseline models. Discrete time survival analysis models include the ones embedded with a generalized linear model (Logit) and tree-based ensembles (Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART), random forests). The baseline models are the refitted/recalibrated pre-treatment and post-treatment McLernon models, considering factors available in our data.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: The discrete time survival analysis models, especially BART, performed better on our data than the baseline models especially at the post-treatment phase. Validation results showed moderate discriminative ability for the pre-treatment model, with a mean AUC 0.69 (95% CI: 0.65, 0.73) and a scaled integrated Brier score (IBS) of 0.13 (13% performance improvement over Kaplan-Meier estimates). For the post-treatment model, discriminative power was strong,…

articles.title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Recurrent Fetal Intracranial Hemorrhage and a Maternally Inherited COL4A1 Variant of Uncertain Significance: A Case Report With Maternal Reverse Phenotyping.
articles.authors: Shi W, Xu H, Pu C et al.
articles.abstract: A 33-year-old woman with two consecutive pregnancies affected by fetal left periventricular germinal matrix hemorrhage (Grade IV) and progressive ventriculomegaly underwent trio whole-exome sequencing. A heterozygous COL4A1 c.4249G>C (p.Gly1417Arg) variant, classified as a variant of uncertain significance, was identified in the fetus of the current pregnancy and found to be maternally inherited; concurrent copy-number analysis incidentally detected a maternal 17p12 microdeletion encompassing PMP22, which was not inherited by the fetus. Systematic reverse phenotyping of the mother revealed right corticospinal tract Wallerian degeneration, persistent microscopic hematuria, a renal cyst, and retinal arteriolar changes-a phenotype compatible with the COL4A1-associated spectrum, although molecular causality remains unproven. Following multidisciplinary review, the pregnancy was terminated at 29 weeks, primarily on the basis of the grave fetal prognosis, with early-onset preeclampsia contributing to the overall maternal risk assessment; the mother's post-termination course was uneventful, with resolution of hypertension and proteinuria. This case illustrates that recurrent anatomically congruent fetal intracranial hemorrhages may prompt maternal reverse phenotyping that identifies maternally inherited COL4A1 variants of uncertain significance, and underscores the need to distinguish phenotypic concordance from proven molecular causality in prenatal counseling.

articles.title: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on endometrial cancer diagnosis: a retrospective observational study.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
articles.authors: Freitas JS, Teixeira JC, Benetti-Pinto CL et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the prevalence of diagnostic hysteroscopies for endometrial cancer, the prevalence of endometrial cancer diagnoses, and the staging of endometrial cancer at the time of diagnosis before and during the COVID-19 pandemic.
METHODS: Retrospective observational study included 631 women who underwent diagnostic hysteroscopy at a tertiary hospital in Campinas. Medical records were analyzed from two periods: two years before the COVID-19 pandemic (2018 and 2019) and two years during the pandemic (2020 and 2021).
RESULTS: The frequency of hysteroscopies before the pandemic was 59.9%, compared to 40.1% during the pandemic. There were no significant differences in average age, body mass index, or cancer prevalence between the two periods. Among women who underwent hysteroscopy during the pandemic, a lower prevalence of comorbidities and postmenopausal status was observed (p = 0.029 and p = 0.004, respectively). During this period, the primary indication for hysteroscopy was abnormal uterine bleeding (p = 0.004).
CONCLUSION: The pandemic led to a reduction in the number of women with comorbidities undergoing hysteroscopy and an increase in indications due to abnormal bleeding. This scenario may suggest that women at higher risk of COVID-19 complications were less likely to seek medical care.

articles.title: DNA Methylation and Hydroxymethylation Quantification Using Vibrational Spectroscopy.
articles.authors: Fatayer R, Sammut SJ, Senthil Murugan G
articles.abstract: Global quantification of DNA cytosine modifications, including 5-methylcytosine (5-mC) and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5-hmC), is important for understanding cancer biology, though established methods require multistep workflows and costly instrumentation. Here, we show that attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy combined with regression modeling enables rapid, label-free, and nondestructive quantification of both modifications from DNA samples. Using Adenomatous Polyposis Coli (APC) promoter DNA standards spanning 0-100% modification, we identified modification-sensitive spectral features and observed that 5-hmC produces greater spectral changes than 5-mC. A univariate peak-ratio approach yielded strong linearity for both modifications (R 2 = 0.97), while partial least-squares regression (PLSR) improved quantification accuracy to R 2 = 0.99 (RMSE = 2.6%) for 5-hmC and R 2 = 0.97 (RMSE = 5.7%) for 5-mC. In composite mixtures containing all three cytosine states, 5-hmC remained highly quantifiable (R 2 = 0.97; RMSE = 5.1%), while 5-mC accuracy decreased (R 2 = 0.90; RMSE = 9.6%), consistent with the greater spectral distinctiveness secondary to the hydroxymethyl group. Transferability was assessed using circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), short cell-free DNA fragments shed from tumor cells into the bloodstream, comprising multiplexed reference material spanning seven genomic regions and a polydisperse fragment-length distribution (155-220 bp). After domain adaptation between synthetic and ctDNA spectra, we obtained a quantitative methylation calibration with R 2 = 0.98 and RMSE = 5.2% under cross-validation. These results support ATR-FTIR spectroscopy as a viable platform for global cytosine modification quantification and establish proof-of-concept applicability to ctDNA analysis.

articles.title: Ensuring Safe and Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging: Pitfalls and Practical Solutions through the Lens of Obstetric Ultrasound.
articles.journal: The Indian journal of radiology & imaging
articles.authors: Chanian R, Thiruvengadam R, Desiraju BK
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied to obstetric and gynecologic ultrasound at a rapid pace. Current applications fall broadly into four categories. Assistive tools support image acquisition and standardization; diagnostic tools are used to detect existing conditions such as anomalies; predictive tools attempt to estimate the probability of adverse pregnancy outcomes such as preterm birth, preeclampsia and stillbirth; and finally, prognostic tools attempt to forecast longer-term clinical trajectories. The first two categories are verifiable at the point of care by a trained sonographer. The last two are not, and this is where most methodological shortcomings arise. In this review, we describe frequent challenges and shortcomings seen in published predictive AI work in maternal and child health imaging. These include amplification of existing inequalities and bias from retrospective data, data leakage, inflated performance from poor external validation, and the confusion of statistical prediction with clinical diagnosis. We then discuss practical solutions including appropriate study design, structured data collection purpose-built for model development, context-specific metrics such as sensitivity and screen-positive rate, and external validation in multiple independent cohorts. We highlight automated gestational age estimation from ultrasound images as an example of how AI can genuinely advance clinical practice when built on prospective data and evaluated rigorously. Although we use maternal and child health imaging as the illustrative context throughout this review, the principles we describe are not specific to this domain and apply to the development and evaluation of any AI application in health care.

articles.title: Short-course letrozole restores fertility in aged azoospermic dogs.
articles.authors: Liu B, Zhang L, Zhu F et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Age-related azoospermia is a clinically important cause of male infertility in dogs, yet effective pharmacological treatments for aged males remain limited. Whether transient aromatase inhibition can restore fertility in aged azoospermic dogs without prolonged exposure is unclear.
METHODS: This study evaluated whether a 1-week course of letrozole, an aromatase inhibitor, could restore spermatogenesis and fertility in aged azoospermic male dogs. Untreated aged azoospermic and young fertile dogs served as comparison groups, and a separate cohort of five aged dogs received 3 months of letrozole for safety assessment. Serum testosterone, semen parameters, testicular histology, fertilization-related transcripts, spermatogonia, seminal plasma metabolites, and serum biochemical markers of liver, kidney, and bone metabolism were assessed before and after treatment over a 6-month follow-up.
RESULTS: Serum testosterone increased within 1 week and peaked at approximately 2 weeks. Spermatozoa reappeared in ejaculates approximately 3 months after treatment and persisted for more than 6 months; treated males subsequently achieved pregnancies with healthy offspring, although litter size remained smaller than that of young fertile dogs. Compared with 3-month administration, 1-week treatment was not associated with detectable changes in serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP).
DISCUSSION: These findings indicate that a 1-week letrozole course can restore spermatogenesis and fertility in aged azoospermic dogs, supporting its further evaluation as a low-exposure therapeutic strategy; larger, breed-stratified studies with extended safety profiling are recommended before clinical adoption.

articles.title: Access to Genetic Testing in Patients With Suspected Genetic Kidney Disease in Europe.
articles.authors: Gosselink ME, Buining F, König J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A genetic diagnosis can transform care for patients with monogenic kidney disease-guiding treatment, prognosis, family-planning, and care for relatives. Despite technological advancements, nephrologists still experience barriers to implementing diagnostic genetic testing in daily practice.
METHODS: We surveyed 240 pediatric nephrologists, adult nephrologists, and clinical geneticists across 39 European countries on the accessibility of and barriers to genetic testing for suspected genetic kidney disease. Using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) model, we assessed barriers at national, hospital, individual, and implementation-process levels. Results were stratified by region (North, East, South, West Europe, and non-Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries). Binary logistic regression identified factors associated with barrier experience.
RESULTS: Overall, 97% regarded genetic testing an important tool to improve care, yet 50% experienced barriers in daily practice. Median barrier severity score was 4.0 (interquartile range [IQR] 4, scale 1-10). Non-OECD countries showed higher scores (6.8 (IQR 3.6), P < 0.001). Most reported national-level barriers were lacking clear professional guidelines and concerns about posttest insurability. Hospital-level barriers included insufficient clinic's resources (costs, time, technical facilities, and staffing), missing protocols for eligible patients or workflow and turnaround time (nonurgent: 12 weeks [IQR 12], urgent: 3 weeks [IQR 2]). Ranking barriers by region revealed a gradient from fewest barriers in Northern Europe, followed by West, South, East, and most in non-OECD countries. Lack of external funding and non-OECD origin were associated with barriers.
CONCLUSION: We identified barriers that must be addressed at a European level and within regions. We provide recommendations to promote equitable care for patients with suspected hereditary kidney disease in Europe.

articles.title: Development of an educational video on family planning for migrant women: a qualitative participatory co-design study in Northern Morocco.
articles.authors: Khalis M, Bouaddi O, Hamidi M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Migrant populations often face poorer sexual and reproductive health outcomes, including limited uptake of contraception. Morocco has become a country of transit and destination for thousands of sub-Saharan African (SSA) migrant women. Although these women are entitled to free contraception, they encounter informational barriers such as lack of knowledge about contraceptive options and limited access to trusted and culturally fit sources of information. Drawing on participatory research and design thinking approaches, this study aimed to co-design interventions to address informational barriers limiting family planning awareness and contraceptive use among SSA migrant women in Morocco.
METHODS: This participatory co-design study engaged 13 French-speaking SSA migrant women aged 18-49, recruited through a local non-governmental organisation (NGO) in Tangier, Morocco. A 1-day co-design workshop was conducted using the five-stage Design Thinking model: empathise, define, ideate, prototype and test. Participants used visual and interactive tools to propose, prioritise and shape educational interventions. The workshop session and post-feedback interviews were recorded, transcribed and analysed using rapid thematic analysis to identify intervention categories and themes.
RESULTS: Participants identified four approaches to address information gaps: culturally adapted educational materials, engagement of health professionals or community actors for direct counselling, outreach educational activities and embedding educational activities with vocational training or direct support activities (eg, provision of food items). They prioritised the first approach based on its feasibility, potential reach, sustainability and ability to directly engage users. Participants co-designed a short-animated video which was prototyped. The video included tailored content on contraceptive methods, information on entitlements to free services and pathways to family planning services. Design features were chosen such as relatable voiceover, skin tone representation, language and a preferred colour palette, in addition to preferred dissemination channels.
CONCLUSIONS: This study shows that co-design is a feasible and meaningful method for developing culturally relevant educational interventions on contraception for migrant women. The next phase will focus on refining, implementing and testing the educational intervention, incorporating user feedback. There is also…

articles.title: Does the use of hormonal contraceptives induce negative metacognitions, brooding, and depressive symptoms in an adolescent community sample?
articles.authors: Kennair LEO, Stavang M, Grønnæss I et al.
articles.abstract: In western countries women are much more likely to suffer from depression than men are. Some reports have suggested that there is an increased risk of depression diagnoses in young women who start using hormonal contraception. Using an established approach to quantifying levels effective dosages of estradiol, progestins, and androgens in specific brands and types of hormonal contraception, we address a) whether hormonal contraception use in general is associated with depressive symptoms, and b) which contraceptive hormonal effects are associated with depressive symptoms as measured with the Beck Depression Inventory, brooding and negative metacognitions about rumination in a community sample of 757 young women (age 16-19). We also consider associations with age and relationship status. We detected no overall effect of hormonal contraception on depressive symptoms. We furthermore detected no effects of specific hormonal dosages on any of the three outcome measures depressive symptoms, brooding or negative metacognitions. The results are discussed in light of previous robust but limited findings of an association and the possibility that health care system contact increases likelihood of more health care services, rather than robust causal effects of hormones.

articles.title: Understanding the interplay between cognitive changes at menopause, the workplace, and mental health: qualitative findings from the MARIE-UK (WP2a) project.
articles.authors: Hinchliff S, Potočnik K, Delanerolle G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive changes are widely experienced during the menopause transition and, when severe, can disrupt women's working lives and negatively impact their mental health. While prior research has documented the detrimental effect of menopausal symptoms on women's quality of life, there remains a paucity of empirical evidence specifically exploring the intersection between cognitive changes and identity reconstruction within occupational settings. The objective of this study was to understand women's experiences of cognitive changes at work during menopause, including how they navigate these difficulties.
METHODS: This qualitative, exploratory study, involved in-depth interviews with 50 women aged 43-67 years (mean 52.3) recruited for the MARIE-UK (WP2a) project. Data were analysed using collaborative reflexive thematic analysis, through the lens of Conservation of Resources (COR) theory. Data trustworthiness was ensured through investigator consensus.
RESULTS: The majority of participants experienced cognitive changes at menopause, such as brain fog and memory problems, which negatively impacted their mental health at work. Participants experienced loss of confidence in their abilities, an increase in anxiety, and a change in their sense of self. Due to the depletion of valuable resources (resources are anything an individual values), they struggled to regain a semblance of normality. Those who received workplace support managed to break the spiral of resource loss and better cope with the detrimental effects of the symptoms.
CONCLUSION: Understanding women's experiences of cognitive changes and mental health in the workplace through the COR theory has shown that menopause is a demand that can significantly deplete women's valuable resources to perform their work duties. Menopausal cognitive changes profoundly disrupted their sense of self and perceived ability to work effectively. The intersection of cognitive and psychological symptoms with workplace stressors exacerbated mental health burdens and perpetuated gender inequalities. Interventions to support workplace wellbeing are required, particularly as the proportion of menopausal women in paid employment increases.

articles.title: Preconceptional Risk Factors Associated With Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Case-Control Study.
articles.authors: Swain D, T P, Mishra T et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a major endocrine problem complicating pregnancy worldwide, and pregnancies complicated by GDM are associated with adverse birth outcomes. This study aimed to identify preconceptional risk factors and birth outcomes associated with GDM.
METHODOLOGY: A hospital-based case-control study was conducted among antenatal mothers seeking routine antenatal care at selected maternity hospitals in Khurdha district, Odisha, India. The study comprised 143 women with GDM and 143 gestational age-matched controls. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and interviews. Data were entered and analyzed using SPSS, version 21 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY).
RESULTS: The point prevalence of GDM in the study population was 9.9%. The preconceptional risk factors, such as preconception body mass index (BMI) (odds ratio (OR) = 3.01, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.78-5.09, P < 0.001), sedentary lifestyle (OR = 2.79, 95% CI: 1.33-5.88, P = 0.00), previous history of diabetes (OR = 3.72, 95% CI: 1.33-10.39, P = 0.00), family history of diabetes (OR = 1.94, 95% CI: 1.16-3.24, P = 0.01), and domestic violence (OR = 2.14, 95% CI: 1.13-4.06, P = 0.02) had significantly higher odds of developing GDM compared with non-GDM women. In relation to the obstetrical risk factors, early age at menarche (≤12 years) (OR = 2.79, 95% CI: 1.72-4.54, P < 0.001), previous history of GDM (OR = 2.42, 95% CI: 1.06-5.52, P = 0.03), primipara mothers (OR = 2.21, 95% CI: 1.38-3.56, P = 0.001), previous history of macrosomia (OR = 16.6, 95% CI: 2.16-127.76, P < 0.001), history of preterm delivery (OR = 2.78, 95% CI: 1.35-5.69, P = 0.004), and history of using steroid medications (OR = 2.42, 95% CI: 1.06-5.52, P = 0.03) increased the likelihood of developing GDM in the subsequent pregnancy. Furthermore, GDM was significantly associated with antepartum depression and adverse intrapartum and neonatal outcomes. Women with GDM had significantly higher odds of developing maternal depression (OR = 2.55, 95% CI: 1.45-4.50, P = 0.001), cesarean delivery (OR = 2.92, 95% CI: 1.79-4.76, P < 0.001), and preterm delivery (OR = 1.94, 95% CI: 1.19-3.15, P = 0.00), and the need for induction of labor was significantly higher among women with GDM (OR = 4.11, 95% CI: 2.47-6.85, P < 0.001) compared with non-GDM women. With respect to neonatal outcomes, mothers with GDM had significantly higher odds of developing neonatal hyperbilirubinemia (OR = 7.05, 95% CI: 1.56-31.84,…

articles.title: Evaluation of a Microhaplotype Marker Panel for Post-Transplant Chimerism Analysis.
articles.journal: Transfusion medicine and hemotherapy : offizielles Organ der Deutschen Gesellschaft fur Transfusionsmedizin und Immunhamatologie
articles.authors: Lang C, Rink G, Lodder L et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Microhaplotypes (MHs) are highly informative genetic markers suitable for forensic and clinical applications, including post-transplant monitoring in liquid biopsy. The aim of this study was to establish and evaluate a highly informative MH marker panel suitable for both chimerism analysis after allogeneic stem cell transplantation and for monitoring organ transplants using cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Two sequencing platforms (Illumina MiSeq and Oxford Nanopore Technologies [ONT]) were compared with regard to their suitability for reliable MH genotyping.
METHODS: Based on 98 candidates selected from the literature, a panel of 74 MH markers was developed and sequenced in 960 anonymized samples of healthy blood donors. Amplification was performed from genomic DNA in two multiplex PCRs generating short amplicons (95-150 bp). Library preparation and sequencing were carried out on the Illumina MiSeq platform (2 × 150 bp) and the ONT MinION (R10.4.1 flow cells). Bioinformatic analysis included quality filtering, read mapping (Bowtie2 and Minimap2), haplotype determination, and calculation of population genetic parameters such as polymorphism information content (PIC), power of discrimination (PD), expected heterozygosity (He), effective number of alleles (Ae), and Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
RESULTS: Evaluation of the sequencing results from 960 samples led to the exclusion of 20 MH markers due to low coverage or nonspecific amplifications. The remaining 54 MH loci were located on 22 chromosomes and comprised a total of 202 single nucleotide variations (SNVs). A balanced allele coverage ratio (>0.6) was observed for 43 loci. In total, 358 different alleles were identified, with most markers exhibiting between four and seven alleles. The PD exceeded 0.6 in 52 loci (mean 0.87), and most markers demonstrated high PIC and He values, indicating substantial genetic variability. Platform comparison revealed that ONT sequencing generated higher absolute read numbers, whereas Illumina sequencing achieved higher relative mapping efficiency and base accuracy. The proportion of uniquely mapped reads was comparable between the platforms. Additionally, previously undescribed SNVs were identified in 23 loci, potentially, further increasing haplotype diversity.
CONCLUSION: The marker panel with 54 MHs demonstrated high genetic diversity and discriminatory power in the studied population. With the small amplicon size the MH marker panel could also be suitable for…

articles.title: Early Metformin for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Does Not Alter Exclusive Breastfeeding at 12 Weeks: Secondary Analysis of the EMERGE Randomized Trial.
articles.authors: Devane D, Fitzgerald M, O'Donnell M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether initiating metformin at 25 weeks' gestation influences exclusive breastfeeding at 12 weeks postpartum in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We performed a prespecified secondary analysis of the Effectiveness of Metformin in Addition to Usual Care in the Reduction of Gestational Diabetes Effects (EMERGE) trial, a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized study. A total of 535 pregnant women (510 with newly diagnosed GDM) were allocated 1:1 to metformin (titrated to 2.5 g/day) or placebo alongside usual care. Infant feeding was prospectively documented at birth and at 4 and 12 weeks postpartum. The primary outcome was exclusive breastfeeding at 12 weeks (intention to treat). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for race, education, smoking, booking BMI, health care access markers, and diagnostic oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) glucose levels.
RESULTS: Twelve-week feeding data were available for 476 pregnancies (236 in the metformin group and 240 in the placebo group). Exclusive breastfeeding at 12 weeks was 27% with metformin and 26% with placebo (absolute difference +1.3%; 95% CI -6.3 to 8.7; P = 0.75). The adjusted odds ratio (OR) for metformin versus placebo was 1.24 (95% CI 0.79-1.96; P = 0.36). Feeding patterns shifted from breastfeeding to formula temporally in both groups (P < 0.001), with no treatment-by-time interaction (P = 0.61). Non-Caucasian ethnicity independently predicted exclusive breastfeeding (adjusted OR 2.37; 95% CI 1.27-4.42).
CONCLUSIONS: Starting metformin treatment at 25 weeks in the GDM group was not associated with differences in exclusive breastfeeding at 12 weeks postpartum. Where metformin was discontinued at delivery, the results support compatibility of antenatal metformin with breastfeeding objectives. Breastfeeding outcomes were more linked to sociodemographic factors than metabolic ones, highlighting the need for culturally appropriate postpartum support.

articles.title: Menopausal symptoms, sexual function, and psychological well-being in women across the menopausal transition.
articles.authors: Brenk-Franz K, Petersen M, Strauß B
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sexual health is an important yet often underrecognized aspect of menopausal health. Previous findings on female sexual dysfunction across menopausal stages remain heterogeneous. This study investigated female sexual function across premenopausal, perimenopausal, and postmenopausal stages and examined its associations with menopause-related symptoms and psychological well-being.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online study included 539 women aged ≥35 years. Menopausal stages were classified using self-reported menstrual characteristics based on principal STRAW+10 criteria. Menopausal symptoms, sexual function, and psychological well-being were assessed using the Menopause Rating Scale (MRS), Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), and WHO-5 Well-Being Index, respectively. Stage differences were examined using ANOVAs and chi-square tests. Multivariate associations with FSFI domains were assessed using a general linear model including age, menopausal symptoms, and psychological well-being.
RESULTS: Mean FSFI total scores were below the screening cut-off of 26.55 across all menopausal stages. Overall, 63.4% of participants scored at or below this threshold, indicating possible sexual dysfunction. Perimenopausal women reported the highest overall menopausal symptom burden and lowest psychological well-being. Postmenopausal women reported significantly lower sexual desire and lubrication than premenopausal women, while FSFI total scores did not differ significantly across stages. Urogenital symptom burden showed the strongest multivariate association with sexual functioning across FSFI domains.
CONCLUSIONS: Reduced sexual functioning was common across all menopausal stages, but stage-specific differences in individual sexual-function domains should be interpreted cautiously. Perimenopause appeared particularly vulnerable due to elevated symptom burden and reduced well-being. Sexual health and potentially menopausal symptoms should be addressed proactively within holistic menopause-related healthcare.

articles.title: The prospects and challenges of the use of cell-free DNA as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for oral cancer in Sub-Saharan Africa.
articles.authors: Bolfrey DA, Temilola DO, Boamah MO et al.
articles.abstract: Oral cancer (OC) represents a group of malignant disorders which affect the oral cavity structures. The majority of oral cancer patients present with oral squamous cell cancer (90%) which is an epithelial-derived malignancy of oral tissues. OC is considered a public health disease of concern in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) due to the rise in the morbidity and mortality associated with this disease. This increase in disease-associated morbidity and mortality has been attributed to factors such as delayed presentation, late diagnosis of the disease, inadequate/poor state of health infrastructure, genetic factors, social practices and poverty. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has emerged as a viable liquid biopsy-based technology that can be explored and harnessed for early diagnosis, treatment and monitoring of progress OC disease in SSA due to its minimal invasiveness and the ability to repeat the test without surgical invasion of the primary tumour. However, the differences in genetic, demographic, environmental and socioeconomic features between the SSA population and that of advanced countries, where most of the available liquid biopsy (LB) studies in the management of OC were done, need to be given the needed consideration prior to application of cfDNA technology in an African population. Also, the lack of standardised technique and databases on OC would require a multicentre SSA studies to contribute information to create a data panel for investigating OC in SSA population. This review article examines the promising application of circulating cfDNA in blood and saliva of OC patients with a focus on African studies. This article also examines the challenges and future opportunities in the use of cfDNA technology in the management of OC in SSA. The understanding of the application of cfDNA technology in the diagnosis and prognosis of OC will be vital for efficient and effective management of the disease entity in the SSA population.

articles.title: Metabolic-inflammatory heterogeneity in PCOS assisted reproduction: a compartmental susceptibility model.
articles.authors: Yuying L
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a heterogeneous endocrine-metabolic disorder rather than a uniform reproductive diagnosis. Women entering assisted reproductive technology (ART) differ in adiposity, insulin sensitivity, lipid metabolism, androgen excess, inflammatory activity, and oxidative stress, but these systemic traits do not map uniformly onto the follicular or endometrial compartments. We propose a testable compartmental susceptibility model in which systemic metabolic-inflammatory burden acts as a background exposure and clinically relevant effects emerge when stage-specific follicular-oocyte or endometrial-maternal vulnerability is also present. Evidence was interpreted with a pragmatic hierarchy that separates guideline/RCT evidence, registry and externally validated prognostic evidence, adjusted observational associations, mechanistic discovery studies, and protocol-only evidence. Current data support metabolic assessment, prevention of excessive ovarian response, and maternal risk surveillance, but they do not validate a metabolic-inflammatory subtype for selecting stimulation, trigger, frozen-embryo-transfer preparation, immune adjuncts, or other phenotype-specific treatment. Local immune, extracellular-vesicle, and multi-omics signals remain discovery tools rather than clinical tests. Precision ART in PCOS will require paired systemic-local phenotyping, external validation, and prospective phenotype-by-treatment interaction studies using cumulative live birth and maternal-neonatal safety as primary endpoints.

articles.title: Strategies for the detection and prevention of human cytomegalovirus from pregnancy to the neonatal period.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: Hu P, Chen W, Zhou Y et al.
articles.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is a major cause of congenital infection worldwide. Maternal infection with HCMV during pregnancy may lead to adverse fetal outcomes and long-term sequelae of congenital infection. In this review, we summarized three specimen sources, their corresponding valid indicators, and mainstream detection methods. Prevention strategies administered based on the results of these tests aim to reduce the risks of maternal infection and maternal-fetal transmission and the development of complications following congenital infection through behavioral and hygiene-related interventions, vaccination, and hyperimmune globulin and antiviral agent administration. In this review, we presented a flowchart for full-process HCMV infection management, which covers three levels of prevention nodes, confirmatory tests at each level, and corresponding interventional approaches. Future efforts require support from the funding, institutional, and educational sectors to accelerate the development of sensitive and inexpensive methods for the rapid identification of potential biomarkers.

articles.title: Identifying Drug-Induced Metabolic Signatures in Comparative Untargeted NMR Metabolomics Using Difference Spectra.
articles.authors: Di Paco G, Ghini V, Mannelli M et al.
articles.abstract: Untargeted NMR-based metabolomics is widely applied to investigate drug-induced metabolic alterations. However, comparative analyses across different biological models are often limited by dominant baseline variability arising from intrinsic metabolic differences and distinct culture conditions. This variability may obscure treatment-related signatures and compromise both multivariate and univariate statistical analyses. Here, we propose a data-processing strategy based on difference spectra as input for statistical modeling. For each treatment condition, difference spectra are first calculated by subtracting each paired control binned spectrum from its corresponding treated binned spectrum. These replicate-level binned difference spectra are then averaged to reduce intersample variability while enhancing the detection of treatment-induced metabolic changes within an untargeted framework. The strategy was validated by testing four structurally diverse gold(I) compounds in two ovarian cancer cell lines characterized by significant differences in basal metabolism and grown in distinct media. While conventional multivariate analysis of individual spectra failed to extract shared drug-related signatures, the difference-spectra approach enabled the identification of conserved metabolic perturbations. Altered pathways across cell models were then evaluated based on univariate analysis. Overall, the proposed method provides a robust and broadly applicable analytical tool for comparative untargeted metabolomics, facilitating the identification of common metabolic fingerprints despite substantial baseline heterogeneity.

articles.title: Factors associated with HIV seropositivity among HIV-exposed infants enrolled in the prevention of mother-to-child transmission program in Mara Region, Tanzania: a mixed-methods study.
articles.authors: Mollel C, Lakati A, Njau B et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HIV remains a persistent public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, including Tanzania. Despite the scale-up of Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission (PMTCT) programs, HIV seropositivity among HIV-exposed infants (HEIs) continues to occur, reflecting gaps in service delivery, maternal adherence, and health system performance. This study aimed to determine factors associated with HIV serostatus among HEIs enrolled in PMTCT in Mara Region, Tanzania.
METHODS: a retrospective cross-sectional study with mixed methods was employed. Quantitative data were extracted from medical records of 253 mother-baby pairs enrolled in PMTCT at four health facilities in Mara Region (January 2021-January 2025). Descriptive statistics and logistic regression were conducted using SPSS. Qualitative data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 healthcare providers and 10 caregivers. Thematic analysis was performed to explore contextual barriers and facilitators influencing PMTCT outcomes.
RESULTS: overall, 21/253 (8.3%) HEIs were HIV-positive. Detectable maternal viral load (AOR=3.12, 95% CI: 1.18-8.25, p=0.022), mixed feeding (AOR=6.45, 95% CI: 1.82-22.84, p=0.004), and poor follow-up adherence (AOR=5.24, 95% CI: 1.12-24.45, p=0.035) were significant predictors. Qualitative findings revealed fear of stigma, mixed feeding due to work pressures, and weak tracking systems as primary barriers.
TCONCLUSION: the 8.3% transmission rate exceeds the UNAIDS target of 4%. Findings underscore that biological factors and behavioural adherence drive transmission. Interventions must prioritise maternal viral suppression, enforce exclusive breastfeeding, and enhance retention in the PMTCT cascade.

articles.title: Postpartum diagnosis of pheochromocytoma presenting as atypical hypertensive disorder of pregnancy: A case report.
articles.authors: Sharma L, Khoo B, Williams D et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pheochromocytoma, a catecholamine-secreting adrenal tumour, is a rare but important cause of hypertension in pregnancy. Its symptoms may mimic more common disorders of pregnancy, making diagnosis challenging. We present a postpartum pheochromocytoma diagnosis with favourable maternal and neonatal outcomes.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 29-year-old woman in her first pregnancy developed proteinuria at 34 weeks and new-onset hypertension at 36 weeks, managed as pre-eclampsia. Worsening hypertension, gestational diabetes and breech presentation led to caesarean section at 36 weeks and 4 days of gestation. Postpartum, she experienced severe headaches, labile blood pressure, tachycardia and sweating. Imaging identified a 4 cm right adrenal mass. Markedly elevated plasma and urinary normetanephrines confirmed pheochromocytoma. Right adrenalectomy was performed seven weeks post-partum, with complete excision. Symptoms resolved postoperatively. Subsequent surveillance imaging showed no recurrence. She later had a second uncomplicated pregnancy.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights how pheochromocytoma in pregnancy can be differentiated from more common conditions. Prompt diagnosis and multidisciplinary management can optimise patient outcomes.

articles.title: Combination of iKIR missing ligand hypothesis and HLA-B T/T genotypes as predictive biomarkers for recurrent pregnancy loss: a novel algorithmic approach.
articles.authors: Laborda RG, Subhi-Issa N, Muñoz EF et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Natural killer (NK) cell alloreactivity at the maternal-fetal interface is regulated by killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptors (KIR) and CD94/NKG2A receptors. A dimorphism at position -21 of the HLA-B leader peptide (-21M/-21T) biases NK education toward NKG2A (when -21M supplies HLA-E-binding peptides) or toward KIR (when -21T fails to do so). We evaluated whether maternal HLA-B leader genotype and inhibitory KIR (iKIR) missing-ligand (ML) status are associated with unexplained recurrent reproductive failure (uRF).
METHODS: Retrospective case-control study comparing recipient HLA-B leader genotype (M+ versus T/T) and iKIR ML across HLA-C groups with outcomes in uRF patients versus healthy controls. 77 women with uRF (43 recurrent pregnancy loss [RPL], 34 recurrent implantation failure [RIF]) and 75 healthy multiparous controls. Maternal KIR, HLA-B and HLA-C genotypes were typed from peripheral blood using Luminex-based SSP/SSO assays.
RESULTS: The centromeric KIR AA haplotype was enriched in uRF versus controls (difference 24%, p=0.0056). iKIR-ML analysis showed higher frequency of KIR2DL2/3 with absent C1 ligands in uRF (p=0.015). The HLA-B -21 analysis revealed increased T/T homozygosity in uRF (p=0.0031). The combination of KIR2DL2/3 (absent C1) with -21 T/T was more prevalent in RPL (p=0.04).
DISCUSSION: HLA-B -21 T/T and iKIR ML (absent C1 for KIR2DL2/3) may aid risk stratification in RPL. Findings warrant validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Geographic Clustering of Idiopathic Subglottic Stenosis in North America: An Ecological Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Harb AS, Carson M, Ahrens B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS) is a recurrent fibroinflammatory narrowing of the subglottis, typically affecting White pre- and perimenopausal women. While its etiology remains uncertain, inflammatory signaling, reflux, hormonal influences, and mycobacterial factors have been proposed. This study evaluated geographic variability in survey-ascertained iSGS prevalence, exploring potential environmental correlates associated with regional disease distribution.
METHODS: A retrospective ecological analysis of self-reported demographic and clinical data from members of an international iSGS online support group was performed. Responses were analyzed by continent, country, and US state or Canadian province. Estimated prevalence per 1,000,000 White females was calculated using census data and examined in relation to environmental and access-related factors, including temperature, humidity, and particulate matter.
RESULTS: Among 4450 survey respondents, 99.3% were female and 83.8% reported symptom onset after age 30. Survey-ascertained prevalence was highest in Wyoming (18.1), Utah (17.4), Iowa (15.3), Colorado (13.9), and Minnesota (12.1), and lowest in New Hampshire (1.2), Montana (1.5), Alaska (2.3), and Indiana (2.3). In Canada, survey-ascertained prevalence was highest in Alberta (85.4) and Saskatchewan (65.3), and lowest in Quebec (2.9). Higher prevalence regions were geographically clustered in areas sharing dry or semi-arid climates, higher elevation, higher temperature and lower humidity. PM2.5 modified the association between elevation and survey-ascertained prevalence but was not independently associated with prevalence.
CONCLUSIONS: iSGS demonstrated geographic clustering in North America associated with higher altitude, lower humidity and higher temperatures; however, these ecological findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant further investigation using patient-level exposure and biologic data.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: This study represents Level 4 evidence given its ecological, cross-sectional design.

articles.title: The Impact of the HeLa Cell in the Field of Otolaryngology: Honoring Henrietta Lacks.
articles.authors: Jamil TL, Thomas CM, Mann S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The HeLa cell, which was first taken from Henrietta Lacks in 1952, was the first in vitro cell line discovered and propagated in mass. From polio vaccine development to understanding cancer biology, the HeLa cell has allowed for immeasurable scientific advances. No prior review has examined how the HeLa cell has influenced the field of otolaryngology.
METHODS: A PRISMA-style approach was taken in this narrative literature review to understand the historical context of the human papilloma virus (HPV) and how the HeLa cell elucidated HPV-mediated cancers. Then, using MeSH terminology, each subspecialty of otolaryngology (i.e., head and neck cancer, audiology, otology, rhinology, and laryngology) was used to identify studies that incorporated HeLa cells to understand how HeLa cells made direct impacts on otolaryngology research.
RESULTS: The HeLa cell was crucial to identifying how HPV causes tumorigenesis, and due to enhanced cervical cancer knowledge, this boosted head and neck tumor discoveries. Basic biology, such as how cisplatin functions, which is now a common chemotherapeutic used for head and neck cancer, was studied using the HeLa cell line. Due to the cells' reliable, accessible, and rapidly dividing characteristics, the HeLa cell was also used broadly in hearing and sensory research.
DISCUSSION: Although the HeLa cell line comes with great bioethical controversy, the HeLa cell has improved the lives of countless people. It is important to consider the lives of historically underserved communities and individuals, such as Henrietta Lacks, to both honor and recognize the contributions diverse people from every racial and economic background make to science.

articles.title: Contextual conditions shaping the upward referral of obstetric emergencies from community health centres in the Eastern Cape: a Straussian Grounded Theory study.
articles.authors: Juqu FZ, Xulu-Kasaba Z, Baloyi OB
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal mortality remains a significant public health concern in South Africa, particularly in resource limited settings where timely access to higher-level care is vital. Community Health Centres are the first point of contact for women faced with obstetric emergencies, yet systemic, contextual, and operational challenges impede effective upward referral. Guided by Straussian Grounded Theory, this qualitative study explored the contextual conditions shaping the upward referral of obstetric emergencies in the OR Tambo district, Eastern Cape.
METHODS: Data was collected through focus group discussions, in-depth interviews, document analysis, and observations, and analysed using open, axial, and selective coding.
RESULTS: Findings revealed four key categories which were resource limitations, workforce and budget gaps, communication and Emergency Medical Services, geographical and socioeconomic barriers.
DISCUSSION: These interrelated conditions contribute to delayed, unsafe, and fragmented referrals, placing mothers and newborns at heightened risk of further complicated conditions. Addressing these systemic challenges requires multi-sectoral interventions, including regular multidisciplinary emergency obstetric training, strengthened referral communication, investment in transport infrastructure and facility-based ambulances.
CONCLUSION: This study indicates that strengthening referral process is essential in enhancing timely and safe obstetric care, ultimately reducing preventable maternal and neonatal mortality.

articles.title: Phytochemical characterization and effects of Dolomiaea costus root extract on ovariectomy-induced metabolic, skeletal, and uterine alterations in rats.
articles.authors: Aldayel TS, Mahmoud HS, Abdelrazek HMA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Estrogen deficiency following ovariectomy produces metabolic, skeletal, and uterine alterations.
METHODS: In this study, we evaluated an authenticated and chemically characterized dichloromethane-methanol (1:1, v/v) root extract of Dolomiaea costus (Syn. Saussurea costus) in ovariectomized female Wistar rats. Thirty rats were assigned to sham-operated, ovariectomized untreated, and ovariectomized extract-treated groups. Beginning 3 weeks after surgery, the treated group received the extract orally at 300 mg/kg body weight/day for 12 weeks. Metabolic and lipid variables, adipokines, antioxidant status, and bone-related biomarkers were determined. Uterine, femoral, hepatic, and adipose tissues were examined histologically, while estrogen receptor-α (ER-α) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF- α) immunoreactivity were evaluated. The extract was characterized using spectrophotometric assays, GC-MS, and HPLC-DAD.
RESULTS: Ovariectomy was associated with increased body and adipose-tissue mass, dyslipidemia, impaired glucose homeostasis, altered adipokine concentrations, decreased antioxidant capacity, and structural alterations in the uterus, bone, liver, and adipose tissue. Compared with untreated ovariectomized rats, extract administration was associated with improvements in several biochemical and histological outcomes and with increased uterine ER-α immunoreactivity. Chemical profiling indicated the presence of sesquiterpene lactones, fatty-acid derivatives, and phenolic metabolites.
CONCLUSION: Increased ER-α immunoreactivity is consistent with an estrogen-responsive effect but does not establish direct estrogen-receptor agonism. These preclinical findings support further standardized pharmacological and toxicological evaluation of the extract; they do not establish efficacy or safety in menopausal women.

articles.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts from cervical cancer modulate protumoral neutrophil functions: evidence from a pilot exploratory study.
articles.authors: Reséndiz-Castillo LJ, Martínez-Barajas MG, Carranza-Aranda AS et al.
articles.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are key regulators of the tumor microenvironment; however, their role in modulating neutrophil function during cervical cancer (CC) progression remains poorly understood. In this study, we evaluated whether CAF supernatants (CSN) derived from early (FIGO I-II) and late stages (FIGO III-IV) of CC differentially regulate neutrophil activity. Peripheral blood neutrophils from healthy donors were stimulated with CSN, and their functional responses were assessed, including cytokine production, metabolic activity (MTT), reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, apoptosis and survival analyses, expression of activation (CD66b) and protease degranulation markers (MMP9 and NE), and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) release. CSN factors promoted a predominantly proinflammatory cytokine profile in neutrophils, characterized by increased production of IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α, and IFN-γ. Additionally, stimulation with CAF enhanced neutrophil metabolic activity, ROS production, survival, and expression of CD66b, MMP9, and neutrophil elastase, suggesting preliminary stage-associated differences in neutrophils responses between CAFs derived from early- and late-stage tumors. Notably, NET formation was significantly higher in neutrophils stimulated with early-stage CAFs, whereas late-stage CAFs induced a metabolically active but lower NETosis release.
