These exploratory findings suggest that cervical cancer-derived CAFs may differentially modulate neutrophil functional responses according to tumor stage, highlighting the CAF-neutrophil axis as a potentially relevant component of the cervical cancer microenvironment.

articles.title: Associations of early-pregnancy triiodothyronine and triglycerides with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Li Y, Ren J, Yang S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroid hormones are associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), but the contribution of triiodothyronine (T3), the biologically active thyroid hormone, remains insufficiently understood. Given the established role of T3 in lipid homeostasis and the association of triglycerides (TG) with HDP, we aimed to examine the associations of early-pregnancy T3 and TG levels with HDP and evaluate the potential role of TG in the association between T3 and HDP.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 13,915 pregnant women who underwent prenatal screening between January 2020 and December 2021. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations of early-pregnancy free triiodothyronine (FT3), total triiodothyronine (TT3), and TG with HDP and its subtypes, while linear regression was used to assess the associations of FT3 and TT3 with TG. Mediation analysis assessed statistical indirect associations through TG, and multiplicative interaction analysis evaluated interactions between T3 and TG.
RESULTS: Higher early-pregnancy FT3, TT3, and TG levels were associated with higher odds of HDP (all P < 0.05), and both FT3 and TT3 were positively associated with TG (P < 0.05). Mediation analysis identified significant indirect associations through TG, representing an estimated 34.1% and 33.5% of the observed associations of FT3 and TT3 with HDP, respectively. Comparable indirect associations were observed for preeclampsia (PE), with estimated proportions of 18.6% and 28.3%, respectively. For gestational hypertension (GH), an indirect association through TG was observed for TT3 (estimated proportion, 42.0%), whereas the corresponding proportion for FT3 was not interpreted because the total association was not statistically significant. No evidence of multiplicative interaction between T3 and TG was observed in relation to HDP.
CONCLUSION: Higher early-pregnancy FT3 and TT3 levels were associated with higher odds of HDP, particularly PE. TG may represent a potential metabolic component involved in the observed associations between T3 and HDP.

articles.title: Functional ovarian reserve in women with Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas.
articles.authors: Filippi F, Serra N, Comana S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hematological malignancies may impair ovarian function even before chemotherapy begins, raising concerns about the effectiveness of oocyte cryopreservation. However, available evidence remains conflicting, partly because of confounding factors and suboptimal study designs. This study investigated whether women with lymphoma show reduced ovarian reserve or impaired ovarian response compared with women without cancer and women with non-hematologic malignancies.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of women with Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas who underwent oocyte cryopreservation for fertility preservation at our Institution. Each patient was age- and study period-matched to two control groups: one comprising women without cancer undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technologies for infertility, allowing comparison of ovarian reserve markers (Anti-Müllerian Hormone, AMH, and antral follicle count, AFC), and another comprising women with non-hematologic solid tumors to compare ovarian stimulation outcomes.
RESULTS: The first comparison included 66 cases and 66 controls without cancer. Median [interquartile range - IQR] serum AMH was 1.97 [1.14-3.23] and 2.94 [2.12-4.60], respectively (p=0.002). However, AFC was similar (18 [12-24] versus 15 [11-21], p=0.16). The second comparison involved 74 cases and 74 non-hematologic cancer controls. Ovarian response was similar between groups, with a median [IQR] number of frozen mature oocytes of 10 [6-15] and 13 [6-16], respectively (p=0.56).
CONCLUSION: Early alterations in follicular function may occur in women with lymphoma. Nevertheless, ovarian response to stimulation appears preserved, supporting the effectiveness of fertility preservation.

articles.title: Past wounds, present bonds, future mothers: item-level analysis of perinatal risk profiles.
articles.authors: Mineo R, Fazio L, Maiorana A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perinatal depression is shaped by interacting psycho-relational risk factors-childhood adversity, current relational functioning, perceived social support, and prenatal attachment. Variable-centered approaches focused on isolated predictors may obscure how these dimensions combine within individuals to generate distinct vulnerability configurations.
OBJECTIVE: To identify person-centered profiles of psychosocial functioning during pregnancy and to examine their association with depressive symptoms across the perinatal period.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: A sample of 774 pregnant women was recruited from full-term and high-risk pregnancy clinics at one of the largest birth centers in Southern Italy. A subsample of 200 women (25.8%) completed the postpartum follow-up at 6 months (T1).
METHODS: An item-level k-means cluster analysis (k = 3) was performed on 44 items from the CTQ-SF, DAS-7, MSSS, and MAAS. Cluster differences in EPDS scores were tested cross-sectionally with one-way ANOVA and a covariate-adjusted model (T0), and longitudinally with a repeated-measures ANOVA (T0-T1). A formal attrition analysis and domain-level sensitivity analyses were also conducted.
RESULTS: Three profiles emerged: Low-Risk (53.7%), Moderately Adjusted (31.7%), and High-Adversity (14.6%). Between-cluster differences in depressive symptoms were significant at T0 (F(2, 771) = 62.52, p < 0.001, η 2 = 0.140), were essentially unchanged after adjustment for sociodemographic and obstetric covariates (F(2, 747) = 58.15, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.135), and persisted across the perinatal period (main effect of cluster: F(2, 197) = 22.74, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.188), with no significant Time effect (F(1, 197) = 0.38, p = 0.54) or Cluster × Time interaction (F(2, 197) = 1.40, p = 0.25). At T0, 11.1, 35.9, and 44.2% of the Low-Risk, Moderately Adjusted, and High-Adversity profiles, respectively, scored above the EPDS clinical cut-off (≥ 9; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Item-level cluster analysis reveals clinically significant heterogeneity in perinatal risk. Between-profile differences in depressive symptoms persisted across the perinatal period and may inform stratified, trauma-informed prevention strategies.

articles.title: Performance of non-invasive prenatal screening for 15q11q13 copy number variations in a cohort of 90,693 pregnancies.
articles.authors: Chen D, Hu L, Niu H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deletions and duplications within the 15q11q13 chromosomal region are associated with Prader-Willi syndrome, Angelman syndrome, and 15q11q13 duplication syndrome. However, prenatal ultrasound findings were unremarkable in the majority of affected fetuses. The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of non-invasive prenatal screening (NIPS) in identifying these syndromes in 90,693 pregnancies within the general population.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 90,693 pregnant women who underwent NIPS at Longgang Maternal and Child Health Hospital in Shenzhen from November 2022 to January 2026. For high-risk 15q11q13 copy number variations (CNVs) identified, we performed chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) on amniotic fluid, followed by methylation-specific multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MS-MLPA) or further CMA to determine the CNVs' genetic origin, with subsequent follow-up.
RESULTS: NIPS screening identified 4 high-risk cases for 15q11q13 deletion and 7 for duplication. Among the deletion cases, 3 were confirmed by CMA to have a 5-6 Mb deletion (2 maternal, 1 unverified), while 1 declined further testing. For duplication, 6 underwent amniocentesis, with CMA confirming 5 cases (2 maternal, 2 paternal, 1 unverified), 1 normal result, and 1 declined further testing. Of the 8 true-positive cases, 7 had normal ultrasounds, but 1 fetus with duplication exhibited growth retardation. Pregnancy outcomes included 6 terminations, one delivery with paternal duplication showing mild language delay at nearly 2 years, and another with maternal duplication lost to follow-up.
CONCLUSION: NIPS can effectively detect CNVs at the 15q11q13 locus with a high positive predictive value, but its sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value, and false-negative rate could not be determined in this study due to the lack of confirmatory testing in low-risk cases. Invasive prenatal diagnosis remains essential for validation.

articles.title: Exploring the Social and Financial Impacts of Cervical Cancer on Caregivers in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: McNair A, Dau H, Nakisige C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cervical cancer disproportionately affects women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where limited healthcare infrastructure often shifts caregiving responsibilities to informal companions such as family members, spouses, and friends. The goal of this scoping review is to map and summarize the social and economic impacts of cervical cancer on the caregivers for women diagnosed with cervical cancer in LMICs.
METHODS: Three databases were searched up to March 30, 2026. Studies were included if they were conducted in a LMIC, included caregivers or companions of cervical cancer patients, and reported on social or financial outcomes. Outcomes were categorized into social impacts (psychosocial burden, education, social support, and sexual relationships) and economic impacts (employment and financial security).
RESULTS: Fifteen unique studies from 11 countries were included (11 cross-sectional and 4 qualitative), and caregiver sample sizes ranged from 7 to 360. Caregivers were predominantly middle-aged, with low to moderate educational attainment and income. Up to 72.1% of caregivers experienced high levels of psychosocial burden. Educational disruptions were reported, with up to 28% of households reporting difficulties paying for education and school absences among family members. Social support experiences varied, with most caregivers reporting stable family relationships but some reporting neglect of other family members. Employment was significantly disrupted, with up to 61% of companions reducing working hours and 28% of households having a member stop working entirely. Financial hardship was pervasive: up to 39% of households experienced partial or total income loss, and coping strategies included selling assets, reducing food consumption, and accumulating debt.
CONCLUSION: Cervical cancer inflicts substantial social and financial consequences on caregivers in LMICs, spanning psychosocial distress, educational disruption, employment loss, and financial hardship. These impacts are shaped by gender dynamics and intergenerational caregiving roles. As the global community pursues cervical cancer elimination, policies integrating caregiver support are essential.

articles.title: A Novel Homozygous ZPBP Frameshift Variant Is Associated With Severe Acrosomal Structural Abnormalities in Asthenoteratozoospermia.
articles.authors: Yang J, Chen Q, Ren H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Experimental disruption of Zpbp homologs in mice causes defective acrosomal biogenesis and male infertility. Human evidence remains limited to a small number of association-based or case-level reports linking ZPBP alterations to abnormal sperm-head or acrosomal phenotypes, without integrated characterization across protein abundance, ultrastructure, sperm chromatin integrity, and proteome-wide changes.
OBJECTIVES: Our study aimed to characterize the genetic, structural, and molecular sperm phenotype associated with a novel homozygous frameshift variant in ZPBP.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) and Sanger sequencing were performed in the proband. Semen parameters, Papanicolaou-stained morphology, and FITC-PSA-defined acrosomal staining patterns were assessed. ZPBP protein abundance was evaluated by Western blotting. Sperm morphology and ultrastructure were examined by light microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Sperm chromatin structure assay, IZUMO1 immunofluorescence, and label-free proteomic profiling were also performed.
RESULTS: A man born to consanguineous parents carried a novel homozygous frameshift variant in ZPBP (NM_007009.3:c.421_422del; p.Phe141Profs*4), classified as a variant of uncertain significance; parental samples were unavailable for segregation analysis. The proband had normal sperm concentration but markedly reduced motility and complete absence of morphologically normal spermatozoa, with predominantly head abnormalities, consistent with severe asthenoteratozoospermia. Head, midpiece, and principal-piece abnormalities occurred in 99.33% ± 0.47%, 14.67% ± 2.62%, and 22.67% ± 3.40% of spermatozoa, respectively. Abnormal, fragmented, or absent FITC-PSA staining was observed in 84.33% ± 1.70%. Western blotting demonstrated absence of ZPBP protein in patient sperm. SEM and TEM showed complete or partial acrosomal loss, membrane and matrix fragmentation, widening of the subacrosomal space, and nuclear-acrosomal detachment. The DNA fragmentation index was 52.25% and high DNA stainability was 5.71%. IZUMO1 staining was markedly reduced or absent in the proband's sperm. Proteomic profiling showed coordinated lower abundance of multiple acrosome-related proteins and negative enrichment of acrosomal pathways.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: The findings associate the novel homozygous ZPBP frameshift variant with severe acrosomal structural abnormalities, impaired…

articles.title: Cerebrospinal fluid cell-free DNA methylation captures disease-specific biology in tauopathies.
articles.authors: Tian H, Zhang J, Zuo H et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDifferentiating tau-related dementias remains challenging, particularly during early disease stages when clinical symptoms overlap. Existing biomarkers mainly reflect downstream pathology and provide limited insight into disease-specific molecular processes.ObjectiveWe examined whether cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation could distinguish Alzheimer's disease (AD), behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP).MethodsPromoter methylation of 20 genes associated with AD risk, neuroinflammation, cellular senescence, and glymphatic or lymphatic regulation was analyzed in CSF and matched plasma cfDNA from controls (n = 15), AD (n = 21), bvFTD (n = 14), and PSP (n = 17). cfDNA concentration and fragmentomic profiles were assessed. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Findings were validated in an independent cohort.ResultsCSF cfDNA concentrations were increased in AD, whereas fragment size distributions were similar across diagnostic groups. Disease-associated methylation signatures were prominent in CSF but weak or absent in plasma. AD demonstrated widespread hypomethylation of inflammatory and senescence-associated genes together with hypermethylation of glymphatic and lymphatic regulators. bvFTD showed intermediate glial- and stress-related methylation changes, while PSP retained relatively preserved inflammatory and clearance-associated profiles. CSF methylation panels consistently outperformed plasma-derived markers for disease classification. ROC analyses demonstrated strong discrimination for AD, with AUC values reaching 0.84-0.85, while plasma-based markers showed limited diagnostic utility.ConclusionsCSF cfDNA methylation captures disease-specific epigenetic states linked to core pathogenic pathways in tau-related dementias. This approach may provide a biologically informative and clinically useful platform for molecular classification and diagnostic stratification.

articles.title: Maternal health service utilization and birth outcomes among female sex workers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, and Nigeria: results from a cross-sectional survey.
articles.authors: Danel I, Moss R, Willis B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Information on maternal health service utilization among female sex workers (FSW) in low- and middle-income countries (LMIC) is limited, with research focusing on HIV. Despite most FSW being mothers, little is known about their childbirth care or birth outcomes. To our knowledge, this is the first multicountry study to describe adverse birth outcomes among FSW in LMIC.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study used a convenience sample of 853 FSW from eight cities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Kenya, and Nigeria to examine antenatal care (ANC) utilization, substance use during pregnancy, skilled birth attendance, and birth outcomes (stillbirth, perinatal mortality, and low birth weight). Self-reported outcomes for the five years preceding data collection were compared descriptively with national survey data for urban women to provide context.
RESULTS: Maternal health service utilization and birth outcomes varied widely by country. FSW participants in Kenya reported high ANC utilization (95.6%) and facility delivery (97.0%), comparable to urban women. ANC utilization and facility delivery were lower among FSW participants in the DRC (ANC: 49.0%; facility delivery: 68.0%) and Nigeria (ANC: 37.5%; facility delivery: 26.1%) compared to urban women. Cost and stigma were the main barriers. Alcohol use during pregnancy was common in all countries. Stillbirth rates among participating FSW were very high (113 per 1000 births in the DRC [95% CI 85-146], 49 in Kenya [95% CI 30-75], and 85 in Nigeria [95% CI 63-111]), as was perinatal mortality. Low birth weight prevalence was high in the two countries with sufficient birthweight data (DRC: 17.1%; Kenya: 9.7%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this study sample, adverse birth outcomes-high stillbirth and perinatal mortality and low birth weight-may reflect the combined effects of limited access to quality maternal health services (MHS) and broader social, economic and health vulnerabilities documented among FSW populations. Kenya's subsidized maternal healthcare system may contribute to higher MHS utilization and better birth outcomes observed in Kenya. Improving equity in maternal and newborn health for FSW requires increasing access to quality MHS and addressing underlying social determinants of health. FSW should be recognized as a high-risk population requiring targeted maternal health interventions.

articles.title: Trends, disparities, and pregnancy outcomes of gestational diabetes mellitus in North West London: A nine-year population-based cohort study.
articles.authors: Sousi S, Glynou SP, Hyman S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) affects approximately 1 in 20 pregnancies in England. North West London (NWL) serves a diverse population of 2.4 million with substantial ethnic and socioeconomic variation. However, population-level epidemiological evidence from NWL remains limited. This study aims to characterise GDM incidence, temporal trends, risk determinants, and associated pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective population-based cohort study using routinely collected data from the Whole Systems Integrated Care database included all birth episodes from 2017 to 2025, categorised as GDM or non-GDM. Incidence per 1,000 births was calculated and temporal trends were analysed. Multivariable generalised estimating equation (GEE) logistic regression models were used to examine maternal risk determinants for GDM and pregnancy outcomes associated with GDM, while controlling for confounders and accounting for within-woman clustering across pregnancies.
RESULTS: Among 172,332 births from 134,991 women, 18,892 (10.9%) were GDM-affected. Overall incidence was 109.6 per 1,000 births (95% CI: 108.2-111.1), rising from 80.5 per 1,000 births in 2017 to 138 per 1,000 births in 2025. Incidence increased with maternal age and deprivation (119 vs. 85.4 in most vs. least deprived quintiles). Asian women had the highest risk (aOR 2.27, 95% CI: 2.15-2.40) relative to White. GDM was associated with higher rates of labour induction (51% vs. 41%), caesarean delivery (47% vs. 36%), preterm birth (7.3% vs. 5.2%), greater maternity care costs (£4,674 vs. £3,971) and longer maternal length of stay (3 vs. 2 days).
CONCLUSION: The incidence of GDM in NWL substantially exceeds national estimates and has nearly doubled over nine years, with pronounced ethnic and socioeconomic disparities. Targeted culturally appropriate prevention strategies and equity-focused service planning are needed in this population.

articles.title: First-trimester aggregate index of systemic inflammation and adverse pregnancy outcomes in hospitalized women with threatened miscarriage: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Haksever M, Zorlu U, Eroğlu ŞK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices have been associated with miscarriage, but the incremental value of the aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI) beyond established indices such as the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) remains uncertain. We examined the association and prognostic performance of first-trimester AISI in hospitalized women with threatened miscarriage.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 312 women hospitalized with threatened miscarriage between January 2020 and December 2022. The primary outcome was a composite of miscarriage before 14 weeks, preterm birth before 37 weeks with or without preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM), or fetal demise from 14 weeks onward. AISI was analyzed continuously on the log2 scale. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, receiver operating characteristic analysis with DeLong comparisons, calibration, 500-resample bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Adverse outcomes occurred in 134 women (42.9%). Median AISI was higher in the adverse-outcome group than in women with term birth (339.9 [IQR 250.2-432.1] vs. 236.6 [167.0-313.9]; p < 0.001). Each doubling of AISI was associated with higher adjusted odds of an adverse outcome (adjusted odds ratio 4.46, 95% CI 2.59-7.67; p < 0.001), with no evidence of nonlinearity (p = 0.499). AISI showed moderate discrimination (AUC 0.717, 95% CI 0.661-0.774), which was not significantly different from SII (AUC 0.696; DeLong p = 0.299). The exploratory AISI cut-off of 287.3 had 66.4% sensitivity (95% CI 58.1-73.9%) and 69.1% specificity (95% CI 62.0-75.4%). Adding AISI to the clinical plus C-reactive protein model increased the bootstrap-corrected AUC from 0.811 to 0.853 and reduced the corrected Brier score from 0.176 to 0.153; the incremental decision-curve benefit was modest.
CONCLUSIONS: First-trimester AISI was independently associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes in this selected hospitalized cohort and added prognostic information to clinical variables and C-reactive protein. However, AISI alone had only moderate discrimination and was not superior to SII. These findings do not support a stand-alone clinical cut-off or a specific management intervention; prospective multicenter validation is required.

articles.title: Effect of Rho Kinase Inhibitor (Y27632) on Spermatogenesis in Azoospermic Mice Model.
articles.authors: Bolboleh S, Peirouvi T, Karimipour S et al.
articles.abstract: Advances in cancer therapy have markedly improved patient survival, thereby increasing the need for effective fertility preservation strategies. Chemotherapeutic agents commonly induce apoptosis in rapidly proliferating cells, including spermatogonia, resulting in long-term testicular damage. Y-27632, a Rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase (ROCK) inhibitor, has been shown to suppress apoptosis in various stem cell populations by modulating Rho GTPase-dependent signaling pathways. This study aimed to evaluate the protective effects of Y-27632 against busulfan-induced testicular injury in a murine model. Eighteen 4-week-old male C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned to three groups: control (no treatment), busulfan (40 mg/kg), and busulfan plus Y-27632 (40 mg/kg busulfan + 5 mg/kg Y-27632). Seventy days after treatment, sperm parameters (count, motility, viability, and plasma membrane integrity) and testicular outcomes, including seminiferous tubule diameter, germinal epithelium thickness, tubular differentiation index, spermatogenesis index, Johnsen score, apoptotic gene expression, malondialdehyde levels, total antioxidant capacity, and TUNEL-positive cells, were assessed. Y-27632 administration significantly improved seminiferous tubule diameter and germinal epithelium thickness and increased tubular differentiation and spermatogenesis indices and Johnsen scores compared with the busulfan group. In addition, Y-27632 treatment was associated with reduced ERK gene expression and a lower number of TUNEL-positive cells. However, sperm parameters and testicular weight remained significantly reduced compared with controls, and no significant differences were observed in lipid peroxidation, total antioxidant capacity, or sperm DNA integrity among groups. In conclusion, Y-27632 partially attenuated busulfan-induced testicular damage by improving histological indices of spermatogenesis and reducing apoptosis, suggesting that ROCK inhibition may represent a potential adjunct strategy for fertility preservation following gonadotoxic cancer therapies.

articles.title: Insilico Analysis of CYP17A1 in the Pathogenesis of Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome by Molecular Dynamics and Genotypic Characterization.
articles.authors: Vetriselvan Y, Murugan M, Samantaray M et al.
articles.abstract: CYP17A1 gene (Cytochrome P45017A1) plays a significant role in the steroidogenic pathway that synthesizes sex steroids and glucocorticoids. In Cytochrome P45017A1, the heme-binding domain region is essential for its catalytic function to synthesize steroids. Mutations in the CYP17A1 gene have been associated with several pathological conditions, including congenital adrenal hyperplasia, Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), now referred to as Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS), and certain types of cancers. This study aimed to identify deleterious missense mutations in CYP17A1 using in silico tools, molecular dynamics simulations, and genotyping to detect both rare and common variants. In silico analyses identified 22 pathogenic mutations using sequence- and structure-based tools. Furthermore, the mutations in the heme-binding domain (F453S, R449C) were characterized using molecular dynamics simulations. Results of Molecular dynamics simulations show that CYP17A1 mutants exhibit significant structural changes, particularly in the heme and steroid-binding regions, which weaken heme coordination and alter heme affinity. Based on the high minor allele frequency (MAF) of 0.04% in the South Indian population, the common variant rs743572 was genotyped in a cohort of (n = 100 PMOS cases and n = 90 healthy controls) to assess its population distribution and potential regulatory role in hormone-related disorders. These changes indicate functional impairments in steroidogenesis, informing the development of targeted therapies for related disorders. Thus, our findings offer valuable insights into the genetic basis of CYP17A1 dysregulation and highlight the need for precision medicine in targeting therapeutics for related disorders.

articles.title: Ferroptosis in health and disease.
articles.authors: Oyedokun PA, Ashonibare VJ, Akhigbe TM et al.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent, non-apoptotic form of regulated cell death that is driven by lipid peroxidation. In the past decade, it has emerged as a core pathogenic mechanism in a wide range of human diseases, such as neurodegenerative disorders, cardiovascular disease, cancer, and notably, reproductive dysfunction. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms underlying ferroptosis with a specific focus on the System Xc⁻-GSH-GPX4 axis, iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, and the regulatory roles of key modulators such as Nrf2, ACSL4, and CISD2. This review also explores the physiological roles of ferroptosis in development, tissue homeostasis, and immune regulation, as well as its pathological contributions to obesity, diabetes mellitus, atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, stroke, cancer, infectious diseases, and reproductive disorders. A substantial part of this review discusses the role of ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of reproductive disorders, such as male reproductive pathologies, including varicocele, testicular ischemia-reperfusion, cryptorchidism, oligospermia, erectile dysfunction, and testicular cancer, and female pathologies like primary ovarian insufficiency, polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, ovarian cancer, and pre-eclampsia. Moreover, the interplay between ferroptosis and immune dysfunction in reproductive tract infections was highlighted. Furthermore, we evaluated current biomarkers, emerging therapeutic strategies, and key translational challenges, highlighting the promise of ferroptosis-modulating agents for novel diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in reproductive medicine and beyond.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and hospital-based cost avoidance of single-port robotic surgery in gynecology: a large comparative cohort study.
articles.authors: Cho CH, Jeon Y, Shin C et al.
articles.abstract: Single-port robotic surgery is increasingly used in gynecologic practice, yet large-scale comparative data describing both postoperative outcomes and the downstream use of hospital resources remain limited. In this study, we aimed to investigate postoperative outcomes and hospital-based economic analysis in single-port robotic surgery and laparoscopic surgery through a large-scale retrospective analysis. We retrospectively evaluated 8,243 consecutive patients who underwent minimally invasive surgery for benign or malignant gynecologic disease at Keimyung University Dongsan Hospital from April 2019 through December 2024. Conventional laparoscopy was performed in 6,109 patients and robotic-assisted surgery using the da Vinci Xi single-site or da Vinci SP platform in 2,134. Length of stay, transfusion, surgical site infection, postoperative complications, mortality, operative and anesthesia times, and 30-day readmission were compared. Hospital-based cost avoidance was estimated from differences in readmission, complications, and length of hospitalization. Compared with laparoscopy, robotic surgery was associated with shorter total hospitalization (2.54 vs. 3.18 days, P < 0.001) and postoperative stay (2.38 vs. 2.90 days, P < 0.001). Transfusion was less frequent after robotic surgery (0.6% vs. 2.5%, P < 0.001), whereas surgical site infection, postoperative complications, mortality, patient-controlled analgesia use, and 30-day readmission did not differ significantly. Operative room and anesthesia times were each approximately 8 min longer in the robotic group. Across 2,134 robotic procedures, differences in postoperative resource use corresponded to an estimated hospital-based medical cost avoidance of US$171,469 (US$80.4 per patient), with reduced length of stay accounting for more than 84% of the total. In this large real-world cohort, single-port robotic surgery was associated with shorter hospitalization and a lower transfusion rate than conventional laparoscopy, without a detectable increase in major perioperative adverse outcomes. The observed reduction in postoperative resource use was also associated with measurable hospital-based cost avoidance. These findings support further prospective evaluation of the clinical and economic value of single-port robotic surgery.

articles.title: Prenatal tobacco exposure and visual disorders in children.
articles.authors: Bomze Z, Babik K, Korniluk J et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal smoking during pregnancy is associated with adverse fetal and perinatal outcomes and may also affect visual system development in offspring. Increasing evidence suggests that prenatal tobacco exposure may also be associated with abnormalities of visual system development in children. However, the extent to which these associations reflect direct effects of tobacco exposure versus indirect pathways mediated by adverse perinatal outcomes remains uncertain. This narrative review summarizes the available evidence regarding the association between prenatal tobacco exposure and visual abnormalities in children, with particular emphasis on retinopathy of prematurity, strabismus, refractive errors, retinal nerve fiber layer abnormalities, and optic nerve hypoplasia. The most consistent evidence concerns retinopathy of prematurity and strabismus, although interpretation is complicated by prematurity, fetal growth restriction, neonatal morbidity, and residual confounding. Evidence regarding refractive errors and amblyopia is less consistent, while data on structural visual pathway abnormalities remain limited. Proposed mechanisms include vascular dysfunction, altered cholinergic signaling, oxidative stress, inflammation, and impaired neurodevelopment.Conclusion: Prenatal tobacco exposure may be associated with selected functional and structural abnormalities of the developing visual system. The strength of evidence varies substantially by outcome, and available data do not establish that prenatal tobacco exposure independently causes all reported visual disorders. Future studies should use objective exposure biomarkers, longitudinal designs and analytical approaches that distinguish direct effects from pathways mediated by prematurity and fetal growth restriction. Smoking cessation during pregnancy remains an important preventive intervention.

articles.title: Self-efficacy, Self-esteem, Cancer Coping, and Psychosocial Adjustment in Women With Gynecological Cancer in Turkey: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.authors: Purtul S, Uslu-Sahan F
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women diagnosed with gynecological cancer face significant psychosocial challenges that impact their self-efficacy, self-esteem, and coping abilities. Understanding these factors is essential for developing effective psychosocial interventions.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the relationships between self-efficacy, self-esteem, cancer coping strategies, and psychosocial adjustment in women with gynecological cancer in Turkey.
METHODS: This correlational cross-sectional study involved 105 women with gynecological cancer from 2 university hospitals in Turkey. Data were collected using the General Self-efficacy Scale, Rosenberg's Self-esteem Scale, Cancer Coping Questionnaire, and Psychosocial Adjustment to Illness Scale. Statistical analyses included independent t tests, 1-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation, and hierarchical regression.
RESULTS: The mean psychosocial adjustment score was 70.22 ± 4.60. Significant negative correlations were found between psychosocial adjustment and self-efficacy (r = -0.572, P = .001), self-esteem (r = -0.277, P = .004), and cancer coping (r = -0.581, P = .001). Hierarchical regression revealed that self-efficacy (β = -0.462, P = .001), cancer coping (β = -0.280, P = .001), and treatment type (β = -0.332, P = .001) collectively explained 55% of the variance in psychosocial adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: Self-efficacy and coping strategies significantly influence psychosocial adjustment in women with gynecological cancer, whereas self-esteem showed no significant effect. These findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to strengthen self-efficacy and coping mechanisms in women with gynecological cancer.
IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Healthcare professionals should implement structured interventions to enhance self-efficacy and coping strategies, as these factors are key to improving psychosocial adjustment and overall well-being in women undergoing gynecological cancer treatment.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Associations of Small, Vulnerable Newborns With Mental Capital in Early School-Aged Children.
articles.authors: Terada S, Isumi A, Fujiwara T
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although mental capital is increasingly recognised as a foundation for children's later well-being, its perinatal determinants remain unclear because traditional classifications such as preterm birth and small for gestational age (SGA) capture only partial and overlapping aspects of vulnerability.
OBJECTIVES: Using the integrated small vulnerable newborn (SVN) framework with mutually exclusive categories, we aimed to assess associations between SVN categories and mental capital at ages 6-7 years by sex.
METHODS: We analysed data from six waves of the Adachi Child Health Impact of Living Difficulty (A-CHILD) study, a population-based repeated cross-sectional survey of first-grade students in Adachi City, Tokyo, conducted between 2015 and 2024 (n = 20,928). Caregivers provided gestational week and birthweight from the Maternal and Child Health Handbook, and children were classified into SVN categories (term non-SGA, term SGA, preterm non-SGA, preterm SGA). Mental capital, including behavioural problems, prosocial behaviour, and resilience, was assessed using the parent-reported Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire and Children's Resilience and Coping Scale. Multivariable regression models were fitted, stratified by biological sex.
RESULTS: Among the 20,928 children, 3402 (16.3%) were term SGA, 1093 (5.2%) were preterm non-SGA, and 227 (1.1%) were preterm SGA. Compared with term non-SGA, term SGA was associated with higher total difficulties scores among girls (standardised β 0.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.05, 0.17) but not among boys (β 0.03, 95% CI -0.03, 0.09). Term SGA girls also showed lower resilience (β -0.07, 95% CI -0.12, -0.01). In contrast, preterm non-SGA boys had higher total difficulties scores (β 0.13, 95% CI 0.04, 0.21). There was no evidence that any SVN category was associated with prosocial behaviour in either sex.
CONCLUSIONS: Term SGA tended to be associated with behavioural problems and lower resilience among girls, whereas preterm non-SGA tended to be associated with behavioural problems among boys.

articles.title: Placental adaptation to maternal overnutrition as an evolutionary trade-off.
articles.journal: Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM
articles.authors: Desoye G, Wells JCK
articles.abstract: The mammalian placenta is genetically identical to the fetus, exposing it to unique selective pressures. In humans, placental evolution has been explored through the lens of nutritional scarcity, with selective pressures assumed to diminish as resources increase. Here, we challenge this assumption, arguing that maternal overnutrition constitutes a distinct and underappreciated selective pressure. Maternal inability to maintain fuel homeostasis exposes the fetus to nutrient overload, elevating fetal insulin and oxygen demand. Selection has favored placental adaptive responses to the resulting oxygen deficit, with insulin as the mechanistic core. However, the role of fetal hyperinsulinemia in protecting brain oxygen supply comes at the cost of excess fetal adiposity. This trade-off carries downstream health risks, including obstetric risks, preterm birth, and intergenerational metabolic disease.

articles.title: Impact of female CFTR variant carrier status on reproductive outcomes.
articles.journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
articles.authors: Jia M, Xue X
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the impact of carrying a single pathogenic or likely pathogenic CFTR variant on reproductive outcomes in women undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART).
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, 4479 vitro fertilization (IVF) /intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) cycles from 3398 patients who had undergone expanded carrier screening (ECS) between January 2022 and November 2024 were analyzed. Cycles were categorized into a control group (n = 4089 cycles) and a CF carrier group (n = 390 cycles) based on the presence of a pathogenic/likely pathogenic CFTR variant in the female partner. The CF carrier group was propensity-score matched to controls at a 1:4 ratio. Subgroup analysis was stratified by variant loci (5T allele or non-5T variants).
RESULTS: Compared with controls, female CF carriers showed lower baseline FSH levels (6.7 ± 2.9 vs. 7.8 ± 4.3, p < 0.05) and a reduced mature oocyte rate (78.4%vs. 84.1%, p < 0.05). In single blastocyst transfer cycles, clinical outcomes were comparable between 5T allele carriers and the control group. Carriers of non-5T CFTR variants had significantly lower clinical pregnancy (34.1%vs. 57.3%, p < 0.05) and live birth rates (25.0%vs. 44.7%, p < 0.05). No significant between-group differences were observed in other ovarian reserve parameters and embryo development.
CONCLUSION: Women carrying a single pathogenic or likely pathogenic CFTR variant (excluding the 5T allele) may exhibit reduced fertility potential and poorer ART outcomes. These results support recommending that women be informed of the possible reproductive implications of CFTR carrier status prior to ART treatment.

articles.title: Low-Dose Aspirin in the Prevention of Recurrent Spontaneous Preterm Birth Stratified by Placental Maternal Vascular Malperfusion: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Trial.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Meliëzer JAL, Landman AJEMC, Gieskes AA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of low-dose aspirin in the prevention of recurrent preterm birth (PTB) in women with signs of maternal vascular malperfusion (MVM) in the placenta of the previous spontaneous PTB.
DESIGN: Secondary analysis of the APRIL study.
SETTING: The APRIL study, conducted in 34 centres in the Netherlands, evaluated low-dose aspirin versus placebo in the prevention of recurrent PTB after spontaneous PTB.
POPULATION: Women with a history of spontaneous PTB participating in the APRIL study, with available placenta histology reports from the previous spontaneous PTB.
METHODS: Placental histology reports were retrieved from participating centres and categorized for presence of MVM as defined by the Amsterdam criteria.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Recurrent PTB.
RESULTS: Placental histology reports of the previous spontaneous PTB were available for 41.3% (160/387) of participants, and MVM was present in 27.5% (44/160). In participants with MVM, recurrent PTB occurred in 4.2% (1/24) of the aspirin group, versus in 45.0% (9/20) in the placebo group (Relative Risk (RR) 0.09; 95% Confidence Interval (CI) 0.01-0.43; p = 0.02). In participants without MVM, PTB occurred in 29.3% (17/58) in the aspirin group compared to 17.2% (10/58) in the placebo group (RR 1.70; 95% CI 0.87-3.56; p = 0.13).
CONCLUSION: In women with a history of spontaneous PTB and signs of MVM in the placenta, a vascular-mediated subgroup, the use of low-dose aspirin in a subsequent pregnancy was associated with a lower rate of recurrent PTB.

articles.title: A new noninvasive prenatal paternity test based on double nucleotide polymorphisms abates sequencing uncertainties and improves sensitivity.
articles.authors: D'Atanasio E, Pistacchia L, Bella E et al.
articles.abstract: Noninvasive prenatal paternity testing (NIPAT) based on fetal cell-free DNA (fetal cfDNA) has gained increasing relevance in forensic genetics. However, its applicability and reliability are often limited by the low fetal DNA fraction and by high-throughput sequencing errors that can be misinterpreted as inherited paternal variants. Here, we present NEWPAT, a novel NIPAT approach based on Double Nucleotide Polymorphisms (DNPs), i.e. biallelic variants composed of two adjacent nucleotides arising from a single mutational event. These markers offer a key advantage compared to single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs): the likelihood of both positions being affected by independent sequencing errors is extremely low, thus improving the specificity of fetal DNA detection. We develop a targeted amplicon-based panel including 979 markers (845 autosomal and 80 X Chromosome DNPs, plus 54 Y SNPs), and test at depths ranging from 1,000× to 10,000× on 42 individuals, including genomic DNA from 4 families, 2 artificial maternal-child mixtures simulating cfDNA and actual cfDNA from 12 pregnant women plus the putative biological fathers. We observe a DNP sequencing error rate of 8.9×10-5, i.e. ~12 times lower than the observed single base error rate. By exploiting the full range of sequencing depths at loci supporting the fetal genotype, we obtain Combined Paternity Index curves that consistently lead to the correct paternity attribution or exclusion in all true or false mother-father pairs. Notably, NEWPAT proves effective even at fetal cfDNA levels as low as 0.2%, when existing SNP-based protocols lead to inconclusive results, offering a highly sensitive and accurate NIPAT strategy.

articles.title: Lifestyle intervention to improve outcomes in dichorionic twin pregnancies: study protocol for a multicentre randomised controlled trial with an integrated pilot study - the LIFETWIN trial.
articles.authors: Lodewyckx K, Shafran YW, Coucke B et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preterm birth and small-for-gestational-age (SGA) infants remain major contributors to neonatal morbidity, mortality and healthcare costs. Twin pregnancies account for a disproportionate share of these adverse outcomes, representing 18%–24% of all preterm births in Europe. Despite this high-risk profile, effective preventive strategies for twin pregnancies remain limited and mainly target cervical length. Emerging evidence suggests that maternal lifestyle factors, including diet, physical activity and stress management, may prolong gestational age and improve fetal growth.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The LIFEstyle intervention to improve TWIN pregnancy (LIFETWIN) - study is a multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled trial. A total of 274 women with dichorionic twin pregnancies will be recruited across 15 sites in Belgium. The full trial will be preceded by an integrated pilot study conducted at four sites to assess feasibility using the RE-AIM framework. Participants will be randomised to standard care or a lifestyle intervention in addition to standard care. The intervention consists of eight midwife-led sessions between gestational weeks 16 and 36, focusing on a Mediterranean-type diet, physical activity, mindfulness and prenatal multivitamin supplementation. Data are collected at baseline, in late pregnancy, at delivery and at 6 weeks postpartum, using clinical records, physical examinations and validated questionnaires. The primary outcome is gestational age at delivery. Secondary outcomes include neonatal birth weight, SGA status, neonatal morbidity and mortality, neonatal intensive care unit admission and length of stay, maternal gestational weight gain, postpartum weight and quality of life. The primary outcome, gestational age at delivery, will be analysed using a linear mixed-effects model, accounting for study-site effects and potential clustering by intervention midwife within the intervention arm. Secondary outcomes will be analysed using models appropriate to the outcome type, including linear mixed models, generalised mixed models and frailty models.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The trial has been approved by the central ethics committee of Leuven (identification number S68251) and by the local ethics committees of each participating site. The trial will be conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. All results, whether positive, negative or inconclusive, will be disseminated at national or international scientific…

articles.title: Can maternal characteristics improve due date prediction without ultrasound? Development and internal validation of a machine-learning prediction model in 600 000 pregnancies in Sweden.
articles.authors: Dutra G, Elinder M, Erixson O
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess whether estimated due dates based on Naegele’s rule can be improved by incorporating routinely collected maternal characteristics into a non-parametric machine learning model, particularly in settings where ultrasound is unavailable.
DESIGN: Population-based retrospective cohort study; development and internal validation of a machine-learning prediction model.
SETTING: Nationwide register data from Sweden.
PARTICIPANTS: 603 861 singleton pregnancies recorded in the Swedish Medical Birth Register between 2008 and 2017. We restricted the sample to spontaneous singleton births with complete information on last menstrual period, ultrasound dating and maternal characteristics and further limited the primary analysis to pregnancies in which both Naegele’s rule and ultrasound-based gestational age at delivery fell between 37 and 42 completed weeks.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was prediction accuracy of the date of delivery. Performance was evaluated using exact-day accuracy, accuracy within ±1 and ±7 days, mean squared error and root mean squared error. Machine-learning predictions were compared with those obtained using Naegele’s rule and ultrasound-based dating under identical inclusion criteria.
RESULTS: The machine-learning model improved prediction accuracy over Naegele’s rule across all evaluated measures, while ultrasound-based dating remained more accurate overall. The model reduced between 25% and 45% of the accuracy gap between Naegele’s rule and ultrasound. Subgroup-specific models provided little additional improvement. Among second-time mothers, however, adding gestational duration from the previous pregnancy yielded markedly greater gains and produced prediction accuracy comparable to, and on some measures slightly better than, ultrasound.
CONCLUSIONS: Incorporating maternal characteristics into a regression-forest model improved due date prediction compared with Naegele’s rule. These improvements may be relevant in settings where ultrasound is unavailable but the routinely collected information and basic digital infrastructure required to apply the model are available. The approach is not intended to replace ultrasound-based dating in routine clinical care. Further research is needed to assess performance in other populations and to evaluate potential implications for clinical decision-making. The model was developed and internally validated in Swedish register data and requires external…

articles.title: Impact of Poor Air Quality and Excess Heat on Pregnancy Outcomes.
articles.journal: The Nursing clinics of North America
articles.authors: Atkin K, Simmonds K
articles.abstract: Climate change is worsening air pollution and increasing global temperatures, which is adversely affecting human health in many ways. Pregnant people appear to be at greater risk for complications related to exposure to excess heat and air pollution due to normal physiologic adaptations that occur in pregnancy. Social and structural determinants of health contribute to disproportionate exposure to environmental hazards among some populations which worsens existing inequities in perinatal outcomes. Nurses are uniquely positioned to educate patients about environmental health risks, promote adaptation strategies to reduce adverse outcomes, and lead advocacy efforts aimed at climate mitigation.

articles.title: Eliminating Disparities and Optimizing Equity in Necrotizing Enterocolitis.
articles.authors: LaFontaine RN, Hair AB, Patel AL et al.
articles.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis is a devastating complication of prematurity with high mortality and lifelong morbidities. The burden of disease is inequitably distributed, with higher incidence and mortality in racialized, socioeconomically disadvantaged, and geographically marginalized populations. These disparities reflect structural inequities in maternal health, preterm birth risk, quality of care, and access to protective interventions such as mother's own milk and donor human milk. Reducing necrotizing enterocolitis disparities requires multilevel solutions spanning health policy, equitable perinatal regionalization, investment in underresourced hospitals, and evidence-based neonatal care. Improving access to mother's own milk and pasteurized donor human milk are potentially the highest yield interventions.

articles.title: Recent Discoveries of Mechanisms Contributing to Necrotizing Enterocolitis.
articles.authors: Parikh R, Sellers-Porter C, Burge K et al.
articles.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a devastating neonatal intestinal disease driven by complex interactions between prematurity, microbial dysbiosis, immune dysregulation, and impaired intestinal barrier function. This article highlights recent advances in NEC pathogenesis, focusing on the role of toll-like receptor 4-mediated inflammatory signaling and the contribution of maternal inflammation and chorioamnionitis to disease susceptibility. Transcriptomic and spatial profiling studies further demonstrate that classical NEC and cardiac NEC possess distinct molecular signatures and identify diverse inflammatory endotypes within classical NEC. These findings support a precision medicine approach to NEC prevention and treatment.

articles.title: Impact of pregnancy on organ damage in systemic lupus erythematosus: a multicentre study.
articles.authors: Zucchi D, Cascarano G, Hulej G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pregnancy in SLE is associated with increased maternal and fetal risks but its impact on irreversible organ damage remains unclear. We assessed whether pregnancy independently contributes to short-term organ damage accrual in women with SLE.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from two tertiary referral centres with dedicated pregnancy clinics. Women fulfilling SLE classification criteria were included if complete damage assessments were available from 2 years before conception to 1 year after conception. Organ damage was assessed using the Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics Damage Index (SDI). Within-patient SDI changes during the pregnancy/early postpartum period were compared with the pre-pregnancy reference period. Given the limited number of events, effect sizes and CIs were prioritised. Sensitivity analyses included non-parametric effect sizes and restriction to one pregnancy per woman.
RESULTS: 165 pregnancies were included. At conception, most women were in remission or low disease activity. During pregnancy, 20.6% experienced disease flares, predominantly mild to moderate. Overall, cumulative damage remained stable: mean SDI increased from 0.18±0.43 one year before conception to 0.22±0.52 one year after conception (mean ΔSDI 0.04±0.21), with a median change of zero. Only seven pregnancies (4.2%; 95% CI 2.1% to 8.5%) showed new damage, limited to a single SDI item. Pre-existing damage was associated with progression (OR 6.77; 95% CI 1.43 to 32.05), and the frequency of progression was similar when the analyses were restricted to a single pregnancy per woman (6/126, 4.8%). By contrast, disease activity at the time of conception, flare-ups, obstetric complications and treatments were inconclusive. In the sensitivity analysis, the association with pre-existing damage was confirmed, and baseline disease activity also emerged as associated with damage progression (rank-biserial r=−0.55; 95% CI −0.78 to −0.27, p=0.030).
CONCLUSIONS: In women with predominantly well-controlled SLE, short-term organ damage accrual during pregnancy and the early postpartum period was uncommon. Pre-existing damage was associated with further accrual, while baseline disease activity also emerged as associated in the sensitivity analysis; however, the small number of events limits conclusions regarding other potential risk factors.

articles.title: A randomized controlled double-blinded trial to assess the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus in non-anemic pregnant women who receive oral iron supplementation.
articles.authors: Varghese J, Jacob M, Venkatesan P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnant women in India are routinely prescribed oral iron supplements as part of the national Anemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) program for anemia control. In women with iron-deficiency anemia, the benefits of iron supplementation during pregnancy, both for the mother and child, are very clear. In non-anemic pregnant women, however, the benefits of iron supplementation vis-à-vis associated risks that have been reported have not been studied adequately. Studies have suggested that iron may impair insulin secretion, thus increasing the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).
PRIMARY OBJECTIVE: To determine the incidence of GDM among non-anemic pregnant women receiving 60 mg/day of elemental iron as oral supplementation, compared with those receiving 30 mg/day.
SECONDARY OBJECTIVES: To assess beta-cell functional capacity and quantify unmethylated insulin promoter DNA (a sensitive and specific marker of beta-cell damage) in blood samples from the two study groups.
METHODS: This study is a randomized, parallel-group, double-blinded clinical trial, with 800 non-anemic primigravidae in each arm. One arm will receive oral supplementation at a dose of 60 mg per day (as per current national guidelines), while the other arm will receive 30 mg per day, for a duration of 12 weeks in the second trimester. The incidence of GDM in the two arms will be compared. Insulin secretion kinetics will be assessed using an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) done at the end of the intervention. Additionally, the unmethylated insulin promoter DNA in circulating free DNA (a marker of beta-cell damage) will be quantified in both arms.
DISCUSSION: The study's findings will provide important evidence relevant to the current national guidelines in India on universal oral iron supplementation during pregnancy. The results are expected to inform future policy decisions on whether universal supplementation for all pregnant women is appropriate or whether it should be targeted to those with low iron status.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: CTRI/2024/04/065301 [registered on 05/04/2024]-trial registered prospectively.

articles.title: Classification of gestational diabetes mellitus placental histopathological images based on MONAI and improved GAMatrix-YOLOv8.
articles.authors: Jiang Z, Wu W, Liu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) poses a significant threat to maternal and fetal health, and placental pathology is crucial for assessing disease severity. Traditional diagnosis relies on clinicians' visual assessment, which is often inefficient and subjective.
METHODS: To address these issues, we developed a MONAI-based image augmentation strategy and integrated the GAMatrix attention module within the YOLOv8 framework. Our study used a dataset of 5,065 placental pathology images (80% for training and 20% for validation) covering five pathology categories, supplemented by an external validation set of 500 images. A MONAI-based image augmentation pipeline was used to increase training-image diversity.
RESULTS: Four model configurations were compared: YOLOv8 trained on the original dataset, YOLOv8 trained with MONAI-based augmentation, GAMatrix-YOLOv8 trained on the original dataset, and GAMatrix-YOLOv8 trained with MONAI-based augmentation. In the original comparative analysis, YOLOv8 trained on the original dataset achieved a macro-F1 score of 95.56% (95% CI, 94.86%-96.26%) in internal validation. The GAMatrix-YOLOv8 model trained with MONAI-based augmentation showed the strongest overall performance among the evaluated configurations, while external image-level evaluation indicated persistent class-specific errors, particularly for thrombotic vascular lesion and chorangiosis.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that attention-enhanced YOLOv8 combined with MONAI-based augmentation may support placental histopathological image classification, but the results should be interpreted as image-level findings and require patient-level, multicenter, and prospective validation.

articles.title: Beyond women's burden: integrating male partners into contraceptive decision-making.
articles.authors: Garg P, Mangla M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contraceptive use and family planning have traditionally been viewed as women's responsibility, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Despite growing evidence highlighting the positive impact of male involvement in improving contraceptive uptake, continuation, and reproductive health outcomes, the participation of male partners remains limited. This review explores the critical role of male partners in contraceptive decision-making and synthesizes current evidence on the barriers impeding their participation. It further identifies strategies and interventions to foster shared responsibility in family planning and promote equitable reproductive health practices.
METHODS: A narrative review approach was adopted to collate global and regional evidence from peer-reviewed literature, policy reports, and relevant case studies. The review is structured around five core themes: sociocultural and gender norms, knowledge and educational barriers, limitations within healthcare systems, misconceptions around male contraceptive methods, and systemic challenges to implementation. The review also presents innovative, context-sensitive strategies for male engagement and future directions to enhance male participation in family planning.
RESULTS: The analysis reveals that male involvement remains suboptimal due to persistent patriarchal norms, misinformation, stigma, and limited access to male-centric contraceptive options. Existing family planning programs often lack couple-focused counseling and fail to provide inclusive services for men. However, interventions such as couple-based education, male-friendly clinics, community advocacy, gamified digital tools, and AI-enabled reproductive health platforms show promise in shifting attitudes and improving engagement. Success stories from countries including Tanzania, Vietnam, and India provide evidence for scalable, culturally adaptive models that facilitate male involvement.
CONCLUSION: Strengthening male participation is pivotal for achieving equitable reproductive health outcomes. Multi-level strategies, such as spanning education, service delivery, community norms, and policy integration, are essential to promote shared responsibility. Addressing systemic barriers, expanding male contraceptive choices, and leveraging technology can catalyze behavioral change and contribute to more inclusive, effective, and sustainable family planning programs.

articles.title: Humanization of care: a geospatial analysis of key indicators of quality and safety of health care and service in the Centre region, Cameroon.
articles.authors: Cheuyem FZL, Amani A, Ajong BN et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Integrating the principles of humanized care into healthcare systems is critical to promoting optimal well-being. In a context of limited resources, improving quality of care means identifying priority sites to optimize cost-effectiveness. The objective was to measure key indicators of quality and safety in health facilities and map priority health districts (HDs) for effective implementation of high-impact interventions in the Centre Region.
METHODS: We conducted a descriptive cross-sectional analysis of retrospective data from 32 HDs in the Centre Region for the period 2018-2022. Data were extracted from the national District Health Information System 2 (DHIS2) database in April 2023 and checked for completeness. The health indicators assessed were those defined in the Cameroon Health Sector Strategy for 2020-2030. Data were analyzed using R statistics version 4.2.3.
RESULTS: The density of the qualified healthcare workers was 13.7 per 10 000 inhabitants in 2022. Over the five-year study period, the density of doctors in rural areas declined by almost 20% by 2020, whereas urban areas experienced a concurrent increase. The Odza HD had the highest inpatient mortality rate over the five-year study period (49%). In rural areas, the Esse HD had the highest mortality rate (32.4%). Esse (18.8%) and Odza (6.7%) HDs had the highest perioperative mortality rates in rural and urban areas, respectively. Most of the urban HDs (5/8 = 62.5%) had a neonatal mortality rate higher than the regional median (RM = 3.1). Half of the rural HDs had a maternal mortality ratio higher than the RM = 118 per 1000 live births and the Mbandjock (357/1,000) and Mvog-Ada (285/1,000) HDs carried the highest burden in rural and urban areas respectively. More than two thirds of urban HDs recorded a proportion of free malaria treatment cases below the RM (14%).
CONCLUSIONS: Efforts to humanize healthcare in the Centre Region are hindered by persistent disparities in care quality and inconsistent policy implementation. Addressing these challenges requires timely implementation of a National Strategic Plan to Improve the Quality of Healthcare and Service Delivery, emphasizing on capacity building through training and supervision.

articles.title: Spectrum, management, and outcomes of non-obstetric neurological disorders in pregnancy: a descriptive case series from a tertiary centre in India.
articles.authors: Singh A, Davile M, Mundle S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurological disorders unrelated to obstetric pathology are an under-recognised cause of maternal morbidity in pregnancy, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Evidence describing their clinical spectrum, management, and outcomes remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective descriptive case series study at a tertiary care centre in central India between April 2024 and November 2025. Pregnant and postpartum women (≤6 weeks) diagnosed with neurological disorders of non-obstetric origin were included. Data on clinical presentation, neurological diagnoses, management, and maternal and neonatal outcomes were collected and analysed descriptively.
RESULTS: Among 1,860 deliveries, 17 women (9.1 per 1,000 deliveries) were diagnosed with non-obstetric neurological disorders. Structural intracranial lesions and autoimmune/demyelinating disorders were the most frequent diagnoses (each 29%). Ten women (65%) underwent caesarean section, and four (24%) required intensive care. Maternal mortality occurred in two women (12%), both with intracranial pathology. Fifteen women (88%) were discharged in stable condition, although three had residual neurological deficits. There were 15 live births; most neonates had favourable short-term outcomes, although preterm birth was common. One neonate developed transient neonatal myasthenia gravis.
CONCLUSIONS: This case series "Spectrum, management, and outcomes of non-obstetric neurological disorders in pregnancy: a descriptive case series from a tertiary centre in India"describes non-obstetric neurological disorders in pregnancy are heterogeneous and associated with significant maternal morbidity, particularly in women with intracranial pathology. Early diagnosis and coordinated multidisciplinary care are essential to optimise maternal and neonatal outcomes. Larger multicentre studies are needed to better define disease burden and predictors of adverse outcomes in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Gasless vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery(vNOTES): a safe and feasible approach for adnexal procedures.
articles.authors: Lu B, Wang Y, Zhang J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) is an important technique in minimally invasive gynecology. However, conventional vNOTES relies on CO₂ pneumoperitoneum, which may lead to complications such as postoperative pain and hypercapnia. Gasless vNOTES has been proposed as an alternative, but existing techniques often require additional abdominal wall lifting devices that increase procedural complexity and trauma. This study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of gasless vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) without abdominal wall retractors in benign adnexal surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective case series included patients who underwent benign adnexal surgery with gasless vNOTES between September 2024 and August 2025 at the International Peace Maternity and Child Health Hospital in Shanghai. Data were collected on baseline characteristics and surgical outcomes were collected, including history of abdominal surgery, pathological types of adnexal masses, surgical procedures, operative time, volume of intraoperative blood loss, complications, postoperative pain scores using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), time to first flatus, and length of postoperative hospital stay.
RESULTS: A total of 373 patients who underwent vNOTES for benign adnexal disease were included in the study. Overall, 370 (99.2%) patients successfully underwent gasless vNOTES, while one case required conversion to gas‑based vNOTES and two cases required conversion to transumbilical laparoendoscopic single-site surgery (TU-LESS) due to pelvic adhesions (conversion rate, 0.8%). In five cases (1.4%), in which the ovarian cyst was located anterior to the uterus and difficult to expose, brief pneumoperitoneum (< 5 min) was applied to retract the mass posterior to the uterus, after which gasless vNOTES was resumed following desufflation. Surgical procedures included ovarian cystectomy (314 cases, 84.9%), surgery for ectopic pregnancies (11 ruptured and 28 unruptured cases, 10.5%), and adnexectomy (10 cases, 2.7%). The mean operative time was 54.41 ± 25.94 min, and mean intraoperative blood loss was 25.63 ± 14.31 mL. No intraoperative complications, such as visceral injury or major hemorrhage, occurred. The median postoperative VAS pain scores were 1.0 (0, 2.0) at 6 h and 0 (0, 1.0) at 12 h. The mean time to first flatus was 7.12 ± 4.51 h, and the mean postoperative hospital stay was 22.09 ± 10.36 h. The postoperative infection…

articles.title: The role of the mitochondrial injury-mediated oxidative stress-sterile inflammation axis in varicocele-induced infertility: a narrative review.
articles.authors: Zhang J, Gao B, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Varicocele (VC) is a common correctable factor in male infertility, yet its effect on fertility and response to repair vary markedly among patients. This narrative review examines whether mitochondrial injury links the hemodynamic lesion to oxidative stress, sterile inflammation, and persistent spermatogenic damage. Venous stasis, hyperthermia, hypoxia, and metabolic disturbance can impair mitochondrial respiration, membrane potential, ATP production, and quality control. These changes increase mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and favor mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) oxidation and release. Oxidized mtDNA can engage cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) signaling in nucleated testicular cells, but the evidence is uneven. Human studies mainly document sperm mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative injury, DNA fragmentation, and altered inflammasome-related factors in seminal plasma. The integrated mtDNA-cGAS-STING-NLRP3 sequence is supported chiefly by animal and non-VC mechanistic models and has not been causally demonstrated in human VC. Anatomical and temporal context is therefore critical. Events in testicular somatic, germ, and immune cells during spermatogenesis cannot be inferred from epididymal, ejaculated-sperm, seminal-plasma, or female-tract findings. Endoplasmic reticulum stress and autophagy or mitophagy may modify mitochondrial injury, whereas programmed cell death, blood-testis barrier disruption, and epigenetic alterations may extend its consequences. Most of these links still require cell-resolved and longitudinal validation. Guideline-directed varicocele repair remains the clinical foundation. Sperm DNA fragmentation and other mechanism-related markers are useful research tools but lack source specificity or validated treatment thresholds, and pathway-directed therapies remain preclinical. The distinctive contribution of this review is a compartment-resolved and evidence-graded model that separates demonstrated findings from plausible links. It also defines the experiments needed to determine whether residual mitochondrial-inflammatory injury predicts reproductive outcomes or response to safe adjunctive treatment.

articles.title: Sarcopenia as an independent associated factor for urinary incontinence in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.authors: Guo Z, Huang L, Chen J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between sarcopenia and urinary incontinence (UI) in adults by synthesizing evidence from observational studies.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and CINAHL from inception until April 20, 2026. Observational studies reporting the odds ratio (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) for UI in adults with sarcopenia versus those without were included. Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed independently by two reviewers. Given anticipated clinical and methodological heterogeneity across the included studies (e.g., differences in sarcopenia diagnostic criteria, UI assessment tools, and study populations), we applied a random‑effects model. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on study design. Sensitivity and meta-regression analyses were performed to explore potential sources of heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Seven observational studies involving 45,273 participants were included. The pooled analysis demonstrated that sarcopenia was significantly associated with an higher odds of UI (OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.41-2.60, p < 0.001). Significant heterogeneity was observed (I² = 63.1%, p = 0.012), which indicates moderate between‑study variation, suggesting that the pooled estimate should be interpreted with caution and that the strength of the association may differ across study settings. In subgroup analysis by study design, the association remained significant in cross‑sectional studies (OR = 2.00, 95% CI: 1.39-2.86, p < 0.001) but was not statistically significant in the single prospective cohort study (OR = 1.70, 95% CI: 0.998-2.90, p = 0.051). Sensitivity and meta-regression analyses did not identify clear sources of the observed heterogeneity.
CONCLUSION: Sarcopenia is significantly associated with higher odds of urinary incontinence in adults. These findings highlight the potential importance of assessing and managing sarcopenia in individuals with or at risk for UI. Further high-quality prospective cohort studies are needed to strengthen causal inference.

articles.title: The Variability in the Pharmacokinetics of Follitropin Alfa: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Kirubakaran R, Michael TJF, Vollenhoven BJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite extensive research on the pharmacodynamics of follitropin alfa, a comprehensive synthesis of its pharmacokinetic variability is lacking. Understanding the interindividual and intraindividual variability in the pharmacokinetics of follitropin alfa may help inform dosing strategies by reducing variability in systemic exposure. This systematic review aimed to characterise the variability in the pharmacokinetics of follitropin alfa.
METHODS: Embase, PubMed, Scopus and citation mining of included articles were searched from database inception to 10 November 2025. Studies performed in humans, published in English which reported the pharmacokinetics, route of administration and dosing regimen of follitropin alfa were eligible for inclusion.
RESULTS: Fifteen eligible studies were evaluated. The pharmacokinetics of follitropin alfa were described by a two-compartment model following intravenous administration, and a one-compartment model with first-order absorption after intramuscular or subcutaneous administration. Follitropin alfa exhibited dose-proportional pharmacokinetics. Moderate interindividual variability (26-42%) in apparent clearance was reported following multiple subcutaneous administrations. Body weight influenced the pharmacokinetics of subcutaneously administered follitropin alfa. Comparable pharmacokinetic characteristics of follitropin alfa were observed across (i) originator and biosimilar preparations, (ii) healthy and infertile individuals, and (iii) subcutaneous and intramuscular routes of administration.
CONCLUSIONS: Weight-based dosing of follitropin alfa may reduce pharmacokinetic interindividual variability. However, whether this reduction in variability translates into more consistent ovarian response remains unclear and requires further investigation.

articles.title: Autoimmunity and Inflammaging in Male Infertility.
articles.authors: Monticciolo I, Di Simone N, Lomuscio V et al.
articles.abstract: Male factors contribute, alone or in combination with female-related ones, to approximately 40-50% of infertility in couples. Within the spectrum of male infertility, growing evidence indicates that autoimmune mechanisms and chronic inflammation can impair spermatogenesis, sperm function, and reproductive outcomes. The disruption of the testicular immune privilege, blood-testis barrier dysfunction, local inflammatory pathways, and antisperm antibodies represent the best-characterized immune-mediated mechanisms, although their clinical relevance varies and several mechanistic observations remain derived from preclinical models. Systemic autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases may also affect male reproductive function through inflammatory cytokines, endocrine dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, sexual dysfunction, and treatment-related gonadotoxicity. Emerging data also implicate the gut-testis axis and age-associated low-grade inflammation (inflammaging) as potential contributors to testicular immune remodeling, oxidative stress, and declining reproductive function. This narrative review is intended to encompass disease-specific available reviews and synthesize original research, clinical studies, and systematic reviews published mainly between 2010 and 2026. We distinguish established clinical evidence from experimental or hypothesis-generating data and discuss implications for fertility preservation, assisted reproduction, and individualized management. Integrating reproductive immunology with the clinical evaluation of male infertility may improve risk stratification while avoiding overinterpretation of still-limited immune biomarkers and therapeutic evidence.
