articles.title: The Gut-Immune-Endometrial Axis in Reproductive Failure: a Structured Narrative Review of Intestinal Dysbiosis, Systemic Inflammation, and Chronic Endometritis.
articles.authors: Rodrigues RS, Fontenele PA, Rocha JC et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic endometritis (CE) is a persistent inflammatory condition of the endometrium characterized by stromal plasma cell infiltration and is increasingly recognized in women with infertility, recurrent implantation failure (RIF), and recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL). Although traditionally considered a localized infectious process, heterogeneous treatment responses and recurrence suggest that broader immunological mechanisms may contribute in selected patients. This structured narrative review synthesizes clinical and mechanistic evidence relevant to a possible gut-immune-endometrial axis. A structured PubMed/MEDLINE search was conducted from database inception to December 31, 2025, and reference lists of relevant reviews and key primary studies were screened. Evidence was synthesized thematically across clinical, immunological, and translational domains. CE is associated with infertility and RPL, whereas findings in RIF populations are heterogeneous and strongly dependent on diagnostic criteria. CE is characterized by plasma cell infiltration, pro-inflammatory signaling, and activation of pathways including toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB). Separately, intestinal dysbiosis and barrier dysfunction may permit systemic translocation of microbial products such as lipopolysaccharide, thereby promoting low-grade inflammatory signaling. However, no direct human study has yet linked gut dysbiosis or endotoxemia to histologically confirmed CE within the same cohort. The proposed axis should therefore be regarded as a hypothesis-generating framework rather than an established causal pathway. CE is biologically heterogeneous and may arise from infectious, local microbial, immune-mediated, or systemic-inflammatory mechanisms that can overlap. Reverse causality and shared confounding factors are also plausible. At present, the model does not justify routine microbiome testing or gut-directed treatment for CE, but it defines priorities for prospective studies integrating microbiome profiling, systemic immune markers, and standardized endometrial phenotyping.

articles.title: Aggregation of Mutant p53 Alters Sialylated and Sulfated Glycan Profiles and Enhances Siglec-9 Ligand Availability in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.journal: Laboratory investigation; a journal of technical methods and pathology
articles.authors: Ikezaki M, Mori N, Takeda-Uchimura Y et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Mutant p53 proteins form aggregates, and the presence of such cytoplasmic p53 aggregates has predicted poor prognosis in several cancers including high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC). The existence of aberrant expressions of sialylated and sulfated glycans is a major feature of various cancers. At present, the correlation between the presence of cytoplasmic p53 aggregates and the existence of aberrant glycosylation in cancers is unclear. Here, we investigated whether the presence of p53 aggregates may affect sialylated and sulfated glycan profiles in HGSOC.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used the CL40 monoclonal antibody that recognizes sialyl 6-sulfo Lewis X and sialyl 6-sulfo N-acetyllactosamine and a cell-permeable p53 aggregation inhibitor ReACp53. HGSOC tissues were examined by immunohistochemistry with CL40. Expressions of GlcNAc-6-O-sulfotransferases (GlcNAc6STs) in HGSOC-derived OVCAR-3 cells were analyzed by means of semi-quantitative PCR. Binding of sialic acid-binding immunoglobulin-like lectin Siglec-9 to OVCAR-3 cells were analyzed by using His-tagged Siglec-9.
RESULTS: OVCAR-3 cells expressed CL40-reactive glycans, but CL40 reactivity was reduced by p53 disaggregation. Immunohistochemical analyses revealed expression of CL40-reactive glycans in p53 aggregate-positive HGSOC cases. Recognition of glycans by CL40 requires 6-O-sulfation of the N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) residues, which are catalyzed by GlcNAc6STs. mRNA expressions of GlcNAc6ST2/CHST4, GlcNAc6ST3/CHST5, and GlcNAc6ST5/CHST6 were down-regulated in the presence of ReACp53. Pretreatment of OVCAR-3 cells with CL40 prevented the binding of Siglec-9 and OVCAR-3 cells, which suggested that CL40 epitopes could be recognized by the Siglec-9 lectin.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results together suggest a novel mechanism of aberrant glycosylation in HGSOC associated with p53 aggregation.

articles.title: Preconception and early-pregnancy serum metal(loid) concentrations in relation to gestational glucose regulation: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Wu X, Meng Y, Wu W et al.
articles.abstract: Although metal(loid) exposure during pregnancy has been increasingly studied, evidence remains limited on whether serum metal(loid) concentrations measured before conception are related to glucose regulation during pregnancy. In this prospective cohort study, serum concentrations of multiple metal(loid)s were measured during the preconception period and early pregnancy. Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) was diagnosed using a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24-28 gestational weeks, and fasting, 1-h, and 2-h plasma glucose (PG) levels were assessed as continuous outcomes. Generalized linear regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR), and a multiple informant model were used to characterize individual, nonlinear, joint, and period-specific associations. During the preconception period, higher nickel (Ni) and lead (Pb) concentrations were associated with higher 2-h PG, whereas strontium (Sr) was inversely associated with fasting PG. During early pregnancy, cadmium (Cd) and titanium (Ti) were positively associated with 1-h PG, whereas Sr was inversely associated with 2-h PG. BKMR analyses were broadly consistent with several element-specific associations identified in the single-metal analyses. The multiple informant model also indicated that associations differed between the preconception and early-pregnancy measurement periods for some metal(loid)s. Overall, serum metal(loid) concentrations measured during the preconception and early-pregnancy periods showed period- and element-specific patterns of association with gestational glucose measures, supporting the need to consider preconception biomarker measurements in future studies.

articles.title: Cardiovascular and thromboembolic risks of sex hormone therapy: from contraception to transgender care.
articles.authors: Bonnet F, Vaduva P, Dosda A
articles.abstract: The risk of venous thromboembolism is increased with combined oral contraceptives, rises with the dose of ethinylestradiol, and is higher with desogestrel, gestodene, drospirenone or cyproterone acetate than with levonorgestrel; the determinant is not the generation of the pill but the residual androgen-receptor activity of the progestin, which modulates the hepatic effect of the estrogen. Age over 35 years, obesity, smoking and a family history of thrombosis amplify it. Pills based on a native estrogen have a more limited hepatic impact and rank below most ethinylestradiol combinations in contemporary cohorts, but their clinical safety is not demonstrated and no comparative outcome data exist for estetrol/drospirenone. Androgenicity is not a general marker of venous safety: injectable depot medroxyprogesterone acetate, given alone at supraphysiological doses, carries an increased risk. Myocardial infarction and stroke are also more frequent, but against a very low background - about 21 additional strokes and 10 additional infarctions per 100,000 person-years, four times fewer than the venous excess - and, unlike venous events, independent of progestin type. Menopause hormone therapy increases venous thromboembolic risk, especially in the first year; the route of administration is the main determinant, transdermal estradiol with micronized progesterone appearing safest. In cisgender men, testosterone deficiency carries increased cardiovascular risk, and randomized and real-world data support the safety of transdermal replacement, although more pulmonary embolism and atrial fibrillation have been observed. In trans women, observational data show an increased risk of stroke and venous thromboembolism, particularly with oral estradiol and cyproterone acetate, whereas recent large-scale data show no excess of major cardiovascular events with testosterone in trans men. The practical consequences are specific: no combined pill is acceptable after a venous thromboembolic event, with a thrombogenic mutation or with migraine with aura, native-estrogen pills included; transdermal estradiol should be preferred for menopause and feminising hormone therapy; and haematocrit should guide the dose and route of testosterone.

articles.title: Can the functional assessment of abdominal, diaphragmatic, and pelvic floor muscles reflect post-prostatectomy urinary incontinence severity?
articles.authors: Meslin M, Metanmo Ndziha S, Rose Dite Modestine J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-prostatectomy incontinence can substantially impair patients' quality of life. While rehabilitation typically targets the pelvic floor muscles, the role of the diaphragm and deep abdominal muscles is under-explored. This study aimed to determine the utility of evaluating and managing the transversus abdominis (TrA), diaphragm, and levator ani muscle (LAM) to facilitate post-prostatectomy urinary incontinence recovery.
METHODS: This single-center observational cohort study included 90 patients. During post-prostatectomy rehabilitation, we regularly assessed muscle capacity using a standardized clinical examinations comprising nine tests. Capacity score ranges were 0-2, 0-3, and 0-4 for the TrA, diaphragm, and levator ani. Data were collected until continence was restored or improvement plateaued, generally by 8 months. Incontinence was classified as severe, moderate, mild, or corrected. Spearman's rho assessed associations between incontinence grade and muscle scores.
RESULTS: Higher muscle scores were associated with lower incontinence severity. The most consistently significant correlation was with the TrA, followed by the diaphragm (P<0.05). LAM scores were no longer significantly correlated with incontinence from month 4 onward. Only patients in the corrected-continence group passed both TrA tests.
CONCLUSION: Improved functional capacity of the TrA, diaphragm, and LAM was associated with the recovery of urinary continence. This association was strongest for the TrA. Our findings support the functional assessment of these three muscles in the evaluation and management of post-prostatectomy urinary incontinence.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: IV (observational, single-center study without a control group).

articles.title: S2 Sacral Root Schwannoma: Laparoscopic Excision With ICG.
articles.authors: Kula H, Gumus RB, Kurt S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To demonstrate intravenous ICG-assisted fluorescence mapping as an assistive tool for improving surgical precision and tissue differentiation during laparoscopic S2 root schwannoma excision.
SETTING: Tertiary center specializing in an advanced laparoscopic surgery.
PARTICIPANTS: A 63-year-old woman presented with severe left-sided S2 dermatomal and pudendal pain and progressive neurologic findings. Her surgical history was notable for prior excision of endometriosis. Preoperative T2-weighted pelvic MRI demonstrated a 3-cm intrapelvic mass arising from the left S2 sacral root, consistent with a schwannoma.
INTERVENTIONS: Laparoscopic excision of the S2 sacral root schwannoma was performed with intravenous ICG fluorescence mapping (0.25 mg/kg, 15 minutes pre-dissection) [1]. Intraoperatively, the schwannoma demonstrated unexpectedly low fluorescence intensity relative to surrounding peripheral nerves and vascular structures, diverging from previously reported patterns of tumor hyperfluorescence. This hypofluorescence provided additional visual contrast alongside standard anatomic landmarks during dissection, without complication. At 6-month follow-up, electric shock-like pain had decreased and pudendal pain had improved from baseline. Deep tendon reflexes remained intact, and MRI confirmed no residual mass.
CONCLUSION: Pelvic schwannomas involving deep sacral nerve roots are rare and diagnostically challenging [2,3]. This case highlights a stepwise neuropelveological approach [4] - from anatomic identification of the S2 root to interfascicular neurolysis and nerve-sparing excision - as a reproducible framework for safe laparoscopic management. Notably, ICG fluorescence mapping did not follow the expected pattern of tumor hyperfluorescence [5]; the schwannoma instead appeared hypofluorescent relative to adjacent vascularized tissue.

articles.title: ZYX knockdown alleviates chemotherapy resistance in epithelial ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Hu X, Wang S, Yang R et al.
articles.abstract: The high mortality of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is largely attributable to chemotherapy resistance. This study identifies Zyxin (ZYX) as a key driver of this resistance. ZYX was overexpressed in chemoresistant EOC patients and corresponding paclitaxel-resistant (A2780/PTX) and cisplatin-resistant (A2780/DDP) cell lines. Functional experiments demonstrated that ZYX knockdown reversed chemoresistance by suppressing proliferation and migration, inducing apoptosis, and causing cell cycle arrest. Mechanistically, ZYX promotes resistance by interacting with Glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK3B), while its knockdown enhances paclitaxel sensitivity via β-tubulin upregulation and inhibits migration by reducing microfilament formation. Furthermore, ZYX knockdown potentiated paclitaxel efficacy in chemosensitive SKOV3 cells, both in vitro and in vivo. Our findings establish ZYX as a promising therapeutic target for overcoming chemotherapy resistance in EOC.

articles.title: A Platinum(IV)-Ursolic Acid Conjugate Overcomes Cisplatin Resistance in Ovarian Cancer by Targeting XPO1 and PARP1.
articles.authors: Pan Z, Qin Z, Qian Z et al.
articles.abstract: Cisplatin is a cornerstone chemotherapeutic for ovarian cancer, yet its clinical utility is constrained by severe systemic toxicity and acquired drug resistance. Here we report a novel platinum (IV) prodrug, US-CIS-OH, generated by conjugating cisplatin with ursolic acid (UA), a natural pentacyclic triterpenoid with intrinsic anticancer activity. US-CIS-OH, markedly increases platinum uptake and DNA platination in cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer cells, induces S- and G2/M-phase arrest and apoptosis, and suppresses cell migration and clonogenic growth. Chemoproteomic profiling indicates that US-CIS-OH directly engages the XPO1 and PARP1, and is associated with increased levels of cleaved caspase-3. In a cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer xenograft model, US-CIS-OH elicits marked tumor regression with minimal toxicity. This dual-acting system achieves synergistic effects from both the intact conjugated and bioreductively released cisplatin. Collectively, these results identify US-CIS-OH as a promising next-generation platinum-based agent to overcome cisplatin resistance by enhancing DNA damage, promoting apoptosis, and limiting metastatic traits.

articles.title: Matrix-Resolved Profiling of the Prenatal Chemical Exposome Reveals Selective Placental Retention and Fetal Transfer.
articles.authors: Marquès M, Gil-Solsona R, González-Ruiz A et al.
articles.abstract: Chemical exposure during human development, especially in utero, can disrupt many biological processes and increase disease vulnerability. Assessing the chemical landscape across the maternal-fetal interface is challenging. Here we address this challenge by conducting an exposome-based analysis across a suite of integrated maternal-fetal biological compartments: maternal urine, maternal serum, placental tissue, and umbilical cord serum. Using wide-scope liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) in 23 mother-infant dyads from the INSULIN cohort (Spain), we profiled 659 chemicals and transformation products, enabling a comprehensive characterization of prenatal chemical exposure and its compartment-specific distribution. We identified 76 unique compounds, including food additives, personal care products, pharmaceuticals, plasticizers, pesticides, flame retardants, industrial chemicals, and tobacco-related biomarkers. Matrix-resolved profiling revealed distinct compartmentalization patterns, with lipophilicity (logP) emerging as the primary physicochemical determinant of placental retention and transplacental transfer, while active transport mechanisms governed the fetal transfer of selected compounds despite properties inconsistent with passive diffusion. We report, for the first time, the transplacental passage of multiple emerging contaminants, including organophosphate esters, food-related compounds and personal care product ingredients. In contrast, several other contaminants─such as selected biomarkers of plastics, smoke, and personal care products─showed no evidence of transplacental transfer. These findings highlight the value of comprehensive, multi-matrix exposome profiling for assessing prenatal chemical exposures and provide a scalable framework for exposome-wide association studies in pregnancy cohorts and beyond.

articles.title: Image-Guided Magnetic Microrobots for Microplastic Capture and Biofilm Removal in the Female Reproductive System.
articles.authors: Yurtsever FM, Arya S, Maráková E et al.
articles.abstract: The health of the female reproductive system is increasingly threatened by emerging environmental contaminants that cause potential bacterial infections, cancer, and fertility problems. Yet effective strategies for the localized removal of these contaminants remain largely unexplored. Among these contaminants, microplastics have emerged as a major global health concern, with growing evidence of their accumulation in human tissues and associated with infectious diseases, carcinogenesis, cellular aging, and infertility due to direct or indirect contact with synthetic fabrics, plastic kitchenware, and disposable feminine hygiene products. Despite these risks, the removal of retained microplastics, particularly from sensitive reproductive environments, remains a significant challenge in biomedical research. Here, we report an image-guided magnetic soft microrobot platform designed for targeted microplastic capture and biofilm eradication within the female reproductive system. Magnetic soft microrobots were fabricated using a droplet solidification method and functionalized with a polydopamine coating via self-polymerization to enhance the surface adhesion and capture efficiency. Real-time visualization and precise navigation were enabled under X-ray fluoroscopy through the incorporation of tantalum-based contrast agents. Functionally, the magnetic soft microrobots inhibited up to 67% of biofilm growth and achieved microplastic capture efficiencies of up to 80% in phosphate-buffered saline and 50% in simulated vaginal fluid, demonstrating a robust performance under biologically relevant conditions. This study demonstrates the integration and application of image-guided microrobots for the removal of microplastics and biofilms in the female reproductive system, offering a promising strategy for minimally invasive interventions to protect reproductive health from environmental pollutants.

articles.title: Haloacetic Acid Disinfection Byproducts in Follicular Fluid and In Vitro Fertilization Outcomes: A Prospective Cohort Study in China.
articles.authors: Zhu JQ, Deng YL, Miao Y et al.
articles.abstract: Drinking water disinfection byproducts (DBPs), particularly haloacetic acids (HAAs), can exert adverse effects on oocyte quality and embryo development. However, there has been a paucity of human evidence. We included 1176 women who underwent 1306 in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles from the Tongji Reproductive and Environmental cohort (2018-2021). Dichloroacetic acid (DCAA) and trichloroacetic acid (TCAA) concentrations in follicular fluid were assessed. Elevated quartiles of DCAA and TCAA concentrations in follicular fluid had significant inverse exposure-response associations with all IVF outcomes (e.g., 16.67% and 10.14% reductions in proportion of clinical pregnancy for the highest vs lowest quartiles of DCAA and TCAA concentrations, respectively; both P for trend <0.01). The effects were more pronounced in women undergoing non-long GnRH agonist regimens and IVF insemination technology. The serial mediation analyses identified that a sequential pathway (oocyte → mature oocyte → zygotes with two pronuclei → good-quality embryos) mediated 21.1%-33.9% of HAA exposure-related inferior clinical pregnancy outcomes (implantation, clinical pregnancy, and live birth). Our findings suggest that elevated levels of HAAs in follicular fluid are associated with decreased oocyte quality and subsequent inferior IVF outcomes, strengthening human evidence that exposure to drinking water DBPs has detrimental effects on early reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: Decentralized Solar-Driven Plant Factories Secure an Adequate Global Vegetable Supply beyond the Electricity Grid and Water Limitations.
articles.authors: Wang C, Zhang D, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Conventional open-field vegetable production is increasingly constrained by climate volatility and natural resource endowments, creating supply instabilities and shortages that threaten global food resilience and human health. Here, we integrate solar photovoltaics and atmospheric water harvesting with plant factories, creating a technically mature off-grid agricultural system using plant factories (OASIS). By decoupling production from local water and grid infrastructure, OASIS significantly expands the area suitable for cultivation. Globally, OASIS can meet the recommended upper vegetable intake (600 g capita-1 day-1) for at least 98.3% of the population, leveraging mostly non-arable land. Cropland substitution could spare approximately 578,000 km2 for staple food production and, under the idealized zero-operational-loss case, reduce agricultural nitrogen and phosphorus losses by up to 9.90 and 0.95 Tg yr-1, respectively. Estimated global, production-weighted levelized costs were 3.8-4.0 USD kg-1 across six scenarios. Under the 600 g capita-1 day-1 scenario with cropland substitution, OASIS offered cost advantages over existing production benchmarks in 115 of 166 comparable countries, including all 26 low-income countries, which could meet modeled supply targets with a 32.2% average cost advantage. These results highlight OASIS's potential to advance resilient, clean vegetable production and the Sustainable Development Goals across food security, health, and land conservation.

articles.title: Multimatrix Biomonitoring and Transplacental Transfer of Legacy and Emerging PFAS in Korean Pregnant Women.
articles.authors: Shin H, Park NY, Lee YA et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal-fetal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) cannot be adequately characterized using single biological matrices because compound-specific distribution patterns vary according to physicochemical properties and elimination pathways. We measured 33 legacy, precursor, and emerging PFAS in maternal serum, plasma, urine, and cord serum from Korean singleton pregnancies (n = 151) to characterize matrix-specific exposure profiles, transplacental transfer, and associations with maternal and neonatal factors. Matrix-specific detection patterns distinguished predominantly protein-bound PFAS detected in blood matrices from short-chain, renally excreted PFAS prevalent in urine at the population level. Notably, the precursor 6:2 diPAP showed a relatively high estimated maternal-cord concentration ratio, whereas the alternative PFAS 9Cl-PF3ONS was consistently detected in maternal blood and cord serum, suggesting compound-specific distribution patterns compared with regulated legacy PFAS. Associations with fetal growth indicators were modest, matrix- and sex-specific, and interpreted as exploratory. Overall, these findings suggest that multimatrix biomonitoring can reveal matrix-specific PFAS detection and distribution patterns that may not be captured by single-matrix approaches. However, maternal-cord comparisons should be interpreted cautiously because maternal samples were collected during pregnancy rather than at delivery.

articles.title: Preconception, Prenatal and Postnatal PM2.5 Exposure and Neurodevelopmental Disorder Risk among Medicaid Recipients.
articles.authors: Shupler M, Qiu X, Huybrechts KF et al.
articles.abstract: Evidence linking ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure to childhood neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) remains mixed. We conducted a cohort study (2001-2013) of 1,547,244 Medicaid-enrolled mother-child pairs to assess associations between zip-code-level PM2.5 exposure during preconception (12-week), prenatal (37-week), and postnatal (3-year) periods and children's NDD risk. Cox proportional hazards models estimated risks of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), learning difficulty (LD), speech/language disorder, developmental coordination disorder (DCD), intellectual disability, and behavioral disorder, adjusting for demographics, meteorological characteristics, and area-level socioeconomic indicators. Distributed lag models assessed critical exposure windows and cumulative effects. A 10 μg/m3 increase in cumulative prenatal PM2.5 exposure was associated with higher ASD risk (Hazard ratio (HR):1.17; 95%CI:1.00,1.37). A critical exposure window for ASD existed during gestational weeks 23-31 (HR:1.09 95%CI:[1.02,1.17]). Cumulative prenatal PM2.5 exposure was associated with increased ID risk among Hispanic individuals (HR:1.57 95%CI:[1.02,2.43]) but not among other races/ethnicities. Postnatal PM2.5 exposure was associated with increased ADHD risk (HR:1.17 95%CI:[0.94,1.46]) at age 0 years and DCD risk (HR:1.72 95%CI:[0.97,3.07]) at age 1 year. No associations between PM2.5 exposure and other NDDs were found. Prenatal and postnatal PM2.5 exposure may increase the risk of some NDDs among low-income U.S. children.

articles.title: Artificial Light at Night and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: Socioeconomic Inequality in the China Birth Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Li YY, Hu LW, Wang LB et al.
articles.abstract: Evidence regarding the association of outdoor artificial light at night (ALAN) with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs) remains limited. Between February 2018 and December 2022, 241,608 participants from the China Birth Cohort Study (CBCS), which enrolled individuals from 17 provinces across China, were included in the analysis. HDP was defined by physician clinical diagnosis. We estimated outdoor ALAN within 500 m, sourced from the VIIRS/DNB, using the address of each participant, and categorized it into quartiles (lowest [Q1] as reference). We used generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) to assess the association between ALAN exposure and HDPs. Effect modification by province-level per capita gross domestic product (GDP), household income, and other factors was also explored. A total of 9383 (3.88%) participants were diagnosed with HDPs. After adjusting for covariates, compared with Q1, the odds ratios (ORs) for HDPs were 1.14 (95% CI: 1.07-1.21) for quartile 2 (Q2), 1.21 (95% CI: 1.13-1.29) for quartile 3 (Q3), and 1.09 (95% CI: 1.02-1.17) for quartile 4 (Q4). Furthermore, province-level per capita GDP and household income modified the associations between the ALAN and HDPs. Compared to participants residing in low-GDP areas with low income, the strongest effect estimate was observed among participants residing in high-GDP areas with low income (OR: 1.15 [1.09-1.20] vs 0.97 [0.91-1.04] for HDPs).

articles.title: Absolute and Amplified Virus Detection by Isotope Dilution after Catalytic Hairpin Assembly.
articles.authors: Peng J, Zhu Y, Zhang X et al.
articles.abstract: The detection of viruses is of great significance for the diagnosis of related diseases. However, current virus detection often faces two challenges: first, due to the complex matrix of physiological samples, detection methods often fail to provide accurate quantitative results; second, conventional PCR-related signal amplification procedures are often challenged by issues such as primer interference and non-specific amplification. Herein, we developed an absolute and amplified virus detection strategy by coupling isotope dilution and catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA). The high-risk cervical cancer-related biomarkers were detected with a wide linear detection range (5-30,000 pM) and detection limits in the pM level. To our best knowledge, this is the first amplified metal isotope dilution quantification strategy for biomolecules.

articles.title: Study on Chenopodiastrum hybridum's Anti-inflammatory and Antioxidant Effects in Zebrafish: Mechanism Against Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Yang S, Feng X, Wu P et al.
articles.abstract: Chenopodiastrum hybridum (CH) is an edible and folk medicinal plant, yet its efficacy and molecular mechanisms against ovarian cancer (OC) remain unclear, restricting its antitumor application. This study investigated the anti-OC effects and underlying mechanisms of CH via dose-effect weighted network pharmacology to provide experimental evidence for its clinical and medicinal development. This study determined the total flavonoid content of CH refined extract (CHRE) and assessed its inhibitory effect on OVCAR-3 cell proliferation. CHRE's antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities were evaluated by free-radical scavenging ability and detection of ROS, NO, TNF-α, and IL-6 levels. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were applied to screen core targets and key pathways, with RT-qPCR verifying target gene expression. Flavonoid-rich CHRE significantly inhibited OVCAR-3 cell growth, exhibiting potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. The estrogen signaling pathway was identified as the core regulatory pathway. CH's key active compounds bound stably to the core targets (epidermal growth factor receptor [EGFR], ESR1, SRC, HSP90AA1, AKT1). RT-qPCR revealed downregulated mRNA levels of EGFR, AKT1, KDR, ESR1, and upregulated HSP90AA1 expression. CH suppresses OC proliferation by activating the estrogen signaling pathway to alleviate oxidative stress and inflammation. This study elucidates CH's anti-OC mechanism, offering valuable references for developing novel natural botanical drugs and auxiliary clinical therapies for OC.

articles.title: Precise Mutation Detection in Low-Abundance Tumor-Derived Extracellular Vesicles via Microfluidic Immunomagnetic Reversible Affinity Capture.
articles.authors: Xu X, Liang S, Chen H et al.
articles.abstract: Molecular diagnostic technologies based on liquid biopsy are increasingly vital for clinical tumor molecular profiling. Compared to highly fragmented and easily degradable cell-free DNA (cfDNA), extracellular vesicles (EVs) offer distinct advantages by protecting nucleic acids from degradation. Enrichment of tumor-derived EVs using specific surface markers significantly enhances the relative abundance of mutant nucleic acids, establishing a foundation for highly sensitive mutation detection. To fully leverage this enrichment strategy, we developed the MIRACLE platform, an integrated system combining microfluidic magneto-controllable reversible affinity capture with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF-MS) for efficient, multiplexed detection of tumor-derived EV DNA mutations. The platform utilizes anti-EpCAM-functionalized magnetic beads to construct a reversible capture interface within a herringbone-structured microfluidic chip, achieving over 98% capture efficiency of tumor-derived EVs under turbulence-enhanced conditions. Following EV lysis, a 7-plex multiplex single base extension assay coupled with MALDI-TOF-MS analysis enables simultaneous and accurate identification of seven mutation sites with single-nucleotide resolution. Furthermore, the platform achieved a detection limit of 0.05% for tumor-derived EVs within a background of wild-type EVs. Validation using plasma samples from 26 colorectal cancer patients demonstrated 96.2% accuracy and 93.3% sensitivity, successfully detecting key mutations including G12V, G13D, and G12D. The tumor EV enrichment-guided mutation detection strategy established in this study provides a precise, multiplexed, and clinically applicable approach for molecular profiling in liquid biopsy.

articles.title: Polarization-Gradient Engineering of InGaN Nanorods for Hybrid Mechanical-Optical Energy Harvesting.
articles.authors: Wong SS, Lin ZY, Chiu YC et al.
articles.abstract: Integrating mechanical and optical energy harvesting within a single piezoelectric semiconductor platform remains challenging because photoexcited carriers readily screen the piezoelectric potential and suppress nanogenerator output. Here, we realize highly crystalline, polarity-defined N-polar InGaN/GaN nanorods with opposite axial In gradients and correspondingly opposite built-in electrostatic profiles. Depth-sensitive, angle-resolved hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (AR-HAXPES) reveals opposite equilibrium band-bending profiles─surface carrier accumulation in In-increasing nanorods but depletion in In-decreasing ones─showing that polarization grading redistributes as-grown mobile carriers and that only the In-increasing configuration establishes the internal electrostatics needed to suppress carrier screening and preserve the piezoelectric potential during nanogenerator operation. In vertically integrated nanogenerators (VINGs), this asymmetry produces a much larger output from the In-increasing device than from the In-decreasing one, together with more favorable transient behavior and energy-storage performance, and is further amplified under illumination, which enhances the output of the In-increasing device while suppressing that of the In-decreasing one, consistent with opposite photoscreening dynamics set by the grading-defined built-in fields. These results demonstrate hybrid mechanical-optical energy harvesting in direct-band gap piezoelectric semiconductors such as III-nitrides, where light and strain act cooperatively rather than competitively.

articles.title: "A new normal": A qualitative study of emotional and psychosocial concerns in early-onset colorectal cancer survivors.
articles.authors: Kravchenko T, Vitous CA, Bradley SE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) has increased over the past three decades. Diagnoses coincide with formative emotional and social life stages, creating challenges for patients overlooked by survivorship guidelines. This study explored the emotional and psychosocial impacts of EOCRC.
METHODS: We conducted interviews with 63 patients with EOCRC at seven academic medical centers. Interviews focused on emotional and psychosocial needs and were analyzed using thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Five themes were identified: (1) emotional and psychosocial distress; (2) dealing with uncertainty; (3) coming to terms with a "new normal"; (4) managing distress; and (5) role of medical providers. Patients described disruptions to life events and access to EOCRC-specific mental health and informational resources was an unmet need.
CONCLUSION: EOCRC profoundly impacts emotional and psychosocial well-being. Individuals experienced difficulties adjusting to a "new normal" affecting identity formation, family planning, and career progression. Access to tailored support services was lacking.

articles.title: The longevity dividend: A systems-thinking framework for harnessing the silver economy in low- and middle-income countries.
articles.authors: Franco ÓH, Trujillo-Cáceres SJ, Verschuren WMM et al.
articles.abstract: Population ageing is accelerating in low- and middle-income countries, where accumulated life-course inequalities, labour informality, and limited social protection shape conditions in later life. Conventional policy narratives have framed older adults as fiscal burdens, overlooking the productive and social value embedded in extended healthy life years and the structural determinants that constrain participation. This narrative review introduces the 'longevity dividend', a systems-thinking conceptual framework that positions functional ability across the life course as the central objective of ageing policy in low- and middle-income countries. Drawing on comparative policy experiences from Vietnam, Brazil, Colombia, Ethiopia, and Sri Lanka, and synthesising evidence from the literature on global health, health systems, and development, we examine how legislative, economic, health and social care, educational, and governance reforms interact to influence functional capacity, equity, and economic participation at older ages. The framework identifies five interconnected policy pillars - legislative and regulatory reforms, financial and economic inclusion, health and social infrastructure, educational and capacity building, and monitoring, surveillance and data systems - as the structural enablers of the longevity dividend. We further delineate cross-cutting opportunities and persistent challenges, including gender-based inequities, digital exclusion, and weak longitudinal data systems. We argue that reframing population ageing as a policy investment in functional capacity and social participation, rather than a demographic liability, provides a coherent foundation for integrating ageing policy within broader development and labour agendas in low- and middle-income countries. A, multisectoral approach oriented to the life course is essential for designing ageing policies that are equitable, sustainable, and institutionally resilient.

articles.title: Hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, and risk of type 2 diabetes: Evidence from the E3N-generations cohort.
articles.authors: Hachem S, Vaduva P, Laouali N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Evidence on hysterectomy and the risk of type 2 diabetes is limited, particularly regarding age at surgery. We assessed whether hysterectomy, with or without bilateral oophorectomy, is associated with incident type 2 diabetes, and whether this association is modified by age at surgery.
STUDY DESIGN: We followed 82,472 women from the E3N-Generations cohort, free of diabetes at baseline in 1992, until 2008 (median follow-up 16 years). Hysterectomy and oophorectomy were modelled as time-dependent exposures. Hazard ratios were estimated using Cox models with age as the time scale, adjusted for lifestyle, metabolic, and reproductive factors.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Incidence of type 2 diabetes.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 2318 women developed type 2 diabetes. In fully adjusted models, hysterectomy combined with bilateral oophorectomy was associated with a higher risk of type 2 diabetes (hazard ratio 1.23, 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.43) compared with women who underwent neither procedure, whereas hysterectomy alone was not (1.06, 0.91-1.24). Bilateral oophorectomy alone was not associated with the risk of incident type 2 diabetes. The association with hysterectomy and bilateral oophorectomy was strongest among women operated on before age 45 (1.70, 1.35-2.15); it was similarly elevated when the age threshold was changed to 40 (1.54, 1.08-2.20). There was significant heterogeneity by age at surgery for hysterectomy with bilateral oophorectomy (p = 0.001) and for hysterectomy alone (p = 0.010).
CONCLUSIONS: Hysterectomy with bilateral oophorectomy was associated with an increased risk of incident type 2 diabetes, independently of conventional metabolic risk factors. This excess risk was particularly pronounced among women who underwent surgery before age 45.

articles.title: Synoptic reporting of cytoreductive surgical procedures for patients with peritoneal malignancy based on the PSOGI-ESGO-ISSPP consensus.
articles.journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
articles.authors: Bhatt A, Moran B, Fotopoulou C et al.
articles.abstract: Cytoreductive surgery (CRS), for peritoneal malignancies (PM) is performed with the goal of achieving a CC-0 resection. However, the extent of peritonectomy and type of visceral resections (oncological versus non-oncological) performed during CRS vary among surgeons and lack standardization. The classification of peritonectomy procedures was revised by a consensus among some of the most experienced CRS surgeons in the world, defining the subdivisions and boundaries of each procedure. A format of documenting the extent of peritoneal resection was created which is an important research tool. To precisely report the extent and complexity of CRS, other aspects like the extent of exploration of the abdominal cavity and occult peritoneal spaces, the peritoneal disease extent and the visceral resections performed should be documented in a uniform manner. In the era of precision medicine, CRS needs to be standardized as much as possible. Thus, the working group for the Lyon consensus has created a form for synoptic reporting for CRS in an effort to further standardize CRS and facilitate future research. This form incorporates the surgical Peritoneal Cancer Index (PCI) including morphological appearance of PM, peritonectomy procedures and extent of peritoneal resection, visceral resections (oncological versus non-oncological), lymphadenectomy, extra-abdominal resections, abdominal wall resections, reconstruction procedures, and residual PCI. An online platform has been developed to generate structured operative reports incorporating all the details in this form (www.crs-report.com). Synoptic reporting will facilitate research and help define surgical strategies. It will help classify CRS according to its complexity clarifying formulation of recommendations for perioperative care.

articles.title: Phase II study of cabozantinib in recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer after progression on platinum-based chemotherapy (CABOCOL).
articles.authors: Coquan E, Vion R, Colomba-Blamemble E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The antiangiogenic pathway is an effective target for recurrent uterine cervical carcinoma (rCC). This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of cabozantinib monotherapy for rCC.
PATIENTS & METHODS: This open-label phase II study (NCT04205799) enrolled patients with rCC who previously received platinum-based chemotherapy. Patients received oral cabozantinib (60 mg daily) until progression or discontinuation from any cause. The main objective was based on joint primary endpoint of efficacy (3-month disease control rate, DCR3) and safety (proportion of patients with grade ≥ 2 (CTCAE v5.0) gastro-intestinal (GI) perforation, GI-vaginal and/or genito-urinary (GU) fistula events) according to a Bryant-and-Day design. Key secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), duration of response (DOR) and safety.
RESULTS: Among 57 patients enrolled, 54 received cabozantinib: median age was 55.5 years, 18 patients (33.3%) had received more than two prior lines of treatment; 28 patients (51.9%) had been previously treated with bevacizumab. Median duration of follow-up was 8.9 months. DCR3 was 46.3% [95% CI, 32.8-60.3]. Fistula/perforation occurred in 5 (9.3%) patients. Objective response rate was 9.3%, with a median DOR of 2.5 months. Median PFS was 2.8 months (95% CI, 2.5-4.6). Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 51.9% of patients, most commonly asthenia (15%), hypertension (9%) and mucositis (6%). Dose reductions and treatment interruptions were reported in 26 (48%) and 24 (44%) patients, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Cabozantinib demonstrates efficacy comparable to other anti-angiogenic monotherapy in rCC; however, modest benefit and toxicity do not support further monotherapy development.

articles.title: Mapping perinatal health interventions for improving perinatal outcomes in Australia: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Mulu GB, Tessema GA, Gebremedhin AT et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To synthesise existing evidence on perinatal health interventions implemented in Australia to improve perinatal outcomes.
STUDY DESIGN: Scoping review.
METHODS: The scoping review followed Arksey and O'Malley's methodological framework, refined by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI), and was reported in accordance with the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews checklist. A systematic search was undertaken in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and CINAHL for literature published from 01 January 2000 to 30 September 2025, supplemented by grey literature. Structured programs, models of care, and policy initiatives aimed at improving perinatal health outcomes in Australia were included and synthesised narratively.
RESULTS: Of the 3649 records identified from five databases and grey literature, 59 studies were included. Observational cohort designs were the most common (18; 30.5%). Most studies (31; 52.5%) were conducted in New South Wales, Victoria, and Queensland, and a few (8; 13.6%) in remote settings. Midwifery continuity-of-care models were the most frequent interventions (16; 27.1%), followed by clinical and biomedical risk-targeted interventions (15; 25.4%). Preterm birth (12; 20.3%) was the most reported outcome. In 52.5% of studies, authors reported improvements in maternal and neonatal outcomes. Only (23; 39%) studies were specifically targeted at Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women. Implementation and sustainability plans were reported in (30: 50.8%) studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Continuity models of care and risk-targeted interventions were associated with improved perinatal outcomes. However, most evidence comes from metropolitan settings; evidence from remote areas, where the burden is greatest, remains uncertain. Equitable progress will require culturally appropriate and community-led models of care in regions of greatest need.

articles.title: Bizarre But Benign: A Case Report of an EHHADH::RAD51B Rearranged Endometrial Polyp With Bizarre Stromal Cells.
articles.journal: International journal of gynecological pathology : official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Pathologists
articles.authors: Cardenas JC, Felicelli C
articles.abstract: Endometrial polyps with bizarre stromal cells are a rare histological variant of endometrial polyps characterized by striking nuclear atypia that can mimic features of malignant mesenchymal neoplasms, particularly Müllerian adenosarcoma (MA). Despite their alarming cytological appearance, these lesions typically follow a benign clinical course, making an accurate diagnosis essential to avoid unnecessary aggressive surgical interventions. Here, we present the case of a 53-yr-old woman with a 3-mo history of postmenopausal bleeding. Imaging revealed an 18 mm endometrial lesion with circumferential Doppler flow. Subsequent hysteroscopic resection and histopathological examination identified an endometrial polyp containing atypical, enlarged, and hyperchromatic stromal spindle cells with characteristic "smudged" chromatin. Mitotic activity was negligible, and there was no evidence of the leaf-like architecture or periglandular cuffing typical of MA. Immunohistochemical profiling showed diffuse positivity for CD10 and HMGA2, p53 wild-type expression, and a low Ki-67 proliferation index (<5%). Molecular analysis via FusionPlex Next Generation Sequencing revealed an EHHADH::RAD51B fusion, a novel gene fusion that expands the limited body of molecular data on endometrial polyps with bizarre stromal cells.

articles.title: Concentration-dependent effects of 2-oxothiazolidine-4-carboxylate during bovine oocyte in vitro maturation on oxidative status and embryo quality.
articles.authors: Yağcıoğlu S, Arıcı R, Ersoy N et al.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of supplementing bovine in vitro maturation medium with 2-oxothiazolidine-4-carboxylate (OTC), a cysteine precursor, on oocyte quality, intracellular oxidative status, embryo development, and gene expression in oocytes and derived blastocysts. Oocytes were matured in TCM-199 maturation medium supplemented with 0 (control), 1, 2, or 4 mM OTC, followed by in vitro fertilization and embryo culture. Nuclear maturation, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), glutathione (GSH) levels, embryo development, blastocyst quality, and expression of genes associated with developmental competence were evaluated. OTC supplementation significantly reduced intracellular ROS levels in all treated groups compared with the control. Intracellular GSH concentrations remained unchanged. OTC supplementation reduced the proportion of oocytes reaching the MII stage, whereas cleavage and blastocyst formation rates were not significantly affected in the separate set of oocytes subjected to IVF. Blastocysts derived from oocytes matured with 1 and 2 mM OTC contained significantly higher total cell numbers than controls. Gene expression analyses demonstrated concentration-dependent changes in selected oocyte and blastocyst transcripts. In conclusion, OTC exerted concentration-dependent effects on bovine oocyte maturation and subsequent embryo characteristics. OTC reduced intracellular ROS without altering total intracellular GSH, while 1-2 mM OTC increased blastocyst total cell number without increasing blastocyst yield. However, OTC supplementation reduced MII-stage maturation, and its effects on selected oocyte and blastocyst transcripts varied with concentration. These findings demonstrate endpoint-specific responses to OTC supplementation and support further investigation of its effects during bovine IVM.

articles.title: Intimate partner violence during pregnancy and adverse birth outcomes in Australia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Sexual & reproductive healthcare : official journal of the Swedish Association of Midwives
articles.authors: Seidu AA, Kundu S, Aggrey PA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Intimate partner violence (IPV) during pregnancy is a serious public health concern with potential harm to mothers and newborns. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised Australian studies examining the association between IPV or family violence during pregnancy and preterm birth (PTB), low birth weight (LBW), small for gestational age (SGA), stillbirth (SB), and miscarriage.
METHODS: English-language, peer-reviewed original studies conducted in Australia and reporting IPV during pregnancy as the exposure and at least one specified adverse birth outcome were sought from inception to March 2026 in Scopus, Medline, Emcare, Web of Science, and CINAHL. Two reviewers independently screened records at title, abstract, and full-text stages, with conflicts resolved by consensus. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects models. Quality was appraised with Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and heterogeneity, publication bias, and sensitivity analyses were assessed.
RESULTS: Ten studies comprising 230,601 women met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of IPV during pregnancy was 7.20% (95% CI, 3.75, 13.37; I2 = 99.9%, p < 0.001). IPV was significantly associated with preterm birth (AOR 1.30; 95% CI: 1.14, 1.48; I2 = 29.7%, p = 0.171) and low birth weight (AOR 1.70; 95% CI: 1.07, 2.69; I2 = 36%, p = 0.179). Higher but non-significant odds were observed for stillbirth (AOR 1.29; 95% CI: 0.21, 7.86; I2 = 83.3%, p = 0.018) and SGA (AOR 1.37; 95% CI: 0.18, 10.43; I2 = 92.2%, p < 0.001). One study reported an unadjusted association with miscarriage (OR 2.00; 95% CI: 1.55, 2.55).
CONCLUSION: IPV during pregnancy is associated with increased odds of adverse birth outcomes, significantly so for PTB and LBW, supporting routine antenatal IPV screening and integrated support within maternity care. Interpretation warrants caution given observational designs, few contributing studies, and substantial heterogeneity. Further Australian research is needed.

articles.title: Prenatal PFOS impairs offspring cognition via HDAC and translational repression.
articles.authors: Niu X, Xi R, Tan Y et al.
articles.abstract: Perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) is a persistent environmental pollutant widely detected in human cord blood and breast milk, raising concerns about its neurodevelopmental toxicity. While epidemiological and animal studies have linked prenatal PFOS exposure to cognitive deficits, the molecular mechanisms-particularly those involving translational regulation-remain unclear. The present study tested whether prenatal PFOS exposure induces hippocampal-dependent cognitive deficits through histone deacetylase (HDAC) overactivation and eukaryotic initiation factor 2α (eIF2α)-mediated translational repression. Pregnant Wistar rats received vehicle or PFOS (0.5 or 2 mg/kg/day) from gestation day 1-21. Offspring cognitive function was assessed using the Morris water maze on postnatal day 28; hippocampal tissue was collected for histopathology, apoptosis, HDAC activity, and expression of phosphorylated PKR-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase (p-PERK), phosphorylated eIF2α (p-eIF2α), activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP), small ubiquitin-like modifier 1/2 (SUMO1/2), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and protein phosphatase 1 (PP1). Maternal PFOS exposure impaired learning and memory, reduced normal neuron density, and increased neuronal apoptosis. PFOS elevated HDAC activity and activated the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP integrated stress response (ISR) pathway, while reduced protein levels of SUMO1/2, BDNF, and PP1-despite elevated mRNA levels, suggesting translational repression. To test whether HDAC overactivation directly contributes to these changes, we pretreated PC12 cells with trichostatin A (TSA), a pan-HDAC inhibitor. TSA partially reversed PFOS-induced apoptosis, suppressed HDAC overactivation, attenuated ISR activation, and restored SUMO1/2, BDNF, and PP1 expression. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that prenatal PFOS exposure causes hippocampal-dependent cognitive deficits through HDAC overactivation and eIF2α-mediated translational repression, shifting the focus from transcriptional to translational control and identifying HDACs as a potential target in PFOS developmental neurotoxicity.

articles.title: Short term effect of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation of the medial sensorimotor cortex for neurogenic pelvic floor dysfunction in multiple sclerosis: a randomized, double blind, sham controlled trial.
articles.authors: Shehata GA, Ahmed GK, Hassan YA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurogenic pelvic floor dysfunction, comprising bladder, bowel and sexual disturbance, affects most people with multiple sclerosis (MS) and responds poorly to pharmacotherapy. The medial sensorimotor cortex contains the pelvic floor representation, but controlled evidence for cortical neuromodulation in MS is scarce and bladder focused.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the short term efficacy and safety of inhibitory (1 Hz) repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the vertex (Cz) in MS-related pelvic floor dysfunction.
METHODS: Forty-five patients with definite MS (Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) ≤6.0) and actionable bladder symptoms Screening Tool (ABSST≥8) were randomized 2:1 in a double-blind, sham-controlled single centre trial to active (n = 30) or sham (n = 15) stimulation: 1 Hz rTMS at 90-100% resting motor threshold (900 pulses) over Cz across 10 weekday sessions; sham used a 90° tilted coil with synchronized scalp electrodes. ABSST, Neurogenic Bowel Dysfunction (NBD) score, Multiple Sclerosis Impact Scale 29(MSIS-29), Multiple Sclerosis Intimacy and Sexuality Questionnaire (MSISQ- 19), Overactive Bladder Questionnaire-Short Form (OAB -q SF) were assessed at baseline and 12 weeks post treatment.
RESULTS: ABSST fell from 18.6 ± 4.5 to 13.9 ± 5.1 with active stimulation versus 17.8 ± 3.8 to 17.1 ± 3.5 with sham (ANCOVA adjusted difference -3.98, 95%CI -6.75 to -1.22; standardized effect -0.93; p = 0.006). After baseline and multiplicity adjustment, benefit persisted for bowel (NBD; FDR adjusted p = 0.004) and sexual (MSISQ-19; p = 0.036) domains, but not OAB-q SF or MSIS-29. Bladder improvement correlated with bowel (r = 0.464) and sexual (r = 0.374) improvement. No serious adverse events occurred. All 45 participants completed all ten sessions and the 12 week assessment.
CONCLUSIONS: Inhibitory vertex rTMS produced sustained, coherent cross domain improvement in MS-related pelvic floor dysfunction exceeding sham, consistent with modulation of a shared central substrate and supports cortical neuromodulation as a promising, well tolerated adjunct.

articles.title: Chlamydia and gonorrhoea prevalence in abortion and prenatal care: a cross-sectional study in a Portuguese centre.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Martins I, Dias J, Órfão S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Infections caused by C. trachomatis (CT) and Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) are increasing in Europe. However, differences in surveillance systems limit accurate epidemiological data on representative populations, such as women receiving prenatal care. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of urogenital CT and NG among pregnant women in two distinct pregnancy-related care contexts at a Portuguese center.
METHODS: A cross-sectional prevalence study was conducted at a Portuguese tertiary care center, including pregnant women undergoing induced abortion (up to 10 weeks of gestation) and those receiving prenatal care (35-37 weeks of gestation). Screening was performed using vaginal swab specimens and testing was performed using NAAT. A sample size of 207 participants was calculated to estimate the prevalence of CT.
RESULTS: A total of 253 pregnant women were included (145 women attending induced abortion care and 108 receiving third-trimester prenatal care). Overall prevalence was 5,5 % for CT and 1,2 % for NG. The highest prevalence of infection was observed among women aged 20-24 years (17,5 %) for CT, and among those under 25 years (3,9 %) for NG. A significantly higher prevalence of CT was observed among women in the induced abortion care group (9,0 % vs. 0,9 %, p = 0,010); all NG cases were identified in this group.
CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of CT and NG was higher than expected among pregnant women attending this center, particularly among those seeking induced abortion. Recognizing the heterogeneity of women receiving pregnancy-related care is essential, as antenatal-focused approaches may underestimate the true burden of infection. This study highlights the need to broaden research across all groups of pregnant women.

articles.title: Preterm birth rates after full-dilatation caesarean section in the first pregnancy: outcomes in contemporary obstetric practice.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Saleem HA, Golob E, Datta T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB) following full dilatation caesarean section (FDCS) has been linked to cervical or lower uterine segment trauma in historical cohorts, but this evidence largely predates modern obstetric practice. This study aimed to determine whether the association persists in a contemporary population, using electronic maternity records from two UK units (BadgerNet, October 2018-February 2026).
RESULTS: Of 11,350 nulliparous women with a term singleton first birth, 3,288 had subsequent pregnancy data available, including 88 (2.7%) who had undergone FDCS. sPTB occurred in 8.0% of women after FDCS, compared with 1.6% after spontaneous vaginal delivery, 0.9% after forceps, 2.7% after ventouse, 0.35% after elective caesarean, and 1.3% after emergency caesarean not at full dilatation. After adjusting for maternal age, BMI, smoking status, and interpregnancy interval, FDCS remained independently associated with sPTB (aOR 7.20, 95% CI 2.91-17.80, p < 0.001). No other mode of delivery, BMI, or smoking status showed a significant independent association.
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest, in a modern obstetric cohort, that the previously reported link between FDCS and subsequent sPTB persists. The strength of association was notable despite adjustment for key confounders, though the small number of events and wide confidence interval limit precision. This observational study does not establish a causal relationship.
CONCLUSION: FDCS in a first pregnancy is associated with a substantially increased risk of sPTB in the subsequent pregnancy. These findings may inform individualised counselling about this risk. This study did not evaluate cervical-length surveillance or preventive interventions. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm this association and evaluate these approaches.

articles.title: The disruption score: a novel bibliometric analysis of obstetrics and gynecology.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Vaughn CR, White M, Chon AH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The disruption score is a bibliometric tool which measures the degree to which publications develop existing ideas of a given medical specialty or shift the direction toward new horizons via disruptive processes. We used disruption score to rank published works in Obstetrics and Gynecology (OBGYN).
STUDY DESIGN: OBGYN journal titles indexed in MEDLINE and PubMed Central were identified and used to pull article abstracts from PubMed published from 1900 to 2021. A disruption score (-1 to +1) was assigned based on each publication's citation patterns. Articles with a negative score were considered developmental works, which often build upon existing ideas. Positive scoring articles were considered disruptive, often introducing innovative ideas. The top 100 highest scoring articles were identified across 3 categories: top cited, top disruption score, top developmental score.
RESULTS: Our search strategy identified 381,677 works in the field of OBGYN. Top papers were drawn most often from American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology (53%) and British Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology (16%). By topic, top cited papers were commonly gynecologically-focused (65% GYN vs 33% OB), as compared to disruptive papers (40% GYN vs 58% OB) and development papers (34% GYN vs 65% OB) (p < 0.005). By study design, top cited papers were observational (40%) and review (31%). Top developmental papers were case report/case series (54%) and observational (17%). Top disruptive papers were observational (37%) and case reports/case series (29%).
CONCLUSION: The disruption score highlighted an entirely different set of OBGYN articles when compared to citation count alone. The disruption score can be utilized to provide a novel analysis of the rich literary history of OBGYN.

articles.title: Clinical significance and diagnostic performance of maternal circulating soluble ST2 in preeclampsia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Simanjuntak AMT, Wirya W, Arta KIP et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Soluble suppression of tumorigenicity-2 (sST2) has emerged as a promising inflammatory biomarker implicated in the pathophysiology of preeclampsia (PE). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated maternal circulating sST2 concentrations according to the timing of sampling, and its diagnostic accuracy for PE.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Epistemonikos, and EBSCOhost were searched from inception to September 20, 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar and citation searching, without language restrictions. Observational studies comparing maternal circulating sST2 between women with PE and normotensive pregnant controls were included. Mean differences (MDs) were pooled using random-effects models, separately for antepartum samples obtained at or after clinical diagnosis and for trimester-specific samples obtained before clinical onset, with subgroup, meta-regression and (when I2 > 50%) sensitivity analyses. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized using generalized linear mixed and bivariate models. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E and, for diagnostic accuracy studies, QUADAS-2.
RESULTS: Eight studies (430 women with PE, 606 controls) were included. In samples obtained at or after clinical diagnosis, sST2 was higher in PE (MD 45.78 ng/mL, 95% CI 14.63-76.93, I2 = 97.1%), consistently across leave-one-out analyses and on standardized (1.35, 0.87-1.83) and ratio-of-means (2.18, 1.68-2.86) scales. Before clinical onset, no first-trimester difference was observed (MD -0.34, -7.23-6.55), and second- and early-third-trimester differences were small and imprecise. Egger's test suggested small-study effects (p < 0.001), and trim-and-fill attenuated the estimate (MD 6.17, -38.23 to 50.57). In three heterogeneous studies (426 women) with different sampling times and thresholds, exploratory summary sensitivity and specificity were 0.76 (0.51-0.90) and 0.80 (0.52-0.94). In the two studies sampling at diagnosis, they were 0.71 (0.42-0.90) and 0.84 (0.63-0.94).
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal circulating sST2 is elevated in established PE, but evidence of elevation before clinical onset is limited and diagnostic accuracy is uncertain. sST2 cannot currently be recommended for the prediction or diagnosis of PE, and prospective studies with standardized assays, gestational-age-specific thresholds and evaluation of incremental value over the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio are required.

articles.title: Impact of artificial intelligence in embryo selection to improve pregnancy rates per transfer in IVF cycles: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Yaghi S, Gasol FF, Espinós JJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Embryo selection is one of the most critical determinants of success in in vitro fertilization (IVF). Conventional approaches based on static morphological grading and time-lapse imaging (TLI) remain subjective and show only modest predictive accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools, including deep learning-based platforms such as iDAScore and KIDScore, have emerged as potentially more standardized alternatives, yet their true clinical impact on per-transfer outcomes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether AI-assisted embryo selection offers measurable clinical advantages over conventional morphology-based methods in IVF.
SEARCH STRATEGY: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted by searching four electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and the Cochrane Library) from January 2013 to April 2024.
SELECTION CRITERIA: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohort studies evaluating AI-assisted embryo selection versus conventional morphology in IVF cycles without preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), reporting at least one of clinical pregnancy rate (CPR), implantation rate (IR), or live birth rate (LBR).
DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Study quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool for the RCT and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for observational studies. Where arm-level data were available, risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: Ten studies were included. Only two reported arm-level outcomes suitable for meta-analysis. The pooled estimate showed no significant difference in clinical pregnancy rate between AI-assisted and morphology-based selection (RR = 0.99, 95% CI 0.87-1.12; I2 = 26.5%), with no statistically significant difference between the two methods. The remaining eight studies reported predictive performance metrics with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.85-0.96, though these did not consistently translate into improved per-cycle outcomes. Implantation and live birth rates were inconsistently reported and could not be pooled.
CONCLUSION: AI-based embryo scoring showed no statistically significant difference compared with conventional morphology for per-transfer clinical pregnancy rate, with potential advantages in standardization and inter-observer consistency. However, superiority remains unconfirmed…

articles.title: IVF outcomes after transvaginal sclerotherapy for ovarian endometrioma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Pow JY, Hamdan M
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether pre-IVF/ICSI transvaginal ethanol sclerotherapy for ovarian endometrioma improves reproductive outcomes compared with expectant management, and to assess whether prior cystectomy modifies treatment effect.
DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE, EMBASE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, major clinical trial registries, PubMed, and Google Scholar were searched from 1980 to November 2025 without language restriction.
METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies included women with ovarian endometrioma undergoing IVF/ICSI, comparing those who received sclerotherapy with those managed expectantly. Eligible study designs included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohorts. Following the screening of 742 records, six studies met the inclusion criteria: one RCT, one prospective comparative study, and four retrospective cohorts.
RESULTS: Six studies (one RCT, four retrospective cohorts, and one prospective comparative study) were included. The primary patient-level live birth analysis (2 studies, 124 patients) showed no statistically significant difference between sclerotherapy and expectant management (OR 2.20, 95% CI 0.66-7.32, p=0.20). The primary patient-level analysis for clinical pregnancy (4 studies, 221 patients) demonstrated that sclerotherapy was associated with a significantly higher clinical pregnancy rate (OR 2.14, 95% CI 1.21-3.79, p=0.009). At the cycle level, sclerotherapy yielded significantly more total oocytes (MD 2.20, 95% CI 0.06-4.34, p=0.04) and total embryos (MD 0.56, 95% CI 0.07-1.05, p=0.02), whereas the increase in mature oocytes was non-significant (MD 1.56, 95% CI -0.14-3.26, p=0.07). According to the GRADE framework, the certainty of evidence for all outcomes was Very Low.
CONCLUSION: Low-certainty evidence suggests that pre-IVF ethanol sclerotherapy for ovarian endometrioma may be associated with improved clinical pregnancy compared with expectant management, with benefits evident regardless of prior cystectomy history. While a positive trend in live births was observed, this finding was not statistically significant at the patient level, highlighting the fragility of the current evidence. These clinical enhancements are supported by overall improvements in oocyte and embryo yields. Sclerotherapy serves as a valuable, fertility-preserving alternative to repeat surgery for selected patients.

articles.title: Effectiveness of prophylactic subcutaneous negative-pressure drainage for the prevention of surgical site infection in gynaecological cancer patients with BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2: a multicentre open-label randomized trial.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Pergialiotis V, Papatheodorou D, Tsolakidis D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether prophylactic subcutaneous negative-pressure drainage reduces the incidence of surgical site infection (SSI) after laparotomy in morbidly obese women undergoing surgery for gynaecological malignancy.
METHODS: In this multicentre open-label randomized trial, 200 women with body mass index (BMI) > 35 kg/m2 were allocated to receive subcutaneous drainage using a Redon drain for at least 3 postoperative days or standard wound closure without drainage. The primary outcome was SSI within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included surgical debridement for SSI, wound haematoma, seroma, wound dehiscence, wound-related fever, duration of antibiotic therapy, length of hospital stay, and 30-day re-admission.
RESULTS: Data from 191 patients were analysed. Median BMI was 39 kg/m2. The incidence of SSI was comparable between the drainage and control groups (15.5% vs 14.9%; p = 0.913). Drain placement reduced postoperative wound haematoma significantly (1.0% vs 7.4%; p = 0.027). Postoperative fever occurred more frequently in the drainage group (18.5% vs 8.5%; p = 0.057). Although this difference did not reach significance, exploratory multivariable analysis demonstrated a similar trend (adjusted odds ratio 2.47, 95% confidence interval 0.98-6.22), suggesting that a clinically relevant increase in postoperative fever cannot be excluded. No differences in overall uncomplicated wound healing were observed.
CONCLUSION: Subcutaneous negative-pressure drainage did not significantly reduce the incidence of SSI following abdominal hysterectomy in morbidly obese patients with gynaecological cancer. Of all predefined secondary outcomes, only postoperative wound haematoma was reduced significantly. Conversely, both the unadjusted and adjusted analyses suggested a potential increase in postoperative fever, although significance was not reached. As these were secondary outcomes, they should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Association of mode of delivery with postpartum disease flares in women with inflammatory rheumatic diseases.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Erzeneoglu BE, Calis P, Tufan A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between mode of delivery and the risk and timing of postpartum flares in women with inflammatory rheumatic diseases (IRDs).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included singleton pregnancies in women with systemic IRDs between 2014 and 2021. Pregnancies with major obstetric complications affecting delivery mode were excluded, and only elective cesarean deliveries were included. Of 1481 screened pregnancies, 433 singleton pregnancies with complete postpartum follow-up were analyzed (201 vaginal delivery [VD], 232 cesarean section [CS]). The primary outcome was postpartum flare within 180 days, defined as symptom recurrence or worsening requiring treatment escalation, rheumatologist-documented increase in disease activity or hospitalization. In the primary multivariable logistic regression analysis evaluating the binary outcome of flare occurrence, adjustments were made for maternal age, gravida, parity, disease subtype, and medication exposure. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing were conducted as secondary time-to-event evaluations.
RESULTS: Postpartum flares occurred in 247 patients (57.0%), more frequently after CS than VD (67.7% vs 44.8%, p < 0.001). In primary multivariable logistic regression analysis, CS remained significantly associated with higher odds of postpartum flare (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.55, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.71-3.80, p < 0.001). Furthermore, in secondary multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis, CS remained significantly associated with a higher hazard of postpartum flare (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.009, 95% CI 1.520-2.655, p < 0.001). Time to flare was significantly shorter in the CS group (log-rank p < 0.001), with a median time of 115.0 days (95% CI: 105.9-124.1 days) in the CS group (not reached in the VD group). Descriptive laboratory evaluation at 6 weeks postpartum showed higher erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein levels alongside lower serum albumin concentrations in the CS group.
CONCLUSION: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk and earlier occurrence of postpartum flares in women with IRDs after adjusting for demographic, disease, and therapeutic covariates. While these observational findings highlight mode of delivery as a potential factor associated with postpartum disease course, confirmation in prospective studies is required before influencing routine…

articles.title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes in pregnancies with cystic fibrosis after lung transplantation or during elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) therapy: a single-center descriptive cohort.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Le Bars S, Tissot A, Danner-Boucher I et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advances in cystic fibrosis (CF) therapy, particularly CFTR modulators such as elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI), are reshaping reproductive outcomes for women with advanced CF. Historically, lung transplantation (LT) was the only means to achieve sufficient respiratory stability for pregnancy. This study provides real-world clinical data describing pregnancies in women with CF after LT and during ETI therapy.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective descriptive study of all pregnancies resulting in live births among women with CF followed at the Nantes University Hospital CF reference center between January 1, 2000 and August 31, 2024. Maternal characteristics, obstetric complications, and neonatal outcomes were collected for pregnancies after LT or under ETI treatment. Analyses were descriptive, with no statistical comparisons between groups due to small sample size and inherent clinical differences. Descriptive values from the 2021 French National Perinatal Survey are reported alongside our results for context only.
RESULTS: Among 95 pregnancies in 46 women, 56 resulted in live births, including 7 after LT and 10 during ETI therapy. In the LT cohort, pre-existing comorbidities were frequent: cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD) (100%), chronic hypertension (50%), and moderate renal impairment (83.3%). Preterm delivery occurred in 57.1% of pregnancies and intensive care unit admission in 42.9%. In ETI-exposed pregnancies, no gestational hypertension or preeclampsia was identified, and no woman required intensive care admission or delivered before 34 weeks. No congenital anomaly was observed in either group. Median gestational age at birth was 38 weeks + 3 days and median birth weight 3190 g in the ETI group, versus 35 weeks + 4 days and 1980 g in the LT group; these values are reported descriptively and were not compared statistically.
