CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, ETI-exposed pregnancies were associated with reassuring maternal and neonatal outcomes, while pregnancies after LT were characterized by frequent transplant-related and vascular morbidity; the two groups were described separately and were not formally compared. These findings support the need for multidisciplinary follow-up and prospective registries to evaluate maternal and pediatric outcomes in the CFTR modulator era.

articles.title: Changes in health-related quality of life measured by the RAND-12 HSI and predictive factors in the early postpartum period: A prospective observational study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Fijean AL, Epstein J, Banasiak C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify the determinants of changes in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) between the immediate and 2-month postpartum periods.
METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of a multicentre prospective cohort study, conducted between 2020 and 2023 in four French maternity wards. Women who delivered singletons after 37 weeks of gestation were eligible for inclusion. The 12-item Short Form Health Survey was completed immediately and 2 months postpartum as an online self-administered questionnaire. The global health composite score (global score), physical health composite (PHC) score and mental health composite (MHC) score were calculated via the RAND-12 Health Status Inventory algorithm. The endpoints were the differences in the global score, PHC score and MHC score between the immediate and 2-month postpartum periods.
RESULTS: Five hundred and eight women responded to the questionnaire. Multivariable analysis revealed that the mean difference in the global score between the immediate and 2-month postpartum periods decreased in women who had undergone an emergency caesarean (-4.86 points, p = 0.03) and increased in multiparous women (+1.80 points, p = 0.04). The MHC score decreased with current professional activity compared with no professional activity (-2.7 points, p = 0.04), and the PHC score decreased by 3.5 points between 37 and 42 weeks of gestation (p = 0.04). Moreover, HRQoL was negatively associated with the Quality of Prenatal Care Questionnaire score in all dimensions.
CONCLUSIONS: Emergency caesarean, multiparity, current professional activity, gestational age at delivery, and perceived quality of prenatal care were associated with changes in HRQoL postpartum. These associations should be interpreted with caution because some observed differences did not reach the minimal clinically important difference.

articles.title: Extracellular matrix collagen remodeling predicts resistance to immune checkpoint blockade in mismatch repair-deficient endometrial cancer.
articles.authors: Grau Bejar JF, Zeng Q, Abdelsayed V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the therapeutic paradigm for mismatch repair-deficient endometrial cancer (MMRd EC). However, a considerable subset of patients fails to achieve durable clinical benefit. This pronounced interpatient variability underscores the urgent unmet need for mechanistic predictive biomarkers beyond MMRd status alone to guide clinical decision-making.
METHODS: We performed a multiproteomic mass spectrometry analysis on tumor specimens from an advanced or recurrent MMRd EC cohort stratified into ICI responders (ICI-R) and non-responders (ICI-NR). Proteomic signatures were validated spatially and structurally using whole-section Masson’s Trichrome digital imaging and polarization-resolved second-harmonic generation microscopy. Machine learning algorithms were constructed to integrate extracellular matrix (ECM) structural metrics with immune parameters to build a multiparametric predictive model of ICI resistance.
RESULTS: ECM remodeling emerged as the dominant proteomic program characterizing ICI resistance. Quantitative spatial imaging revealed that increased intratumoral collagen density and peripheral fiber disorganization were significantly associated with impaired CD8+ T-cell infiltration and immunotherapy failure. Integrating collagen structural metrics with immune parameters yielded a predictive score that showed promising discrimination between ICI-Rs and ICI-NRs in our cohort, providing a framework for future validation in independent cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings implicate ECM remodeling as a key determinant of immune exclusion and ICI resistance in MMRd EC. These findings support developing collagen-based spatial biomarkers and stromal-targeted approaches, though the clinical utility of this predictive score requires further validation in larger, independent cohorts.

articles.title: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor in human fertility: A systematic review of clinical and reproductive implications, 2015-2025.
articles.authors: Hoseinzadeh S, Moradi F, Amjadi FS et al.
articles.abstract: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) is a pleiotropic cytokine involved in inflammatory and immune regulation. This systematic review evaluated current evidence on the association between MIF and human reproductive function in male and female populations. PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Google Scholar were systematically searched for studies published from 2015 to 2025. After duplicate removal and eligibility screening, 12 studies were included. Data on study design, population characteristics, reproductive conditions, and MIF expression were extracted and synthesized qualitatively. The included studies reported associations between altered or elevated MIF levels and several reproductive and pregnancy-related conditions, including endometriosis, polycystic ovary syndrome, recurrent pregnancy loss, endometrioma, and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. MIF was frequently implicated in inflammatory pathways and hormonal regulation within reproductive tissues. The available evidence suggests that MIF may be involved in disease pathophysiology and may have potential as a biomarker in selected reproductive disorders. Overall, current evidence indicates that MIF is associated with multiple reproductive pathologies and may contribute to inflammatory and endocrine regulation in fertility-related conditions. However, further well-designed studies are needed to clarify its diagnostic and clinical utility in reproductive medicine.

articles.title: The role of cadherins and catenins in endometrial function and embryo implantation: A comprehensive review.
articles.authors: Costanzi F, De Marco MP, Giannini A et al.
articles.abstract: Cadherins and catenins are essential transmembrane proteins and cytoplasmic binding partners that mediate cell-cell adhesion, intracellular signaling, and the maintenance of tissue architecture. Their coordinated functions are central to endometrial biology and embryo implantation, a process that requires complex cell-cell interactions and tissue remodeling for pregnancy to be established. In this review, we summarize current evidence on the molecular mechanisms through which cadherins and catenins regulate endometrial receptivity and support embryo attachment to maternal tissue. We also discuss how advances in molecular biology and reproductive medicine have clarified the roles of cadherin-catenin complexes in cell adhesion, intracellular signaling, including Wnt/β-catenin signaling, and the regulation of trophoblast invasion. In addition, we examine the potential clinical relevance of dysfunction in these complexes, which has been associated with implantation failure and infertility. A clearer understanding of cadherin-catenin function in the endometrium may support the development of diagnostic tools and therapeutic targets for infertility.

articles.title: Telemonitoring for high-risk pregnancies (PregnaDigit EU): an international hybrid type 2 study protocol.
articles.authors: van Oorschot HFC, Vellekoop-van Ravenswaaij R, Bel EWW et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Healthcare systems worldwide are under increasing pressure from workforce shortages, rising costs and growing demands for care. Obstetric care is also affected because high-risk pregnancies require frequent in-hospital monitoring. This strains the healthcare system and reduces the quality of life for patients. Telemonitoring offers a promising solution by shifting care from hospital to home, thereby addressing these demands without compromising care quality. Despite demonstrated benefits, implementation remains limited due to challenges not anticipated in controlled research settings. Aiming to facilitate international implementation of telemonitoring as the new standard of care, we established the PregnaDigit EU consortium. In this consortium, we investigate clinical outcomes, patient experience, healthcare consumption and implementation of telemonitoring in high-risk pregnancies across four European hospitals. Ultimately, our goal is to ensure that pregnancy care remains accessible to all while reducing pressure on the healthcare system.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This multicentre, prospective, hybrid type 2 implementation study is performed at four tertiary centres in three European countries: University Medical Centre Utrecht and Erasmus Medical Centre Rotterdam in the Netherlands, Vall d’Hebron University Hospital in Spain and Karolinska University Hospital in Sweden. This study design allows for the simultaneous evaluation of clinical and implementation outcomes of telemonitoring. Eligible participants are ≥18 years with a singleton pregnancy and gestational age of at least 24+0 weeks requiring frequent cardiotocography (CTG) monitoring for a high-risk pregnancy according to local protocols. The telemonitoring care pathway comprises self-recorded home CTG and blood pressure measurements, which are reviewed by trained professionals who provide same-day feedback and clinical management via teleconsultation. Additionally, the care pathway includes standardised outpatient care and additional assessments, such as ultrasounds and laboratory testing, per local protocol. The primary clinical outcome is a composite of adverse perinatal and maternal events. Secondary clinical outcomes include all individual components of the primary clinical outcome, additional adverse perinatal events and healthcare consumption outcomes. The primary implementation outcomes are assessed using the taxonomy of Proctor et al during three sequential phases:…

articles.title: Clinical yield and operational cost-threshold analysis of HPV self-sampling send-outs for long-term non-attenders in cervical cancer screening: a population-based, real-world, registry study in Sweden.
articles.authors: Fridljung J, Bergengren L, Lillsunde-Larsson G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the clinical yield and operational costs of a targeted ‘send-to-all’ human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling strategy for long-term non-attenders in cervical cancer screening.
DESIGN: Population-based, real-world observational registry study.
SETTING: The regional organised cervical cancer screening programme in Region Örebro County, Sweden.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 9123 women identified as long-term non-attenders. Long-term non-attendance was defined as having no recorded cervical screening test for at least one routine screening interval plus an additional 4 years.
INTERVENTIONS: A total of 11 283 vaginal HPV self-sampling kits were dispatched via direct mail to the registered home addresses of all 9123 eligible women between 2022 and 2024.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: Clinical yield was evaluated using the number of tests analysed (NTA) and number of kits dispatched (NKD) to detect one case of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or worse (HSIL+). Resource utilisation was measured as the average cost per screened woman/detected HSIL+, and the economic break-even point against standard letter invitations was established using a deterministic threshold analysis.
RESULTS: Of the 11 283 self-sampling kits dispatched, 1826 kits were returned and analysed. This direct response yielded 27 HSIL+ cases (NTA: 68; NKD: 418), at an average cost of 2031 SEK (€183) per screened woman and 134 103 SEK (€12,114) per histologically confirmed HSIL+ case. Incorporating an additional 190 long-term non-attenders who underwent clinical screening within 1 year of dispatch yielded a total of 32 HSIL+ cases. This cumulative response decreased the NTA to 63 and the NKD to 353, with an average cost of 2045 SEK (€185) per screened woman and 126 068 SEK (€11 388) per HSIL+ case. To match the cost per screened woman of the self-sampling strategy, standard letter invitations must achieve a participation rate of 9.5% (based on kit returns alone) or 6.4% (based on cumulative participation).
CONCLUSIONS: Direct mailing of HPV self-sampling kits effectively identifies high-grade lesions in a hard-to-reach population. From an operational perspective, previous research indicates that participation from standard letters rarely reaches the calculated 6.4%–9.5% break-even points, suggesting self-sampling is a resource-efficient initial outreach strategy for long-term non-attenders. However, full economic evaluations incorporating long-term health…

articles.title: Psychometric properties and cross-cultural adaptation of the HPV testing knowledge scale: a cross-sectional methodological study among Turkish women.
articles.authors: Ergöz Aksoy SZ, Bilgic D
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the psychometric properties of the Human Papillomavirus Testing Knowledge Scale (HPV-TKS) among Turkish women.
DESIGN: A cross-sectional methodological study.
SETTING: Data were collected through an online survey conducted in Türkiye between September 2023 and February 2024, using non-probability convenience and snowball sampling.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 234 women were initially recruited, of whom 205 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final analysis. Eligible participants were women aged 30–65 years who were able to read and understand Turkish and provided informed consent. Women with a history of total hysterectomy or cervical cancer were excluded.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcomes were the validity and reliability of the HPV-TKS. Content validity was assessed using the Content Validity Index (CVI), and structural validity was evaluated through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Convergent validity was assessed using average variance extracted, known-groups and discriminant validity were assessed using independent-samples t-tests and criterion validity was assessed using logistic regression. Reliability was examined using Cronbach’s alpha, McDonald’s omega and item-total correlations, along with floor/ceiling effects.
RESULTS: The mean HPV-TKS score was 2.67±2.10. CVI was found to be 0.94, indicating excellent content validity. EFA initially suggested a two-factor structure explaining 50.8% of the total variance (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin test=0.807; Bartlett’s test: χ²=330.527, p<0.001). Using the same sample, CFA with the weighted least squares mean and variance adjusted estimator was subsequently applied to formally compare the one-factor and two-factor structures; the one-factor structure was retained based on its excellent absolute fit (χ²(20)=25.3, p=0.190; comparative fit index (CFI)=0.99; Tucker-Lewis index (TLI)=0.99; root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA)=0.036; standardised root mean square residual (SRMR)=0.066), consistency with the original scale and the absence of a conceptually meaningful distinction between factors, with item factor loadings ranging from 0.36 to 0.92. Internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach’s alpha=0.76, McDonald’s omega=0.90). Item-total correlation coefficients ranged from 0.159 to 0.588.
CONCLUSIONS: The Turkish version of the HPV-TKS is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing…

articles.title: Cervical cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.
articles.authors: Lorusso D, Cibula D, Colombo I et al.
articles.abstract: • This ESMO CPG provides key recommendations and algorithms for managing cervical cancer. • Treatment and management algorithms for locoregional and recurrent/metastatic disease are provided based on the latest data. • Includes new surgical treatment recommendations for early-stage, locally advanced, and recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer. • Recommendations are based on available scientific data and the authors’ collective expert opinion. • The ESMO-MCBS scores and LoE/GoRs describe the evidence for treatment and can aid with setting choice priorities.

articles.title: Effects of maternal Jussara (Euterpe edulis Mart.) supplementation on metabolic parameters and hypothalamic cytokine markers in male offspring at weaning following maternal trans fat intake.
articles.authors: Minari TP, Morais CA, de Rosso VV et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal consumption of trans fatty acids (TFA) during pregnancy and lactation is associated with adverse metabolic and hypothalamic cytokine-related alterations in offspring. Anthocyanin-rich fruits such as Jussara (Euterpe edulis Mart.) may counteract these effects through their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory potential. Pregnant Wistar rats (n = 24) were assigned to four diets during pregnancy and lactation: control (C), control +0.5% Jussara (CJ), trans fat-enriched (T), or trans fat + Jussara (TJ). Litters were standardized to eight pups, and only male offspring were analyzed at weaning (21 days). Male offspring from six litters per group were included in the analyses. Statistical analyses considered the litter as the experimental unit. Growth, biochemical, and hypothalamic cytokine-related markers were assessed. Jussara supplementation increased hypothalamic IL-10 mRNA expression, improved the IL-10/TNF-α ratio, and reduced TNF-α protein levels, while IL-6 remained unchanged. Supplemented groups showed reduced body weight gain, fasting glucose, triglycerides, and total cholesterol levels, particularly with trans fat exposure. Jussara showed antioxidant activity, and a generalized linear model supported metabolic effects. Maternal Jussara supplementation was associated with increased hypothalamic IL-10 mRNA expression, improved the IL-10/TNF-α balance, and reduced TNF-α protein levels, alongside improved metabolic parameters in male offspring exposed to a TFA-enriched maternal diet. These findings are limited to male pups, a single supplementation dose, and one early postnatal time point. Further studies should evaluate long-term, sex-specific, and mechanistic effects.

articles.title: Targeted α-Therapy with 211At-Labeled Trastuzumab Overcomes Trastuzumab Resistance in Uterine Serous Carcinoma in Mice.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.authors: Li HK, Anko M, Banno K et al.
articles.abstract: Uterine serous carcinoma (USC) is an aggressive endometrial cancer frequently associated with human epidermal growth factor receptor type 2 (HER2) overexpression and poor prognosis. Although trastuzumab improves outcomes, resistance remains a major clinical problem. This study determined whether targeted α-therapy using 211At-labeled trastuzumab (211At-trastuzumab) can overcome trastuzumab resistance in HER2-positive USC. Methods: 211At-trastuzumab was synthesized, and its binding and cytotoxicity in HER2-positive USC cell lines were evaluated. Three trastuzumab-resistant peritoneal metastasis mouse models were established: intrinsic resistance, trastuzumab-induced resistance, and acquired resistance. After a single intravenous administration (1.85 MBq), therapeutic efficacy was assessed using bioluminescence imaging and biodistribution analysis. Results: 211At-trastuzumab showed specific binding to HER2-positive USC cells and significantly reduced cell viability relative to the controls. In vivo, tumor uptake reached 17.4 ± 1.9 %ID/g at 24 h. A single dose significantly suppressed tumor growth in all 3 resistant models: intrinsic, induced, and acquired resistance (P < 0.05 vs. controls). No severe toxicity was observed. Conclusion: 211At-trastuzumab demonstrates potent antitumor efficacy against trastuzumab-resistant HER2-positive USC in preclinical models. Targeted α-therapy may represent a promising strategy to overcome resistance to HER2-targeted therapy.

articles.title: Pregnancy Outcomes After Living Kidney Donation.
articles.authors: Wang C, Naylor KL, McArthur E et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth.
RESULTS: The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor…

articles.title: Green synthesis of SnO2 nanoparticles using Calophyllum inophyllum seed shell extract and their biological and environmental applications.
articles.authors: Jayaseelan C, Paramanathan B, Jayabalan J et al.
articles.abstract: In this research, tin oxide nanoparticles (SnO2 NPs) were green synthesized using Calophyllum inophyllum seed shell extract (CISSE) as both the stabilizing and capping agent, providing an ecologically friendly, sustainable, and cost-efficient synthesis route. The synthesized nanoparticles were comprehensively characterized to determine their optical properties, crystalline structure, functional groups, morphology, particle size, elemental composition, surface chemistry, and colloidal stability. The most prominent absorption peak (λmax) in the UV-visible spectrum was found at 280 nm. FESEM and HR-TEM examination indicated that the synthesized nanoparticles had quasi spherical to spherical shape with an average size of 19.29 ± 5.25 nm. According to DLS analysis, the polydispersity index (PDI) was 0.389, and the mean hydrodynamic size was 85 nm. The zeta potential value of -27.9 mV suggested notable colloidal stability. Raman spectroscopy revealed a unique vibrational peak at 631 cm-1, indicating the effective production of crystalline SnO2 NPs. XPS analysis confirmed the presence of Sn and O, with Sn 3d peaks consistent with Sn4+ in SnO2 and C 1s signals indicating oxygen-containing carbonaceous species associated with the nanoparticle surface. The biosynthesized SnO2 NPs exhibited potent larvicidal, antibacterial, antibiofilm, antiproliferative, and photocatalytic activities. They showed effective larvicidal activity against Aedes aegypti (LC50 = 9.0 mg/L) and Culex quinquefasciatus (LC50 = 7.5 mg/L) with minimal toxicity toward non-target organisms. The nanoparticles demonstrated strong antibacterial activity, with maximum inhibition zones of 23 mm against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, and pronounced antibiofilm activity, achieving 91.08% biofilm inhibition against Acinetobacter baumannii. Furthermore, SnO2 NPs exhibited enhanced antiproliferative activity against SiHa cervical cancer cells (IC50 = 57.81 μg/mL) compared with the crude extract (IC50 = 233.56 μg/mL). Also, the synthesized SnO2 NPs efficiently photocatalytically degraded ibuprofen under UV irradiation, highlighting its prospects for therapeutic and environmental uses.

articles.title: Bladder neck vs midurethral placement of autologous retropubic fascial slings: a systematic review.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Konci R, Reuveni-Salzman A, Sirmakesyan S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the objective and subjective cure or improvement rates and surgical outcomes between traditional bladder neck sling placement and midurethral sling placement of autologous retropubic pubovaginal slings in women with stress or mixed urinary incontinence.
DATA SOURCES: A systematic search of MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted using standardized medical subject headings terms from inception to March 2025 (PROSPERO-registered). Studies underwent double screening, and a third reviewer resolved any discrepancies.
STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials and observational studies that evaluated outcomes of retropubic autologous fascial slings for stress urinary incontinence or mixed urinary incontinence. Studies published in English or French were eligible for inclusion. We included slings performed for recurrent stress or mixed urinary incontinence, as well as those placed concomitantly with prolapse surgery, provided that a minimum postoperative follow-up of 6 weeks was reported. We excluded systematic reviews, meta-analyses, review articles, case reports, studies that lacked details on surgical approach or sling material, and studies evaluating nonautologous slings.
METHODS: We evaluated study quality using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized controlled trials, and the National Heart Lung and Blood Institute Quality Assessment Tool for Observational Cohort and Cross-Sectional Studies. We present odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals to estimate the effect of sling placement location on each outcome through random-effects logistic regression.
RESULTS: We screened 5578 abstracts, assessed 233 full texts for eligibility, and retained 61 studies. Of the 61 studies, 13 were randomized controlled trials and 48 were observational studies. Objective (74.0% vs 81.1%; odds ratio, 1.10 [95% confidence interval, 0.37-3.28]) and subjective cure (70.8% vs 58.6 %; odds ratio 0.46 [95% confidence interval, 0.19-1.10]) were not statistically significantly different between bladder neck and midurethral placement of retropubic autologous fascial sling at a median of 2.4 years [0.3-6.8] postoperatively. Objective improvement (90.5% vs 84.5%; odds ratio, 0.41 [95% confidence interval, 0.10-1.67]) and subjective improvement (85.9% vs 85.1%; odds ratio, 0.77 [95% confidence interval, 0.31-1.92]) rates were also similar between the groups. Most adverse events…

articles.title: Ineupatorolide B alleviates postpartum depression-like behaviors via the gut microbiota-butyrate-brain axis.
articles.authors: Duan X, Tian F, Liu W et al.
articles.abstract: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a common mood disorder after childbirth and is associated with abrupt hormonal withdrawal, systemic inflammation, and neurobiological dysfunction. Increasing evidence implicates dysregulation of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in PPD pathophysiology, but safe and effective treatments remain limited. Here, we investigated the antidepressant-like effects and mechanisms of ineupatorolide B (InB), a bioactive compound isolated from Inula species, using a hormone-simulated withdrawal mouse model of PPD. InB significantly alleviated depressive- and anhedonia-like behaviors, as shown by reduced immobility in the tail suspension and forced swim tests and restored sucrose preference, with efficacy comparable to fluoxetine. InB also reduced serum interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α levels and restored the expression of postsynaptic density protein 95 and brain-derived neurotrophic factor in the prefrontal cortex. Gut microbiota analysis revealed marked alterations in microbial diversity and composition in hormone-withdrawal mice, accompanied by reduced fecal butyrate levels, which were largely normalized by InB treatment. Correlation analyses suggested associations among specific bacterial phyla, short-chain fatty acid metabolism, and behavioral outcomes. Notably, oral administration of butyric acid also alleviated depressive-like behaviors, suppressed systemic inflammation, and restored PSD-95, BDNF, and occludin expression in the prefrontal cortex of hormone-withdrawal mice. Together, these findings suggest that InB ameliorates PPD-like phenotypes, possibly through modulation of the gut microbiota, butyrate metabolism, systemic inflammation, and synaptic plasticity. However, the causal relationships among these changes remain to be established.

articles.title: In vitro maturation of porcine oocytes as a potential alternative testing model for reproductive toxicology studies.
articles.authors: Lee Y, Choi S, Kim G et al.
articles.abstract: Numerous chemicals have been reported to be detrimental to human and animal health, particularly to the female reproductive system. Chemical exposure can lead to reproductive disorders by disrupting the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and affecting the endocrine system, ovaries, follicular fluid, and germ cells. In addition, chemical exposure can impair female reproduction by directly affecting oocyte maturation, which is completed within the follicular fluid before ovulation. Therefore, evaluating the toxic effects of these chemicals on oocyte maturation has become increasingly important. In vitro maturation (IVM) of oocytes is an essential platform for elucidating the mechanisms underlying oocyte maturation. In particular, IVM of porcine oocytes may be a more suitable model for studying human oocyte maturation because pigs share greater physiological and genetic similarities with humans than other commonly used animal models do. Moreover, because porcine oocyte IVM uses immature oocytes obtained from ovaries collected as slaughterhouse by-products, this system avoids the use of experimental animals, offering both ethical and practical advantages. Despite the growing number of reproductive toxicology studies using porcine oocyte IVM, comprehensive summaries of the indicators used for porcine oocyte quality assessment remain limited. Therefore, this review aims to summarize the methods for assessing porcine oocyte quality, along with their underlying principles and applications, thereby providing an integrative overview to advance the use of porcine IVM as a model for reproductive toxicity evaluation.

articles.title: Outcomes and Feasibility of Robotic Pelvic Exenteration for Palliative and Mixed Intent.
articles.authors: Erdemoglu E, Varea IC, Magrina J et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: Pelvic exenteration is typically reserved for recurrent gynecologic malignancies, most often with curative intent. Its role in palliation, particularly using minimally invasive techniques, is less well defined.
DESIGN AND SETTING: This retospective case series evaluates the feasibility and outcomes of robotic-assisted pelvic exenteration performed with palliative intent between 2015 and 2025 at a single tertiary care institution.
PARTICIPANTS AND INTERVENTIONS: Eleven patients with recurrent or advanced gynecologic cancers underwent robotic exenteration primarily for symptom relief-pain, bleeding, fistulae, or obstruction-without curative expectation.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Final pathology reclassified five cases as "mixed intent" due to R0 margins or unexpectedly limited disease burden, while six remained palliative. R0 resection was achieved in 9 of 11 patients; one had no residual tumor, and one had microscopic residual disease. Median estimated blood loss was 350 mL. Postoperative complications occurred in 63.6% of patients, with three reoperations, and there was no intraoperative or 30-day mortality. Readmissions occurred in 54.5% of patients. Local recurrence was observed in 45.5%, and three patients received postoperative adjuvant therapy. Overall survival was 100% at 6 months and 83.3% (95% CI 27.3 to 97.5) at 12 months, based on a single death.
CONCLUSION: Further research is needed to evaluate long-term outcomes and quality of life in this population. Robotic-assisted pelvic exenteration is technically feasible in this highly selected palliative cohort. Perioperative morbidity was substantial, although within the range reported for pelvic exenteration4,23. No standardized symptom or quality-of-life instrument was applied, so symptomatic benefit cannot be inferred. The survival estimate rests on a single death with a wide confidence interval and is exploratory; median overall survival was not reached. The R0 rate raises the possibility that curative potential is underestimated preoperatively in some patients, but the small sample, retrospective design, and post hoc reclassification of intent require careful interpretation. Prospective evaluation of long-term outcomes and quality of life is needed.

articles.title: Bovine leptospirosis: Pathogenic species and serovars of Leptospira associated with dairy cows.
articles.authors: Hamond C, Stone NE, Browne AS et al.
articles.abstract: Leptospirosis is an economically important zoonotic bacterial infection of livestock that causes abortions, stillbirths, infertility, and loss of milk production. Bovine leptospirosis occurs worldwide and is caused by infection with pathogenic bacteria in the genus Leptospira that can colonize the kidney or genital tract of both males and females to maintain disease transmission via shedding in urine, the reproductive tract, or via vertical transmission to a fetus. Cattle are a reservoir host for L. borgpetersenii serovar Hardjo but can also shed other pathogenic species and serovars associated with bovine infection and zoonotic transmission. In this observational study, urine samples (n = 384) were collected from dairy cows in a California slaughterhouse to test for the presence of pathogenic Leptospira. In total, 56 urine samples (15%) were positive, with 55 (14%) positive by lipL32 rtPCR and 24 (6%) positive by culture. Characterization of cultured isolates identified L. borgpetersenii serovar Hardjo (n = 18), L. interrogans serovar Pomona (n = 5), and L. interrogans serovar Copenhageni (n = 1). Leptospira targeted amplicon sequencing analysis of 32 lipL32 PCR-positive but culture-negative urine samples identified 23 as positive for L. borgpetersenii, one as positive for a mixed infection comprising L. borgpetersenii and L. santarosai, and 4 as positive for L. santarosai; 4 remained undefined. Phylogenetics identified a new genotype of L. borgpetersenii that was not readily amenable to culture using current medium formulations. The identification of species and serovars of Leptospira currently circulating in cattle is critical for efficacious surveillance, diagnostic, and prevention strategies.

articles.title: Optimizing embryo transfer management in cows: Ultrasound-based pre-transfer screening and management of non-eligible recipients.
articles.authors: Xiao J, Tian M, Wang B et al.
articles.abstract: A single pre-transfer ultrasound screening cannot capture dynamic changes from estrus to ovulation. This may leads to inaccurate recipient selection and undetected reproductive abnormalities in non-eligible cows. We established a dynamic ultrasound monitoring (DUM) protocol with examinations on estrus day D0 (estrus detection), D1 (ovulation confirmation), and D6 (morphological assessment of the corpus luteum [CL]), and provided stage-specific management for non-eligible recipients. A total of 2,329 cows were randomly assigned to a control group (n = 1,165; a single ultrasonographic evaluation at the time of embryo transfer [ET]) or DUM group (n = 1,164). Before ET, first-service cows received a Presynch11/Ovsynch protocol, whereas second- and third-service cows were either observed for estrus or treated with an Ovsynch protocol based on whether or not they were observed in estrus up to pregnancy diagnosis of the previous breeding. In the control group, all non-eligible cows uniformly received Ovsynch + timed artificial insemination (AI). In the DUM group, non-eligible cows received stage-specific treatments based on ultrasound findings. In both groups, non-eligible cows were subsequently bred only via AI. The DUM group had a higher proportion of reconfirmed pregnancies per ET (43.2% vs. 37.4%). Among DUM cows, larger follicle diameter on D0 increased the proportion of reconfirmed pregnancies per ET (OR = 1.504), while severe bleeding at transfer reduced it (OR = 0.464). The non-eligible rates were similar between groups (28.9% in the control group and 28.2% in the DUM group). In the control group, the reasons for non-eligibility were predominantly absent CL (70.9%) or poor CL quality (17.2%), based on the single D7 evaluation. In the DUM group, the reasons were distributed across time points: 31.6% on D0 (presence of a large CL), and on D6, 26.7% due to no CL and 23.4% due to poor CL quality. Among non-eligible cows, the DUM group had a higher proportion of pregnancies per subsequent AI (42.9% vs. 28.5%), fewer services per pregnancy (2.53 vs. 2.82) and shorter days open (130.10 vs. 135.88). The cost per successful pregnancy in eligible recipients was $78.69 lower in the DUM group than in the control group. In conclusion, the DUM protocol improves both ET success and subsequent fertility of non-eligible recipients, offering an efficient management strategy for dairy herds.

articles.title: Cancer Cell CD73 Loss Promotes a Dual Inflammatory and Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Endometrial Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Lee HN, Zhang X, Crumley SM et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: CD73 is an emerging immunotherapy target that is overexpressed in many tumors and generates an adenosine-rich microenvironment to suppress antitumor immunity. In low-grade endometrial carcinoma, CD73 expression varies, and its impact on tumor immunobiology is unknown. Using two microsatellite-stable, grade 2 endometrioid endometrial carcinoma cohorts, in vitro NT5E (CD73) knockout/knockdown, and single-cell and spatial analyses, we show that cancer cell CD73 loss promotes a dual inflammatory and immunosuppressive microenvironment. Cancer cell CD73 loss was associated with increased lymphovascular space invasion and worse recurrence-free and overall survival, whereas stromal CD73 expression did not correlate with outcomes. CD73 downregulation induced pro-inflammatory gene expression, which strongly correlated with upregulation of immunosuppressive genes, including CD274 (PD-L1), suggesting a compensatory mechanism limiting antitumor immunity. Tumors with low cancer cell CD73 exhibited higher PD-L1 expression that correlated with increased CD3+ T-cell infiltration, reflecting an immune-engaged but checkpoint-restrained microenvironment. Single-cell analyses demonstrated that NT5E+ nonimmune cells in immune-responsive clusters were three times less likely to express CD274. In clinically relevant low-grade endometrial carcinoma models, functional studies confirmed that CD73 loss promoted both pro-inflammatory and immunosuppressive programs. These results reveal a context-specific role for CD73 in shaping the immune landscape of low-grade endometrial carcinoma that is distinct from its function in other solid tumors.
SIGNIFICANCE: Unlike most cancers, in which CD73 drives immunosuppression via overexpression, we show that cancer cell CD73 loss promotes an inflammatory yet compensatory immunosuppressive microenvironment in low-grade endometrial carcinoma, revealing a context-specific role. CD73 loss in endometrial carcinoma therefore may be as immunologically significant as its overexpression in other cancers.

articles.title: Targeted lactate depletion via gluconeogenesis by engineered hepatocyte-based micronanorobots for radiosensitization and immune activation.
articles.authors: Fan Y, Ye J, Chen Y et al.
articles.abstract: Radiotherapy is often limited by tumor-intrinsic DNA repair and an immunosuppressive microenvironment, both of which are reinforced by lactate accumulation. Here, we develop a CXCR4-engineered enucleated hepatocyte cytoplast platform decorated with Au-Pt Janus nanorobots (AP/LCCXCR4) to deplete intratumoral lactate and amplify radiation-induced oxidative stress. The hepatocyte cytoplasts home to tumors and consume lactate through gluconeogenesis, reducing repair-associated protein lactylation and impairing MRE11-RAD50-NBS1 (MRN) co-fractionation and chromatin recruitment, thereby impairing double-strand break repair. In parallel, the Au-Pt nanorobots enhance reactive oxygen species generation under acidic tumor conditions, increasing radiation damage. In radioresistant colorectal cancer models and a metastatic cervical cancer model, AP/LCCXCR4 combined with radiotherapy sustains DNA damage, promotes immunogenic cell death, reduces immunosuppressive myeloid and regulatory T (Treg) cell populations, enhances dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell activation, and improves tumor control and survival.

articles.title: Technological advances and comparative analyses of robotic surgery in the management of gynecologic cancer: surgical systems, evidence, and clinical outcomes.
articles.authors: Salum-Rodríguez L, Zalapa-Gómez MF, Santillán-Gómez A et al.
articles.abstract: Robotic surgery has transformed gynecologic oncologic surgical practice over the past two decades. The development of advanced systems such as the Da Vinci Xi, DV5 and SP, Hugo™ RAS, Versius®, and Senhance®, Hinotori, has expanded the capabilities of minimally invasive approaches, particularly in complex scenarios like surgical management of gynecological cancers. This review summarizes key technological advancements, discusses their clinical applicability, and compares robotic surgery with other surgical approaches (conventional laparoscopy and open surgery), with emphasis on quality of life, complications and oncology outcomes.

articles.title: Menopause and Neurology: Clinical Essentials.
articles.authors: Thornton HF, Bove R, Moores G et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Menopause is a neurobiological transition with important implications for neurologic care. This review summarizes the physiology and hormonal changes of spontaneous menopause and its treatment as applied to cognition, epilepsy, migraine, multiple sclerosis (MS), and stroke. It aims to serve as a resource for neurologists when managing patients in this transitional life stage.
RECENT FINDINGS: Hormonal shifts associated with menopause, particularly declining estrogen and fluctuating estrogen-to-progesterone ratios, influence symptoms, disease expression, and treatment across multiple neurologic conditions. Perimenopause is often associated with subjective cognitive complaints, in part attributed to hypoestrogenism, along with secondary effects from sleep disturbance, vasomotor symptoms, and mood changes. Cognitive symptoms are often transient and rarely with objective neuropsychological deficits or progression. In epilepsy, menopause-related endogenous and exogenous hormones may influence seizure susceptibility and alter antiseizure medication metabolism. Migraine may worsen during perimenopause, especially in estrogen-sensitive phenotypes, with postmenopause stabilization once hormones plateau. In MS, perimenopause and postmenopause contribute to overlapping age-related and MS-related symptoms and is a period of high clinical need with potential acceleration in disability progression despite reduced relapse rate. Ischemic stroke risk rises sharply in postmenopausal women driven by advancing age, accumulation of cardiometabolic risk, and loss of estrogen's protective effects. Oral estrogen-containing systemic menopause hormone therapy (MHT) is associated with increased thromboembolic events (including stroke), whereas transdermal regimens seem safer and are preferred at low or standard doses (≤50 mcg estradiol patch or ≤1.5 mg [or 2 pumps] per day of 0.06% estradiol gel). Timing of initiation also modulates this risk and plays a critical role with a favorable risk:benefit window when initiated in women younger than 60 years or within 10 years of menopause onset.
SUMMARY: Neurologists should routinely consider reproductive history, menopausal stage, symptom burden, and disease risk factors when evaluating midlife and older female patients. When appropriately selected, MHT can be safely used in many neurologic populations, with nonoral routes for estrogen and nonhormonal options generally preferred. Incorporating menopausal considerations…

articles.title: The Impact of Telemedicine Interventions on Maternal and Fetal Outcomes in Women With Gestational Diabetes: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.authors: He H, Deng J, Liu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) has a rising global prevalence and brings short-term and long-term adverse risks for mothers and fetuses. Conventional in-person GDM care is limited by time and geographic barriers, often resulting in suboptimal compliance and delayed individualized interventions. Telemedicine is increasingly applied in GDM management; however, randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence remains inconsistent.
OBJECTIVE: The study aims to pool data from RCTs to quantify the effects of telemedicine on glycemic control and pregnancy-related outcomes in women with GDM and to inform optimized clinical management.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus up to August 16, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study screening and data extraction. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Meta-analyses were conducted in Stata 18.0. For heterogeneous outcomes, 95% prediction intervals (PIs) were calculated to estimate effect ranges for future studies. Heterogeneity was explored via leave-one-out sensitivity, meta-regression, and subgroup analyses. The GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) framework rated evidence certainty. Publication bias was evaluated for outcomes reported in ≥10 studies.
RESULTS: Twenty-three RCTs (3055 women with GDM) were included. Pooled estimates suggested that telemedicine may reduce fasting glucose (mean difference [MD] -0.26, 95% CI -0.42 to -0.09, 95% PI -0.93 to 0.42; P=.002), 2-hour postprandial glucose (MD -0.50, 95% CI -0.87 to -0.14, 95% PI -1.84 to 0.84; P=.007), and gestational weight gain (MD -0.78, 95% CI -1.40 to -0.17, 95% PI -2.83 to 1.26; P=.01). Telemedicine was also associated with lower risks of cesarean section, emergency cesarean section, macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycemia, and neonatal respiratory distress. No significant differences were found for hemoglobin A1c, preterm birth, or neonatal intensive care unit admission. Notably, fasting glucose, 2-hour postprandial glucose, and gestational weight gain exhibited very high unexplained heterogeneity (I²>90%), with their 95% PIs crossing the null value despite statistically significant pooled effects. The GRADE certainty of evidence was very low to low across all assessed outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Telemedicine may improve selected glycemic and perinatal outcomes for women with GDM and may serve as a promising supplementary option for prenatal care, particularly in…

articles.title: Modified allostatic load and stress urinary incontinence in women: Evidence from a hospital-based cohort and NHANES.
articles.authors: Qiu G, Wang Y, Zhou Y et al.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveStress urinary incontinence (SUI) is common in women and is traditionally attributed to pelvic floor support failure and reproductive factors. However, emerging evidence suggests that systemic metabolic and inflammatory disturbances may also contribute to SUI. Modified allostatic load (MAL) integrates adiposity, blood pressure, glucose-lipid metabolism, and inflammation, but its association with SUI remains unclear. We examined this association in two independent cohorts.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included women from the Third Xiangya Hospital cohort (2017-2025) and the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 2005-2020). MAL was constructed from seven indicators: waist-to-height ratio, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, fasting glucose, triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and white blood cell count. Logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Dose-response, subgroup, sensitivity, and model-comparison analyses assessed robustness and model discrimination.ResultsThe main analyses included 8,932 women from the Third Xiangya Hospital cohort and 4,964 women from NHANES. Higher MAL was consistently associated with higher odds of SUI. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-point increase in MAL was associated with 15% higher odds of SUI in both cohorts. Compared with Q1, the highest MAL quartile was associated with increased odds of SUI in the Third Xiangya Hospital cohort (OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.66-2.18) and NHANES cohort (OR 1.88, 95% CI 1.48-2.37). The fully adjusted models including MAL showed limited discrimination (AUCs 0.674 and 0.599); adding MAL increased the AUC only slightly (by 0.011 and 0.022). Results were robust in sensitivity analyses, including MAL based on common fixed thresholds.ConclusionsHigher MAL was consistently associated with higher odds of prevalent SUI in two independent female cohorts. These cross-sectional findings support a multisystem physiological dysregulation framework for understanding SUI but do not establish causality or longitudinal predictive utility.

articles.title: Adolescent pregnancy and depressive symptoms in adulthood: A population-based longitudinal analysis examining substance use and socioeconomic pathways.
articles.authors: Jang H, Son H, Park H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Adolescent pregnancy has well-documented socioeconomic consequences, yet its long-term associations with adult mental health remain underexplored. This study examines associations between adolescent pregnancy outcomes (live birth, miscarriage, abortion) and adult depressive symptoms, exploring substance use and socioeconomic attainment as potential pathways.
STUDY DESIGN: Prospective longitudinal cohort study using a nationally representative sample of US women (n = 6163) followed from adolescence into adulthood.
METHODS: Using four waves of the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health (Add Health), we estimated lagged dependent variable regression models with school fixed effects to address baseline differences and unobserved school-level confounding. Cigarette smoking, binge drinking, educational attainment, and personal earnings were tested as mediators via delta-method mediation analysis.
RESULTS: Adolescent miscarriage (β = 0.645, 95% CI: 0.106, 1.183) and live birth (β = 0.365, 95% CI: 0.104, 0.627) were associated with elevated adult depressive symptoms in fully adjusted models, corresponding to approximately 25% and 14% of the outcome standard deviation, respectively. The association for abortion was not statistically significant. Educational attainment and cigarette smoking emerged as statistically significant mediators. Joint indirect effects accounted for 0.091 (95% CI: 0.023, 0.160), 0.099 (95% CI: 0.032, 0.166), and 0.126 (95% CI: 0.082, 0.169) for miscarriage, abortion, and live birth, respectively, corresponding to roughly 14%, 30%, and 35% of the total effect.
CONCLUSIONS: Adolescent pregnancy is associated with elevated adult depressive symptoms, particularly for miscarriage and live birth. Part of these associations was accounted for by educational disruption and increased substance use. Public health efforts should prioritize prevention of social disadvantage, early identification of at-risk adolescents, and integrated reproductive and mental health services for young women who experience adolescent pregnancy.

articles.title: Factors associated with embryo recovery in mares: A retrospective multicenter analysis and practical overview of embryo flushing protocols.
articles.authors: Sala-Ayala L, Pietrani M, Losinno L et al.
articles.abstract: Embryo recovery (ER) is a major determinant of efficiency in equine embryo-transfer programs and may be influenced by biological, management, and technical factors. This retrospective multicenter study aimed to identify factors associated with positive ER and to describe the embryo-flushing (EF) techniques used in three commercial embryo-transfer programs. We hypothesized that factors associated with ER would differ among clinics because of differences in mare populations, semen types, management practices, and flushing systems. The study included 2861 EF cycles: 465 cycles from 196 mares in Clinic 1, 661 cycles from 265 mares in Clinic 2, and 1735 cycles from 277 mares in Clinic 3. Factors associated with positive ER were evaluated separately for each clinic using multivariable generalized linear mixed models, with mare identity included as a random intercept. Additional univariable analyses were used to examine selected factors individually. Overall ER was 55.7%, 51.4%, and 73.5% in Clinics 1, 2, and 3, respectively. In the multivariable analyses, none of the evaluated fixed effects were significantly associated with ER in Clinic 1. In Clinic 2, semen type was the only significant fixed effect, with greater odds of ER using chilled than frozen semen (OR = 2.07, 95% CI: 1.37-3.11; p < 0.001). Clinic 3 used fresh semen exclusively, and donor mare age was the only significant fixed effect, with the odds of ER decreasing by 9% for each additional year of age (OR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.88-0.94; p < 0.001). Although the overall effect of season phase was not significant in Clinic 3, ER was lower during mid-season than early season (OR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.46-0.99; p = 0.043). Mare identity had a significant random effect in all three clinics (p ≤ 0.05), indicating substantial between-mare variability. Repeated EF within the same season did not reduce ER in any clinic, including among mares undergoing four or more cycles. In the additional analyses, multiple ovulation was associated with higher ER in Clinics 1 and 3 but not in Clinic 2. In Clinic 2, experienced operators showed a tendency toward higher ER than less experienced operators (52.4% vs. 37.7%; p = 0.06). In conclusion, factors associated with ER differed among clinical settings. The consistent mare effect, the absence of a decline in ER with repeated flushing, and the potential influence of operator experience emphasize the importance of individual mare fertility and clinic-specific management when…

articles.title: Diagnostic value of breast MRI and Kaiser score in BIRADS 0 and 4 lesions compared with histopathology and follow-up.
articles.authors: Zengin E, Şimşir BD, Çevik ME et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed cancer type in women, and early detection and treatment significantly improve survival rates. In conventional imaging methods (mammography and ultrasound), lesions classified as BI-RADS 0 or 4 often lead to a high rate of unnecessary biopsies, resulting in both superfluous invasive procedures for patients and increased costs for the healthcare system. The aim of our study is to investigate the diagnostic validity of the Kaiser score in predicting malignancy in patients who underwent breast MRI following inconclusive or suspicious findings (BI-RADS 0 or 4) on conventional imaging, based on pathology results or clinical follow-up.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between September 2022 and April 2024, 99 patients who underwent breast MRI due to inconclusive results from conventional breast imaging methods (mammography and breast ultrasound) or the detection of suspicious findings (BI-RADS 0 or 4), and who had either histopathological evaluation following biopsy under US or MG guidance or were followed for at least 12 months, were included in this single-center retrospective study. The 99 patients included in the study were divided into two groups based on histopathology or follow-up outcomes (benign lesion group and malignant lesion group). Comparisons were made between these two groups.
RESULTS: When comparing benign and malignant groups, statistically significant differences were observed for age (p < 0,001), age at menarche (p = 0,004), breastfeeding status (p = 0,009), menopausal status (p = 0,017), and use of hormone replacement therapy (p = 0,036). MRI BI-RADS (p < 0,001) and Kaiser scores (p < 0,001) were notably higher in the malignant group. Kaiser score was identified as the strongest diagnostic predictor of malignancy (AUC = 0,977, 95 % CI: 0.955-0.999; p < 0,001). Using a cut-off value of Kaiser score > 5, the sensitivity and specificity were 97 % (95 % CI: 84.2 %-99.9 %) and 87.9 % (95 % CI: 77.5 %-94.6 %), respectively. The MRI BI-RADS ranked second with a cut-off value > 4 (AUC = 0.878, 95 % CI: 0.805-0.950; p < 0.001); at this threshold, the sensitivity and specificity were 60.6 % (95 % CI: 42.1 %-77.1 %) and 100 % (95 % CI: 94.6 %-100.0 %), respectively. In multivariable logistic regression, higher Kaiser score (OR = 4.25, p < 0.001) and older age (OR = 1.16, p = 0.041) were associated with higher odds of malignancy, whereas older age at menarche was associated with lower odds (OR = 0.347,…

articles.title: Ovarian reserve and miscarriage risk outside assisted reproduction: a large cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Murugesu S, Wainwright E, Grant Z et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Miscarriage is the most common pregnancy complication and is associated with significant psychological morbidity. Previous studies, largely conducted in infertile patients and those undergoing assisted reproduction, have reported an association between low ovarian reserve and miscarriage. However, these findings may not generalise to women in the general population where evidence remains limited and inconsistent. This study investigates whether age-adjusted ovarian reserve is associated with a history of miscarriage among women accessing reproductive health testing services, independent of assisted reproduction.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This study leverages a large, structured digital reproductive health assessment capturing menstrual, symptom, lifestyle and medical history data to enable population-scale reproductive phenotyping. This was a retrospective cohort study of women who underwent diagnostic blood testing including AMH testing (September 2020-February 2025), outside of a fertility clinic setting. AMH was categorised into age-specific centiles (low, moderately low, within range, moderately high, high) and modelled as age-normalised z-scores. Pregnancy outcomes were grouped as live birth(s) only (LBO), miscarriage(s) only (MO), live birth(s) and miscarriage(s) (LBM), or never been pregnant (NBP). Binary logistic regression assessed associations between AMH range and history of miscarriage, adjusting for potential confounders. Miscarriage rate was calculated as miscarriages divided by total pregnancies and modelled against AMH z-scores.
RESULTS: Among 6,827 women reporting previous pregnancy, 4,141 (60.7 %) reported at least one miscarriage. AMH distribution differed across pregnancy history groups; however, associations observed in unadjusted analyses between moderately low or high AMH and miscarriage were attenuated after multivariable adjustment. Age-adjusted AMH z-scores demonstrated no clear relationship with miscarriage rate. Secondary analyses including women who had never been pregnant showed higher median AMH in this group.
CONCLUSION: In this large cohort, outside assisted reproduction settings, age-adjusted AMH was not independently associated with miscarriage history or miscarriage rate. These findings suggest ovarian reserve should not be used to retrospectively explain pregnancy loss or infer miscarriage risk in women outside ART settings.

articles.title: Incidence and clinical impact of venous thromboembolism during immunotherapy for gynecologic cancer.
articles.authors: Abdeen CS, Sciuva J, O'Connor RM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the incidence, risk factors, and clinical outcomes associated with venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with gynecologic cancer treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with gynecologic malignancies treated with ICI at a single institution between January 2017 and April 2026. The primary outcome was the development of VTE from ICI initiation through one month after the final cycle. Incidence, clinical characteristics, risk factors, and healthcare utilization were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 458 patients who received ICI therapy, 37 (8.1%) experienced a VTE. Deep vein thrombosis was the most common event (48.6%, n = 18), followed by pulmonary embolism (40.5%, n = 15). The median time from ICI initiation to VTE was 1.43 months (IQR, 0.70-2.93). Endometrial cancer was the most common disease site among patients with VTE (54.1%, n = 20). Smoking history differed significantly between groups (p < 0.01). ICI monotherapy was more common among patients who experienced VTE compared with those who did not (64.9% vs. 44.9%, p = 0.020), and patients with VTE had received fewer total lines of therapy (2.4 vs. 3.3, p = 0.008). Most events required emergency department evaluation (64.9%, n = 24) and hospitalization (59.5%, n = 22), and ICI therapy was delayed in 24.3% (n = 9) of cases. Breakthrough thrombosis was observed in 18.9% (n = 7) of patients receiving anticoagulation.
CONCLUSION: VTE occurred in 8.1% of gynecologic cancer patients receiving ICI, was early in onset, and carried significant clinical burden. These data can guide provider awareness and patient counseling when initiating ICI in this population.

articles.title: Low-grade serous ovarian cancer: 2026 expert consensus report.
articles.authors: Grisham RN, Slomovitz B, Podder V et al.
articles.abstract: Low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (LGSOC) is a rare epithelial malignancy characterized by frequent mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway alterations, hormone receptor expression, relative resistance to cytotoxic chemotherapy, and a prolonged, relapsing clinical course. Since publication of the 2023 international expert consensus, significant advances have reshaped the management of both newly diagnosed and recurrent disease. The 2026 LGSOC Consensus Conference convened an international multidisciplinary panel of experts in the field to review emerging evidence and update recommendations across pathology, molecular testing, translational biology, frontline and recurrent treatment, imaging, treatment-associated toxicity, regulatory strategy, patient advocacy, and future research priorities. Recommendations were informed by contemporary clinical evidence, multidisciplinary discussion, and patient perspectives. The updated consensus incorporates practice-changing data from NRG-GY019 supporting chemotherapy-containing postoperative therapy as the current reference approach for stage II-IV disease while recognizing selected circumstances in which endocrine monotherapy may represent individualized de-escalation. It also integrates recent advances in recurrent disease, including the US Food and Drug Administration's accelerated approval of avutometinib in combination with defactinib for KRAS-mutated LGSOC, emerging evidence supporting endocrine therapy combined with CDK4/6 inhibition, and refined guidance for biomarker-directed treatment selection, imaging assessment, toxicity management, and patient-centered survivorship. The panel emphasizes treatment-specific biomarker interpretation, multidisciplinary care, central pathology review for clinical trials, and the continued need for prospective studies addressing treatment sequencing, predictive biomarkers, and quality-of-life outcomes. This updated international consensus provides an evidence-based framework for the diagnosis and management of LGSOC while identifying priorities for future clinical research and drug development.

articles.title: A cross-sectional survey exploring experiences in accessing hormone replacement therapy following risk-reducing surgery for individuals with hereditary ovarian cancer risk.
articles.authors: Thornton S, O'Loughlin M, Nuk J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the current landscape of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) to treat surgical menopause following bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO) in individuals with hereditary ovarian cancer risk in British Columbia, Canada. We aimed to describe current use of HRT, identify factors associated with HRT use and identify potential barriers for uptake and access.
METHODS: Individuals with germline pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in an ovarian cancer susceptibility gene were identified through the BC Cancer Hereditary Cancer Program (HCP) Progeny database. A cross-sectional survey was administered to collect participant demographics, personal and family cancer history, and participant experiences with HRT. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the sample and logistic regression used to explore associations between sociodemographic variables and reported HRT use. Open text fields were analyzed using inductive quantitative content analysis.
RESULTS: In total, 374 responses were received from 1284 potential participants (29.1% response rate). Of participants who have had a BSO, 41% (101/245) report HRT use. In open-text responses, 22% of participants reported lack of support by healthcare professionals and 26% described gaps in counselling about HRT and surgical menopause. In the regression analysis, HRT use was less likely in individuals who: were of increasing age, reported a history of any cancer type and who reported receiving no counselling about HRT (all p < 0.0011 after Bonferroni correction).
CONCLUSION: Barriers to HRT access and uptake exist for individuals at increased risk of ovarian cancer. Together this data indicates that patients require additional support in this area particularly as it relates to education and resources.

articles.title: Comparison of DXA- and CT-based measurements of abdominal visceral adipose tissue in premenopausal women.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical densitometry : the official journal of the International Society for Clinical Densitometry
articles.authors: Olenick AA, Melanson EL, Shanbhag P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and computed tomography (CT) for estimating visceral adipose tissue (VAT) area in premenopausal women, and to evaluate whether DXA can track VAT changes over time.
METHODS: VAT area (cm²) was measured using DXA and CT on the same day in 66 premenopausal women before (baseline) and after a 20-week prospective intervention trial; the current study is a secondary analysis of these data. Correlation, Bland-Altman, and regression analyses were performed. A regression-based adjustment equation was developed to align DXA with CT values and applied to baseline and follow-up data, with robustness assessed using bootstrap resampling. Analyses were stratified by body mass index (BMI: normal, overweight, obese).
RESULTS: At baseline, DXA significantly overestimated VAT compared with CT (DXA: 98.7 ± 49.5 cm² vs CT: 67.7 ± 33.1 cm²; mean difference +31.0 ± 7.3 cm², p ≤ 0.001), though measures were strongly correlated (r² = 0.87, p ≤ 0.001). Overestimation increased with higher BMI. However, DXA and CT measures of VAT change over 20 weeks were not correlated (r² = 0.00, p = 0.834). A regression-based adjustment equation reduced baseline bias (+31.0 cm² to +4.0 ± 5.8 cm² difference) but did not improve agreement for longitudinal changes.
CONCLUSIONS: DXA provides a correlated but biased estimate of VAT area at a single time point compared with CT, with greater overestimation at higher BMI. A regression-based adjustment equation improves baseline agreement but does not enhance the detection of VAT change over time. DXA should be used cautiously for monitoring longitudinal VAT changes in women.

articles.title: Sex differences in human papillomavirus vaccination among Japanese university students and associated factors: a cross-sectional study examining the mediating effect of knowledge and interactions.
articles.authors: Yodawara C, Iio Y, Ejiri H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rates among Japanese university students, especially among males, remain low. Following the suspension of active recommendations in 2013, vaccination rates have not improved since their resumption in 2022; male vaccination has not been established as a routine.
OBJECTIVES: To describe sex-specific HPV vaccination status and associated factors, examine sex differences in associated patterns, and examine the potential mediating role of HPV-related knowledge.
METHODS: This web-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among undergraduates at a Japanese university in April 2025. The data of 3203 participants (1760 males, 1443 females) were analyzed. Self-reported vaccination history was the primary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression, bootstrap-based mediation analysis, and interaction analysis were performed.
RESULTS: The vaccination rate was 30.1% (3.2% among males vs. 62.9% among females; P < 0.001). Male sex was strongly negatively associated with vaccination (OR = 0.024; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.017-0.034). Knowledge of free vaccination (OR = 3.477) and HPV-related diseases (OR = 1.758) showed positive associations. In females, only knowledge variables were significant, whereas in males, lifestyle variables were also associated. The indirect effect of sex on vaccination via HPV-related knowledge was statistically significant (indirect effect β = -0.263; 95% CI: -0.383 to -0.141), indicating partial mediation. Among unvaccinated males, 81.1% reported not needing the vaccine; 50.4% of unvaccinated females cited concerns about adverse effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Legislation mandating routine vaccination for males, subsidized costs, parental education, and sex-specific university-based programs are needed.

articles.title: Advanced ovarian cancer in women aged ≥80 years: a retrospective single-center study.
articles.journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
articles.authors: Schoenen S, Martinez Gomez C, Bresson L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Approximately one-third of ovarian cancers occur in women older than 70 years, and this proportion is expected to increase with population ageing. Complete cytoreductive surgery remains a key component of treatment. However, elderly patients are frequently undertreated due to concerns about frailty and surgical morbidity. The primary objective of this study was to assess the feasibility and outcomes of cytoreductive surgery in carefully selected patients aged ≥80 years with advanced ovarian cancer.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study including patients aged ≥80 years treated for advanced ovarian cancer (FIGO stages III-IV) between 2017 and 2024 at the Oscar Lambret Cancer Center, Lille, France. Clinical characteristics, geriatric parameters, treatment strategies, surgical procedures, and oncological and postoperative outcomes were collected.
RESULTS: Among 638 patients treated for advanced ovarian cancer during this period, 42 were aged ≥80 years (median: 82). Thirteen patients (31.0%) underwent cytoreductive surgery, of whom 9 (69.2%) underwent interval debulking procedures after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. No gross residual disease was achieved in 11 patients (84.6%). The median hospital stay was 11 days (IQR, 8-11). All patients lived at home before cytoreductive surgery, and 12 (92.3%) were discharged directly home postoperatively, while one patient was transferred to a nursing home. In the cytoreductive surgery group, the 2-year progression-free survival and overall survival rates were 55.9% (CI95%, 23.4-79.3) and 81.5% (CI95%, 43.5-95.1), respectively.
CONCLUSION: In patients aged ≥80 years with advanced ovarian cancer, cytoreductive surgery is feasible in carefully selected individuals. Importantly, surgical management should remain as simple as possible, after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, if necessary, with the aim of achieving no gross residual disease while preserving functional independence.

articles.title: Maternal antibody repertoires in preeclampsia revealed by phage immunoprecipitation sequencing.
articles.authors: Vesterlund G, Wedenoja S, Vallo T et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Preeclampsia (PE) is a pregnancy-associated hypertensive disorder characterized by maternal systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Although aberrant maternal-fetal immunotolerance plays a role in the pathogenesis, the breadth and specificity of maternal antibody responses remain poorly defined.
METHODS: We performed phage immunoprecipitation sequencing (PhIP-Seq) to profile antibody reactivity against 42,692 peptides representing 16,296 proteins across 661 species in women with PE (n = 15) and control pregnancies (n = 33). Selected autoantigens were further evaluated using germline and placental expression datasets and RT-qPCR in independent placental samples.
RESULTS: Maternal antibody repertoires in PE differed from controls at the level of individual antigens despite a similar overall number of antibody targets. Among 59 endogenous targets enriched in PE, 48 showed male germline associated expression, including CATSPERZ, DCAF8L2, and NBPF3. Many of these targets also showed expression in placental and vascular tissue, and placental expression of selected targets was confirmed by RT-qPCR in an independent cohort. In addition, selective differences in microbial and viral antibody reactivity were observed, including enrichment of Streptococcus dysgalactiae, EBV and influenza A virus antigens in PE, and reduced recognition of HSV-1 antigens.
CONCLUSION: PE is associated with an altered maternal antibody profile characterized by autoreactivity to placental and developmental antigens. The overlap between antibody targets and placental expression identifies a previously unrecognized pattern of maternal immune recognition involving shared placental and male germline-associated antigen programs in PE. These findings suggest that maternal immune responses are associated with disease pathophysiology.

articles.title: The short version of the Postpartum Bonding Questionnaire: A cross-country psychometric study of mothers.
articles.authors: Jarašiūnaitė-Fedosejeva G, Radoš SN, Ayers S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Postpartum Bonding Questionnaire (PBQ) is widely used and considered a robust measure in terms of psychometric characteristics to assess difficulties in mother-infant bonding; however, the original 25-item version has yielded inconsistent factor solutions across studies and cultural contexts. Shorter versions may enhance feasibility for routine screening. Using multicountry data, the present study aimed to establish a short version of the PBQ that reflects the original structure and demonstrates adequate psychometric properties across countries.
METHODS: Data were collected from 1731 postpartum women across five European countries participating in the INTERSECT study. Participants completed the PBQ and the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale at 6-12 weeks postpartum, with a subsample reassessed at 26 weeks postpartum (n = 352). Item reduction and factor structure were examined using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses on split samples. Measurement invariance, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and associations with depressive symptoms were assessed.
RESULTS: Analyses supported a unidimensional 10-item PBQ version with good model fit (RMSEA= .072; CFI=.973, TLI=.965, SRMR=.052), internal consistency (McDonald's ω=.82), and test-retest reliability (ICC=.73). This version showed a strong correlation with the original PBQ and demonstrated configural, metric, and scalar measurement invariance across countries. The short version was moderately associated with depressive symptoms.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings support a brief, reliable PBQ version for assessing maternal bonding difficulties and suggest that variability in prior factor structures reflects differences in item stability rather than the absence of a coherent underlying construct.

articles.title: Multi-omics analysis reveals ITGA2 mediates DEHP-induced decidual endothelial dysfunction in recurrent pregnancy loss.
articles.authors: Jiang Z, Wu X, Luo Y et al.
articles.abstract: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP), a ubiquitous environmental endocrine disruptor, has been detected in over 97% of pregnant women. Epidemiological studies have linked DEHP exposure to increased risk of recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL); however, the underlying mechanistic pathways remain poorly characterized. This study employed an integrated multi-omics approach combining network toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization (MR), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which DEHP exposure induces RPL. Network toxicology analysis identified 143 shared targets between DEHP-associated genes and RPL-related genes, which were significantly enriched in focal adhesion and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways. Integration of machine learning analysis on RPL transcriptomic data with MR identified ITGA2 as a genetically supported protective factor causally associated with RPL. scRNA-seq precisely localized ITGA2 expression to decidual endothelial cells, where it was significantly downregulated in RPL patients.
