In silico gene knockout predicted that ITGA2 deficiency leads to dysregulation of angiogenesis- and immune regulation-associated genes, impairing decidual endothelial cell function and the immunological microenvironment. MD simulation predicted that DEHP forms a direct, stable complex with the extracellular domain of ITGA2. In HUVECs, DEHP dose-dependently reduced ITGA2 mRNA and protein levels and impaired migration. Silencing ITGA2 reproduced this migration defect, indicating that ITGA2 downregulation contributes to DEHP-induced endothelial dysfunction. Collectively, these findings identify ITGA2 as a biologically and genetically supported candidate linking DEHP exposure to impaired decidual endothelial function in RPL and provide a basis for future biomarker and mechanistic studies.

articles.title: Impact of an Extra Virgin Olive Oil-enriched Diet in Diabetic Dams on the Decidua of offspring Prone to Gestational Diabetes.
articles.authors: Gatti CR, Roberti SL, Montero V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During early pregnancy, the decidua supports embryo development and maternal adaptations to pregnancy. Maternal diabetes programs gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in offspring, and a pro-oxidant intrauterine environment has been implicated. Diets enriched with extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) can provide antioxidant effects. This study hypothesized that EVOO-enriched diets administered to pregestational diabetic pregnant rats (F0) would confer beneficial effects on the decidua of their early-pregnant offspring (F1), who are prone to developing GDM.
AIMS: To evaluate signaling pathways and pro-oxidant state markers in the decidua of 9 d pregnant offspring of diabetic dams who either received or did not receive a 6% EVOO-enriched diet during the F0 pregnancy.
METHODS: Rats with mild diabetes and controls were fed diets with or without 6% EVOO during F0 pregnancy, and their 9 d pregnant offspring were then evaluated. Markers of decidual function (prolactin, PPAR and mTOR pathways) and the pro-oxidant state were evaluated in the decidua.
RESULTS: Despite normal maternal glycemia and progesterone levels, the decidua of 9 d pregnant offspring of diabetic dams exhibited reduced prolactin and mTOR pathway activity. PPAR levels decreased, while microRNAs that regulate their expression increased. These alterations were not prevented by the EVOO-enriched diet provided in the F0 generation. Levels of FABP4 (involved in decidualization and a marker of a pro-oxidant state) and lipoperoxidation were increased in the decidua of 9 d pregnant offspring of diabetic dams. The EVOO-enriched diet prevented these alterations.
CONCLUSION: Maternal diabetes programs impaired markers of decidualization and the pro-oxidant state in early-pregnancy offspring. These alterations were partially ameliorated by maternal diets enriched with EVOO.

articles.title: Loss of KAT5-dependent H2A.Z acetylation provokes chromosomal instability in recurrent pregnancy loss.
articles.authors: Bi S, Chen Y, Zhang L et al.
articles.abstract: Placenta defects are one of the major causes of miscarriages, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that trophoblast-specific depletion of the acetyltransferase Kat5, or introduction of acetylation-defective mutants Kat5-Q377E G380E and Kat5-Y47A, induces severe chromosomal instability (CIN) during trophoblast cells division, leading to embryonic lethality. Moreover, mutation of a key lysine acetyltransferase 5 (KAT5) substrate, H2A.Z, via the introduction of H2az1-K5R K8R K12R K14R (which prevents H2A.Z acetylation), phenocopies the effects of KAT5 loss. Integrated RNA sequencing and CUT&Tag in mouse trophoblast stem cells reveal that KAT5, through H2A.Z acetylation, regulates transcription of key mitotic genes (Aurka, Aurkb, and Cenpa). We extend our finding to human trophoblast stem cells, demonstrating a conserved role for KAT5 in preventing CIN. Clinical analysis of placental villi from recurrent pregnancy loss patients with copy number variations revealed reduced expression of KAT5 and acetylated H2A.Z. This study demonstrates that the conserved KAT5-H2A.Z acetylation pathway safeguards chromosomal stability in trophoblast cells, supporting placenta development and successful pregnancy.

articles.title: Interferon-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells protects against congenital Zika virus infection.
articles.authors: Dedloff MR, Reinhardt TR, Ropp TF et al.
articles.abstract: Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor (Ifnar1-/-) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors (Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/-) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection in Ifnar1-/- dams compared to Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/- dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus of Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/- dams compared to Ifnar1-/- dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ-responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

articles.title: Molecular profiling of ovarian cancer is feasible and provides valuable therapeutic and research information to women in Aotearoa New Zealand.
articles.authors: Simcock B, Wilson M, Vaughan M et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Molecular profiling of ovarian cancer is feasible and provides valuable therapeutic and research information to women in Aotearoa New Zealand.
METHOD: Sixteen women consecutively diagnosed with apparent advanced ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer underwent molecular profiling as part of INOVATe (Individualised Ovarian Cancer Treatment through Integration of Genomic Pathology into Multidisciplinary Care), an ovarian cancer precision medicine programme conducted in New South Wales, Australia.
RESULTS: All eligible women who were approached agreed to participate in the study. Molecular profiling was successfully undertaken on tumour tissue samples stored after primary surgery and in two of three core biopsy samples. Six of 9 women (67%) with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma had tumour samples classified as having homologous recombination deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) repair deficiency, an alteration that predicts response to poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors. Overall, 7/15 (47%) with a sample available for testing had a tier 1 molecular alteration, indicating the potential for a Food and Drug Administration-approved therapy. Additional potentially targetable alterations included CCNE1 gene amplification in two patients with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, and PIK3CA mutations in two patients with clear cell ovarian cancer.
CONCLUSION: Molecular profiling of ovarian cancer is feasible and provides valuable information that can guide available therapeutic options and selection into clinical trials.

articles.title: Initiation of Medical Therapy for Storage Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms After Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Surgery.
articles.authors: Uy M, DiBianco JM, Mansour S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: De novo anticholinergic or beta-3 agonist (Ach/B3a) initiation for storage lower urinary tract symptoms is a clinically significant but understudied outcome after benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) surgery. We estimated procedure-specific cumulative incidence of Ach/B3a medication initiation and identified associated patient- and procedure-level factors.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using Michigan statewide claims data (2017-2022) from the Michigan Value Collaborative, Ach/B3a-naive patients who underwent BPH surgery were identified. Procedures included transurethral resection of the prostate, laser photovaporization (PVP), laser enucleation of the prostate, robotic waterjet therapy, prostatic urethral lift, water vapor thermal therapy, transurethral microwave thermotherapy, prostatic artery embolization, and simple prostatectomy. De novo Ach/B3a initiation was defined as a prescription fill for an Ach/B3a between 3 and 12 months postoperatively. Cumulative incidence was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis; Cox proportional hazards models identified associated factors.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 11,519 Ach/B3a medication-naive patients. Twelve-month cumulative incidence ranged from 5.7% (transurethral microwave thermotherapy) to 11% (PVP). On multivariable analysis, PVP was associated with higher hazard of initiation compared with transurethral resection of the prostate (HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.25-1.79). Prior BPH medication use and prior anticoagulation use were associated with higher hazard of initiation, whereas preoperative catheter dependence was associated with lower hazard.
CONCLUSION: In this statewide cohort of Ach/B3a-naive patients undergoing contemporary BPH procedures, de novo Ach/B3a medication initiation was uncommon but procedure-specific, with 12-month cumulative incidence ranging from 5.7% to 11%, with PVP carrying the highest hazard. These findings provide real-world benchmarks to guide counseling across contemporary BPH interventions.

articles.title: Male-First Evaluation Reduces Costs and Time to Pregnancy in Couples with a Varicocele: A Theoretical, Discrete-Time Markov Model.
articles.authors: Wayne G, Ha A, Egbuonu K et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to develop a discrete-time Markov model estimating pregnancy success rates and costs of a male-first evaluation compared with alternative infertility treatment approaches in couples where the male partner has a clinically significant varicocele.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A novel discrete-time Markov chain was constructed using transition probabilities, treatment success, and discontinuation rates derived from published data. Simulation analyses were performed across varying levels of varicocele repair efficacy. The model evaluated hypothetical couples younger than 35 years with ≥ 12 months of infertility due to varicocele-associated oligospermia. Four treatment strategies were compared: current practice (CP), male-first evaluation (MFE), intrauterine insemination first (IUI), and in vitro fertilization first (IVF). The primary outcomes were time and mean cost estimates for the population.
RESULTS: At a 1% post-varicocele repair improvement, 75% achieved pregnancy at 20.1 months ($35,551) with CP, 21.2 months ($38,892) with MFE, 16.8 months ($41,325) with IUI, and 12.3 months ($49,537) with IVF. At a 5% improvement, MFE became cost favorable (19.2 months, $33,977) in comparison with CP (19.9 months, $34,172). At 15%, MFE reduced time to pregnancy by 1.7 months and cost by approximately $6000 compared with CP and remained $11,000-$21,000 less costly than IUI or IVF. Results remained robust across all 3 analyses (analytic propagation and both Monte Carlo simulations).
CONCLUSIONS: In varicocele-related infertility, MFE modestly reduces cost and time to pregnancy compared with CP. Immediate assisted reproductive technologies shorten time to pregnancy but increase costs by 40% to 80%. MFE represents a cost-conscious strategy that may optimize outcomes for the selected population.

articles.title: Precancerous cervical lesions and associated factors among HIV-positive women in Southern and Eastern African countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Alemu GG, Bazezew AM, Yirsaw AN et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women living with HIV (WLHIV) face a sixfold increased risk of cervical cancer compared to HIV-negative women. Most WLHIV residing in the Southern and Eastern African regions have a substantial HIV-related cervical cancer burden. Studies on precancerous cervical lesions (PCCL) and associated factors in WLHIV from these regions have inconsistent and inconclusive findings. Therefore, we aimed to synthesize the pooled prevalence of PCCL and associated factors among WLHIV in Southern and Eastern Africa.
METHODS: This study was registered under PROSPERO (CRD420251123583) and conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 standards. Primary studies published from inception to 2025 in Southern and Eastern Africa were included. The methodological quality of studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale. Data extraction and statistical analyses were done in Microsoft Excel and STATA 17, respectively. Pooled prevalence, publication bias, subgroup, and sensitivity analysis were conducted. Associations were expressed as odds ratios (OR), and a p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: 44 studies met the inclusion criteria, with a sample size of 47,009. The pooled prevalence of PCCL was 22.25% (95% CI: 19.57, 24.93). Age at first sexual intercourse (< 18 years) (OR = 2.99, (2.34, 3.82)), multiparity (OR = 4.97, (3.21, 7.69)), having multiple sexual partners (OR = 3.06 (2.45, 3.83)), having a history of sexually transmitted infections (STI) (OR = 3.93 (3.23, 4.78)), smoking (OR = 7.01, (3.39, 14.49)), ever taking oral contraceptive pills (OR = 2.69, (1.85, 3.90)), low CD4 count (OR = 1.79, (1.56, 2.05)), and having not initiated antiretroviral therapy (ART) (OR = 2.02, (1.56, 2.62)) were significantly associated with an increased risk of PCCL.
CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS: The pooled prevalence of PCCL was high. Additionally, early first sexual intercourse, parity, STIs, multiple sexual partners, smoking, oral contraceptive use, CD4 count, and ART were positively associated with the occurrence of PCCL. Therefore, stakeholders shall implement interventions to avert future incidents of PCCL and address the identified factors.

articles.title: Si-scRNA-seq: Enabling ambient-stable single-cell transcriptomics through spatially confined biosilicification.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.ta: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.authors: Zhou L, Ruan T, He Y et al.
articles.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is constrained by rapid RNA degradation during sample storage, necessitating cold-chain logistics. Here we present spatially confined biosilicification (SCB), wherein RNA is encapsulated within a nanoscopic layer of amorphous silicon dioxide, as a highly effective methodology enabling ambient-temperature preservation of single-cell transcriptomes. By judiciously incorporating a silicification inhibitor, SCB achieves spatiotemporal control over both intra- and extracellular silica deposition, preventing excessive crosslinking and cell aggregation while preserving RNA biointegrity and accessibility. scRNA-seq performed with biosilicified cells (Si-scRNA-seq) maintained high transcriptomic fidelity with fresh samples (R2 = 0.95 after 7 d) extending RNA half-life to 54.8 d at 25 °C, a 685-fold improvement compared to unprotected samples. Furthermore, Si-scRNA-seq confers robust resistance against oxidative and UV degradation. Compatible with mainstream platforms at ~0.1 RMB per sample, Si-scRNA-seq successfully resolves cellular heterogeneity in clinical lung, liver, and ovarian cancer specimens after extended room-temperature storage. Si-scRNA-seq provides a scalable and cold-chain-free solution for single-cell transcriptomics in research and clinical settings.

articles.title: Interobserver variability in the interpretation of Papanicolaou tests using the Hologic Genius Digital Diagnostics System: detailed analysis of cytology verification in a large academic laboratory.
articles.authors: Corbin H, Matsko J, Charity T et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Whole-slide digital imaging technology paired with artificial intelligence is transforming the practice of cervical cancer screening. We aimed to evaluate the performance of the Hologic Genius Digital Diagnostics System (HGDDS) for detection of neoplasia and to investigate interobserver variability among users who have undergone HGDDS training.
METHODS: A total of 110 ThinPrep Papanicolaou tests were selected, with original diagnoses that included 47 cases of low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or worse (LSIL+); 4 cases of unsatisfactory findings; and 59 cases negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM), including 23 cases with microorganisms. All cases were reviewed by 16 cytologists or cytopathologists using the HGDDS. Interobserver variability and correlation with original diagnoses were assessed.
RESULTS: The HGDDS showed greater than 95% sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and accuracy for LSIL+ disease. The overall misinterpretation rate was 5.5%. In total, 3 cases had poor interpretation (≥7/16 misinterpretations), including a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion case with 2 adenocarcinoma responses, an LSIL response, and 4 unsatisfactory responses, as well as 2 NILM cases interpreted as unsatisfactory by most participants due to borderline cellularity. Of 23 cases with microorganisms, organisms were not present in the 60-image gallery for 4 cases. Sensitivity was highest for Trichomonas (93.8%) but was low for other microorganisms (58.9%-68.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: In a large academic cytology laboratory, HGDDS review by trained users demonstrated high concordance with adjudicated diagnoses for detection of LSIL+, supporting its effectiveness for identifying epithelial abnormalities. However, user experience with digital morphology is important. During early implementation, laboratories should monitor discordance and consider temporary dual review, with particular attention to borderline cellularity cases and microorganism detection.

articles.title: Prevalence, associated factors, and functional impact of low back pain among pregnant women attending antenatal care in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Ouédraogo M, Diabri MB, Bayala YLT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low back pain (LBP) is a common musculoskeletal disorder during pregnancy that can affect quality of life. While extensively studied in high-income countries, data from sub-Saharan Africa remain scarce. This study aimed to determine the prevalence, identify associated factors, and assess the impact of LBP among pregnant women in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted from February to May 2024 in 11 primary healthcare centers across five health districts of Ouagadougou. Pregnant women receiving antenatal care were consecutively recruited. Data, including sociodemographic characteristics, obstetric history, and the Pregnancy Mobility Index (PMI), were collected via standardized questionnaires. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with LBP.
RESULTS: Among the 1,159 pregnant women (mean age 26.86 ± 5.91 years), the prevalence of LBP was 21.83%. The mean PMI was 13.31 ± 9.40. Although 45.42% of women reported reduced activity levels, 71.71% considered their LBP to be nonsignificant. Multivariable analysis identified urban residence (aOR: 1.85, 95% CI: 1.20-2.93, p = 0.007), low activity level (aOR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.14-2.15, p = 0.006), and personal history of low back pain (aOR: 14.89, 95% CI: 9.64-23.53, p < 0.001) as associated factors for LBP.
CONCLUSION: Although LBP affects one in five pregnant women in Ouagadougou, it is often considered nonsignificant despite its impact on daily activities. Urban residence, reduced activity level, and personal history of low back pain emerged as key associated factors.

articles.title: Exploring barriers to implementing adolescent pregnancy prevention interventions in low- and middle-income countries: Perspectives from international experts.
articles.authors: Nkurunziza A, Nkurikiyintwali JMV, Ndayisenga JP et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescent pregnancy remains a significant public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Although various interventions have been implemented to address this issue, many have failed to achieve positive outcomes due to numerous barriers.
OBJECTIVE: To explore the barriers to implementing adolescent pregnancy prevention interventions in LMICs.
METHODS: This qualitative exploratory study involved 19 adolescent pregnancy prevention program implementers across 24 LMICs. Data were collected through virtual in-depth individual interviews, organized using Dedoose software, and analyzed thematically.
RESULTS: Findings highlighted seven interrelated challenges shaping programme reach, acceptability, and sustainability. Experts reported that adolescents' engagement depended on perceived usefulness and, at times, material or social benefits of attendance, while stigma made participation social risky and encouraged private information-seeking. Prevention efforts were further constrained by gendered allocation and unequal decision-making power, which limited boys' participation and girls' agency. Separately, poverty, household material insecurity, and transactional marriage practices such as bride price contributed to early unions and subsequent childbearing, while programme legitimacy is challenged by taboo, religious opposition, contraception myths, and the normalization of violence. Finally, implementation was hindered by administrative delays, weak institutional backing, school-level resistance, and unstable or poorly enforced policy environments, limiting continuity and scale-up of interventions.
CONCLUSION: Effective teenage pregnancy prevention in LMICs requires more than delivering sexual and reproductive health (SRH) information; programmes must be designed to feel relevant to adolescents while reducing stigma and protecting confidentiality to support genuine engagement. Interventions also need to address gendered power dynamics and gatekeeper control, alongside community-level legitimacy barriers such as taboo, religious opposition, contraception myths, and normalized violence. Sustainable impact will depend on enabling implementation conditions, including reduced bureaucratic delays, stronger institutional and school support, coherent policies, reliable financing beyond donor cycles, and better data to guide targeted action.

articles.title: Do community pharmacies unnecessarily recommend oral emergency contraception? A nationwide mystery caller investigation in Germany.
articles.authors: Langer B, Beck A, Dreier AM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Since 2015, oral emergency contraceptives (ECs) have been available in German community pharmacies without prescription as over-the-counter medicines. Given the financial burden, unnecessary hormonal exposure and associated side effects, systematic information gathering is crucial to prevent unnecessary recommendations. This study aimed to determine whether pharmacy staff ask the checklist questions recommended by the German Federal Chamber of Pharmacists (BAK) guideline and provide correct recommendations when oral EC is not indicated (appropriate outcome), and to examine associated factors.
METHODS: A nationwide study using the simulated patient methodology - considered the "gold standard" - was conducted with a stratified random sample of 376 community pharmacies across Germany. Eight trained female mystery callers aged 21-24 simulated a scenario in which a combined oral contraceptive was forgotten once after sexual intercourse. However, the pill could still be taken within the 12-hour window, making oral EC unnecessary according to the BAK guideline. To ensure quality, each call was monitored by a second observer.
RESULTS: Of 376 mystery calls conducted, 322 were included in the primary analysis. An appropriate outcome was achieved in 44.4% (143/322), while oral EC was unnecessarily recommended in 49.1% (158/322). The median questioning score was 2.0 of 4.0 points. A multivariable logistic regression model showed that a higher questioning score and mystery caller identity were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome. Qualitative findings indicated both positive counseling practices and notable deficiencies among pharmacy staff.
CONCLUSION: The results show deficits in information gathering and appropriate recommendations. To improve counseling, the consistent use of the BAK checklist during telephone consultations should be explicitly recommended in the relevant guideline. Targeted training for pharmacy staff may help address professional and communication deficits. Surprisingly, some mystery callers were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome, highlighting the need for further research on the influence of vocal characteristics and last names in telephone consultations.

articles.title: Risky sexual behaviors and associated factors among adolescent girls and young women in the context of HIV prevention pre-exposure prophylaxis in Tanzania: Analysis of the Tanzania HIV Impact Survey 2022-2023.
articles.authors: Mwakilasa MT, Kakoko D, Gilmore J et al.
articles.abstract: Risky sexual behavior contributes to HIV acquisition among adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), including Tanzania. However, nationally representative evidence on its prevalence and associated factors remains limited. This study examines the prevalence and associated factors of risky sexual behavior among AGYW aged 15-24 years in Tanzania, in the context of the expanding Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) provision. A secondary analysis of nationally representative data from the 2022-2023 Tanzania HIV Impact Survey (THIS) was conducted among 3,669 sexually active AGYW aged 15-24 who answered PrEP-related questions. Survey-weighted descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression were carried out. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.The survey-weighted prevalence of risky sexual behaviors was 38.29%, higher among those aged 15-17 years than 18-24 years (61.57% versus 35.63%). Not being in a union was associated with increased odds of risky sexual behaviors among participants aged 15-17 years (AOR = 8.72, 95% CI: 4.33-17.55; p < 0.001) and 18-24 years (AOR = 15.13, 95% CI: 11.40-20.08; p < 0.001). Alcohol use was also associated with increased odds in both age groups (15-17 years: AOR = 13.38, 95% CI: 1.53-116.64; p = 0.019; 18-24 years: AOR = 2.47, 95% CI: 1.57-3.89; p < 0.001). Among young women aged 18-24 years, health facility attendance, family planning use and willingness to use PrEP were associated with higher odds, whereas secondary or higher education, parent or guardian communication about sex or HIV, and prior HIV testing were associated with lower odds. Risky sexual behavior remains common among Tanzanian AGYW, particularly those aged 15-17 years. Age-responsive prevention programmes need to integrate behavioral and biomedical interventions, prioritizing AGYW who are not in a union and who use alcohol or have limited access to PrEP.

articles.title: Exploring urogenital microbiome differences in children with and without overactive bladder: first approach.
articles.journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
articles.authors: Moratilla Lapeña L, Mingorance J, Nava B et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Overactive bladder (OAB) affects up to 10% of healthy children, with poorly understood mechanisms. Recent adult data implicate the urogenital microbiome in lower urinary tract symptoms. This pilot study explored the relationship between the urogenital microbiome and OAB in children.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted in children aged 5-11 years with OAB and age matched controls (2020-2023). Midstream voided urine samples were analyzed using standard urine culture and long-read, near full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing with the Nanopore 16S Barcoding kit and MinION system.
RESULTS: Fifteen OAB patients and twelve controls were included, with similar ages (9.19±2.19 vs 8.35±2.92 years; p=0.386). Microbiome analysis was completed in 15 cases and 8 controls after exclusion of PCR negative samples. The most frequently detected bacteria were Campylobacter ureolyticus (32%), Ezakiella massiliensis (22%) and Peptoniphilus harei (20%). Alpha and beta diversity were both low, with no statistically significant differences between groups. Microbiome composition analysis showed a higher relative abundance of Gram-positive genera, including Streptococcus, Staphylococcus and Anaerococcus, in OAB patients compared with controls.
CONCLUSION: This exploratory pilot study suggests qualitative urogenital microbiome differences in children with OAB, particularly a higher relative abundance of Gram-positive genera, despite no significant differences in diversity; larger studies are needed to confirm the clinical relevance of these hypothesis-generating findings.

articles.title: Taxanes versus platinum derivatives for ovarian cancer: a comparative disproportionality analysis using the FDA adverse event reporting system database.
articles.journal: The International journal of pharmacy practice
articles.authors: Jacob M, Roy Edakkarote A, Lingamagunta S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Platinum derivatives and taxanes are first line in the pharmacotherapy of ovarian cancer. However, both classes are associated with a wide array of adverse events (AEs). This study aimed to assess and compare AEs associated with platinum derivatives and taxanes through disproportionality analysis.
METHODS: Data mining of the FAERS (FDA adverse event reporting system) database was conducted via OpenVigil 2.1 from 2003Q4 to 2024Q4. In frequentist methods, AE reports with a frequency of ≤3 were excluded, and duplicates were removed from the raw data. Proportional reporting ratio (PRR), reporting odds ratio (ROR), and chi-squared (χ2) were used for signal detection. Data analysis was performed using R software version 4.4.1. MedDRA version 28.0 was employed to link preferred terms (PTs) to their respective system organ classes (SOCs).
KEY FINDINGS: After excluding irrelevant AEs, the frequency of PTs for platinum derivatives and taxanes was 322/246. The most reported AE in both classes was dyspnea, with 172 reports for taxanes and 272 for platinum derivatives. Reports were mainly from the USA and France, mostly involving patients aged 60-70 years. Disproportionality analysis flagged 150 signals for platinum derivatives and 125 for taxanes, accounting for 46.58% and 50.81% of PTs, respectively. The AEs for platinum derivatives and taxanes targeted 22 and 21 SOCs, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Signals were identified for both drug classes across multiple SOCs. AE reports were higher for platinum derivatives than taxanes, with gastrointestinal and general disorders and administration site conditions most frequently reported. Overall, the findings suggest the usefulness of FAERS data mining in identifying signals.

articles.title: FSH-secreting pituitary adenomas presenting with spontaneous ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome in children and adolescents: two cases, a literature review, and long-term follow-up.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.authors: Mammadova J, Kara C, Çelebi Bitkin E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Functioning FSH-secreting pituitary adenomas (FSHomas) are exceedingly rare in children; only nine pediatric patients, seven girls and two boys, have been reported previously. In girls, they commonly present with spontaneous ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (sOHSS). The clinical presentation, management, and long-term outcomes of these tumors remain incompletely characterized.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report two girls aged 10.1 and 16 years with prolonged menstrual bleeding and bilateral multicystic ovarian enlargement due to FSHoma-associated sOHSS. Both demonstrated markedly elevated estradiol, suppressed LH, and nonsuppressed (inappropriately normal) FSH, with pituitary adenomas of 14 × 11 × 13 mm and 9 × 9 mm on MRI; immunohistochemistry was FSHβ-positive in both. Case 1 underwent transsphenoidal adenectomy after medical treatment with letrozole and cabergoline; despite residual tumor tissue, she remained stable over 10 years of follow-up. Case 2 underwent transsphenoidal resection but developed recurrent hyperestrogenism and ovarian enlargement 5 years later despite radiological stability of the residual adenoma, and subsequently required emergency surgery for ovarian torsion (excision of the left ovary, right ovarian cystectomy). All 11 pediatric patients, including the present two, were compared for presentation, treatment, and long-term outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: These cases provide 10 and 9 years of follow-up after diagnosis. Biochemical recurrence may occur independently of radiological tumor progression, and persistent ovarian stimulation from residual adenoma tissue may cause irreversible complications, including ovarian torsion. Long-term multidisciplinary surveillance with serial hormonal assessment, pelvic imaging, and pituitary MRI is essential, and early pituitary-directed intervention may prevent unnecessary gynecological surgery.

articles.title: Whole-Body Vibration Induces Structural Remodeling of Skeletal Muscle Fibers and Neuromuscular Junctions in Oophorectomized Wistar Female Rats.
articles.journal: Microscopy and microanalysis : the official journal of Microscopy Society of America, Microbeam Analysis Society, Microscopical Society of Canada
articles.authors: Filho DP, Zazula MF, Mattana WDS et al.
articles.abstract: Menopause-associated hypoestrogenism promotes structural and functional alterations in skeletal muscle, contributing to muscle structural adaptation and neuromuscular impairment. Whole-body vibration (WBV) has emerged as a potential non-pharmacological intervention to attenuate these alterations; however, its effects on skeletal muscle fibers and neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) under hypoestrogenic conditions remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of WBV on the extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscle of oophorectomized Wistar rats. Sixty-four female Wistar rats were allocated into four experimental groups: SHAM-SED, SHAM-WBV, OOPHX-SED, and OOPHX-WBV. Sixty days after surgery, animals assigned to WBV groups were subjected to mechanical vibration (60 Hz, 2 mm, 10 min/session, three times weekly) for 8 weeks. Morphological, morphometric, ultrastructural, and NMJ analyses were performed in the EDL muscle. Oophorectomy promoted significant skeletal muscle remodeling, characterized by reduced muscle fiber cross-sectional area, altered fiber-type distribution, reduced NMJ dimensions, and decreased myonuclear parameters. WBV treatment induced additional structural adaptations, including increased NMJ area and altered sarcomere organization. Ultrastructural analysis demonstrated increased Z-line dissolution in WBV-treated animals. Although WBV promoted neuromuscular remodeling, it did not prevent the reduction in muscle fiber size associated with oophorectomy. These findings demonstrate that hypoestrogenism induces significant structural alterations in skeletal muscle and NMJs, while WBV promotes selective neuromuscular and ultrastructural reorganization in oophorectomized animals. The results indicate that WBV induces selective structural and neuromuscular remodeling, although its effects on muscle fiber preservation appear limited under hypoestrogenic conditions.

articles.title: Women's experiences regarding the care received in the hospital setting during the abortion process.
articles.authors: Balestre ME, Lino IGT, Silva MEPD et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: to understand how women recall the care they received in the hospital setting during the abortion process.
METHODS: a descriptive qualitative study grounded in the conceptual framework of the National Humanization Policy. Data were collected between May and September 2024 through audio recorded interviews, conducted either in person or remotely, with 19 women, and analyzed using thematic content analysis.
RESULTS: two categories emerged: Experiencing disrespectful care, which reflects dissatisfaction with communication, insufficient information, devaluation of complaints and emotional suffering, lack of privacy, and hospitalization alongside pregnant women; and Positive care experiences, which include humanized care, emotional support, and active listening.
FINAL CONSIDERATIONS: women generally recall the care received in a negative way, highlighting the need for adopting and implementing good obstetric practices and reinforcing the guidelines of the National Humanization Policy in care provided during the abortion process.

articles.title: Approaches, challenges, and recommendations for clinical practice in gestational syphilis: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Silveira CR, Carlotto FD, Krüger LA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: to map the scientific evidence on the approach to gestational syphilis, the sociodemographic profile of pregnant women, and the challenges related to its management and follow-up.
METHOD: scoping review carried out in October 2024 in the following data sources: Virtual Health Library, Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature, National Library of Medicine, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Original articles in English, Portuguese, and Spanish, covering the period from 2019 to 2024 and addressing gestational syphilis as their main topic, were included. The snowballing technique, recommended by the JBI, was used as a strategy to achieve literature saturation. The studies were organized into three main themes, and content analysis of the data was performed.
RESULTS: 39 studies were included. Late diagnosis of syphilis during prenatal care and the failure to address sexual partners stand out as persistent challenges. Sociodemographic factors such as Black or Brown race/skin color, low educational level, and difficulties in accessing health services contribute to the persistence of these scenarios.
CONCLUSION: the increase in the incidence of gestational syphilis cases and regional and socioeconomic inequities persists. Failures in the screening and management of the disease were identified, requiring actions in prenatal care and equitable policies.

articles.title: Childbirth complications in Brazil: An analysis of socioeconomic, epidemiological, and health care factors.
articles.journal: Revista brasileira de epidemiologia = Brazilian journal of epidemiology
articles.authors: Rocha NM, Almeida WDS, Szwarcwald CL
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the factors associated with the occurrence of childbirth complications in Brazil.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted using data from the 2019 National Health Survey (Pesquisa Nacional de Saúde - PNS). Data from 2,875 women were analyzed. Chi-square tests and logistic regression were used to investigate the association between sociodemographic characteristics, childbirth care indicators, and the occurrence of childbirth complications (outcome).
RESULTS: The prevalence of childbirth complications was 12.3% (95%CI 10.6-14.2). Childbirth complications were more prevalent among women with lower educational attainment (14.4%) and lower income (13.9%), chronic hypertension (37.1%) or hypertension occurring only during pregnancy (29.8%), cesarean delivery (13.9%), and delivery through the Brazilian Unified Health System (Sistema Único de Saúde - SUS) (14.5%), compared with their respective reference groups (p<0.05). The multivariate logistic regression model showed significant associations between the outcome and chronic hypertension (OR=5.49; 95%CI 2.90-10.41), gestational hypertension (OR=4.18; 95%CI 2.47-7.08), absence of blood pressure measurement during prenatal visits (OR=2.16; 95%CI 1.01-4.67), delivery through SUS (OR=1.99; 95%CI 1.06-3.71), cesarean delivery without labor (OR=1.75; 95%CI 1.10-2.80), and medically indicated cesarean delivery (OR=1.90; 95%CI 1.06-3.41). Among women who experienced childbirth complications, the odds of neonatal problems were higher (OR=4.12; 95%CI 2.48-6.85), as were the odds of low birth weight (OR=2.59; 95%CI 1.58-4.23) and preterm birth (OR=2.43; 95%CI 1.60-3.68).
CONCLUSION: Clinical factors and characteristics of childbirth care were associated with the occurrence of childbirth complications in Brazil. Furthermore, women who experienced childbirth complications had higher odds of adverse neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Association of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor A-2549 I/D polymorphism with polycystic ovary syndrome susceptibility in Turkish women.
articles.authors: Aci R, Nacar MC, Yigit S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this case-control study was to evaluate whether the Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor A promoter rs35569394 (-2549 insertion/deletion) polymorphism is associated with polycystic ovary syndrome risk and related clinical-metabolic features.
METHODS: The study included 104 women with polycystic ovary syndrome diagnosed according to Rotterdam criteria and 128 controls. Clinical, hormonal, and metabolic variables were recorded, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance was calculated, and Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor A-2549 insertion/deletion genotypes were determined by direct polymerase chain reaction. Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium was assessed in controls. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate-adjusted p-values were calculated for the 11 clinical comparisons, while prespecified Bonferroni-adjusted p-values were retained for genotype and family-history contrasts.
RESULTS: Body mass index, prolactin, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance, insulin, follicle stimulating hormone, luteinizing harmone, and total testosterone were higher in the polycystic ovary syndrome group. Overall genotype distribution differed between groups (Cramer's V=0.20; chi-square=8.87, p=0.012). The detection/deletion genotype was more frequent in polycystic ovary syndrome patients than controls (30.77% vs. 15.63%; Cohen's h=0.36; raw p=0.007; Bonferroni-adjusted p=0.028; OR 2.40, 95%CI 1.28-4.51). The family-history detection/deletion comparison did not remain significant after adjustment (raw p=0.018; adjusted p=0.072). Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium analysis in controls yielded an exact p-value of 0.050 and a Pearson p-value of 0.037.
CONCLUSION: In this Turkish case-control sample, the Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor A-2549 insertion/deletion detection/deletion genotype was more frequent among women with polycystic ovary syndrome than among controls. This observed association does not establish causality, a functional effect, phenotype-specific relevance, or clinical utility. Deviation from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium in controls, residual confounding from incomplete matching, limited power, and lack of functional validation make the finding preliminary. Independent validation in larger, well-matched cohorts with prespecified genotyping quality control, phenotype stratification, and functional studies is required.

articles.title: Intrapartum rectovaginal distance as a predictor of obstetric anal sphincter injury: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Bademci EG, Erdim YŞ, Özsoy EY et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the relationship between intrapartum rectovaginal distance measured by transperineal ultrasonography and obstetric anal sphincter injury severity and second-stage labor duration in nulliparous women undergoing vaginal delivery.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary referral center in Istanbul, between September 2021 and January 2022. Of 200 consecutive nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies at ≥37 weeks' gestation, 148 who underwent vaginal delivery were included in the primary analysis. Intrapartum rectovaginal distance was measured in the midsagittal plane by 2D transperineal ultrasonography using a single operator during the inter-contraction rest period, at a fetal head station ranging from -1 to +1. Angle of progression and levator ani anteroposterior diameter were also recorded. Obstetric injury was graded per American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists 2016 criteria; grade 3-4 laceration (severe obstetric anal sphincter injury) was the primary outcome.
RESULTS: Severe obstetric anal sphincter injury occurred in 18 vaginal deliveries (12.2%). Rectovaginal distance was significantly shorter in women with severe obstetric anal sphincter injury (6.91±1.33 mm vs. 9.94±2.75 mm, p<0.001). Second-stage duration was longer with severe obstetric anal sphincter injury (125.8±6.5 vs. 91.3±18.0 min, p<0.001). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an rectovaginal distance cut-off of 8.1 mm (AUC=0.846; sensitivity 88.9%, specificity 80.8%). On multivariate logistic regression, rectovaginal distance (OR 0.516, 95%CI 0.373-0.713) and body mass index (OR 1.280, 95%CI 1.078-1.521) were independently associated with severe obstetric anal sphincter injury.
CONCLUSION: Intrapartum rectovaginal distance measurement by transperineal ultrasonography is a noninvasive, readily obtainable parameter that independently predicts severe obstetric anal sphincter injury and may support individualized intrapartum risk stratification. Multicenter validation with larger samples is warranted.

articles.title: Maternal death surveillance and Primary Health Care nurses' performance in a Brazilian capital city.
articles.authors: Pereira NAPG, Durval SF, Souza AS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: to identify the factors related to Primary Health Care nurses' performance in maternal death surveillance.
METHOD: an epidemiological and descriptive-analytical study conducted with 143 nurses from a capital city in the Brazilian Midwest region. The data were collected by means of a structured and self-applied questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive and inferential statistics using the Chi-square test and via a multivariate analysis resorting to binary logistic regression, considering a 5% significance level.
RESULTS: most of the participants had been working in their current job position for less than five years and had not undergone any training in maternal death surveillance; however, they were aware about its objective and about the Municipal Maternal Mortality Committee (and its goals). The participants' time in their current job position was associated with participation in training, with conducting investigation procedures, with knowing about the committee and with taking part in its meetings. Training was associated with knowing about the investigation objective, the committee, its goals and participation in meetings. The nurses that had attended training presented an Odds Ratio of 5.82 (95%CI: 2.46-13.75) as for already having conducted a maternal death investigation process.
CONCLUSION: permanent education is a predictive factor for nurses' performance and should be enhanced by institutional policies.

articles.title: Multi-omics analysis of high-grade serous ovarian cancers reveals heterogeneity and distinct immunological patterns based upon clinico-genomic status.
articles.authors: Qian J, Bassiouni R, Jin Y et al.
articles.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is characterized by remarkable intratumoral heterogeneity and variable tissue architectures, dictating differential therapeutic responses. Although BRCA1/2 mutations correlate with improved responses to DNA-damaging agents, how BRCA genotype shapes the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated whole exome sequencing, total RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to profile a cohort of BRCA-mutated (BRCA-MT) and non-BRCA-mutated (BRCA-WT) HGSOC tumors. While bulk transcriptomics highlighted global phenotypic shifts, suggesting a more pro-inflammatory milieu in BRCA-MT tumors, spatially resolved analysis revealed how these differences manifest within specific tissue architectures. Integrated clustering revealed recurrent spatial transcriptional states across genotypes. Specifically, we identified a transcriptionally distinct immune-enriched region (IC7) characterized by low tumor purity, interferon signaling, and antigen-presentation programs. Reference-based RCTD deconvolution provided orthogonal computational support that IC7 was enriched for T/NK and dendritic cells relative to non-IC7 regions. At the patient level, the functional state of IC7 was highly BRCA-dependent: BRCA-MT tumors exhibited stronger enrichment of interferon-α/γ responses and inflammatory signaling than BRCA-WT tumors. Exploratory CellChat analysis further suggested genotype-associated differences in predicted immune-related signaling. We also identify a conserved structural interface between CAF-like region (IC3) and macrophage-rich region (IC4), accompanied by a predicted CXCL12-CXCR4 chemokine recruitment axis. Taken together, these findings support a model in which BRCA mutation status is associated with functional differences within broadly conserved spatial regions, rather than extensive reorganization of the overall spatial architecture. This spatially resolved framework identifies BRCA-associated immune transcriptional patterns in HGSOC and provides a basis for future mechanistic validation.

articles.title: PREnatal Syphilis point-of-care ScreenING in an urban low-barrier clinic (PRESSING) study: Protocol for a prospective single arm feasibility trial.
articles.authors: Sanya N, Vaccaro ME, Uppal M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Syphilis has resurged across North America, including syphilis in pregnancy. Congenital syphilis can be prevented by timely treatment of syphilis in pregnancy, but conventional syphilis screening is problematic for people facing barriers to care. Syphilis point-of-care tests (POCT) have improved prenatal syphilis management in low- and middle-income countries. There is minimal literature regarding POCT feasibility and effectiveness for prenatal syphilis screening in high-income countries, where barriers and challenges may differ.
METHODS: Academic and community partners co-designed a prospective single-arm feasibility trial to evaluate syphilis POCT implementation at a low-barrier prenatal clinic in Hamilton, Canada. The INSTI HIV/syphilis POCT was integrated into routine clinical care for pregnant people with ≥1 risk factor for syphilis (unstable housing in the past year; substance use or accessing addictions services in the past year; > 1 sexual partner in the past year; history of sexually transmitted or blood-borne infection; presentation to care >20 weeks gestation). Sexual partners of newly diagnosed pregnant people are also offered POCT. Individuals offered POCT are invited to enroll in the study. The primary feasibility outcome is the proportion of pregnant participants who accept POCT at first offer. Secondary feasibility outcomes include valid POCT results on clinician's first attempt and accurate POCT interpretation by clinicians. Secondary clinical outcomes include time to treatment initiation and completion of treatment among syphilis-positive participants. To promote inclusion of groups facing structural barriers to research, individuals declining study participation are enrolled for limited prospective chart review (primary feasibility outcome only). Target enrollment is N = 62 pregnant participants over 18 months. Baseline participant characteristics and outcomes will be descriptively analyzed. Community-based knowledge mobilization is ongoing.
CONCLUSION: This pilot study will generate novel feasibility data regarding prenatal syphilis screening with POCT in high-income countries and inform design of a multicenter implementation trial.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT06829602; February 17, 2025. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06829602.

articles.title: Incidence and predictors of mother-to-child transmission of HIV among HIV-exposed infants in public General hospitals of Tigray, Ethiopia, 2020: Retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Gerezgiher GG, Gebreslassie T, Woldemariam GT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) remains a major public health challenge, particularly in low-income countries. Previous studies conducted in Ethiopia were largely limited to single health facilities and did not adequately assess important predictors, including maternal viral load, paternal enrollment in antiretroviral therapy (ART), and breastfeeding duration. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of MTCT of HIV among HIV-exposed infants in public general hospitals of Tigray, Ethiopia.
METHODS: Hospital-based retrospective cohort study on 485 randomly selected HIV exposed infants attending in public General Hospitals was conducted. All HIV exposed infants attending in public general hospitals of Tigray were the source of population. Data were entered into Epidata version 4.6.1 and exported to SPSS version 23 for analysis. Binary logistic regression model was used and variables at p-value < 0.25 in bivariate analysis were entered into a multivariable logistic regression analysis to examine the predictors of mother-to-child transmission of HIV. Level of significance was declared at p-value <0.05.
RESULT: A total of 444(91.5%) records were included in the analysis. At the end of follow up, 17 (3.8%) (95% CI: 2.3%-5.8%) of the HIV exposed infants became HIV positive. Poor infant adherence (AOR: 5.6; 95% CI: 1.02-30.2), father not enrolled to ART (AOR: 4.4; 95% CI: 1.2-16.7), age of infant at enrolment >6 weeks (AOR: 4.4; 95% CI: 1.2-17.0), mothers enrolled to PMTCT during labor and delivery or after (AOR: 7.9; 95% CI: 1.4-44.7) and mothers on advanced WHO clinical stage at base line(AOR: 4.2; 95% CI: 1.02-17.89) were significantly associated with mother-to-child transmission of HIV.
CONCLUSION: In this study MTCT of HIV is still high. Poor adherence of infant for PMTCT, HIV positive father not enrolled to ART, infant age > 6 weeks at enrollment, mothers enrolled to PMTCT during labor and delivery or after and mothers on advanced WHO clinical stage were predictors of mother to child transmission of HIV.

articles.title: Pregnancy outcomes after amniocentesis in ART-Conceived versus spontaneously conceived twin pregnancies: A single-center retrospective study.
articles.authors: Weng W, Lu Y, Wang C et al.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo compare the pregnancy outcomes following amniocentesis in twin pregnancies conceived with assisted reproduction technology (ART) versus spontaneously conceived twins.MethodsIn this retrospective study, the 40case records of twin pregnancies in which amniocentesis was performed at HuizhouCentral People's Hospital between 2021 and 2024 were reviewed. Pregnancy outcomes and neonatal outcomes of twin pregnancies were compared between the ART group (n = 25)and spontaneous twin pregnancy group(n = 15).ResultsThere was no statistically significant difference in pregnancy loss rate between the groups(4.00% vs. 6.67%, P = 1.000). The pregnancy loss rate before 24 weeks of gestation in the two groups were 4.00% and 6.67%, respectively (P = 1.000). No pregnancy loss occurred within 4 weeks after the amniocentesis in bothgroup. The preterm birthrate before 37weeks of gestation in the two groups were 76.00% and 46.67%, respectively, and showed no significant difference (P =0.089).There were significant differences between-group in birth weight and Apgar score at 10 min (both P< 0.05), while there were no significant differences in low birth weight (<2500 g), Apgar score at 1 min, Apgar score at 5 min, and neonatal/pediatric department transfer (all P> 0.05).ConclusionNo statistically significant increase in the risk of pregnancy loss after amniocentesis was observed among ART-conceived twin pregnancies compared with spontaneously conceived twin pregnancies.However, they should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence or absence of a clinically meaningful difference.Given the limited sample size, these findings should be confirmed in larger, multicenter studies.

articles.title: First-trimester plasma asprosin and its association with gestational diabetes mellitus: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Inthavong S, Jatavan P, Kumfu S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asprosin a glucogenic adipokine associated with insulin resistance, has been found to be elevated in the plasma of women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Emerging evidence indicates that it can serve as a promising biomarker for the diagnosis of GDM during the second trimester. However, its utility in the first trimester has not yet been investigated. Therefore, the present study aimed to establish first-trimester reference ranges for plasma asprosin and to evaluate its predictive performance for the subsequent development of GDM.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, low-risk women with singleton pregnancies at 10-14 weeks of gestation were consecutively enrolled. Participants with pregestational diabetes were excluded. Baseline clinical characteristics were documented, and blood samples were obtained for the measurement of plasma asprosin concentrations. The diagnosis of GDM at 24-28 weeks of gestation was established using the two-step screening approach.
RESULTS: Among the 302 participants, 98 (32.5%) developed GDM. Asprosin concentrations did not differ significantly across gestational ages between 10 and 14 weeks. However, asprosin levels increased significantly with maternal BMI (p < 0.001), demonstrating a quadratic relationship. A first-trimester reference range for plasma asprosin was established. Nevertheless, first-trimester asprosin showed poor predictive performance for subsequent GDM (AUC = 0.516), whereas maternal BMI and age showed modest predictive ability.
CONCLUSION: First, a reference range for first-trimester asprosin was established, which may serve as a valuable benchmark for future investigations examining various aspects of diabetes in pregnancy. Second, first-trimester asprosin concentrations did not discriminate between women who subsequently developed GDM and those who did not.

articles.title: Discovery of a Novel Dual Inhibitor Targeting Tubulin and Histone Deacetylase 8 for Treatment of the Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Cai S, Shi F, Chen J et al.
articles.abstract: In this work, a series of novel dual inhibitors against both tubulin and histone deacetylase (HDAC) were designed and synthesized by integrating the natural product Millepachine with the key pharmacophore of HDAC inhibitors. Among them, compound 6 exhibited potent antiproliferative activity against 12 cancer cell lines, with IC50 values ranging from 0.020 to 0.244 μM. Mechanistic investigations revealed that compound 6 inhibited both tubulin polymerization (IC50 2.0 μM) and HDAC8 (IC50 0.110 μM), with 54-, 27- and 132-fold selectivity over HDAC1, HDAC4 and HDAC6, respectively. In an ovarian cancer xenograft mouse model, compound 6 exhibited significant inhibitory effect on tumor growth with a favorable safety profile. These findings identify compound 6 as a promising tubulin/HDAC8 dual inhibitor for further investigation.

articles.title: Discovery of Diaryl Pyrimidine-Guanidine Derivatives as Jumonji C Domain-Containing Lysine Histone Demethylase (KDM) Inhibitors with In Vivo Anti-Cervical Cancer Activity.
articles.authors: Ni D, Wang T, Yang J et al.
articles.abstract: JMJD family histone demethylases are highly expressed in cervical cancer and promote tumor progression, highlighting their potential as therapeutic targets for this malignancy. Using a scaffold-hopping-based virtual screening, we discovered a series of diaryl pyrimidine-guanidine derivatives as KDM6B inhibitors. The optimized compound 40 exhibited potent KDM6B inhibitory activity comparable to that of GSK-J4, but differs mechanistically by being non-competitive with 2-OG. Although 40 showed pan-KDM inhibition in enzymatic level, it selectively elevated H3K27me3 levels in C33A cells without affecting H3K4me3 or H3K9me3. In C33A cells, 40 suppressed proliferation, induced cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis. In a xenograft mouse model, 40 inhibited tumor growth, downregulated Ki-67, and upregulated cleaved caspase-3, p-H2A.X, and H3K27me3. Collectively, 40 represents a promising chemical probe for investigating JMJD KDMs and H3K27 modifications in cervical cancer and establishes a foundation for developing targeted agents.

articles.title: Design, Synthesis, and Pharmacological Profiling of Serine/Threonine Kinase 33 (STK33) Inhibitors for Nonhormonal Male Contraception.
articles.authors: Ku AF, Ta HM, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Serine/threonine kinase 33 (STK33) is a male germ-specific nonhormonal contraceptive target that is both genetically and chemically validated. Building on our previously reported reversible male contraceptive inhibitor, CDD-2807, we conducted systematic structure-activity relationship (SAR) and structure-property relationship (SPR) studies on the 3-(biphenylethynyl)-1H-indazole scaffold to address key drug development liabilities, most notably poor kinetic solubility. These efforts identified CDD-3094, which exhibits a balanced profile characterized by retained nanomolar cellular potency, >100 μM kinetic solubility, comparable metabolic stability, reduced human ether-à-go-go-related gene (hERG) channel inhibition, and a favorable cellular kinase profile, with 278 of 300 kinases (92.7%) displaying <30% occupancy at 1000 nM. Leveraging X-ray crystallography of the STK33/CDD-3094 complex, we performed structure-based modifications to specifically target the primary off-target liability, CDC-like kinase 4 (CLK4). This work culminated in the discovery of compound 40, which achieved 446-fold biochemical selectivity for STK33 over CLK4. While its cellular potency is attenuated to >1 μM, this analog provides a valuable biochemical tool for investigating STK33 selectivity and highlights the challenges of balancing kinase discrimination with intracellular activity. Collectively, these studies establish a foundation for developing soluble STK33 inhibitors, facilitating further preclinical refinement of nonhormonal male contraceptives.

articles.title: Discovery of 4-Aminoquinazoline Derivatives as Potent PKMYT1 Inhibitors via Hydrogen Bond Donor-To-Acceptor Conversion for CCNE1-Amplified Cancers.
articles.authors: Qi H, Lu R, Zhu Y et al.
articles.abstract: PKMYT1 is a critical regulator of the cell cycle and has emerged as a promising synthetic lethal target for CCNE1-amplified cancers. In this study, we report the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of a novel series of 4-aminoquinazoline-based PKMYT1 inhibitors. A hydrogen bond donor-to-acceptor conversion strategy was successfully employed to reduce the hydrogen bond donor (HBD) count, thereby improving the drug-likeness of this series. Among them, compound 12f exhibited nanomolar inhibitory activity against PKMYT1 and potent antiproliferative activity in the OVCAR-3 ovarian cancer cell line. Furthermore, compound 12f demonstrated synergistic antiproliferative effects when combined with PARP inhibitors. Along with an acceptable oral pharmacokinetic profile, compound 12f demonstrated robust in vivo efficacy in OVCAR-3 xenograft models. Notably, compound 12f was well-tolerated, demonstrating no significant body weight loss or apparent toxicity to major organs. Collectively, these results underscore the therapeutic potential of compound 12f as a promising PKMYT1 inhibitor against CCNE1-amplified cancers.

articles.title: Discovery of INCB127443: A Potent and Orally Available Inhibitor of Cyclin-Dependent Kinase 2.
articles.authors: Mukai K, Smith BR, Ye Q et al.
articles.abstract: CDK2 is a critical regulator of cell-cycle progression and is an attractive therapeutic target for cancers characterized by dysregulated cyclin E1 signaling. Despite this biological rationale, CDK2 has historically been challenging to target due to the difficulty of achieving selectivity over related CDK isoforms, particularly CDK1, where off-target inhibition may limit the therapeutic window. Building on our previously reported (4-pyrazolyl)-2-aminopyrimidine series, we pursued a multiparameter optimization strategy aimed at improving selectivity for CDK2 over CDK1 while balancing pharmacokinetic and physicochemical properties. Computationally guided replacement of the pyrazole with an imidazole led to a (4-imidazolyl)-2-aminopyrimidine series and culminated in the discovery of INCB127443 (30), a potent and orally bioavailable CDK2 inhibitor. INCB127443 combined favorable selectivity over CDK1 with a relatively flat pharmacokinetic profile, supporting sustained projected CDK2 coverage while limiting potential CDK1 engagement. In vivo, INCB127443 demonstrated dose-dependent inhibition of Rb phosphorylation and antitumor efficacy in CCNE1-high ovarian cancer xenograft models.

articles.title: Weight Gain During Pregnancy and Severe Maternal Morbidity.
articles.authors: Khademioore S, Darling EK, D'Souza R et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Severe maternal morbidity (SMM) carries serious consequences for pregnant individuals, yet the association between gestational weight gain (GWG) and SMM remains poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between GWG and SMM across prepregnancy body mass index (BMI) categories.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study used linked birth registry data from Better Outcomes Registry & Network Ontario and hospitalization data from the Canadian Institute for Health Information for singleton pregnancies with a hospital delivery at a gestational age of 20 weeks or greater in Ontario, Canada, from April 1, 2012, to March 31, 2022. Data were analyzed from May 1 to November 1, 2025.
EXPOSURES: Continuous GWG as mean weekly gain in the second and third trimesters and categorical GWG (inadequate, adequate, or excessive) according to the 2009 Institute of Medicine recommendations based on prepregnancy BMI.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: SMM, defined as a composite of 13 indicators per the Canadian Perinatal Surveillance System, occurring during delivery hospitalization.
RESULTS: Among 1 035 927 pregnancies, 192 731 (18.6%) had inadequate, 296 448 (28.6%) had adequate, and 546 748 (52.8%) had excessive GWG; 15 119 (14.59 per 1000 births) experienced SMM. Compared with adequate GWG, excessive GWG was associated with increased SMM across all BMI categories: underweight (adjusted rate ratio [ARR], 1.33 [95% CI, 1.15-1.53]), normal weight (ARR, 1.24 [95% CI, 1.17-1.31]), overweight (ARR, 1.16 [95% CI, 1.06-1.27]), obesity class I (ARR, 1.21 [95% CI, 1.08-1.35]), obesity class II (ARR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.07-1.54]), and obesity class III (ARR, 1.24 [95% CI, 1.03-1.48]). Inadequate GWG was associated with increased SMM predominantly among individuals with normal weight (ARR, 1.13 [95% CI, 1.06-1.21]) and overweight (ARR, 1.19 [95% CI, 1.05-1.35]). GWG showed nonlinear associations with SMM across all BMI categories, with risk elevated at both low and high GWG in individuals with underweight, normal weight, and overweight, while in those with obesity classes I to III, risk was concentrated at high GWG values. Estimated SMM rates were lowest at 0.4 kg/wk GWG for underweight through overweight BMI categories and declined across obesity classes to 0.1 kg/wk GWG for the obesity class III category.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of 1 035 927 pregnancies, GWG outside Institute of Medicine-recommended ranges was associated…

articles.title: Telehealth vs In-Clinic Medication Abortion Provision.
articles.authors: Fiastro AE, Thayer EK, Fredman SN et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In states that restrict abortion provision, residents rely on telehealth medication abortion (teleMAB) or travel out of state for in-clinic care; however, little is known about how patients using these modalities differ.
OBJECTIVE: To compare characteristics of Kansas and Texas residents receiving teleMAB vs in-clinic medication abortion and to assess geographic and socioeconomic factors associated with modality of care.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cross-sectional analysis used electronic medical record data for patients residing in Kansas or Texas who received medication abortion care from a teleMAB service or from an abortion facility in Kansas from February 1 to June 30, 2024. Patients younger than 18 years were excluded because only the telehealth site served this age group.
EXPOSURE: Patient sociodemographic characteristics (age, race and ethnicity, and number of children), gestational age, and county-level distance to the nearest abortion facility, social vulnerability, and rural-urban designation.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcome was receipt of teleMAB vs in-clinic care. Differences between patients who received teleMAB vs in-clinic care were assessed using χ2 and t tests for bivariate variables and multivariable logistic regression for adjusted comparisons.
RESULTS: The teleMAB service served 12 823 patients (Texas: n = 12 552; Kansas: n = 271); the clinic served 725 patients (Texas: n = 587; Kansas: n = 138). Mean (SD) age was 26 (6) years for Kansas residents and 27 (6) years for Texas residents. In both states, more telehealth patients self-identified as Hispanic, Latino, Latina, or Latine (Texas: 3739 of 12 552 [32%]; Kansas: 48 of 271 [18%]) than in-clinic patients (Texas: 14 of 587 [3%]; Kansas: 8 of 138 [7%]) (P < .001). This difference remained among Texas residents after adjustment. In both states, compared with in-clinic patients, telehealth patients were more likely to be at less than 6 weeks' gestation (Texas: 7648 of 12 552 [61%] vs 155 of 587 [27%]; Kansas: 159 of 271 [59%] vs 45 of 138 [33%]; P < .001) and to have no children (Texas: 5545 of 12 552 [44%] vs 42 of 587 [7%]; Kansas: 137 of 271 [51%] vs 5 of 138 [4%]; P < .001). In Texas, patients who lived farthest from in-clinic care were more likely to receive telehealth than those who lived shorter distances (average marginal effect, 0.003; 95% CI, 0.002-0.004).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional study of patients…

articles.title: Placental mitochondrial impairment in preeclampsia patients.
articles.authors: Vaka R, Hinton E, Edwards K et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy-specific hypertensive disorder characterized by new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation, accompanied by end-organ dysfunction with or without proteinuria. Affecting approximately 5-7% of pregnancies worldwide, it remains a leading cause of maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality. Despite decades of research, the underlying pathophysiology of preeclampsia remains incompletely understood. However, increasing evidence implicates placental mitochondrial oxidative stress in its pathogenesis. In this review, we summarize the current literature pertaining to ultrastructural evidence of mitochondrial damage, defects in oxidative phosphorylation and electron transport chain activity, and alterations in reactive oxygen species production, antioxidant defense, and mitochondrial biogenesis. Finally, we discuss translational considerations and highlight how therapeutic strategies targeted at restoring mitochondrial function may represent a promising approach for managing preeclampsia.

articles.title: Modulation of the NAMPT/SIRT axis in HeLa cells exposed to adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell-conditioned medium.
articles.authors: Roozbehani M, Vafaei S, Keyvani H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer cell survival depends on coordinated metabolic and stress response pathways. Adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem/stormal cells (AD-MSCs) release soluble factors and extracellular vesicle cargo that can alter tumor cell behavior, but their effects on the NAMPT/sirtuin axis in cervical cancer cells are not well defined. We therefore examined how AD-MSC-conditioned medium (CM) affects HeLa cell viability, apoptosis, and expression of NAMPT, SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT7.
METHODS: Previously isolated, characterized, and cryopreserved human AD-MSCs were thawed, expanded, and used to prepare CM. HeLa cells were exposed to 10%-100% CM for 48 h, and viability was measured by MTT assay. The 20% and 60% CM conditions were then evaluated by Annexin V/PI flow cytometry and qRT-PCR. NAMPT, SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT7 transcripts were quantified relative to GAPDH.
RESULTS: CM exposure reduced HeLa cell viability, with an estimated IC50 at 38.99%. The 20% condition increased the apoptotic cell fraction, whereas the response to 60% CM was not significant. At 20% CM, SIRT2 (p = 0.0036) expression decreased, SIRT7 expression increased (p = 0.0036), SIRT1 (p = 0.6286) and NAMPT(p = 0.3277) expression did not differ significantly from the comparison groups.
CONCLUSION: Under the conditions tested, AD-MSC-CM reduced HeLa cell viability and promoted apoptosis most clearly at 20% CM. The accompanying decrease in SIRT2 and increase in SIRT7 point to a paracrine response involving metabolic and sirtuin related signaling. Identification of the active CM components and confirmation at the protein, enzyme-activity, and pathway levels are required before a causal mechanism can be assigned.

articles.title: Decision-relevant patient information in YouTube videos on robotic surgery for endometriosis: a cross-sectional content analysis.
articles.authors: Karakas S, Serhanoglu Z, Çakıroğlu B
articles.abstract: To evaluate decision-relevant content completeness, patient-oriented communication, and source transparency of YouTube videos on robotic surgery for endometriosis. Cross-sectional content analysis. Publicly accessible YouTube content identified through six English- and Turkish-language search strings in September 2026; the retained records document search dates for only a subset. Seventy-six fully accessible videos explicitly addressing robotic surgery for endometriosis, selected from 101 unique records after exclusion of inaccessible videos and records without confirmed eligibility. No clinical intervention. Two reviewers independently coded eligible videos using the study checklist and resolved differences by consensus; reviewer-specific ratings were not retained. In a post hoc strict recoding of the indication/patient-selection domain from retained video/page notes, 18 videos (23.7%) qualified; a broad surgery/candidacy reference was present in 73 (96.1%). The recalculated median DRCCI was 1 of 9 (IQR, 0-2); under a sensitivity rule counting any broad reference, the median was 2 (IQR, 1-3). Deep endometriosis and organ involvement were discussed in 29 (38.2%) and 25 (32.9%) videos; non-surgical options, comparison with laparoscopy, risks, fertility/ovarian reserve, recurrence, and multidisciplinary care were present in 5 (6.6%), 6 (7.9%), 7 (9.2%), 14 (18.4%), 2 (2.6%), and 5 (6.6%), respectively. Selected decision-relevant topics were infrequently present in this exploratory sample of public videos. Because intended audience and purpose were not classified, these findings do not establish that all videos were intended for patient counseling or that omissions affected viewers.

articles.title: Translational applications and clinical utility of organoids in ovarian cancer: a systematic review.
articles.authors: ALzahrani R, Alghadmi MA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecological malignancy, largely due to late-stage diagnosis and the rapid emergence of platinum resistance. Traditional treatment selection relies on population-level guidelines that often fail to account for individual tumor heterogeneity. Patient-derived organoids have emerged as potential functional avatars for personalized therapy, providing a real-time read-out of tumor sensitivity.
METHODS: This systematic review synthesized data from 13 studies evaluating the feasibility, histological fidelity, and clinical concordance of ovarian cancer patient-derived organoids. Studies were assessed for quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and QUADAS-2.
RESULTS: A pooled analysis identified a mean success rate of 71% for obtaining patient-derived tumor organoids in early passages, with short-term assays showing high feasibility for immediate therapy guidance. Because the majority of the included studies relied on short-term cultures, these figures represent early-passage obtention rather than the true "establishment" of stable, cryopreservable lines that can be propagated beyond five passages. Indeed, a direct comparison of establishment rates for such long-term lines was precluded by the inconsistent reporting of total sample sizes (denominators) across the included publications-an important reporting gap that should be addressed in future studies. While 92.3% of studies reported high concordance between PDTO drug sensitivity and patient outcomes for platinum and PARP inhibitors, critical discordance in specific models suggests that growth robustness does not always guarantee predictive accuracy.
CONCLUSION: PDOs represent a robust platform for functional drug screening within a clinically actionable 21-day window. To move into routine practice, the field requires standardized proficiency testing, harmonized reporting of establishment denominators, and the integration of complex stroma-containing models to better reflect the tumor microenvironment.

articles.title: "I Feel Like I Am a Winner:" High Levels of Autonomous Decision-Making Among Women Receiving HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) Choice Counselling in Sub-Saharan Africa.
articles.authors: Segawa I, Sisel H, Kyampire C et al.
articles.abstract: As pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) options expand, providers play a critical role in supporting clients to select the method that best meets their needs. We examined how client-provider interactions during PrEP choice counselling influenced women's autonomous decision-making and early continuation on PrEP. CATALYST was a mixed-methods study that delivered an informed choice of oral PrEP, the dapivirine vaginal ring, and injectable cabotegravir among women attending 28 public-sector facilities in Kenya, Lesotho, South Africa, Uganda, and Zimbabwe. We analysed cohort data collected between June 2024 and January 2025 and adapted a family planning Autonomous Decision-Making (ADM) scale into a six-item PrEP-specific measure (PrEP-ADM scale). Factor analysis assessed scale structure, and logistic regression identified factors associated with fully autonomous decision-making (PrEP-ADM score of 18/18) and refilling PrEP within three months. Twenty-six in-depth interviews explored counselling experiences. Among 2,488 women, 92% reported fully autonomous decision-making.
