Two subscales were identified: "communicating information" and "supporting informed choice". Women in sero-different partnerships had higher odds of reporting fully autonomous decision-making (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 1.63, 95% CI: 1.11-2.39), whereas pregnant (aOR: 0.29, 95% CI: 0.17-0.47) and breastfeeding women (aOR: 0.46, 95% CI: 0.28-0.76) had lower odds. Autonomous decision-making was not associated with PrEP refill. Qualitative findings confirmed clear information exchange and supportive counselling, although pregnant and breastfeeding women described more constrained choices. High levels of perceived autonomous decision-making were observed, though further work is needed to refine these measures and identify the essential elements of informed PrEP choice counselling.

articles.title: Patient-reported outcome sub-analysis of a phase 2 trial of bladder preservation therapy with atezolizumab and radiation therapy (BPT-ART) for invasive bladder cancer.
articles.authors: Mathis BJ, Nagumo Y, Kimura T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Impacts on quality of life (QoL) from bladder preservation therapy with atezolizumab and radiation therapy (BPT-ART), as assessed by patient reported outcomes (PROs), remains unanalyzed. We delineated temporal effects of BPT-ART on urinary QoL across multiple domains using established PRO tools.
METHODS: This was a planned sub-analysis for the Phase 2 BPT-ART trial. PRO instruments included the EuroQol 5-item 5-point questionnaire (EQ-5D-5L), OABSS (Overactive Bladder Symptom Score) and IPSS (International Prostate Symptom Score). Forty-four total participants from 9 Japanese hospitals were surveyed from January 2019 to June 2024. Changes from baseline for each PRO tool were summarized over time as mean changes with 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: EQ-5D-5L utility showed a transient decline during treatment, followed by recovery during follow-up. At the dimension level, pain/discomfort showed the largest transient decrease during radiotherapy (mean change - 0.60, 95% CI -0.90 to -0.31), followed by recovery after treatment. Total OABSS showed a modest increase during radiotherapy and recovered after treatment. Among OABSS components, urgency showed the largest increase (+ 0.95, 95% CI 0.44 to 1.46), followed by urgency incontinence (+ 0.53, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.96) and nighttime frequency (+ 0.33, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.62), while daytime frequency remained stable (+ 0.05, 95% CI -0.17 to 0.26). Baseline symptom burden was associated with absolute scores, but trajectories appeared comparable, and global health status remained stable across subgroups.
CONCLUSION: PROs outlined a temporal pattern of QoL decline but progressive recovery, as measured across patient-reported functional domains. These results support BPT-ART as effective for maintaining patient QoL.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy of Medical Therapies for Heavy Menstrual Bleeding in Adolescents and Young Adults With Bleeding Disorders.
articles.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
articles.authors: Huang H, Isaacson E, Weyand AC et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adolescent and young adult (AYA) females with bleeding disorders (BDs) frequently experience heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB), posing substantial clinical challenges. Data comparing the efficacy of specific hormonal treatment options in this population remain limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective review of AYA females (≤21 years) with BD and HMB referred to a multidisciplinary Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology-Pediatric Hematology joint clinic between November 2016 and December 2023. Treatment efficacy was defined as achieving a patient-reported significant reduction in or cessation of menstrual bleeding. The primary objective was to compare the efficacy of different hormonal and hemostatic therapies.
RESULTS: Among 121 AYA females with BD, von Willebrand disease was the most common diagnosis (67.0%). HMB developed within 1 year of menarche in 79.3% of cases, and 73.6% received their BD diagnosis only after HMB onset. Combined estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) were the most common initial therapy (62.8%), yet 58.7% required switching to alternative regimens. Oral progestins demonstrated the highest efficacy (89.8%), followed by levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (81.5%) and OCPs (65.5%). Only 17.4% achieved complete amenorrhea, though most experienced clinically meaningful bleeding reduction. Treatment efficacy differed significantly across modalities (p < .001).
DISCUSSION: Progestin-based therapies, particularly norethindrone and norethindrone acetate, offer superior bleeding control and should be considered first-line treatment in AYA with BD. Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system and OCPs are also effective alternatives. Given the difficulty of achieving complete amenorrhea, clinical goals should prioritize meaningful bleeding reduction that supports quality of life. Early multidisciplinary referral is recommended to optimize individualized care.

articles.title: Bromocriptine for Myocardial Recovery in Peripartum Cardiomyopathy: Design and Rationale of the REBIRTH Trial.
articles.authors: Wang T, Ibarra AJ, Simpson D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is evidence suggesting that bromocriptine potentially improves outcomes among women with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM); however, there is currently no randomized controlled trial comparing bromocriptine vs placebo on top of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in a diverse, multiethnic cohort in North America.
OBJECTIVES: The REBIRTH trial will enroll 200 women with PPCM to evaluate whether the addition of oral bromocriptine to GDMT is superior to placebo for improving myocardial function and event-free survival. In addition to the randomized trial, REBIRTH will enroll 50 women with PPCM excluded from randomization because of breastfeeding into an observational cohort.
METHODS: The principal inclusion criteria are ≥18 years of age, within 5-months postpartum, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤40%. The primary endpoint is LVEF at 6 months postrandomization. Secondary endpoints include LVEF at 12 months, survival free from major events (ie, death, heart transplantation, or implantation of a durable left ventricular assist device), and survival free from heart failure hospitalization for up to 3 years.
RESULTS: The study is currently enrolling women in both the randomized trial and observational breastfeeding cohort. Primary results are expected to be reported in 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: REBIRTH will determine whether the addition of bromocriptine to GDMT for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction improves postpartum myocardial recovery and clinical outcomes in a diverse cohort of women with PPCM. (Randomized Evaluation of Bromocriptine in Myocardial Recovery Therapy for PPCM [REBIRTH]; NCT05180773).

articles.title: Clinical Performance and User-Informed Refinement of an Indigenous HPV Self-Collection Device for Cervical Cancer Screening in Resource-Constrained Settings.
articles.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
articles.authors: Singhal S, Tanwar P, Jayraj AS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: HPV self-sampling has improved screening participation but remains constrained by cost and lack of optimised collection devices in resource-constrained settings. This study reports the iterative development of an indigenous self-collection device across successive prototypes.
METHODS: In this prospective study, women ≥ 30 years were recruited from community and higher-risk clinical cohorts including women living with HIV and colposcopy referrals. Each participant used one of three CERVICHECK™ prototypes (P1-P3) for vaginal self-sampling, followed by physician-collected cervical sampling. Self-collected samples were tested using an indigenous PCR-based HPV assay and physician-collected samples using Cobas 6800. Clinical performance was assessed against histologically confirmed CIN2+ as the primary endpoint.
RESULTS: Of 756 enrolled women, 743 paired samples were evaluable; invalidity rate was 1.7%. Iterative device refinement was associated with stepwise improvements in analytical agreement with reference standard (Cohen's κ: P1:0.49; P2:0.47; P3:0.67). Clinical sensitivity for CIN2+ detection using self-collected samples increased from 40.0% (95%CI 5.3-85.3) with P1 to 75.0% (95%CI 34.9-96.8) with P2 and 93.6% (95%CI 78.6-99.2) with P3. For P3, clinical sensitivity and specificity of self-collected samples was 93.6% (95%CI 78.6-99.2) for CIN2+ and 67.4% (95%CI 58.6-75.4) for ≤CIN1 lesions, yielding a relative clinical sensitivity of 1.0. Reported concerns declined across successive prototypes (P1:47.6%, P2:25.5%, P3:13.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: Iterative, user-informed refinement of indigenous HPV self-collection device achieved clinically meaningful performance comparable to standard sampling for CIN2+ detection.
IMPACT: Optimised affordable indigenous self-collection solutions may offer scalable and equitable options for implementing HPV-based cervical cancer screening in resource-constrained settings.

articles.title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes in women with inflammatory bowel disease following different biologic utilization trajectories in pregnancy.
articles.authors: Van den Broeck E, De Dycker E, Annaert Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The 2025 Global Consensus recommends continuing biologics throughout pregnancy in women with inflammatory bowel disease. Real-world evidence on biologic treatment patterns and outcomes remains limited. This study compared maternal and neonatal outcomes across different biologic use trajectories during pregnancy.
METHODS: This retrospective study included pregnant women with inflammatory bowel disease treated or delivering at University Hospitals Leuven, Belgium, between 2017 and 2025. Patients were categorized as biologic continuers, discontinuers, non-users, or initiators during pregnancy.
RESULTS: Among 211 pregnancies, 75 (35.5%) were continuers, 66 (31.3%) discontinuers, 63 (29.9%) non-users, and seven (3.3%) initiators. Before conception, 66.8% (N = 211) used biologics. Third-trimester disease activity occurred in 42.9% of initiators (3/7), 19.7% of discontinuers (13/66), 18.7% of continuers (14/75), and 17.5% of non-users (11/63). C-sections occurred more in non-users (41.3%, 26/63) and discontinuers (39.4%, 26/66), than in continuers (31.1%, 23/74). Preterm birth was more common among initiators (14.3%, 1/7) and discontinuers (12.1%, 8/66) than continuers (8.0%, 6/75) and non-users (3.2%, 2/62). Low birthweight occurred most in initiators (14.3%, 1/7), continuers (8.1%, 6/74), and discontinuers (6.1%, 4/66). Small-for-gestational-age was numerically more frequent among continuers (14.9%, 11/74) and initiators (14.3%, 1/7), than discontinuers (7.6%, 5/66) and non-users (6.5%, 4/62) (P = 0.21).
CONCLUSIONS: Discontinuers had numerically more C-sections, preterm births, and third-trimester disease activity than continuers. The numerically higher small-for-gestational-age rate among continuers warrants further investigation. Initiators showed the poorest outcomes, highlighting the need for adequate disease control before and during pregnancy. Larger, confounder-adjusted studies are needed to clarify the relationship between biologic use, disease activity, and outcomes.

articles.title: Deep brain stimulation of the nucleus basalis magnocellularis ameliorates autistic behavior in a rat model of autism via cholinergic modulation in the prefrontal cortex.
articles.authors: Rusadze KZ, Burjanadze MA, Beselia GV et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In the present study, we investigated whether deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the nucleus basalis magnocellularis (NBM) improves autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related behavioral abnormalities in a valproic acid (VPA)-induced rat model of autism, consistent with changes in cholinergic markers in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC).
METHODS: On the 12.5th day of gestation, pregnant rats ( n  = 16) received a single intraperitoneal injection of 500 mg/kg sodium valproate dissolved in 0.9% saline, while others ( n  = 5) received saline alone. Male offspring were allowed to reach 3 months of age and then were randomly assigned to one of four experimental groups: Contr - prenatally saline injected, VPA - prenatally VPA-injected, VPA/I - VPA-injected with electrode implantation in the NBM, and VPA/S - VPA-injected with electrical stimulation. DBS was initiated in rats of the VPA/S group 10 days after surgery (two consecutive hours per day, every day for 2 weeks; DBS parameters: 60 Hz, 120 µs, and 50 µA).
RESULTS: The prenatally VPA-exposed rats demonstrate deficits in social behavior, increased locomotor activity, and reduced anxiety levels. Immunohistochemical evaluation shows a decrease in the number of acetylcholinesterase-immunoreactive neurons in the mPFC and choline acetyltransferase-immunoreactive neurons in the NBM. NBM-DBS improves VPA-induced autistic behavior and increases the number of acetylcholinesterase-immunoreactive neurons in the PFC.
CONCLUSION: The correlation between ASD-like behavior and cholinergic markers in the mPFC supports our hypothesis that NBM-DBS improves behavioral deficits by modulating cholinergic neurotransmission in the PFC in a rat model of autism.

articles.title: Triglyceride-glucose index and preeclampsia risk: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Liu W, Yuan Z, Lv Q et al.
articles.abstract: Insulin resistance plays a role in preeclampsia (PE), yet the clinical utility of the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between the TyG index and PE, as well as its diagnostic accuracy. We searched eight databases for observational studies published from inception to December 31, 2025. Data were synthesized using random-effects models, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses addressing heterogeneity. Our analysis included 12 studies involving 103,702 pregnant women. A higher TyG index was linked to increased odds of PE, with a pooled odds ratio of 1.85 (95% CI: 1.48-2.32). Significant heterogeneity was observed across studies (I² = 71.2%). In five studies, the pooled sensitivity was 0.65 (95% CI: 0.49-0.78), specificity was 0.58 (95% CI: 0.50-0.65), and the area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.64 (95% CI: 0.59-0.68), suggesting limited discriminatory power. Limitations included substantial heterogeneity, a predominance of Chinese populations, and TyG measurements taken near or after PE onset in some studies. While the TyG index is an exploratory metabolic marker associated with PE, these findings do not confirm its prospective predictive value or support its use as a standalone screening tool. Its incremental contribution to multivariable prediction models requires prospective validation in diverse populations, using standardized measurement timing and predefined thresholds.

articles.title: A Global Survey of Skin Concerns and Treatment Interests in Perimenopausal and Menopausal Patients.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.authors: Fabi SG, Nikolis A, Haddad A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore factors affecting women undergoing menopause transition, focusing on lifestyle, facial-skin changes, and current aesthetic treatment interests for this.
METHODS: Quantitative research (online questionnaire) was undertaken by women aged 45 to 60 years from 9 countries to understand their menopause experiences, determine their level of knowledge and perceptions of menopause, and to gain further insights into their current skin care, as well as understand menopause-related skin changes and skin concerns.
RESULTS: Across 4,303 respondents, perimenopause and menopause affected facial wrinkles/fine lines (59%), loss of firmness/elasticity (58%), increased dryness (56%), and duller skin tone (40%), which negatively impacted perceived attractiveness (60% agreed/strongly agreed), creating anxiety or low mood (57% agreed/strongly agreed) and impacting self-confidence (55%). The most common treatments to reduce effects of perimenopause and menopause were food supplements (51%), everyday skincare (47%), and dietary changes (46%). Only 15% of the women used specialist aesthetic treatments for menopause, but 88% of them were satisfied/very satisfied with these treatments reducing the effects of menopause. The main triggers that encouraged the respondents to seek aesthetic treatments were health care professionals' (HCPs) recommendation (46%), cost-related affordability (40%), and information/education (40%).
CONCLUSION: This international survey demonstrated that changes to facial skin during perimenopause and menopause negatively affect perceived facial attractiveness, creating anxiety and reducing self-confidence. Specialist aesthetic treatments might play a key role in reducing the effects of menopause on the skin, with health care professionals aiding understanding.

articles.title: Breast Microbiome Dysbiosis in Plasma Cell Mastitis: A Ribosomal RNA Gene Sequencing Study.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Ren X, Zhu S et al.
articles.abstract: Plasma cell mastitis (PCM) is a chronic breast condition with limited effective treatment options. Surgical intervention is a standard treatment approach but may be associated with postoperative complications. Recent studies suggest that alterations in the microbiome may be associated with the onset, progression, and recurrence of PCM. In this study, high-throughput 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing was used to compare the breast tissue microbiota of patients with PCM with that of the non-PCM control (NC) group. A total of 86 participants were enrolled. No significant differences were observed between the groups in age, body mass index (BMI), or lymphocyte count, whereas white blood cell (WBC) count, neutrophil count, prolactin level, and the prevalence of nipple inversion differed significantly between the groups. A total of 214 bacterial genera showed nominally significant differences in relative abundance between the two groups based on unadjusted P values. Staphylococcus and Bacteroides were more abundant in the PCM group, whereas Plesiomonas and Acinetobacter were more abundant in the NC group. These results indicate that the breast tissue microbiota differed between the PCM and NC groups. The findings demonstrate alterations in the breast microbiome associated with PCM and provide a basis for further investigation of their potential relevance to PCM and future treatment strategies.

articles.title: Exploring Vitamin D Metabolism in Gynaecological Malignancies: Redox-Dependent and Redox-Independent Anticancer Mechanisms From Preclinical Models to Clinical Evidence.
articles.authors: Chan HCC, Bhoora S, Zhou E et al.
articles.abstract: Gynaecological malignancies account for over 1.4 million new diagnoses, with outcomes constrained by late-stage presentation and chemoresistance. Dysregulated redox homeostasis is a hallmark of tumourigenesis. Tumour cells maintain elevated basal reactive oxygen species (ROS), which support proliferative signalling but may also increase susceptibility to further oxidative stress. Vitamin D, acting through the vitamin D receptor (VDR), has antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic effects across cancer models, but its ability to amplify ROS beyond an apoptotic threshold in gynaecological malignancies remains unresolved. We conducted a narrative literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov and the Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results databases, using terms related to vitamin D and its metabolites, ROS/oxidative stress, apoptosis and gynaecological malignancies. Preclinical evidence indicates that calcitriol and related compounds can induce ROS-mediated mitochondrial apoptosis, modulate autophagy and arrest the cell cycle. In ovarian cancer, non-HGSOC cell data suggest that mutant TP53 may alter calcitriol responses, requiring validation in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma models. In cervical cancer, calcitriol radiosensitises human papillomavirus-positive cell lines through autophagy suppression, whilst an in vivo calcitriol-cisplatin study reported improved survival. In endometrial cancer, thioredoxin-interacting protein induction is a candidate mechanism for selective ROS-mediated apoptosis, although this remains context-dependent. Clinical evidence is heterogeneous: higher 25-hydroxyvitamin D status has shown modest inverse associations with ovarian cancer mortality; small trials report regression or reduced recurrence of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia; no randomised controlled trial evidence supports efficacy in invasive cervical cancer; and associations with endometrial cancer incidence are largely null. Current evidence does not support vitamin D supplementation as an oncology-specific intervention. Future research should prioritise biomarker-stratified trials incorporating VDR genotype, CYP24A1 profiling, pre-specified 25(OH)D targets and pharmacokinetically informed dosing.

articles.title: Unintended Pregnancies and Breastfeeding Studies during Central Nervous System Drug Development: How Are they Handled, Is There Room for Improvement?: Maintaining the Gap: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding in CNS Clinical Trials.
articles.authors: Schoenmakers S, Bakker C, Ganev A et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnant and breastfeeding individuals are routinely excluded from clinical drug development, creating persistent evidence gaps in pharmacology, safety, and dosing. Despite mandatory contraception and pregnancy testing, unintended pregnancies occur, particularly during the development of central nervous system (CNS) medicines used by women of reproductive age. Once exposure to an investigational medicinal product (IMP) has occurred, these pregnancies may provide valuable prospective human data; however, treatment or trial participation is often discontinued and follow-up may be incomplete. This study assessed how unintended pregnancies and breastfeeding data were reported, managed, and evaluated in clinical trials supporting marketing authorization applications (MAAs) for CNS products. We reviewed 35 MAAs for centrally authorized CNS products submitted to the European Medicines Agency between 2012 and 2022. Pregnancy frequency, IMP exposure, pregnancy outcomes, breastfeeding data and regulatory comments were extracted from MAA dossiers, Day 120 Lists of Questions and Summaries of Product Characteristics. Overall, 451 pregnancies were identified, including 343 with IMP exposure. Of these, 108 occurred in pivotal phase 3 trials, resulting in 39 live births, 23 elective terminations, 17 spontaneous pregnancy losses, and 29 unknown or ongoing outcomes. Regulators raised 19 pregnancy-related and six breastfeeding-related concerns. Only one dossier included a dedicated human lactation study. Pregnancy reporting varied substantially in location, format and case-level detail, while 27% of pivotal IMP-exposed pregnancies had unknown or ongoing outcomes at assessment. More structured reporting and follow-up, including relevant exposure and pharmacokinetic data where feasible, could strengthen clinical pharmacology and regulatory evidence and support more informative product information.

articles.title: RETRACTED: Abou-ElNaga et al. Novel Nano-Therapeutic Approach Actively Targets Human Ovarian Cancer Stem Cells After Xenograft into Nude Mice. Int. J. Mol. Sci. 2017, 18, 813.
articles.authors: Abou-ElNaga A, Mutawa G, El-Sherbiny IM et al.
articles.abstract: The journal retracts the article titled "Novel Nano-Therapeutic Approach Actively Targets Human Ovarian Cancer Stem Cells after Xenograft into Nude Mice" [...].

articles.title: Immunologic and placental responses to the VSV-EBOV vaccine in a pregnant mouse model.
articles.authors: Lewkowicz AP, Wang Y, Mendoza MI et al.
articles.abstract: Ebola virus disease is a severe viral hemorrhagic illness with high maternal and perinatal mortality. Although the replication-competent vesicular stomatitis virus-based Ebola vaccine (VSV-EBOV) has been deployed successfully in outbreak settings, pregnant women were excluded from clinical trials, leaving critical safety gaps. To address this, we developed a murine model to assess pregnancy outcomes following VSV-EBOV exposure at different gestational stages. Pregnant C57BL/6 mice vaccinated at embryonic day 7 (E7), E10, or E15 mounted robust anti-Ebola virus (anti-EBOV) antibody responses comparable to those of non-pregnant controls and efficiently cleared the vaccine virus without evidence of vertical transmission. However, peri-implantation vaccination modestly increased fetal resorption and early postnatal mortality, accompanied by placental pathology characterized by vascular remodeling defects and inflammation. Later gestational vaccination had minimal impact on survival or offspring development. Mechanistic studies revealed that these adverse effects were mediated by type I interferon signaling rather than direct viral infection, as IFN-β-deficient mice exhibited normal pregnancy outcomes and blocking interferon receptor activity ameliorated placental pathology despite higher viral loads. To our knowledge, these findings represent the first comprehensive preclinical safety evaluation of VSV-EBOV vaccination during pregnancy and identify a critical window of vulnerability early in gestation. More broadly, this work underscores the central role of interferons in shaping placental immune responses and provides an experimental framework to guide evaluation of live-virus vaccines in pregnancy.

articles.title: Maternal genitourinary tract infections and spontaneous preterm labor: A narrative review of pathogens, pathways, and prevention.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Malik MMUD, Saraf A, Lamghare PK
articles.abstract: Preterm birth is the leading cause of death among children aged under 5 years of age worldwide. Maternal genitourinary tract infections (GUTIs) are among the few modifiable risk factors for spontaneous preterm labor (sPTL), yet the gap between association and effective intervention remains unresolved. This narrative review consolidates recent evidence on GUTIs and sPTL, integrating pathogens, ascending and hematogenous pathways, and prevention. MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Scopus were searched (January 2000-January 2026); evidence was synthesized narratively and stratified by preterm-birth subtype where possible. Pooled estimates showed increased odds of preterm birth with urinary tract infection (odds ratio [OR] 1.92, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.62-2.27), asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB; OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.30-2.01), bacterial vaginosis (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.32-2.43), Ureaplasma colonization (OR 2.76, 95% CI 1.63-4.68), Trichomonas vaginalis (relative risk 1.42, 95% CI 1.15-1.75), and Chlamydia trachomatis (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.11-2.22). A 2026 Swedish register cohort (n = 684 595) demonstrates that the hazard for preterm birth after urinary tract infection (UTI) diagnosis is highest in the first 6 days and declines with advancing gestation (adjusted hazard ratios 18.5, 13.5, and 6.7 at 22-27, 28-31, and 32-36 weeks). Gene-environment analyses further indicate that preterm birth subtypes differ in susceptibility to UTI versus vaginal infection. Antibiotic treatment of ASB reduces pyelonephritis (RR 0.24), but its effect on preterm birth in unselected populations is uncertain. Ascending infection drives decidual cytokine release and premature myometrial activation; amniotic-fluid sludge on transvaginal ultrasound is an accessible marker of subclinical intra-amniotic infection. Targeted screening, evidence-based antibiotic selection, and antimicrobial stewardship remain the practical priorities.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Benmelstobart Plus Anlotinib in Advanced Endometrial Cancer: Results of a Multi-Cohort, Phase II Study (ETER200).
articles.authors: Liang S, Chen X, Wang K et al.
articles.abstract: Patients with advanced endometrial cancer (EC) have a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options after failure of prior systemic therapy. In this multi-cohort Phase II study (ETER200), patients with metastatic or recurrent EC who had received at least one chemotherapy regimen were enrolled. Based on MSI/MMR status, patients received benmelstobart plus anlotinib (Cohort 1), benmelstobart (Cohort 2), or anlotinib (Cohort 3) every 3 weeks. Primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) assessed by independent review committee (IRC) per RECIST v1.1. Here, the results of Cohort 1 expansion stage were reported. As of May 9, 2024, 85 of the 107 non-MSI-H/pMMR EC patients enrolled in Cohort 1 constituted the expansion stage population for primary efficacy analysis. The IRC-assessed ORR was 34.1% (95% CI, 24.2-45.2), with a median duration of response of 15.2 months (95% CI, 6.9-not evaluable). Median progression-free and overall survival were 8.8 months (95% CI, 5.8-15.2) and 21.8 months (95% CI, 19.5-29.1), respectively. Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 69.2% of patients, most commonly hypertension (21.2%) and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome (9.4%). Overall, benmelstobart plus anlotinib showed promising anti-tumor activity and an acceptable safety profile in advanced non-MSI-H/pMMR EC, supporting further evaluation of this combination in randomized Phase III studies. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04574284.

articles.title: First-morning urinary luteinizing hormone and bone age decomposition for diagnosis of central precocious puberty in girls: a two-step prediction model study.
articles.authors: Huang M, Lu X, Liu P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The diagnosis of central precocious puberty (CPP) in girls relies on the invasive gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test. Urinary luteinizing hormone (LH) is a noninvasive candidate biomarker, but evidence from Chinese populations and its integration into multivariable prediction frameworks remain limited. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of first-morning urinary LH for CPP, established sex- and pubertal stage-specific reference intervals, and developed a two-step prediction model based on a bone age decomposition.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, we enrolled 808 children: 295 girls with early breast development (146 CPP, 149 non-CPP), 271 healthy girls, and 242 healthy boys (reference intervals only). First-morning urine was assayed for LH, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), and creatinine. Diagnostic performance was evaluated primarily in the 295 symptomatic girls, with an extended analysis in 566 girls including healthy controls; multivariable logistic regression decomposed bone age into chronological age (CA) and the BA-CA difference as separate predictors.
RESULTS: Urinary LH showed moderate accuracy for CPP in the primary symptomatic cohort (AUC 0.692, 95% CI 0.630-0.752), peaking in girls aged 7-8 years (AUC 0.708, 95% CI 0.621-0.785); the extended cohort gave similar results (AUC 0.712; secondary, spectrum-extended estimate). The LH-to-creatinine ratio offered no improvement. Basal serum LH was the superior single marker (AUC 0.868 vs 0.692, P < 0.001). The noninvasive Model 1 (CA + BA-CA + urinary LH + breast Tanner stage + uterine length) achieved a C-statistic of 0.853 (sensitivity 73.3%, specificity 83.2%), with CA, BA-CA, and urinary LH as independent predictors. Adding basal serum LH and FSH (Model 2) improved the C-statistic to 0.909; urinary LH retained independent significance (aOR 1.280, P = 0.024), whereas basal FSH was inversely associated with CPP. Bootstrap-corrected C-statistics were 0.838 (Model 1) and 0.893 (Model 2). Pubertal-onset cutoffs were >1.02 mIU/mL in girls and >0.95 mIU/mL in boys.
CONCLUSIONS: Decomposing bone age into CA and BA-CA enables tiered CPP risk stratification: the noninvasive model supports initial screening without blood sampling, and the complete model refines risk once serum gonadotropins become available. Urinary LH is a clinically useful component of tiered diagnostic algorithms for CPP.

articles.title: Hypoxia Reprograms a Ciliary Scaffold into a Metabolic-Epigenetic Trafficking Hub via a Succinate-Driven DNMT3L-ASXL2 Axis.
articles.authors: Yin J, Zhong Z, Zhang M et al.
articles.abstract: Environmental hypoxia is a major yet mechanistically unresolved driver of male infertility. While the canonical hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) pathways dominate current models, how chronic oxygen deprivation persistently rewires spermatogenic epigenetics and flagellar architecture remains unknown. Here, we identify CEP162-traditionally defined as a static ciliary transition zone scaffold-as a dynamic oxygen-sensitive signaling hub that orchestrates a pathogenic metabolic-epigenetic-trafficking axis. In human asthenozoospermia and murine hypoxia models, CEP162 is aberrantly upregulated and strongly correlates with flagellar malformation and motility loss. Mechanistically, hypoxia inhibits succinate dehydrogenase, driving the accumulation of intracellular succinate, which disrupts the DNA methyltransferase 3-like (DNMT3L)-additional sex combs-like 2 (ASXL2) epigenetic repressor complex in a HIF-independent manner. This triggers CEP162 promoter hypomethylation and transcriptional derepression, establishing a stable epigenetic switch. Functionally, elevated levels of CEP162 act as a dominant negative regulator of ciliary protein delivery: biolayer interferometry and nucleotide exchange assays revealed that CEP162 spatially sequesters Rab1a and noncompetitively inhibits TRAPPC9-mediated GTP loading, thereby uncoupling vesicular trafficking from axonemal cargo delivery. Consequently, TEKT2 is not incorporated into the growing flagellum, leading to microtubule doublet destabilization and structural collapse. Genetic silencing of CEP162 or restoration of DNMT3L/ASXL2 activity fully rescues Rab1a activation, vesicular targeting, and sperm motility. Clinically, sperm CEP162 levels showed promising diagnostic potential in our initial cohort (area under the curve [AUC] >0.9) and were inversely correlated with progressive motility. This study redefines CEP162 from a passive structural component to an active metabolic-epigenetic sensor, reveals a noncanonical mechanism of Rab guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase) regulation and establishes a reversible succinate-driven epigenetic trajectory in environmentally induced infertility. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for metabolic-epigenetic coupling in polarized cells, identify actionable targets for environmentally induced male infertility and highlight a pathogenic axis that may warrant further investigation in the context of broader ciliopathies.

articles.title: Peripartum Esketamine: A Narrative Review of Analgesia, Postpartum Depressive Symptoms, Sleep-Related Outcomes, and Safety.
articles.authors: Zhong Z, Liao B, Peng D et al.
articles.abstract: Pain, depressive symptoms, and sleep disruption frequently overlap during the peripartum period, although their relationships are associative rather than established as causal. Esketamine, an N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor antagonist, has attracted interest as a peripartum intervention with potential effects on pain, mood, and sleep. This narrative review evaluates the clinical and mechanistic evidence for peripartum esketamine in analgesia, postpartum depressive symptoms, sleep-related outcomes, and maternal-infant safety, with particular attention to the directness and interpretability of the evidence. Most direct clinical evidence derives from cesarean-delivery studies, many of which are single-center trials. Evidence is most consistent for short-term analgesic benefit, whereas opioid-sparing effects are less consistent across individual studies and evidence syntheses. Several randomized trials suggest that low-dose peri-delivery esketamine may reduce early EPDS-defined screen-positive postpartum depressive symptoms, while evidence based on structured diagnostic outcomes remains limited. Evidence for sleep-related benefit remains preliminary and relies predominantly on subjective measures, with no direct postpartum polysomnographic evidence. Studied low-dose regimens have generally shown acceptable short-term maternal and neonatal tolerability in selected populations, but pregnancy-specific pharmacokinetics, lactation, and long-term offspring neurodevelopment remain insufficiently characterized. Overall, esketamine may represent an individualized adjunct in peripartum care, but current evidence does not support its routine prophylactic use. Future multicenter studies should incorporate diagnostic mood outcomes, objective sleep assessment, standardized treatment protocols, and long-term maternal and infant follow-up.

articles.title: Adolescent and Early-Onset Adenomyosis: Phenotypes, Diagnostic Challenges, and Fertility-Conscious Care.
articles.authors: Yang S, Chen Y, Ma X
articles.abstract: Adolescent and early-onset adenomyosis is increasingly recognized in symptomatic young patients, but its clinical significance remains uncertain. This narrative review synthesizes English-language literature on adolescent and early-onset adenomyosis, distinguishing direct adolescent and young-adult evidence from supportive evidence derived from adult populations. Current data suggest that adenomyosis-like imaging features may be identified in adolescents with severe dysmenorrhea, heavy menstrual bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, or coexisting endometriosis. Early disease often appears as subtle diffuse inner-myometrial change, focal lesions, or cystic/juvenile forms rather than the classic diffuse adult phenotype. Ultrasound is the first-line imaging modality, whereas MRI is reserved for equivocal findings, atypical cystic lesions, suspected congenital anomalies, or endometriosis overlap. Management requires a stepwise, symptom-oriented approach that considers future reproductive options and avoids unnecessary uterine intervention. Overall, adolescent adenomyosis should be considered in patients with severe or treatment-resistant menstrual symptoms, while uncertain imaging findings should not be overinterpreted.

articles.title: Evaluation of vaginal ampicillin administration in late gestation sows on pelvic organ prolapse in relation to perineal score and litter characteristics.
articles.authors: Kiefer ZE, Johnson EM, Studer JM et al.
articles.abstract: Within the last decade, increased sow mortality resulting from pelvic organ prolapse (POP) has become a growing concern in the swine industry. Despite being widely acknowledged as a sow welfare and production issue, mitigation strategies are scarce. Previous studies have demonstrated differences in the vaginal microbiome are associated with risk for POP during late gestation, representing a potential target for prevention strategies. The objective of the current study was to evaluate effects of vaginal infusion of ampicillin during late gestation on POP incidence. To accomplish this, the hypothesis that vaginal infusions of antibiotics would reduce POP risk during late gestation was tested. Ampicillin was infused into the vagina at two timepoints during late gestation. The first dose (10 mL at 200 mg/mL) was administered at gestational day 96 ± 0.09 followed by a second, equivalent dose at gestational day 112 ± 0.10. Sows were randomly assigned to treated (TRT; n = 824) and non-treated (CON; n = 739) groups based on gestation pen. At gestational days 107 to 116, sows (n = 1076) were evaluated for POP risk using a three-point perineal scoring system. Briefly, a perineal score (PS) of 1 (PS1) presumes little to no risk of POP, and a PS of 3 (PS3) presumes high risk of POP. From the 1076 sows assigned a PS, 46.5%, 49.7% and 3.8% of sows were assigned PS1, PS2, or PS3, respectively. Ampicillin treatment had no effect on PS (P = 0.20), with 45.6%, 51.6% and 2.8% of CON sows and 47.2%, 48.1% and 4.7% of TRT sows scoring a PS1, PS2, or PS3, respectively. Additionally, treatment did not affect (P = 0.74) POP incidence, with 4.5% of CON sows and 4.7% of TRT sows subsequently experiencing POP. Ampicillin treatment did not affect (P ≥ 0.54) litter characteristics. However, there was an effect of PS on litter characteristics observed with total born and stillborn piglets (P < 0.01), and a tendency for a difference in liveborn piglets (P = 0.09) between sows scored PS3 and PS1. Sows assigned a PS3 had fewer piglets born alive, presumably due to the increased number of stillborn piglets. Additionally, PS3 sows had 1 more total born on average within their litters compared to PS1 assigned sows (P < 0.01). In conclusion, vaginal infusion of ampicillin had no effect on PS, POP incidence, or litter characteristics, but PS did have an effect on the number of piglets born alive.

articles.title: Origin-Level Uterine Artery Ligation in Laparoscopic Hysterectomy for Intraligamentary Myoma.
articles.journal: JSLS : Journal of the Society of Laparoendoscopic Surgeons
articles.authors: Dağlı U, Kantarcı S, Karabulut A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Intraligamentary myomas distort broad-ligament anatomy and carry a high risk of bleeding during hysterectomy. We examined whether concomitant origin-level uterine artery ligation was associated with lower estimated blood loss.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort, 170 consecutive women underwent total laparoscopic hysterectomy for intraligamentary myoma (2015-2025); 91 received bilateral origin-level ligation. Estimated blood loss was compared with a multivariable regression model adjusted for patient characteristics, myoma diameter, and lateral localization.
RESULTS: Myomas in the ligation group were larger (median 9 vs 7 centimeters) and more often lateral (48% vs 14%), whereas crude mean blood loss was similar. In the regression analysis of mean blood loss, ligation was associated with lower blood loss only after adjustment (adjusted mean ratio 0.84; 95% confidence interval, 0.78 to 0.89), corresponding to an adjusted absolute reduction of 18 milliliters (95% confidence interval, 11 to 25). The postoperative hemoglobin decrease was smaller in the ligation group; operative time, hospital stay, transfusion, and complications did not differ significantly (few events).
CONCLUSION: In this nonrandomized cohort, origin-level ligation was associated with a modest reduction in adjusted estimated blood loss, without a detectable increase in operative time. Because it was selected intraoperatively for larger, more complex myomas, confounding by indication cannot be excluded; the findings are hypothesis-generating rather than causal.

articles.title: Quercetin upregulates TLE4 to block the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway and inhibit cell migration and invasion of cervical cancer cells.
articles.authors: Mai Y, Ju K, Yang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
METHODS: Using established TLE4-overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9-knockout cervical cancer cell lines and nude mouse tumorigenesis models, we verified the biological function and regulatory mechanism of TLE4 in cervical cancer.
RESULTS: Quercetin treatment upregulated the expression of TLE4 in HeLa cells. Compared with normal cervical tissues from clinical specimens, the expression of TLE4 in the nucleus of cervical cancer tissues was significantly downregulated. Transwell assays showed that the migration and invasion of C-33A TLE4-overexpression cells were significantly suppressed, accompanied by an upregulation of the expression of E-cadherin and a downregulation of the expression of N-cadherin, Vimentin, and Snail. Conversely, the migration and invasion of Ca Ski TLE4-knockout cells were significantly enhanced, and the expressions of these EMT-related markers showed the opposite trend. Meanwhile, the in vivo xenograft experiment revealed that the Ca Ski TLE4-knockout group exhibited faster tumor growth compared with the wild-type group. Furthermore, we examined the role of TLE4 in the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. In C-33A TLE4-overexpression cells, β-catenin, TCF-1, TCF-4, CyclinD1, c-Myc, and MMP-7 were decreased, p-β-catenin expression was increased, whereas in Ca Ski TLE4-knockout cells, the expression trends of these factors were opposite. After treating TLE4-knockout Ca Ski cells with quercetin, the enhanced migration and invasion capabilities induced by TLE4 knockout were effectively reversed.
CONCLUSION: Quercetin targets and upregulates the expression of TLE4, which inhibits the migration and invasion of cervical cancer cells by blocking the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, thereby providing theoretical and experimental evidence for quercetin therapy in cervical cancer.

articles.title: Placental immunopathology and congenital transmission of Zika virus and Trypanosoma cruzi: comparative mechanisms, immune disturbances, and potential co-infection scenarios.
articles.authors: Rodriguez-Salazar CA, Recalde-Reyes DP, Garg NJ et al.
articles.abstract: Congenital transmission of Zika virus (ZIKV) and Trypanosoma cruzi (T. cruzi) remains a major public health concern in the Americas. Both pathogens cross the placental barrier and cause severe neonatal outcomes, yet no confirmed congenital co-infections have been reported, and their combined effects on maternal-fetal health are unknown. Critical gaps persist regarding placental immunopathology, fetal immune programming, and long-term consequences of prenatal exposure. This review synthesizes current evidence on the routes and mechanisms of placental transmission of ZIKV and T. cruzi, their tropism for placental and fetal tissues, and their distinct immunological footprints. We summarize how congenital infection perturbs fetal immune maturation, including dysregulation of type I/type III interferons, Th1-skewed inflammation, altered immune-tolerance pathways involving HLA-G and PD-1/PD-L1 signaling, and early innate imprinting. We review advances in vaccine development (spanning inactivated, DNA, mRNA, subunit, and viral vector platforms) and highlight barriers such as antibody-dependent enhancement in ZIKV vaccines and the scarcity of pregnancy-relevant preclinical models for T. cruzi. Promising candidates with evidence of fetal or maternal protection in animal studies are described. Therapeutic approaches, including antiviral discovery, immunomodulatory strategies, and emerging anti-T. cruzi compounds are also examined. A detailed understanding of the immunopathology of congenital ZIKV and T. cruzi infections is essential to improve diagnostic accuracy, preventive strategies, and maternal-fetal clinical care. Integrated mechanistic and translational research is urgently needed to assess the plausibility of co-infection, identify biomarkers of fetal risk, and guide the development of pregnancy-safe vaccines and therapeutics, particularly in resource-limited, endemic settings.

articles.title: Results from the VANISH study: A prospective multicenter study validating a single-nucleotide polymorphism-based noninvasive prenatal test to assess aneuploidy risk in surviving twins of vanishing twin pregnancies.
articles.authors: Dugoff L, Mumford SL, Rochon ML et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To develop and validate a single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based noninvasive prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening algorithm capable of identifying the cfDNA signal of the living fetus in vanishing twin (VT) pregnancies and assessing that twin's aneuploidy risk.
METHODS: Prospective study enrolling participants ≥18 years old at ≥9 weeks' gestation with an ultrasound-confirmed VT at 21 US sites (August 2021 to August 2023). The study protocol specified SNP-based cfDNA screening at enrollment and at two additional 3-week intervals. Neonatal buccal swabs evaluated the SNP profile of the living fetus. Cases lost to follow-up and with missing samples were excluded. Using SNP-based technology, an algorithm to identify the living fetus was developed based on the number of fetoplacental cfDNA signals and individual fetal fraction measurements. Concordance between cfDNA in maternal plasma and newborn buccal-swab SNP profiles was used to validate the algorithm in correctly identifying the living fetus. Common aneuploidies and fetal sex were determined for the living fetus.
RESULTS: Of 136 participants enrolled, 106 met criteria for the final analysis; 45 for development and 61 for validation. In the validation cohort, median gestational age was 10.7 weeks (range: 8.0-16.1 weeks) at ultrasound diagnosis of a VT. In 93.4% of validation cases, the algorithm identified the living fetus and gave an aneuploidy result; 90.2% within the first two blood draws. At the time the living fetus was identified, 39 samples had two fetoplacental signals and 18 had one. Aneuploidy results included 56 low-risk and one high-risk result for trisomy 21. Neonatal buccal swabs confirmed that the VT algorithm correctly identified the living twin and gave a correct aneuploidy result in 57/57 cases (100%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 93.5%, 100.0%). Among 29 participants with all three blood draws and two fetoplacental signals at enrollment, two signals persisted in 93.1% at the second blood draw and 72.4% at the third.
CONCLUSIONS: The SNP-based algorithm accurately identified the living fetus in VT pregnancies in this small study. Aneuploidy risk assessment was validated in all cases where the cfDNA signal for the living twin was identified, though these findings should be interpreted with caution given the limited sample size.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05004337.

articles.title: Factors associated with self-management behavior among pregnant women with diet-controlled gestational diabetes mellitus in China: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Xu J, Tachasuksri T, Lapvongwatana P
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) poses escalating global health threats, particularly in China, with significant maternal-fetal health risks. Effective self-management is crucial to mitigate adverse maternal-neonatal outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to describe the status of self-management behavior and its associated factors in pregnant women with diet-controlled GDM.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study recruited 160 pregnant women with diet-controlled GDM from the antenatal clinic of the Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University from August to October 2024. Eligible participants were identified in the hospital's antenatal registration system and selected using simple random sampling based on assigned queue numbers. Data were collected through self-administered questionnaires assessing SMB, GDM knowledge, illness perception, self-efficacy, social support, and perception of care received. Data were analyzed using SPSS 27.0 with hierarchical multiple regression analysis.
RESULTS: A moderate level of SMB was observed in 45.6% of the participants (n = 73). Scores for exercise (M = 13.60, SD = 5.60) and glucose monitoring (M = 11.86, SD = 4.32) ranked lowest among SMB domains. The final hierarchical multiple regression model explained 60.6% of the variance in SMB among pregnant women with GDM (R2 = 0.606, F(6,153) = 39.28, p < 0.001). Significant factors associated with SMB included GDM knowledge (β = 0.296, 95% CI: 0.869 to 2.161, p < 0.001), social support (β = 0.252, 95% CI: 0.455 to 1.358, p < 0.001), illness perception (β = 0.188, 95% CI: 0.137 to 0.635, p = 0.003), self-efficacy (β = 0.183, 95% CI: 0.086 to 0.499, p = 0.006), and pregnancy-related anxiety (β = -0.188, 95% CI: -1.187 to -0.286, p = 0.002). Perception of care received was not significantly associated with SMB (β = 0.033, 95% CI: -0.303 to 0.579, p = 0.537).
CONCLUSION: These findings identify potential correlates for further nursing interventions, suggesting that tailored, culturally sensitive education, family-centered support, and multidisciplinary care may be beneficial in supporting SMB. Such efforts should prioritize reducing anxiety while fostering knowledge, self-efficacy, and social support.

articles.title: Comparison of short-term oncological and functional outcomes between the da Vinci and toumai platforms in robotic radical prostatectomy.
articles.authors: Buffa A, Tobia I, Martinez PF et al.
articles.abstract: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) is a standard treatment for localized prostate cancer (PCa). As new, lower-cost robotic platforms reach Latin America, comparative evidence remains scarce. We compared complications, and short-term oncological and functional outcomes between the da Vinci and the new Toumai platforms in RARP. Single-center, prospective, non-randomized study of patients older than 40 years with localized PCa undergoing RARP between June 2025 and July 2026. The first 100 consecutive Toumai cases were compared with 100 consecutive da Vinci cases operated during the same period; platform allocation depended on operating-room availability, without matching or randomization. Salvage RARP was excluded. Perioperative variables, Clavien-Dindo complications, pathological outcomes, positive surgical margins (PSM), undetectable PSA (< 0.1 ng/mL) and continence (pads/day) at one and three months were analyzed. Two hundred patients were analyzed (100 Toumai vs. 100 da Vinci) with comparable baseline characteristics. Operative time (215.0 vs. 200.3 min) and console time (193.6 vs. 178.0 min) were longer with Toumai (p = 0.001 and p < 0.001, respectively), while docking time did not differ significantly (21.4 vs. 22.3 min; p = 0.147). Hospital stay (1.6 days; p = 0.819), catheter duration (10.7 vs. 10.8 days; p = 0.671), overall complications (18% vs. 10%; p = 0.103), PSM (19% vs. 17%; p = 0.713) and undetectable PSA (96% vs. 93%; p = 0.352) were similar. Continence (no pads) was 84% vs. 73% at one month (p = 0.058) and 87% vs. 85% at three months (p = 0.314). In a high-volume center, the da Vinci and Toumai platforms showed comparable short-term oncological, functional, and complication outcomes, including similar platform docking times despite longer total operative and console times with Toumai.

articles.title: Dissecting polycystic metabolic ovarian syndrome heterogeneity (PMOS): multi-omics, AI subtyping, and precision management.
articles.authors: Pradhan S, Gopalakrishnan AV
articles.abstract: Polycystic metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is the most common endocrine disorder, affecting 8-12% of women of reproductive age and increasing the risk of infertility, type 2 diabetes, and heart disease. However, traditional symptom-based diagnostic criteria do not fully capture the underlying biological diversity of PMOS. Recent research using multi-omics and artificial intelligence (AI) has revealed that PMOS is best understood as a syndrome with multiple subtypes. Data-driven clustering of clinical variables consistently identifies four major subtypes: HA-PCOS, OB-PCOS, SHBG-PCOS, and LH-PCOS. Each subtype shows unique hormonal, metabolic, and genetic features, including distinct patterns in lipid, amino acid, and energy metabolism. Immune system disruptions and impaired blood clot breakdown in the ovarian environment are also notable features. Novel findings suggest that altered lactate metabolism and changes in histone lactylation may contribute to granulosa cell dysfunction, although further studies are needed to confirm these mechanisms. Machine learning models that integrate clinical, metabolic, and genetic data have achieved high diagnostic accuracy and can provide interpretable results. Potential targeted therapies, such as GLP-1 receptor agonists, SGLT2 inhibitors, N-acetylcysteine, and NK3R antagonists, have been proposed for specific subtypes, but have yet to be validated in clinical trials. Remaining challenges include small and homogeneous study cohorts, limited long-term data, and barriers to care in low-resource settings. Overall, recognizing PMOS as a syndrome with distinct subtypes highlights the promise of AI-powered, personalized approaches for more effective and equitable management.

articles.title: Change in alcohol consumption and all-cause mortality among postmenopausal women diagnosed with breast cancer.
articles.authors: Rees S, Bodelon C, Chakraborty S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evidence is inconsistent regarding an association between alcohol consumption and survival following a breast cancer diagnosis; therefore, we examined how change in alcohol consumption affects all-cause mortality (ACM) in a population of breast cancer survivors.
METHODS: We prospectively assessed pre-diagnosis, pre- to post-diagnosis, and post-diagnosis change in alcohol consumption among 1,558 postmenopausal women (mean age-at-diagnosis: 71 years) diagnosed with non-metastatic invasive breast cancer from the American Cancer Society Cancer Prevention Study-II Nutrition Cohort (baseline: 1992-1993). Five categories of alcohol intake were determined at each assessment; change in alcohol consumption was categorized as stable, quit, reduced, and increased. Change occurred at a median of two years before (pre-diagnosis) and two years after (post-diagnosis) diagnosis. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the associations between change groups and ACM.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 12.6 years, 750 women died (130 breast cancer deaths). Compared to stable consumption, the association between cessation and ACM varied by change interval: pre-diagnosis (HR:0.91, CI:0.69-1.21), pre- to post-diagnosis: (HR:1.39, CI:1.12-1.73), post-diagnosis: (HR:0.98, CI:0.70-1.35). Alcohol reduction was not associated with ACM. Among women consuming ≥ 1 drink/day pre-diagnosis, increasing consumption elevated ACM risk (HR:1.83, 95%CI:1.02-3.31).
CONCLUSION: Alcohol reduction or cessation was not associated with a decrease in ACM among older breast cancer survivors. Among those drinking ≥ 1 drink/day, an increase in consumption pre-diagnosis was associated with higher mortality. Findings may be limited by uncontrolled confounding, a low prevalence of heavy drinking, or an insufficient duration of sustained change.

articles.title: Beyond infection: the longitudinal impact of genitourinary tuberculosis on urologic and reproductive health.
articles.authors: Kazal FH, Horns JJ, Myers JB et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To address the limited understanding of the long-term morbidity of genitourinary tuberculosis (GUTB), by characterizing the clinical course and risk of urologic events (UE) both preceding and following GUTB diagnosis.
METHODS: This retrospective age-, sex- and comorbidity-matched cohort study evaluated all patients with GUTB in Merative Marketscan (2011-2021). Patients were followed throughout enrollment to capture comorbid diseases (pulmonary tuberculosis and HIV) and urologic events (diagnoses and procedures). Events- and diagnoses-of-interest that occurred both prior and after GUTB diagnosis were included. UEs were classified as low-grade events, high-grade events, or infertility. Multivariable cox proportional hazards models compared the risk of UEs over time.
RESULTS: 1503 patients with GUTB were identified. Mean patient age was 43 years. Most patients were otherwise healthy (63% CCI ≤ 1). GUTB was associated with 2.5-fold the risk of high-grade UE prior to diagnosis (HR 2.5, p < 0.001) and 2.7-fold the risk after diagnosis (HR 2.7, p < 0.001). It was also associated with two-fold the risk of low-grade UE prior to diagnosis (HR 2.0, p < 0.001) and a 1.6-fold after diagnosis (HR 1.6, p < 0.001). Infertility risk was significant among GUTB patients in the pre-diagnosis setting (HR 2.6, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: GUTB is associated with a substantial increase in urologic morbidity, with elevated risks of low- and high-grade events before and after diagnosis, suggesting a prolonged and perhaps unrecognized subclinical disease course. The increased risk of infertility prior to diagnosis highlights importance of considering GUTB in unexplained infertility, particularly in TB-endemic regions.

articles.title: Gynaecological complications and vulvovaginal graft-versus-host disease after allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a retrospective study.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.authors: Plaziat M, Georgescu D, Rives N et al.
articles.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), a key treatment for haematological malignancies and other bone marrow disorders, may lead to complications such as vulvovaginal GvHD, an under-recognised and frequently under-diagnosed condition. We conducted an observational, retrospective, single-centre study at the Centre Henri Becquerel in Rouen, including all women who underwent allogeneic HSCT since 2017 and had at least one gynaecological consultation; data were collected between April 2023 and April 2024. Among the 110 patients analysed, vulvovaginal GvHD was identified in 25.5%, most often with late onset and severe forms. Treatment, mainly topical with systemic therapy in more severe cases, led to clinical improvement or resolution in 65.4% of cases. Other post-transplant gynaecological complications were also assessed: rates of HPV positivity and cervical cytological abnormalities were not significantly increased after transplantation; menometrorrhagia was observed in 6.5% of patients; and premature ovarian insufficiency occurred in 53.3% of women under 40 years. Sexual dysfunction was markedly more frequent in women with vulvovaginal GvHD, particularly vaginal dryness (57.1% vs. 28.8%; p = 0.014) and dyspareunia (73.9% vs. 26.2%; p < 0.001). These findings highlight that vulvovaginal GvHD and other gynaecological sequelae remain under-estimated, underscoring the need for systematic and individualised gynaecological follow-up after allogeneic HSCT.

articles.title: Anatomical Variations and Morphometry of the Pudendal Nerve: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Plutecki D, Wilk J, Mordarski M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: The aim of this meta-analysis was to comprehensively review the available literature and determine the pooled prevalence of the morphometric and topographical characteristics of the pudendal nerve (PN), providing a better understanding of its anatomical variations and, consequently, enhancing patient safety during pelvic procedures.
METHODS: A comprehensive search was performed across various major databases including PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science to find all articles regarding the morphology and anatomy of the PN. A total of 29 studies were included in this meta-analysis.
RESULTS: The most common type of PN trunk was a single trunk with 61.27% (95% CI 48.02-73.74%) prevalence, followed by double PN trunk with 27.94% (95% CI 17.74-39.41%). The mean diameter of the PN in the cadaveric studies was 3.73 mm (SE 0.33). The mean length of the PN in the cadaveric studies was 56.08 mm (SE 0.82).
CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis highlights the substantial anatomical variability of the pudendal nerve, which limits the feasibility of a single, universally applicable classification system. A comprehensive understanding of its morphology and branching patterns is essential for improving the safety and effectiveness of surgical and anesthetic procedures in the pelvic region. The findings emphasize the need for standardized methodologies and nomenclature in future anatomical studies to enhance comparability and clinical applicability. Ultimately, improved anatomical knowledge of the pudendal nerve may contribute to better diagnostic accuracy and reduced risk of iatrogenic injury.

articles.title: Prevalence of Urinary Incontinence and Associated Factors in Women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: de Oliveira Lima T, Alves MAT, de Almeida Nogueira M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) can compromise the pelvic floor muscles, with the possible occurrence of urinary incontinence (UI). This study aimed to determine the prevalence of UI and associated factors in women with SLE.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted over 12 months in women with SLE. UI was assessed using the three Incontinence Questions (3IQ), severity using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire - Short Form (ICIQ-SF), impact of urinary symptoms using the Urinary Impact Questionnaire (UIQ-7), quality of life (QoL) using the 12-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12), and functional performance using the 30-s Sit-to-Stand (SIT) and Timed Up and Go (TUG) tests. Descriptive and bivariate analyses were performed, and factors associated with urinary incontinence (UI) were investigated using Poisson regression with robust variance, with prevalence ratios (PR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 231 women (age 47 ± 12 years) were included. UI was identified in 52% (95% CI 46.0-58.7) of the participants. In the bivariate analysis, UI was associated with age, paid employment, family income, and some clinical and obstetric characteristics. In the final multivariate Poisson regression model, lower physical and mental health scores were associated with UI (PCS PR 0.99; 95% CI 0.97-1.00; p = 0.024; MCS PR 0.99; 95% CI 0.97-1.00; p = 0.033).
CONCLUSIONS: UI was present in more than half of the women with SLE and was associated with worse QoL.

articles.title: Vaginal Canal Segmentation with nnU-Net Algorithm from MRI Defecography for Biomechanical Analysis.
articles.authors: Aydın S, Sarıkaya AF, Karakuş E et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Accurate three-dimensional segmentation of the vaginal canal is essential for patient-specific pelvic floor modeling, biomechanical analysis, and the development of personalized intravaginal devices. However, manual segmentation of magnetic resonance defecography (MRD) images is time-consuming and prone to observer variability. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an automated deep learning pipeline using the nnU-Net framework for vaginal canal segmentation from MRD images.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 47 women who underwent MRD for symptoms of pelvic floor dysfunction were included. The vaginal canal was manually annotated on three-dimensional T2-weighted MRD volumes using 3D Slicer to generate ground-truth binary masks. A 3D full-resolution nnU-Net model was trained and evaluated using fivefold cross-validation. Segmentation accuracy was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU). Predicted masks were further processed using hole filling, marching cubes surface reconstruction, and Taubin smoothing to generate three-dimensional meshes and extract vaginal volume and surface area.
RESULTS: The nnU-Net model achieved high segmentation accuracy, with a mean DSC of 0.9714 and a mean IoU of 0.9675. Automated segmentation of a full 3D MRD volume required < 1 s, compared with approximately 30-45 min for manual segmentation. The mean vaginal volume was 38.74 ± 13.98 cm3, and the mean vaginal surface area was 82.31 ± 19.31 cm2.
CONCLUSIONS: The nnU-Net framework enables rapid, accurate, and reproducible segmentation of the gel-distended vaginal lumen from MRD images. This automated pipeline may facilitate standardized three-dimensional measurement of the visible vaginal cavity and provide geometry for patient-specific biomechanical modeling.

articles.title: Trophoblast-derived extracellular vesicles elicit long-term effects on maternal cardiovascular function in a postpartum model of chronic hypertension.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.ta: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.authors: Piesse S, Lau SY, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract: The hypertensive disease of pregnancy, preeclampsia, is a risk factor for future maternal cardiovascular disease while normal pregnancy is cardioprotective in the long term. Trophoblast-derived extracellular vesicles (T-EVs) released by the placenta are implicated in the development of vascular dysfunction and are widely thought to have a role in the pathogenesis of preeclampsia. This study tested the effects of T-EVs from both normotensive and preeclamptic pregnancies on long-term cardiovascular outcomes in a pregnant hypertensive model. Spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) received intravenous vehicle control (CTEV; n = 11), and T-EVs from normotensive (NT; n = 10), early onset preeclamptic (EOPE; n = 10), or late-onset preeclamptic (LOPE; n = 10) pregnancies between days 8.5 and 18.5 of pregnancy (term = 22.5 days). SHRs were monitored during pregnancy and up to 12 mo postpartum, with noninvasive blood pressure plethysmography and echocardiography, followed by wire myography and histology. The NT group demonstrated significantly lower postpartum systolic blood pressure (SBP) compared with CTEV (P < 0.0001), whereas SBP in the EOPE group was increased (P < 0.0001). SBP was not significantly different between the CTEV and LOPE groups (P > 0.05). Terminal wire myography revealed that vessels from the NT group were more vasodilatory in response to acetylcholine (P = 0.0103) and less contractile in response to phenylephrine (P = 0.0435) and endothelin-1 (P < 0.0001). Vascular structure, cardiac function, and cardiac morphology were not different between all four T-EV groups. Exposure to T-EVs during pregnancy continued to influence maternal vascular function long after their administration. These findings confirm the role of T-EVs in regulating maternal vasculature long after the removal of the placenta at birth.NEW & NOTEWORTHY We have shown that normotensive T-EVs reduce blood pressure and promote a provasodilatory vascular phenotype for at least 12 mo after administration during pregnancy in a rat model. Administration of EOPE preeclamptic T-EVs prevented the natural decrease in blood pressure during pregnancy and increased blood pressure long-term. Together, these results suggest T-EVs play a key role in modulating maternal vascular function not only in pregnancy but also in determining future cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Performance of AI-based models in prenatal detection of trisomy 21 via ultrasonography: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Ahmadi S, Mohseni Dafrazi F, Abdol Homayuni MR
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the performance, strengths, and limitations of artificial intelligence (AI) models for trisomy 21 classification and risk prediction, and for enabling ultrasound tasks, using fetal ultrasound.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception through October 2026, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. Original, peer-reviewed studies that developed or validated AI models for trisomy 21 classification or risk prediction, or for enabling ultrasound tasks (nuchal translucency and facial marker measurement, segmentation, and plane recognition), using human fetal ultrasound images or ultrasound-derived measurements and reporting quantitative performance metrics were eligible. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias with PROBAST (prediction-model studies) and QUADAS-2 (enabling-task studies), resolving disagreements by consensus. Studies were categorized by primary task and synthesized narratively, without meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Nineteen studies published between 2015 and 2026 were included: eight image-based classifiers, seven marker-based risk models, and four enabling-task studies. Image-based classifiers reported accuracies of 84-98.3% and AUCs of 0.95-0.985. Marker-based models reported AUCs of 0.84-0.983; detection rates of 90-100% at false-positive rates of about 3.6-3.9% came from one research group, whereas the largest cohort reported a sensitivity of 84% at a false-positive rate of 2.28%. Enabling-task studies were evaluated with task-specific metrics and were not compared with classification performance. Ten of fifteen prediction-model studies were at high risk of bias, mainly in the analysis domain; seven reported only image counts, and leakage between training and test data was likely in six. Most studies were retrospective with limited external validation.
CONCLUSION: Reported performance of AI models for trisomy 21 is high but comes mostly from retrospective, internally validated studies, and benefits for screening performance, invasive testing, or operator dependence have not been demonstrated. No study compared AI with cell-free DNA screening, so the role of these tools within current screening pathways remains undefined. Prospective, multicenter validation with karyotype-confirmed outcomes and standardized reporting is needed before clinical integration can be supported.

articles.title: Diagnostic overlap between necrotic leiomyoma, adenomyoma and uterine sarcoma: an ultrasound challenge.
articles.authors: Pellecchia G, Moro F, Campolo F et al.
articles.abstract: Atypical myometrial lesions may represent a significant diagnostic challenge even for experienced sonographers, particularly when ultrasound and MRI findings overlap among benign, borderline, and malignant entities. Reporting these cases may contribute to improving pattern recognition and refining the diagnostic work-up in clinical practice. We report the case of a 47-year-old woman presenting with menometrorrhagia, severe anemia, chronic pelvic pain, and rapid enlargement of a myometrial lesion. Transvaginal ultrasound revealed a 9-cm atypical myometrial mass with uncertain echostructure, difficult to classify unequivocally according to the MUSA criteria due to its ambiguous nature of poorly structured solid ('cooked') appearance versus cystic content. MRI findings and radiologist's conclusions were also inconclusive. Concomitant deep infiltrating endometriosis further complicated the interpretation. Because malignancy could not be excluded, the patient underwent surgery. Histopathological examination revealed an apoplectic leiomyoma with extensive infarct-type necrosis and no cytological atypia or mitoticfigures. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of atypical necrotic leiomyomas and the potential overlap of imaging features between benign degenerative lesions and malignant uterine tumors. In challenging cases, integration of ultrasound findings with MRI, clinical history, and histopathological examination remains essential.

articles.title: Mimosa pudica L. extract attenuates endometrial hyperplasia and proliferation of its malignant cell lines: transcript-level insights from a dual in vivo-in vitro model.
articles.authors: Swathi CM, Vignesh K, Archana Devi C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrium is the innermost layer of the uterus that respond to and synthesize estrogens in connection with its synchronized thickening and shedding during menstrual cycle. Since its thickening is essential for implantation of the embryo, its hyperplasia at chronicity could lead to uterus-associated infertility. if untreated.
METHODS: Qualitative and quantitative analysis of phytochemical constituents, antioxidant efficacy, and GC-MS analysis of M. pudica leaf extract were done. The antiproliferative efficacy of the extract was assessed by MTT assay, fluorescent staining, and mRNA studies of apoptotic-related genes in endometrial cancer cells (Ishikawa and AN3CA). About 25 female rats were assigned to five groups, control (Group 1) and DES-induced endometrial hyperplasia (Groups 2-5). in this, Groups 3-5 were treated with M. pudica leaf extract at increasing doses to assess its restorative efficacy in terms of estrous cycle, structure of ovary, and uterine weight adopting quantification of hormones, ROS, and mRNA expression of genes associated with inflammation (IL-6, NCOR1, and DLK1), angiogenesis (VEGF), and progression of endometrial hyperplasia (ARID1A, SMARCA4, PIK3CA and KRAS).
RESULTS: Administration of M. pudica leaf extract restored the estrous cycle, bringing to normalcy the structure and function of the ovary and uterus, balancing hormones, and reducing inflammation. The expression of ARID1A and SMARCA4, were enhanced while those of genes associated with proliferation, angiogenesis, and inflammation were mitigated.
CONCLUSION: M. pudica leaf extract is potentially effective as a therapeutic agent against endometrial hyperplasia and its cancer cell proliferation by restoring nearly all the dysregulations up to mRNA expression level.

articles.title: Comorbidities and outcomes associated with young adult hip fracture: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.authors: Herath M, Giri R, Rodriguez AJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognosis of hip fracture in younger adults (YAs) aged 18-50 years is unestablished. Large studies that rigorously assess risk factors for hip fracture in YAs, their associated functional outcomes and mortality are lacking. While international guidelines recommend comprehensive bone health assessment and consideration of pharmacotherapy in YAs with major fragility fractures, rates of implementation of these guidelines are unknown.
METHODS: We systematically reviewed the existing literature on YAs with hip fracture to identify (1) clinical risk factors for hip fracture, (2) functional outcomes beyond 12 months from hip fracture (including employment and mortality) and (3) referral rates for bone health assessment.
RESULTS: Forty-four studies were included from 1875 eligible abstracts. Twenty-three studies reported data on question 1. Psychiatric disease (15% [10-23%]), glucocorticoid exposure (5% [2-14%]), psychotropic exposure (12% [3-42%]), alcohol excess (15% [6-38%]) and cigarette smoking (36% [25-49%]) were highly prevalent in YAs with hip fracture. Twenty-six studies contributed data on question 2, including four that provided mortality data. There is either good or excellent functional recovery in ≥80% of YAs by 12 months following hip fracture; however, up to 15% experience poor outcomes at two years. Mortality rates beyond one year were only reported in one study. Only eight studies were designed specifically to investigate risk factors for, or outcomes associated with, YA hip fracture. Three studies reported outcomes of interest by fracture mechanism. The Quality in Prognosis Studies tool was used to assess the risk of bias of included studies. 24/44 (54.5%) were found to have a moderate or high risk of bias. One study reported data on question 3.
CONCLUSION: Psychiatric morbidity, alcohol excess and smoking were the major risk factors associated with hip fracture in YAs. Further research is required to establish the risk factors for minimal trauma hip fracture in YAs.
