Limited data on mortality in YAs following hip fracture are concerning and deserve further investigation.

articles.title: Association between the frequency of achieving recommended daily step counts and a decline in quantitative ultrasound measurements in premenopausal and postmenopausal women: a 4-year prospective study of the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort study.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.authors: Sato K, Chiba I, Nakaya N et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Achieving 7000 steps/day on ≥3 days/week significantly reduced the risk of decline in quantitative ultrasound measurements in premenopausal women, but not in postmenopausal women. Less frequent achievement (1-2 days/week) showed no significant association in either group.
PURPOSE: To examine the association between the frequency of achieving the recommended daily step count (7000 steps/day) and the incidence of a decline in quantitative ultrasound (QUS) measurements among pre- and postmenopausal women.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study of the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort, baseline and follow-up surveys were conducted between 2013-2016 and 2017-2021 (mean follow-up: 42.5 months). Participants were 3529 women (1013 premenopausal, 2516 postmenopausal). Daily steps were objectively measured using pedometers. The number of days per week achieving 7000 steps was categorized as Inactive (0 days), Low active (1-2 days), and Active (≥3 days). The outcome was the incidence of a decline in QUS measurements, defined as a QUS T-score ≤-2.5 or a self-reported diagnosis of osteoporosis. Adjusted risk ratio (RR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated using modified Poisson regression models, with the Inactive group as the reference.
RESULTS: During follow-up, the outcome occurred in 70 premenopausal and 662 postmenopausal women. In premenopausal women, the Active group had a significantly lower risk of the outcome compared to the Inactive group (RR: 0.478, 95% CI: 0.271 to 0.843). In postmenopausal women, no statistically significant association was observed (RR for the Active group: 0.937, 95% CI: 0.807 to 1.088).
CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that the association appeared to differ by menopausal status, achieving 7000 steps/day on ≥3 days/week was associated with a significantly reduced risk of a decline in QUS measurements in premenopausal women. However, for postmenopausal women, walking alone may be an insufficient strategy.

articles.title: Serum Response Factor Cooperates With Progesterone Receptor to Regulate Oviductal Smooth Muscle Gene Expression During Preimplantation Embryo Transport.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.authors: Lais PF, Marquardt RM, Wu SP et al.
articles.abstract: The oviduct (fallopian tube) houses the site of fertilization and transports embryos to the uterus for on-time implantation. Hormone-regulated contractions of the oviductal smooth muscle (myosalpinx) are thought to participate in this process. Serum response factor (SRF) is a widely expressed transcription factor shown to facilitate smooth muscle development as well as murine oviductal function. Our past work in the uterus has suggested that SRF transcriptional activity is associated with the master pregnancy regulator progesterone receptor (PGR). We therefore hypothesized that SRF and PGR work together to influence oviductal gene expression. Ablation of Srf in the Pgr-expressing cells of the mouse oviduct resulted in extensive transcriptomic consequences. Of 1670 differentially expressed genes in the Srf-deficient oviduct, 306 also contained an SRF binding region within 10 kb of the TSS, including cytoskeletal, contractile, and extracellular matrix genes important for muscle structure and function. Histological analysis confirmed disruption of the smooth muscle layer in the Srf-deficient oviduct, and functional contractility analyses demonstrated that contractile activity was deficient and irregular. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of oviducts deficient in smooth muscle Pgr expression uncovered parallel downregulation of extracellular matrix organization pathways and smooth muscle contraction processes. Integration of SRF and PGR cistromic analyses identified a set of structural and contractile smooth muscle genes co-occupied and co-regulated by SRF and PGR including Myh11, Actg2, and Des. Our findings highlight a prominent regulatory mechanism for SRF and PGR in the oviduct, disruption of which contributes to impaired myosalpinx function and infertility.

articles.title: Cardiac Structure and Function in Women After Preeclampsia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Yao JV, Wang B, Wong C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia increases the risk of long-term heart failure (HF) by 4-fold. Unfortunately, however, universal guidelines for postpartum HF surveillance are lacking. Stage B/subclinical HF has been shown to predict risk of major adverse cardiac outcomes. Some suggest that initiating cardioprotective therapy at this early stage can reduce progression to symptomatic HF.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to explore cardiac structure and function in women with a history of preeclampsia and to identify when subclinical HF develops in this group.
METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE and CINAHL was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines to identify all studies assessing left ventricular function on transthoracic echocardiography in women with a history of preeclampsia.
RESULTS: A total of 45 case-control studies comprising 8,991 women, including 2,288 women with a history of preeclampsia, were included in the final analysis. During pregnancy, women with preeclampsia had a higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (standard mean difference: 10.85 [95% CI: 6.30-15.39]), relative wall thickness (0.05 [95% CI: 0.03-0.08]), E/e' (1.58 [95% CI: 1.02-2.13]), isovolumetric relaxation time (8.74 [95% CI: 3.14-14.34]), lower E/A ratio (-0.27 [95% CI: -0.51 to -0.04]) and reduced absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS) values (2.27 [95% CI: 0.43-4.11]), indicating reduced myocardial function compared with normotensive controls. Postpartum, GLS remained reduced, and LVMI remained elevated in women with a history of preeclampsia. This difference persisted out to 10 years postpartum. There was no significant difference in all other variables >6 months postpartum. Evidence for persistent LVMI elevation >6 months postpartum was not robust in sensitivity analyses excluding overlapping cohorts. Left ventricular ejection fraction and right ventricular function remained similar in the preeclampsia and control groups throughout.
CONCLUSIONS: Preeclampsia is associated with subclinical myocardial dysfunction, characterized by impaired GLS and increased LVMI. Persistent impairment in GLS was observed up to 10 years postpartum, whereas the association with elevated LVMI beyond 6 months postpartum should be interpreted with caution. Further studies are required to assess when subclinical myocardial dysfunction progresses to symptomatic clinical HF.

articles.title: Fertility preservation counselling in women with cancer: knowledge, preferences, and unmet needs from a cross-sectional survey.
articles.authors: Corrado G, Zace D, Peters I et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fertility preservation (FP) is a critical survivorship issue for young women with cancer, yet gaps persist between guidelines and clinical practice. This study assesses knowledge, attitudes, and unmet needs among women referred for specialist counseling.
METHODS: An observational cross-sectional survey was conducted (November 2022 - June 2026) among women referred to a single tertiary oncofertility center in Rome. A Delphi-informed online questionnaire was completed before the clinical visit. Descriptive statistics and exploratory multivariable logistic regression examined post-diagnosis intention.
RESULTS: Among 284 women invited to participate, 260 completed the survey (response rate, 91.5%); 240 patients with a confirmed cancer diagnosis were included in the final analysis (median age, 32 years). Overall, 69.6% were interested in FP, and 94.2% recognized that gonadotoxic treatments could impair fertility. While 89.6% had heard of FP, only half received this information from healthcare professionals, and 24.2% knew of no specific options. Over half reported concerns regarding treatment delay, safety, effectiveness, and cost. Before diagnosis, 73.7% planned to have children; post-diagnosis, positive intention remained common, while those previously without intentions shifted toward uncertainty. In the 188-case model, pre-diagnosis intention showed the strongest association (OR 11.64, 95% CI 4.45-30.48). Given limited model performance (pseudo-R²=0.19), estimates warrant caution.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center referred cohort, informational gaps and uncertainty remained despite high awareness. Findings confirm and contextualize prior evidence in an Italian tertiary setting and may inform similar referral pathways, but require validation in broader populations.

articles.title: Pathogenesis of bronchopulmonary dysplasia: an immunological perspective.
articles.authors: Riley D, Bhandari V
articles.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), the most common chronic lung disease of prematurity, is at its mechanistic core an immune-developmental disease in which inflammatory injury disrupts normal lung maturation. In the United States, BPD remains among the most common morbidities of very preterm birth, affecting a substantial proportion of infants born before 32 weeks' gestation. These infants are born before alveolarization is complete, into an inflammatory environment that can impair ongoing lung development. This review advances a single thesis: the heterogeneous prenatal and postnatal insults that precede BPD (chorioamnionitis and the fetal inflammatory response syndrome, Ureaplasma colonization, hyperoxia, mechanical ventilation, sepsis, and intestinal dysbiosis) converge on a small number of innate sensing pathways, principally TLR2 and TLR4 signaling through NF-κB to the NLRP3 inflammasome - with parallel sterile inputs (mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and additional pattern-recognition receptors) feeding the same inflammasome node. We argue that this convergence is what separates BPD from ordinary neonatal lung injury, and that the outcome depends less on the magnitude of the initiating injurious hits than on failure of the resolution program that should terminate them - a hypothesis supported by convergent preclinical evidence but not yet established in preterm infants. Evidence is assembled across three domains: the cellular substrate (M1-skewed, classically activated-like alveolar macrophages, NETs, Th17/Treg imbalance, deficient transplacental IgG transfer); the mediator network (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α, and the loss of endogenous brakes - specialized pro-resolving mediators, IL-37, Nrf2, short-chain fatty acids); and the signaling architecture (NF-κB, the NLRP3 inflammasome, and trained immunity). We also discuss the mechanistically supported, druggable nodes and the developmental phase in which each is engageable.

articles.title: A nanoengineered MSC therapeutic for synergistic therapy of lupus nephritis via cfDNA clearance and targeted immunomodulation.
articles.authors: Tian J, Xu Q, Wang Z et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Lupus nephritis (LN) remains a clinical challenge due to the dose-limiting toxicity of conventional immunosuppressants and the poor engraftment/efficacy of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapies.
METHODS: We report a novel nanoengineered MSC therapeutic for LN by engineering MSCs with a cell-free DNA (cfDNA)-targeting dendritic nanogel. To obtain the hybrid MSC-G3K@T system, we coupled tacrolimus-loaded, disulfide-crosslinked polylysine dendrimer nanogels (G3K@T) onto the MSC membrane. Our system exploits two synergistic targeting strategies: the innate homing capacity of MSCs, plus the specific affinity of the cationic G3K dendrimer for anionic cfDNA, which enriches in inflamed kidneys.
RESULTS: Our system acts through two coordinated actions: the nanogel responds to the oxidative renal microenvironment and releases tacrolimus in a spatiotemporally controlled manner, thereby suppressing T-cell activation. At the same time, it scavenges cfDNA, blocking TLR-mediated pro-inflammatory signaling. Working together with the inherent immunomodulatory functions of MSCs, this dual-action strategy yielded robust efficacy in MRL/lpr mice, including a significant reversal of T-cell dysregulation, restoration of glomerular integrity, and reduction of proteinuria and IgG deposition.
CONCLUSIONS: We propose that MSC-G3K@T offers a promising route to augment cell-based therapies, creating a versatile platform that could be used to treat autoimmune and inflammatory diseases.

articles.title: Prevalence and Pattern of Hemoglobinopathies Among Women of Reproductive Age Attending a Tertiary Care Center in Central Uttar Pradesh: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Khan H, Gupta N, Gupta R et al.
articles.abstract: Background Hemoglobinopathies are an important public health concern in India, with considerable variation across regions. Screening women of reproductive age can help identify carriers early and provide opportunities for reproductive counselling. This study assessed the prevalence and pattern of hemoglobinopathies among women attending a tertiary care center in Central Uttar Pradesh. Methods A prospective observational study was conducted among women aged 15-49 years attending antenatal and outpatient services at a tertiary care hospital in Kanpur from 3 February 2025 to 2 February 2026. A total of 5,285 participants were screened. Those with abnormal or suggestive findings underwent further evaluation using complete blood count parameters and high-performance liquid chromatography. Diagnostic categories and hematological parameters were compared using appropriate statistical tests. Results Hemoglobinopathy was identified in 206 of 5,285 participants, giving an overall prevalence of 3.89%. Among the 207 participants with sufficient diagnostic information, beta-thalassemia trait was the most common finding (185; 89.4%), followed by hemoglobin E trait (20; 9.7%) and delta-beta-thalassemia trait (1; 0.5%). The prevalence of beta-thalassemia trait among the screened population was 3.5%. Significant differences were observed in red cell distribution width, hemoglobin, hemoglobin A, hemoglobin A2, and fetal hemoglobin (all p<0.001), while mean corpuscular volume and mean corpuscular hemoglobin did not differ significantly. Anemia severity also differed significantly (p=0.017). Conclusion Hemoglobinopathies were identified in a notable proportion of women screened, with beta-thalassemia trait being the predominant finding. These findings highlight the importance of carrier screening among women of reproductive age. The hospital-based design should be considered when interpreting the prevalence estimates.

articles.title: A proposed psychometabolic endotype of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: bidirectional interplay between psychological distress, eating dysfunction, sleep disruption, chronic stress, and metabolic deterioration.
articles.authors: Li H, Yin T, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome was renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) in 2026 to better represent its multisystem biology. Psychological distress, eating dysregulation, sleep disturbance, and metabolic dysfunction frequently coexist, yet clinical care and research commonly treat them as parallel comorbidities.
OBJECTIVE: To define the proposed psychometabolic construct operationally; position it relative to conventional phenotypes and data-driven clusters; and grade evidence for association, temporal prediction, causation, and treatment response across psychological, behavioral, sleep-stress, neuroendocrine, and metabolic pathways.
METHODS: We conducted a targeted narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through 15 September 2026. Seven structured topic blocks returned 1,278 records, 1,009 unique identifiers after PubMed identifier (PMID)-based deduplication, and 1,008 retrievable article records for title/abstract screening. Guidelines, systematic reviews, longitudinal or causal studies, trials, and informative human mechanistic studies were prioritized; general-population and preclinical evidence was used only when its indirectness was explicit.
EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: Depression and anxiety, body-image concerns, binge- and bulimia-spectrum symptoms, poor sleep, and obstructive sleep apnea are reported more often in PMOS than in comparison populations, but most estimates are cross-sectional and heterogeneous. One tertiary cohort found that baseline depression and/or anxiety history predicted incident metabolic syndrome over a median seven years (adjusted hazard ratio 1.45, 95% confidence interval 1.02-2.06); this supports prognostic enrichment, not causality. General-population longitudinal and genetic studies support reciprocal depression-metabolic relationships, whereas PMOS-specific causal evidence is inconsistent. Plausible links include insulin-androgen-adipose interactions, neuroactive steroid signaling, ovarian sympathetic input, sleep fragmentation, stress and autonomic regulation, reward-related eating, treatment exposure, stigma, and social context. None validates a discrete endotype.
CONCLUSIONS: We define a candidate psychometabolic endotype as a cross-cutting, mechanistically coupled pattern that may occur within any conventional PMOS phenotype. Clinical co-occurrence is only an entry profile; endotype status requires replicated longitudinal coupling, incremental prognostic value, interpretable transitions,…

articles.title: Blood-based inflammatory biomarkers in ovarian cancer: addressing the challenge of early detection, metastasis, and prognostic stratification.
articles.authors: Obeagu EI
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains a major cause of gynaecological cancer mortality, largely because early disease is frequently asymptomatic and reliable population-based screening remains unavailable. Systemic inflammation is increasingly recognised as an important component of ovarian cancer biology, linking tumour progression, immune dysregulation, angiogenesis, metastasis and treatment resistance. This narrative review critically evaluates blood-based inflammatory biomarkers, including C-reactive protein, interleukin-6, interleukin-8, tumour necrosis factor-α, fibrinogen, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) and pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), across early detection, metastatic assessment, treatment decision-making and prognostic stratification. Available evidence indicates that elevated inflammatory indices are consistently associated with advanced disease and adverse outcomes, although substantial heterogeneity exists in biomarker thresholds, populations, timing of measurement and analytical approaches. Recent evidence also suggests that preoperative NLR and SII may contribute to treatment selection, including neoadjuvant chemotherapy, although prognostic independence is not consistently demonstrated. Importantly, inflammatory biomarkers lack sufficient specificity for standalone ovarian cancer screening and should not replace CA-125, HE4, imaging or histopathological assessment. Their greatest clinical potential lies in multimarker models integrating systemic inflammatory, tumour-specific, molecular and clinical variables. Future research should prioritise prospective multicentre validation, standardised thresholds, longitudinal assessment and clinically interpretable prediction models to determine whether inflammatory profiling can advance precision risk stratification and treatment selection in ovarian cancer.

articles.title: The role of maternal gut microbiota in prenatal depression and offspring neurodevelopment.
articles.authors: Jia Q, Diao C, Liu S et al.
articles.abstract: Prenatal depression is a prevalent complication during pregnancy that not only adversely affects maternal mental health and elevates the risk of postpartum depression but also has enduring implications for offspring development. Alterations in the host metabolome and gut microbiome have been linked to the onset and progression of depression; however, the biological mechanisms underlying the association between maternal mood disorders and fetal brain development remain inadequately understood. Recent studies have associated prenatal depression and psychological stress with alterations in the maternal gut microbiota, microbial metabolism, and immune signaling. However, most human evidence remains observational, and it remains unclear whether these microbial alterations precede depressive symptoms, arise as a consequence of depression or psychological stress, or act as intermediate factors within the maternal gut-brain axis. These findings offer novel strategies for the prevention and treatment of threats to maternal-fetal health. This article systematically reviews recent advancements in research concerning the "microbiota-gut-brain" axis in the context of maternal-fetal health. It investigates the roles and mechanisms of gut microbiota through preclinical and clinical studies, assesses the feasibility of potential therapeutic strategies, and suggests directions for future research. The aim is to provide a theoretical foundation for interventions targeting maternal-fetal health in cases of prenatal depression.

articles.title: Cost-Utility and Clinical Impact of a Multicomponent Maternal Safety and High-Dependency Care Model in Three Colombian Caribbean Hospitals: A Before-and-After Study.
articles.authors: Rojas-Suárez J, Durán C, Lora N et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Obstetric high-dependency units may improve rescue care when embedded within broader maternal safety strategies. Objective: To evaluate a multi-component maternal safety and technological strengthening model, including obstetric high-dependency capacity, across three Colombian Caribbean institutions with different governance models. Methods: We conducted a multisite before-and-after implementation evaluation within a Ministry-funded maternal safety project. The model was implemented in one private clinic and two public hospitals in La Guajira and Bolívar, Colombia, with staggered implementation and varying data maturity. Data sources included billing records, administrative databases, and monthly quality indicators. Costs, severe maternal morbidity indicators, and longitudinal quality metrics were analysed by institutional implementation window. Pandemic-period variation from 2018 to 2023 was treated descriptively. Interrupted time series analyses were performed where post-implementation data allowed. Findings: Implementation was associated with heterogeneous but generally favourable patterns. At Clínica CEDES, costs increased after implementation, while intensive care utilisation and several severe maternal morbidity indicators declined. At ESE Hospital San José de Maicao, mature post-implementation economic and conventional pre/post-clinical comparisons were unavailable; however, interrupted time series analyses showed favourable changes in longitudinal quality indicators, including reductions in weighted adverse outcome score (WAOS) level (β = -8.30, P = 0.0016) and slope (β = -1.20, P = 0.0064), adverse outcome index (AOI) level (β = -1.13, P = 0.0032), and severity index (SI) slope (β = -0.27, P = 0.030). ESE Hospital La Divina Misericordia showed mixed early clinical signals and descriptive quality improvement, but follow-up was limited. Conclusions: A multi-component maternal safety model including obstetric high-dependency capacity may improve maternal care in high-risk settings, although effects vary by institutional context. High-dependency units appear most effective as part of an integrated rescue system rather than isolated infrastructure.

articles.title: Fertility in Ethiopia: factors associated with the number of live births -a survey-adjusted poisson regression analysis of the 2019 ethiopian mini demographic and health survey.
articles.authors: Mesfin MD, Wondu AY, Galgalo DA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fertility is a key demographic and public health phenomenon reflecting actual childbearing within a population. It can be characterized using several measures, including total fertility rate, age-specific fertility rates, children ever born, and the number of births occurring within a defined reference period. These measures capture different dimensions of reproductive experience and are associated with a complex interplay of socioeconomic, demographic, cultural, biological, and policy-related factors.
METHODS: By dividing the nine regions into urban and rural categories, twenty-one sampling strata were created. The survey employed a two-stage stratified cluster sampling design. In the first stage, 305 enumeration areas (EAs) were selected from the national sampling frame using probability proportional to size. A total of 8,885 women were included in the descriptive analysis, while the primary multivariable analysis was restricted to 6,585 ever-married/partnered women. A survey-adjusted Poisson regression model was used to examine associations between explanatory variables and the number of live births during the five years preceding the survey. Statistical significance was assessed using a two-sided p-value of <0.05.
RESULT AND CONCLUSION: The mean age of the participants was 27.6 years. More than four-fifths of women had either no formal education (40.4%) or primary education (41.7%). Compared with women aged 15-19 years, the expected number of recent live births was higher among women aged 20-24 years (aIRR = 2.129, 95% CI: 1.759-2.577). Women residing in Amhara had a lower expected number of recent live births than women residing in Tigray (aIRR = 0.765, 95% CI: 0.658-0.890). Lower expected counts were also observed in Addis Ababa (aIRR = 0.818, 95% CI: 0.684-0.979) and Dire Dawa (aIRR = 0.792, 95% CI: 0.659-0.952). An inverse association was observed between household wealth and recent live-birth counts. These findings highlight the multifactorial nature of recent live births in Ethiopia and suggest that fertility patterns are associated with a combination of individual, household, and contextual factors. These insights may help inform evidence-based reproductive health and family planning policies tailored to the Ethiopian context.

articles.title: Plasticity and immune marker profiling of tumour- and ascites-derived microtumours in serous ovarian cancer: relevance for short-term culture models.
articles.authors: Hell L, Ding Y, Pellens C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Serous ovarian cancer (SOC) is characterized by tumour heterogeneity, cellular plasticity, and immune suppression, contributing to limited therapeutic responses. Understanding tumour -immune dynamics at the cellular level is essential for developing personalized treatment strategies.
METHODS: We established a patient-derived microtumour (MT) platform from solid tumour tissue and malignant ascites of 18 treatment-naïve SOC patients. Using multiparametric flow cytometry, we analysed plasticity-associated markers (CD10, CD24, CD44, CD90, CD133), immunoregulatory molecules (PD-L1, PVR, PVRL2, CD47, Calreticulin, CD39, CD73), and antigen presentation molecules (HLA-A/B/C, HLA-DR/DP/DQ) during short-term culture.
RESULTS: Plasticity-associated marker expression was largely conserved across compartments, with substantial interpatient heterogeneity and only modest differences in an exploratory composite plasticity score. Compared with tumour-derived MTs, ascites-derived MTs exhibited significantly higher calreticulin expression and lower expression of the ectonucleotidase CD39. Short-term culture induced CD44 upregulation and CD90 downregulation as well as dynamic modulation of immune markers, such as increased PVR and PVRL2 expression. HLA expression showed substantial interindividual heterogeneity rather than clear compartment-specific differences. Co-expression analyses revealed associations between plasticity-associated and immunoregulatory features, such as CD10/CD24 with PD-L1 and CD47. Finally, exploratory autologous co-cultures demonstrated the feasibility of combining patient-derived MTs with matched immune cells. Two of five samples showed moderate responses to anti-PD-L1 and anti-TIGIT, reflected by increased granzyme B expression and accompanied by compensatory changes in TIGIT and PD-L1 expression.
DISCUSSION: Taken together, these findings indicate an association between tumour cell plasticity and an immune-evasive phenotype in ovarian cancer and support patient-derived MTs as an exploratory short-term platform for capturing patient-specific tumour -immune interactions, while highlighting dynamic immune checkpoint molecule expression during cultivation.

articles.title: Lived experiences of obstetric anal sphincter injury among women from ethnically diverse backgrounds in the UK: a qualitative study.
articles.authors: Olakotan O, Lim JNW, Bhavsar M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) is a severe childbirth-related injury that can have significant physical, psychological and social consequences, with potentially lasting effects on women's quality of life. Understanding the lived experiences of ethnic minority women affected by OASI is important for improving the care and support provided to them.
AIM: This study explores the lived experiences of ethnic minority women with OASI in Leicester, UK, with a focus on their childbirth experiences, healthcare challenges, and the broader impact on their overall well-being.
METHODOLOGY: A focus group discussion (FGD) was held virtually with underrepresented women from Leicester who had experienced OASI in the past one to five years. The discussion was recorded and transcribed. Invitations to participate in the study were sent out via email through the local maternity and neonatal voices partnership in Leicester, UK. The data were analysed using the six-step thematic analysis approach by Braun and Clarke.
RESULTS: Ten women from underrepresented groups identified several key themes such as childbirth experiences, complications and reflection, societal influence and childbirth choices, cultural silence, stigmatization, and mental health issues. The women reported feeling uninformed and unprepared about possible complications and risks such as third and fourth-degree tears, resulting in traumatic birthing experiences, aggravated by inadequate healthcare communication and support from healthcare providers.
CONCLUSION: There is the need for future research to integrate physical, physiological and mental health support, as well as sustained follow-up into OASIS care bundle. This will essentially support women's health and well-being during the perinatal period.

articles.title: Physical activity and structured exercise patterns in perimenopausal women: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Duaso-Iriarte A, Piedrafita E, Sarría A et al.
articles.abstract: Perimenopause is a critical midlife transition within women's aging, with implications for cardiometabolic, musculoskeletal, functional, and psychosocial health. Although physical activity and structured exercise are relevant components of healthy aging, evidence remains limited regarding how perimenopausal women organize their real-world exercise behavior, including exercise modalities and supervision. This cross-sectional study used a primarily descriptive approach to characterize physical activity habits and exercise patterns in perimenopausal women. Specifically, weekly physical activity level and intensity, exercise modalities, reported training time, and supervision status were examined, together with secondary exploratory comparisons across physical activity categories and according to selected sociodemographic and reproductive variables. An anonymous online questionnaire was completed by 121 women; 57 met the eligibility criteria, and 51 were included in the final analyses after exclusion of responses that did not allow calculation of total metabolic equivalent minutes per week (MET·min/week). Weekly physical activity was assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form. Mean total physical activity was 2258.1 ± 1447.3 MET·min/week. Moderate and high physical activity levels predominated, accounting for 43.1% and 39.2% of participants, respectively, whereas 17.6% were classified as having low physical activity. Endurance training (66.7%) and strength training (62.7%) were the most frequently reported exercise modalities, while sport-based activities were less common (35.3%). Endurance and strength training were reported more frequently in the higher physical activity categories. No statistically significant differences in total physical activity were identified according to the sociodemographic and reproductive variables examined, although a secondary exploratory comparison showed greater reported weekly strength training time among women aged 50 years or older than among younger participants. Participants reporting fully or partially supervised exercise showed descriptively higher total physical activity and more frequent participation in the exercise modalities examined, although the inferential comparisons of total physical activity and reported training time were not statistically significant. These findings provide a descriptive account of heterogeneous physical activity and exercise patterns in the sample examined.…

articles.title: Diagnostic approaches for tubal factor infertility: a systematic review of HSG, HyCoSy, HyFoSy, and laparoscopy.
articles.authors: Alenova A, Kauysheva A, Korkan A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tubal pathology remains a major cause of female infertility, making accurate assessment of tubal patency and morphology important for clinical decision-making. Several diagnostic approaches are available, including hysterosalpingography (HSG), hysterosalpingo-contrast sonography (HyCoSy), hysterosalpingo-foam sonography (HyFoSy), and laparoscopy with chromopertubation. This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on their diagnostic performance, clinical applicability, and role in contemporary diagnostic pathways.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched for studies published between January 2015 and March 2026. Studies evaluating methods for tubal patency or morphological assessment in women undergoing infertility investigation were considered. A total of 21 studies were included. Owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, particularly differences in study populations, diagnostic thresholds, and reference standards, the findings were synthesized qualitatively.
RESULTS: HSG generally demonstrated high sensitivity but variable specificity, limiting its reliability for confirming tubal occlusion. HyCoSy showed potentially useful diagnostic performance as a non-invasive screening method, although estimates varied across studies. Several studies reported favorable specificity, predictive values, and agreement measures for HyFoSy, together with improved patient tolerability; however, findings were not uniform and were influenced by methodological heterogeneity and differences in reference standards. Laparoscopy with chromopertubation remained the reference standard for assessing tubal patency and identifying concomitant pelvic pathology, although its invasive nature limits its routine use.
DISCUSSION: Current evidence supports a stepwise approach to tubal assessment in which less invasive methods may be used initially, with confirmatory or invasive techniques reserved for selected cases. Such an approach may improve diagnostic confidence while reducing unnecessary procedural burden and risks. Further well-designed comparative studies using standardized reference standards and outcome definitions are needed to clarify the relative diagnostic value of available techniques.

articles.title: Uterine-cavity Lactobacillus relative abundance and endometrial polyp recurrence after hysteroscopic polypectomy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Zheng T, Guo C, Zhou Z
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial polyps are among the most common benign uterine lesions, yet their recurrence after hysteroscopic polypectomy remains poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests that uterine-cavity microbial composition may be related to endometrial inflammation and tissue biology. However, the association between uterine microbiome composition and polyp recurrence has not been systematically investigated.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 288 women who underwent hysteroscopic polypectomy between January 2021 and June 2024. Uterine cavity fluid was collected intraoperatively for 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing (V3-V4 region). Patients were classified into Lactobacillus-Dominant (LD, n = 156) and Lactobacillus-Non-Dominant (LND, n = 132) groups based on Lactobacillus relative abundance ≥70%. The primary outcome was endometrial polyp recurrence confirmed by hysteroscopy at 12 months. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression identified independent predictors of recurrence.
RESULTS: The 12-month recurrence rate was higher in the LND group than in the LD group (31.8% vs. 14.1%, p < 0.001). LND samples had higher relative abundances of Gardnerella (15.3%), Prevotella (12.1%), and Streptococcus (8.7%), higher Shannon diversity (3.87 ± 0.98 vs. 1.34 ± 0.52, p < 0.001), and higher serum IL-6 and CRP levels. In the multivariable Cox model, LND status remained associated with recurrence (adjusted HR 2.41; 95% CI 1.48-3.93; p = 0.001). BMI ≥ 28 kg/m2, polyp size ≥15 mm, multiplicity, and postoperative hormonal therapy were also associated with recurrence; the hormonal-therapy estimate indicated lower recurrence (adjusted HR 0.48). These estimates are observational and may be affected by residual confounding.
CONCLUSION: Lactobacillus-non-dominant uterine-cavity microbiome status was associated with higher 12-month endometrial polyp recurrence after hysteroscopic polypectomy after adjustment for measured clinical factors. These findings support further evaluation of uterine microbiome profiles as potential risk-stratification markers, but they do not establish causality or justify routine antimicrobial or microbiome-guided treatment.

articles.title: Efficacy of a standardized cranberry supplement on overactive bladder symptoms and urobiome alterations in young women: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: Ito A, Akagawa S, Akagawa Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Urobiome dysbiosis has been implicated in the pathogenesis of overactive bladder (OAB). In this study, the efficacy of a cranberry supplement for OAB symptoms was investigated, and concurrent urobiome alterations were evaluated in young women.
METHODS: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial enrolled 26 women (median age, 23 years) with OAB (Overactive Bladder Symptom Score [OABSS] ≥ 3), who received either a cranberry supplement (36 mg proanthocyanidins per day) or placebo for 4 weeks. Clinical efficacy was assessed using the OABSS reduction rate, and urobiome composition was evaluated by 16S rRNA gene sequencing.
RESULTS: Twenty-five participants were included in the analysis. At 4 weeks, the OABSS reduction rate was greater in the cranberry group than in the placebo group (median, 66.7% vs. 40.0%; p = 0.039). At baseline, the urobiome was dominated by Lactobacillus (median relative abundance, 64.2%). After cranberry supplementation, the relative abundance of Lactobacillus decreased within the cranberry group (median change, -4.39%; p = 0.027; q = 0.096). No compositional changes were observed in the placebo group.
CONCLUSIONS: Cranberry supplementation was associated with greater improvement in OAB symptoms than was observed with placebo in young women, while a decrease in Lactobacillus relative abundance was observed within the cranberry group. Given the small sample size of this exploratory pilot trial and the limited species-level resolution of 16S rRNA sequencing, these concurrent findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrant further investigation.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.umin.ac.jp/ctr/, identifier UMIN000057544.

articles.title: Depression as a multidimensional host factor and oncologic outcomes in breast and gynecologic cancers: A narrative review.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Cuello MA, Ibañez C, Bustos M et al.
articles.abstract: Depressive disorders and clinically significant depressive symptoms are common in women with breast and gynecologic cancers, although prevalence estimates range from approximately 12% to more than 50% depending on instrument, threshold, timing, and setting. This narrative review, structured according to SANRA criteria, examines evidence on depression and oncologic outcomes in breast and gynecologic cancers and grades each claim by type and strength of evidence. Meta-analyses of observational studies consistently associate depression with recurrence and with cancer-specific and all-cause mortality (pooled relative risks of approximately 1.2-1.3 in breast cancer), and with lower adherence to adjuvant endocrine therapy and radiotherapy. These are prognostic associations; residual confounding by stage, symptom burden, comorbidity, socioeconomic disadvantage, and access to care, and reverse causation, cannot be excluded. Neuroendocrine, inflammatory, and immune mechanisms are best characterized in ovarian cancer, largely in preclinical models and often in relation to chronic stress rather than clinical depression, and whether depression modifies the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in gynecologic cancers has not been studied. No adequately powered trial has tested whether treating depression improves cancer outcomes; available data come from broader psychosocial interventions and secondary analyses. We propose the Women's Biobehavioral Oncology Framework, an unvalidated conceptual model distinguishing depression as a prognostic marker, a possible causal contributor, and a treatment target, and a prioritized research agenda. Screening and treatment of depression are justified on clinical grounds; its use for risk stratification or treatment selection requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Respectful maternity care: A multinational survey of maternity care providers by the World Association of Trainees in Obstetrics and Gynecology.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Ubom AE, Mughal M, Portilla FJR et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates maternity care providers' knowledge, practice, and perspectives on respectful maternity care (RMC).
METHODS: A global cross-sectional online survey on RMC was conducted by the World Association of Trainees in Obstetrics and Gynecology (WATOG).
RESULTS: A total of 458 maternity care providers from 48 countries across six global regions participated in the study. One in five providers (93, 20.3%) had never heard of RMC, and nearly half (223, 48.7%) had received no formal RMC training. Only 74 (16.2%) demonstrated good knowledge of the seven categories of maternal disrespect and abuse. There was no association between RMC knowledge and practice (P = 0.066). Despite 429 (93.7%) of respondents agreeing that RMC could improve feto-maternal outcomes, self-reported practices inconsistent with RMC were common, including verbal abuse (285, 62.2%), detention for unpaid bills and non-confidential care (262, 57.2%), discrimination (203, 44.3%), abandonment/denial of care (187, 40.8%), and physical abuse (119, 26.0%). The most frequently reported barriers to RMC implementation were time constraints owing to staff and resource shortages (361, 78.8%), inadequate training (356, 77.7%), lack of sanctions for disrespectful care (239, 52.2%), and restrictive cultural and religious norms (203, 44.3%).
CONCLUSION: There are critical gaps in maternity care providers' knowledge and practice of RMC, despite widespread recognition of its importance for good feto-maternal outcomes. Institutionalized RMC education, adequate staffing and resources, strengthened institutional accountability and reporting mechanisms, and workplace cultures that prioritize patient dignity and autonomy are critical steps toward ensuring RMC for all women.

articles.title: Evaluation of collection efficiency and safety of a precise distention fluid collection device compared to traditional devices in hysteroscopic surgery.
articles.authors: Ying Y, Lan H
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to validate the effectiveness of this device in collecting distension fluid during hysteroscopic surgery, providing a more reliable tool for monitoring fluid outflow.
METHODS: A total of 164 patients scheduled for elective hysteroscopy were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the precision collection group or the control group. The precision collection group utilized a precision distension fluid collection device for hysteroscopic distension fluid collection, while the control group used a conventional collection device. The primary outcome was the hysteroscopic distension fluid collection rate. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of adverse events, operating room cleaning time, and satisfaction levels of surgeons, nurses, and operating room support staff.
RESULTS: There were no significant differences in baseline patient characteristics or surgical types between the two groups. Compared to the conventional fluid collection device, the precision distension fluid collection device significantly improved the hysteroscopic distension fluid collection rate (95% vs. 48%, P < 0.001) and reduced the operating room turnover time for staff (4.1 min vs. 6.4 min, P < 0.001), while also substantially increasing surgical team satisfaction.
CONCLUSION: The precision distension fluid collection device effectively enhances the collection rate of hysteroscopic distension fluid, reduces risks associated with improper fluid management, shortens operating room turnover time, and improves the satisfaction of the surgical team.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn, identifier ChiCTR2500101460.

articles.title: Development and validation of interpretable machine learning models for predicting cumulative live birth rates in assisted reproductive technology: a SHAP-based analysis.
articles.authors: Fu X, Qin Y, Huang Q et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate interpretable machine-learning models predicting cumulative live birth rate (CLBR) in ART patients.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort (January 2019-June 2024), 7,773 oocyte retrieval cycles were analysed. XGBoost gain ranking, applied to all screened cycles with native handling of missing values, selected eight predictors that were complete in every cycle, so no cycle was excluded for missing data. Six algorithms were compared by stratified 10-fold cross-validation (n=5,441) and an independent test set (n=2,332). We further performed temporal validation (2019-2022 vs 2023-2024), benchmarked against a McLernon-style logistic regression and against a gradient-boosting model restricted to pre-treatment variables, and assessed age-stratified calibration, discrimination (AUC), decision-curve analysis (DCA), and SHAP interpretability.
RESULTS: Gradient boosting showed the best discrimination on the random-split test set (AUC 0.762; 95% CI, 0.743-0.781; Brier 0.185). Under temporal validation, performance remained robust (AUC 0.712; 95% CI, 0.686-0.737). The full model significantly exceeded the logistic-regression benchmark (0.761 vs 0.691; DeLong p<0.0001; NRI 0.629, 95% CI 0.550-0.712; IDI 0.105, 95% CI 0.090-0.121). However, a gradient-boosting model restricted to the same pre-treatment variables did not outperform that benchmark (0.693 vs 0.691; p=0.72), indicating that the gain was attributable to the inclusion of embryological information rather than to the learning algorithm itself. DCA demonstrated positive net benefit across thresholds 0.01-0.94. SHAP identified female age (mean |SHAP| 0.494) and embryo quality (0.451) as dominant predictors, with an inflection at 38-40 years.
CONCLUSIONS: This interpretable framework delivers robust, well-calibrated CLBR prediction that remains stable under temporal validation while preserving transparency via SHAP. Its advantage over an established pre-treatment benchmark derives from incorporating embryological information rather than from the machine learning algorithm: precise estimation of cumulative live birth requires embryological data that become available only after oocyte retrieval and embryo development, rather than depending on which algorithm is used to model that information.

articles.title: Astragaloside IV attenuates ferroptosis-related testicular injury in rats with experimental varicocele.
articles.authors: Gao B, Liu S, Sun M et al.
articles.abstract: Varicocele is an important correctable cause of male infertility. Oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation contribute to the associated testicular injury, but the role of ferroptosis remains controversial. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV), a quality-control metabolite of Astragali radix, has antioxidant activity and can modulate ferroptosis-related processes, yet its effect in varicocele is unclear. This study evaluated whether AS-IV attenuates testicular injury in experimental varicocele and examined ferroptosis-related mechanisms. A Sprague-Dawley rat model was established by partial ligation of the left renal vein and treated with oral AS-IV; Ferrostatin-1 served as a pharmacological comparator. Label-free proteomics, histopathology, biochemical assays and targeted molecular analyses were combined with a TM4 Sertoli-cell model of RSL3-induced injury. AS-IV lessened tubular injury and improved Johnsen scores in a dose-related manner, reduced testicular Fe2+, ROS and MDA, and raised the GSH/GSSG ratio. Proteomics showed partial reversal of lipid-metabolism and ferroptosis-related enrichment after AS-IV. These changes were accompanied by recovery of androgen receptor (AR) and MBOAT2. In TM4 cells, AS-IV improved viability and lowered C11-BODIPY oxidation after RSL3; enzalutamide weakened the effects of AS-IV on lipid peroxidation and MBOAT2 and only partly reduced the viability rescue. The findings provide experimental evidence that AS-IV ameliorates varicocele-related testicular injury and that AR/MBOAT2-related signalling may participate.

articles.title: Global, regional and national cancer burden and trends of middle-aged and older populations: a GBD 2021-based analysis, prediction and prevention.
articles.authors: Sun R, Shi F, Tang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Middle-aged and older adults (MAOs; defined as individuals aged ≥40 years) account for the global cancer burden, contributing to 70-80% of cases. Characterizing cancer profiles in this demographic is essential for developing targeted prevention and treatment strategies to mitigate global impacts.
METHODS: Using Global Burden of Diseases (GBD) 2021 data, we analyzed incidence, prevalence, mortality and Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) for 31 cancers among MAOs (aged≥40) across 204 countries/21 regions(1990-2021). Trends were quantified via Joinpoint regression, and autoregressive integrated moving-average (ARIMA) models projected the burden through 2035. Risk attribution utilized population attributable fractions across Socio-demographic Index (SDI) quintiles. An order-independent Shapley decomposition attributed projected cancer incidence changes during 2021-2035 to population growth, aging, and age-specific incidence rate shifts.
RESULTS: In 2021, MAOs accounted for 48,804,114 incident cases and 9,434,210 deaths. Females exhibited a 1.14-fold higher age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) than males, yet males had a higher age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR). Projections suggested a continued rise in cancer burden through 2035. Peak incidence occurred in ages 60-69 and the highest mortality in ages 70-79. Breast cancer was the main cancer in females; tracheal/bronchus/lung cancer in males. Tracheal/bronchus/lung cancer dominated mortality across all groups except middle-aged women (breast cancer). High-SDI regions bore the greatest burden, characterized by tracheal/bronchus/lung and colorectal cancers, while low-SDI regions shifted toward breast, cervical and stomach cancer. Risk factor analysis from 2010-2021 revealed rising metabolic risks, with high body mass index (BMI) and fasting plasma glucose-attributable DALYs increasing by 12.39% and 11.36% respectively, especially in high-SDI regions. Conversely, while most behavioral risks declined, smoking remained the leading risk factor, contributing over 60% to lung cancer DALYs. In low-SDI regions, behavioral drivers such as unsafe sex (accounting for >90% of cervical cancer risk) and air pollution remained the dominant persistent risks.
DISCUSSION: This study, the first focusing on MAOs' global cancer burden, reveals heterogeneous patterns by age, gender, and SDI. Lung cancer was the leading cause of death (smoking as main risk). Metabolic risks rose in high-SDI regions, behavioral…

articles.title: Laparoscopic para-aortic and pelvic lymphadenectomy before chemoradiotherapy was not associated with improved survival in patients with FIGO stage IIB-IIIC cervical cancer: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.authors: Zhang Q, Li L, Li X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Currently, whether surgical staging can confer a survival benefit in patients with cervical cancer remains controversial, and its efficacy is similarly uncertain across different subgroups. The primary aim of this study was to assess the efficacy of laparoscopic para-aortic and pelvic lymphadenectomy prior to chemoradiotherapy in patients with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage IIB-IIIC cervical cancer. The secondary aim was to identify the main prognostic factors.
METHODS: A total of 396 patients were included in this retrospective study, 97 patients who underwent laparoscopic para-aortic and pelvic lymphadenectomy before chemoradiotherapy comprised the surgical staging group, and 299 patients who received chemoradiotherapy alone comprised the clinical staging group. Kaplan-Meier and log-rank methods were used to construct and compare progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) curves, respectively. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to identify independent prognostic factors.
RESULTS: There were no statistically significant differences in PFS (p = 0.187) or OS (p = 0.490) between the two groups. The estimated 5-year PFS rates were 67.0% (95%CI, 56.9%-75.7%) in the surgical staging group and 73.6% (95%CI, 67.4%-78.7%) in the clinical staging group. The corresponding 5-year OS rates were 76.3% (95%CI, 66.0%-83.9%) and 78.6% (95%CI, 72.7%-83.2%), respectively. Subgroup analysis stratified by imaging lymph node status demonstrated comparable survival outcomes. Multivariate analysis identified adenocarcinoma, pelvic wall involvement, and imaging-positive lymph nodes as independent risk factors for PFS; adenocarcinoma, adenosquamous carcinoma, pelvic wall involvement, and imaging-positive lymph nodes were independent predictors of OS.
CONCLUSIONS: Laparoscopic para-aortic and pelvic lymphadenectomy before chemoradiotherapy was not associated with improved PFS or OS in this retrospective cohort, Tumor histology, pelvic wall involvement, and imaging-positive lymph nodes were the main prognostic factors.

articles.title: The comparison between short-term fertilization and conventional fertilization in in vitro fertilization treatment: a propensity score matching study.
articles.authors: Han D, Kong X, Liu J et al.
articles.abstract: Short-term IVF (S-IVF) is a fertilization approach to co-incubate the sperm and oocyte for a short duration and denude the cumulus cells afterwards. The S-IVF combined with early rescue intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) strategy can reduce the occurrence of both total fertilization failure (TFF) and the lower fertilization rate (<30%). However, there is still no consensus regarding the use of S-IVF. This study aimed to compare short-term in vitro fertilization (S-IVF) with conventional in vitro fertilization (C-IVF) in terms of fertilization, embryo developmental potential, and clinical outcomes. We used propensity score matching (PSM) to construct a 1:5 cohort of S-IVF and C-IVF cycles and compared fertilization, embryo developmental potential, and clinical outcomes between the two groups. We screened 68 S-IVF and 340 C-IVF patients (each in their first ART cycle-so cycle and patient numbers are identical) by baseline characteristics. The primary outcome was the fertilization rate, and the secondary outcomes were the pregnancy rate and abortion rate in cohort. The results showed that the C-IVF group had a higher fertilization rate [84% vs. 78%, p < 0.05], two-pronucleus (2PN) rate [67% vs. 60%, p < 0.05], and one-pronucleus (1PN) rate [5% vs. 3%, p < 0.05] compared with the S-IVF group. Furthermore, in the C-IVF group, the zero-pronucleus (0PN) rate was lower than in the S-IVF group (11% vs. 20%, mean difference -9 percentage points, 95% CI -12.5 to -5.5, p < 0.001). The good-quality blastocyst rate was numerically higher in the C-IVF group than in the S-IVF group, but the difference was not statistically significant. There was no significant difference in pregnancy rate or abortion rate in cohort between the two groups (early abortion rate among clinical pregnancies: 15.1% [14/93] in C-IVF versus 13.0% [3/23] in S-IVF, p = 1.000). In conclusion, C-IVF had a higher fertilization rate, 2PN rate, and 1PN rate but a lower 0PN rate compared with S-IVF, while there was no difference in embryo development and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: The Sakinah method-targeted education of traditional midwives supplemented with clean birth kits.
articles.authors: Malick SM, Sukhera A, Malick S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pakistan continues to experience high maternal and neonatal mortality. Mortality is concentrated in rural, underserved populations where home birth is common and access to skilled care is limited.
OBJECTIVE: We set out to evaluate the impact of a community-delivered intervention combining clean birth kits (CBKs) with structured midwifery training on maternal and neonatal outcomes in rural Pakistan.
STUDY DESIGN: This was conducted as a pragmatic, community-based study in rural Punjab, beginning in September 2022 in Sillanwali and expanding to eight additional deprived sites. The intervention combined competency-based midwifery training with CBKs containing infection and hemorrhage prevention components, including misoprostol. Maternal and neonatal outcomes were prospectively recorded via a bespoke digital platform; paper forms were used in low-connectivity areas and later digitized. Implementation was monitored through supervision and record verification. The data was verified independently through structured postpartum follow-up.
RESULTS: In 5327 births, there were no maternal deaths. Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) of 500 to 1000 mL was seen in 8.2%, and >1000 mL in 0.51% of pregnancies. Gestation at birth was at >37 weeks in 83.4%, with late preterm (35-36 weeks) accounting for 14.9%. There were 5245 (98.5%) live births, with 82 stillbirths (15.4/1000) and 113 neonatal deaths (21.2/1000), with a perinatal mortality rate of 36.6 per 1000. Perinatal loss was largely associated with prematurity. Compared with national outcomes (maternal mortality ratio [MMR] 155-160/100,000; stillbirth 27-28/1000; neonatal mortality 38-39/1000), the intervention cohort demonstrated lower maternal and perinatal mortality (P<.05 for MMR, P<.001 for neonatal mortality rate). PPH incidence (8.8%) was comparable to national levels (∼9%-11%).
CONCLUSION: A community-embedded package combining CBKs with structured midwifery training was associated with zero maternal deaths and reduced perinatal mortality, suggesting a cost-effective scalable strategy to improve outcomes and reduce inequities in high-risk low-resource and home-birth settings. This project embedded misoprostol within CBKs and transitioned comprehensively from abandoning poly-filament threads as cord ties to sterile clamps with early adoption of chlorhexidine. An almost 50% reduction in neonatal mortality versus national estimates underscores the effectiveness of an integrated, evidence-based package…

articles.title: Therapeutic role of granulocyte-colony stimulating factor and aspirin in unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss: a retrospective study.
articles.authors: Huang X, Luo Q, Luo Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL), the loss of two or more clinically confirmed pregnancies, is observed in approximately 1%-5% of couples trying to conceive. Immune dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a contributing factor. This study evaluated pregnancy outcomes among women with unexplained RPL treated with combined recombinant human granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (rhG-CSF) and low-dose aspirin, while acknowledging that the evidence base for rhG-CSF in unexplained RPL remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 300 women aged 18-45 years with at least two consecutive unexplained pregnancy losses were treated with subcutaneous rhG-CSF and low-dose aspirin. Eligible women had documented ovulation, no major uterine abnormality, and no male-factor infertility. Source records were reviewed for mode of conception; all 300 index pregnancies were documented as spontaneous conceptions, and no pregnancies achieved by assisted reproductive technology (ART) were included. rhG-CSF was initiated on the sixth day after ovulation and continued until menstruation or completion of 9 gestational weeks; aspirin 75 mg/day was initiated at the same post-ovulatory time point and continued until 36 gestational weeks unless pregnancy loss or a safety indication required discontinuation. Clinical pregnancy, live birth, miscarriage, stillbirth, neonatal outcomes, and adverse events were assessed. Maternal age was treated as a clinically relevant covariate. Analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS version 27.
RESULTS: Live birth at or after 20 weeks of gestation occurred in 211/300 women (70.3%) according to the institutional obstetric registry definition used in the source records. All index pregnancies were verified as spontaneous conceptions, with no ART pregnancies included. Clinical pregnancy, defined as an intrauterine gestational sac with fetal cardiac activity at 6-7 gestational weeks, was observed in 99.3% of participants. In the age-adjusted model, a higher pretreatment systolic/diastolic ratio remained associated with lower odds of live birth (adjusted OR = 0.34, 95% CI 0.22-0.52, p < 0.001), while increasing maternal age was also associated with lower live-birth odds (adjusted OR per year = 0.94, 95% CI 0.89-0.99, p = 0.031). The miscarriage rate was 29.7%, median neonatal birth weight was 3,012 g, and congenital anomalies were documented in 12.6% of recorded neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Serum miRNA expression profile in responders to acupuncture treatment for diminished ovarian reserve: a study protocol for a nested case-control study.
articles.authors: An D, Yang L, Li J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) leads to subfertility, infertility, and premature menopause, significantly compromising women's reproductive health. Although clinical evidence supports the effectiveness of acupuncture in improving ovarian reserve, treatment responses vary considerably among DOR patients, and the factors associated with favorable outcomes remain unclear. Serum microRNAs may serve as potential biomarkers for distinguishing acupuncture responders, warranting further investigation.
DESIGN AND METHODS: This prospective nested case-control study will enroll women with DOR who undergo acupuncture treatment. Treatment response will be evaluated based on changes in anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels, antral follicle count (AFC), serum follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) levels and clinical pregnancy. According to their response, participants demonstrating greater improvement will be assigned to the experimental group (responders), while non-responders will be matched in a 1:1 ratio to form the control group. Serum microRNA profiles from both groups will be analyzed using high-throughput sequencing to identify differentially expressed microRNAs. Candidate microRNAs will subsequently be validated via real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis will be performed to evaluate their predictive value for acupuncture treatment response.
DISCUSSION: This is the first clinical study to characterize the serum miRNA expression profiles of DOR patients who benefit from acupuncture. The findings are expected to provide evidence supporting the precise identification of acupuncture-responsive individuals within this patient population.
STUDY PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/mgt/project/view/-4614215526207679163, identifier ITMCTR2025000004.

articles.title: Total gonadotropin dose is not associated with live birth or embryo quality in fresh cycles at equivalent levels of ovarian response: a retrospective cohort study stratified by ovarian response.
articles.authors: Feng K, Wang L, Wei H et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Whether the total gonadotropin (Gn) dose used for controlled ovarian stimulation is independently associated with live birth and embryo quality remains controversial, largely because the dose is individualized according to patient prognosis, which generates confounding by indication. We examined this association within homogeneous levels of ovarian response.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study analyzed 3,711 fresh autologous embryo transfer cycles (female age ≤35 years, follicular-phase long protocol, January 2016 to June 2025); cycles with trigger-day progesterone ≥1.5 ng/mL were excluded because fresh transfer was canceled per center policy. Cycles were stratified by oocyte yield into poor (<10, n=1,346), normal (10-15, n=1,582), and high (>15, n=783) response. The exposure was the total Gn dose. The primary outcome was the fresh embryo transfer live birth rate; secondary outcomes included clinical pregnancy, early miscarriage, and morphological embryo-quality indicators. We modeled dose-response relationships with restricted cubic splines (RCS), compared dose quartiles within strata using sequentially adjusted logistic regression, controlled the false discovery rate (FDR) by the Benjamini-Hochberg method, and prespecified five sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: In the overall cohort, the total Gn dose showed neither a linear (P=0.871) nor a nonlinear (P=0.701) association with live birth. Compared with the lowest dose quartile (Q1), fully adjusted odds ratios for Q2, Q3, and Q4 were 1.18 (95% CI: 0.90-1.55), 1.08 (0.78-1.49), and 1.34 (0.92-1.95), and no stratum showed a significant association. In the normal-response stratum, the highest quartile was associated with reduced live birth in the crude model (OR=0.70, P=0.036), but the association attenuated and disappeared with sequential adjustment (aOR=1.08, P=0.757), which quantitatively illustrates how confounding by indication arises and how it can be corrected. No secondary outcome remained significant after FDR correction (minimum q=0.137), and all sensitivity analyses agreed with the main analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Within the same level of ovarian response, the total Gn dose was not significantly associated with fresh embryo transfer live birth or morphological embryo quality. Within the dose range studied (700-8,025 IU; interquartile range 1,650-2,725 IU), escalating the Gn dose to improve embryo quality or live birth lacks evidential support, and moderate dose increases…

articles.title: The relationship between symptoms of adenomyosis and current ultrasonographic diagnostic criteria.
articles.authors: Ivanisevic S, Dason ES, Hanna C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adenomyosis is a uterine disorder defined by presence of endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium with surrounding myometrial hyperplasia. Research has shown that ultrasound (US) can play a key role in early adenomyosis diagnosis and treatment. The Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) recently published standardized criteria for ultrasonographic diagnosis of adenomyosis, but the relationship between these criteria and clinical symptoms, has yet to be clinically validated.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the prevalence of MUSA ultrasound criteria of adenomyosis and relationship between rates of ultrasound features and clinical symptoms of adenomyosis.
METHODS: This is an analytical cross-sectional study of patients aged 18-52 receiving a transvaginal ultrasound for any indication at a single outpatient imaging center. Patients were excluded if they had a hysterectomy and/or bilateral oophorectomy, were in menopause, or had active gynecologic malignancy. Patients completed a survey to assess for infertility or fertility-related healthcare use, heavy menstrual bleeding, and pelvic pain. Ultrasound images were assessed by a radiologist using MUSA criteria to evaluate for adenomyosis. Multivariate analyses assessed association between MUSA features and patient-reported symptoms.
RESULTS: Of 271 recruited participants, 11.4% had at least one direct feature of adenomyosis, 57.6% had no direct features but at least one indirect feature, and 31.0% had no features. After controlling for potential confounders in multivariable analysis, patients with direct features resulted in 5.955-point higher heavy bleeding scores compared to those with no features (95% CI 1.970-9.939, p=0.004). When controlling for covariates, the association between indirect features and adenomyosis symptoms were not significant. Subjects with middle myometrium invasion reported increased rates of infertility (p=0.006), whereas subjects with outer myometrial involvement reported significantly higher heavy bleeding (p=0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Per MUSA criteria, 1 in 10 participants displayed ultrasonographic findings strongly suggestive of presence of adenomyosis. Patients with direct features were more likely to experience heavy menstrual bleeding. Layer of uterine involvement were found to have greater association with infertility and pelvic pain than any one MUSA feature.

articles.title: Duplication of the SOX3 gene in an SRY-negative boy with a 46,XX karyotype: a case report and a review of the literature.
articles.authors: Martinková J, Řezáčová H, Šantavá A et al.
articles.abstract: 46,XX testicular disorder of sex development (DSD), also known as XX male syndrome, is a rare condition where an individual with a 46,XX karyotype develops a male phenotype. In 90% of cases, the syndrome results from the translocation of the SRY gene to the X chromosome or an autosome. The remaining 10% of individuals lack the SRY gene. We report a case of an SRY-negative 3-year-old boy with a 46,XX karyotype exhibiting normal male external genitalia. Array CGH analysis revealed a 723-kb duplication of the Xq27.1q27.2 region, encompassing the SOX3 gene. The duplication was tandem. An imbalance in X chromosome methylation was observed, with a ratio of 4.5:1. The patient's mother and grandmother, both with a 46,XX karyotype, were asymptomatic carriers of this duplication. To date, SOX3 duplication has been documented in 12 SRY-negative male patients and one female patient; eleven of these individuals exhibited various disorders of genital development. In contrast, only two previously reported patients displayed normal male genitalia, although associated with infertility. This case, the first reported in the Czech Republic, further supports the hypothesis that SOX3 overexpression during gonadal development, accompanied by imbalanced X-chromosome inactivation, may induce testis formation, thereby compensating for the absence of the SRY gene in SRY-negative 46,XX male patients.

articles.title: Association between adverse pregnancy outcomes and long-term postpartum blood pressure trajectories: a community-based cohort study.
articles.authors: Liu ND, Chen LH, Wang DT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) increase the future risk of hypertension, but their impact on long-term postpartum blood pressure (BP) trajectories remains unclear. We aimed to characterize these trajectories and compare trajectory membership between women with and without APOs.
METHODS: This community-based cohort study included 1,346 women with documented deliveries (2004-2020) from the Kailuan Study who underwent at least three postpartum health examinations between 2006 and 2022. APOs included hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (gestational hypertension and preeclampsia/eclampsia), gestational diabetes mellitus, preterm birth, and low birth weight. Generalized additive mixed models were used to characterize longitudinal changes in systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP), and mean arterial pressure (MAP). Group-based trajectory modeling was applied to identify distinct BP trajectory groups. Multinomial logistic regression with marginal standardization estimated adjusted risk ratio (aRR).
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 9.2 years, SBP showed a nonlinear increase, with an average slope of 1.13 mmHg/year (95% CI, 0.93-1.33) during the first 6.4 years, followed by slower increases of 0.73 and 0.59 mmHg/year during 6.4-10 and 10-15 years, respectively. DBP showed a near-linear increasing pattern, whereas MAP increased linearly. Three trajectory groups were identified for each BP component. APOs were associated with higher risks of high-level SBP (aRR = 1.64; 95% CI: 1.19-2.66), DBP (aRR = 1.61, 95% CI: 1.24-1.87), and MAP (aRR = 2.11, 95% CI: 1.16-3.64) trajectories compared with membership in the low-level BP trajectory groups. Associations varied across APOs subtypes. GDM and PTB were associated with higher risk of membership in the high-level SBP, DBP, and MAP trajectory groups compared with the corresponding low-level trajectory groups.
CONCLUSION: Different BP components exhibit distinct longitudinal patterns after delivery, APOs are associated with heterogeneous and unfavorable long-term postpartum BP trajectories.

articles.title: Progesterone levels on hCG trigger day and neonatal outcomes in fresh embryo transfers: a retrospective threshold analysis of GnRH antagonist versus agonist long protocols.
articles.authors: Wu J, Zhang H, Huang J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated progesterone levels on the day of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) trigger are known to adversely affect pregnancy outcomes in fresh embryo transfer (fET) cycles, but their impact on neonatal outcomes remains poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between progesterone levels on hCG trigger day and neonatal outcomes, and to explore the progesterone threshold, so as to provide reference for clinical decision-making.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 2, 201 patients who achieved singleton live births following fET between April 1, 2021 and December 31, 2024. All patients were ≤ 42 years of age and underwent either a GnRH antagonist protocol or an agonist long protocol. A multivariable regression analysis was performed to detect the relationship between progesterone level and neonatal outcomes. Smooth curve fitting and threshold effect analysis were used to evaluate the cutoff value of progesterone level.
RESULTS: In the overall population, higher progesterone levels were significantly associated with increased risks of preterm delivery (PTD) (adjusted OR: 1.89, 95% CI: 1.03 to 3.47, P = 0.0399) and low birthweight (LBW) (adjusted OR: 2.67, 95% CI: 1.14 to 6.24, P = 0.0231). These associations were observed only in the GnRH antagonist protocol, particularly with progesterone ≥ 1.0 ng/mL significantly elevating the risks of PTD (adjusted OR: 4.54, 95% CI: 2.16 to 9.56, P = 0.0021) and LBW (adjusted OR: 4.16, 95% CI: 1.15 to 15.07, P = 0.0378). Threshold analysis further identified progesterone > 0.90 ng/mL as the inflection point for PTD (adjusted OR: 6.60, 95% CI: 2.52 to 14.56, P = 0.0131) and progesterone > 0.98 ng/mL for LBW (adjusted OR: 7.50, 95% CI: 3.71 to 15.87, P = 0.0038) in antagonist cycles. No such associations were found in the GnRH agonist long protocol.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that in GnRH antagonist cycles, a serum progesterone level exceeding 0.90 ng/mL on hCG trigger day may serve as an independent predictor of an increased risk of PTD in singletons born after fET. These results highlight the need for enhanced perinatal surveillance in this population, and call for further validation in larger prospective multicenter studies.

articles.title: Efficacy of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy in improving pregnancy outcome among couples with azoospermia: study protocol for a multicenter, randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: He Y, Huang J, Yan J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Azoospermia affects up to one in ten infertile couples and represents one of the most challenging conditions in male infertility. Although the development of intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) enables azoospermic men to achieve biological parenthood, overall success rates remain modest. Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) is increasingly promoted and used worldwide to improve pregnancy outcomes and enhance the efficiency of ICSI; however, its efficacy for couples with azoospermia remains uncertain. Robust evidence from adequately powered randomized controlled trials (RCTs) is still lacking to determine whether PGT-A can increase the live birth rate as the primary outcome in this context.
METHODS: This trial is designed as a prospective, multicenter, open-label RCT. Couples with azoospermia (female age 20-37 years; male age 20-55 years) who intend to undergo ICSI with partner's sperm will be screened for eligibility. Women who have at least two blastocysts available on day 5 of embryo culture will be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either PGT-A or conventional ICSI.
