A freeze-all strategy with single frozen-thawed blastocyst transfer will be implemented in both groups. The primary outcome is live birth rate.
DISCUSSION: The findings of this trial are expected to provide high-quality evidence regarding the efficacy of PGT-A for couples with azoospermia, helping optimize individualized patient management and improve overall treatment efficiency.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: http://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2100043421.

articles.title: Predicting cumulative live birth after IVF with growth hormone supplementation: the role of pretreatment duration and machine learning-based models.
articles.authors: Chen Y, Dai Z, Wang P et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate the association between growth hormone (GH) pretreatment duration and cumulative live birth (CLB), identify key prognostic factors, and develop predictive models using logistic regression (LR) and machine learning (ML) algorithms among women undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF) with GH supplementation.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of women undergoing IVF/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) with GH between February 2015 and June 2023 at a single tertiary center. Five models were developed: LR, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM). Performance was assessed with cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. AUROC and Brier scores evaluated discrimination and calibration.
RESULTS: Among 1,782 women, 763 (42.82%) achieved at least one live birth. Maternal age, anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), antral follicle count (AFC), the assisted reproductive technology (ART) cycle number, and GH duration were significant predictors. LR performed best (AUROC 0.782; Brier 0.187), showing strong calibration and interpretability. ML models had moderate discrimination but inferior calibration. AMH, AFC, and GH duration were key predictors across all methods.
CONCLUSIONS: Both logistic regression and machine learning effectively predicted CLB after GH-pretreated IVF, but LR provided favorable discrimination, calibration, and interpretability. GH pretreatment ≥2 months was independently associated with higher odds of cumulative live birth.

articles.title: Maternal mental health and its intergenerational transmission in-utero: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Seema M, Afoakwah C, Byrnes J
articles.abstract: Maternal mental health during pregnancy is important for maternal wellbeing and offspring development. Prenatal depression, anxiety, stress, and psychological distress have been associated with offspring emotional, behavioural, cognitive, and mental health outcomes, but evidence remains dispersed across conditions, outcomes, and proposed mechanisms. This scoping review synthesises empirical evidence on maternal mental health during pregnancy as a potential intergenerational exposure, including potential in-utero pathways.Five databases (MEDLINE, Scopus, PsycInfo, CINAHL, and Embase) were searched from 1995 to 24 February 2026, following PRISMA-ScR guidance. Eligible sources of evidence examined maternal mental health during pregnancy in relation to postnatal offspring outcomes. Data were extracted using a structured framework and synthesised narratively. Twenty sources of evidence met the inclusion criteria. Across diverse designs and populations, prenatal depression, anxiety, stress, and psychological distress were commonly associated with adverse offspring outcomes, including emotional and behavioural difficulties, neurocognitive impairments, and increased risk of psychiatric conditions from childhood to adulthood. Several primary studies reported associations independent of traditional birth outcomes, consistent with potential in-utero pathways. Plausible mechanisms included stress-related neuroendocrine processes, inflammation, and epigenetic regulation. However, heterogeneity in exposure measurement, outcome definitions, and follow-up periods limited comparability and causal interpretation.Maternal mental health during pregnancy may be an important early-life and intergenerational exposure associated with offspring developmental trajectories, but observational evidence does not establish causal in-utero transmission. Stronger causal inference, longitudinal data linkage, and incorporation of economic and policy-relevant outcomes are priorities for future research.

articles.title: Prevention and treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women.
articles.authors: Stevenson J
articles.abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is a major public health concern characterised by rapid loss of bone mineral density due to estrogen deficiency, leading to increased risk of fragility fractures. This article reviews current clinical strategies for the prevention and treatment of the condition in postmenopausal women. Primary prevention discusses lifestyle modification, including adequate dietary intake of calcium and vitamin D, regular weight-bearing exercise and cessation of smoking and excess alcohol consumption. For women at elevated fracture risk, pharmacological interventions are essential. Therapies include hormone replacement therapy (HRT), bisphosphonates, Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators (SERMS) and RANKL inhibitors like denosumab, which function as antiresorptive agents to slow bone breakdown. For those with high fracture history, anabolic agents such as teriparatide or romozosumab are utilised. Early identification via personalised risk assessment, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) screening and treatment where indicated is essential. Combining adjunctive lifestyle modification with pharmacological intervention offers a framework to maintain skeletal health, preserve independence and enhance long-term quality of life post menopause.

articles.title: Retrospective Assessment of Pulmonary Embolism in Pregnancy and Evaluation of Pregnancy-Adapted YEARS Algorithm.
articles.authors: Birdsey M, Wang S, Khullar K
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the diagnostic performance of the pregnancy adapted YEARS algorithm applied to an Australian patient population with concurrent evaluation of its efficacy towards scan reduction.
METHODS: The pregnancy adapted YEARS algorithm was applied to pregnant patients retrospectively at this single site study to determine a theoretical pathway in comparison to actual management.
RESULTS: Of 119 included patients, six (5%) had pulmonary emboli (PE). Retrospective application of the pregnancy-adapted YEARS algorithm missed no PE diagnosis. Theoretical application would have resulted in an 11.7% reduction in total CTPA and V/Q scans performed.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study supports the diagnostic performance benefits of the pregnancy adapted YEARS algorithm and can potentially reduce unnecessary imaging.

articles.title: Euploid embryo counts in IVF: Associations with maternal age, vitamin D, sleep quality, and BMI.
articles.authors: Armeanu Popescu T, Popescu D, Maftei R et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal age is a known correlate of embryo euploidy, but the associations with vitamin D status, sleep quality, and body mass index (BMI) are not fully understood. This study investigated these factors in relation to euploid embryo counts per in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycle. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 42 women undergoing a single IVF cycle with preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy at one center. Serum vitamin D levels, BMI, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores were recorded before ovarian stimulation. Analyses involved multivariable linear regression, bootstrapping with 1,000 resamples, sensitivity analysis, and binomial models that accounted for the number of embryos tested. Linear regression revealed negative associations between maternal age and PSQI scores with euploid embryo counts, while vitamin D was positively associated (regression coefficient = 0.055; p = 0.006). BMI was not a significant factor. Vitamin D was the only factor whose bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap 95% confidence interval excluded zero (0.006-0.145), and its association remained significant in sensitivity analysis. Higher vitamin D levels were also linked to a higher euploidy rate in binomial models (p = 0.017), including models adjusted separately for anti-Müllerian hormone (p = 0.026) or antral follicle count (p = 0.044). Maternal age, BMI, and PSQI scores were not significant in these models. Across all analyses, vitamin D demonstrated the most consistent association with embryo euploidy. These preliminary findings from a small observational cohort warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies and do not establish causality.

articles.title: A Community Partnership Initiative in Utah to Enhance Prehospital Perinatal Care in the Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage.
articles.authors: Larson J, Kaiser JE, Frost CJ et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In Utah, a confluence of factors over the last 10 years has led to an increase in prehospital births attended by emergency medical system (EMS) providers. Utah is a rural and frontier state where a large segment of the population lives far from obstetric care and where transport times to a facility for birth can be long or hazardous because of seasonal weather. Before March 2024, Utah EMS protocol guidelines only allowed paramedics to administer oxytocin and then only for the treatment of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). In many cases, a paramedic is not available (because rural fire agencies are often staffed by volunteers, tight budgets do not support full paramedic coverage, or paramedics are not required), and thus, advanced emergency medical technicians (AEMTs) are first on the scene. A community-based interprofessional quality improvement initiative was designed and implemented to expand state EMS protocol guidelines to address the timing, route and administrator of oxytocin.
PROCESS: Using stepwise processes from Powell's Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change implementation science taxonomy, we combined bottom-up and top-down strategies, including stakeholder and decision-maker interviews, community-level focus groups, partner surveys, and coalition building to foster change.
OUTCOMES: In April 2024, the Utah EMS protocol guidelines were successfully changed to include the administration of oxytocin by paramedics for the prevention of PPH and to AEMTs for intramuscular prevention and treatment of PPH.
DISCUSSION: This expansion of medication administration provides an additional tool to prevent PPH while increasing safety and equity of prehospital birth services. This may be particularly crucial in a rural and frontier state where maternity deserts, desire for community-based birth, and obstetric-care hurdles are increasing. It is hoped this quality improvement initiative can serve as a guide to others wanting to implement similar practice changes in their state.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of cladribine tablets for the treatment of active relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis in the United Kingdom.
articles.authors: Jones M, Alexopoulos ST, Fontrier AM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The approved indication of cladribine tablets has recently been expanded in the United Kingdom for the treatment of all adult patients with active relapsing multiple sclerosis. This analysis assessed the cost-effectiveness of cladribine tablets from the perspective of the National Health Service in patients with active relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS).
METHODS: A cohort-based Markov model with 11 health states (10 disability states plus death) was developed. In addition to best supportive care without disease-modifying therapy (DMT), 12 recommended DMTs were included as comparators to cladribine tablets over a 50-year horizon. Treatment effects were modelled using hazard ratios for 6-month confirmed disability progression (CDP); relapses and drug-related adverse events were modelled via annualized relapse rates and event probabilities. Associated costs (inflated to 2023 pounds sterling) and quality-adjusted life year (QALY) losses were discounted at 3.5% annually. Sensitivity analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: Cladribine tablets were dominant (i.e. less costly and more effective) vs ponesimod, ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, dimethyl fumarate, diroximel fumarate, and teriflunomide in pairwise comparisons. Over a lifetime horizon, the model predicted discounted cost-savings with cladribine tablets vs high-efficacy comparators (ponesimod, ocrelizumab, and ofatumumab). In most scenarios, the cost-savings resulted from lower lifetime drug acquisition costs due to the unique fixed course posology of cladribine tablets, in addition to delayed disease progression. Sensitivity analyses supported the base case that cladribine tablets are cost-effective vs ponesimod, ofatumumab, and ocrelizumab; the main source of uncertainty was related to the large credible intervals associated with 6-month CDP.
CONCLUSIONS: This economic analysis demonstrated that cladribine tablets are a cost-effective treatment option for patients with active RRMS.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic Complications in Pregnancy and Biological Ageing in the Offspring: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Mekonnen EG, Bianco-Miotto T, Liu K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic complications in pregnancy may alter the intrauterine environment, influence offspring biological ageing and potentially increase the risk of chronic diseases later in life.
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to examine associations between diabetes in pregnancy, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, maternal BMI and metabolic syndrome, and offspring biological ageing markers, including telomere length and DNA methylation.
DATA SOURCES: Studies were retrieved from PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus and Web of Science.
STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Study characteristics, exposures and outcomes were independently extracted and summarised.
SYNTHESIS: Standardised mean differences in telomere length were calculated using Hedges' g, and random effects meta-analysis was applied to pool effect estimates.
RESULTS: Of the 123 studies, 90 assessed DNA methylation, 28 reported telomere length and 5 reported both outcomes. No differences in telomere length were observed in offspring exposed to gestational diabetes (7 studies) or hypertensive disorders (14 studies). Each unit increase in maternal BMI was associated with a 0.27% decrease in offspring telomere length (3 studies). Exposure to cardiometabolic complications was associated with aberrant DNA methylation patterns in genes related to cardiometabolic pathways. Higher mean methylation level was reported in cord blood (2 studies) and placenta (7 studies) following exposure to diabetes and hypertensive disorders.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher maternal BMI was associated with slightly shorter offspring telomeres, while no differences were observed following exposure to gestational diabetes or hypertensive disorders. Altered DNA methylation in cardiometabolic genes suggests epigenetic effects of in utero exposure, although heterogeneity in biospecimens and measurement methods limits definitive conclusions.

articles.title: Different Proportions of Round-Headed Spermatozoa: Impacts on Sperm Function and IVF/ICSI Outcomes.
articles.authors: Long S, Yang F, Yu L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although complete globozoospermia is well characterized, it is clinically rare. Partial globozoospermia is more prevalent, yet the impact of varying round-headed sperm ratios on disease severity remains unclear. Notably, even low proportions often signal compromised semen quality and spermatogenic dysfunction. This study investigates the impact of these proportions on sperm function and ART outcomes to provide evidence for individualized clinical management.
METHODS: This was a retrospective case-control study. After balancing baseline characteristics by propensity score matching (PSM), 728 subjects were included in both the round-headed sperm group (proportion ≥ 5%) and the control group. A machine learning-based automatic sperm morphology analysis system was used to quantify the proportion of round-headed sperm and their head parameters. Sperm function indicators (DNA integrity, acrosome function, mitochondrial membrane potential) were detected, and 166 couples from the round-headed sperm group who received IVF/ICSI were included for reproductive outcome analysis.
RESULTS: After PSM, the round-headed sperm group showed significantly lower normal morphology rate, sperm kinematic parameters, nucleoprotein maturation, acrosome integrity, and acrosin activity compared with the control group. The sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI) and high DNA stainability (HDS) were higher in the round-headed sperm group (p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis based on clinical pregnancy outcomes determined that the cut-off value for the proportion of round-headed sperm is 7.2%. The high-proportion group (> 7.2%) exhibited significantly lower IVF fertilization rate and high-quality embryo rate than the low-proportion group (≤ 7.2%) (p < 0.01). In ICSI cycles, the high-proportion group had significantly lower high-quality embryo rate (48.48% vs. 40.33%, p = 0.016), clinical pregnancy rate (58.82% vs. 41.43%, p = 0.048), and live birth rate (50.98% vs. 32.86%, p = 0.028) than the low-proportion group.
CONCLUSIONS: The proportion of round-headed sperm can serve as an objective predictor for sperm function and outcomes before assisted reproductive technology treatment.

articles.title: Personalized Prediction of Uterine Fibroid Shrinkage During GnRH Antagonist Treatment via Pretreatment T2-Weighted MRI Signal Intensity.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Motoshima S, Nomiyama H, Hashimoto K et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To develop and internally validate a pretreatment quantitative magnetic resonance imaging-based predictive model for uterine fibroid volume reduction following gonadotropin-releasing hormone antagonist therapy.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, 106 women with uterine fibroids treated with relugolix underwent pre- and intratreatment magnetic resonance imaging. The dominant fibroid was assessed for T2-weighted imaging fibroid-to-iliopsoas signal intensity ratio, apparent diffusion coefficient, flow voids, and fibroid location. The primary outcome was a ≥ 30% reduction in dominant fibroid volume between pre and intratreatment magnetic resonance imaging. Eight baseline variables were entered into a Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator-penalized logistic regression model with bootstrap internal validation.
RESULTS: Sixty patients (56.6%) achieved a ≥ 30% volume reduction. In the univariate analyses, a higher T2-weighted imaging signal intensity ratio and location were significantly associated with response. A purely data-driven Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator model retained two predictors: dichotomized T2-weighted imaging signal intensity ratio and location. A T2-weighted imaging ratio ≥ 2.0 was the strongest positive predictor, whereas subserosal and cervical locations showed negative associations and submucosal location showed a slight positive association relative to intramural fibroids. The model showed moderate discrimination (apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.746; optimism-corrected area, 0.671) with acceptable calibration.
CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative pretreatment T2-weighted imaging (ratio ≥ 2.0) is strongly associated with fibroid volume reduction under gonadotropin-releasing hormone antagonist therapy. An internally validated Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator-based model incorporating T2-weighted imaging signal intensity and location may aid individualized treatment selection and preoperative planning.

articles.title: Estradiol-PGC-1 signaling in mitochondrial health: Implications for perimenopause and cardiovascular disease.
articles.authors: Parten AL, Rowe GC
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in aging women. While CVD etiology is multifactorial, mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by reduced content, impaired energy production, and increased oxidative stress, is an underlying contributor. These impairments reduce the ability of the heart and vasculature to support peripheral tissues. Estradiol, a key sex hormone with widespread physiological effects, supports mitochondrial function, lipid oxidation, vascular endothelial cell and smooth muscle function, and redox balance, contributing to its cardioprotective effects in women. Perimenopause is marked by hormonal variability and an overall decline in estradiol concentrations that may compromise mitochondrial quality and vascular function, increasing CVD risk. Mitochondrial quality and maintenance are largely controlled by the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator-1 (PGC-1) family of transcriptional coactivators. Impairments in PGC-1 isoform expression have been linked to cardiovascular and metabolic decline and may be exacerbated by estradiol loss during the menopause transition. However, the mechanisms by which estradiol signaling regulates PGC-1 isoforms, and how this interaction contributes to mitochondrial dysfunction and CVD development following menopause, have not been comprehensively described. Thus, this review aims to highlight current evidence on the individual and overlapping roles of estradiol and PGC-1 isoforms and examine how their interaction may contribute to the development of CVD following menopause.

articles.title: Reversing the trend: The critical need for in-utero transfer to optimise preterm outcomes in tropical LMICs.
articles.authors: Siddiqui SA, Siddiqui GF, Singh R
articles.abstract: There is an inherent structural paradox faced by low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) when it comes to the field of maternal and child health. Whereas there has been success in providing basic obstetric care in the form of healthcare services in peripheral locations, modern neonatal and preterm birth care are concentrated in tertiary urban settings. Thus, high-risk pregnancies are delivered in peripheral clinics, but the fragile preterm neonates are brought to higher centres only after efforts to stabilise their clinical condition fail and severe physiological deterioration occurs. These 'outborn' infants present in critically ill condition, leading to unnecessary mortality and morbidity. This suggests a serious need for the implementation of pro-active rather than reactive transport through anticipated in-utero transfer. The uterus of the mother then acts as an ideal physiological transport incubator.

articles.title: Multimodal Ultrasound for Early Prognostic Assessment During Definitive Radiotherapy in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer.
articles.authors: Xia Z, Huang X, Miao Q et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the prognostic value of early multimodal ultrasound parameters in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) undergoing definitive radiotherapy.
METHODS: This retrospective exploratory study included 31 patients with histologically confirmed cervical squamous cell carcinoma who underwent definitive radiotherapy with or without concurrent chemotherapy. Grayscale ultrasound and shear wave elastography (SWE) were performed in all patients at baseline and approximately 2 weeks after radiotherapy initiation, whereas complete contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) data were available for 22 patients. Unfavorable outcomes were defined as progression, recurrence, or death during follow-up after radiotherapy initiation. ROC analysis was performed to evaluate individual parameters, and a logistic regression model incorporating baseline SWEmean and tumor maximum diameter at the two-week assessment was internally validated using 1000 bootstrap resamples to estimate optimism-corrected performance. Exploratory time-dependent ROC analyses were performed using progression-free survival data to assess model discrimination at different follow-up time points.
RESULTS: Patients with unfavorable outcomes showed higher baseline SWEmean values (153 vs. 106.5 kPa, p = 0.039) and larger residual tumor maximum diameters 2 weeks after radiotherapy initiation (36 vs. 32 mm, p = 0.045). The combined model showed an apparent AUC of 0.775 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.735. Exploratory time-dependent ROC analysis yielded AUC values of 0.855, 0.840, and 0.719 at 12, 24, and 36 months, respectively. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated shorter progression-free survival in the higher-risk group than in the lower-risk group according to the combined model (log-rank p = 0.022). In exploratory CEUS subgroup analysis, a greater reduction in time to peak was associated with unfavorable outcomes (p = 0.039).
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline tumor stiffness and early residual tumor size assessed by multimodal ultrasound may offer complementary prognostic information for exploratory risk stratification in patients with LACC undergoing definitive radiotherapy. Further prospective validation is warranted.

articles.title: Incidental detection of maternal malignancy in non-reportable results from non-invasive prenatal testing: experience in Hong Kong and literature review.
articles.journal: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi
articles.authors: Chan YYY, Xue S, Yu ELM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) for fetal aneuploidy occasionally yields non-reportable results due to persistent 'noisy' signals, which may indicate occult maternal malignancy. This study investigated the clinical and genetic implications of non-reportable NIPT results, focusing on multiple chromosomal aberrations associated with maternal malignancy, with the goal of developing standardised management protocols for pregnant women with such suspicious NIPT results.
METHODS: From 2020 to 2023, women with persistent non-reportable NIPT results were identified and followed up in Hong Kong. Cancer cases were analysed for clinical history and chromosomal patterns. Incidental cancer detection rates were calculated and compared with literature reports. Tag Z-score chromosomal abnormalities were compared between cancer and non-cancer groups; the corresponding sensitivity and specificity were calculated.
RESULTS: Among 84 446 NIPT tests, 151 (0.18%) showed persistent noisy signals. Of 131 patients with follow-up data, five (3.82%) were diagnosed with maternal malignancy; the overall incidental detection rate was 0.006% (5 of 84 446). Although three women delivered healthy babies, most presented with late-stage cancer confirmed by imaging and biopsy. All five cases exhibited ≥3 chromosomal aberrations on repeat NIPT; chromosome 18 was consistently involved. Univariate analysis revealed significant differences in Tag Z-score frequencies for chromosomes 18 (P=0.026) and 21 (P=0.029) between cancer and non-cancer groups. A clinical flowchart was developed to guide management of patients with multiple aberrations.
CONCLUSION: Although rare, occult maternal malignancy represents 3.82% of non-reportable NIPT results. This risk should be included in pre-test counselling and may warrant early oncological evaluation. Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging should be considered to facilitate cancer diagnosis.

articles.title: "Being seen, heard, witnessed and acknowledged": a reflexive thematic analysis of peer support following termination for medical reasons among women in Great Britain.
articles.authors: Robinson H, Vowles E, Marshall P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Termination for medical reasons (TFMR) is associated with profound distress, grief and emotional trauma, as well as stigma and isolation. While peer support has been reported to reduce isolation and validate emotions in broader contexts, the distinct ethical and emotional complexities surrounding TFMR mean these findings cannot be assumed to transfer directly. TFMR‑specific evidence is therefore needed.
AIM: To explore women's perspectives on peer support following termination for medical reasons (TFMR) in order to make policy and practice recommendations to improve support.
METHODS: This study was a reflexive thematic analysis, conducted using qualitative data from 6 facilitated online focus groups with 28 women in total, aged 18 or older who had experienced TFMR in Great Britain within the past 10 years.
RESULTS: Five key themes were developed: 1) Blindsided and isolated with a silenced grief; 2) They just "get it" - the unique value of TFMR-specific peer support; 3) Navigating the abyss: support that hinges on luck; 4) Shared journey, differing and evolving support needs; and 5) The other edge of the sword: when others' stories are heavy.
CONCLUSIONS: TFMR is a profoundly distressing experience, and women's accounts highlight significant gaps in the availability and consistency of support. Peer support represents a potentially effective and low‑cost intervention, but access is currently dependent on chance rather than a clear pathway. Strengthening collaboration between statutory and voluntary sectors could enable the development of varied, TFMR‑specific peer support options that reflect the differing needs of those affected. Further research is needed to understand how peer support is experienced across diverse groups and how it can be tailored to ensure equitable, sensitive, and sustainable provision.

articles.title: Carbetocin and peri-operative hemoglobin change at cesarean delivery in a setting of self-paid use: an 8-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Chen SY, Chang MH, Lai KJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is a leading cause of maternal morbidity, most often from uterine atony. Carbetocin, a long-acting heat-stable oxytocin analogue, reduces blood loss at cesarean delivery in randomized trials, but real-world data are sparse from settings where carbetocin is self-paid and not yet routine, such as Taiwan. We examined the association between carbetocin and peri-operative hemoglobin change at cesarean delivery in a setting of rising, patient-funded use.
METHODS: Single-center retrospective cohort of deliveries between 2017 and 2025. Carbetocin (100 µg intravenously) was self-paid and chosen by the patient; comparators received the institutional standard (oxytocin alone at cesarean). The primary outcome was the peri-operative hemoglobin change (post- minus pre-delivery, g/dL) at cesarean delivery. Multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, BMI, parity, birth weight, and high-risk status, with calendar year added to address the secular trend in uptake; propensity-score inverse-probability weighting was a sensitivity analysis (complete-case). Because the recorded vaginal blood-loss field showed treatment-linked recording heterogeneity, only the binary PPH endpoint is reported for vaginal delivery.
RESULTS: Of 6,266 deliveries with documented carbetocin status, 2,112 were cesarean. Among cesarean deliveries with paired peri-operative hemoglobin (carbetocin n = 734; no carbetocin n = 484; complete-case analytic n = 1,061), the median hemoglobin change was - 0.60 g/dL with carbetocin versus - 1.30 g/dL without; pre-delivery hemoglobin was identical between arms. The adjusted mean difference was + 0.79 g/dL (95% CI 0.65 to 0.94), consistent in low-risk (+ 0.84) and high-risk (+ 0.76) strata and under propensity weighting. A severe hemoglobin decline (≥ 2 g/dL) occurred in 11% versus 25% (supportive, sensitive to missing data). For vaginal delivery, PPH (≥ 500 mL) occurred in 3.2% versus 4.2% (year-adjusted odds ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.46 to 1.01; not significant).
CONCLUSIONS: In this non-randomized, self-paid cohort, carbetocin was associated with a smaller peri-operative hemoglobin decline at cesarean delivery, directionally consistent with randomized evidence; the magnitude was larger than pooled trial estimates and is likely inflated by selection. Carbetocin was not associated with a lower incidence of PPH. Findings are associations and require cautious interpretation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable; this is a…

articles.title: Persian version of the international consultation on incontinence questionnaire-pediatric lower urinary tract symptoms caregiver module: translation, validation and cultural adaptation.
articles.authors: Norouzi M, Aghaei E, Alizadeh F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Currently, the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Pediatric Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms (ICIQ-CLUTS), a well-established tool for assessing LUTS in children, is not available in Persian. This study aims to translate and validate this tool for Persian-speaking caregivers.
METHODS: The ICIQ-CLUTS was translated and validated following ICIQ recommendations. The final version was self-administered by 67 caregivers of children aged 5 to 9 years. The study was conducted between June and November 2024. A concise clinical diagnosis of LUTS was used as a diagnostic reference. Internal consistency (Cronbach's α) and test-retest reliability (Intraclass Correlation Coefficient, ICC) were computed to assess the reliability. Construct validity was measured through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) by principal component analysis (PCA) using varimax rotation. Discriminative validity was measured using ROC analysis and diagnostic accuracy metrics.
RESULTS: Of the total 67 participants, 32 were cases. Internal consistency was good (α = 0.768), and test-retest reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.983). Standard error of measurement and minimum detectable change were 0.53 and 1.46, respectively. EFA found three factors-urgency, incontinence and bladder control, and voiding and bowel dysfunction-accounting for 72.1% of the variance. The questionnaire demonstrated excellent discriminative capability (AUC = 0.917, 95% CI: 0.848-0.986). Additionally, 75% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and 88.1% accuracy were obtained for a cut-off point of 15.5.
CONCLUSION: ICIQ-CLUTS-Pe is psychometrically sound and culturally adapted to discriminate LUTS among Persian-speaking caregivers. The tool is validated to effectively quantify symptom severity and monitor treatment response in both clinical and research settings.

articles.title: Post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation and hydrocephalus in preterm infants: a five-year retrospective cohort study from a tertiary referral center.
articles.authors: Barzegar H, Khorasani E, Vardanjani HM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus (PHH) is a serious complication of intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) in preterm infants and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Although neonatal risk factors are well described, the contribution of maternal and perinatal factors remains inconsistent across studies.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the incidence, clinical characteristics, and independent predictors of PHH among preterm neonates with IVH, and to evaluate early outcomes in a tertiary referral center.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included preterm neonates (< 34 weeks' gestation or birth weight ≤ 1500 g) with ultrasound-confirmed IVH admitted to Namazi Hospital, Shiraz, Iran, between March 2019 and March 2024. Demographic, maternal, perinatal, and neonatal variables were extracted from medical records. PHH was defined as progressive ventricular dilatation following IVH. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of PHH.
RESULTS: Among 507 neonates with IVH, 154 (30.4%) developed PHH. Infants with PHH had significantly lower birth weight and gestational age and higher rates of maternal diabetes and neonatal meningitis.Each 100-g increase in birth weight was associated with a 24% reduction in the odds of developing post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus (OR 0.76; 95% CI 0.7-0.83; p < 0.001).Maternal gestational diabetes mellitus/diabetes was a significant risk factor (OR 2.14; 95% CI 1.39-3.29; p = 0.001) Antenatal steroid exposure was associated with lower odds of PHH, possibly reflecting reduced hemorrhage severity(OR 0.53; 95% CI 0.35-0.80; p = 0.003).Mortality was borderline higher among infants with PHH (p = 0.05), while the need for surgical intervention was significantly higher in this group (p < 0.001).The primary clinical model demonstrated good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.19) and acceptable discrimination (AUC = 0.75).
CONCLUSION: PHH remains a frequent and severe complication of IVH in preterm neonates. Both neonatal and selected maternal factors contribute to PHH risk, underscoring the importance of comprehensive perinatal assessment and early identification of high-risk infants.

articles.title: Clinician vs. self-assessment of mFG hirsutism scores in PCOS: can patient self-assessment serve as a reliable screening and triage tool?
articles.authors: Su D, Gao Y, Sun X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine the discrepancy between patient- and clinician-assessed modified Ferriman-Gallwey (mFG) hirsutism scores across four PCOS phenotypes and nine body sites, and to evaluate whether patient self-assessment could serve as a reliable tool for preliminary hirsutism screening and outpatient triage.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 157 Han Chinese female patients aged 18-36 years, who were diagnosed with PCOS according to the Rotterdam criteria at an outpatient gynecological endocrinology clinic. All participants completed a self-assessment questionnaire, scoring terminal hair growth across nine body areas using the mFG scale. These self-assessed scores were compared with clinician-assessed scores independently obtained by two trained physicians who were blinded to patient self-assessment results.
RESULTS: Patient self-assessed mFG scores were significantly higher than clinician-assessed scores in the overall PCOS cohort and phenotypes A and B (all P < 0.05), while no significant score differences were detected in phenotypes C and D. Despite higher self-assessed scores, Cohen's kappa coefficients ranged from 0.551 to 0.855 across phenotypes, indicating moderate to almost perfect diagnostic agreement. Analyses for phenotype D were purely descriptive due to inadequate statistical power. Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated minimal mean scoring bias across all groups, yet the wide 95% limits of agreement (LoA) indicated poor precision for individual-level assessment. The borderline range of self-assessed mFG (5-10), where the cumulative concordance rate fell below the 90% threshold, showed a rate of only 70.6% and was the primary zone of concern. By contrast, patients with scores less than 5 and more than 10 had a concordance rate greater than 90%. ROC curve analysis verified the excellent diagnostic performance of self-assessment (overall AUC = 0.922), with clinician-assessed scores used as an internal reference.
CONCLUSION: For Han Chinese women with PCOS, self-assessed mFG scoring is a reliable tool for preliminary hirsutism screening and outpatient triage but cannot fully replace clinician assessment. We recommend confirmatory clinician review for patients with self-assessed mFG scores in the borderline zone.

articles.title: Pharmacy role in the proMotion of continencE (PRIME): a co-production study to develop a pharmacy bladder and bowel service.
articles.authors: Cotterill N, Uren A, Williams A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary and faecal incontinence affects millions. Community pharmacies provide local community healthcare highlighting opportunity for innovation in continence promotion. The Pharmacy Role In the proMotion of continencE (PRIME) study was conducted to investigate development of a Pharmacy Bladder and Bowel Service (PBBS) incorporating key stakeholder engagement.
METHODS: A UK online survey, employing convenience sampling of community pharmacy staff identified current practice, and barriers and facilitators to PBBS development, between July and November 2022. These findings were incorporated into an evidence brief supported by findings from earlier PRIME sub-studies (systematic literature review and qualitative interviews). The evidence brief guided stakeholder participant workshop discussions using co-production methodology, during April and June 2023, to derive a protocolised service specification for the PBBS, detailing underpinning requirements and scope of service, as the final stage of this study.
RESULTS: Twenty-nine community pharmacy participants completed the survey reporting some provision of lifestyle advice in practice with clear scope for expansion. Subsequently, sixteen participants including Community Pharmacists, Bladder and Bowel Service staff, Service users and healthcare commissioners participated in two workshops. The PPBS service specification outlined three tiers of service provision: tier 1 - awareness raising, education and signposting; tier 2 - assessment and self-help advice; tier 3 - specialist input involving specific treatment strategies. Acknowledged limitations are the pressures and relatively novel nature of pharmacy research which presents challenge in promoting participation.
CONCLUSIONS: This is the first evidence-based PBBS service specification, developed to inform future practice. Key requirements include record sharing, advances in training, and reimbursement to enable the PBBS to be viable for community pharmacy provision. The PBBS provides potential for early identification, promotion of continence health, and self-help activation in community settings.

articles.title: Association of rs3736228 polymorphism in LRP5 gene with bone fracture and osteoporosis: a systematic review and updated meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Zhang C, Liu W, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 5 (LRP5) gene is a key regulator of bone mineral density and skeletal metabolism. The rs3736228 (Ala1330Val) polymorphism in LRP5 has been firmly established as a genome-wide significant locus for bone mineral density and fracture risk in large-scale GWAS. However, demographic and clinical subgroups that are frequently underrepresented in GWAS cohorts, such as sex, menopausal status and ethnicity, may have different impact sizes and ideal genetic models. Previous candidate-gene meta-analyses, while informative, did not systematically evaluate these subgroup-specific effects, owing to limited sample sizes and incomplete stratification. Therefore, we conducted this updated systematic review and meta-analysis to provide granular, subgroup-stratified risk estimates that complement existing GWAS evidence.
METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. A comprehensive electronic search was performed across five databases: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Ovid. The literature search was conducted using a combination of Medical Subject Headings(MeSH)terms, such as"osteoporosis, "fracture, "LRP5,"and"polymorphism,"along with their related synonyms. We also manually screened reference lists of retrieved articles to identify additional relevant studies. To address heterogeneity, we employed both the Cochran's Q test and the I²statistic. A fixed-effects model was used when I²<50%and P ≥ 0.05; otherwise, a random-effects model was applied. All analyses were performed using STATA software version 17.0, and the odds ratios(ORs)and their corresponding 95%confidence interval(CI)values were calculated using fixed effects or random effects model. We carried out a subgroup analysis to explore the source of heterogeneity according to gender, race, disease, genotyping methods, control resources, female menopause, and HWE balance.
RESULTS: The current meta-analysis involved 14 studies, comprising 16 independent comparisons, including 1,549 patients and 3,345 control subjects. The analyses revealed a significant association between LRP5 rs3736228 polymorphism and an increased risk of osteoporosis and fractures. Specifically,in the overall analysis, the polymorphism showed a higher likelihood of osteoporosis and fractures in the allelic model [OR=1.17, 95%CI(1.04-1.31), P=0.011], homozygous model [OR=1.47, 95%CI(1.07-2.01), P=0.018], dominant model [OR=1.44,…

articles.title: Anxiety in pregnancy complicated by gestational and pre-gestational diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Limruangrong P, Ukhawounam U, Pornsuriyasak P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and pregestational diabetes mellitus (pre-GDM) affect approximately 20% of pregnancies worldwide, requiring intensive management, alongside pregnancy-related concerns and broader psychosocial factors, all of which may contribute to increased psychological distress. While anxiety is associated with adverse maternal and child outcomes, evidence in women with diabetes during pregnancy remains fragmented. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined anxiety in pregnant and postpartum women with GDM and pre-GDM.
METHODS: This study searched MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, EBSCO, Cochrane Library, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP from inception to April 2025. Observational studies reporting anxiety outcomes in pregnant or postpartum women with GDM or pre-GDM were included. Two reviewers independently screened articles, extracted data, and assessed quality using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklists. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed, with subgroup analyses by region and measurement instrument. Meta-regression explored heterogeneity sources. The study followed PRISMA 2020 and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251063824).
RESULTS: Thirty-four studies (n = 994,189; 38,584 GDM; 156 pre-GDM; 955,449 healthy controls) were included. Women with GDM had higher odds of antenatal anxiety than healthy controls (OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.20-2.37) and higher mean anxiety scores (SMD = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.07-0.34). Among eight single-arm studies reporting the prevalence of screen-positive antenatal anxiety in women with GDM, all conducted in Asia, the pooled prevalence was 36% (95% CI: 22-50%); however, this estimate should be interpreted very cautiously because of extreme heterogeneity (I2 = 98.7%), with individual study estimates ranging from 12 to 61%. Subgroup analyses indicated stronger antenatal anxiety associations in Asian studies (SMD = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.27-0.55). Postpartum anxiety did not differ significantly between women with GDM and healthy controls (RR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.93-1.05). Evidence regarding pre-GDM was limited and should be considered preliminary.
CONCLUSIONS: A high burden of antenatal anxiety was observed among women with GDM, particularly in Asian populations, although precise prevalence estimates remain uncertain due to extreme heterogeneity. Postpartum anxiety appeared comparable to that of healthy women. Evidence regarding pre-GDM was based on only two studies and remains insufficient to…

articles.title: Associations of pre-pregnancy BMI and gestational weight gain with large-for-gestational-age in women with gestational diabetes mellitus in Southwestern China.
articles.authors: Qian S, Yang J, Tian Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large-for-gestational-age (LGA) infants are a common complication of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), increasing the risk of obstetric trauma and long-term metabolic disorders. Pre-pregnancy body mass index (ppBMI) and gestational weight gain (GWG) are modifiable maternal factors, but their joint impact on LGA in sub-high-altitude, multiethnic populations remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the independent and combined associations of ppBMI and GWG with LGA risk among women with GDM in a sub-high-altitude, multiethnic region of southwestern China.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, clinical data from 407 women with GDM, diagnosed according to the Chinese national guideline (WS 331-2011) at 24-28 weeks of gestation, were analyzed. ppBMI and GWG were categorized according to national criteria. LGA was defined using Chinese birth weight references, with sensitivity analyses applying INTERGROWTH-21st standards. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated independent and combined associations, adjusting for maternal age, infant sex, and gestational age at delivery. Sensitivity analyses additionally accounted for maternal insulin use, parity, and gravidity.
RESULTS: Women with overweight/obese ppBMI combined with excessive GWG had the highest risk of LGA (adjusted OR 4.03, 95% CI 1.61-10.11). Excessive GWG among normal/underweight women showed a non-significant trend toward increased LGA risk (adjusted OR 2.60, 95% CI 0.95-7.14). Male infant sex was consistently associated with higher LGA odds. Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses and alternative birth weight standards.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated ppBMI combined with excessive GWG is associated with higher LGA risk in women with GDM in sub-high-altitude, multiethnic regions. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating, and may inform hypotheses for future research on BMI-stratified gestational weight patterns and potential intervention strategies. Prospective studies are warranted to confirm these associations and optimize maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Antepartum electronic fetal monitoring interpretation: multicenter observational study.
articles.authors: Vigil-De Gracia P, Robledo Paz C, Campos Ávila C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antepartum EFM is the most widely used method worldwide to evaluate fetal well-being. However, neither NST nor other surveillance techniques can precisely determine the onset or degree of fetal hypoxemia and acidemia. The presence of accelerations seems to reflect fetal well-being; however, their absence does not predict fetal compromise. Evidence regarding the perinatal prognosis of normal NSTs with one or no accelerations compared with those classified as reactive remains insufficient.
OBJECTIVE: To compare perinatal outcomes of the non-stress test (NST) interpreted by the usual reactive/non-reactive criterion versus the NST reported as "fetal well-being preserved" when there is one or no fetal heart rate (FHR) acceleration with moderate variability.
METHODS: Multicenter, non-randomized, observational, comparative non-inferiority study evaluating two different NST interpretation criteria, conducted in Panama among high-risk pregnant patients with ≥ 34 weeks' gestation. A reactive NST was defined as a tracing with baseline FHR 110-160 beats per minute, variability 6-25 [beats/min], no bradycardia, and at least two accelerations within 20 min. When one or no acceleration was present while the other criteria were maintained, the NST was defined as showing "fetal well-being preserved" (normal/reassuring).
RESULTS: We analyzed 1,206 NSTs from 699 patients. There were no significant differences in gestational age at birth, time elapsed since the first NST, mode of delivery, 1- and 5-minute Apgar scores, or the presence of variable decelerations. No perinatal death was associated with follow-up by NST report. Twelve cases (0.99%) were reported as abnormal at the second NST performed 7 days after the initial NST. In those cases, no perinatal deaths occurred; two cases had a 5-minute Apgar < 7, one in each reporting group. Across the entire population, there were 6 deaths with no significant differences related to the initial NST reporting category.
CONCLUSION: This observational non-inferiority study reporting the NST as reactive (≥ 2 accelerations) or as fetal well-being preserved/reassuring (normal variability with ≤ 1 acceleration) yields no large differences in fetal well-being outcomes.

articles.title: Evaluating the landscape and characteristics of endometriosis research published between 1990 and 2024.
articles.authors: Mago S, Grimes DR, Feng Q et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We aimed to assess the landscape of endometriosis randomised-controlled trials (RCTs) between 1990 and 2024 by characterising RCTs by management type, primary outcome, country of origin, trial registration, sample size and minimum detectable difference based upon standard RCT power targets of 80% and 90%.
METHODS: We identified all endometriosis RCTs from Dimensions.AI with an English abstract. Articles were examined for sample size, theme and primary outcome. Sample sizes were used to calculate minimum detectable effect size (MDES) of studies at 80% and 90% power.
RESULTS: We analysed 536 RCTs using 'R'. 55.6% (N = 298) of studies investigated medical management of endometriosis, of which 177 investigated Gonadotrophin Releasing Hormone (GnRH) analogues. RCTs investigating complementary therapies rose from 0.847% (N = 1) in 1990-1999 to 28.7% (N = 31) of medical management RCTs in 2020-2024. The US and China led publishing with 70 and 65 RCTs total, respectively. Importantly, of 445 RCTs with at least one continuous outcome, we found that at 90% power, 55.7% (N = 248) of RCTs would only detect a standardised mean difference which was 'large' or greater.
CONCLUSION: We noted several trends within endometriosis RCTs. In line with wider literature, China accounts for a growing proportion of RCTs. Although complementary therapy is increasingly recognised as a management option requiring further research, most medical management RCTs focussed on GnRH analogues as part of their treatment regime despite these being considered second-line management options. A high proportion of RCTs was underpowered to detect potentially clinically significant effects of intervention-potentially indicating significant resource wastage.

articles.title: The Role of RNA Interactions with PIWI in Regulating Gametogenesis, Fertilization, and Early Development Across Species.
articles.authors: Haddadi M, Safari-Alighiarloo N, Mikaeeli G et al.
articles.abstract: Small RNA-mediated regulatory systems maintain DNA integrity and proper functioning of the germ cell lineage. One such system consists of P-element-induced wimpy testis (PIWI) proteins and PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs). Researchers initially identified piRNAs as repressors of transposable elements. Subsequent studies have identified additional roles, including regulating epigenetic programming, maintaining maternal transcript homeostasis and controlling processes involved in early embryonic development. Comparative studies of piRNAs and their functions across species have revealed substantial differences, including sex- and species-specific patterns of piRNA expression, differences in piRNA cluster organization, and functional diversity among PIWI proteins. These differences may reflect the diverse reproductive strategies and evolutionary adaptations of the species examined. Disruption of the piRNA pathway has been associated with infertility and germ-cell tumors in various studies; however, the species involved and the nature of these associations (e.g., mechanistic vs. correlative) require further investigation. These findings indicate a need for further study of piRNA regulation at the cellular level and its clinical relevance to reproductive biology. This review examines the biogenesis and biological functions of PIWI/piRNA complexes, compares PIWI/piRNA biology across species, evaluates conserved and species-specific aspects of these processes, and identifies important questions that remain underexplored in the literature.

articles.title: Urinary haloacetic acid concentrations and asthenozoospermia risk: a case-control study in China.
articles.journal: Journal of exposure science & environmental epidemiology
articles.authors: Ge L, Zhang M, Deng YL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disinfection byproducts (DBPs), particularly haloacetic acids (HAAs), exhibit male reproductive toxicity. However, their associations with asthenozoospermia remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate associations of urinary trichloroacetic acid (TCAA) and dichloroacetic acid (DCAA), the predominant HAAs, with asthenozoospermia risk, and further to evaluate their joint effects.
METHODS: An age-matched case-control study (135 asthenozoospermia cases and 270 controls) nested within the TREE cohort was conducted. Repeated measurements of urinary HAAs were utilized to improve exposure assessment. Associations were assessed using conditional logistic regression, and additive and multiplicative interactions analyses.
RESULTS: Higher levels of urinary DCAA and TCAA were associated with an increased risk of asthenozoospermia (OR = 2.05; 95% CI: 1.10, 3.83; P for trend = 0.04 and OR = 2.13; 95% CI: 1.11, 4.09; P for trend =  0.05 for the highest vs. lowest quartiles of urinary DCAA and TCAA, respectively). Co-exposure to high levels of both DCAA and TCAA had a 2.62-fold (95% CI: 1.48, 4.69) higher risk of asthenozoospermia relative to low both such exposures, with evidence of multiplicative (P = 0.01) and additive interactions (RERI = 1.98, 95% CI: 0.61, 4.40; AP = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.29, 1.04).
SIGNIFICANCE: Exposures to TCAA and DCAA are individually associated with increased risk of asthenozoospermia, and co-exposure to such two compounds suggest an additive effect. These findings highlight the importance of assessing joint effects of two HAA biomarkers on male reproduction.
IMPACT: DBPs are the ubiquitous contaminants formed during drinking water treatment, and human exposure is unavoidable. This age-matched case-control study among men undergoing ART treatment provides novel human evidence that exposures to DCAA and TCAA are individually associated with increased risk of asthenozoospermia, a major contributor to male infertility. Co-exposure to DCAA and TCAA is associated with an additive increase in the risk of asthenozoospermia. These findings emphasize the need to reduce HAA levels in drinking water and also offer important clues for clinical decision-making and public health strategies.

articles.title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images.
articles.authors: Wu CI, Banda K, Arora R et al.
articles.abstract: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

articles.title: Oropouche virus disrupts neurodevelopment and exhibits congenital infection potential.
articles.authors: Bannerman C, Philip DT, Kennedy EA et al.
articles.abstract: Oropouche virus (OROV) historically caused a self-limiting disease, yet recent strains have been clinically linked to congenital infection and neurodevelopmental disease. These observations highlight the need to study OROV as a congenital pathogen. Here, using both a historical and currently circulating strain, we show OROV infects neurons across differentiation states in human forebrain organoids. Compared with the neurotropic congenital pathogen Zika virus (ZIKV), OROV exhibits a heightened capacity for neuroinfection and pathology in both forebrain organoids and neonatal mice. The increased permissiveness of OROV is driven, in part, by a broader neuronal tropism and a relative insensitivity to neuronal type I interferon-mediated antiviral responses. Consistent with clinical observations, neonatal neuroinfection results in rapid and severe neuropathology marked by cerebral hemorrhage. Finally, using a transient type I interferon-blockade model, we demonstrate that OROV can productively infect the murine placenta and cause fetal growth restriction. Together, our complementary models support a unified framework in which placental and fetal barriers limit productive fetal brain infection, yet OROV exhibits marked neurotropism and neuropathogenic potential upon gaining access to developing neural tissues. These findings reinforce the need for vigilant monitoring of OROV as an emerging pathogen associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and congenital disease.

articles.title: Actionable genetic landscape and dynamics in circulating DNA from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer.
articles.authors: Leshchiner I, Medford AJ, Cha J et al.
articles.abstract: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a sensitive, noninvasive tool for monitoring the genomic landscape, heterogeneity, and evolution of cancer, aggregating genetic information from multiple metastatic sites. Here, we study 15,564 cfDNA samples from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer (MBC). We classify samples, deep-sequenced with Guardant360, into MBC subtypes using our trained random forest model. Most patients have variants associated with therapeutic resistance and targetability of approved and experimental therapies, including in PIK3CA, ESR1, PTEN, and AKT1. Frequencies of multiple actionable alterations differed from primary disease, and multiple variants per gene suggest independent resistant clones. The large cohort size enables uncovering clonal co-behaviors, including co-existence and exclusivity of alleles and correlation of allele fractions. cfDNA testing is now recommended in multiple advanced malignancies, including eligibility assessment for clinical trials. We envision this large collection of MBC cfDNA data as an invaluable resource for the design and planning of future clinical trials.

articles.title: Suzetrigine (JOURNAVX) for Acute Postoperative Pain: Evidence, Perioperative Integration, and Clinical Guidance.
articles.authors: Pribyl K, Farooq Anwar MA, Yi PK et al.
articles.abstract: Suzetrigine (JOURNAVX) is an oral, first-in-class selective NaV1.8 inhibitor approved in the United States for adults with moderate-to-severe acute pain. In 4 randomized controlled trials (n = 2768) using bunionectomy and abdominoplasty models, suzetrigine improved SPID48 versus placebo and showed similar efficacy to hydrocodone/acetaminophen 5/325 mg. Its short-term safety profile differs from opioids, with less nausea and dizziness but more pruritus and muscle spasms. Clinicians must screen for CYP3A interactions and counsel patients using certain hormonal contraceptives. This review summarizes pharmacology, clinical evidence, and perioperative implementation considerations.

articles.title: Therapeutic Drug Monitoring Considerations in Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Krasowski MD
articles.abstract: Physiological changes during pregnancy can impact the pharmacokinetics of medications. Due to a variety of practical and ethical factors, clinical pharmacokinetic studies are challenging to perform during pregnancy. In addition, information on fetal toxicity of drugs requires years of study. As a result, evidence-based guidance for optimizing drug dosing in pregnancy, including therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM), is currently sparse. The most complete practice guidelines are related to antiseizure medications, with data also accumulating for antipsychotic and antidepressant medications. There are many avenues for future research and clinical practice improvement for TDM in pregnancy.

articles.title: Understanding and Addressing Anovulatory Infertility.
articles.journal: Endocrinology and metabolism clinics of North America
articles.authors: Violette CJ, Eaton JL
articles.abstract: Anovulation is a common and heterogenous cause of infertility with significant implications for metabolic health. Ovulatory disorders arise from disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and are often characterized using the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics hypothalamic dysfunction, pituitary dysfunction, ovarian dysfunction, and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) pathophysiologic framework. While many hypothalamic and pituitary causes of anovulatory infertility are treatable, primary ovarian insufficiency often requires assisted reproductive technology. In PMOS (formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome), ovulation induction with an oral agent such as letrozole is considered first-line to reduce the risks of multiple gestation and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.

articles.title: Contraceptive Decision-making.
articles.journal: Endocrinology and metabolism clinics of North America
articles.authors: Cahill EP, Amaya S
articles.abstract: Contraceptive counseling is an essential component of endocrine care because many endocrine disorders and treatments influence fertility, pregnancy outcomes, and contraceptive eligibility. This article outlines a patient-centered approach that incorporates reproductive goals, shared decision-making, and assessment using The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention medical eligibility criteria. It summarizes the efficacy, mechanisms, benefits, and risks of nonhormonal and hormonal contraceptive methods. Special considerations for patients with obesity, diabetes, thyroid disorders, and polycystic ovarian syndrome are discussed, along with potential medication interactions. Integrating contraception counseling into endocrinology practice can reduce unintended pregnancies and support optimal reproductive health outcomes.

articles.title: Postpartum and Lifelong Cardiometabolic Risk after Gestational Diabetes and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Endocrinology and metabolism clinics of North America
articles.authors: Prentice D, Rickert M, Valent AM
articles.abstract: Approximately 1 in 5 pregnancies are complicated by gestational diabetes and/or hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Rates of both perinatal complications are rising in parallel and share risk factors such as obesity, advanced maternal age at delivery, and insulin resistance. Moreover, both conditions are associated with cardiometabolic morbidities following pregnancy including type 2 diabetes, renal disease, cardiovascular disease, dyslipidemia, and cerebrovascular accidents. Professional organizations have recognized these conditions as key risk factors for metabolic, cardiovascular, and cerebrovascular morbidity and mortality. Additionally, these conditions impact the uterine environment, leading to increased risk of cardiometabolic disorders in the offspring.

articles.title: Endocrine Evaluation of Hyperandrogenism in Women.
articles.journal: Endocrinology and metabolism clinics of North America
articles.authors: Grennan KN, Chang AY
articles.abstract: Hyperandrogenism in women encompasses a spectrum of clinical manifestations including hirsutism, acne, androgenetic alopecia, menstrual dysfunction, and virilization. Although polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome accounts for the majority of cases, a systematic endocrine evaluation is essential to identify less common but clinically significant etiologies including androgen-secreting tumors, ovarian hyperthecosis, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, and cortisol excess. Total testosterone liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry measurement in women has refined thresholds for further evaluation across the reproductive lifespan leading to appropriate diagnosis. This article synthesizes current evidence and expert guidance on clinical assessment, biochemical testing, and diagnostic strategies for hyperandrogenism.

articles.title: Addressing Female Sexual Dysfunction.
articles.journal: Endocrinology and metabolism clinics of North America
articles.authors: Pope R
articles.abstract: Female sexual dysfunction is a prevalent yet under-recognized condition encompassing disorders of sexual desire, arousal, orgasm, and genitopelvic pain. The International Society for the Study of Women's Sexual Health advocates a biopsychosocial, patient-centered framework integrating routine sexual health assessment, comprehensive evaluation, and individualized treatment. Common conditions include hypoactive sexual desire disorder, arousal and lubrication disorders associated with genitourinary syndrome of menopause, female orgasmic disorder, and genitopelvic pain/penetration disorder. Management combines behavioral, psychological, hormonal, pharmacologic, and physical therapy interventions. Improved clinician education, multidisciplinary collaboration, and proactive sexual health discussions are essential to enhance diagnosis, treatment, and quality-of-life outcomes.

articles.title: Redefining Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: New Phenotypic Classifications and Implications.
articles.journal: Endocrinology and metabolism clinics of North America
articles.authors: Vafea MT, Dunaif A
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a complex disorder resulting from the interaction of susceptibility genes with environmental factors. Current diagnostic criteria were established by expert consensus. Genome-wide association studies have shown that the phenotypes defined by these criteria share similar genetic architectures and do not reflect meaningful biological differences. Many complex disorders are defined by criteria designed to accommodate phenotypic diversity, yet such criteria often group the convergent expression of multiple genetic etiologies under a single clinical diagnosis. Data-driven mathematical methods, enabled by large phenotypic datasets, offer a strategy for partitioning this variation into groups corresponding to divergent genetic underpinnings.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Reproductive Health: Implications for Contraception, Fertility, and Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Endocrinology and metabolism clinics of North America
articles.authors: Porterfield F, Mulligan J, Salim K et al.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have rapidly expanded in use for the treatment of obesity and type 2 diabetes, including among women of reproductive age. Emerging evidence suggests that GLP-1 signaling may influence reproductive physiology through central effects on the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and indirect metabolic pathways. In women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), GLP-1 RAs improve insulin resistance and androgen profiles and may improve menstrual regularity. Most GLP-1 RAs do not significantly affect oral contraceptive pharmacokinetics, although tirzepatide may require temporary backup contraception. Evidence regarding fertility outcomes and pregnancy safety remains limited.

articles.title: Hormone Therapy Considerations for Breast Cancer Survivors and High-Risk Women.
articles.journal: Endocrinology and metabolism clinics of North America
articles.authors: Sanserino K
articles.abstract: Menopause in breast cancer survivors and high-risk women is abrupt, severe, and treatment-induced. Hormone therapy remains the most effective treatment of vasomotor symptoms and genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM), but it is frequently avoided because of concerns about cancer risk. Randomized trial data support avoidance of systemic hormone therapy in breast cancer survivors, although risk varies by patient population and formulation. Nonhormonal therapies are effective options for vasomotor symptoms, and low-dose vaginal estrogen is safe for most patients with GSM. Management requires balancing oncologic risk with symptom burden, taking into account tumor biology, baseline risk, and patient preferences.

articles.title: Managing Perimenopausal Bone Loss: The Role of Bisphosphonate Treatment.
articles.journal: Endocrinology and metabolism clinics of North America
articles.authors: McClung MR, Clark AL
articles.abstract: Preventing the rapid loss of bone density and structure that occurs during the perimenopause is a unique opportunity to prevent the development of postmenopausal osteoporosis and high fracture risk. For women who are not candidates for estrogen therapy, low-dose bisphosphonate therapy for 3 to 5 years can prevent perimenopausal bone loss, after which intermittent bisphosphonate therapy can maintain skeletal health indefinitely. Identifying women at high risk for developing osteoporosis with bone density testing as they approach or enter perimenopause and considering prevention therapy should be a routine part of the clinical management of midlife women.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Health in Women: Navigating Menopause and Beyond.
articles.journal: Endocrinology and metabolism clinics of North America
articles.authors: Obaed N, Mihaj I, Nudy M
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD), specifically atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD), remains the leading cause of death among women globally and persistent cardiovascular disparities exist for women compared to men. The menopausal transition represents a critical cardiometabolic inflection point during which women experience accelerated adverse changes in lipid profiles, body composition, vascular function, and metabolic parameters independent of aging alone. Traditional ASCVD risk factors such as diabetes, hypertension, smoking, and obesity may exert disproportionately greater cardiovascular effects among women compared with men. In conclusion, a lifespan approach that recognizes menopause as a critical inflection point for ASCVD prevention is essential.

articles.title: Loss-of-function variants in CFAP57, SEPTIN4, SPEM2, and CFAP46 cause asthenoteratozoospermia.
articles.authors: Nawaz S, Kitakaze H, Abdulla MA et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: What are the genetic causes of asthenoteratozoospermia in consanguineous families, and what is the specific role of cilia- and flagella-associated proteins (CFAP) 46 in mammalian spermiogenesis?
SUMMARY ANSWER: CFAP46 is a central apparatus protein essential for sperm flagellar assembly and head remodeling.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Asthenoteratozoospermia is a genetically heterogeneous condition characterized by reduced sperm motility and abnormal morphology. While several CFAPs are known to support axonemal organization, the functional role of CFAP46 in mammals remained uncharacterized prior to this study.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: We performed whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing on 13 consanguineous families affected by primary male infertility. Functional validation was conducted using three CRISPR/Cas9-engineered mouse models: a null allele, a FLAG-tagged knock-in, and a humanized patient-specific nonsense allele.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Genomic DNA from affected individuals and fertile relatives was analyzed by NGS and validated via Sanger sequencing. Mouse phenotypes were characterized through sperm analysis, immunofluorescence, and electron microscopy. Protein interactions were identified via immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry. Additionally, a gene-level burden analysis was applied to unresolved cases across 345 spermiogenesis-associated genes.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: We identified homozygous loss-of-function variants in CFAP46, CFAP57, SEPTIN4, and SPEM2 segregating with infertility. Cfap46-deficient males were infertile due to significantly decreased sperm count, motility, and severe axonemal disruptions. CFAP46 was found to form an in vivo complex with CFAP54, CFAP74, and CFAP221. In families without a monogenic cause, affected individuals harbored a significantly higher burden of rare deleterious variants (4-16 genes) compared to fertile controls.
LARGE SCALE DATA: Large-scale datasets and scripts are available via GitHub (https://github.com/sirusb/Nawaz_et_al_scripts).
LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: While functional mouse data strongly supports the identified variants, the rare-variant burden analysis identifies associations that require further functional validation to confirm specific oligogenic interactions.
WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: This study establishes CFAP46 as a regulator of mammalian spermiogenesis and suggests that, beyond monogenic defects, aggregated…

articles.title: Atlas-assisted segment anything model for fetal brain MRI (FeTal-SAM).
articles.authors: Zeng Q, Liu W, Li B et al.
articles.abstract: This paper presents FeTal-SAM, a novel adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) tailored for fetal brain MRI segmentation. Traditional deep learning methods often require large annotated datasets for a fixed set of labels, making them inflexible when clinical or research needs change. By integrating atlas-based prompts and foundation-model principles, FeTal-SAM addresses two key limitations in fetal brain MRI segmentation: (1) the need to retrain models for varying label definitions, and (2) the lack of insight into whether segmentations are driven by genuine image contrast or merely inferred by learned spatial priors. We leverage multi-atlas registration to generate spatially aligned label templates that serve as dense prompts, alongside a bounding-box prompt, for SAM's segmentation decoder. This strategy enables binary segmentation on a per-structure basis, which is subsequently fused to reconstruct the full 3D segmentation volumes. Evaluations on two datasets, the dHCP dataset and an in-house dataset demonstrate FeTal-SAM's robust performance across gestational ages. Notably, it achieves Dice scores comparable to state-of-the-art baselines which were trained for each dataset and label definition for well-contrasted structures like cortical plate and cerebellum, while maintaining the flexibility to segment anatomical structures that could be templated by compatible atlas image and label sample pairs. Although slightly lower accuracy is observed for subtle, low-contrast structures (e.g., hippocampus, amygdala), our results highlight FeTal-SAM's potential as a flexible atlas-conditioned segmentation framework without requiring a separately trained model for each supported parcellation. This method thus constitutes a promising step toward clinically adaptable fetal brain MRI analysis tools.

articles.title: Analytical validation of MethyLiverDx-Sigma, a plasma cfDNA methylation assay for hepatocellular carcinoma detection.
articles.authors: Kim SC, Choi H, Chung J et al.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance relies on ultrasonography and alpha-fetoprotein, both limited in sensitivity for early-stage disease; aberrant methylation of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) offers a promising blood-based approach. Reported here is the analytical validation of MethyLiverDx-Sigma (MLDx-s), an assay that detects methylated RNF135 and DNMT3A in bisulfite-converted plasma cfDNA by methylation-specific PCR with high-resolution melting (HRM), with GAPDH as an endogenous control. Performance was evaluated following CLSI EP05-A3, EP07, EP12-A2, and EP37.
