Precision of quantification cycle (Cq) and melting peak temperature (Tm) was assessed by variance-component analysis within one site and across two sites and two operators. Because precision studies used bulk bisulfite-converted reference DNA, the reported coefficients of variation (CVs) primarily characterize the PCR-HRM detection module; end-to-end variability in clinical plasma specimens may be higher. Interference and cross-reactivity were evaluated in low-positive and contrived-negative samples against reproducibility-derived limits, with dose-response testing of reactive substances. Detection was 100% at both levels, and every run met control-validity criteria. Cq repeatability CVs ranged from 0.53% to 1.68%, and total reproducibility CVs ranged from 1.10% to 2.37%; all Tm CVs were ≤0.20%. All 18 interferents and 16 microbial cross-reactants evaluated in low-positive samples met the predefined acceptance criteria. In negative samples, hemoglobin, SARS-CoV-2, and measles virus produced concentration-dependent non-specific amplification, and dose-response testing established their respective no-effect concentrations. These findings characterize the analytical precision and multisite reproducibility of the PCR-HRM detection module and the analytical specificity of MLDx-s, complementing its previously reported clinical performance for plasma-based HCC detection.

articles.title: From polycystic ovary syndrome to polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: A practical clinical review.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.authors: Yanes Cardozo LL, Eissa MA, Basnet J et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), recently renamed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS), is the most common endocrine disorder affecting women of reproductive age. The new nomenclature reflects growing recognition that this condition extends far beyond ovarian dysfunction, encompassing complex endocrine, metabolic, cardiovascular, and psychological abnormalities. Although the diagnostic criteria remain unchanged, the name change emphasizes the multisystem nature of the disorder and may improve disease recognition and patient care. This review provides a practical, evidence-based overview of the diagnosis and management of PMOS/PCOS, highlighting recent updates from the 2023 International Evidence-Based Guideline. We discuss the evaluation of hyperandrogenism and ovulatory dysfunction in reproductive-aged women, as well as the assessment and treatment of obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obstructive sleep apnea, and mental health disorders. Finally, we summarize current pharmacological therapies and emerging treatment strategies, highlighting key knowledge gaps that must be bridged to optimize long-term cardiometabolic and reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: Effects of metformin and omega-3 fatty acids on neurobehavioural outcomes in letrozole-induced polycystic ovary syndrome mice.
articles.authors: Yadav A, Mishra A, Sharma A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder associated with reproductive, metabolic, and neurobehavioural abnormalities, including anxiety, depression, and cognitive impairment. Omega-3 fatty acids have anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties that may ameliorate these complications.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of metformin, fish oil, and flaxseed oil on anxiety-like behaviour, depressive-like behaviour, locomotor activity, and cognitive function in a letrozole-induced PCOS mouse model.
METHODS: Thirty female Swiss albino mice were divided into five groups: Control, PCOS, PCOS + Metformin, PCOS + Flaxseed Oil, and PCOS + Fish Oil. PCOS was induced with letrozole (2 mg/kg, orally). These neurobehavioral tests were conducted: Open Field Test, Elevated Plus Maze, Morris Water Maze, Forced Swim Test, and Actophotometer Test. Data were analysed using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test.
RESULTS: The PCOS Group exhibited anxiety- and depression-like behaviours and impaired spatial learning and memory compared with controls. Treatment effects varied across behavioural domains. Fish oil improved selected behavioural outcomes, particularly immobility and locomotor activity, whereas effects on spatial memory and other measures were less consistent. Flaxseed oil and metformin showed moderate beneficial effects on the behaviour of PCOS mice.
CONCLUSION: In letrozole-induced PCOS mice, metformin, flaxseed oil, and fish oil showed distinct impacts on neurobehavioral outcomes. The results indicate that several behavioural changes linked to experimental PCOS may be modulated by omega-3-rich oils; nevertheless, additional mechanistic and clinical research is required to determine their therapeutic significance.

articles.title: Emerging contaminants and male reproductive health: Mechanistic insights, clinical evidence, and research priorities.
articles.authors: Gautam R, Priyadarshini E, Gupta S et al.
articles.abstract: Male infertility contributes to around 40-50% of the infertility cases worldwide. Emerging environmental pollutants (microplastics, engineered nanoparticles, radiofrequency electromagnetic radiation (RF-EMR), pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs)) have received significant attention because of their environmental persistence and potential adverse effects on male reproductive health. This review critically synthesizes evidences from experimental, epidemiological and systematic studies, with emphasis on mechanistic pathways. Micro- and nanoplastics are now detected in human blood, testes and semen, act as carriers that alter the transport and bio-availability of co-contaminants.Results from animal studies reported that emerging pollutants impair male reproductive function via interconnected mechanisms namely, oxidative stress, enhanced reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage, chronic inflammation, endocrine disruption, blood-testis barrier impairment and apoptosis. Chronic RF-EMR exposure perturbs testicular homeostasis via oxidative injury, calcium channel modulation, hormonal imbalance, and disruption of the blood-testis barrier. Engineered nanoparticles readily cross biological barriers and accumulate in reproductive tissues. PPCPs particularly endocrine-disrupting contaminants cause impairment of steroidogenesis and hormonal homeostasis, resulting in impaired male fertility. Collectively, these pollutants converge on interconnected mechanism that affect sperm count, motility, morphology, viability and fertilization capacity. While animal studies provide evidence of reproductive toxicity, longitudinal human studies with biomonitoring, semen analysis, hormonal profiling and molecular endpoints are required to propose safe exposure thresholds, establish casual relationship and determine the effects of mixture pollutants. These emerging pollutants thus represent a major yet potentially preventable risk for male infertility.

articles.title: Impact of Office-Based Nitrous Oxide on Operating Room Utilization for Endometrial Sampling.
articles.authors: Howe M, Hung YY, Srinivasan S et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between nitrous oxide analgesia availability and the proportion of endometrial sampling procedures (endometrial biopsies, dilation and curettages, and hysteroscopies) performed in the office vs the operating room.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort study.
SETTING: Community-based integrated healthcare system.
PARTICIPANTS: About 1803 patients who underwent endometrial sampling between March 2023 and January 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Office availability of nitrous oxide analgesia.
RESULTS: Following the introduction of nitrous oxide, the proportion of endometrial sampling procedures (hysteroscopies with and without morcellation, dilation and curettage and endometrial biopsies) performed in the operating room decreased significantly from 28% to 16% (p <0.001), with a corresponding increase in office-based procedures from 72% to 84% (p <.001). After nitrous oxide withdrawal, operating room-based procedures increased to 25% (p <.01), and office-based procedures decreased to 76% (p <.01). Similarly, the proportion of hysteroscopies (with and without morcellation) done in the operating room decreased from 89% to 69% during nitrous oxide implementation (p <.001), with a corresponding increase in office-based hysteroscopies from 11% to 31% (p <.001). Operating room-based endometrial biopsies and D&Cs decreased from 3.6% to 2.3% (p = .17) during nitrous oxide implementation. Office-based endometrial biopsies and D&Cs correspondingly rose from 96.4% to 97.7% (p = .17) during nitrous oxide implementation. In addition, the proportion of insufficient endometrial sampling (defined as inadequate tissue for pathologic diagnosis) was similar between the preimplementation and nitrous oxide implementation periods (10.8% vs 9.3%, p = .37).
CONCLUSION: In an outpatient gynecology setting, the availability of nitrous oxide analgesia was associated with a higher proportion of endometrial sampling procedures performed in the office rather than the operating room. This association was driven predominantly by a shift in hysteroscopic procedures.

articles.title: Beyond antifracture efficacy: Osteoanabolic versus antiresorptive therapy for chronic pain after osteoporotic vertebral fractures. A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Massei L, Valentini S, Chiaramonte C et al.
articles.abstract: Osteoporotic vertebral fractures (OVFs) associated pain can last long, reducing health-related quality of life. Concurrent risk of new fractures warrants osteoporosis therapies, i.e., antiresorptive [bisphosphonates and the anti-RANKL monoclonal antibody (mAb) denosumab] or osteoanabolic (teriparatide, abaloparatide, and the anti-sclerostin mAb romosozumab) agents, the latter demonstrating greater antifracture efficacy, but unclear effect on post-fracture pain. The present systematic review and meta-analysis explore whether osteoanabolics exert better pain control compared to antiresorptives in the medium- (3-6 months) to long-term (12-24 months) treatment of OVFs patients. After search in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, fifteen studies (4029 patients) were included: six randomized controlled trials (RCTs, 2345 patients) and nine non-randomized studies of interventions (NRSIs, 1684 patients), whose risk of bias was assessed by using RoB-2 and ROBINS-I V2 tools, respectively. Data on pain measurement by using the Visual Analogue Scale, the Numeric Rating Scale, or dedicated domains of health-related quality-of-life instruments (QUALEFFO-41) were extracted and, when possible, meta-analyzed. Separate meta-analyses of RCTs or NRSIs showed no statistically significant difference in pain control between osteoanabolic and antiresorptive drugs. Combined exploratory meta-analysis of RCTs and NRSIs favored osteoanabolic therapy, but in association with very high heterogeneity and no robustness in sensitivity analyses, thus just regarded as hypothesis-generating. Future studies should clarify the pathophysiological mechanisms of persistent pain following OVFs and their correlation with different clinical phenotypes predictive of differential responses to antifracture therapies. The applied protocol for this systematic review/meta-analysis was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; registration number: CRD420261281929).

articles.title: Coordinating Pelvic Floor Physical Therapy Care Across the Perinatal Period.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN
articles.authors: Dreisbach C
articles.abstract: Perineal injury during childbirth can contribute to maternal morbidity through pain, impaired bowel control, and limitations in activities of daily living. Nurses can help patients access pelvic floor physical therapy during pregnancy and postpartum recovery. In this column, I examine evidence on pelvic floor interventions for birth preparation and rehabilitation after perineal injury. I describe opportunities for nurses to support pelvic floor care through patient education, assessment of barriers to care, and care coordination with physical therapists and obstetric clinicians. I also discuss interdisciplinary care models that nurses can adapt to support continuity of pelvic floor care across the perinatal period.

articles.title: Ultrasound in fetal growth restriction.
articles.authors: Kehl S
articles.abstract: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with increased perinatal morbidity and mortality. Its recognition requires differentiation from a constitutionally small-for-gestational-age (SGA) fetus. Based on the current AWMF S2k guideline, this CME review summarizes the ultrasound assessment and clinical management of suspected FGR. Accurate first-trimester dating, standardized fetal biometry, assessment of amniotic fluid volume, and detailed anatomical evaluation form the basis of diagnosis. Consensus-based criteria distinguish early FGR before 32 + 0 weeks' gestation from late FGR at or beyond 32 + 0 weeks' gestation. Multivessel Doppler assessment of the umbilical artery, middle cerebral artery, cerebroplacental ratio, and ductus venosus provides complementary information on placental resistance, fetal redistribution, and cardiovascular decompensation. Cardiotocography, including computerized analysis of short-term variation in early FGR, is used as part of multimodal surveillance and should not be interpreted in isolation. The review discusses appropriate monitoring intervals, indications for inpatient care, antenatal corticosteroids and fetal neuroprotection when preterm birth is anticipated, as well as gestational-age- and finding-dependent timing and mode of delivery. A practical clinical case illustrates the diagnostic pathway from abnormal fetal biometry to delivery planning.

articles.title: CBCT-guided plan-of-the-day adaptive radiotherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer: Feasibility and dosimetric evaluation in a resource-limited setting.
articles.authors: Ben Rejeb M, Lahiouel S, Hamdoun A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interfractional anatomical variations during pelvic radiotherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer may compromise target coverage and increase organ-at-risk (OAR) irradiation. This study evaluated the feasibility and dosimetric impact of a cone-beam CT (CBCT)-guided Plan-of-the-Day (PoD) adaptive radiotherapy where resources are limited.
METHODS: Twenty patients treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy were prospectively enrolled. Three volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) plans were generated for each patient using planning target volume margins of 7, 10, and 15 mm around the cervical tumour clinical target volume. Daily CBCT imaging was used to select the most appropriate plan according to daily anatomy. The workflow was implemented using standard CBCT-guided IGRT resources without dedicated online adaptive radiotherapy software. Anatomical variations were assessed over 500 treatment fractions, and dose recalculation was performed on 410 fractions.
RESULTS: Substantial interfractional anatomical variations were observed. Bladder volume was lower than the planning value in 68.2% of fractions, whereas rectal distension exceeded planning values in 74.4%. The reduced-margin plan was selected in 58.8% of fractions, followed by the standard (27%) and large-margin plans (14.2%). Plan selection was significantly associated with bladder and rectal anatomical variations. Target coverage remained satisfactory across all plans (mean PTV V42.75Gy: 96.8-97.5%), with the predefined V95% criterion achieved in 85.7%, 79.8%, and 89.3% of recalculated fractions for the 7-, 10-, and 15 mm plans, respectively. Larger margins significantly increased bladder and rectal V30Gy and V40Gy values.
CONCLUSION: A CBCT-guided PoD strategy was feasible using standard IGRT resources and generally maintained high target coverage despite substantial interfractional anatomical variations. Larger margins increased OAR dose-volume parameters, supporting individualized daily plan selection where dedicated online ART infrastructure is unavailable.
IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: CBCT-guided PoD offers a strategy where online adaptive radiotherapy is unavailable.

articles.title: Trauma-informed mHealth intervention for improving childbirth self-efficacy following perinatal loss: a mixed-methods development and pilot validation study.
articles.authors: Benly NE, Jingsung J, Pritami RF
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy after perinatal loss may involve fear of recurrence, emotional ambivalence, and difficulty engaging with pregnancy-related information. This study developed and preliminarily evaluated a trauma-informed mobile health (mHealth) intervention to support childbirth self-efficacy among pregnant women with a history of perinatal loss.
METHODS: A sequential mixed-methods design comprised three phases: qualitative needs assessment, trauma-informed prototype development, and pilot quasi-experimental evaluation. The evaluation included 100 pregnant women at 10 primary health centres in Muna and West Muna Regencies, Indonesia, with 50 receiving the intervention and 50 receiving routine antenatal care. The four-week intervention included a Trauma-Filter Switch, Manual Kick Counter, Safe Space Journal, Midwife Direct Chat, and optional Moderated Peer Support. The primary outcome was change in total score on an adapted Childbirth Self-Efficacy Inventory (CBSEI).
RESULTS: Mean adapted CBSEI scores increased from 2.392 ± 1.198 to 3.631 ± 0.912 in the intervention group and from 2.291 ± 0.904 to 2.523 ± 0.901 in the routine-care group. The between-group difference in mean change was 1.007 points (independent-samples t(98)=3.25, p = 0.002 on change scores; Cohen's d = 0.65). The intervention group showed significant within-group improvement (t(49)=5.27, p < 0.001), whereas the routine-care group did not (t(49)=1.15, p = 0.256). The adapted CBSEI demonstrated excellent internal consistency (α=0.94, 95% CI 0.91-0.95 at baseline; α=0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.94 post-intervention).
CONCLUSIONS: The trauma-informed mHealth intervention was associated with substantial improvement in childbirth self-efficacy in this pilot evaluation. Findings support integrating emotional safety, choice, control, and empowerment into digital antenatal support following perinatal loss. Larger randomized trials with longer follow-up and a conventional mHealth comparator are warranted.

articles.title: Pointing at communicative, cognitive, linguistic, and motor skills in preterm and full-term infants at 18 months.
articles.authors: Verganti C, Suttora C, Frank V et al.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth represents a risk for vulnerability across neurodevelopmental domains. However, its impact on early communication and cross-domain associations remains underexplored. This study compared preterm and full-term infants at 18 months on communicative, cognitive, linguistic, and motor abilities, and examined associations between pointing and these skills. Thirty-nine preterm and 28 full-term infants participated. Pointing (hand, index), vocal productions (vocalizations, babbling, words), and expression modalities (unimodal gestural, unimodal vocal, bimodal gestural-vocal) were elicited using the "decorated room" task and coded with ELAN. Cognitive, language (receptive, expressive), and motor (fine, gross) abilities were assessed with the BSID-III. Preterm infants produced fewer index points, babbling, and bimodal expressions, and showed lower scores across all BSID-III scales. Only in preterm infants, index pointing significantly correlated with developmental scores, particularly cognitive and fine-motor ones. Findings highlight interconnected cross-domain developmental trajectories in the preterm population, with index pointing as a key developmental marker at 18 months.

articles.title: Adenomyosis and association between ultrasonographic features and pregnancy outcomes in women with infertility or pregnancy loss: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Brandt NB, Lindner C, Abrahamsen KH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adenomyosis has been shown to reduce live birth rates and increase the risk of pregnancy loss. The diagnosis is often established by ultrasonographic assessment using the revised Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) criteria. However, the reproductive impact of specific sonographic features remains unclear. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to investigate whether individual ultrasonographic adenomyosis features influence pregnancy outcomes in women with infertility or pregnancy loss.
METHODS: We searched MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Cochrane Library (CENTRAL), Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar (most recent 200 records) from inception to May 11th, 2026. Observational and interventional studies reporting specific ultrasonographic features of adenomyosis in women with infertility and/or pregnancy loss were included. Primary outcomes were clinical pregnancy, live birth, and pregnancy loss. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools, as appropriate by study design. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models, with common-effects models applied where appropriate; remaining evidence was synthesised narratively. Certainty of evidence was assessed by GRADE. The protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251077005).
FINDINGS: Of 2322 records screened, 29 studies comprising 19,510 patients (7569 with adenomyosis) were included. Diffuse adenomyosis was associated with lower odds of live birth compared with no adenomyosis (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.34-0.79; I2 = 63%), as well as internal adenomyosis compared with no adenomyosis (OR 0.49 95% CI 0.42-0.57 I2 = 0%). Narrative synthesis suggested poorer reproductive outcomes with adenomyosis features located near the endometrium and with larger uterine volume. The overall certainty was low or very low for 20 out of 21 outcomes, and moderate for one, primarily driven by imprecision and indirectness related to variation in diagnostic criteria across studies.
INTERPRETATION: Reproductive outcomes in adenomyosis vary according to specific ultrasonographic features, supporting feature-based reporting beyond a binary diagnosis. Substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, including inconsistent ultrasonographic diagnostic criteria, variable application of MUSA definitions, and differences in fertility treatment protocols, warrants cautious interpretation…

articles.title: Prenatal exposure to PFAS and multimodal structural brain development across childhood.
articles.authors: Rocha S, Uy JP, Antonacci C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are ubiquitous environmental pollutants that are posited to be neurotoxic to the developing brain; however, the impact of prenatal exposure to PFAS - particularly to newer, short-chain PFAS - on brain development across childhood is unclear.
METHODS: Concentrations of 9 PFAS were quantified in cord blood plasma of 452 infants (440 for the diffusion sample) who later participated in structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at ages 4.5, 6, 7.5, and 10.5 years, providing estimates of regional cortical thickness and surface area, subcortical volumes, and fractional anisotropy (FA) of key white matter tracts. Longitudinal mixed-effect models estimated associations of PFAS with age 4.5 brain metrics and their developmental trajectories across childhood after correcting for the false discovery rate within PFAS and outcome domains.
RESULTS: Higher concentrations of PFNA and PFDA in cord blood were associated with lower model-estimated age 4.5 surface area of the right paracentral lobule. PFHpA was associated with faster surface area growth in the left rostral anterior cingulate and slower growth in the right caudal middle frontal gyrus from 4.5 to 10.5 years. The short-chain compound PFBS was linked with greater model-estimated age 4.5 FA in 12 white matter tracts, while PFOA and PFNA were linked with lower FA in the middle cerebellar peduncle and the left corticospinal tract, respectively. Associations of PFBS with FA attenuated with age in several tracts.
CONCLUSIONS: Prenatal exposure to PFAS was associated with altered development of frontal and paracentral regions and of white matter microstructure. These findings highlight the need for further research examining the long-term associations of prenatal exposure to PFAS with children's neurodevelopment.

articles.title: Longitudinal pathways from prenatal alcohol exposure and infant behaviors to verbal IQ and working memory.
articles.authors: Singer LT, Schultheis E, Albert JM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Assess infant behaviors as early predictors of Verbal IQ and Working Memory (V/WM) differences related to prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) from 4 to 21 years of age.
STUDY DESIGN: Longitudinal observational study of 387 infants (60% PAE; 48% male; 81% Black), from birth to 21 years. Verbal IQ or Working Memory was measured at 4, 9, 15, or 21yrs. with tests of intellectual functioning. Infants were administered a visual preference task and the Neurobehavioral Assessment (NB) at birth, the Fagan Test of Infant Intelligence (FTII) at 6.5 /12 mo. and Mental Development Index (MDI) of the Bayley Scales at 6.5, 12, 24 mos. Latent growth curve modeling assessed the association of PAE with V/WM over time, assessing infant behaviors as predictors.
RESULTS: 2-year Bayley MDI (Indirect effect (IE) = -0.11, SE = 0.045; p = 0.015) was linked to both PAE and V/WM. Abnormal NB correlated with V/WM (β = -0.21, p = 0.023; β = 0.23, p = 0.047, for intercept and slope, respectively). FTII at 6.5 months correlated with MDI (β = 0.16, p = 0.007) and FTII at 1 year (β=0.17, p = 0.005). Neonatal visual preference marginally correlated with FTII at 6.5 months (β = -0.13, p = 0.097). All relationships were controlled for other prenatal exposures, the home environment, and blood lead level.
CONCLUSIONS: PAE was related to poorer Verbal IQ and WM from 4 to 21 years of age, via 2-year cognitive outcomes associated with 6- and 12-month infant mental and visual recognition performance. Neonatal neurobehavioral abnormalities were related to V/WM independent of PAE. Infant assessments could aid early identification of cognitive sequelae of PAE in high-risk populations.

articles.title: Validity Evidence for Procedure-Specific Competence Assessment Tools in Obstetrics and Gynecology: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Orsten J, Machhiwala M, Green N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Competency-based medical education emphasizes direct learner observation, frequent feedback and clear documentation. To support these goals for training residents in Obstetrics and Gynecology (O&G), there is a need for high quality, objective assessment tools to assess performance. Our study aims to comprehensively review the existing literature on procedure-specific competence assessment tools in O&G.
DESIGN: Using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) guideline, a systematic search was conducted of 6 databases to identify studies containing procedure-specific assessment tools in O&G. Two independent reviewers assessed these tools for validity using Messick's framework, which includes 5 sources of validity: content, response, process, internal structure, relationship to other variables and consequence validity. The educational utility was measured using the Medical Education Research Study Quality Instrument (MERSQI). Methodological quality was measured using the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education tool for evaluating the quality of assessment methods (ACGME). The reviewers compared results and consensus discussion was used to arrive at a single score for each tool.
RESULTS: About 5571 studies were identified, 37 studies underwent full text review, with 14 meeting inclusion criteria. A variety of surgical procedures were evaluated including cesarean section, vaginal hysterectomy, laparoscopic hysterectomy (total and with salpingo-oophorectomy), large loop excision of the transformation zone (LLETZ), Fetoscopic Laser Therapy, laparoscopic salpingectomy, cystoscopy, laparoscopic tubal banding, and myomectomy. Six of these studies assessed simulation-based tools and the remaining 8 studies evaluated live operative or video-based assessments. Most tools demonstrated strong internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.91-0.97), interrater reliability (ICC > 0.80), and construct validity through demonstrated ability to discriminate between experience levels. While many tools demonstrated strong reliability and the ability to distinguish between levels of experience, evidence across other domains of validity was inconsistent. These findings highlight both the feasibility of procedure-specific assessment in O&G and the substantial work that remains to support its use within CBME.
CONCLUSIONS: With a cultural shift in the design of surgical education toward more formal evaluation of resident…

articles.title: Characteristics of Women Ages 40-60 with Menopausal Symptoms: United States, 2025.
articles.authors: Vahratian A, Clayton JA
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The menopausal transition is a critical window for the health of women and may serve as an inflection point for the onset of chronic disease. During this transition, a woman's ovaries become less efficient at producing estrogen and progesterone, and women may experience symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, insomnia or sleep disturbances, and abnormal uterine bleeding. This report describes demographic and geographic characteristics of women ages 40-60 who had menopausal symptoms in the past 12 months using data from the 2025 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS). Estimates of current prescription medication use for menopausal symptoms by age are also provided.
METHODS: NHIS is a nationally representative household survey of the civilian, non-institutionalized U.S. population. Point estimates and the corresponding confidence intervals for this analysis were calculated using SAS-callable SUDAAN software to account for the complex sample design of NHIS.
KEY FINDINGS: In 2025, nearly one in two women (49.4%) ages 40-60 who were not currently pregnant, postpartum, or in surgical menopause reported menopausal symptoms in the past 12 months. The presence of symptoms varied by age, race and ethnicity, educational attainment, and urbanization level. Women ages 48-51 (62.0%) and 52-55 (67.4%) were the most likely to report menopausal symptoms compared with younger and older women. Among women who reported menopausal symptoms in the past 12 months, 15.6% indicated that they were currently taking a prescription medication for those symptoms. Of these women, prescription use was highest among women ages 52-55 and 56-60.

articles.title: Modular Chemical Barcodes Enable Pooled Screening of Multimaterial Nanoparticle Libraries via GC-MS Quantitation.
articles.authors: Vaidya K, Karmaker S, Boehnke N et al.
articles.abstract: Nanoparticle barcoding is a powerful approach to accelerate preclinical screening of nanotherapeutics by enabling rapid collection of high-volume data using fewer biological resources, with reduced experimental labor and fewer confounding variables across experiments. We previously introduced aryl halide-based tags (halocodes) as a barcoding technology with sensitive gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) detection, enabling nanoparticle tracking with minimal halocode incorporation and without measurably altering nanoparticle physicochemical properties. Building on this foundation, in this work, we developed a next generation of alkoxy-modified halocodes with tunable chemical properties that enhance encapsulation and stability within nanomaterials and extend the halocoding platform to lipid-based systems. By systematically varying halocode chemical structure and nanoparticle synthesis parameters, we established design rules governing halocode loading and retention in both polymeric nanoparticles and liposomes. We then leveraged next generation halocodes to perform a pooled in vitro screen of a mixed-core PLGA and liposomal-based nanoparticle library to identify nanoparticle core and surface chemistries with the highest affinity for ovarian cancer cells. Together, next generation halocodes provide a more modular and broadly compatible barcoding toolkit that simplifies pooled screening and supports quantitative evaluation of diverse nanocarrier libraries across biological settings.

articles.title: Individualizing Diagnosis and Management of Stress Urinary Incontinence in Neurogenic Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction.
articles.authors: Feinberg A, Koch GE, Patel HV et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI), defined as involuntary leakage with effort, exertion, sneezing, or coughing, remains a significant cause of morbidity. While well characterized in the general population, SUI in the setting of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction (NLUTD) poses unique diagnostic and management challenges. This review outlines sex-specific epidemiology, diagnostic strategies, and evolving management approaches for SUI in NLUTD, emphasizing individualized and mechanism-based care.
RECENT FINDINGS: Incontinence prevalence varies by neurologic diagnosis, with estimates ranging from 23.6% in patients who suffered from stroke to over 50% in patients with spinal cord injury (SCI) and multiple sclerosis (MS). The underlying pathophysiology is highly variable, with neurologic disease influencing detrusor and sphincter function in unpredictable ways. Urodynamic studies have proven especially valuable in this population for distinguishing between sphincteric incompetence and detrusor-driven incontinence, guiding treatment decisions that help safeguard renal function. Noninvasive strategies, including pelvic floor therapy, mechanical devices, and limited pharmacologic options, offer modest benefit and often are constrained by neurologic deficits. Surgical interventions, such as urethral slings, artificial urinary sphincters (AUS), and, in select salvage cases, bladder neck closure, remain central for refractory disease. Recent multicenter studies highlight variable outcomes, with AUS demonstrating durable efficacy, while urethral slings remain appropriate in carefully selected patients with variable anatomy.

articles.title: Microbial Imprints of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Longitudinal Shifts in Breast Milk, Areola Skin, and Infant Gut.
articles.authors: Hong Z, Luo J, Xie Z et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) has been associated with alterations in maternal and infant gut microbiota. However, it remains unclear whether these associations extend to other maternal-infant microbial niches and persist during early infancy. This study aimed to characterise longitudinal associations between GDM and microbiota across human milk, areolar skin, and infant faecal niches during early life. We followed 104 mother-infant pairs (52 GDM and 52 controls) from delivery through 6 months postpartum. Human milk, areolar skin, and infant faecal samples were collected at 1, 4, and 6 months postpartum and profiled using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Longitudinal associations were evaluated using mixed-effects models, permutational multivariate analysis of variance, and Spearman correlation. GDM was associated with differences in maternal and infant microbiota across all three niches. Reduced alpha diversity was observed in areolar skin, whereas significant GDM-by-time interactions were identified in human milk and infant faecal microbiota. Beta-diversity analyses revealed persistent differences in microbial community composition. At the genus level, GDM was associated with enrichment of Staphylococcus and temporal changes in Stenotrophomonas in human milk, decreases in Rothia in areolar skin, and an increase in Staphylococcus in infant faeces. Significant associations were also observed between several GDM-related maternal taxa and corresponding infant faecal taxa. In conclusion, GDM was associated with persistent and niche-specific microbial differences across interconnected maternal-infant microbial niches during early life. These findings provide new insights into maternal-infant microbiota in the context of GDM and support future mechanistic investigations.

articles.title: Negotiating Reproductive Identity After Cancer: A Qualitative Systematic Review of Female Survivors' Post-Treatment Fertility Experiences.
articles.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
articles.authors: Wang Y, Turnbull ML, Oktavianus J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fertility concerns are common among female cancer survivors and are shaped by sociocultural influences that extend beyond biomedical outcomes. Previous systematic reviews have consolidated evidence on fertility-related distress but have tended to operate within clinical or descriptive frameworks. Although identity-related findings have emerged in existing reviews, they received limited conceptual attention.
OBJECTIVE: Guided by the concept of reproductive identity, this review systematically synthesises qualitative research on how female cancer survivors experience, negotiate, and reconstruct their reproductive identities within the broader context of post-cancer survivorship.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in eight databases for qualitative studies published in English and Chinese between January 2010 and February 2026. The review followed PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024604353). Data were synthesised using thematic synthesis, with coding conducted inductively before the reproductive identity framework was applied as an interpretive lens.
RESULTS: Thirty studies met the inclusion criteria. Three analytical themes were identified: (1) macro-level discourses and structures shape reproductive identity-fertility is positioned as secondary to survival within cancer care and constrained by sociocultural motherhood narratives; (2) micro-level relational dynamics and internal processes shape reproductive identity-fertility concerns are navigated within intimate relationships and through ongoing (re)working of reproductive selfhood; and (3) lived experience informs the reimagining of macro-level care-participants' experiences of structural constraints generated insight into how care systems could better support reproductive identity across survivorship.
CONCLUSION: The findings of this review highlight that post-cancer fertility is a dynamic process of identity negotiation shaped by the interplay between macro-level discourses and micro-level relational and internal processes. This reinforces the importance of embedding reproductive identity literacy into survivorship care through proactive, clinician-initiated fertility conversations and coordinated referral pathways that extend beyond the treatment phase.
PATIENT AND PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patient and public involvement were not formally incorporated into this review. However, the first author is a female cancer survivor with lived experience of…

articles.title: The Role of Natural Killer Cells and Immune Factors in Implantation Failure in Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.authors: Eslaminia F, Fakhri F, Baig MR et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine-metabolic disorder linked to infertility and adverse reproductive outcomes. Emerging evidence highlights immune dysregulation, particularly involving natural killer (NK) cells, as a key driver of PCOS-associated implantation failure. Successful embryo implantation requires precise dialogue between the embryo and maternal endometrium, mediated by immune cells. Uterine NK (uNK) cells, the dominant immune population at the maternal-fetal interface in early pregnancy, display low cytotoxicity and high immunoregulatory and angiogenic activity. These features support trophoblast invasion, spiral artery remodeling, and maternal-fetal tolerance. In PCOS, chronic low-grade inflammation, hyperandrogenism, and insulin resistance alter immune cell phenotypes, cytokine production, and NK cell function. Such disruptions compromise the immunological balance essential for endometrial receptivity, potentially triggering recurrent implantation failure and early pregnancy loss. This review analyzes the role of NK cells and immune factors in PCOS-related implantation failure. Clarifying the crosstalk between endocrine, metabolic, and immune pathways provides deeper insights into reproductive dysfunction in PCOS, offering potential therapeutic targets to enhance implantation rates and pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Application of Immersive and Semi-Immersive Extended Reality Training Systems in Acupuncture Education: Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Jeong H, Park H, Ahn J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acupuncture training requires precise acupoint localization and needle control, yet peer-to-peer practice raises safety concerns and physical phantoms offer limited anatomical fidelity. Extended reality (XR) is increasingly used in health professions education, but immersive and semi-immersive XR training systems for acupuncture have not been mapped.
OBJECTIVE: This scoping review aimed to map the applications, hardware modalities, and reported technical and educational outcomes of immersive and semi-immersive XR training systems in acupuncture education.
METHODS: This review followed the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) and the five-stage scoping review framework of Arksey and O'Malley, as refined by Levac and colleagues. On September 19, 2026, we searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, CNKI, RISS, ScienceOn, and OASIS. No language or date restrictions were applied. Backward and forward citation searching supplemented the database search. Eligible sources were peer-reviewed original studies or full conference papers describing virtual reality (VR; either fully immersive [IVR] or semi-immersive [SIVR]), augmented reality (AR), or mixed reality (MR) systems for acupuncture training. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted the study design, hardware, training task, and outcomes. Each study was assigned an evidence tier.
RESULTS: Of 6176 records, 3378 were screened after removal of duplicates and ineligible document types, 80 reports were assessed in full text, and 26 studies were included (25 from databases and 1 from citation searching). Most studies came from East Asia (25/26, 96.2%), mainly China (n=18), and 20 (76.9%) were published between 2020 and 2026. Systems used VR (n=15), AR (n=5), or MR (n=6); 19 were IVR and 7 were SIVR. Training tasks addressed acupoint localization (n=13), needling skills (n=11), and clinical reasoning (n=2). Localization errors were reported with different metrics and were not directly comparable across systems. In a randomized comparison, a VR group scored higher on practical skills than a conventional instruction group (32.52, SD 2.28 vs 28.62, SD 2.77 points; P<.001). In an MR simulator with depth-responsive vibrotactile feedback active in both sessions, mean depth error decreased from 6.41 mm in the first practice session to 3.58 mm in the second. Of the 26 studies, 7 used a comparative design; the rest were…

articles.title: Hypoxia-Driven CA2 Promotes Trophoblast Dysfunction in Preeclampsia.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.authors: Chen L, Zhu C, Zhao J et al.
articles.abstract: Explore the potential function of Carbonic Anhydrase 2 (CA2) in the pathophysiology of preeclampsia. Peripheral blood and placental samples were collected from healthy pregnant women and patients with preeclampsia. Placental CA2 expression was validated in independent clinical cohorts and experimental mouse models. HTR-8/SVneo cells were cultured and transfected with a CA2 overexpression plasmid to evaluate trophoblast dysfunction. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed to identify downstream genes associated with CA2 overexpression, followed by VEGFA rescue experiments. Hypoxia-related regulation of CA2 was investigated. Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated siRNA against CA2 was constructed in an L-NAME-induced PE model to evaluate therapeutic effects. CA2 expression was significantly increased in placental tissues and maternal serum from women with PE and was also elevated in experimental PE mouse models. CA2 predominantly localized in trophoblast cells, and correlated positively with serum creatinine and urea and correlated negatively with fetal birth weight. CA2 overexpression markedly suppressed trophoblast proliferation, migration, and invasion, without affecting apoptosis. Transcriptomic analysis suggested that vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) acted as a downstream mediator of CA2, and VEGFA overexpression partially rescued CA2-induced trophoblast dysfunction. CA2 expression was upregulated under hypoxic conditions and regulated by hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α). LNP-mediated CA2 silencing partially improved placental structure and fetal outcomes in vivo. CA2 is upregulated in the preeclamptic placenta and is associated with placental dysfunction and adverse fetal outcomes. Mechanistically, CA2 may act downstream of HIF-1α and contribute to trophoblast dysfunction partly through modulation of VEGFA signaling, and CA2 silencing partially improved maternal and fetal outcomes, highlighting CA2 as a potential therapeutic target for preeclampsia.

articles.title: Building digital pregnancies from the single cell up.
articles.authors: Scott AK
articles.abstract: Single-cell digital twins connect in vitro drug screening studies with clinical outcomes, providing a new framework to evaluate therapies and advance precision medicine in pregnancy.

articles.title: DMRT1 is required at two steps of ovarian differentiation in rabbits.
articles.authors: Dujardin E, Poulat F, Aura IB et al.
articles.abstract: The transcription factor Doublesex and Mab-3 Related Transcription Factor 1 (DMRT1) is essential for testis differentiation and male fertility, but less is known about its potential involvement in ovarian differentiation. In mice, Dmrt1-/- females are fertile, although they show a reduction of Stra8 expression. Using our DMRT1 mutant rabbit model, we analyzed ovarian differentiation when DMRT1 expression is abolished. First, we observed that during early gonadal development, DMRT1-/- gonads display a specific transcriptome different from control ovaries and control testes. Second, we assessed the infertility phenotype of mutant females. DMRT1 is highly expressed in germ cells until meiosis initiation, and its disruption leads to a down-regulation of key genes involved in the meiotic process. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing data highlighted that DMRT1 can bind these genes in the rabbit ovary. Our study using the rabbit model shows that in addition to its role in testicular differentiation, DMRT1 has two important functions in ovarian differentiation: an initial involvement in the differentiation of somatic cells and a pivotal role in the differentiation of germ cells. Our data suggested that DMRT1 could be considered in human health as a gene necessary for female fertility.

articles.title: Single-cell-level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies.
articles.authors: Einhaus J, Neidlinger P, Fondeur O et al.
articles.abstract: Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type-specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell-level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO's digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4+ T cells.

articles.title: Beyond conventional indicators: Reproductive coercion and its overlap with measured intimate partner violence in Bangladesh.
articles.authors: Khan MN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reproductive coercion is an under-recognised form of violence against women and is not routinely captured by standard measures of intimate partner violence, which commonly focus on physical, sexual, and emotional violence. This study examined the association between reproductive coercion and these measured forms of intimate partner violence and estimated the proportion of women who reported reproductive coercion without reporting any of the physical, sexual, or emotional violence items included in the survey.
METHODS: We analysed nationally representative data from 24,951 ever-married women, including 22,161 currently married women, in the Bangladesh Violence Against Women Survey 2024. Outcomes were physical, sexual, emotional, and any conventional IPV, assessed in the past 12 months among currently married women and over the lifetime among ever-married women. Exposures were reproductive coercion pattern and contraceptive coercion typology. Survey-weighted Poisson regression with robust standard errors estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% CIs for associations with conventional IPV. Survey-weighted logistic regression examined factors associated with reproductive coercion without reported conventional IPV and was considered exploratory because of the small number of events. Survey-weighted prevalence estimates were applied to 2022 census population counts to derive population estimates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs).
FINDINGS: In the past 12 months, 27.30% of currently married women reported conventional IPV and 3.59% reported reproductive coercion; corresponding lifetime prevalences among ever-married women were 60.40% and 9.25%. Including reproductive coercion increased the prevalence of any reported abuse to 28.61% and 61.18%, respectively. Reproductive coercion was associated with a higher prevalence of each form of conventional IPV, with the largest aPRs among women reporting multiple forms of reproductive coercion. Reproductive coercion without reported conventional IPV was reported by 1.31% (95% CI 1.08-1.59) of currently married women in the past 12 months and 0.78% (0.60-1.01) of ever-married women over the lifetime, corresponding to approximately 645,483 (95% UI 532,154-783,449) and 437,414 (337,106-567,462) women, respectively.
INTERPRETATION: Reproductive coercion captures a dimension of violence against women that is only partly reflected in conventional IPV measures. Women reporting reproductive coercion…

articles.title: Carboplatin Plus Mirvetuximab Soravtansine In Platinum-Sensitive Ovarian Cancer: A Phase 2 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
articles.authors: Konecny GE, Lim PC, Santin AD et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evaluate efficacy and safety of carboplatin plus mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV) in folate receptor alpha (FRa)-expressing recurrent PSOC.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This phase 2, single arm trial enrolled patients with recurrent FRa-expressing (≥25% of tumor cells with ≥2+ membrane intensity) PSOC and 1 prior platinum-based therapy. Patients received up to 6-8 cycles of carboplatin (AUC 5) plus MIRV (6mg/kg AIBW) Q3W, followed by single-agent MIRV. Primary and key secondary endpoints were investigator-assessed objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 in the FRa ≥50% group and FRa ≥25% group (ie, overall population), respectively.
RESULTS: Among 125 enrolled patients (102 FRα ≥50%; 61 prior PARPi), ORR by end of 6 combination cycles was 62.7% (95% CI, 52.6-72.1) in the FRα ≥50% group and 62.4% (95% CI, 53.3-70.9) in the overall population. Most patients (n=101; 81%) transitioned to single-agent MIRV continuation with durable responses. Patients with FRa ≥25% had median duration of response of 11.2 months (95% CI, 8.5-13.6) and median progression-free survival of 11.0 months (95% CI, 9.8-13.1). Most common adverse events (AEs) were blurred vision (81%) and corneal events (74%); 96.7% of corneal cases resolved or had final grade 1. Treatment-emergent AEs led to MIRV and carboplatin discontinuation in 15% and 9%, respectively. Adjudicated treatment-related pneumonitis occurred in 19 (15.2%) patients: 14 grade 1-2; 3 grade 3-4, and 2 fatal cases.
CONCLUSIONS: Carboplatin plus MIRV was manageable with dose modifications for AEs and showed meaningful activity, including in PARPi-exposed patients, supporting further evaluation in PSOC.

articles.title: Predictors of preeclampsia with severe features: A multi-center analysis of maternal and health system factors in Thai tertiary hospitals.
articles.authors: Boonyaporn T, Limruangrong P, Ratinthorn A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia (PE) with severe features threatens maternal and neonatal health. This study examined maternal and health-service factors associated with severe features and compared maternal and neonatal outcomes in Thailand.
METHODS: This case-control study enrolled 156 postpartum women with PE (52 with and 104 without severe features) and 111 nurse-midwives in antenatal care, labor, and postpartum units across four Thai tertiary hospitals. Data were collected using postpartum and nurse-midwife questionnaires, and a maternal-neonatal health record form. Group differences were assessed using independent t-test, chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Multivariable binary logistic regression examined factors associated with severe features, adjusting for antenatal care visits and gravidity.
RESULTS: Women with severe features more often had a history of PE (32.7% vs. 13.5%, p = 0.006) and differed in BMI distribution (p = 0.007). Three maternal factors were independently associated with severe features: history of PE (aOR = 5.99, 95% CI 2.13-16.83), BMI (aOR = 0.92 per kg/m2, 95% CI 0.86-0.98), and moderate versus low PE knowledge (aOR = 0.13, 95% CI 0.04-0.50). No health-service variable, including nurse training, was independently associated with severe features after adjustment (all p > 0.05). The model explained 29.4% (Nagelkerke R2) of the variance in PE severity and correctly classified 75.8% of cases. Infant birth weight was lower among women with severe features (p < 0.05); delivery mode, hospital stay, birth asphyxia, and NICU admission did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSION: A history of PE was associated with higher odds, and moderate (versus low) PE knowledge and higher BMI with lower odds, of severe features. These findings support prioritizing screening for prior PE history and structured antenatal knowledge counseling, together with adequately powered, multilevel studies to clarify the role of health-service factors in PE severity.

articles.title: Childhood Cancer Risk After Assisted Reproductive Technology.
articles.authors: Mose K, Kjaer SK, Jensen A et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Childhood cancer risk after assisted reproductive technology (ART) remains uncertain, particularly by procedure and cancer type.
OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between ART and childhood cancer overall and by ART modality and cancer type.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND POPULATION: Nationwide Danish cohort of 1 086 136 live-born children from 1996 to 2012, of whom 37 228 (3.4%) were conceived using ART, with follow-up through 2023.
EXPOSURES: Maternal ART, classified as in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection, or frozen embryo transfer.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Incident childhood cancer. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs); Poisson models estimated incidence rates. Non-ART births were the primary reference; secondary analyses used children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 20 years, 3736 cancers occurred. Compared with non-ART births (incidence rate, 18.3 per 100 000 person-years), children conceived using ART had higher cancer incidence (incidence rate, 23.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 1.07-1.48]). Rates were higher after frozen embryo transfer (incidence rate, 41.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.18 [95% CI, 1.45-3.29]) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (incidence rate, 27.9 per 100 000; HR, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.16-1.89]) but not IVF (incidence rate, 18.5 per 100 000; HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.79-1.28]). Frozen embryo transfer was associated with leukemia (incidence rate, 11.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.36 [95% CI, 1.06-5.28]), lymphomas (HR, 3.03 [95% CI, 1.13-8.12]), and soft tissue sarcomas (HR, 7.63 [95% CI, 2.82-20.62]); intracytoplasmic sperm injection was associated with lymphomas (incidence rate, 4.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.94 [95% CI, 1.07-3.54]), soft tissue sarcomas (incidence rate, 3.3 per 100 000; HR, 3.28 [95% CI, 1.54-7.00]), and central nervous system neoplasms (incidence rate, 8.2 per 100 000; HR, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.04-2.57]); no associations were observed for IVF. Findings were similar in secondary analyses using children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: ART, particularly frozen embryo transfer and intracytoplasmic sperm injection, was associated with increased childhood cancer risk, but absolute risks were low. The consistent results in secondary analyses of children with maternal infertility history or conceived via IVF suggest…

articles.title: Effects of a maternal ketogenic diet on maternal and offspring metabolic health in mice.
articles.authors: Ruano AH, Kracaw RA, Cervantes IA et al.
articles.abstract: Ketogenic (keto) diets have gained popularity due to their potential benefits on weight loss and metabolic conditions. However, the consequences of consuming a keto diet before, during, and after pregnancy on maternal and offspring health remain incompletely understood. To investigate this, female Swiss Webster mice were randomly assigned to either a keto or control diet. After 6 weeks on diet, females were mated and maintained on their respective diets throughout pregnancy and lactation. In experiment 1, glucose tolerance tests (GTT) were performed on pregnant dams at gestational day (GD) 16.5. At GD 17.5, dams were euthanized, urine was collected for ketone analysis, and fetal and placental weights were recorded. In experiment 2, dams delivered naturally and one male and one female offspring per dam were retained and weighed weekly. At 12 weeks of age, offspring underwent GTT, followed by euthanasia and serum collection for insulin and leptin analysis. Compared with controls, keto dams exhibited increased body weight, impaired glucose tolerance, elevated urinary ketones, and reduced circulating insulin during late gestation (p < 0.05). Fetuses from keto dams were significantly smaller (p < 0.05), whereas placental weight and placental efficiency were unchanged. Offspring from keto dams tended to have lower body weights during early postnatal development; however, longitudinal analysis did not identify a significant overall effect of maternal diet or a maternal diet x time interaction. At 12 weeks, keto offspring exhibited a modest but statistically significant improvement in glucose tolerance compared to control offspring (p < 0.05). Male keto offspring had significantly decreased serum insulin (p < 0.05) compared to male control offspring, while no differences were observed in females. Serum leptin levels did not differ between diet groups, although sex differences present in control offspring were not observed in keto offspring. In this exploratory mouse study, ketogenic diet consumption was associated with altered maternal glucose homeostasis during pregnancy and reduced fetal growth, although these maternal and fetal findings were derived from a limited number of independent pregnancies and require confirmation in larger studies. Offspring exposed to maternal ketogenic diet demonstrated modest metabolic differences at 12 weeks of age. Together, these findings support further investigation of the maternal and developmental consequences of ketogenic…

articles.title: Estimated incidence and number of new cases with prenatal alcohol exposure and fetal alcohol spectrum disorders in Finland 1990-2025.
articles.authors: Jolma M, Koivu-Jolma M, Gissler M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD) arising from prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) are the leading preventable cause of neurobehavioral disorders. Early pregnancy is particularly vulnerable to ethanol toxicity, yet alcohol use often continues until pregnancy recognition. In Finland, national incidence estimates of PAE and FASD remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the incidence of any PAE and heavy PAE in Finland between 1990 and 2025, and to model the annual number of children with FASD born in Finland.
METHODS: We developed a mathematical modelling framework integrating studies on alcohol use during pregnancy in Finland, biomarker-based estimates of heavy PAE, national population statistics, and international active case ascertainment studies on FASD prevalence. Incidence of any PAE was estimated from self-reported alcohol use, including pre-recognition exposure. Heavy PAE was estimated by combining binge-drinking prevalence, delayed pregnancy recognition, biomarker data and anonymous self-reports. FASD incidence was modelled using two approaches: 1) an international multiplier linking FASD prevalence to heavy episodic drinking prevalence among women (Model M), and 2) a conventional epidemiological ratio between any PAE and FASD (Model L).
RESULTS: Self-reported alcohol use during pregnancy declined following abstinence recommendations in the early 2000s, while pre-recognition use remained relatively stable. Heavy PAE decreased from 9% (uncertainty range 7-11%) in the 1990s to 6% (4-8%) in the early 2020s. Any PAE declined from 75% (60-85%) to 32% (26-38%). Modelled FASD incidence showed similar decreasing trends, ranging from 6.8% to 5.6% (Model M), and from 6% to 3% (Model L).
CONCLUSION: PAE remains common in Finland, and the burden of FASD is substantial despite declining trends. Additional biomarker-based studies of PAE and active case ascertainment of FASD are needed to refine current estimates. Strengthened public health efforts to reduce PAE, including the efforts before recognition of pregnancy, are essential.

articles.title: Systematic differences between ultrasound and MRI assessment of fetal ventricular width in cases of fetal mild ventriculomegaly: a cohort study.
articles.authors: Mikulska B, Jaczynska R, Sobieraj-Binkiewicz P et al.
articles.abstract: Prenatal assessment of the lateral ventricles is essential for detecting and classifying fetal ventriculomegaly (VM). Although ultrasound (US) is the primary screening tool, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is increasingly used to complement diagnosis. However, discrepancies between US and MRI measurements, particularly in mild VM, may affect classification, counseling, and planning clinical management. The aim of the study is to compare US and MRI measurements of the fetal lateral ventricles, evaluate the agreement between both methods, with particular focus on mild ventriculomegaly, and additionally assess the feasibility of deriving conversion formulas between both modalities. Methods This cohort study included 120 fetuses examined between 2011 and 2021 at a referral center: 75 with isolated mild VM and 45 controls. All underwent a standardized US assessment and fetal MRI. Ventricular width was measured twice for each modality; mean values were used for statistical comparison. Analysis included Wilcoxon tests, Friedman tests, Bland-Altman plots, Pearson's chi-square tests, Theil-Sen regression, and linear modeling. Results MRI systematically provided greater ventricular measurements than US. In the study group, the bias was 0.71mm for coronal MRI and 0.33mm for axial MRI. Agreement between methods was limited, with measurement discrepancies observed in 34% of cases (coronal) and 33.3% (axial). Combined analysis of both groups confirmed persistent measurement discrepancies, though the overall axial MRI bias decreased to 0.15mm. Theil-Sen modelling enabled the development of conversion formulas for both measurement planes. Conclusions MRI measurements of the fetal lateral ventricles tend to be slightly higher than ultrasound measurements, particularly in the coronal plane. These systematic differences may change the VM classification and should be considered in clinical interpretation. Ultrasound demonstrated better measurement reproducibility. The obtained formulas may support improved cross-modality comparison in clinical practice.

articles.title: Australian women's perspectives on gendered vulnerability, commercial power, and resistance to the commercialization of menopause.
articles.authors: Thomas SL, McCarthy S, Pitt H et al.
articles.abstract: A range of commercial actors actively shape how menopause is understood, experienced, and managed. While existing research highlights concerns about commercial influence, much less is known about how women themselves interpret, negotiate, and respond to these commercialized menopause environments. Using an online qualitative survey, this study explored the opinions of n = 362 Australian cisgender women (45-64 years) about the commercialization of menopause. Data were interpreted using a reflexive approach to thematic analysis, with three themes constructed from the data. (i) 'Commercialization as awareness raising, knowledge and choice'-in which women viewed the growing commercial interest in menopause as a positive development and evidence that women's experiences were being recognized. (ii) 'Profiting from gendered vulnerability'-where women felt that the rapid commercialization of menopause created at least some level of financial or emotional risk. They questioned whether commercial interests were genuinely motivated by concern for women's well-being, or financial gain. (iii) 'Navigating crowded menopause information environments'-in which women stated that the sheer volume of menopause content available online and particularly through social media platforms, often contributed to feelings of confusion, information fatigue, and disengagement. Commercial attention to menopause blurs the boundaries between information and marketing and shifts responsibility for navigating risk onto individuals. A critical approach to menopause must address the commercial systems that shape what women know, what they are encouraged to celebrate or fear, what they are invited to buy, and what forms of care and support are made available to them.

articles.title: Intraoperative Ultrasound Guided Sling Adjustment During Transobturator Sling Placement: A Preliminary Pilot Report of the Technical Protocol and Feasibility.
articles.journal: International journal of urology : official journal of the Japanese Urological Association
articles.authors: Huang WC, Yang JM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe a qualitative intraoperative ultrasound protocol for transobturator mid-urethral sling adjustment and assess technical feasibility.
METHODS: This retrospective pilot series included 58 consecutive women with urodynamically confirmed stress urinary incontinence or stress-predominant mixed urinary incontinence undergoing outside-in transobturator sling placement. Sagittal and axial images guided gentle traction for a visible tape-urethra gap and tension release for urethral encroachment. Sling-arm oscillation supplemented assessment when acoustic shadowing limited visualization. Feasibility measures included visualization, adjustment frequency, final sonographic findings, scanning duration, and intraoperative complications. Clinical outcomes were summarized using available cases.
RESULTS: The tape was visualized in all 58 procedures and adjusted in 26 (44.8%). No final residual gap or encroachment was observed. Median scanning duration was 3 min 45 s (interquartile range, 3-4 min); no intraoperative complications were recorded. All 58 women provided baseline and 3-month questionnaire data. Mean six-item Urogenital Distress Inventory scores decreased from 68.3 ± 17.2 to 20.0 ± 6.7; seven-item Incontinence Impact Questionnaire scores decreased from 75.4 ± 10.5 to 18.2 ± 6.7. At 36 months, 20/58 women (34.5%) had outcome data. All 20 met the objective stress continence criterion (exact two-sided 95% confidence interval, 83.2%-100%); none met the objective voiding dysfunction criterion (exact two-sided 95% confidence interval, 0%-16.8%). These findings concern only the retained subgroup.
CONCLUSIONS: The protocol was technically feasible in this single-surgeon, single-center series. Reproducibility, workflow burden, and clinical benefit require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Personal Menstrual Health Knowledge in Individuals With Intellectual Disabilities.
articles.journal: Journal of applied research in intellectual disabilities : JARID
articles.authors: St John L, Panech A, McHugh TL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with intellectual disabilities are at risk of having poor health literacy related to menstrual health due to persistent barriers in accessing education, healthcare, and tailored resources; however, no research has explored this.
OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study is to assess menstrual health knowledge in individuals with intellectual disabilities.
METHOD: A cross-sectional survey design was used. Data were collected from 75 Special Olympics athletes (age 37.3 years) using a subset of questions from the Socio-Sexual Knowledge and Attitudes Test-Revised (SSKAAT-R).
RESULTS: The final analyses included 72 participants. Total scores on the SSKAAT-R ranged from 0-8, with a median total score of 5. Few participants (n = 25; 35%) were able to correctly respond to questions related to hygiene practices, with 65% (n = 47) responding incorrectly.
CONCLUSION: Future research should focus on addressing the critical need for inclusive and accessible menstrual health education and resources for this population.

articles.title: Releasing the syndrome from captivity: why renaming PCOS to PMOS widens reproductive care beyond the anovulatory frame.
articles.authors: Piltonen TT, Teede HJ, Bahri Khomami M
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) has long been focused on the ovary and infertility aspects, rooted in the early observations by Stein and Leventhal (1935). The aggregated data, however, show that the syndrome has a wide comorbidity risk beyond fertility aspects involving several endocrine and metabolic derangements, yet without a true risk of ovarian cysts, benign or pathological, as expected with the old name. Moreover, with modern fertility care, women with the condition can reach cumulative childbirth rates comparable to those of unaffected women. The women may have spontaneous ovulations and pregnancies across the reproductive life course and, having high ovarian reserve, enter the menopause later. The endometrium and pregnancy complications have, however, been the blind spots in fertility care. Taking all this into account, in May 2026, a multi-step global consensus process culminating in a Lancet statement renamed the condition polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), with transitional adoption already underway in current international guidance and consolidation into the next major international evidence-based guideline update scheduled for 2028. This opinion argues that the rename is not a cosmetic relabelling but a clinical mandate to widen fertility and pregnancy care, address fragmented care across primary, fertility, obstetric, and endocrine services, and acknowledge the endocrine, metabolic, psychological, and oncological burden. For Human Reproduction's readership, the 2028 guideline update is the concrete deadline around which language, registry coding, trial protocols, education, and clinical practice can align.

articles.title: Perinatal health outcomes in relation to principal applicant and live-in caregiver status among economic class immigrants to Canada: A retrospective analysis of births from 1993 to 2017.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of public health = Revue canadienne de sante publique
articles.authors: Shapiro GD, Ng E, Ramadan M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Economic class immigrants to Canada tend to have better health outcomes than other immigrant groups. However, variation may exist even within this population.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of data from the Migrant Maternal and Infant Morbidity and Mortality (MMIMM) dataset, which linked Canadian birth and infant death records (1993-2017) with maternal immigration records (1952-2017). All singleton births to economic class immigrant women at least 18 years of age at immigration were analyzed. Women were classified as principal applicants (PA), non-principal applicants (NPA), or former live-in caregivers (LIC); all analyses were stratified by marital status at landing. Outcomes examined included preterm birth (PTB), small- and large-for-gestational-age birth (SGA and LGA, respectively), stillbirth, and infant mortality. Risk ratios for adverse outcomes by PA and former LIC status were estimated with adjustment for parental, birth, and immigration characteristics.
RESULTS: The cohort included 490,310 births (165,850 births to PAs, 267,200 to NPAs, 57,160 to former LICs). In adjusted analyses, among women who were single at landing, NPA had slightly lower rates of LGA (fully adjusted risk ratio (aRR) = 0.92, 95% CI 0.87-0.98) and stillbirth (aRR = 0.72, 95% CI 0.53-0.97) compared to PA, and former LICs had slightly elevated rates of PTB (aRR 1.05, 95% CI 1.00-1.11) and SGA (1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.10).
CONCLUSION: These findings add to existing literature highlighting the vulnerability of live-in caregivers in Canada while shedding light on possible differences between principal and non-principal applicants.

articles.title: Incorporating Lesion-Level Heterogeneity in a Branching-Process Model of Ovarian Cancer Metastasis.
articles.authors: Levy D
articles.abstract: Danesh et al. (J. Theor. Biol., 2012) estimated the ovarian cancer screening window at roughly 2.9 years, using a multi-type branching process and the hitting time of an aggregate mass threshold. We extend the model of Danesh et al. to incorporate the lesion-level heterogeneity characteristic of intraperitoneal metastasis, replacing the homogeneous secondary compartment by a vector of distinct lesions whose formation follows a Chinese Restaurant Process with concentration parameter α . We prove three results. Because established metastases divide faster than the peritoneal source compartment, the rate of de novo lesion formation is almost surely integrable, so only finitely many lesions ever form and no Yule-Simon power law emerges. Mapping the system to a time-inhomogeneous Hoppe-Polya urn yields a martingale whose almost-sure convergence fixes relative lesion masses at values set by early stochastic events. Kurtz fluid limits give a closed-form trajectory for the largest lesion, whose hitting time of the radiological resolution threshold replaces aggregate mass as the clinical endpoint. A parameter-free criterion follows: the disease is radiologically detectable before it becomes lethal precisely when the largest lesion's share of the total metastatic mass exceeds the ratio of the imaging resolution limit to the lethal burden. Simulation validates each result and shows the phenotype is governed jointly by α and the peritoneal migration intensity. Calibrating against published surgical series, a fit to the reported prevalence of miliary disease reproduces the observed implant-size dichotomy out of sample and predicts a monotone decline of the screening window with lesion count.

articles.title: Diagnosis and management of polycystic ovary syndrome/polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: unmet needs and areas of clinical confidence among European endocrinologists.
articles.authors: Livadas S, Yildiz BO, Obermayer-Pietsch B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) or polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a common, heterogeneous endocrine disorder whose diagnosis and management remain variable across clinical settings. Despite contemporary international guidance, several diagnostic definitions and therapeutic decisions are not consistently applied.
OBJECTIVE: To identify persistent unmet needs and areas of clinical confidence in PCOS/PMOS care, using the 2023 survey of the European Society of Endocrinology PCOS Special Interest Group as the principal data source.
METHODS: This manuscript presents a secondary, survey-informed analysis of aggregate data from an electronic cross-sectional survey distributed to members of the European Society of Endocrinology. A total of 505 respondents participated. Survey findings were interpreted in the context of current guidelines, contemporary evidence, the previous 2014 European survey, and patient-reported priorities.
RESULTS: Considerable variation was observed in the operational definition of chronic ovulatory dysfunction, the assessment of hirsutism, the biochemical evaluation of androgen excess, and the interpretation of ovarian morphology. Only one quarter of respondents reported access to liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry for steroid measurement. Uncertainty also persisted regarding the choice and duration of combined oral contraceptive therapy and the optimal pharmacological approach to chronic anovulation. Conversely, several areas of clinical confidence were evident. Respondents commonly assessed metabolic risk and lifestyle behaviours, recognized the psychological burden of PCOS/PMOS, emphasized lifestyle intervention, and supported multidisciplinary care.
