Physician priorities also showed increasing concordance with the concerns reported by women with PCOS/PMOS.
CONCLUSIONS: PCOS/PMOS care in Europe combines important progress in patient-centered, metabolic, and multidisciplinary management with persistent diagnostic and therapeutic variability. Greater standardization of operational diagnostic definitions, wider access to accurate steroid assays, and adequately powered comparative trials of commonly used treatments are required. These initiatives should be developed alongside, rather than at the expense of, the patient-centered practices that are already well established.
STUDY DESIGN: Secondary analysis and expert interpretation of cross-sectional survey data.

articles.title: The INTERGROWTH-21st Preterm Postnatal Growth Standards are robust across geographical settings and time.
articles.authors: Giuliani F, Gunier RB, Lapillonne A et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: We investigated the robustness of the INTERGROWTH-21st Preterm Postnatal Growth Standards for monitoring the postnatal growth of preterm infants a decade after the original study that produced them. The INTERPRACTICE-21st Study assessed the early postnatal growth of all infants born preterm in 15 study sites across 14 countries. From this sample, we selected a 'standard-like' cohort of mother-newborn dyads as in the original study. Thus, we selected all singleton babies of healthy mothers, born between 27 and < 37 weeks' gestation, without congenital malformations, fetal growth restriction or severe postnatal morbidity, i.e. confirming their eligibility for inclusion in the original standards. We used, across all study sites, the same standardised anthropometric measurements and feeding practices based on human milk. The main outcomes were the skeletal, fat-free mass indicators head circumference and length, following WHO recommendations. Variance component analysis and second-degree fractional polynomial regression models in a multi-level framework accounting for repeated measures were used to compare the growth trajectory of the 'standard-like' cohort to the standards. Of 3634 preterm babies enrolled, 1998 were singletons with complete birth anthropometric data. Among these, 1073 (54%) mother-baby dyads met the 'standard-like' eligibility criteria. The between-site differences in early postnatal growth of head circumference and length accounted for only 10.2% and 12.7% of the total variability of these repeated measures, proportions considerably lower than those for the total between individuals within a site variance of 80% and 79%, respectively. These low proportions supported pooling data across study sites and reinforced the consistency of the original results across geographical settings.
CONCLUSION: The early growth of healthy preterm infants in the INTERPRACTICE-21st 'standard-like' cohort, assessed a decade after the original study, closely matched the pattern originally described by the INTERGROWTH-21st standards, which appear therefore robust to geographical changes and time.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • The INTERGROWTH-21st Preterm Postnatal Growth Standards are the only international standards, based on the WHO prescriptive approach, for monitoring the growth of preterm infants. They were produced by following, from early pregnancy, uncomplicated preterm infants who were born to healthy mothers and achieved adequate growth and development at…

articles.title: Inferring tissue origin from cell-free DNA in metastatic cancer.
articles.authors: Shu A, Li Y, Sun Q et al.
articles.abstract: A major clinical challenge in metastatic cancer management is determining not only the presence of tumor-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) but also the tissue lineage and organ context reflected by circulating cfDNA signals. CfDNA supports such inference by retaining molecular signatures specific to its tissue-of-origin, including DNA methylation, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), fragmentomic profiles, nucleosome positioning patterns, and histone modifications. This review examines the biological principles underlying cfDNA-based tissue-of-origin determination, the computational frameworks used to interpret these signals, and the key barriers to clinical translation. We additionally compare representative deconvolution and classification strategies, including linear and probabilistic models, machine/deep learning, and single-cell-informed reference approaches. Despite substantial progress, clinical integration remains hindered by low tumor fractions, heterogeneous contributions from multiple tissues, background noise from nonmalignant cell death, and a lack of robust prospective validation. We further emphasize that source estimates in metastatic plasma should be interpreted in the context of mixed tissue contributions, differential shedding, reference design, and model uncertainty, rather than as direct measures of anatomical metastatic burden.

articles.title: GSTP1 promoter hypermethylation in prostate cancer detection: current evidence, clinical positioning, and translational gaps.
articles.authors: Joo JL, Wong RS, Goh BH et al.
articles.abstract: GSTP1 promoter hypermethylation is one of the most consistently documented molecular alterations in prostate cancer, with high prevalence in malignant tissue and a well-established relationship with transcriptional silencing. However, despite more than two decades of biological and diagnostic investigation, GSTP1-based testing has not acquired a clearly defined stand-alone role in contemporary prostate cancer detection. This narrative review examines why extensive biological evidence has not translated into routine clinical use and where, if anywhere, GSTP1 testing might provide meaningful value within current diagnostic pathways. Evidence from prostate tissue, urine and circulating cell-free DNA is considered alongside the effects of biospecimen selection, preanalytical handling, CpG target selection, assay design and interpretation thresholds. Tissue demonstrates the most reproducible signal and has achieved partial clinical translation through multiplex testing such as ConfirmMDx, whereas urinary and blood-based approaches remain investigational. Recent urinary findings, including in men with moderately elevated PSA, are promising but remain preliminary and have not established incremental value beyond contemporary risk assessment, biomarkers and multiparametric MRI. The translational priority is therefore not to demonstrate again that GSTP1 detects prostate cancer, but to determine whether a standardised assay provides reproducible, nonredundant and clinically actionable information at a defined decision point. Future development should prioritise clearly specified target populations, analytically validated assay configurations, clinically significant prostate cancer as the relevant endpoint, and prospective evaluation against contemporary diagnostic pathways.

articles.title: The effects of perinatal depression and anxiety on memory, attention, and cognitive flexibility: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Sobral M, Ferreira AM, Tomás A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Women in the perinatal period often report experiencing cognitive difficulties, such as forgetfulness, disorientation, and a reduced attention span. However, evidence from objective neuropsychological studies is inconsistent. Depressive and anxiety symptoms have been proposed as potential contributors to these cognitive challenges, with some studies suggesting a negative association between mood disturbances and cognitive performance during pregnancy and postpartum. This review aims to characterize the relationship between perinatal depressive and anxiety symptoms and cognitive functioning (memory, attention, and cognitive flexibility).
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science and PsycINFO electronic databases. Where at least three studies with comparable designs and outcomes were available, exploratory meta-analyses were conducted and are reported in supplementary material.
RESULTS: We included 42 studies in the present review. The most consistent finding was a significant positive association between depressive symptoms and self-reported cognitive complaints across six studies. Results for objective tasks were inconsistent for working memory (k = 11), attention (k = 24), and cognitive flexibility (k = 5). Autobiographical memory was associated with depressive symptoms, but evidence was based on few studies (k = 3). Verbal memory (k = 8) and recognition memory (k = 2) were not associated with depressive or anxiety symptoms. Across domains, most studies were cross-sectional, relied on self-report symptom measures, used heterogeneous non-ecological cognitive tasks and rarely assessed anxiety, limiting the strength and generalizability of conclusions.
CONCLUSION: Depressive symptoms are consistently associated with subjective cognitive complaints, but evidence for objective cognitive impairment in the perinatal period is inconclusive. The discrepancy between perceived and measured performance highlights the possible influence of mood, sleep, mental load, and sociocultural narratives on maternal cognition. More robust longitudinal and ecologically valid studies are needed to clarify these relationships and mechanisms, and to inform the development of targeted interventions.

articles.title: Interobserver agreement in prenatal ultrasound assessment of fetal urinary tract dilatation.
articles.authors: Spinnato S, Brinkman LAM, Duin LK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess interobserver agreement in the evaluation of the fetal urinary tract in fetuses with urinary tract dilatation (UTD).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study evaluating interobserver agreement on renal tract features using third-trimester renal ultrasound images of fetuses with UTD. Two fetal medicine specialists and two pediatric nephrologists independently and systematically assessed ultrasound features of the fetal renal parenchyma and urinary bladder, as well as the Society for Fetal Urology (SFU) and the ONEN grading systems. Interobserver variability was analyzed using Cohen's kappa statistics and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC).
RESULTS: A total of 1639 ultrasound images from 144 fetuses with antenatal UTD were analyzed. Slight to moderate agreement was observed for most renal ultrasound parameters, including cortico-medullary differentiation (κ = 0.28-0.50), renal echogenicity (κ = 0.18-0.45), and cortical cysts (κ = 0.02-0.15). A similar pattern was observed for the subjective assessment of bladder features. In contrast, both the SFU and the ONEN grading system demonstrated moderate to substantial agreement, with ICC values ranging from 0.61 to 0.73 and 0.55 to 0.66, respectively, and kappa values from 0.38 to 0.63 and 0.48 to 0.67.
CONCLUSION: Significant interobserver variability exists in the interpretation of commonly used prenatal ultrasound features for evaluating the fetal urinary tract and predicting postnatal outcomes in UTD. The SFU and the ONEN grading systems improved agreement, supporting the need for standardized ultrasound assessment tools to enhance prenatal counseling and antenatal management in fetuses with UTD.

articles.title: Cumulative Incidence and Surgical Risk Factors for Severe Postoperative Complications in the Treatment of Primary Uterovaginal Prolapse: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Wolff DT, D'Amico MJ, Santis-Moya F et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Apical repairs for uterovaginal prolapse (UPOP) are generally elective procedures with significant quality-of-life benefit; however, uncommon and potentially severe complications may occur. Our goal was to perform a systematic review and meta-analysis to understand risks for and estimate the incidence of major complications of common surgical approaches to UPOP repair.
METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, we searched MEDLINE and EMBASE through 11/11/25 for studies describing risk factors for, or incidence of, severe complications due to surgical UPOP repair. Data collected included risk factor analysis and incidence data for major intraoperative injury (bowel, bladder, ureteral, or nerve) and major surgical complications (transfusion, small bowel obstruction, perioperative death, mesh complication, reoperations, and readmissions, and sum of any major complication). Pooled proportions were estimated using a random-effects meta-analysis of proportions, and between-group comparisons were performed using mixed-effects meta-regression for major surgical approaches to UPOP repair (vaginal native tissue (VNT), minimally invasive sacrocolpopexy (MIS SCP), transvaginal mesh (TVM); all transabdominal MIS (laparoscopic/robotic), all vaginal reconstructive; VNT with hysterectomy, and VNT with hysteropexy).
RESULTS: Of the 8890 abstracts screened, 46 studies met the inclusion criteria. Overall quality of evidence was moderate. MIS had higher pooled incidence of intraoperative bowel injury compared to vaginal approaches (0.48%; CI 0.27-0.84 vs 0.18%; CI 0.09-0.35, p = 0.028); however, with lower risk of transfusion (0.35%; CI 0.14%-0.87% vs 0.99%; CI 0.67%-1.46%, p = 0.04). Total intraoperative injury estimates were similar between groups (0.11%; CI 0.01-0.81 vs 0.65%; CI 0.20-2.06. p = 0.135). TVM was associated with higher total major complications (17.98%; CI 9.44-31.56) than VNT (5.01%; CI 3.07-8.07) or MIS SCP (6.41%; CI 4.13-9.84) p = 0.007. A narrative review of risk factors for surgical complications identified significant heterogeneity and low confidence in reported risk factors.
CONCLUSIONS: Severe complications following repair of primary UPOP are infrequent. Abdominal MIS carry higher risk of bowel injury, with lower risk of transfusion compared to vaginal approaches. These data should inform shared decision-making for surgeons and patients considering…

articles.title: Pelvic Floor Yoga for Women with Overactive Bladder-Wet: A Subgroup Analysis of a Multisite Randomized Trial.
articles.authors: Enemchukwu E, Subak LL, Lisha NE et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Pelvic floor yoga has been proposed as a community-based therapeutic modality for disruptive overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms such as urgency urinary incontinence (UUI) and urinary frequency, but evidence of its efficacy is limited. We examined the efficacy of pelvic floor yoga versus nonspecific physical conditioning exercise for managing OAB-wet symptoms in women.
METHODS: We present a prespecified subgroup analysis of women with OAB-wet in a multicenter trial involving randomization to 12 weeks of group instruction and self-directed practice of pelvic floor yoga techniques versus time-equivalent instruction and practice of skeletal muscle conditioning exercises. Linear mixed models examined changes in OAB symptoms over 6 and 12 weeks assessed by diary and the Urogenital Distress Inventory-6 (UDI-6).
RESULTS: Among 140 women with OAB-wet (71 randomized to pelvic floor yoga, 69 to physical conditioning), mean baseline UUI frequency was 2.8 (± 1.9) episodes/day. Average UUI frequency decreased by 1.9 episodes/day in the yoga and 1.6 episodes/day in the physical conditioning group over 6 and 12 weeks (nonsignificant between-group difference of -0.3 episodes/day [95% CI -0.7, 0.2]). UDI-6 scores decreased by 10.3 points with yoga and 3.3 with physical conditioning, although neither within-group change was significant. The between-group difference was -7.1 [95% CI -12.2, -1.8]), favoring yoga. Modestly greater improvements in daytime voiding were observed with yoga (between-group difference -0.7 episodes/day [95% CI -1.4, -0.01].
CONCLUSIONS: Women with OAB-wet symptoms reported improvement from both pelvic floor yoga and general physical conditioning exercise, with yoga showing modestly greater reductions in urinary distress and daytime voiding frequency.

articles.title: Pathophysiological Mechanisms and Clinical Implications of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Patients with Deep Endometriosis: A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Šumak R, Serdinšek T
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory condition characterized by endometrium-like tissue outside the uterus. Deep endometriosis (DE) frequently involves the posterior pelvic compartment and can affect the urinary tract directly or indirectly, leading to a wide spectrum of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS). This narrative review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the mechanisms underlying LUTS in women with deep endometriosis, including direct urinary tract involvement, extra-urinary mechanisms, and postoperative dysfunction, and to discuss their diagnostic and therapeutic implications.
METHODS: A structured, non-systematic literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE for English-language publications from 2000 to July 2026. Four thematic domains were considered: (1) prevalence and pathophysiological mechanisms of LUTS in endometriosis; (2) LUTS due to direct urinary tract involvement; (3) LUTS without direct urinary tract involvement; and (4) de novo LUTS after surgery for deep endometriosis.
RESULTS: In women with DE undergoing preoperative urodynamic assessment, pooled estimates indicated voiding dysfunction in 21% and detrusor overactivity in 15%, with substantial heterogeneity. LUTS may reflect direct urinary tract involvement, neural dysfunction, inflammation, or surgical injury. Evidence for proposed neuroinflammatory and nociplastic mechanisms remains largely indirect or experimental.
CONCLUSIONS: Multiple pathophysiological mechanisms may contribute to LUTS in DE. Clinicians should be aware of the association between these two conditions and address treatment of both, which often requires a multidisciplinary approach. Where surgery is indicated, nerve-sparing techniques should be considered when technically feasible to reduce the risk of postoperative urinary dysfunction. Emerging mechanistic and phenotype-based approaches require further validation.

articles.title: Pathways Towards Prevention-Stakeholders' Perspective in Eliminating Obstetric Fistula in Seharti District, Tigray, Ethiopia.
articles.authors: Sisay HT, Lindgren H, Hadi BA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Multifaceted interventions, within Project Zero, are aimed at preventing obstetric fistula through community engagement, capacity building, patient identification and treatment, and strengthening maternal health care services. Although these approaches are promising, effectiveness in practice depends on underexplored contextual factors. Understanding stakeholders' perspectives is essential for identifying factors that influence the effectiveness of interventions. The goal is to explore contextual factors affecting the implementation of a multifaceted intervention with the purpose of eliminating obstetric fistula from the perspectives of key stakeholders.
METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured individual interviews (n = 27) and focus group discussions (n = 6) with purposively selected stakeholders, including health care personnel, midwives, health extension workers, community leaders and beneficiaries, and the data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's six-phase framework.
RESULTS: Stakeholders identified key contextual factors influencing intervention effectiveness in 1 overarching theme, 4 themes and 11 sub-themes, such as raising awareness and promoting health-seeking behaviour, capacity building and mentorship of health care personnel, midwives' leadership in monitoring and managing maternal care, accessibility of services, including free transportation and referrals, and multisectoral collaboration and community engagement. Effective implementation relied on combining community education, health-system strengthening, and supportive referral pathways.
CONCLUSIONS: Preventing obstetric fistula requires holistic and integrated interventions that address both social determinants and health system limitations. Sustainable impact depends on community-informed approaches integrated into existing the maternal health system, strengthened workforce capacity, midwifery leadership and improved access to maternal health services.

articles.title: Managing the transition without hormones.
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.authors: Stute P, Pavicic E, Richina SF et al.
articles.abstract: Perimenopause is a heterogeneous clinical transition characterized by fluctuating function of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and a broad range of symptoms that frequently occur in overlapping clusters. Although menopause hormone therapy (MHT) is effective, many women require or prefer non-hormonal approaches, and several clinically relevant symptoms are not adequately addressed by MHT alone. This review summarizes evidence-based non-hormonal strategies for the management of vasomotor symptoms, sleep disturbance and fatigue, psychological and cognitive concerns, musculoskeletal complaints, and sexual, vulvovaginal and urinary issues. The article also proposes a structured, symptom-oriented clinical framework based on assessment of symptom burden and consideration for functional impact, patient priorities, comorbidities, contraindications and differential diagnoses. Management options include cognitive behavioral therapy, neurokinin receptor antagonists, selected antidepressants and other targeted pharmacotherapies, pelvic floor therapy and individualized lifestyle interventions. Treatment should be selected through shared decision-making, reassessed after a defined interval, and combined or escalated when response is insufficient. A structured algorithm can support consistent clinical decision-making while preserving the individualized and multidimensional care required during the menopausal transition.

articles.title: Understanding the role of lifetime ovulatory years and DNA repair variants on ovarian cancer risk in the United Kingdom Biobank.
articles.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
articles.authors: Garofalo DC, Cleary CR, Ottman R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) risk factors span protective exposures such as parity and contraceptive use, and risk-elevating traits including early menarche and late menopause. Together, these factors dictate lifetime ovulatory years (LOY), which may drive carcinogenesis via an ovulation-induced, DNA-damage promoting microenvironment.
METHODS: This study tested the theory that DNA repair capacity and LOY are synergistic partners by evaluating gene-environment interaction between DNA repair capacity (the presence of pathogenic variants in DNA repair genes in 251,476 at-risk females in the United Kingdom (UK) Biobank, including 847 incident EOC cases) and LOY, using a novel DNA repair capacity score.
RESULTS: We confirmed the association between increasing LOYs and EOC risk in the UK Biobank (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.15 [1.10, 1.20] per 5-year increase in LOY). We also observed strong associations between pathogenic DNA repair variants and ovarian cancer; individuals with at least one variant in 163 DNA repair genes evaluated had a significantly increased hazard of EOC (HR: 1.27, 95% CI: 1.05, 1.55). Participants with both high LOY and at least one variant had an HR of 2.00 (1.54, 2.59), however we did not observe gene-LOY interaction.
CONCLUSIONS: We detected evidence that increasing LOYs and pathogenic DNA repair variants are independent risk factors of EOC, with no evidence of synergy in this population.
IMPACT: In the UK Biobank, greater lifetime ovulations were associated with ovarian cancer risk. Rare pathogenic DNA repair variants also conferred high risk, independent of ovulatory years.

articles.title: Nanotechnology-Driven Precision Diagnostics and Therapeutics for Preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Akbarzadeh I, Nwoke SO, Liao J et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia originates in placental dysfunction yet it is detected only after maternal hypertension and proteinuria or other organ damage emerge, by which point disease-modifying interventions are not available, and delivery of the baby and placenta remains the only cure. Nanotechnology offers a route to reduce this diagnostic-therapeutic latency. Nanostructured biosensors and liquid biopsy platforms detect placental proteins, cell-free RNA/DNA, and extracellular vesicles at femtomolar concentrations and in a multiplex manner, enabling earlier risk stratification when integrated with machine-learning models. In parallel, placenta-targeted lipid-, peptide-, polymeric-, dendrimeric-, and small extracellular vesicle-based nanocarriers deliver angiogenic mRNA, antiangiogenic siRNA, antioxidants, and immunomodulators selectively to the trophoblast cells while limiting fetal exposure. Placenta-on-a-chip platforms and ex vivo placental perfusion models provide human-relevant test beds for these systems. We critically appraise these advances, examine the safety-by-design, manufacturing bottlenecks, and regulatory constraints unique to obstetric nanomedicine, and outline the convergence of theranostics and digital health that could move preeclampsia care from reactive symptom management toward proactive, placenta-targeted monitoring and therapy.

articles.title: Insights into Cytoplasmic Maturation in Human Oocytes: Organelle Dynamics, Ionic Homeostasis, and Translational Regulation.
articles.authors: Burillo L, Esbert M
articles.abstract: Oocyte maturation is a fundamental biological process required for fertilization and the acquisition of developmental competence. Although nuclear events such as meiotic resumption and chromosomal segregation have historically attracted more scientific interest, cytoplasmic remodeling constitutes an equally essential determinant of oocyte quality. This review synthesizes recent evidence on the dynamic reorganization of organelles, regulation of protein synthesis and post-translational modifications, ionic homeostasis, and the distinct cytoplasmic signatures that characterize in vivo and in vitro maturation. During oocyte maturation, the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), mitochondria, and cortical granules undergo stage-specific structural and spatial reorganization. Changes in maternal protein abundance and intracellular zinc (Zn2+) and calcium (Ca2+) signaling also accompany meiotic progression and acquisition of developmental competence. In the context of assisted reproduction, a subset of oocytes retrieved after controlled ovarian stimulation remains immature, typically at the germinal vesicle (GV) or metaphase I (MI) stage, prompting the use of rescue in vitro maturation (r-IVM) protocols to complete their development. Evidence suggests that such oocytes matured in vitro may display aberrant cytoplasmic architecture, impaired organelle distribution, and reduced functional competence, features that may account for the suboptimal outcomes frequently reported after r-IVM. Advancing our understanding of these cytoplasmic processes is likely to facilitate the refinement of in vitro maturation systems, improve oocyte utilization, and ultimately enhance the efficacy of clinical interventions in human reproduction.

articles.title: Early Skin-To-Skin Contact and Breastfeeding in Infants Born Before 35 Gestational Weeks: A Register Study.
articles.authors: Härmestad A, Linnér A, Mägi CO et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The aim was to investigate if there was an association between early skin-to-skin contact after preterm birth and breastfeeding status at discharge.
METHODS: This was a register-based study using data from the Swedish Neonatal Quality register 2020-2024. In total, 9914 infants born before 35 weeks of gestation were included. The outcome was breastfeeding at discharge from the neonatal unit, assessed using two variables: breastfeeding at the breast and receiving breast milk. The exposure was early skin-to-skin contact, defined as within the first 24 h after birth. Odds ratios were estimated for the total population and stratified for gestational age groups.
RESULTS: Skin-to-skin contact within the first 24 h was associated with higher odds of partial breastfeeding at the breast at discharge, aOR 1.47 (95% CI 1.32-1.64), and higher odds of partially and exclusively receiving breast milk. Among extremely preterm infants, skin-to-skin contact was associated with higher odds of exclusive breastfeeding at the breast, aOR 2.22 (95% CI 1.35-3.64).
CONCLUSION: Early skin-to-skin contact was associated with higher odds of partial breastfeeding at discharge in the total study population and with exclusive breastfeeding in extremely preterm infants.

articles.title: The Effect of Conservative Treatment on Bladder Diary Parameters in Women With Urgency Urinary Incontinence and Mixed Urinary Incontinence.
articles.authors: Olofsson A, Wadensten T, Lindam A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary incontinence (the involuntary loss of urine) is a worldwide problem, and bladder diaries are used to characterize the nature and severity of the disease. eHealth and mobile apps are used as tools to aid in conservative treatment, and the mobile app TätII has been developed for the treatment of urgency urinary incontinence (UUI) and mixed urinary incontinence (MUI) in women.
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to evaluate how conservative treatment affected bladder diary parameters in women with UUI and MUI.
METHODS: For this purpose, bladder diaries produced by 123 participants in a previously performed randomized controlled trial (RCT) using TätII were analyzed before and after 15 weeks of treatment. The variables extracted from the bladder diaries included measures of voiding volume, voiding frequency, urinary leakage, and urgency; these were analyzed with non-parametric methods, with between-group comparisons performed using the Mann-Whitney U test.
RESULTS: Compared to the control group, the participants in the treatment group reported a significant decrease (p < 0.01) in voiding frequency (6 vs. 7.5), leakage episodes (0.5 vs. 1.5), leakage grade (0.5 vs. 1.29), and urgency intensity (1.17 vs. 1.5) at the 15-week follow-up. Interestingly, the voiding volume did not change.
CONCLUSION: The results show that treatment of UUI and MUI with TätII has a significant effect on bladder diary parameters. This is the first study to describe a change in bladder diary parameters after conservative treatment of UUI and MUI and provides objective measurements of treatment effects.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov-NCT03097549.

articles.title: Urinary Symptoms, Mobility Limitation, and Subsequent Falls in Older Adults Across Two Longitudinal Cohorts.
articles.authors: Huang R, Huang M, Zhang R
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To examine whether urinary symptoms were associated with subsequent falls according to reported mobility limitation and whether they added meaningful information.
METHODS: We analysed the first eligible window for adults aged ≥ 60 years in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; N = 11,676) and Mexican Health and Aging Study (MHAS; N = 11,071). ELSA assessed generic urinary incontinence over 12 months; MHAS assessed urgency urinary incontinence over 2 years. Mobility was a cohort-specific high-demand walking limitation, and the outcome was any next-wave fall. Modified Poisson RRs, multiple imputation, marginal standardized risks, interaction, and effect modification were used.
RESULTS: With neither urinary symptoms nor mobility limitation as the reference, urinary-only RRs were 1.29 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.19-1.39) in ELSA and 1.14 (95% CI 1.07-1.22) in MHAS; risk differences were +7.6 and +5.9 percentage points. ELSA showed sub-multiplicative interaction with mobility limitation (ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.70-0.92) and age attenuation; at ≥ 75 years, the urinary-only RR was 1.03 (95% CI 0.88-1.21). Optimism-corrected ΔAUC was 0.0044 in ELSA and 0.0015 in MHAS.
CONCLUSIONS: Urinary symptoms were associated with subsequent falls without reported mobility limitation, but the association was context-dependent. ELSA showed mobility-context and age heterogeneity, and incremental discrimination was small. Urinary symptoms were not supported as a stand-alone or universal fall-screening marker.

articles.title: Research Progress on the Precise Classification and Individualized Diagnosis and Treatment of Nocturia.
articles.authors: Sheng X, Xiaodan L, Hongqin F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nocturia is a common urological symptom whose prevalence increases progressively with age. It not only impairs sleep and quality of life but also increases the risk of adverse events, including falls and fractures. Clinical management remains limited by inadequate evaluation of underlying etiologies, imprecise phenotyping, and suboptimal therapeutic responses.
SUMMARY: To facilitate standardized diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, we reviewed and summarized relevant literature published over the past decade. Focusing on four major subtypes, nocturnal polyuria (NP), diminished bladder capacity (DBC), global polyuria (GP), and sleep disorder-predominant nocturia (SDP), we developed a clinical framework integrating precise assessment, phenotypic classification, and individualized treatment. This review compares the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying different phenotypes, identifies the voiding diary as the cornerstone of assessment, and proposes a streamlined three-step clinical phenotyping algorithm. A stepwise treatment strategy tailored to different subtypes is outlined, incorporating psychological counseling, lifestyle modification, pharmacotherapy, physical therapy, and surgery.
KEY MESSAGES: This review provides a reference for the precise and individualized management of nocturia and highlights the potential future roles of digital assessment and multidisciplinary care.

articles.title: Molecular Targets and Potential Mechanisms of Luteolin Against Cervical Carcinoma: Integrative Approach Combining Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics Simulations, and In Vitro Validation.
articles.authors: Pan X, Liu D, Chen J et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical carcinoma ranks among the most prevalent malignant neoplasms in gynecology, distinguished by elevated incidence and fatality rates. Therefore, novel treatment strategies are urgently needed. An effective approach for the revelation of natural active components and their molecular mechanisms was provided by network pharmacology, molecular dynamics simulation, and cell biology methods. Olives contain various bioactive components with antioxidant and antitumor activities. Among these, luteolin, as one of the main natural flavonoids, was proven to possess significant antitumor activity. This research identified C-X-C chemokine Ligand 8 (CXCL8) as a significant target linked to the progression of cervical carcinoma, and luteolin was found to have a strong and stable interaction with CXCL8 that significantly downregulated its expression in HeLa cells. Meanwhile, luteolin could significantly suppressed the proliferation, migration, and lipid droplet formation capacity of HeLa cells. These results suggested that luteolin derived from olives could potentially inhibit HeLa cells through the regulation of CXCL8 and offered a theoretical foundation for the utilization of olive-derived bioactive components in the antitumor treatment of cervical carcinoma.

articles.title: Multitask Deep Learning Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis and Disease-Free Survival From Cytology Images in Bladder Cancer: A Multicenter Study With Pan-Cytology Validation.
articles.authors: Hong G, Jiang F, Xie Y et al.
articles.abstract: Accurate prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) and survival outcomes is crucial for personalized treatment in bladder cancer, yet remains clinically challenging. This study aimed to develop a Cytology-based multitask predictive Network (CytoNet) to simultaneously predict LNM and disease-free survival (DFS) in bladder cancer, and to evaluate its generalizability in cervical and thyroid cancers. This study included a multicenter cohort of 5273 patients, with bladder cancer (n = 1134), cervical cancer (n = 598), and thyroid cancer (n = 3541). CytoNet was constructed through a three-stage pipeline comprising self-supervised pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and multitask prediction. In bladder cancer, CytoNet achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.831-0.881 for LNM prediction and a C index of 0.680-0.710 for DFS prediction across all cohorts, outperforming single-task models and standard radiological assessments. In cervical cancer, CytoNet demonstrated robust performance for both LNM prediction (AUC 0.847-0.862) and DFS prediction (C index 0.690-0.709), while in thyroid cancer, it achieved an AUC of 0.819-0.855 for LNM prediction. In conclusion, CytoNet represents a reliable tool for predicting LNM and prognosis from cytopathology images across multiple cancer types, showing potential as a valuable adjunct to current clinical decision-making. Further prospective validation is warranted to assess its clinical utility.

articles.title: Where to Begin? Prioritizing Procedures for Surgical Skills Training Development: SELF Series Article 2.
articles.authors: Levi A, Jeffcoach DR, Roy N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The shortage of practitioners trained to provide essential surgical care remains among the most stubborn contributors to the global burden of disease. Scaling the global surgical care workforce through independent procedural skills training is essential to address unmet surgical needs, particularly in resource constrained settings. This is a dauntingly large task; prioritization of a sub-set of surgical skills is required in order to make an impactful start. During the 2023 Surgical Education Learners Forum (SELF) Symposium, participants developed criteria to prioritize the development of self-directed and simulation-based training modules to address the most urgent needs in surgery, critical care, and perioperative care. This is the second article in the SELF series.
METHODS: The SELF community of practice members from diverse geographies convened at the SELF Symposium to gain a common understanding of the environments where SELF training modules are deployed and articulate how to prioritize the development of those materials. Participants voted to prioritize 262 procedures by impact and then effectiveness, "deployability", and outcome variability.
RESULTS: Fifty seven procedures were identified as high-priority for surgical skills development. Of these, 20 were trauma and critical care procedures, 21 were general surgical procedures, 11 were pediatric surgical procedures, and 5 were obstetrics, gynecology, and family planning procedures.
CONCLUSIONS: When faced with the dauntingly large need for surgical, critical care and perioperative procedural skills training, prioritizing the identified areas will guide training development efforts toward the greatest impacts.

articles.title: Access to Reproductive Health Services for Women Incarcerated in the United States: A Federal and State Policy Review.
articles.journal: Perspectives on sexual and reproductive health
articles.authors: Kotlar B, Matthews M, Piontkowski K et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The United States (US) has the highest incarceration rate in the world. Women's incarceration has grown significantly since 1980, disproportionately affecting marginalized communities. Most individuals experiencing incarceration are of reproductive age, yet studies have suggested limited access to reproductive health services. State and federal policies could be a mechanism to ensure access to reproductive health services during incarceration.
METHODS: We conducted a policy review using WestLaw in August 2023 and March 2024 of federal and state statutes and regulations addressing individuals who are incarcerated containing language on reproductive health, including pregnancy testing, pregnancy options counseling, contraception, and abortion.
RESULTS: Policies in eight states mandated pregnancy testing ranging from universal testing to the option to opt-out. Four states and the federal government mandate pregnancy options counseling for positive tests. Two states mandate the provision of contraceptives outside of sexual assault; Texas and the federal government mandate the provision of emergency contraceptives in the case of sexual assault. Five states and the federal government limit or prohibit the use of sterilization during incarceration. Four states and the federal government mandate provision of abortion care. No statutes or regulations provided mechanisms to enforce carceral facilities' compliance with stated policies.
CONCLUSION: Policies ensuring reproductive health services for individuals experiencing incarceration are extremely limited across the country. States and the federal government should consider passing laws codifying access to pregnancy testing, pregnancy options counseling, contraceptives, and abortion, with clear enforcement mechanisms to protect the reproductive autonomy of this marginalized population.

articles.title: Chronic High-Dose Ketamine Fails to Induce a Cystitis-Like Phenotype in Mice Despite High Urinary Metabolite Levels.
articles.authors: Dewez J, Caldwell A, Schillebeeckx L et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Ketamine‑induced cystitis (KIC) is a severe complication of chronic ketamine misuse, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Established rodent models have demonstrated variable changes in voiding behavior and bladder histology, without exploring the sensory mechanisms underlying altered voiding and pain at all. This study aimed to establish a murine model of chronic ketamine-induced cystitis to investigate changes in pain behavior and sensory signaling.
METHODS: Male and female C57BL/6 J mice received intraperitoneal ketamine (100 mg/kg, n = 20) or saline (n = 20) for 12 weeks. Urine and plasma ketamine, norketamine, and dehydronorketamine concentrations were determined using LC-QTOF/MS. Voiding behavior was assessed fortnightly using spontaneous voiding assays, suprapubic mechanical sensitivity was evaluated using von Frey filaments, and wellbeing was assessed using nesting and open field assays. Finally, histopathological analysis was performed on bladder and kidney tissues.
RESULTS: Despite high urinary and plasma concentrations of ketamine, norketamine, and dehydronorketamine, ketamine-treated mice showed no significant differences in voiding behavior, suprapubic sensitivity, natural behavior, or bladder and kidney histopathology compared with controls.
CONCLUSION: Chronic high-dose ketamine treatment did not induce a robust phenotype of ketamine-induced cystitis in C57BL/6 J mice, highlighting limitations of using rodent models for recapitulating human ketamine‑induced cystitis.

articles.title: Prognosticating Factors in PET CT and MRI of Cervical Cancer Treated With Chemoradiotherapy.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation oncology
articles.authors: Ku D, Wei W, Rutherford N
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We aim to evaluate the functional and anatomical imaging characteristics of locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) to identify potential prognosticating imaging biomarkers in the context of chemoradiotherapy treatment (CRT).
METHOD: This retrospective review analysed patient data over a period of seven years. Patients with locally advanced cervical cancer who have undergone FDG PET CT and MRI were identified through Report Analytics. Patients with LACC who have undergone chemoradiotherapy were identified through review of the electronic records. Pre and post-treatment imaging were analysed and compared. The patients were dichotomised into complete metabolic responders (CMR) and non-complete metabolic responders (N-CMR) as per European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) criteria. Imaging parameters in PET CT and MRI including SUV max, SUV mean, total lesion glycolysis (TLG), lesion metabolic tumour volume (MTV), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) minimum were examined. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to evaluate differences in overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) between the CMR and N-CMR groups. Pearson's correlation and Fischer's exact test were used to evaluate the potential prognosticating value of the PET CT and MRI imaging parameters as predictors of metabolic response to CRT.
RESULTS: A total of 159 FDG PET CT scans were conducted in the 7-year period, of which there were 61 individual patients identified for inclusion into the present study. The average imaging follow-up for the patients included between 2019 and 2024 was 63.3 months, and chemoradiotherapy follow-up was 62.9 months. The patients were dichotomized into CMR and N-CMR groups. There is a statistically significant difference in overall survival, with 1 mortality (5%) in the CMR group vs. 19 mortality (70%) in the N-CMR group (p = 0.0001). However, no statistically significant difference in follow-up 87.1 months vs. 57.1 months (p = 0.20). In the overall cervical cancer cohort as well as the squamous cell carcinoma subgroup (n = 32), the comparison of CMR and N-CMR groups revealed a statistically significant difference in the following FDG PET imaging parameters: SUV max, SUV mean, ADC minimum and MTV. The CMR group has tumours with higher SUV max and SUV mean (difference of 7.5 and 5.1 respectively) and smaller MTV (difference of 20.1 cm3). However, there was no demonstrable difference in TLG and MRI ADC min values between the…

articles.title: Regional growth patterns of fetal corpus callosum at 18-32 weeks' gestation assessed by three-dimensional transvaginal neurosonography.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Chen Y, Liao Y, Zhang Q et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the normal development of the fetal corpus callosum (CC) between 18 and 32 weeks' gestation using three-dimensional (3D) transvaginal neurosonography and to assess the effect of volume contrast imaging (VCI) on the measurement of fetal CC biometry.
METHODS: This study included two cohorts of women with a singleton pregnancy: a prospective cohort attending the research clinic at Prince of Wales Hospital in Hong Kong SAR, China, between April 2019 and February 2025, at which 3D fetal brain volumes were acquired prospectively, and a retrospective cohort attending CRIFM Prenatal Medical Clinic in Osaka, Japan, between December 2018 and March 2025, from which archived 3D fetal brain volume datasets were retrieved. In both cohorts, 3D fetal brain volume data of the CC were acquired using transvaginal neurosonography between 18 and 32 weeks' gestation using the same acquisition protocol. Inclusion criteria were appropriately grown fetuses at 18 + 0 to 32 + 6 weeks' gestation, without suspected structural or chromosomal defects. In the midsagittal plane, using 3D volume multiplanar imaging, the CC length and total area were obtained and regional thickness at the genu, body and splenium were measured following a modified Garel's method. Additionally, the areas of five vertical CC segments defined by arithmetic fractions of the CC length following Witelson's classification (anterior one-third, anterior midbody, posterior midbody, isthmus and splenium) were obtained. All fetal biometric measurements were performed using non-VCI and VCI modes. Measurements obtained using non-VCI and VCI modes were compared using the paired t-test. Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape (GAMLSS) were used to explore the relationship between all biometric measurements of the fetal CC and gestational age. The final models were used to derive percentiles and construct reference curves. Intra- and interobserver variability were assessed using 30 randomly selected cases.
RESULTS: A total of 956 fetuses at 18-32 weeks' gestation were included. Gestational age-specific trajectories of fetal CC biometry were established, demonstrating distinct, non-linear growth patterns in CC length, total area, genu, body and splenium thicknesses and the areas of five individual CC subdivisions from 18 to 32 weeks. Overall, the genu and body thicknesses increased sharply from 18 weeks to 23 weeks. Thereafter, genu thickness continued to increase gradually until…

articles.title: Beyond the minipill: a review of progestin-only oral contraception.
articles.authors: Zu V, Uhm S
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF THE REVIEW: Progestin-only pills (POPs) represent an underutilized contraceptive option despite expanding evidence for their safety, efficacy, and noncontraceptive applications. This article updates the 2022 review of progestin-only contraception by Liu et al ., describing currently available POP formulations and their characteristics.
RECENT FINDINGS: Contraceptive POPs vary substantially by formulation in mechanism of action, efficacy, and tolerability. The three available in the US contain norethindrone, norgestrel, and drospirenone. While current recommendations are largely based on outdated information, more recent research considers the more nuanced characteristics and noncontraceptive applications of different POPs. Typical-use failure rates are likely lower than historically reported, and the 3-h window (the recommended cutoff for a 'late' dose) has limited evidentiary support and does not apply uniformly across formulations. Drospirenone's unique antiandrogenic and antimineralocorticoid properties, improved bleeding profile, and ovulation suppression distinguish it from other POPs; recent data may support continuous dosing and expand off-label applications. Importantly, this review discusses specific safety considerations and highlights the availability of norgestrel over-the-counter as a major milestone in contraceptive accessibility.
SUMMARY: Understanding the distinct contraceptive and noncontraceptive characteristics of each POP formulation allows clinicians to offer individualized counseling that aligns with each patient's reproductive and healthcare goals.

articles.title: Real-world utilization of gonadotropins and the associated cumulative live birth rates in the United States: a retrospective claims database analysis.
articles.authors: Xue W, Jungheim E, Yang M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Gonadotropins approved in the United States (US) for ovarian follicle stimulation and pregnancy include follitropin alfa, follitropin beta, and Highly Purified Human Menopausal gonadotropin (HP-hMG). This study assessed the real-world utilization of these gonadotropins and associated cumulative live birth rates (CLBR) in US women with infertility.
METHODS: Females (age 18-42 years) who received gonadotropins after infertility diagnosis were identified from the IQVIA PharMetrics Plus database (1/2016-6/2022). Four cohorts were constructed based on the treatment on the index date (first gonadotropin use): HP-hMG monotherapy, follitropin alfa monotherapy, follitropin beta monotherapy, and mixed protocol (HP-hMG with follitropin alfa or follitropin beta). Gonadotropin utilization and incidence of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) and severe OHSS were described during 2016-2021. CLBR was assessed for the first live births associated with the index gonadotropin regimen using logistic regression adjusting for baseline characteristics.
RESULTS: Among 14,174 women, the mean age was 34.7 (SD: 4.1) years, with 47.1% <35 years. During 2016-2021, HP-hMG use in a mixed protocol (60.1-71.2%) or as monotherapy (4.3-5.7%) increased, while use of follitropin alfa (21.7-11.4%) and follitropin beta (13.9-11.6%) monotherapy decreased. Compared to follitropin alfa, the adjusted odds of live birth were significantly higher after the mixed protocol (OR [95% CI]: 1.31 [1.20-1.45]) and HP-hMG monotherapy (1.28 [1.08-1.53]); the estimate for follitropin beta versus follitropin alfa was closer to the null (0.96 [0.84-1.10]). The rate of OHSS was low across all cohorts (1.2-2.9%) and severe OHSS was rare (0.1%).
LIMITATIONS: As an observational analysis lacking data on key predictors of IVF success, associations should not be interpreted as comparative efficacy.
CONCLUSIONS: In US women with infertility, HP-hMG as monotherapy or in a mixed protocol increased in use during 2016-2021 and was associated with higher odds of CLBR compared to follitropin alfa monotherapy.

articles.title: Role of Uterine Artery Doppler Indices in Predicting Endometrial Pathology in Perimenopausal and Postmenopausal Women Presenting with Abnormal Uterine Bleeding.
articles.authors: Sarvesh A, Kandavar SS, Rai S
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) in perimenopausal and postmenopausal women requires evaluation to exclude premalignant and malignant endometrial pathology. Uterine artery Doppler may improve diagnostic accuracy when combined with transvaginal ultrasonography (TVS).
AIM: The aim of this study is to evaluate the diagnostic utility of uterine artery Doppler indices in predicting endometrial pathology among perimenopausal and postmenopausal women presenting with AUB.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: This was a prospective, observational study conducted at a tertiary care hospital.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: A total of 175 perimenopausal and postmenopausal women with AUB underwent TVS with assessment of endometrial thickness (ET), uterine artery pulsatility index (PI), and resistance index (RI). Endometrial tissue samples obtained by Pipelle biopsy or dilatation and curettage underwent histopathological examination. Histopathological diagnoses were established using standard diagnostic criteria and correlated with the PALM-COEIN classification.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to assess the cutoff point and diagnostic performance․.
RESULTS: Among 175 women, 157 (89.7%) had benign pathology and 18 (10.3%) had premalignant/malignant lesions. PI and RI were significantly lower in premalignant/malignant lesions. In perimenopausal women, PI and RI showed excellent diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.946 and 0.973, respectively). In postmenopausal women, AUCs were 0.798 and 0.674, respectively. Optimal cutoffs were PI ≤1.12 and RI ≤0.425 for perimenopausal women and PI ≤1.77 and RI ≤0.575 for postmenopausal women. Combined assessment of ET, PI, and RI achieved the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0.851).
CONCLUSIONS: Uterine artery Doppler indices improve the ability of TVS to distinguish benign from premalignant/malignant endometrial pathology and may serve as a useful noninvasive risk stratification tool in women with AUB.

articles.title: Association of Thyroid Disorder and Liver Function Tests in Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Haider A, Singh S, Perween S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroid disease is prevalent among women of reproductive age and has a complex interplay with liver function, affecting both healthy and diseased states, including during pregnancy. To determine the relationship between thyroid disorders and liver function abnormalities during pregnancy among pregnant women.
METHODS: This was an unmatched case-control study over a period of 2 years. A total of 90 pregnant women who were above 24 weeks of gestation were recruited in the study. They were divided into two groups of 45 antenatal women each; those with normal liver function tests (LFT) were taken as controls (Group A) and those with abnormal LFT were considered as cases (Group B). Women in both these groups were then subjected to thyroid function tests. The number of women with thyroid disorder in both these groups was compared, and data analysis was done.
RESULTS: Among 90 pregnant women (45 cases with deranged LFT and 45 controls with normal liver functions), baseline demographic characteristics were comparable between groups. Liver enzymes and bilirubin levels were significantly higher in cases (P < 0.05). Mean serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) was also significantly elevated in cases (3.3 ± 2.4 mIU/L) compared to controls (2.3 ± 1.1 mIU/L; P = 0.011). Women with elevated TSH (>3 mIU/L) had significantly higher odds of abnormal liver function (adjusted odds ratio = 3.6-3.8; P = 0.008).
CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate a significant association between thyroid dysfunction and liver function abnormalities in pregnancy. Early and combined screening of thyroid and liver function may facilitate timely diagnosis and management, thereby improving maternal and fetal outcomes.

articles.title: Advancing the science on measurement, determinants, and outcomes of pregnancy and abortion coercion in global settings: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Liang M, Landers C, Casey SE et al.
articles.abstract: Reproductive coercion-behaviors that interfere with women's autonomous reproductive decision-making-is increasingly recognized but remains unevenly defined and measured across settings. We conducted a scoping review and searched MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, for English-language studies from 1995 to April 2023. Of 8,515 records identified, 119 studies met inclusion criteria; 56% were quantitative, 55% were published during 2020-2023, and most were conducted in high-income settings (58% United States; 13% Australia). Conceptualizations evolved from a narrow focus on pregnancy coercion and birth control sabotage toward inclusion of abortion coercion, provider-level dynamics, and experiences during motherhood, though consensus is lacking. Measurement was dominated by the Miller reproductive control scale and adaptations; act-based items for abortion coercion were scarce. Reported prevalence spanned ∼1%-58% depending on timeframe, setting, and measure. Multi-level risk factors included unstable or non-marital partnerships, partner concurrency, co-residence with in-laws, and lower household wealth; partner education and employment were protective in several contexts. Reproductive coercion frequently co-occurred with intimate partner, sexual, and domestic violence yet showed independent associations with reduced contraceptive self-efficacy and use, increased covert contraception, unintended pregnancy, sexually transmitted infection, and adverse mental health. Evidence on interventions centers on clinic-based, trauma-informed education and counselling, with implementation barriers related to training, time, and referral pathways. Advancing the field requires a harmonized, intent-sensitive, act-based definition and improved measures, especially for abortion coercion, together with more diverse research in low- and middle-income countries and coordinated legal, health, educational, and community responses to protect women's reproductive autonomy.

articles.title: Ultrasound modalities and age-specific normative findings in pediatric and adolescent gynecology.
articles.authors: Policriti MA, Cooper N, Seah MA et al.
articles.abstract: Ultrasound is the first-line modality for imaging the female gynecological organs in children and adolescents. Its interpretation relies on understanding the physiological changes in organ appearance from birth through puberty. This narrative review considers different ultrasound approaches including transabdominal, transvaginal, transrectal, transperineal, Doppler and three-dimensional ultrasound, and when magnetic resonance imaging may add useful information. It then describes how normal uterine, ovarian, and endometrial appearances change across development. Although the evidence is drawn mainly from cross-sectional studies using different equipment, measurement methods, and reporting approaches, the studies describe a broadly consistent developmental pattern. A central practical message emerges: thresholds and diagnostic criteria derived from adults translate poorly to the developing pelvis, so interpretation rests not on memorizing cut-offs but on knowing what to expect at each age and stage, and on recognizing how wide normal physiological variation is. The review also identifies the principal evidence gaps: sparse data at the youngest ages, limited representation of diverse populations, an absence of longitudinal studies, a reliance on adult-derived criteria for diagnosing pathology such as adnexal masses, adenomyosis and endometriosis, and the lack of a standardized reporting framework. It then sets out priorities for future research.

articles.title: Molecular Mechanisms and Signaling Pathways Underlying the Synergistic Effect of Metformin and Paclitaxel in Preclinical Cancer Models: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Omidi Sarajar B, Khederzadeh A, Payoon A et al.
articles.abstract: Paclitaxel is a standard chemotherapeutic agent for various malignancies, but drug resistance frequently limits its clinical efficacy. Metformin, a widely used antidiabetic drug, has demonstrated anticancer properties. This systematic review evaluates the molecular mechanisms and signaling pathways underlying the synergistic interaction between metformin and paclitaxel in preclinical cancer models. A systematic search of Embase, Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted up to February 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. English-language preclinical studies examining the combined use of metformin and paclitaxel in cancer cell lines and animal models were included. Thirty-six studies met the eligibility criteria, including 28 in vitro and 8 in vivo studies. The majority demonstrated synergistic effects across endometrial, melanoma, triple-negative breast, prostate, and ovarian cancer models. Metformin enhances paclitaxel activity through several defined mechanisms. These include the activation of AMPK with subsequent suppression of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, epigenetic silencing of the oncogenic lncRNA SNHG7, induction of reactive oxygen species and mitochondrial apoptosis, and inhibition of cancer stemness via FOXO3a regulation. Additionally, metformin increases intracellular paclitaxel accumulation through OCT3 transporters. In vivo studies confirmed that metformin reduces tumor volume when combined with paclitaxel, utilizing both AMPK-dependent and AMPK-independent mechanisms such as cyclin D1 downregulation and gut microbiota modulation. Preclinical evidence indicates that metformin acts as a chemosensitizer, potentiating paclitaxel efficacy through multiple molecular pathways. This combination allows for reduced effective paclitaxel doses and may help overcome drug resistance, particularly in endometrial cancer, melanoma, and triple-negative breast cancer. Future clinical studies should optimize dosing regimens and validate predictive biomarkers, such as OCT1 and OCT3 expression, to improve clinical translation.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Analysis of Hospitalisations and Mortality From Gynaecological Cancers in Ecuador, 2015-2024.
articles.authors: Lalangui-Vivanco K, Jaramillo-Feijoo LE, Real-Cotto JJ et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To analyse the spatiotemporal patterns of hospitalisations and mortality due to gynaecological cancers in Ecuador (2015-2024), identify provincial geographic disparities, and examine the association between healthcare infrastructure and clustering patterns.
METHODS: This population-based ecological study used INEC hospital discharge and general death records for women with gynaecological cancers (ICD-10: C51-C57) in Ecuador from 2015 to 2024. Age-standardised rates per 100,000 women were calculated by year, cause, age group, and province of residence. K-means clustering was applied separately to hospitalisation and mortality rates to identify provinces with similar temporal trajectories. Global and local Moran's I assessed spatial autocorrelation, and Spearman correlations and Kruskal-Wallis tests examined associations with healthcare infrastructure.
RESULTS: Between 2015 and 2024, 39,492 hospitalisations and 11,410 deaths were recorded. Cervical cancer accounted for 45.4% of hospitalisations and 42.2% of deaths, followed by ovarian cancer (32.6% and 22.0%). Hospitalisations declined markedly in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Trajectory-based k-means identified three clusters for each outcome. The highest hospitalisation rates were concentrated in the southern provinces, with significant global spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = 0.48-0.64, all p ≤ 0.002) and a persistent High-High spatial cluster, while the highest mortality occurred in the northern and central Sierra and the Amazon, without consistent spatial autocorrelation. Nine provinces had high mortality, low hospitalisation, and lower bed density (224.9 vs 260.1 per 100,000 women). Bed density was not significantly correlated with hospitalisation (rho = 0.35, p = 0.097) or mortality (rho = -0.27, p = 0.205); bed density did not differ across mortality clusters (p = 0.52).
CONCLUSION: The mismatch between hospitalisation and mortality clustering patterns, together with lower healthcare infrastructure in high-mortality provinces, suggests that unequal access to timely care may contribute to excess mortality, although these associations were not statistically significant.

articles.title: Healthcare professionals' communication practices and preparedness in organised human papillomavirus-based cervical Cancer screening: A cross-sectional study in Central Portugal.
articles.authors: Sousa R, Fonseca-Moutinho JA, Gomes F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes, communication confidence and practices within an organised human papillomavirus (HPV)-based cervical cancer screening programme and identify factors associated with communication practices.
METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 470 general practitioners and nurses involved in organised cervical cancer screening in Portugal's Central Region, January-March 2024. Participants completed a 28-item questionnaire. Exploratory factor analysis identified communication domains, and generalised linear models examined factors associated with communication practices.
RESULTS: Knowledge of HPV infection and screening was relatively high, with gaps in HPV test interpretation and clinical management. General practitioners reported greater communication confidence than nurses. HPV infection- and screening-related information was communicated more frequently than information concerning HPV transmission and oncogenic risk. Professional group, knowledge of HPV infection and screening guidelines, communication confidence and communication of HPV test results were independently associated with the HPV infection and screening-related communication domain. No significant associations were identified for communication of HPV transmission and oncogenic risk.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite relatively high knowledge, gaps remained in knowledge and communication practices, particularly regarding HPV transmission and oncogenic risk. Professional training integrating clinical knowledge with communication about HPV, cervical cancer screening and cancer risk may strengthen healthcare professionals' preparedness for HPV-based screening.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Progestin Intervention for Non-Atypical Endometrial Hyperplasia in Infertile Females with Anovulation: A Retrospective Study.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Xu Z, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy of progestin intervention for non-atypical endometrial hyperplasia (non-atypical EH) in infertile patients with ovulatory dysfunction, and to explore factors associated with histological regression.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary reproductive medicine center. A total of 171 infertile females with anovulation diagnosed with non-atypical EH by hysteroscopic biopsy between March 2021 and August 2024 were enrolled. Patients were divided into polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) group (n=89) and diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) group (n=82) according to ovarian reserve function. All patients received 3-month oral progestin therapy. The study aims to analyze and compare the regression of endometrial hyperplasia after 3 months of treatment. Multivariate logistic regression was used to analyze independent factors affecting treatment response.
RESULTS: After progestin treatment, the overall EH regression rate was 82.46%, with no significant difference between the DOR group (84.15%) and PCOS group (80.90%) (P=0.577). In the DOR subgroup, high-potency progestins achieved a significantly higher regression rate than dydrogesterone (89.83% vs 69.57%, P=0.040), while no such difference was found in the PCOS group (P=0.527). The clinical pregnancy rate (31.71% vs 48.31%, P=0.027) and live birth rate (14.63% vs 38.20%, P<0.001) were significantly lower in the DOR group. But no significant association was observed between progestin type and clinical pregnancy (P = 0.097, OR = 0.586, 95% CI 0.312-1.101).Multivariate analysis revealed that lower body mass index (BMI) (OR=0.893, 95% CI: 0.809-0.985, P=0.024) and high-potency progestin regimen (OR=2.913, 95% CI: 1.147-7.400, P=0.025) were independent protective factors for EH regression.
CONCLUSION: Progestin provides comparable histological regression for non-atypical EH in infertile females with anovulation. A potential benefit of high-potency progestins was observed among patients with DOR.

articles.title: Long-Term Exposure to Ambient Air Pollution and Cervical Cancer Outcomes in Chinese Women: A Prospective Study on Recurrence and Mortality Risks.
articles.authors: Lin Y, Qiu J, Jiang L et al.
articles.abstract: The impact of air pollution on the prognosis of cervical cancer (CC) remains unclear. This study examined the associations of major air pollutants on recurrence and mortality among CC patients. We enrolled 3,758 women diagnosed with primary CC at the Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University between 2019 and 2022, following them annually until June 2024. Air pollution exposure was estimated using high-resolution spatiotemporal models based on residential addresses. Weighted Cox proportional hazards models based on the Fine-Gray approach were used to estimate the risk of recurrence, while stratified Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the risk of death, adjusting for demographic, clinical, and meteorological factors. Among the patients (median follow-up ∼ 3 years), 217 recurrences (5.8%) and 113 deaths (3.0%) occurred. Each interquartile range increase in fine particulate matter (PM2.5), inhalable particulate matter (PM10), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and sulfur dioxide (SO2) was associated with elevated recurrence risk, with subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs) of 1.93 (95% Confidence Interval (CI): 1.40-2.66), 1.65 (1.13-2.42), 1.60 (1.14-2.24), and 1.26 (1.07-1.48), respectively. Higher exposure to PM2.5, PM10, and NO2 was also linked to increased mortality risk, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 2.55 (95% CI: 1.78-3.67), 2.21 (1.38-3.54), and 1.37 (1.03-1.84), respectively. No significant association was observed for ozone (O3). Exposure-response and sensitivity analyses supported these findings. This cohort study provides the first evidence that long-term exposure to air pollution after surgery is associated with increased risks of recurrence and mortality in primary CC patients, highlighting it as a modifiable environmental determinant of CC prognosis.

articles.title: Evaluating concordance of preimplantation genetic testing-whole-genome sequencing with genetic findings in live-born children.
articles.authors: Li S, Podgursky B, Katz M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To clinically assess concordance between preimplantation genetic testing-whole-genome sequencing (PGT-WGS) and whole-genome sequencing results from corresponding live-born children, including evaluation of genome-wide variants, targeted gene panels, de novo variants, and genetic risk scores.
DESIGN: Patients underwent a standard in vitro fertilization workflow with PGT-WGS. After pregnancy or live birth, patients were contacted for consent to participate in this study. This small study included 10 biopsy-child pairs. Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) samples were collected from children, and whole-genome sequencing was performed accordingly. Genetic findings from PGT-WGS were compared with the child's whole-genome sequencing results. For de novo variant assessment (3 biopsy-child pairs), parental samples were also requested.
SUBJECTS: Clinical trophectoderm biopsy samples, corresponding live-born children, and parental DNA samples.
EXPOSURE: No applicable.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Variant concordance across the whole genome and within designated gene panels; concordance of clinically relevant variants and de novo variants; concordance of functionally significant single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), including HLA and APOE; and resulting genetic risk scores.
RESULTS: Analysis of single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) and insertions/deletions (indels) identified an average of 3,562,534 variants genome-wide and 2,656 variants within the 1,200-gene panel per embryo-child pair, yielding a sensitivity of 97.6% and a precision of 98.4% on genome and 98.4% and 98.7% respectively, on monogenic panels.Traditional PGT approaches do not enable prospective screening for de novo variants. In this study, all 42 confirmed de novo variants detected in live-born children were also identified in the corresponding PGT-WGS results. High concordance (>99%) was observed on HLA, APOE, as well as SNPs used for genetic risk scores.
CONCLUSION: This study provides a small clinical study comparing PGT-WGS results with whole-genome sequencing findings in live-born children. Preimplantation genetic testing-whole-genome sequencing, offered using an opt-in panel of approximately 1,200 genes, demonstrated high sensitivity and precision and enabled direct interrogation of the trophectoderm genome. It has the feasibility to identify de novo variants.

articles.title: Malignant transformation of endometriosis into endometrioid ovarian carcinoma with a contralateral borderline seromucinous tumour: A rare case report.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics & gynecology and reproductive biology: X
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol X
articles.authors: Kiruthika T, Rao DR, Rao A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis-associated ovarian cancer is uncommon and is most often represented by endometrioid and clear cell carcinomas. Synchronous contralateral borderline ovarian tumours are uncommon and may be missed when gross intraoperative assessment is reassuring.
CASE: A 43-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of endometriosis for approximately 5 years presented with worsening pelvic pain and menstrual symptoms. A left ovarian endometrioma increased from 6.1 × 6.8 × 5.2 cm in April 2024 to 8.8 × 9 × 9.5 cm in April 2025, with subsequent MRI showing a complex mass with solid components (O-RADS MRI 5). CA-125 was 408.6 U/mL and CA 19-9 was 643.58 U/mL; RMI-I was 1225.8 (U = 3, M = 1, CA-125 = 408.6). Staging laparotomy was performed. Histopathology demonstrated grade 2 endometrioid adenocarcinoma arising in an endometriotic cyst of the left ovary, FIGO stage IC1, while the grossly normal-appearing right ovary contained a borderline seromucinous tumour with endometrioid differentiation. The omentum, peritoneal cytology, and all 31 sampled lymph nodes were negative for malignancy. Immunohistochemistry supported endometrioid carcinoma.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of interval change and suspicious imaging features in an endometrioma, the limitations of gross intraoperative assessment of the contralateral ovary, and the value of complete histopathological examination in identifying synchronous bilateral ovarian pathology.

articles.title: Combined plasma and liquid-based cytology microRNA signatures as biomarkers of high-grade cervical lesions: association with HPV infection and p16 expression.
articles.authors: Hasan T, Eltayeb H, Alanazi AN et al.
articles.abstract: MicroRNA (miRNA) dysregulation may provide complementary molecular information for cervical lesion assessment and triage. This prospective observational study evaluated six candidate miRNAs in paired plasma and liquid-based cytology (LBC) specimens and their associations with cytological severity, high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV), and p16 expression. Among 328 women, cytology was classified as normal (n = 52), atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US; n = 44), low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL; n = 42), high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL; n = 82), or squamous cell carcinoma (SCC; n = 108). hrHPV positivity increased from 0% in normal cytology to 93.5% in SCC and p16 positivity from 0% to 95.4% (both P < 0.001). In paired plasma and LBC specimens, miR-21-5p, miR-155-5p, miR-9-5p, and miR-15b-5p progressively increased with cytological severity, whereas miR-375-3p and miR-145-5p decreased (all p < 0.001). For discrimination of HSIL/SCC from normal/ASC-US/LSIL, individual-miRNA areas under the curve (AUCs) ranged from 0.970 to 0.993. After stratified 10-fold cross-validation, AUCs were 0.818 (95% CI, 0.765-0.869) for hrHPV, 0.807 (0.751-0.860) for p16, and 0.840 (0.789-0.888) for hrHPV + p16. The six-miRNA LBC panel achieved an AUC of 0.9999 (0.9996-1.000), 99.5% sensitivity, 100.0% specificity, and a Brier score of 0.006. These findings demonstrate strong internal discrimination by LBC-derived miRNAs; however, validation against histologically confirmed endpoints in independent, clinically representative populations is required before clinical application.

articles.title: Microfluidic sperm separation for intracytoplasmic sperm injection yields similar blastocyst rates compared with density gradient, however, may be of benefit for male factor infertility: a randomized sibling oocyte study.
articles.authors: Fritz R, Arnott A, Tozour J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To study whether microfluidic sperm separation in intracytoplasmic sperm injection cycles provides any benefit over density gradient sperm separation for good-quality embryo formation.
DESIGN: Randomized sibling oocyte study.
SUBJECTS: Patients undergoing intracytoplasmic sperm injection.
INTERVENTION: Microfluidic sperm separation vs. density gradient sperm separation.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcomes were percentage of good-quality blastocyst formation. Secondary outcomes included sperm parameters after sperm separation, including percent motility, grade of forward progression, fertilization rates, blastocyst formation rates, and ploidy rates in the event that preimplantation testing for aneuploidy was performed. Additionally, subanalysis on those with male factor infertility was performed, evaluating primary and secondary outcomes above.
RESULTS: A total of 34 cycles enrolled into the study, yielding 456 oocytes, 231 randomized to microfluidics and 225 to density gradient (DG).
