Average microfluidic fertilization rate was 76.1% ± 19.2% and 72.4% ± 26.6% for DG. Microfluidic blastocyst formation rate was 58.4% ± 31.9% compared with 58.7% ± 30.5% for DG. Good-quality blastocyst formation rate for microfluidics was 51.4% ± 29.7% and for DG was 51.7% ± 30.9%. Euploid rates were 43.8% ± 35.5% in the microfluidics cohort and 33.7% ± 33.3% in the DG cohort. Subanalysis of cycles with male factor infertility revealed good-quality blastocyst formation rate was 45.9% ± 30.9% after microfluidics and 55.1% ± 29.2% for DG. Subanalysis of cycles with male factor infertility revealed an euploid rate of 50.0% ± 37.6% after microfluidics compared with 18.4% ± 24.5% for DG.
CONCLUSION: There were similar rates of good-quality embryo formation after intracytoplasmic sperm injection using sperm separated with microfluidics compared with density gradient; however, subanalysis of the male factor infertility group revealed higher euploid rates with microfluidics.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was registered in clinicaltrials.gov, ID number NCT04818593. URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04818593. Date of registration: 3/25/2021. Date of first enrollment: 6/18/2021.

articles.title: Patient-Centered menopause health management and menopausal hormone therapy uptake: A real-world study from a tertiary Hospital in China.
articles.authors: Huang H, Men X, Lin X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether a patient-centered integrated menopause clinic model was associated with menopausal hormone therapy initiation, self-reported medication habits, and menopause-related knowledge among women with indications for treatment.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 405 women aged 40-60 years with MHT indications who attended Peking University First Hospital in 2023. Outcomes were compared between the MHT Integrated and Patient-Centered Clinic (MIPCC; n = 192) and a general menopause clinic (GMC; n = 213) after one year.
RESULTS: MIPCC patients were slightly older and more often postmenopausal. Insomnia, reduced libido, dyspareunia, vaginal dryness, and recurrent vaginitis were more frequent in the MIPCC group. MHT initiation was higher in the MIPCC group than in the GMC group (165/192 [85.94%] vs. 94/213 [44.13%]; adjusted OR 7.60, 95% CI 4.63, 12.49). Discontinuation among initiators was numerically lower in the MIPCC group (18.29% vs. 20.21%), but no statistically significant difference was observed. Selected self-reported medication-habit and knowledge responses were more favorable among MIPCC patients.
CONCLUSIONS: The MIPCC model was associated with higher MHT initiation and more favorable responses to selected self-reported medication-habit and knowledge items. Patient-centered menopause management may represent a useful preventive health strategy, but prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm its effectiveness and generalizability.

articles.title: Outcomes with intracytoplasmic sperm injection using fresh vs. frozen elongated spermatids from microsurgical testicular sperm extraction.
articles.authors: Elliott JE, Labos C, Meriano JS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the reproductive outcomes of intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) using fresh and frozen-thawed elongated spermatids obtained from microsurgical testicular sperm extraction (mTESE) from men with nonobstructive azoospermia.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SUBJECTS: A total of 256 infertile men underwent one or more mTESE procedures between 2004 and 2017, with the intention of attempting to conceive via ICSI with their female partners.
EXPOSURE: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection was performed using fresh or frozen-thawed elongated spermatids.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Sperm retrieval rate, fertilization rate, blastulation rate, embryo transfer rate, positive β-human chorionic gonadotropin level, clinical pregnancy rate, live birth rate, miscarriage rate.
RESULTS: A total of 256 men with nonobstructive azoospermia underwent 292 mTESE procedures. Of these, 90 men underwent 99 mTESE procedures in which only elongated spermatids were retrieved, and ICSI was performed later. One hundred-thirty eight ICSI cycles were performed using fresh or frozen elongated spermatids. Overall, fertilization and blastulation rates were 35.3% and 19.3%, respectively. Clinical pregnancy and live birth rates were 4.3% and 2.9%, respectively. There were no differences between live birth outcomes with fresh and frozen elongated spermatids. This relationship persisted after adjusting for male age at the time of mTESE, female age at the time of ICSI, and number of oocytes inseminated (fresh vs. frozen-thawed, odds ratio = 0.40 [0.03-5.33]).
CONCLUSION: A nonsignificant difference in reproductive outcomes between fresh and frozen-thawed elongated spermatids can facilitate scheduling of the mTESE procedure before or concurrently with ovarian stimulation cycles without compromising patient outcomes. However, the overall very poor reproductive outcomes with elongated spermatids suggest that very thorough counseling of patients utilizing spermatids should be mandatory, and use of donor sperm should be strongly considered to improve chances of a live birth.

articles.title: Tumor microenvironment-responsive manganese nanocarriers for on-demand release of methotrexate and DNAzyme in MiR-155-driven cervical cancer.
articles.authors: Yang Z, Zhang L, Wang Z et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer is a prevalent form of cancer that affects women on a global scale. MicroRNA-155 (miR-155) has been identified as a key player in cervical cancer, with its over-expression signifying a promising target for therapeutic interventions. However, the molecular mechanisms by which miR-155 contributes to the invasive progression of cervical cancer, as well as miRNA-based therapeutic approaches, remain to be elucidated. To address the issues, we initially investigated the functional role of miR-155 in cervical cancer progression. In vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that miR-155 was closely associated with the malignant progression of cervical cancer through regulation of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) process, specifically by directly targeting ZFPM2 protein, thereby exerting oncogenic effects. Based on these findings, we designed manganese-based composite agents, namely MnO2@PDA-DNAzyme-substrate-methotrexate nanoparticles (MPDM NPs), for simultaneous miRNA imaging and chemotherapy toward cervical cancer. The MPDM NPs exhibited favorable biocompatibility and tumor microenvironment (TME) responsive release behavior, allowing controlled release of Mn2+, methotrexate (MTX), and DNAzyme probes for miR-155 detection and therapeutic intervention. In vivo studies with tumor-bearing mice indicated that the MPDM NPs could effectively target tumors. The Mn2+-activate miRNA imaging achieved a detection limit for miR-155 of 0.3 nM. Moreover, the drug MTX enabled tumor chemotherapy by regulating the EMT process. This, in turn, has resulted in an impressive tumor inhibition rate of 86.2%. This proposed strategy indicated significant potential for the advancement of precision theranostics in the context of cervical cancer.

articles.title: Whole systems traditional Chinese medicine utilization among women undergoing frozen embryo transfers at an academic fertility center.
articles.authors: Rodgers-Melnick SN, Hullender Rubin L, Kim ST et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate sociodemographic and clinical variables associated with Whole Systems Traditional Chinese Medicine (WS-TCM) utilization alongside frozen embryo transfers (FETs) after in vitro fertilization.
DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective review of all autologous FETs performed within an academic medical center's fertility clinic between January 2019 and March 2024. One FET cycle per patient was randomly selected for analysis. After conducting bivariate analyses, a logistic regression model was employed to examine independent associations with WS-TCM utilization.
SUBJECTS: Women aged 21-42 who underwent an FET after in vitro fertilization. FETs involving donor egg embryos, gestational carriers, and those with missing live birth outcome data were excluded.
EXPOSURE: Attending ≥1 WS-TCM appointment between 120 days pre- and 12 days post-FET. Whole Systems Traditional Chinese Medicine treatment modalities included individualized acupuncture, nutritional and lifestyle modifications, and focused dietary supplements.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Sociodemographic and clinical variables associated with WS-TCM utilization.
RESULTS: Of 799 women studied, 162 (20.3%) utilized WS-TCM, receiving a median of 5.5 treatments between 120 days pre- and 12 days post-FET. Whole Systems Traditional Chinese Medicine users resided in neighborhoods with higher median income ($83,025 vs. $75,602). Previous medical histories of women incorporating WS-TCM included higher rates of migraine/headache (21.6% vs. 13.3%), musculoskeletal pain (37.0% vs. 27.5%), recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL; 25.9% vs. 12.9%), pain associated with genital organs (21.0% vs. 14.1%), and undergoing more assisted reproductive technology cycles. Higher neighborhood median income (adjusted odds ratio and 95% confidence interval: 1.36 [1.13, 1.64]), recurrent pregnancy loss (2.15 [1.33, 3.47]), and undergoing ≥3 vs. 0-1 assisted reproductive technology cycles (1.78 [1.02, 3.06]) were independently associated with higher odds of WS-TCM engagement, whereas higher body mass index (0.79 [0.64, 0.97]), undergoing preimplantation genetic testing (0.61 [0.39, 0.94]), and having a history of salpingitis/oophoritis/pelvic inflammatory disease (0.59 [0.37, 0.92]) or high-risk pregnancy supervision (0.53 [0.30, 0.93]) were associated with lower odds.
CONCLUSION: Within this cohort, multiple pain- and reproductive health-related diagnoses were more prevalent among individuals utilizing WS-TCM. Findings inform…

articles.title: High Prevalence and Limited Perinatal Prediction of Kidney Dysfunction in Adolescents Born Extremely Preterm.
articles.authors: Sanderson KR, Vazquez JE, Flythe JE et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Extremely preterm birth (< 28 weeks' gestation) increases chronic kidney disease (CKD) risk. However, among those born extremely preterm, the prevalence of abnormal kidney health during adolescence and its perinatal predictors remain poorly defined.
METHODS: Adolescents from the Extremely Low Gestational Age Newborn -Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ELGAN-ECHO) cohort (14 US hospitals) were assessed for abnormal kidney health defined as ≥ 1 indicator-chronic kidney disease in children (CKiD) U25 estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 90 ml/min per 1.73 m2, blood pressure (BP) ≥ 120/80 mm Hg, or microalbuminuria > 30 mg/g.Five feature selection methods screened perinatal covariate predictors using a 60 to 40 training-test split. Multiple imputation addressed missing data in sensitivity analyses. Area under the curve (AUC) was the primary performance metric.
RESULTS: Of the 675 adolescents (mean age 18 years), 354 (52%) had a classifiable kidney health status, as follows: 188 with all 3 measurements and 166 with partial measurements showing ≥ 1 abnormality. The prevalence of abnormal kidney health was 66% among complete cases (125/188) and 82% among all determinate cases (291/354). In the full cohort, prevalence ranged from 43% to 91% (bounding estimates accounting for missing data). Individual measurements revealed 30.5% with reduced eGFR, 42% with elevated BP, and 9% with microalbuminuria. Across all methods, perinatal covariates achieved random test-set discrimination (AUC: 0.48-0.55) for abnormal kidney health prediction, compared with training set AUCs of 0.66-0.72.
CONCLUSION: Abnormal kidney health is highly prevalent after extremely preterm birth, underscoring the importance of protocolized longitudinal kidney health surveillance throughout childhood to enable early identification of CKD and elevated BP in children born extremely preterm. The perinatal factors we examined did not meaningfully predict kidney health abnormalities and variable importance did not translate to individual-level prediction in this cohort.

articles.title: Chemoresistance in cervical cancer: identifying and exploiting non-coding RNAs.
articles.authors: Makgoo L, Mbita Z
articles.abstract: Drug resistance continues to pose a significant challenge, accounting for a large proportion of relapses and playing a major role in cervical cancer-related mortality worldwide. Emerging evidence has indicated that the aberrant expression of non-coding RNAs, especially circular RNAs (circRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and microRNAs (miRNAs) is responsible for drug resistance, which poses a significant challenge to the success of chemotherapy. Addressing drug resistance is crucial for improving patient outcomes and reducing the burden of cervical cancer on healthcare systems. In this review, we summarize the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which circRNAs, miRNAs and lncRNAs mediate drug resistance to common drugs used in the treatment of cervical cancer. This work underscores non-coding RNAs as a promising therapeutic target, offering a potential avenue for overcoming chemoresistance in cervical cancer.

articles.title: Evaluating carbon affinity in catalytic methane decomposition using UBI-QEP energetics and DFT carbon-binding analysis.
articles.authors: Sorkhe Y
articles.abstract: Catalytic methane decomposition produces hydrogen and solid carbon, but carbon growth does not necessarily cause catalyst deactivation. This study examines the usefulness and limitations of carbon affinity as a descriptor using UBI-QEP energetics for Fe, Ni, Pt and Cu, supported by published density functional theory (DFT) and experimental evidence. The methane-to-adsorbed-carbon enthalpy, D C, correlates strongly with the carbon chemisorption energy (r = -0.994) and almost exactly with the combined carbon and hydrogen binding term, Q(C) + 4Q(H). These relationships reveal its algebraic dependence on the underlying adsorption energies, rather than establishing an independent descriptor. Closing the thermochemical cycle to gaseous H2 eliminates the hydrogen-binding contribution and clarifies the physical meaning of the chosen endpoint. An internally consistent DFT dataset covering 14 transition metals provides an external energetic comparison of carbon-binding order. For the four core metals, carbon-binding magnitudes show strong correlation (r = 0.929), although the Ni-Pt ordering is reversed. Facet-dependent adsorption, carbon migration barriers and experimental comparisons further demonstrate why elemental carbon affinity alone cannot predict activity or catalyst lifetime. Neither the DFT energetic comparison nor the heterogeneous experimental contrasts constitute validation of an out-of-sample model for catalytic activity or catalyst lifetime. Graphite-referenced equilibrium calculations quantify temperature and pressure effects without assuming quasi-equilibrium among the adsorbed CH x intermediates. The analysis retains D C as a transparent semi-empirical reaction-energy index while identifying carbon transport, nucleation and catalyst-state evolution as essential to interpreting filament growth, encapsulation and sustained hydrogen production.

articles.title: Ischemic Stroke Associated With Vertebral Artery Occlusion Following Cervical Spine Manipulation in a Young Woman With Underlying Vascular Risk Factors: A Case Report.
articles.authors: González-Delatorre A, Alvarado-Velásquez J, Ruiz-Alayón B et al.
articles.abstract: A 35-year-old woman with migraine and oral contraceptive use presented with pontine stroke and right vertebral artery occlusion following cervical manipulation by a lay practitioner. Managed conservatively outside the reperfusion window, she achieved progressive recovery. This case highlights a plausible temporal association between neck manipulation and ischemic events.

articles.title: Live births following universal single-step warming across multiple vitrification systems.
articles.authors: Parmegiani L, Vajta G, Lynch C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report live birth and neonatal outcomes across multiple commercial kit brands, including cross-brand combinations, thereby providing clinical validation of a universal warming method on the basis of single-step elution using 1 M nonpermeating solutes (NPS). Human blastocysts are routinely vitrified using commercial kits with minor compositional differences. Previous studies have shown that simplified single-step warming with 1 M NPS can reduce handling time and improve laboratory efficiency. However, this universal ultrafast warming approach has not been systematically evaluated across different warming kits or mixed vitrification-warming combinations.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.
SUBJECTS: A total of 469 vitrified blastocysts warmed between January 1, 2024 and December 31, 2024.
EXPOSURE: Blastocysts were vitrified using four commercially available kits and warmed by single-step elution in 1 M NPS from the corresponding thawing solutions, generating 12 vitrification-warming combinations. Vitrification was performed at room temperature (12-15 min in equilibration solution followed by 60 s in vitrification solution before plunging). Warming consisted of a single step in thawing solution (1 M NPS) at 37 °C.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Cryosurvival, clinical pregnancy, implantation, live birth and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS: Overall, 469 blastocysts were warmed and transferred in 428 cycles, resulting in 100% survival, a clinical pregnancy rate of 45.8%, an implantation rate of 43.1%, and a live birth rate of 36.0%, with 159 babies born. No significant differences were observed between groups in pregnancy, implantation or live birth rates. Mean neonatal weight was 3.2 ± 0.4 kg and was comparable between groups, ranging from 3.0 ± 0.7 to 3.6 ± 0.5 kg, and similar to that observed following fresh embryo transfers during the same period. The preterm live birth rate was 6.3%, with no difference between groups, and was comparable with fresh transfers and national Assisted Reproductive Technology registry data. Sex distribution was balanced (48.4% male, 51.6% female) and comparable between groups, fresh transfers (46.9% male, 53.1% female), and national registry data. No major congenital anomalies or severe neonatal diseases were reported. Some between-group comparisons are limited by small sample sizes and high survival rates, so nonsignificant P values may be due to low statistical power rather than true group similarity.
CONCLUSION: This…

articles.title: Fertility and Obstetric Outcomes Among Procedural and Nonprocedural Physicians: A Call for Improved Fertility Education for Medical Students and Trainees.
articles.journal: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
articles.authors: O'Neill ES, Hendizadeh AN, Diep QM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most physicians are in training during the time of known fertility decline, and trainees postpone parenthood for a variety of reasons. The aim of this study is to describe differences between the experiences of proceduralists versus nonproceduralists.
METHODS: An 11-item anonymous survey addressing experiences with pregnancy, fertility, and assisted reproductive technology (ART) was distributed to physicians (n = 2098) at 2 academic medical centers.
RESULTS: There was a 20% (n = 423) response rate. The median age was 31 years. Of the respondents, 293 (69%) were female. Two hundred seventy-six (66%) were trainees and 154 (36%) were proceduralists. Of 293, 137 (46.8%) female respondents reported having ever been pregnant. Of those, 55 (40%) reported pregnancy or obstetric complications. The overall birth rate was 2.57 (SD 0.95) live births per woman. Proceduralists had a lower number of live births (mean [SD], 2.3 [0.93] versus 2.7 [0.94]; P < 0.014). Of all respondents, 302 (72%) of 423 reported no prior education about fertility or ART. Proceduralists were significantly more likely to report never having received information on fertility and ART during residency (123 of 154 [80%] versus 179 of 269 [67%]; P = 0.007).
CONCLUSIONS: We found a high prevalence of pregnancy and obstetric complications as well as pregnancy loss, with significantly fewer live births among proceduralists versus nonproceduralists. Medical school and residency curricula should include relevant fertility data and education to allow trainees to make informed decisions regarding family planning and fertility preservation.

articles.title: A predictive model based on maternal immune-inflammatory markers for ARDS identification in mechanically ventilated late-preterm and term neonates.
articles.authors: Zhang C, Jing H, Xu D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally evaluate a model that uses maternal blood markers obtained before delivery to differentiate neonatal acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) from other causes of respiratory distress in late-preterm and term neonates requiring mechanical ventilation.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 227 mother-infant pairs from two tertiary hospitals between June 2024 and January 2026. Neonates born at 34-40 weeks' gestation with ventilation-dependent respiratory distress were divided into a training cohort and an internal test cohort. Predictors were screened using elastic-net regression with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Four feature sets and six algorithms were then compared by 20 repeats of stratified five-fold cross-validation, and a six-predictor random forest (RF) was ultimately selected. Discrimination, calibration and net benefit were assessed, with 500-resample bootstrap optimism correction and Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) interpretation.
RESULTS: Maternal systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and related inflammatory ratios were higher, and antenatal infection was more frequent, in the ARDS group, whereas recorded antenatal corticosteroid (ACS) use was less frequent (P < 0.001). Six predictors were retained in the final model: SII, antenatal infection, maternal age, gestational hypothyroidism, gestational diabetes mellitus and ACS use. The principal internal performance estimate, the mean training-set cross-validated area under the curve (AUC) was 0.729 ± 0.080, the fixed-pipeline optimism-corrected AUC was 0.793 and the internal test-set AUC was 0.827 (95% CI, 0.712-0.923), with an average precision of 0.828 and a Brier score of 0.175. These three values are not interchangeable and are reported as one principal and two secondary estimates, and none represents fully independent performance. At the training-derived threshold of 0.424, sensitivity was 78.8% and specificity 77.8%. SHAP identified SII as the largest contributor, without implying a causal effect for any predictor. Logistic regression using the same six predictors reached a numerically higher internal test-set AUC (0.838 versus 0.827, ΔAUC = -0.011, P = 0.744) and a cross-validated AUC of 0.706 ± 0.082 versus 0.729 ± 0.080, the RF therefore conferred no discriminative advantage.
CONCLUSIONS: In mechanical ventilation needed neonates born at 34-40 weeks' gestation with respiratory distress, the six-predictor RF showed moderate discrimination,…

articles.title: Expression of estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor in endometrial cancer and their correlations with clinicopathological features.
articles.authors: Li EP, Hong Y, Wei JZ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the expression levels of estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR) in endometrial carcinoma (EC) and their correlations with standardized clinicopathological parameters in a single-center surgical cohort.
METHODS: Retrospective clinical and pathological data of 78 EC patients receiving primary surgery at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of Kiang Wu Hospital between Jan 2016 and Aug 2022 were collected. ER/PR expression was quantified via immunohistochemistry (IHC) using the Allred scoring system. Dichotomous receptor positivity (Allred 0-2 negative/3-8 positive) and continuous total Allred scores were analyzed separately. Fisher's exact test or χ² test was used for categorical comparison; Kruskal-Wallis H test with adjusted post-hoc pairwise tests and Wilcoxon rank-sum test were applied for ordinal Allred score data. Exact P values, test statistics and degrees of freedom were reported for all analyses.
RESULTS: The overall cohort included 71 endometrioid carcinoma (EC) and 7 non-endometrioid carcinoma (NEC) cases. ER and PR positive rates were significantly higher in endometrioid lesions (97.2% and 94.4%) than non-endometrioid subtypes (57.1% for both, P = 0.018/P = 0.018). Continuous Allred scores of ER and PR declined significantly with worsening tumor differentiation (all adjusted P<0.05). For FIGO staging, significantly reduced ER and PR Allred scores were observed in Stage II compared with Stage I. The single Stage-III case was reported descriptively and was not included in formal statistical testing. Patients with lymph node metastasis exhibited lower PR Allred scores (P = 0.021), while ER expression showed no statistically significant difference (P = 0.076). No significant associations were found between ER/PR scores and depth of myometrial invasion or lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) (all P>0.05).
CONCLUSION: Reduced ER and PR expression correlates with poorer tumor differentiation and advanced FIGO stage in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma; PR loss is independently associated with lymph node metastasis. This study only identifies crude cross-sectional correlations without survival or multivariable adjustment data, so ER/PR may merely serve as auxiliary morphological markers reflecting tumor aggressive potential, rather than standalone indicators for prognosis or individualized hormone therapy guidance.

articles.title: Thalassaemia prevention in Asia: progress, challenges, and future directions.
articles.journal: The Lancet regional health. Southeast Asia
articles.authors: Angastiniotis M, Fucharoen S, Paiboonsukwong K et al.
articles.abstract: Thalassaemia remains a major public health burden in Asia, where high carrier frequencies, diverse mutation spectra, and variable healthcare capacity continue to influence disease prevention and control. This Series paper summarises the status of thalassaemia prevention programmes across 14 Asian countries and highlights the key challenges and opportunities affecting their implementation. Singapore, Malaysia, the Maldives, and Thailand have established the most structured prevention strategies, incorporating combinations of public awareness, carrier screening, genetic counselling, and prenatal diagnosis, with measurable success most clearly demonstrated in Singapore and, to a specific extent, Thailand. In contrast, many other countries in the region continue to face fragmented services, limited national coordination, shortages of trained personnel, inadequate epidemiological data, and financial, technological, cultural, and social barriers. Differences in prevention efforts broadly reflect wider disparities in health system development. Strengthening national prevention programmes should be viewed as both a public health priority and a cost-effective investment in reducing long-term disease burden.

articles.title: Association between pre-delivery maternal red blood cell distribution width and birth weight discordance in twin pregnancies: a twin pregnancy cohort study.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Su J, Yue L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Twin growth discordance, commonly defined as an inter-twin birth weight difference ≥20%, is linked to increased neonatal morbidity, but simple maternal laboratory markers to aid late-pregnancy risk assessment are limited. Red blood cell distribution width (RDW), a routine hematological parameter associated with inflammation and placental dysfunction, has been associated with adverse perinatal outcomes in singleton pregnancies; however, its role in twin growth discordance remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the association between pre-delivery RDW measured within 1 week before delivery and twin growth discordance in a cohort of Chinese twin pregnancies.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included 1,714 women with twin pregnancies who delivered at the Gansu Provincial Maternity and Childcare Hospital between July 2020 and February 2024. Pre-delivery RDW was obtained from the last prenatal complete blood count within 1 week before delivery. Twin growth discordance was defined as inter-twin birth weight discordance ≥20%. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, with RDW modeled continuously and categorically (<14.3, 14.3-16.0%, and ≥16.1%). Restricted cubic spline, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: Overall, 231 women (13.5%) had twin growth discordance. Compared with the lowest RDW category, the highest category was associated with increased odds of twin growth discordance after adjustment for maternal age, IVF status, chorionicity, gestational age, pregestational body mass index, parity, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, gestational diabetes mellitus, and hemoglobin [odds ratio (OR) 1.89, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.28-2.80; p = 0.001]. A significant trend was observed across RDW categories (p for trend = 0.001). RDW modeled as a continuous variable showed a borderline association after full adjustment (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.00-1.12; p = 0.060). Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested a nonlinear association (p for non-linearity = 0.013). Results were similar using discordance ≥25% (OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.31-3.83; p = 0.003).
CONCLUSION: Higher pre-delivery RDW was associated with greater odds of twin growth discordance. Prospective studies with serial RDW measurements are needed to confirm these findings and determine their clinical relevance.

articles.title: Uterine infection-induced transcriptomic changes in the bovine endometrium.
articles.authors: Adnan MR, Lee CN, Khadka VS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uterine infections negatively impact cow health and productivity, increasing herd health costs, infertility, and culling. They also interfere with immune efficiency, sperm transport, embryonic development, and implantation, thus leading to pregnancy failure and infertility. Most previous studies have focused on transcriptomic changes induced by uterine infection in dairy cows. The present study aimed to investigate the changes in the endometrial transcript caused by uterine infections in beef cows.
METHODS: To achieve this, we examined the reproductive tract of over 200 Angus cows at a local slaughterhouse and collected intercaruncular endometrial tissues from a subset of infected cows (uteri filled with pus) and normal cyclic cows (n = 5/group). After isolating total RNA, the samples were subjected to high-throughput RNA sequencing (n = 5/group), and differentially expressed genes were validated using qPCR.
RESULTS: RNA seq revealed 954 differentially expressed genes (538 upregulated and 416 downregulated) in the bovine endometrium compared to infectious and normal uterine samples. The Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) showed 822 genes enriched in the bovine endometrium, with 530 upregulated and 292 downregulated in response to uterine infection. The activated immune system components include TLR receptors, NLR receptors, RLR receptors, cytokines, and chemokines. This enrichment of genes and molecules affects various biological processes and pathways, such as inflammatory and immune responses, cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, and chemokine signaling.
CONCLUSIONS: In summary, uterine infection alters the transcriptomic profile of the endometrium in infectious beef cows, potentially leading to pregnancy failure and infertility.

articles.title: An intravaginal ring for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis: assessment of safety and pharmacokinetics in a randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: Vincent KL, Moss JA, Marzinke MA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In Eastern and Southern Africa, 63% of new HIV infections occurred in women and girls, with adolescent girls and young women representing a particularly vulnerable subpopulation. Effective vaginal products for HIV prevention are desirable because they are underrepresented in the currently approved portfolio and have attributes motivating product use. In this trial, we evaluated an innovative intravaginal ring (pod-IVR) as a platform for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP).
OBJECTIVE: To measure the safety and multicompartment pharmacokinetics (PKs) of a pod-IVR delivering tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) combined with emtricitabine (FTC) in healthy women over 28 days.
METHODS: The Phase 1 clinical trial consisted of a randomized order, controlled, double-blinded, crossover design. Ten women received either an active TDF-FTC pod-IVR or a placebo pod-IVR for 28 days, determined by 1:1 randomization, followed by product crossover for another 28 days. Safety was assessed in terms of adverse events related to product use, colposcopic examination, cervicovaginal epithelium thickness measurement by optical coherence tomography, and culture-independent assessment of the vaginal microbiome. Drug and/or drug metabolite concentrations were measured in cervicovaginal fluid (CVF), vaginal tissue, rectal tissue, rectal fluid, and plasma.
RESULTS: There was no evidence of a statistically significant difference in related adverse-event counts between study products. There also was no evidence suggesting the study product altered the vaginal microbiome systematically or reproducibly. Systemic plasma exposure to tenofovir (TFV) and FTC was low, consistent with topical delivery. High median CVF concentrations of TFV (38.9 ng mg-1; 135×103 fmol mg-1) and FTC (239 ng mg-1; 966×103 fmol mg-1) were measured. Median vaginal tissue concentrations of the anabolites responsible for inhibition of HIV reverse transcriptase exceeded our target concentrations: TFV diphosphate 0.651×103 fmol mg-1 and FTC triphosphate 0.180×103 fmol mg-1. Drug concentrations in rectal tissue samples generally were below the analytical lower limits of quantification, but were quantifiable in rectal fluids, 130 (TFV) and 300 (FTC) times lower than in CVF.
CONCLUSIONS: The TDF-FTC pod-IVRs were safe and well-tolerated over the 28 days of consecutive use. The PK data met the target benchmarks associated with protection from vaginal HIV infection.
