articles.title: Navigating the Unknown: A Qualitative Exploration of the Lived Experiences of People With Multiple Sclerosis During Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Chen V, Shah S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People with multiple sclerosis (MS) face challenges in family planning and pregnancy due to the unpredictable nature of the disease and a lack of clear guidelines for approaching pregnancy-related care. The objective of this qualitative study was to explore the pregnancy experiences of people with MS, focusing on uncertainty and mental health.
METHODS: Semistructured interviews were conducted at the Duke Neurological Disorders Clinic (N = 10). Thematic analysis was conducted inductively to identify main themes.
RESULTS: Participants, aged 26 to 40 years, had a range of 1 to 12 years since MS diagnosis and an average of 2 pregnancies and 1.3 children per participant. Three main types of uncertainty were identified: (1) anticipation of the future (relapses, impact of MS on motherhood, health care factors); (2) experienced symptoms (differentiating MS from pregnancy, role of MS in peripartum challenges); and (3) availability of information (insufficient research, provider counseling, external support). These uncertainties negatively impacted mental health, with most participants reporting mental health challenges (n = 7, 70%) and utilizing mental health resources (n = 8, 80%), including talk therapy, psychiatric medications, and support groups.
CONCLUSIONS: People with MS experience disease-related uncertainty during and around pregnancy. This study highlights the need for proactive counseling on medication safety, lactation, risks of infertility, and pregnancy complications. We also identify a need to address uncertainty and its impacts on the mental health of pregnant people with MS. Clear provider recommendations, timely communication, enhanced mental health screening, and augmented social support are likely to be beneficial in this setting.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of cfDNA-Based Liquid Biopsy for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Liu J, Zhang Y, Yang S et al.
articles.abstract: Conventional surveillance tools for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) have limited sensitivity. Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA)-based liquid biopsy is a promising minimally invasive approach; however, its overall diagnostic performance remains unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of cfDNA-based liquid biopsy in HCC. Following PRISMA-DTA guidelines, we searched PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science until July 2026. Diagnostic accuracy data were pooled using bivariate random-effects models. Methodological quality was assessed using QUADAS-2 and NOS. A total of 29 studies (4250 HCC patients, 7982 controls) were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity of cfDNA-based testing were 0.82 (95% CI: 0.76-0.86) and 0.91 (95% CI: 0.88-0.93). The area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.93 (95% CI: 0.91-0.96). Subgroup analyses showed higher sensitivity in advanced HCC 0.91 (95% CI: 0.85-0.95) than early HCC 0.77 (95% CI: 0.71-0.83). Methylation profiling yielded relatively higher sensitivity 0.84 (95% CI: 0.77-0.89), whereas fragmentomics showed relatively favorable specificity 0.93 (95% CI: 0.88-0.96). Combining cfDNA-based testing with alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) significantly improved sensitivity compared with cfDNA alone (0.78 vs. 0.65). No significant publication bias was detected (p = 0.83). cfDNA-based liquid biopsy achieves high diagnostic accuracy for HCC. As exploratory observations, methylation-based assays with relatively higher sensitivity may have potential value for screening high-risk populations, while fragmentomics-based assays with relatively favorable specificity may aid differential diagnosis. Combining cfDNA-based liquid biopsy with AFP further improves diagnostic performance, supporting cfDNA as a promising noninvasive tool for HCC detection. Trial Registration: This systematic review was registered on PROSPERO: CRD420261293877 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/).

articles.title: Maternal Smoking and Sex Distribution Among Live Births in Western Sydney: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Trinh LTT, Clague L, Naz S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal smoking may affect fetal survival, but evidence regarding offspring sex is inconsistent. We estimated the male proportion among live births and did not assess sex determination or pregnancy loss before the perinatal reporting threshold.
AIMS: To examine whether smoking during the first half of pregnancy was associated with male live birth and whether the association differed by smoking intensity.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analysed singleton live births of Western Sydney residents in the New South Wales Perinatal Data Collection, 2016-2023. Smoking was classified as non-smoking, ≤ 10 cigarettes/day, or > 10 cigarettes/day. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs), adjusted for calendar year and maternal demographic, socioeconomic and clinical characteristics.
RESULTS: Of 119 756 eligible births, 721 (0.6%) had unknown smoking information, leaving 119,035 births. Male births comprised 51.6% among non-smokers, 52.2% among women smoking ≤ 10 cigarettes/day, and 52.4% among women smoking > 10 cigarettes/day. Crude differences were + 0.60 and + 0.78 percentage points (p = 0.608). The adjusted model included 117,745 births; adjusted ORs were 1.02 (95% CI 0.96-1.08) and 1.02 (95% CI 0.90-1.16), respectively. The heavier-smoking estimate was imprecise (n = 964).
CONCLUSIONS: Lower-intensity smoking was not meaningfully associated with male live birth. Estimates for > 10 cigarettes/day were imprecise, and moderate effects in either direction could not be excluded. Findings apply only to live births reaching the reporting threshold.

articles.title: Effects of virtual reality and music intervention on pain relief in outpatient hysteroscopy.
articles.journal: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi
articles.authors: Yip KM, Chan SSC, Cheung ECW et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Outpatient hysteroscopy is an essential gynaecological procedure used to evaluate and treat any intrauterine pathologies. However, the most common reason for procedure failure is pain. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of virtual reality (VR) and music for pain management during outpatient hysteroscopy.
METHODS: This was a non-blinded randomised controlled trial conducted at a single tertiary hospital in Hong Kong. Eligible patients were randomised at a 1:1:1 ratio into three groups: VR, music, and control. Patients' pain scores were assessed using the Numerical Pain Rating Scale from 0 to 10 at various timepoints during hysteroscopy. The primary outcome was the maximum pain score during hysteroscopy. Secondary outcomes included pain scores at specific timepoints during hysteroscopy, other symptoms, patient satisfaction scores, and acceptance of undergoing future hysteroscopy in the same setting if needed.
RESULTS: A total of 210 patients were analysed in the study. Overall, 65.7% of patients underwent diagnostic hysteroscopy, and 34.3% underwent additional procedures. The mean maximum pain scores did not significantly differ among the three groups (P=0.131). However, acceptance of future hysteroscopy was significantly higher in both the music group (mean ± standard deviation: 8.8 ± 2.1; P=0.002) and the VR group (8.6 ± 1.6; P=0.009) than in the control group (7.5 ± 2.7; overall P=0.001).
CONCLUSION: The use of VR and music during outpatient hysteroscopy did not result in a statistically significant reduction in pain. However, patient acceptance of future hysteroscopy was significantly improved in both intervention groups.

articles.title: Association of Intralipid Infusions With Birth Outcomes and First-Trimester Placental Biomarkers in Frozen Embryo Transfer Cycles: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Kamal N, Woodman R, Tremellen K
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intralipid is used as an adjunctive therapy in assisted reproductive technology (ART), but data regarding pregnancy outcomes and early placental biomarkers are limited.
AIMS: To evaluate the association between Intralipid exposure during frozen embryo transfer (FET) cycles and pregnancy outcomes, birthweight and first-trimester placental biomarkers.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 729 women undergoing FET cycles resulting in delivery beyond 20 weeks at a private assisted reproduction clinic between 2017 and 2023. Outcomes were compared between women receiving intravenous Intralipid (n = 136) and those not receiving Intralipid (n = 593). Multivariable analyses adjusted for maternal age, body mass index, parity, plurality, foetal sex, cycle type, intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) use and preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) status.
RESULTS: Individual pregnancy outcomes, including preterm birth, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, gestational diabetes, foetal growth restriction, congenital anomalies and stillbirth, did not differ significantly between groups. Intralipid exposure was not independently associated with the composite adverse pregnancy outcome after adjustment (adjusted OR 2.08, 95% CI 0.73-5.96; p = 0.171). Intralipid-exposed pregnancies had lower first-trimester PAPP-A MoM values after adjustment (adjusted geometric mean ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.76-0.98; p = 0.021), whereas PlGF and free β-hCG concentrations did not differ significantly. Lower PAPP-A concentrations were not associated with birthweight z-scores.
CONCLUSIONS: Intralipid exposure was not independently associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes after adjustment. Pregnancies exposed to Intralipid had lower first-trimester PAPP-A measures without corresponding differences in other placental biomarkers or birthweight z-scores. Linkage of the Australia and New Zealand Assisted Reproduction Database with perinatal outcome registries, with routine capture of adjunctive ART therapies, would support more comprehensive maternal and neonatal safety evaluation.

articles.title: From efficacy to effectiveness in gynecologic oncology: social determinants, therapeutic transportability, and biological weathering.
articles.authors: Zheng Z, Chen Y, Yao X et al.
articles.abstract: Precision therapeutics have improved outcomes in gynecologic oncology, but their population-level impact depends on both biological efficacy and reliable treatment delivery. Randomized controlled trials establish causal effects under defined conditions; real-world evidence characterizes implementation and transportability while introducing distinct confounding and measurement challenges. This contextual narrative review integrates pivotal and updated therapeutic studies with clinical, social and translational evidence available through September 2026. Progression-free survival and overall survival are distinct endpoints, whereas effectiveness concerns benefit in routine care; cross-study interpretation requires aligned populations, treatment strategies, follow-up and estimands. The benefits of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors and immunotherapy are examined separately by molecular subgroup and treatment setting. Financial hardship, geographic access, caregiving and health-system constraints can affect initiation, tolerable exposure and continuity. We use the proposed term "social discontinuation" for treatment disruption with a material social contribution, while distinguishing clinical reasons and patient preference. Biological weathering provides plausible links between cumulative adversity and inflammatory, neuroendocrine, epigenetic and immune phenotypes. Human epidemiological associations, translational findings and experimental mechanisms support different inferences; mediation through treatment delivery remains distinct from biological modification of treatment effect. Priorities include justified broader eligibility, prospective social-needs and exposure measurement, responsive symptom management, navigation and hybrid care. Automated extraction and prediction tools require external validation, fairness assessment and prospective clinical-impact evaluation. Integrating randomized and real-world evidence can identify remediable barriers without diminishing the clinical value of effective therapies.

articles.title: Changes in the diagnosis and management of polycystic ovary syndrome in adolescents based on recommendations of scientific societies over the last decade.
articles.authors: Kamińska G, Chmiela S, Kucharska A
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: he paper presents a systematic review of current guidelines from scientific societies regarding polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in adolescents published over the past decade.
AIM OF THE STUDY: To summarize and compare recent international and national PCOS guidelines with emphasis on areas of consensus and divergence.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A systematic review of guidelines published between 2015 and 2025 was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Ultimately, twelve documents containing adolescent-specific content were included.
RESULTS: In adolescents with PCOS, clinical symptoms of hyperandrogenism and menstrual irregularities are the main diagnostic criteria, whereas polycystic ovarian morphology and anti-Müllerian hormone concentration are not considered reliable indicators in adolescents. The current approach to PCOS also emphasizes the assessment and management of metabolic and psychological comorbidities.
CONCLUSIONS: The diagnosis and treatment of PCOS in girls require a separate approach related to age and ongoing puberty. According to the latest recommendations, lifestyle changes should be a mandatory part of therapy regardless of the background of the presented disorder. The pharmacological treatment should be tailored to the dominant symptoms.

articles.title: Effects of early menarche on adolescent health: a single-centre retrospective study.
articles.authors: Akin SB, Özgen IT, Cesur Y
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Over the past century, the onset of puberty and age at menarche in girls has progressively occurred earlier. This study investigates the effects of early menarche on final height, psychological health, and gynaecological outcomes in adolescent girls.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 58 female patients who were diagnosed with early menarche at ages 9.5 to 10.75 years. Target height (TH) was calculated based on medical records from their initial clinic visit. Data on final adult height (FAH), TH, weight, menstrual patterns, dysmenorrhoea, abnormal bleeding, the time taken for menstrual regularisation, diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), and any psychiatric or psychological disorders requiring medication were collected via questionnaire. FAH was compared to TH.
RESULTS: The average TH of the patients was 159.27 ±4.52 cm, and FAH was 157.71 ±5.19 cm (p = 0.029). The TH standard deviation score (SDS) was 0.64 ±0.76, and the FAH SDS was 0.81 ±0.91 (p = 0.160). It was noted that 6 out of the 11 patients who experienced a reduction of more than -1 SDS in their height compared to the TH also had a chronic illness (especially asthma). Half of the girls reported experiencing dysmenorrhoea, and around 15% were diagnosed with PCOS. Psychological problems were found in 22.4% of the patients (n = 13), and 15.5% of the patients (n = 9) were receiving treatment for mental health conditions.
CONCLUSIONS: Early menarche was associated with a higher prevalence of PCOS and psychiatric/psychological disorders, with a more pronounced adverse impact on final height among those with chronic illnesses.

articles.title: Maternal kidney disease and composite kidney outcomes in the offspring.
articles.authors: Hsu CN, Li LC, Chien SJ et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, but its relationship with long-term offspring kidney health remains uncertain. This retrospective maternal-child cohort study examined whether maternal CKD or reduced kidney function before or during pregnancy was associated with a composite kidney outcome in offspring. Live births in the Taiwan Mother and Child Health cohort from 2007 to 2017 were followed through 2018. In the primary cohort, maternal kidney disease was defined as claims-based CKD meeting chronicity criteria before or during pregnancy; the maternal eGFR subcohort additionally included eGFR-defined reduced kidney function. The primary outcome comprised ICD-defined CKD, reduced eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or ≥30% eGFR decline at age ≥2 years, or kidney replacement therapy. Laboratory components were interpreted as reduced kidney function rather than definitive CKD unless diagnostic chronicity was documented. Models adjusted for maternal, pregnancy, offspring, and perinatal covariates. Among 79,036 children, 4,687 (5.9%) met the composite kidney outcome. Maternal kidney disease was associated with modestly higher odds of the composite outcome (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.00-1.66) and offspring all-cause mortality (aOR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.15-3.09). Analyses of individual components of the composite outcome, sex-stratified subgroups, and trimester-specific exposure windows were exploratory, imprecise, and not adjusted for multiplicity. Maternal CKD or reduced kidney function may identify dyads who warrant long-term kidney surveillance, although causal pathways require confirmation.

articles.title: Prenatal diagnosis of severe glutaric acidemia type II due to a novel homozygous ETFDH frameshift variant: Case report and literature review.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Kaplan S, Polat BB, Melekoğlu R
articles.abstract: Glutaric acidemia type II (GA2) is a rare autosomal recessive fatty acid oxidation disorder that can present prenatally with bilateral hyperechoic cystic kidneys. We report a 23-year-old gravida 2 woman who was referred at 18+2 weeks for suspected fetal renal anomalies, with a history of consanguinity and a prior unexplained neonatal death. Quantitative fluorescent polymerase chain reaction and microarray were normal; whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous ETFDH frameshift variant (c.1200_1203del; p.His401GlnfsTer3). The parents were heterozygous, and the variant was classified as likely pathogenic. The family terminated the pregnancy after counseling. This case highlights both GA2 in the differential diagnosis of fetal renal anomalies and the value of prenatal exome sequencing for diagnosis and counseling.

articles.title: Sexual function and surgical outcomes after vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery versus total laparoscopic hysterectomy.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Bulat Çim H, Altuğ İnan M, Taştekin Ş et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) and total laparoscopic hysterectomy (TLH) differ in postoperative sexual health, patient-reported recovery measures, and perioperative outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Sexually active women treated with vNOTES or TLH for benign gynaecological indications between January 2023 and January 2026 were included in this ambispective cohort. Clinical and operative information was retrieved retrospectively, while patient-reported postoperative data were obtained prospectively a minimum of six months after surgery. Sexual function was measured with the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI). Additional outcomes included dyspareunia, time to resumption of sexual intercourse, return to work, postoperative satisfaction, and willingness to undergo the same procedure again. Selected outcomes were further examined using multivariable regression models incorporating clinically relevant confounding variables.
RESULTS: The analysis comprised 159 women, of whom 105 underwent TLH and 54 underwent vNOTES. Compared with TLH, vNOTES was associated with a shorter operative duration [160 (60) vs. 198 (90) minutes, p<0.01], earlier return to sexual intercourse [8 (3) vs. 9 (4) weeks, p<0.01], and higher postoperative satisfaction [10 (9-10) vs. 9 (8-10), p<0.01]. In adjusted analyses, the associations with shorter operative time [β=-27.24, 95% confidence interval (CI): -50.62 to -3.86; p=0.02] and earlier resumption of intercourse (β=-1.60 weeks, 95% CI: -2.93 to -0.27; p=0.01) persisted. No significant differences were identified in FSFI-based sexual function, dyspareunia, time to return to work, or composite adverse events.
CONCLUSION: vNOTES and TLH showed comparable postoperative sexual function and dyspareunia outcomes. vNOTES was associated with an earlier return to sexual intercourse, greater postoperative satisfaction, and shorter operative duration. Further prospective multicentre research is required to clarify longer-term sexual outcomes after these procedures.

articles.title: "A Minefield for the Novice": Australian Women's Experiences Seeking Health Information Online About Perimenopause.
articles.authors: Boer N, Jovanovski N, Saling L
articles.abstract: During perimenopause, many women experience psychological and physiological symptoms that can seriously impact quality of life and future health. However, they report challenges accessing appropriate information and medical support, likely exacerbated by clinician knowledge gaps, stigma, and a persistent lack of research, consistent with a documented pattern of structural sexism in health systems. Consequently, women increasingly turn to alternative sources, particularly online, for support. Although scholarship exists on online health-information seeking and women's digital health engagement, limited research examines how women navigate online health information under clinical and structural invalidation. This study gathered responses from 58 perimenopausal women through an online qualitative survey and constructed three themes using reflexive thematic analysis: (a) the search for validation; (b) trust erosion and the support gap; and (c) self-efficacy, agency and kinship. Interpreted through an epistemic injustice lens, the findings indicated that participants used digital literacy strategies to reassert epistemic standing and compensate for structural lack of support, yet were left to navigate variable-quality health information. Therefore, health information providers and policymakers should acknowledge perimenopausal complexity, model knowledge-appraisal strategies rather than present information as resolved, and mandate training to address the support gap. Health professionals should also validate women's epistemic standing before clinically interpreting symptoms.

articles.title: Dysregulation of the miR-29c-3p/collagen axis induces spermatogenic failure in heat stress and non-obstructive azoospermia.
articles.authors: Zhang SB, Zhou MK, Zhao YS et al.
articles.abstract: Rising global temperatures have intensified male infertility linked to testicular heat stress. While microRNAs play pivotal roles in spermatogenesis, the reason for aberrant microRNA expression following heat stress-induced spermatogenic disorders remains largely unclear. We established a murine heat stress model and performed small RNA sequencing. Candidate microRNAs were obtained via intersection with additional spermatogenic arrest and Sertoli cell-only syndrome datasets. The proliferation of germ cells was assessed by cholecystokinin-8 and 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine assays. Bioinformatic analysis was applied to predict downstream miRNA targets, and enrichment analysis was performed. Fluorescence in situ hybridization and immunofluorescence assays were utilized to determine the expression of miRNAs and their targets in Sertoli cell-only syndrome models and clinical testicular samples. In total, testicular heat stress resulted in 102 upregulated and 114 downregulated miRNAs. Four candidate microRNAs (miR-378a-3p, miR-29c-3p, let-7a-5p, and miR-9-5p) were screened for further investigation. Functional assays demonstrated that elevated expression of miR-378a-3p, miR-29c-3p, or silencing of miR-9-5p, notably inhibited the proliferation ability of spermatogonia (GC-1 cells). Common targets of these microRNAs were highly enriched in collagen-related pathways, predominantly through the inhibition of miR-29c-3p-targeted collagen type I alpha 1 and type III alpha 1 chain 1. Compared with normal tissue samples, tissue samples from Sertoli cell-only syndrome model mice and from those with spermatogenic disorders also exhibited high miR-29c-3p expression levels. In summary, our study identified microRNA expression patterns during testicular heat stress and preliminarily investigated the roles of specific microRNAs. miR-29c-3p and the collagen synthesis pathway could be utilized as biomarkers and therapeutic targets for heat-induced spermatogenic disorders.

articles.title: The Characteristics of Tumor Microenvironment by the Single Cell Profile in Endometrial Cancer of no Specific Molecular Profile (NSMP) Subtype.
articles.authors: Yuan X, Zhai Z, Jing C et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) of no specific molecular profile (NSMP) subtype lacks specific molecular features, and the relationship of tumor microenvironment (TME) and relapse in NSMP EC remains incompletely understood. This study integrates single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunohistochemistry to elucidate the TME and mechanisms of relapse in NSMP EC. The results showed reduced immune infiltration and increased immune-suppressive cells, including SPP1+ macrophages and regulatory T cells (Tregs) in NSMP EC. More epithelial cell clusters with high stemness scores are observed in primary NSMP EC tumors collected before recurrence. In NSMP EC, tip endothelial cells and MMP11+ LEF1+ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are linked with angiogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and CD4+ T cells remain in a stress-response state and are functionally impaired. Interestingly, a subset of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) characterized by SPP1 expression is discovered, which may remodel the tumor microenvironment by potentially promoting CD4+ T cells stress and maintaining epithelial cells stemness through SPP1-CD44, thereby potentially contributing to the proliferation and migration of tumor cells, which has verified by in vitro experiments. This study advances the mechanistic understanding of recurrence-related TME and provides a foundation for the development of personalized treatments for NSMP EC patients.

articles.title: Racial Disparities in Severe Maternal Morbidity: The Role of Maternal Comorbidities.
articles.authors: Milazzo A
articles.abstract: The U.S. maternal health crisis disproportionately affects Black women, who face nearly twice the risk of severe maternal morbidity (SMM) compared with White women. Using 2016-2022 Texas hospital discharge data and a validated obstetric comorbidity score, the analysis first documents that the prevalence of SMM increased by 18% between 2016 and 2022, whereas maternal comorbidity burden increased by 42% over the same period. To better assess the role of comorbidities, the comorbidity score is disaggregated into underlying health and pregnancy-specific conditions. Oaxaca-Blinder decompositions indicate that the former accounts for the largest share-49 to 53%-of the Black-White SMM gap, while the latter accounts for an additional third of the disparity. After accounting for these factors, a residual Black-White SMM gap of 17%-20% persists across and within hospitals, including among women treated by the same physician. Overall, the findings underscore the critical need to improve women's health well before childbirth hospitalization and throughout the reproductive life course, while also strengthening prenatal care to prevent and effectively manage conditions that arise during pregnancy.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitude, and contraceptive use among married women attending a maternity hospital in Kabul, Afghanistan: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Hussainzada MR, Muhammadi FA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family planning is a foundational component of reproductive health that empowers individuals to make informed decisions about childbearing. In Afghanistan, where maternal mortality remains critically high and contraceptive prevalence is low, understanding family planning dynamics is essential for improving reproductive outcomes. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and contraceptive use among married women attending a major maternity hospital in Kabul.
METHODS: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 356 married women attending Rabia Balkhi Maternity Hospital in Kabul, Afghanistan, from October 2024 to March 2025. Participants were selected using convenience sampling. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a structured, validated questionnaire. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were employed for analysis using SPSS version 26. Statistical significance was set at p <.05.
RESULTS: Out of 356 women, 86.2% had heard of family planning methods. Overall, 77.8% demonstrated good knowledge, and 22.2% demonstrated poor knowledge. Healthcare providers were the primary information source (75.0%), followed by family or friends (46.1%). Regarding attitudes, 84.3% held positive attitudes toward family planning, while 15.7% exhibited negative attitudes. The majority (86.5%) considered family planning important for family well-being. Ever-use of contraceptives was reported by 79.2%, with 72.5% currently using a method. Combined oral contraceptives (COCs) (21.5%) and depot medroxyprogesterone acetate intramuscular injectable (DMPA-IM) (21.4%) were the most commonly used methods. Key barriers to use included husband disapproval (9.6%), lack of knowledge (5.3%), and religious/cultural beliefs (4.8%). Side effects (17.1%) and desire for pregnancy (25.8%) were the primary reasons for discontinuation. Strong positive associations were observed between knowledge and attitude (p <.001), knowledge and practice (p <.001), and attitude and practice (p <.001). Multivariate logistic regression revealed that higher education (AOR = 3.42, 95% CI: 1.87-6.25, p <.001), husband's supportive attitude (AOR = 2.89, 95% CI: 1.65-5.06, p <.001), and higher household income (AOR = 2.31, 95% CI: 1.34-3.98, p =.002) were significant independent predictors of current contraceptive use.
CONCLUSION: Among married women attending this hospital, most demonstrated good knowledge (77.8%), positive attitudes (84.3%), and current contraceptive…

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of oral pharmacological and complementary interventions for premenstrual syndrome: a protocol for a systematic review and a network meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Degen B, Locher C, Koechlin H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) affects around 48% of women of reproductive age worldwide, interfering with psychological and physical well-being as well as functioning. A multitude of interventions exists for PMS, including oral pharmacological interventions, such as antidepressants, combined oral contraceptives, or alternative and complementary interventions. While the use of pharmacological interventions for PMS is linked to multiple side effects, evidence is limited for complementary interventions. Further, placebo effects are high in PMS intervention studies, affecting the estimation of the true treatment effect. An analysis of the relative efficacy between different treatment options is currently lacking, yet urgently needed for clinical decision-making.
METHODS: We plan a network meta-analysis to compare the relative efficacy and safety of oral pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions for PMS, including all available randomized controlled trials, such as comparator or placebo-controlled trials. Primary outcomes will be symptom intensity and interference; secondary outcomes will be psychological and somatic symptom intensity. Safety will be assessed by the proportion of patients reporting treatment-related adverse events, unwanted events, and by dropouts due to side effects. Published trials will be retrieved from online electronic databases. At least two independent reviewers will screen, select references, and extract data independently. Risk of Bias will be assessed using the Cochrane risk of bias assessment 2 (RoB2) tool. We will conduct a random-effect network meta-analysis within a frequentist framework for each outcome to synthesize all available evidence and compare and rank available oral treatments.
DISCUSSION: Several interventions are available for PMS, a disabling condition that affects a large proportion of women worldwide. To our knowledge, this will be the first network meta-analysis to synthesize the existing evidence of oral PMS interventions systematically. Comparing the efficacy and safety of all available interventions is necessary to inform clinicians, patients and clinical guidelines to elect the best treatment regimen.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42020214716.

articles.title: Systemic immune and coagulation amplifiers resolve diagnostic ambiguity in endometriosis-associated ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Luo L, Tu Y, Zhu Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative discrimination between endometriosis-associated ovarian cancer (EAOC) and benign ovarian endometrioma (OE) remains challenging because imaging findings overlap and CA125 is frequently elevated by benign pelvic inflammation. We hypothesized that EAOC is associated with a systemic immune-coagulation signature that could improve risk stratification beyond tumor markers alone.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed treatment-naive patients who underwent primary surgery for ovarian masses between January 2015 and February 2025. EAOC (n = 49) and OE (n = 146) were confirmed histopathologically according to the Sampson-Scott criteria. Preoperative laboratory indices obtained within 2 weeks before surgery included fibrinogen, albumin, absolute monocyte count (AMC), CA125, and HE4; the fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio (FAR) was calculated. A multivariable logistic regression model integrating age, menopausal status, AMC, FAR, CA125, and HE4 was developed as the CO-MHF nomogram. Supplementary data-driven analyses included least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression, Akaike information criterion (AIC)-based stepwise selection, and add-one/drop-one marginal contribution analysis. Discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), bootstrap-derived confidence interval (CI), the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: FAR and AMC were significantly higher in EAOC than in OE (median FAR 0.10 versus 0.07; median AMC 0.39 versus 0.31 × 109/L). The CO-MHF model showed favorable internal discrimination (AUC 0.932, 95% CI 0.887-0.968), outperforming HE4 (0.835), FAR (0.786), CA125 (0.769), and AMC (0.657). At the Youden-derived threshold (0.468), sensitivity was 75.5% and specificity 95.9%, with a positive predictive value (PPV) of 86.0% and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 92.1%. Lower thresholds increased sensitivity to 85.7%-93.9% at the cost of reduced specificity. Supplementary data-driven analyses supported the predictor set: AIC-based stepwise selection identified the same variables, and LASSO retained all CO-MHF predictors. Calibration was acceptable (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.225), and DCA showed greater net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities.
CONCLUSIONS: A mechanism-informed nomogram combining FAR and AMC with established tumor markers may improve preoperative risk stratification for EAOC. This…

articles.title: Nutritional status of school-going adolescent girls is associated with their cognitive function but not academic performance: insights from Ten2Twenty-Ghana baseline study.
articles.authors: Saeed N, Ayimbire MA, Hammond AY et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The link between nutritional status and cognitive performance is well-documented in early childhood, but limited data exist on adolescents, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. This study examines the associations between nutritional status, overall cognitive function and its subdomains, and academic performance among adolescent girls in Ghana.
METHODS: Cross-sectional data from the Ten2Twenty-Ghana study were analysed, including 845 girls aged 10-17 from 19 primary schools in the Mion District. Fluid cognition, a composite measure of cognitive function, was assessed using the National Institutes of Health Toolbox Cognition Battery. The cognition battery comprised five subdomains: executive function, attention control, processing speed, working memory, and episodic memory. Academic performance was assessed using examination scores in Mathematics, English, and General Science. Anthropometry was used to calculate the body mass index-for-age z-score (BAZ) and the height-for-age z-score (HAZ) using WHO AnthroPlus. Generalised linear mixed-effects models with a random intercept for school, assessed associations while adjusting for potential confounding variables, including age, anaemia, dietary diversity, menarche status, health complaints, school attendance, household food security, wealth, dependency, and literacy ratios, school feeding status, and interviewer effect.
RESULTS: The mean HAZ was -0.9 ± 1.2, BAZ was -0.7 ± 0.9, fluid cognition was 26.7 ± 9.6, and academic performance was 53.8 ± 13.1%. BAZ was positively associated with the fluid cognition composite score (adjusted β = 1.12, 95% CI: 0.39, 1.83) and with processing speed subdomain (adjusted β = 1.31, 95% CI: 0.49, 2.13). HAZ was positively associated with processing speed after full adjustment (adjusted β = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.06, 1.29). No significant associations were found between anthropometric indices and academic performance.
CONCLUSION: Nutritional status was positively associated with the fluid cognition composite score and processing speed subdomain among adolescent girls, while no association was observed with academic performance. These findings underscore the importance of improving adolescent nutrition to support cognitive development in rural settings.

articles.title: Association of serum uric acid during pre-pregnancy with adverse pregnancy outcomes among women conceived by in-vitro fertilization: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Lan K, Yin S, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal serum uric acid (UA) levels have been linked to adverse pregnancy outcomes, but no studies have yet examined this association in women undergoing assisted reproductive technology. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between pre-pregnancy UA levels and adverse pregnancy outcomes in women conceived via in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 2 111 singleton pregnancies conceived via IVF-ET, delivered at Peking University Third Hospital between 1 January 2017 and 30 April 2022. Restricted cubic splines were used to test nonlinear relationships between serum UA during pre-pregnancy and adverse outcomes, and multivariable logistic regression to calculate odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (CI).
RESULTS: Of the 2 111 women, no significant associations were found between pre-pregnancy UA levels and preeclampsia, preterm birth, or macrosomia. However, a J-shaped relationship was observed for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and low birth weight (LBW), and an inverse U-shaped relationship for gestational hypertension (GH). Reflecting these distinct non-linear topologies, statistically significant peak risks were observed and reported at different strata: women in the higher quintile (4th quintile) of UA had a 3.20-fold increased risk of GH (adjusted OR 3.20, 95% CI 1.23, 8.33) and a 1.38-fold increased risk of GDM (adjusted OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.01, 1.88) compared with the lowest quintile. Conversely, the risk of LBW accelerated sharply and peaked at the highest quintile (5th quintile) (adjusted OR 1.98, 95% CI 1.11, 3.54). In the subgroup analysis, the positive association between pre-pregnancy UA and LBW was more pronounced among patients with day 5 embryo transfer.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that optimizing serum UA levels in women planning pregnancy, particularly those undergoing IVF-ET, may have important clinical implications for improving pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Trends in the uptake of nipple sparing mastectomy in BRCA1/2, PALB2 and other pathogenic variant carriers undergoing risk reducing mastectomy.
articles.authors: Alsuhaibani M, Melanson A, Viezel-Mathieu A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Risk-reducing mastectomy (RRM) for germline pathogenic variant (GPVs) carriers were historically performed as total mastectomy (TM) or skin-sparing mastectomy (SSM), although nipple-sparing mastectomy (NSM) has recently emerged as an oncologically safe RRM option.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included all female patients with confirmed BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, or other high-penetrance GPVs at two academic institutions in Canada between 2003 and 2024. Temporal trends in NSM uptake were assessed using the Mantel-Haenszel test for trend and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: After exclusions, 559 GPV carriers including 319 (57%) affected carriers and 240 (43%) unaffected carriers comprised the study cohort. The median age at RRM was 45 years old (range 22-76) and most were BRCA1 carriers (46.7%) or BRCA2 carriers (44.4%). Overall, 310 carriers (55.5%) underwent NSM, 174 (31.1%) underwent SSM, and 75 (13.4%) underwent TM. NSM uptake was highest among patients aged 40-49 years (56%) and lowest in those ≥ 60 years (42%, p = 0.03). Relative to unaffected carriers, affected carriers (47% vs. 66%, p < 0.001) and those with prior radiation were less likely to undergo NSM (34.3% vs. 62.7%, p < 0.001). A clear increase in NSM occurred over time, from 11.9% pre-2012 to 74.4% after 2022 (p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis adjusting for age, GPV, parity, menopausal status, and personal history of breast cancer identified normal BMI (OR 1.99, 95% CI 1.18-3.34), lack of radiation exposure (OR 3.03, 95% CI 1.76-5.23), and year of surgery as independent predictors of NSM receipt (OR 1.25, 95% CI 1.19-1.32).
CONCLUSION: There has been a significant increase in NSM use among BRCA1/2, PALB2 and other GPV carriers over the last two decades.

articles.title: Health systems interventions for prevention of maternal peripartum infection in low and middle-income countries: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Abwao R, Mapesa J, Tenambergen W et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Globally, there is growing recognition that a functional health system is key to improving maternal health and reducing maternal mortality. Maternal peripartum infection remains a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. This infection is a multifaceted problem with many players. Adopting a health systems approach could help avert this preventable infection by addressing the gaps across all the components of care.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this systematic review was to identify and evaluate interventions to prevent maternal peripartum infection in LMICs.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in Cochrane Library, CINAHL, MEDLINE (via PubMed) and Scopus, World Health Organization (WHO), and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) websites to identify primary articles reporting on interventions for preventing maternal peripartum infection using the PRISMA model. The article search was conducted for a period of 3 months (01/08/2022 to 30/10/2022). Search terms were "Peripartum", "Infection", "Genital tract", and their MESH terms. The inclusion criteria were primary interventional studies that reported interventions for the prevention of maternal peripartum infection, studies from LMICs, and those written in the English language. Cochrane Risk of Bias tools were used to appraise the quality of the studies.
RESULTS: Out of 1662 articles, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria comprising of 55,982 participants. The interventions were grouped into five domains: antibiotic prophylaxis 10(42%) of studies), self-care training 6 (25%), skin preparation 5 (21%), Traditional Birth Attendant training 2(2%) and use of Clean Delivery Kit 1(1%)0.11 studies reported a significantly lower risk of infection. Four studies reported a significantly improved knowledge and practice of women regarding maternal peripartum infection. While six studies reported no change in the risk of infection with the intervention.
CONCLUSION: A range of interventions targeting maternal peripartum infection prevention in LMICs were identified in this review. They were all targeting a single intervention without integrating other system components. The review highlights the need for integrated health systems interventions and further research to generate stronger evidence and inform effective implementation.
STUDY REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42022342550.

articles.title: Postpartum contraception receipt among Oregon Medicaid-funded births with stimulant and substance use disorder.
articles.authors: Lindner SR, Kaufman M, Martinez Acevedo A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare postpartum contraceptive receipt among (i) Medicaid beneficiaries with stimulant-related substance use disorder (SUD) to those without SUD; and (ii) Medicaid beneficiaries with other SUD to those without SUD.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of birthing events using Oregon's linked Medicaid claims and vital statistics data 2012-2019 (N = 141,479). We described demographic characteristics, birth outcomes, and substances used, and compared rates of contraception receipt (i) immediately postpartum (IPP), (ii) within 60 days postpartum excluding IPP, and (iii) within 60 days postpartum including IPP.
RESULTS: Prevalence of stimulant-related and other SUD diagnosis was 3.8% and 9.4%, respectively. After adjusting for demographic and clinical factors, contraception receipt within 60 days postpartum including IPP and contraception receipt IPP were greater for birth events with a stimulant-related SUD compared to birth events without SUD (adjusted relative risk [aRR], 60-days postpartum including IPP: 1.12, 95% CI: 1.07-1.17; aRR, IPP: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.24-1.40). Adjusted rates of contraception receipt were also elevated for birth events with other SUD compared to birth events with no SUD (aRR, 60-days postpartum including IPP: 1.12, 95% CI: 1.09-1.15; aRR, IPP: 1.21, 95% CI: 1.16-1.26; aRR, 60-days postpartum excluding IPP: 1.09, 95% CI: 1.06-1.13).
CONCLUSIONS: Birthing people enrolled in Medicaid who misused stimulants were more likely than those without SUD, controlling for relevant factors, to receive postpartum contraception within 60 days due to elevated contraception receipt during the IPP period. Further research may examine whether these findings can be replicated outside of Oregon.

articles.title: Acceptability and uptake of COVID-19 vaccines among pregnant and lactating women seeking services at a tertiary public hospital in Kampala, Uganda.
articles.authors: Katana EB, Odongpiny EAL, Simbwa BN et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Globally, several vaccines, including COVID-19 vaccines, have been routinely recommended during pregnancy and lactation. However, data on COVID-19 vaccine acceptability and uptake among pregnant and lactating women are limited in Sub-Saharan Africa. While COVID-19 is no longer a public health emergency it is important to take stock of lessons learnt to prepare for future health threats including those that disproportionately affect pregnant/lactating women. We aimed to assess acceptability and uptake of COVID-19 vaccines among pregnant and lactating women in Uganda.
METHODS: This was a cross-sectional study conducted among 424 pregnant and lactating women, who were seeking maternal and child health care at Kawempe National Referral Hospital in Kampala conducted between May and July 2023. We obtained data on vaccine acceptability defined as willingness to accept vaccines using interviewer-administered questionnaires. In addition, we assessed vaccination status. Factors associated with COVID-19 vaccine acceptability and uptake were evaluated using modified Poisson regression.
RESULTS: The mean age of the respondents was 26.9 years (SD = 5.7), ranging from 14 to 45 years. Among 424 respondents, 51.6% had received at least one dose of COVID-19 vaccine, 94.1% had received tetanus toxoid vaccine, and 48.4% regardless of their vaccination status, were willing to receive COVID-19 vaccines. Only 5/212(2.4%) had received COVID-19 vaccines while lactating with none having been received during pregnancy. Factors associated with COVID-19 vaccine uptake included history of testing for COVID-19 (aPR = 1.92, CI:1.46-2.54) and having a vaccinated household member (aPR = 1.34, CI:1.03-1.84). COVID-19 vaccine willingness was significantly associated with being a household head (aPR = 2.2, CI:1.12-4.27) and having a vaccinated household member (aPR = 1.33, CI:1.04-1.76).
CONCLUSION: COVID-19 vaccine acceptance among pregnant and lactating women remains suboptimal despite high acceptance of other maternal vaccines. These findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve the acceptance and uptake of COVID-19 vaccines, during pregnancy and lactation. Strengthening risk communication, addressing safety concerns, and leveraging trusted sources of information may enhance vaccine confidence and improve uptake during pregnancy and lactation.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of non-hormonal pharmacotherapies for depressive and anxiety symptoms during the menopausal transition and postmenopause: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Hedayati Ch M, Bostani Khalesi Z, Abedinzade M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-hormonal pharmacotherapies are widely used to manage depressive and anxiety symptoms in peri- and postmenopausal women, but comparative evidence across drug classes remains heterogeneous.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of non-hormonal pharmacological interventions for depressive and anxiety symptoms during the menopausal transition and postmenopause.
METHODS: A systematic review of six databases and trial registries identified randomized and non-randomized studies evaluating SSRIs, SNRIs, gabapentinoids, and other pharmacotherapies. Due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, a structured Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) approach was applied.
RESULTS: A total of Thirty-one studies (n = 8,124 participants) were included. SNRIs showed more frequent positive effects on depressive symptoms compared with other pharmacological classes, while SSRIs demonstrated modest and variable effects. Gabapentinoids consistently improved vasomotor symptoms but showed limited and low-certainty effects on mood outcomes. Evidence for anxiety outcomes was inconsistent across all drug classes. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate.
CONCLUSIONS: Non-hormonal pharmacotherapies may provide benefit for mood symptoms during the menopausal transition and postmenopause, particularly SNRIs; however, conclusions are limited by heterogeneity, indirectness, and lack of head-to-head comparative trials.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Prenatal statin exposure and adverse birth outcomes in Asian women: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Ye S, Wu F, Sun D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The safety of statin use during pregnancy remains controversial. We aimed to evaluate the association between prenatal statin exposure and pregnancy outcomes in Asian women, including low birth weight, preterm birth, and congenital anomalies.
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of studies in Asian populations evaluating prenatal statin exposure. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and trial registries were searched through January 31, 2026. Eligible randomized and observational studies included Asian populations and reported low birth weight, preterm birth, or congenital anomalies. Adjusted risk ratios were pooled using random-effects inverse-variance models, and risk of bias was assessed with standard tools.
RESULTS: Three nationwide observational cohort studies from Taiwan and South Korea were included in the quantitative synthesis, and one Indonesian randomized trial of pravastatin for preeclampsia prevention was reviewed qualitatively. Prenatal statin exposure was not associated with congenital anomalies (RR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.89-1.08; I2 = 0%), but was associated with low birth weight (RR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49; I2 = 49%). The association with preterm birth was not statistically significant (RR, 1.24; 95% CI, 0.95-1.62; I2 = 87%). Sensitivity analyses restricted to exposed versus unexposed comparisons yielded similar conclusions.
CONCLUSIONS: The available Asian evidence, largely derived from nationwide East Asian cohorts, suggests no clear association between prenatal statin exposure or continuation and congenital anomalies. A modest association with low birth weight was observed, whereas evidence for preterm birth remained inconclusive. The low-birth-weight finding should be interpreted cautiously because of residual confounding, comparator heterogeneity, prematurity-related low birth weight, and pharmacological heterogeneity across statins.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251235975.

articles.title: Derivation of a risk model to predict urinary incontinence during pregnancy: a research article.
articles.authors: Carrera-Boix A, Cassadó Garriga J, Blanch J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The onset of urinary incontinence (UI) during pregnancy is related to urinary incontinence persistence in the postpartum and later years. We aimed to design a prediction model of urinary incontinence that could be used at the beginning of pregnancy and included clinical and ultrasound variables.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Design: Prospective cohort study.
SETTINGS: Obstetrics and Gynecology Service of Santa Caterina's Hospital (Girona, Spain) between 2018 and 2020.
POPULATION: Women at 12-14 weeks' gestation were invited to participate by consecutive sampling and a follow-up visit was carried out at 32-35 pregnancy weeks.
METHODS: During the visits, we collected clinical data, measured 2D ultrasound variables, and administered the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ-SF). We built a multivariable model to predict urinary incontinence, assessed its calibration and discrimination (with the area under the ROC curve), and performed an internal validation. All the analyses were carried out using the R software (version 4.1).
RESULTS: We recruited 174 nulliparous pregnant women during the study period and designed two models to predict urinary incontinence based on the significant variables in the univariate analysis: the urethral mobility and body mass index (BMI). The OR (95% CI) for the BMI category > 30 kg/m2 was 4.24 (1.48-12.30) in the first model (introital urethral mobility and BMI) and 3.31 (1.13-9.62) in the second model (transperineal urethral mobility and BMI). The area under the ROC curve was 0.725 for the first model and 0.687 for the second model. These models were used to create an online urinary incontinence prediction calculator.
CONCLUSION: We built two multivariable models to predict, at the beginning of pregnancy, the individual risk of each pregnant woman to develop moderate/severe urinary incontinence in the third trimester. These models may provide a foundation for the future development of tailored primary prevention strategies.

articles.title: Adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes and associated factors among malaria infected parturient at Wallaga University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Western Ethiopia.
articles.authors: Alemu D, Tilahun T, Tiruneh G
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malaria during pregnancy remains a major public health challenge, significantly contributing to poor fetal and neonatal outcomes. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and associated factors of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes among malaria-infected parturient at Wallaga University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Western Ethiopia.
METHODS: An institution-based retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using medical records of 271 malaria-infected parturient from March 10, 2024, to March 9, 2025. Data were extracted using a standardized checklist, entered into Microsoft Excel, and analyzed using SPSS version 27. Multivariable logistic regression was employed to identify independent predictors, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: The prevalence of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes was 37.27% (95% CI: 32.0%-42.9%), with low birth weight being the most common complication. Independent predictors included residing in rural area (AOR = 4.97; 95% Cl, 1.92-12.90), being primigravida (AOR = 5.41; 95% Cl, 1.95-15.05), having moderate anemia (AOR = 3.25; 95% Cl, 1.46-7.25), having severe anemia (AOR = 4.89; 95% Cl, 1.95-12.29) and having four or fewer antenatal care contacts (AOR = 5.70; 95% Cl, 2.56-12.72).
CONCLUSION: Nearly four in ten study participants experienced adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes. The risk is highest for participants from rural areas, experiencing their first pregnancy, struggling with moderate to severe anemia, or failing to complete at least five antenatal care contacts. Therefore, targeted interventions should prioritize anemia prevention and management, specialized monitoring for primigravidas, and rural outreach to ensure women complete at least five antenatal care contacts.

articles.title: Urinary incontinence among older adults in Saudi Arabia: prevalence, severity, and associated factors.
articles.authors: Alharbi A, AlRamadan S, Alhejazi F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urinary incontinence (UI) is a common yet under-recognized condition among older adults, particularly in outpatient settings, where symptoms are often underreported. Despite its significant impact on quality of life, data on the prevalence and clinical factors associated with UI in Saudi Arabian outpatient populations remain limited.
METHOD: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 290 adults aged > = 60 years attending NGHA outpatient clinics in Riyadh and Dammam, Saudi Arabia. Participants were recruited consecutively during the study period. Urinary incontinence was assessed using the validated Arabic version of the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire - Short Form (ICIQ-SF), and multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors independently associated with urinary incontinence.
RESULT: Urinary incontinence was reported in 40.3% of participants and was more common among women than men. In multivariable analysis, a history of urinary tract infection was strongly associated with urinary incontinence (AOR 3.73; 95% CI 2.19-6.35; p < 0.001), while benign prostatic hyperplasia was independently associated with urinary incontinence among men (AOR 2.81; 95% CI 1.05-7.49; p = 0.039). Other demographic and clinical variables were not independently associated with urinary incontinence.
CONCLUSION: Urinary incontinence is common among older adults attending outpatient clinics, with urinary tract infection and benign prostatic hyperplasia identified as key associated factors.

articles.title: Relationship between hyperuricemia and cardiovascular risk among postmenopausal women in cameroon: a community-based study.
articles.authors: Mbouna SFM, Nkeck JR, Atabe NN et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite the known association between hyperuricemia and an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, the prevalence and epidemiology of hyperuricemia in postmenopausal women in Cameroon are not yet fully understood. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of hyperuricemia, identify its associated factors, and examine its association with cardiovascular risk markers among postmenopausal women living in Yaoundé.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Yaoundé from November 2024 to June 2025, involving 206 postmenopausal women. Biological measurements were performed at PRIMA Lab using the Cobas 6000®. Independent associated factors with hyperuricemia were analyzed using logistic regression. Association between hyperuricemia and cardiovascular risk markers was assessed, using chi2. The significance level was set at 5%. SPSS 28 was used for statistical analysis.
RESULTS: Out of 206 postmenopausal women, the mean age was 63.5 ± 8.7 [48-87] years. The prevalence of hyperuricemia was 37.9%. Menopausal duration ≥ 14 years (OR = 2.8; P = 0.016), overweight/obesity (OR = 1.9; P = 0.030) and hypertension (OR = 2.0; P = 0.036). Hyperuricemia was significantly associated with non-HDL cholesterol ≥ 130 mg/dL (P = 0.001), LDL/HDL ratio (P = 0.001), WHO CVR score ≥ 10% (P = 0.018), and non-HDL/total cholesterol ratio (P = 0.045).
CONCLUSION: More than one-third of postmenopausal women have been diagnosed with hyperuricemia. Long duration of menopause, overweight/obesity and hypertension were independently associated with hyperuricemia. Hyperuricemia was significantly associate with non-HDL cholesterol, LDL/HDL ratio, non-HDL/total cholesterol ratio and WHO CVR score.

articles.title: Self-Harm Ideation in Perinatal Mothers in Home Visiting Programs.
articles.authors: Ammerman RT, Folger AT, Messer EP et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine the prevalence and predictors of self-harm ideation during the perinatal period among mothers (N = 9638) enrolled in a home visiting program.
METHODS: Subjects were all mothers enrolled in a home visiting program in the United States between 2006 and 2023 who completed the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS; Cox et al., 1987) prenatally and/or at up to 6 months postpartum. Item 10 of the EPDS, reflecting thoughts of self-harm, was used to operationalize self-harm ideation and severity. Demographic and clinical variables were examined as predictors of self-harm ideation and change over the two time points.
RESULTS: 6.8% of the sample reported self-harm ideation prenatally, with 33.8% of these mothers endorsing the two highest levels of severity. 4.0% of the sample reported self-harm ideation postnatally. Of those who reported self-harm ideation prenatally, 77.9% no longer reported it postnatally. Reporting of self-harm ideation was associated with mean EPDS scores above the established clinical cutoff (≥ 13). Younger mothers reported higher levels of ideation compared with older mothers.
CONCLUSIONS FOR PRACTICE: A large proportion of mothers reported self-harm ideation prenatally, and younger mothers reported higher levels of ideation compared with older mothers. Given the dangers of unrecognized and untreated suicide risk in perinatal mothers, home visitors are in a unique and important position to support and link mothers to mental health services.

articles.title: A breast clinical scoring system to identify women with Idiopathic granulomatous Mastitis.
articles.authors: Mehra S, Hong J, Yeh C et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Idiopathic granulomatous mastitis (IGM) is a benign inflammatory breast condition that can resemble mastitis or malignancy clinically and radiographically. We aimed to develop a quantitative scoring system, based off the Komen Inflammatory Breast Cancer (IBC) scoring system [1], evaluating clinical and radiologic features to distinguish IGM from benign and malignant breast conditions.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective chart review of biopsy-proven IGM patients diagnosed from 2014 to 2025 via institutional electronic medical records. Clinical symptom onset, features, and diagnostic imaging were analyzed. A continuous scoring scale (1-50) was created, encompassing three categories: symptom onset, clinical features, and radiographic findings. Scores of IGM patients were compared with those of patients diagnosed with IBC, mastitis (lactational and non-lactational), and locally advanced breast cancer (LABC). Welch's two-sample t-test assessed statistical differences, and Youden index identified the optimal score threshold for predicting IGM.
RESULTS: Among 148 IGM patients, predominantly Hispanic (56.8%) and Asian (26.7%), the mean age was 37.2 years, older than mastitis patients and younger than IBC patients. Key clinical features included pain or painful breast mass (100%), fistula or draining wound (77.7%), erythema (94.6%), and phlegmon (87.8%). Imaging revealed mass with collection in 84.6% and multiple masses/collections in 38.9%. The mean IGM score (35.5) was significantly higher than scores for IBC, mastitis, and LABC groups (14.4, 18, and 15.2, respectively; p ≤ 0.05). A score ≥ 24.5 predicted IGM with 93% sensitivity and 95% specificity.
CONCLUSIONS: This novel scoring system provides an objective framework to differentiate IGM from similar breast conditions, facilitating early diagnosis and guiding appropriate management.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: not applicable.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary approach and rehabilitation practice for defecatory disorders in Italy: a snapshot survey on behalf of the Italian Society of Colorectal Surgery (SICCR).
articles.authors: Zigiotto D, La Greca G, Elio A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Defecatory disorders and pelvic floor dysfunctions are prevalent and significantly impact quality of life. Due to their multifactorial etiology, a multidisciplinary approach and pelvic floor rehabilitation (PFR) are recommended; however, their implementation varies widely. This study aimed to evaluate current practices in multidisciplinary management and rehabilitation strategies for defecatory disorders in Italy.
METHODS: A 25-item, web-based survey was distributed to members of the Italian Society of Colorectal Surgery between May and July 2024. The questionnaire explored the professional background of the responders, the availability and composition of the multidisciplinary team (MDT), and the use of PFR and related clinical practices.
RESULTS: A total of 183 colorectal surgeons from 20 Italian regions completed the survey. Only 49% reported the presence of a structured MDT, with frequent absence of a urologist, gastroenterologist, and radiologist. Combined pelvic floor surgery was rarely performed, despite its clinical advantages. PFR services were available in just over half of the centers, often without psychological or nutritional support. Rehabilitative techniques varied, with volumetric rehabilitation and tibial nerve stimulation being underutilized. Referral rates to rehabilitation remained low, regardless of institution type or surgical experience. Despite the lack of standardized protocols, a quarter of responders utilized perioperative rehabilitation in the context of rectal prolapse surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Significant variability exists in the multidisciplinary and rehabilitative management of defecatory disorders in Italy. To optimize care, greater integration of MDT, wider access to a standardized PFR, and the adoption of combined surgical approaches are needed.

articles.title: Single-oocyte proteome-transcriptome co-profiling reveals a role of dysregulated lactate metabolism in oocyte aging.
articles.authors: Cao L, Wu H, Jiang Y et al.
articles.abstract: The age-related decline in oocyte quality is a major risk factor for female infertility. Although transcriptome has been examined in aged oocytes, proteomic landscape, which reflects primary gene functional executors, remains largely unexplored. This gap limits our understanding of oocyte aging. To address this, we perform single-cell proteome/transcriptome co-profiling of GV/MII-aged oocytes from mice and humans, revealing species- and stage-specific proteomic/transcriptomic changes during oocyte aging. Strikingly, we observe uncoupled proteomic and transcriptomic alterations, indicating that proteomic changes in aged oocytes are not primarily driven by RNA levels. Furthermore, we capture molecular heterogeneity in aged oocytes and identify MCT4 as a candidate marker of oocyte aging. Functional studies suggest MCT4 contributes to aging-associated oocyte defects via lactate export, and its inhibition improves aged-oocyte quality. These findings indicate altered lactate metabolism as a candidate marker and intervention target for oocyte aging and underscore the value of our profiling in dissecting oocyte aging.

articles.title: Using Artificial Intelligence in Qualitative Lupus Pregnancy Research: The Potential of Large Language Models and Prompting Strategies.
articles.authors: Boers JRM, Terry G, Rodrigues L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to evaluate the ability of different large language models (LLMs) to translate and analyze qualitative interviews describing pregnancy experiences among women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). An additional objective was to compare themes identified by LLMs with those identified by human researchers.
METHODS: We analyzed 26 semistructured interviews originally conducted in Portuguese by Rodrigues et al among women with SLE exploring their perinatal care experiences. Three prompting strategies (zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought) were used on the transcripts across four state-of-the-art LLMs (GPT-4o, OpenAI; Claude Sonnet 4.5, Anthropic; Gemini 2.5 Flash, Google; and DeepSeek R, DeepSeek) to generate key themes. Model outputs were evaluated using an LLM-as-a-judge framework assessing thematic coverage, thematic unity, and semantic similarity.
RESULTS: Across models and prompting strategies, LLMs generated similar themes that closely aligned with those identified by human researchers. LLM-as-a-judge evaluations demonstrated high thematic unity and semantic similarity. Claude Sonnet 4.5 showed the most consistent performance. Few-shot prompting consistently outperformed zero-shot and chain-of-thought approaches.
CONCLUSION: LLMs show promise as supportive tools for analyzing qualitative research by preserving thematic coherence and capturing the complexity of pregnancy experiences in women with SLE. Although zero-shot prompting is widely used, it produced lower thematic results in our study, whereas few-shot prompting achieved the most comprehensive and coherent theme extraction. LLM-assisted qualitative analysis may complement human interpretation and has the potential to support the inclusion of non-English language data and diverse patient perspectives in lupus research.

articles.title: Associations between dietary scores and metabolic health in later reproductive years: results from the ROLO longitudinal study.
articles.journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
articles.authors: Akinsooto OE, Callanan S, Douglass A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in women globally. Healthy dietary patterns are associated with favourable metabolic health profiles in women; however, most studies focus on the reproductive years or post menopause. This research aimed to explore associations between dietary scores and cardiometabolic health in women in later reproductive years.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This is a cross-sectional analysis of 372 women from the ROLO (Randomised cOntrol trial of a LOw glycaemic index diet in pregnancy to prevent macrosomia) longitudinal study with mean age of 42.7 (range 31.6-52.4 years), 10 years postpartum. Food frequency questionnaires were used to calculate Energy-Adjusted Dietary Inflammatory Index (E-DII) and Healthy Eating Index-2015 (HEI-2015) scores. Anthropometry, body composition and non-fasting blood samples were obtained. Metabolic outcomes were examined across E-DII and HEI-2015 score tertiles. Linear regression models examined associations between dietary scores and metabolic outcomes to adjust for confounders. The median (IQR) HEI-2015 score was 62.8 (60.0,66.7) and the median (IQR) E-DII score was -0.77 (-1.5,0.12). In crude and adjusted models, highest E-DII scores (more pro-inflammatory diet) were associated with lower 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels (nmol/L) (Tertile 3: B = -10.2, 95% CI -19.5, -0.94; p = 0.031), compared to the lowest E-DII scores (more anti-inflammatory diet). No significant associations between HEI-2015 score and metabolic outcomes were found.
CONCLUSIONS: The inflammatory potential of the diet may be associated with cardiometabolic health in women in later reproductive years, highlighting an avenue for further investigation to reduce cardiovascular risk in midlife.

articles.title: Sexual and reproductive health service receipt among sexually active adolescent and young adult men by race and ethnicity and disability status.
articles.authors: Zionskowski K, Hoyle J, Stevens JD et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Little is known about receipt of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services among adolescent and young adult men with disabilities or by race and ethnicity.
OBJECTIVE: To examine differences in SRH service receipt by disability status, race, and ethnicity.
METHODS: We analyzed 2011-2019 National Survey of Family Growth data for sexually active men aged 15-25 (n = 4802). Groups reflected disability status and race and ethnicity, with non-Hispanic White men without disabilities as the reference. Modified Poisson regression was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Men with disabilities had similar or higher receipt of the SRH services examined. Compared with non-Hispanic White men without disabilities, non-Hispanic White men with disabilities had higher prevalence of STI testing (aPR, 1.80; 95% CI, 1.42-2.28) and being asked about type of sex (aPR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.34-1.88). Hispanic men with disabilities had higher prevalence of being asked about type of sex (aPR, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.65-2.68) and receiving family planning services (aPR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.30-2.01). Non-Hispanic Black men with disabilities had the highest service receipt, including STI testing (aPR, 2.56; 95% CI, 2.39-2.74) and being asked about condom use (aPR, 2.11; 95% CI, 1.65-2.70).
CONCLUSIONS: Contrary to expectations, men with disabilities across racial and ethnic groups had higher SRH service receipt than non-Hispanic White men without disabilities. However, receipt remained low, with fewer than one-third receiving many recommended services, indicating missed opportunities to provide SRH care.

articles.title: Fertility evaluation of infertile women: a committee opinion.
articles.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
articles.abstract: Diagnostic evaluation for infertility in women should be conducted in a systematic, expeditious, and cost-effective manner to identify all the relevant factors with an initial emphasis on the least invasive methods for detecting the most common causes of infertility. The purpose of this committee opinion is to provide a critical review of the current methods and procedures for the evaluation of infertile women, and it replaces the document of the same name, last published in 2021 (Fertil Steril 2021;116:1255-65).

articles.title: AI-Powered CURA Application for Identifying At-Risk Pregnancies in Obstetrics Management (CURAte): protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Li S, Por CWS, Ramlal H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early identification of high-risk pregnancies is a cornerstone of obstetric care, yet antenatal risk assessment in routine practice remains imprecise and highly variable. Evidence from contemporary cohort studies suggests that only a minority of pregnancies that subsequently experience adverse maternal or fetal/neonatal outcomes are identified as high risk in the first trimester, with reported detection rates in the range of 20%–30%. Despite rapid advances in machine-learning (ML) methods for clinical risk prediction, no ML-based approach for general early antenatal risk categorisation has yet been evaluated against standard care within a randomised controlled trial (RCT) to assess impact on maternity outcomes. We hypothesise that adoption of an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted antenatal risk stratification approach will improve the accuracy of categorising pregnancies into high-risk and low-risk groups and will reduce the composite incidence of adverse maternal and fetal/neonatal outcomes.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: We will conduct an RCT comparing outcomes between participants allocated to an intervention arm employing AI-assisted risk stratification and those in the control arm receiving standard antenatal care without AI support. 1700 participants will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio using block randomisation, stratified by ethnicity and parity. Participants will be blinded to allocation. AI-assisted risk assessment using maternal sociodemographic, clinical and obstetrical data, will be applied at two time points: (1) a first trimester antenatal visit and (2) between 31 and 33 weeks’ gestation. AI categorisation outputs (intervention: ‘high-risk’ or ‘low-risk’; control: ‘undisclosed’) will be displayed to attending clinicians at both time points, and subsequent management will follow a predefined clinical protocol, one written for pregnancies categorised as high-risk and one for low-risk. For any pregnancy categorised as high-risk, the clinician works through predefined referral criteria for the maternal-fetal medicine-led high-risk clinic and completes the specified actionable investigations and interventions before referral. Participants are followed until 6 weeks after the end of pregnancy. The primary composite outcome is extracted from medical records 6 weeks after the end of pregnancy. The two arms are compared on an intention-to-treat basis once the database has been locked. There is no interim analysis of the primary outcome.

articles.title: Multiregional characterisation of collaboration between clinical and community-based organisations for postpartum transition care delivery: A mixed methods study protocol.
articles.authors: Smith B, MacEwan SR, Winters C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The USA exhibits the highest rate of maternal mortality among developed high-income countries. These deaths most commonly occur during the postpartum year and are largely preventable. Individuals that live in medically underserved areas and lack access to transitional care following childbirth are at higher risk for maternal mortality, severe maternal morbidity and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
