National US organisations have proposed implementation of innovative models, including coordinated postpartum service delivery across clinical and community-based organisations (CBOs), to help overcome key challenges contributing to postpartum health disparities. Yet, experiences of clinical and community organisations in forging postpartum service partnerships remain poorly defined. This study aims to characterise how clinical organisations and CBOs identify effective practices in postpartum transition care that best address disparities in pregnancy-related morbidity and mortality among individuals residing in maternity care deserts and low-resource communities.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This study uses a convergent mixed methods research design. Semi-structured qualitative interviews will be conducted with CBO representatives to assess current practices and implementation strategies of postpartum transition care within community organisations. Additionally, a needs assessment survey will be administered to clinicians from safety-net health systems and staff members from CBOs to evaluate perceptions, practices and needs associated with integrated clinical and community-based postpartum service delivery. Data analysis will be conducted through qualitative thematic analysis and quantitative descriptive statistics and regression analyses.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study was approved by The Ohio State University’s Institutional Review Board (Protocol #2024H0450). We will disseminate our study findings through academic products including peer-reviewed manuscripts and professional conference presentations as well as through community-centred lay-language summaries shared with our participating organisations, Stakeholder Advisory Committee and research consortium partners.

articles.title: Stakeholders' perspectives on communication gaps in cervical cancer prevention among women of Turkish, Moroccan and Syrian origin: a focus group study in the Netherlands.
articles.authors: Veeravagu T, Hamdiui N, Stein ML et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To gather stakeholders’ perspectives on the gaps between the information needs of women of Turkish, Moroccan and Syrian origin and the current communication practices regarding cervical cancer (CC) prevention programmes.
DESIGN: This qualitative study employed five focus group discussions (FGDs) with three categories of stakeholders. The social ecological model (SEM) guided the selection of stakeholders at the interpersonal, community and system level and the interpretation of findings.
SETTING: Data were collected in the Netherlands between January and February 2024.
PARTICIPANTS: (1) Two FGDs with key community figures (n=20, interpersonal and community level), (2) two FGDs with healthcare professionals (n=12, interpersonal and system level) and (3) one FGD with communication experts, programme managers and policy makers (n=8, system level). Discussions with key community figures focused on cultural, religious, emotional and practical aspects of CC prevention programmes among women of Turkish, Moroccan and Syrian origin. Healthcare professionals discussed barriers and facilitators in communication practices, and the communication experts, programme managers and policy makers discussed the feasibility of suggested interventions by the first two stakeholder groups. The FGDs were transcribed verbatim in Dutch and thematically analysed.
RESULTS: The analysis resulted in six themes: (1) stakeholders’ perceptions on the considerations that women of Turkish, Moroccan and Syrian origin have when seeking, understanding and applying information about CC and CC prevention programmes; (2) current approach for health communication practices; (3) suggestions for interventions focused on women of Turkish, Moroccan and Syrian origin; (4) suggestions for interventions focused on the target population’s network; (5) variations among women of Turkish, Moroccan and Syrian origin that need to be considered and (6) conditions that the interventions should meet. Stakeholders described substantial gaps between women’s information needs and current communication practices, mainly related to misconceptions, limited awareness and doubts about the effectiveness of the CC prevention programmes. They characterised existing communication as predominantly top-down, from stakeholders at the system level to women at the individual level. Therefore, stakeholders emphasised the need to involve community-level stakeholders and to strengthen their communication skills and…

articles.title: Cracking the fertility code: a comprehensive review of biomarkers and functional measures.
articles.authors: Woodman-Sousa MF, Grive K
articles.abstract: Human fertility is regulated by a complex, integrated network of biological systems that collectively determine reproductive competence in males and females. Conventional fertility assessment relies on established clinical biomarkers, including reproductive hormone profiles, gamete-based functional assessments and imaging indicators of gonadal structure and function. While clinically informative, these measures capture only partial views of molecular and cellular processes underlying gametogenesis and reproductive capacity. Recent advances in reproductive medicine have expanded the biomarker landscape through genetic and epigenetic profiling, enabling identification of pathogenic variants, chromosomal abnormalities and regulatory modifications associated with infertility syndromes. In parallel, multi-omics approaches are increasingly being used to characterize molecular networks governing gamete development, meiotic integrity, DNA repair and cellular differentiation. This review presents a comprehensive synthesis of fertility biomarkers, spanning endocrine, genetic, epigenetic, structural, metabolic and inflammatory systems. Current evidence is examined on endocrine and reproductive hormone biomarkers, followed by an investigation of genetic and epigenetic markers of reproductive dysfunction, as well as structural and imaging-based biomarkers and inflammatory and metabolic indicators. Finally, emerging biomarker platforms are highlighted as key advances towards precision reproductive medicine. Collectively, these developments support a shift towards a more comprehensive, biomarker-driven framework for the evaluation and management of infertility.

articles.title: Maternal Education in Context: Reassessing the Infant Health Paradox among Latin American Immigrants.
articles.authors: Liu TT, Hamilton TG
articles.abstract: One aspect of the Hispanic Health Paradox is the longstanding observation that Latin American immigrants in the United States often experience equal or better health outcomes than U.S.-born counterparts despite greater socioeconomic disadvantage. This advantage extends to their infants and is most pronounced among mothers with the least education. Whether such patterns reflect selective migration remains unclear. This study evaluates the role of educational selectivity in explaining nativity disparities in infant health. Using U.S. natality data among immigrants from Mexico, Cuba, El Salvador, Guatemala, the Dominican Republic, Colombia, Honduras, and Venezuela (2012-2023), linked with internationally harmonized educational data, we assess preterm birth disparities using two measures of maternal education: absolute and relative attainment. Immigrants at the bottom of the U.S. education distribution often rank much higher in their origin countries, consistent with positive selection. For most births to Latin American mothers (except Colombian and Venezuelan), measuring education relative to origin-country distributions reverses immigrant advantages. At equivalent relative education ranks, immigrant mothers face comparable or higher risks of preterm birth than U.S.-born Hispanic mothers. These findings offer a new perspective on the Hispanic Health Paradox, highlighting the importance of relative education in understanding the association between maternal education and infant health.

articles.title: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins to detect cervical cancer: a preclinical feasibility study.
articles.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
articles.authors: Szita DB, Béres E, Szabó JP et al.
articles.abstract: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins targeting prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) seem promising candidates for positron emission tomography (PET)-based molecular imaging of cervical cancer. Here, we evaluated the performance of gallium-68-labelled 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HPβCD) and randomly methylated β-cyclodextrin (RAMEB) for the in vivo PET detection of cervical cancer. P-glycoprotein positive (Pgp+) KB-V-1 and P-glycoprotein negative (Pgp-) KB-3-1 cervical carcinoma xenografts of varying sizes (small-, medium-, large-sized) were established and subjected to [68Ga]Ga-NODAGA-HPβCD and [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA-RAMEB PET imaging followed by ex vivo biodistribution and immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of PGE2 and Pgp expression. In line with the IHC results, PET data revealed the capability of both radiotracers to reliably detect each tumor types independent of tumor size. Nevertheless, the modest increase in uptake observed with increasing size may indicate enhanced tumor aggressiveness and angiogenic activity. Comparable radiotracer accumulation in MDR-positive and MDR-negative tumors suggests that HPβCD and RAMEB derivatives are unlikely to serve as substrates of Pgp enabling tumor detection across different tumor types. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that radiolabelled cyclodextrins are promising PET tracers for the in vivo detection of cervical cancer, irrespective of tumor size and Pgp expression.

articles.title: LRH-1 is a novel regulator of neutrophil-driven immune responses within the tumor microenvironment.
articles.authors: Wang Y, Duong B, Keeley S et al.
articles.abstract: Plasma cholesterol is correlated with worse outcomes in breast and ovarian cancer. Prior work indicates that myeloid immune cells are highly responsive to cholesterol metabolism. Interestingly, Liver Receptor Homolog-1 (LRH-1, or NR5A2), a key transcriptional regulator of cholesterol homeostasis is highly expressed in neutrophils and is associated with increased survival time. However, the roles of LRH-1 within neutrophils remain unclear. We therefore focused on how LRH-1 influences neutrophil behaviors relevant to cancer. Small molecule ligands for LRH-1 regulated neutrophil migration towards cancer cells. Phagocytosis was also regulated by LRH-1 ligands, the extent being dependent on type of bait (e. coli vs. cancer cells). In T cell co-cultures, neutrophils pretreated with an LRH-1 agonist promoted greater T cell expansion, particularly in CD4+ cells, while LRH-1 inhibition suppressed this response. NETosis is a known trigger of recurrence from dormancy and subsequent tumor growth. Importantly LRH-1 activation reduced NETosis, while treatment with an antagonist or inverse agonist enhanced NETosis, likely through altered reactive oxygen species. Treatment of mice with an inverse agonist of LRH-1 increased the growth of mammary tumors in a NET-dependent manner. Mice harboring dormant D2.0R mammary cancer lesions treated with an LRH-1 inverse agonist exhibited earlier tumor recurrence and enhanced metastatic progression. In contrast, treatment with BL001, a small chemical LRH-1 agonist, delayed recurrence in D2.0R-grafted mice. These findings reveal that LRH-1 is a novel regulator of neutrophil-driven immune responses within the tumor microenvironment. LRH-1 is thus a promising therapeutic target to suppress the progression of breast and ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Systems pharmacology reveals the molecular mechanisms of nerolidol against polycystic ovary syndrome through integrated transcriptomic, network pharmacology and experimental validation.
articles.authors: Kumar GS, Soni A, Pattanayak N et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a heterogeneous endocrine and metabolic disorder marked by hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, insulin resistance, chronic inflammation and oxidative stress, arising from dysregulation across several interconnected molecular pathways. Because its pathogenesis is multifactorial, therapies targeting diverse biological processes at once remain scarce. Nerolidol, a naturally occurring sesquiterpene alcohol with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective properties, has an action against PCOS whose molecular basis remains unresolved. Transcriptomic differences associated with PCOS were examined using the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) dataset GSE34526. Exploratory differential-expression screening identified nominally altered probes using an unadjusted P < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1; however, no individual probe remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction at FDR < 0.05. Functional enrichment analysis was subsequently used to investigate biological processes and pathways represented by these exploratory transcriptional signals. Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG enrichment were applied to pinpoint dysregulated biological processes and signalling pathways. Computational findings were tested in a letrozole-induced PCOS rat model treated with nerolidol, with efficacy judged from oestrous cyclicity, ovarian histopathology, reproductive hormone profiles, oxidative stress biomarkers, inflammatory mediators and metabolic parameters. Transcriptomic analysis showed marked enrichment of processes related to kinase regulation, insulin secretion, intrinsic apoptotic signalling, receptor-mediated signalling and the DNA damage response, while KEGG analysis pointed to pathways governing endocrine regulation, cell signalling and metabolic homeostasis. In animal experiments, nerolidol restored oestrous cyclicity, improved ovarian morphology, corrected endocrine disturbances, and reduced oxidative stress and PCOS-related pathology. These phenotypic effects were functionally concordant with several biological processes highlighted by the computational analyses. However, because the predicted signalling molecules and pathways were not directly measured in ovarian tissue following nerolidol treatment, the proposed molecular mechanisms remain hypotheses requiring targeted experimental validation.

articles.title: From blue dye to multimodal-guided surgery: The evolution of sentinel lymph node mapping in vulvar cancer - A narrative review.
articles.authors: D'Angelo G, Ascione M, Palumbo M et al.
articles.abstract: The surgical management of inguinofemoral lymph nodes in early-stage vulvar cancer has progressively shifted from complete lymphadenectomy toward selective sentinel lymph node (SLN) biopsy, reducing treatment-related morbidity while preserving oncologic safety. This narrative review summarizes the historical, technical, and clinical evolution of SLN mapping, from vital blue dyes to radiotracer-based validation and contemporary multimodal image-guided approaches. A literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus was performed through May 2026, including landmark prospective studies, multicenter validation trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, and studies evaluating indocyanine green (ICG) and hybrid radioactive-fluorescent tracers. Early blue dye studies established the feasibility of lymphatic mapping, whereas technetium-99m, lymphoscintigraphy, and gamma-probe guidance provided the reproducibility required for prospective validation. GROINSS-V I supported safe omission of complete inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy in carefully selected SLN-negative patients, complemented by diagnostic validation in GOG-173; subsequent evidence linked SLN tumor burden to prognosis and enabled risk-adapted management of positive nodes. ICG-based near-infrared fluorescence has emerged as a valuable tool for real-time visualization and may improve intraoperative guidance. However, most comparative studies have evaluated fluorescence after radiotracer-based localization or defined the SLN according to technetium uptake, limiting conclusions regarding stand-alone interchangeability. Current evidence therefore supports ICG primarily as an adjunct within multimodal mapping rather than as a validated replacement for technetium-99m. Future progress should focus on standardized fluorescence protocols, rigorously sequenced ICG-first validation, hybrid radioactive-fluorescent strategies, and integration of imaging-derived and artificial intelligence-based tools into individualized groin management.

articles.title: Maternal high-fat diet and metformin treatment affect palatable diet preference and central reward system gene expression in rat offspring in a sex-specific manner.
articles.authors: Hu S, Cui J, Wang R et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal metformin (MT) treatment improves the metabolic phenotype of high-fat (HF) diet-exposed offspring, but its effect on offspring's palatable food preference remains unclear. We assessed HF diet and sucrose preferences in adult offspring from Sprague-Dawley rat dams fed a control diet, an HF diet with or without MT treatment. Additionally, we measured the mRNA expression of sweet taste perception-related genes in taste buds and dopamine- and opioid-related genes in the central reward system. In adult males, maternal HF diet increased HF food preference and decreased dopamine-related gene expression in the reward system. Furthermore, maternal MT treatment decreased low-concentration sucrose preference, and reduced opioid-related gene expression in the reward system. Maternal HF diet elevated sweet taste perception-related gene expression in taste buds, while maternal MT treatment reversed these changes. In adult females, neither maternal HF diet nor MT treatment affected HF food preference. However, maternal HF diet decreased low-concentration sucrose preference and reduced the expression of sweet taste perception-related genes, while maternal MT treatment did not reverse it. At weaning, maternal MT treatment generally decreased dopamine- and opioid-related gene expression in the central reward system across both sexes. Notably, this early-life central reward transcriptional suppression persisted into adulthood in males but not in females. Our results indicate that maternal HF diet and MT treatment influence HF diet and low-concentration sucrose preferences in adult offspring in a sex-specific manner, which may be associated with altered gene expression in the central reward system and the peripheral taste perception pathways.

articles.title: Ovariectomy abolishes cardioprotection against diastolic dysfunction and impairs cardiac glucose oxidation in female mice with type 2 diabetes.
articles.authors: Chan JSF, Saed CT, Kirschenman R et al.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) increases the risk for diabetic cardiomyopathy (DbCM), which is often characterized by diastolic dysfunction. Pre-menopausal women have a reduced incidence of both T2D and DbCM, but this disappears following menopause. Our goal was to evaluate the potential role for ovarian hormones in mediating these differences. The effect of ovariectomy (OVX) was investigated in female mice with experimental T2D following high-fat diet feeding for 12-weeks in combination with a low-dose treatment of streptozotocin at week 4. Body weight and body composition, glucose homeostasis, cardiac structure/function via ultrasound echocardiography, and myocardial substrate metabolism via isolated working heart perfusions were assessed. Sham and OVX female mice with T2D exhibited increases in body weight and fat mass, as well as impaired glucose homeostasis, though these parameters were more prominent in OVX than sham females when compared to their lean counterparts. However, only OVX female mice with T2D developed diastolic dysfunction as reflected by a significant decrease in the mitral E/A and tissue Doppler e'/a' ratios, as well as an increase in the E/e' ratio. Isolated working hearts from both sham and OVX female mice with T2D exhibited a reduction in glucose oxidation, though this was more pronounced in the latter. Lastly, only OVX female mice with T2D demonstrated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. Our data illustrate key roles for ovarian hormones in impacting how T2D impacts the progression of DbCM in females, which may have relevance to women living with T2D as they transition to menopause.

articles.title: Divergent effects of Trichomonas vaginalis on cervical cancer cells HPV-positive and HPV-negative: Interplay with purinergic signaling.
articles.authors: Galego GB, Holanda LF, Willig JB et al.
articles.abstract: Trichomonas vaginalis is the protozoan that causes trichomoniasis, the most common non-viral sexually transmitted infection in the world. Recently, studies have highlighted the possible association between T. vaginalis and the development of cervical cancer, as well as co-infection with human papillomavirus (HPV), suggesting a role of the protozoan in oncogenesis. In the cervical cancer context, the purinergic signaling influences immunosuppression and angiogenesis, while high concentrations of adenosine can induce cell death. T. vaginalis uptakes adenosine for survival as well it takes advantage in its immunomodulatory effects. Thus, the presence of T. vaginalis could influence cell survival, modulating the tumor microenvironment. Our study demonstrated that, in ex vivo models, T. vaginalis increased cell proliferation, immune infiltrate, and vascularization. Meanwhile, in in vitro 2D cell culture models, T. vaginalis combined with purinergic signaling differentially affects the viability of HPV-positive (SiHa) and HPV-negative (C33A) cervical cancer cell lines, with significant impact in the cell line without HPV. The ATP and adenosine signaling did not affect the cytotoxicity exerted by conditioned medium against both cell lines. T. vaginalis reduced the IL-6 production and E6 oncogene expression by SiHa cells. The Ki-67 gene expression was modulated by the parasite and ATP/adenosine metabolism, highlighting the plasticity of the purinergic signaling combined with the parasite. These findings indicate that T. vaginalis exerts cytotoxicity and modulation of pathways relevant to the tumor microenvironment, influencing cell death, inflammation, and tissue remodeling processes, and shed light to further studies on the interactions between T. vaginalis and host cells.

articles.title: Perceptions of Maternal Mortality Risk and Influences Among Women of Color.
articles.authors: Renbarger KM, Salahshoor S, Place JM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to explore perceptions of maternal mortality among women of color who identify as Black, Hispanic, or multiracial, including their understanding of perceived risk factors and the influence of recent perinatal experiences on these perceptions.
DESIGN: A qualitative, descriptive design was used to conduct this study.
SETTING: Participants were recruited for a semistructured, virtual interview to discuss their perceptions related to maternal mortality.
PARTICIPANTS: Thirty women of color who identify as Black, Hispanic, or multiracial and live in Indiana participated in interviews.
RESULTS: Six themes emerged: (a) limited understanding of maternal mortality, (b) increased awareness of factors related to maternal mortality after experiences of perinatal complications, (c) fear due to perceived high risk of perinatal complications, (d) feeling dismissed during perinatal care, (e) barriers to quality perinatal care and lack of trust in health care systems, and (f) social support and advocacy as protective factors for preventing maternal mortality.
CONCLUSION: Women of color need more awareness of warning signs for maternal mortality; they frequently have negative perinatal care experiences and can benefit from social support. Nurses can improve perinatal practice by increasing knowledge of maternal mortality, promoting a respectful maternity care framework, and increasing social support.

articles.title: Qualitative Descriptive Exploration of Women's Experiences of Outpatient Hysteroscopy in Ireland.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN
articles.authors: Henry C, Lloyd B, Bradshaw C
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore women's experiences of outpatient hysteroscopy (OPH) and identify factors that influenced those experiences.
DESIGN: Qualitative descriptive.
SETTING: Ambulatory gynecology unit in Ireland.
PARTICIPANTS: Eleven women aged 40 to 49 years who underwent OHP at the research setting.
METHODS: We collected data using semistructured interviews and analyzed the data using a reflexive thematic analysis framework.
RESULTS: We identified three themes: The Experience of Pain, Preparation and the Procedure, and Importance of the Environment. Participants described a spectrum of pain experiences that ranged from mild discomfort to severe pain. They emphasized the importance of preparation for the procedure and the care provided during and after the procedure. Participants also identified environmental factors that enhanced their experience of OPH.
CONCLUSION: Health care practitioners should explicitly discuss the possibility of pain when providing information about OPH to ensure that women can make informed choices. Researchers should further investigate the optimal type and timing of pre-procedure analgesia. Health care practitioners should also recognize the importance of the environment in shaping women's experiences of intrusive and intimate procedures from a holistic perspective. These findings are relevant to all health care practitioners involved in OPH services, particularly nursing staff who provide care to women before, during, and after these procedures.

articles.title: Outcomes of Mindful Mood Balance for Moms, online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for perinatal depressive relapse prevention in the USA: a two-arm, single-blind, pragmatic randomised clinical trial.
articles.authors: Dimidjian S, Gallop R, Goodman SH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective and accessible approaches to prevent depressive relapse and reduce symptoms are crucial for addressing the major public health problem of depression among perinatal women. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of Mindful Mood Balance (MMB) for Moms plus usual care (hereafter MMB for Moms)-a web-based mindfulness-based cognitive therapy programme customised for perinatal women-compared with usual care only, in reducing depressive relapse and symptoms.
METHODS: This single-blind, randomised clinical trial was done across the USA, in euthymic pregnant women with recurrent depression who were on recent or current antidepressant medication. Recruitment occurred from March 7, 2019, to July 8, 2020 (data collection was completed Sept 12, 2021). Participants were randomly assigned to MMB for Moms, or usual care. Primary outcomes were reduction in depressive relapse risk and symptom burden, assessed using the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview and Patient Health Questionaire-9, respectively, across the study period. Outcomes were assessed from baseline until 6-months postpartum in three phases (intervention, end of intervention to delivery, and postpartum). The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03623620, and is complete.
FINDINGS: Participants were recruited between March 7, 2019, and July 8, 2020. Data from 500 randomly assigned participants (mean age 32 years [SD 4·5] and mean 11·5 [2·8] weeks gestation), were analysed as the intention-to-treat sample. Of the 500 participants (249 assigned to MMB for Moms and 251 assigned to usual care), 383 [77%] provided assessment data at 3 months and 389 [78%] at 6 months postpartum. MMB for Moms had significantly lower risk of depressive relapse compared with usual care during the full trial period (up to 6 months postpartum): 81 (33%) of 249 participants assigned to MMB for Moms and 111 (44%) of 251 participants in usual care had depressive relapse (hazard ratio 0·74 [95% CI 0·56-0·99]; p=0·045; adjusted false discovery rate p=0·045). MMB for Moms was also associated with a significant reduction in depression symptom burden during the 12 week intervention phase (average decrease of 0·75 [SE 0·13] in the MMB for Moms group and 0·31 [0·13] in the usual care group) but not during the full trial period (average decrease of 0·61 [SE 0·18] in the MMB for Moms group and 0·54 [0·17] in the usual care group).
INTERPRETATION: MMB for Moms resulted in lower risk of relapse compared…

articles.title: Gestational exposure to hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid impairs the reproductive function of male offspring through the LCN2-ferroptosis axis in spermatocytes.
articles.authors: Zhao Y, Luo Y, Yu Z et al.
articles.abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA), introduced as an industrial replacement for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), has raised concern regarding its potential bioaccumulation and toxicity. However, the reproductive toxicity and mechanistic basis of HFPO-TA prenatal exposure in male offspring remain unclear. A mouse model of gestational HFPO-TA exposure (0.4 and 1 mg/kg/day) was established, and integrated histopathological assessment, single-cell transcriptomics, and molecular simulation approaches were performed to characterize its effects on male offspring. HFPO-TA exposure significantly impaired the reproductive function in F1 male mice, as indicated by reduced testicular weight and sex hormone levels, compromised sperm quality, spermatocyte meiotic arrest, and increased germ cell apoptosis. Single-cell sequencing revealed that prenatal HFPO-TA exposure triggered ferroptosis in spermatocytes of male offspring mice and identified lipocalin-2 (Lcn2) as a key regulator of this response. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations confirmed stable binding between HFPO-TA and LCN2. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that HFPO-TA induced spermatocyte ferroptosis through lipid peroxidation and iron overload, while these effects were reversed by treatment with the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 or by Lcn2 overexpression. Collectively, this study delineated a mechanistic framework in which prenatal HFPO-TA exposure induces spermatocyte-specific injury of male offspring through the LCN2-ferroptosis pathway, providing a scientific basis for health risk assessment and regulation in the use of next-generation per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances.

articles.title: Prenatal exposure to di(isononyl) cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylate and adverse birth outcomes in the USA: a prospective analysis of births in a large American birth cohort.
articles.authors: Trasande L, Nelson ME, Alshawabkeh A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A large body of evidence has documented the effects of ortho-phthalates, additives to soft plastic used in food packaging, on premature birth. Ortho-phthalates are increasingly replaced with alternatives including tere-phthalates and di(isononyl) cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylate (DINCH). A limited toxicological literature suggests that DINCH metabolites disrupt sex hormones and promote oxidant stress known to contribute to adverse birth outcomes, and epidemiologic studies have also been limited in sample size, inclusivity of different populations and measurements at different time points in pregnancy.
METHODS: We leveraged a large American cohort comprised of mother-child dyads from twenty-two cohorts to assess associations of trimester-specific and pregnancy-wide DINCH metabolites with birth weight (BW) and gestational age (GA).
FINDINGS: Average prenatal urinary DINCH was inversely associated with birth length, birthweight, and birthweight for gestational age z-scores, but not GA. A tenfold increase in the pregnancy-averaged DINCH metabolite cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid-monocarboxy isooctyl ester (MCOCH) was associated with a decrease of 27.43 g (95%CI: -54.81, -0.04) in birthweight. Trimester-specific analyses revealed stronger associations for third trimester DINCH exposure with birth outcomes.
INTERPRETATION: In a large American cohort representing a broad range of backgrounds, we identified an inverse association of DINCH with standardized measures of birth size, but not gestational age. Further studies should examine joint exposures to DINCH, tere- and orthophthalates, and repeated measures across pregnancy.

articles.title: Integrated serum pharmacochemistry , network pharmacology, untargeted metabolomics and experimental validation to explore the mechanism of Wenjian Qigong Decoction in the treatment of polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.authors: Wang X, Liu C, Zhang Z et al.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent endocrine and metabolic disorder among women of reproductive age, currently has no definitive treatment. Qigong Wan (QGW), first documented in Yifang Jijie, is a classic prescription for infertility in obese women. Given the heterogeneous and complex nature of PCOS, Wenjian Qigong Decoction (WJQG), a modified formula derived from QGW that incorporates medicinal ingredients from Jiawei Buzhong Yiqi Decoction (JWBZYQ), Guishen Wan (GSW), and Jiaotai Wan (JTW), exhibits remarkable therapeutic efficacy for obese PCOS in clinical practice. The efficacy of all constituent herbs in WJQG has been confirmed, whereas its pharmacological mechanisms remain to be clarified.
AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the potential therapeutic benefits of WJQG for the treatment of PCOS and provide mechanistic insights into its mode of action.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An obese PCOS rat model was established via testosterone propionate (TP) injection combined with a 45% high-fat diet (HFD). The therapeutic efficacy of WJQG, as well as the validity of the model, was evaluated by assessing body weight, visceral fat content, estrous cycle, clinical chemistry indicators, and histopathology. Furthermore, a comprehensive approach integrating ovarian untargeted metabolomics, serum pharmacochemistry , network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation was employed to systematically elucidate the potential mechanism of action of WJQG in treating obese PCOS.
RESULTS: WJQG significantly attenuated body weight gain, reduced abdominal visceral fat, restored estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian morphology, and corrected hyperandrogenemia and endocrine dysregulation in obese PCOS rats. Serum pharmacochemistry identified 22 bioactive prototype compounds absorbed into the blood. Network pharmacology predicted hub targets including TNF, IL6, CASP3, and PTGS2. Subsequent molecular docking simulations indicated favorable binding affinities between these proteins and representative prototype constituents such as narirutin, ginsenoside Rc, and hyperoside. Untargeted metabolomics suggested that WJQG substantially remodeled the ovarian metabolome, specifically suppressing the hyperactivated arachidonic acid metabolism pathway and downregulating downstream pro-inflammatory lipid mediators (PGF2α, PGA2, PGE2, and 10,11-dihydro-20-hydroxy-LTB4). Mechanistically, WJQG inhibited the enzymatic cascade of p-cPLA2, COX-2…

articles.title: Ubiquitin-specific proteases and the immune microenvironment in cervical cancer: mechanistic evidence, immunotherapy resistance, and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Zhu L, Xia L et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global health burden, and resistance limits the benefit of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Ubiquitin-specific proteases (USPs) regulate protein homeostasis and may connect human papillomavirus-associated oncogenesis with immune evasion. This narrative review evaluates USP-dependent mechanisms relevant to cervical cancer, distinguishing disease-specific findings from evidence in other tumor types and proposed pathways. Cervical cancer studies support USP7-associated immune-checkpoint regulation and USP14-dependent MCT4 stabilization and lactate export, although the immune consequences of the latter remain inferred. Evidence linking USPs to regulatory T-cell function, STING signaling, antigen presentation, and immunosuppressive metabolism derives largely from non-cervical experimental systems. The proposed E6-USP7 and E7-USP1 immune pathways therefore require direct validation. We discuss small-molecule inhibitors, targeted protein degradation and stabilization, combination strategies, and biomarker development. Compensatory USP Reprogramming (CUR) and a proposed USP-based tumor immune microenvironment (USP-TIME) framework are presented as hypotheses for investigating treatment-associated adaptation and the relationship between USP profiles and immune architecture, respectively. Therapeutic development must account for the possibility that USP inhibition also impairs antigen presentation or effector lymphocyte function. Although USP-directed approaches provide a rationale for further investigation, their clinical benefit in cervical cancer remains unproven. Progress requires cell-type-resolved mechanistic studies, immunocompetent models, validated pharmacodynamic assays, and compound-specific safety assessment.

articles.title: How slow should we go? Variation and outcomes of steroid tapering for immunotherapy-related toxicities in gynecologic cancer.
articles.authors: Velasquez J, Chalif J, Glassman D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined both National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guideline concordance and steroid taper duration with clinical outcomes in patients with gynecologic malignancies experiencing immune-related AEs.
METHODS: This single-institution retrospective cohort included patients with gynecologic malignancies treated with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) from August 2016 to September 2025 who developed grade 3 or 4 immune-related AEs requiring systemic steroids. Clinical and steroid treatment data were abstracted. NCCN guideline concordance and outcomes were assessed.
RESULTS: 63 patients contributing 73 steroid tapers were included. Most patients had endometrial (41.3%), cervical (27.0%), or ovarian cancer (23.8%), and pembrolizumab was the most used ICI (74.6%). 46 tapers (63.0%) were NCCN guideline concordant and 27 (37.0%) were NCCN guideline discordant, with discordance most often driven by taper length and premature initiation. 14 (19.2%) were < 28 days, and 59 (80.8%) were ≥ 28 days. NCCN discordant tapers were more likely to require additional supportive medications for irAE management (e.g. secondary steroids) than concordant tapers (81.5% vs 56.2%, p = 0.0300). NCCN concordance was associated with longer time to ICI restart (56 vs 21 days, p = 0.0241). Tapers <28 days were more likely to require additional supportive medications (100% vs 57.6%, p = 0.0027) and steroids (35.7% vs 8.4%, p = 0.0253) than tapers ≥28 days. Tapers ≥28 days were associated with higher rates of ICI discontinuation due to toxicity (59.3% vs 28.6%, p = 0.0381). Rates of hospitalization, ICU admission, and AE resolution did not differ by NCCN concordance or taper duration.
CONCLUSIONS: Corticosteroid taper practices varied substantially in patients with gynecologic malignancies experiencing severe irAEs; shorter and guideline-discordant tapers were associated with greater treatment escalation and steroid reinitiation.

articles.title: Implementation and sustainability of surgical randomized trials in gynecologic oncology: Adoption beyond publication.
articles.authors: Agusti N, Bercow A, Ramirez PT et al.
articles.abstract: Surgical randomized trials have transformed gynecologic oncology by redefining the extent and route of surgery, nodal assessment, and multimodality care. However, the effect of a surgical trial does not end at publication. Unlike medical therapies, surgical interventions depend on operator expertise, team coordination, pathology support and perioperative infrastructure. Beyond controlled trial settings, these conditions may change, creating technical drift, indication drift, and inequitable adoption. Implementation should therefore be considered a distinct, structured phase of surgical research. The period is particularly vulnerable because landmark trials often evaluate de-escalation or technically complex innovations. Expanding de-escalation beyond trial-tested eligibility can cause undertreatment, whereas diffusion of complex procedures without sufficient expertise or infrastructure can increase morbidity. Disparities in access to specialist surgeons, imaging, pathology, molecular testing, perioperative support, and long-term follow-up amplify these risks. Responsible translation requires trial reports to define the technical, institutional, and patient-selection conditions under which outcomes were achieved. Strategies may include credentialing expectations, operative standards, and risk-appropriate guidelines. Once findings sufficiently resolve equipoise, post-implementation surveillance should determine whether effective procedures are adopted-or ineffective ones abandoned-and whether appropriate use, technical fidelity, safety, equity, and outcomes are maintained as practice spreads. Secondary databases can evaluate utilization, perioperative safety, equity, practice-change attribution, and selected real-world outcomes at scale, but incompletely capture appropriateness, technical fidelity, granular complications, recurrence, and patient-reported quality of life. Surveillance should therefore use a multilevel approach that matches each objective to where information is generated and supplements broad databases with targeted clinical, procedural, and patient-reported data. Treated as an active research phase, surveillance can ensure that surgical innovation reaches the right patients and settings, with outcomes consistent with the supporting evidence.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Ovarian Cancer Tumor-Infiltrating T Cells with Those in Melanoma and before and after PD-1 Blockade.
articles.authors: Colombo I, Meteleva K, Stone SC et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: CD8+ T cells are involved in natural tumor immune surveillance and are known to play a critical role in mediating responses to programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade. High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) exhibits intrinsic resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), despite the presence of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) in the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). In this study, we characterized the phenotype and frequency of TILs in the tumor samples of patients with HGSOC and compared our findings with TILs from melanoma, a tumor highly sensitive to ICI. Melanoma harbored an increased density of CD8+ TILs compared with HGSOC. However, CD8+ T cells from HGSOC tumor samples expressed higher levels of exhaustion markers such as 2B4 and PD-1 compared with the CD8+ melanoma TILs, with evidence for antigen-specific CD8+ TILs. Our study demonstrates that despite the presence of CD8+ T cells that are phenotypically exhausted, there is limited expansion of CD8+ cells after treatment with anti-PD-1 in patients with HGSOC. These data indicate that CD8+ T cells from ovarian cancer express markers associated with antigen specificity and are on the exhaustion trajectory yet are unable to contribute to a measurable antitumor response after PD-1 blockade.
SIGNIFICANCE: By analyzing the TIME in patient-derived samples of HGSOC and comparing them with melanoma, we identify a lower density of CD8+ cells. These cells are characterized by a higher level of immune exhaustion with a poor response after treatment with anti-PD-1.

articles.title: Syphilis Screening in Pregnancy During Emergency Department Gonorrhea and Chlamydia Testing.
articles.journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
articles.authors: Phelan MP, Dewey EN, Hustey FM et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital syphilis is rising in the United States, especially among infants born to women with limited prenatal care. Emergency departments (ED) offer opportunities for early detection, particularly among patients evaluated for urogenital sexually transmitted infection (STI) concerns. In October 2019, our health system implemented an ED STI order set that promoted HIV co-testing and included a preselected option for syphilis testing. In this study, we evaluated change in syphilis testing during the post-implementation period among ED encounters with both pregnancy and gonorrhea/chlamydia (GC/CT) testing.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, quasi-experimental study across 20 EDs, using health record data from 2018 to 2023 for patients aged 15-44 years who received both pregnancy and GC/CT testing. We measured annual syphilis and HIV testing and positivity, stratified by pregnancy status. The primary study outcome was syphilis testing during the encounter; HIV testing and detection outcomes were secondary.
RESULTS: Among 59,171 ED encounters with pregnancy and GC/CT testing, 5,178 (8.8%) involved pregnant patients, and 9,538 (16.1%) received syphilis testing. Syphilis testing among pregnant patients increased from .9% in 2018 to 46.1% in 2023 (+45.1 percentage points [95% CI, 40.4-49.6]). Testing among nonpregnant patients rose from 1.2% to 35.9% (+34.6 percentage points [95% CI, 33.3-35.9]). Overall, only 1,068 of 5,178 pregnant encounters received a syphilis test (20.6%). Among 1,068 syphilis-tested pregnant encounters, 15 (1.4%) were treponemal-positive and 9 (.8%; 843 per 100,000 tested) met the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention surveillance definition for active syphilis (approximately 1 per 119 tests). Using all pregnant encounters with GC/CT testing as the denominator, the encounter-based active syphilis rate was 173.8 per 100,000 (.17%). HIV testing increased similarly (pregnant: .4% in 2018 to 44.5% in 2023), while HIV positivity remained rare (2 pregnant; 13 overall).
CONCLUSION: Syphilis testing and case detection increased during the postimplementation period following introduction of a preselected STI order set in the electronic health record. Many encounters in the analytic cohort still did not include syphilis testing. These findings support the ED as an important setting for identifying syphilis in pregnancy while underscoring the need for further work to understand remaining testing gaps.

articles.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound After Medical Screening Exam Reduces Time to Ruptured Ectopic Pregnancy Diagnosis and Surgery.
articles.journal: The western journal of emergency medicine
articles.authors: Morris VL, Vu M, Lee Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ectopic pregnancy remains the leading cause of first-trimester maternal mortality. Delays in diagnosis and operative management increase morbidity and may be exacerbated by emergency department (ED) crowding. We evaluated whether integration of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) into the medical screening exam of pregnant patients-the obstetric medical screening exam-was associated with improved timeliness of care for patients with surgically managed ectopic pregnancy.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adult patients undergoing operative management for ruptured ectopic pregnancy between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2023, at a county safety-net hospital. The obstetric screening exam was implemented July 12, 2021, and incorporated focused transabdominal pelvic and right upper quadrant ultrasound into the initial ED evaluation, often prior to bed assignment. The primary outcome was time from ED arrival to operating room (OR). Secondary outcomes included time to obstetric consultation, time to hospital admission, ED length of stay (LOS), and POCUS use. Nonparametric testing was used for skewed time data. Logistic regression evaluated the odds of reaching the OR within four hours. Patient-level interrupted time series analysis assessed temporal trends.
RESULTS: A total of 150 patients were included (87 pre- and 63 post-implementation). Median arrival-to-OR time decreased from 516 minutes (interquartile range [IQR] 324-709.5) to 391 minutes (IQR 220-619), a 125-minute reduction (P = .020; bootstrap 95% CI, 8-233). The proportion of patients reaching the OR within four hours increased from 16.1% to 31.8% (odds ratio 2.42; 95% CI, 1.11-5.29; P = .02). Time to obstetric consultation (210 vs 146 minutes; P = .003), time to hospital admission (345 vs 250 minutes; P = .005), and ED LOS (451 vs 367 minutes; P = .03) were all reduced. Point-of-care ultrasound use increased from 41.4% to 66.7% (P < .001), while the remainder underwent radiology ultrasound. Interrupted time series analysis demonstrated no significant immediate change after implementation (P = .790), but a significant postintervention trend toward reduced arrival-to-OR time (-0.45 minutes/day, P = .01).
CONCLUSION: Embedding POCUS into the medical screening examination in triage was associated with sustained improvement in operative timeliness for ruptured ectopic pregnancy. Early diagnostic integration within ED workflow may mitigate system-level delays…

articles.title: Findings from the inaugural national Canadian Resident Census.
articles.journal: Canadian Urological Association journal = Journal de l'Association des urologues du Canada
articles.authors: Wong J, Otiono K, Caterini J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite the importance of residents and fellows to the national urologic workforce, comprehensive data describing Canadian urology trainees has been limited. This study reports findings from the inaugural Canadian Urological Association (CUA) Resident Census.
METHODS: A national, cross-sectional, anonymous, electronic survey of Canadian urology residents and fellows was conducted between May and August 2025. Survey development was led by the CUA Resident and Fellow Committee and the Postgraduate Training Committee. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize demographics, recruitment, training experiences, workload, career planning, and future priorities.
RESULTS: Of 271 eligible trainees, 143 responded (53%), including 116 residents (81%) and 27 fellows (19%); 33.7% of respondents were female and 2% were queer/non-binary. Urology trainees reported high satisfaction with the residency match process. Almost all residents (89%) indicated their intention to pursue fellowship training, most commonly in oncology and endourology. Insufficient exposure was greatest among andrology, urogynecology/reconstructive pelvic surgery, and gender-affirming care subspecialties. Trainees reported working an average of 75 clinical hours per week, with over half exceeding 80 hours. Over one-third (36%) reported experiencing mistreatment during training, most frequently from clinical supervisors.
CONCLUSIONS: This first national CUA Resident Census identified changing trends in demographics, while also highlighting potential issues such as high workload and variable subspecialty exposure. Limitations included a moderate response rate, regional overrepresentation of larger provinces, and reliance on self-reported data. These findings establish a baseline to inform advocacy, educational planning, and future longitudinal assessment.

articles.title: Extended Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing for Chromosomal and Monogenic Disorders by Cell-Free DNA Sequencing: A Blinded Comparison With Amniocentesis.
articles.authors: Mesoraca A, Margiotti K, Fabiani M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether molecular integrated non-invasive fetal exome sequencing (iNIFS), using clinical exome sequencing of maternal-plasma cell-free DNA, concords per pregnancy with paired amniocentesis.
METHOD: Prospective, blinded, single center, paired sample diagnostic accuracy study in 641 consecutive pregnancies referred for clinically indicated amniocentesis at 16-18 weeks. Plasma cell-free DNA underwent low-pass whole-genome sequencing for aneuploidies and CNVs and, after short-fragment enrichment, clinical exome sequencing within a parent fetus trio design. The reference standard comprised QF-PCR, karyotyping, array-comparative genomic hybridization and, where indicated, trio clinical exome sequencing on amniotic-fluid DNA.
RESULTS: iNIFS was reportable in 624/641 pregnancies (97.3%); 612 (95.5%) had complete paired data and formed the analysis population. The reference established a pathogenic or likely pathogenic finding in 107/612 (17.5%). NIPT gave 106 true positives, 503 true negatives, 2 discordant positives and 1 discordant negative: sensitivity 99.1% (95% CI 94.9-99.8), specificity 99.6% (98.6-99.9), PPV 98.1% (93.5-99.5), NPV 99.8% (98.9-100.0), agreement 99.5% and Cohen's κ 0.98. The discordant negative was a maternally inherited variant, the class for which distinguishing maternal from fetal contributions is most challenging.
CONCLUSION: Molecular iNIFS showed high concordance with paired amniocentesis across chromosomal, copy-number and monogenic findings, while retaining an explicit no call rate. Multicentre validation and invasive confirmation of positive findings remain necessary.

articles.title: Urinary and sexual function do not mediate psychological distress reduction in the PC-PEP randomized controlled trial A secondary mediation analysis.
articles.journal: Canadian Urological Association journal = Journal de l'Association des urologues du Canada
articles.authors: Salman B, Smith NK, Ilie G et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Psychological distress is common among men treated for localized prostate cancer and is often presumed to stem from treatment-related urinary and sexual sequelae. The Prostate Cancer-Patient Empowerment Program (PC-PEP), a six-month, comprehensive, digital intervention, reduces psychological distress and improves patient-reported urinary and sexual function. This secondary analysis tested whether improvements in urinary incontinence, urinary irritative/obstructive symptoms, or sexual function explain PC-PEP's effect on psychological distress.
METHODS: In a randomized controlled trial, 128 men with localized prostate cancer were assigned to PC-PEP (n=66) or standard care (n=62) for six months. Psychological distress was measured using the Kessler psychological distress scale (K10), and urinary and sexual function were assessed using the expanded prostate cancer index composite (EPIC) at baseline and six months. Mediation models adjusted for age, relationship status, use of medications for anxiety or depression, Charlson comorbidity index, treatment modality, time from randomization to treatment, and baseline K10 and EPIC scores.
RESULTS: PC-PEP produced significant improvements in urinary incontinence and urinary irritative/obstructive symptoms across the full cohort and attenuated postoperative declines in sexual function; however, none of these urinary or sexual outcomes mediated the program's effect on psychological distress.
CONCLUSIONS: While PC-PEP enhances key urinary and postoperative sexual outcomes, these functional gains do not account for its mental health benefits. This challenges the assumption that psychological distress in prostate cancer survivorship is predominantly driven by urinary or sexual sequelae and highlights the importance of addressing broader psychosocial and behavioral determinants of mental health in survivorship care.

articles.title: Analysis of urinary tract infections as a predictor of obstruction in women with a history of urethral sling surgery.
articles.journal: Canadian Urological Association journal = Journal de l'Association des urologues du Canada
articles.authors: Wadhwa A, Gan AML, Ross J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Midurethral sling (MUS) remains a widely used and effective treatment for stress urinary incontinence, although complications such as voiding dysfunction and urinary tract infections (UTIs) may occur. Prior research has shown that up to 60% of women with chronic lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) after MUS surgery meet objective criteria for bladder outlet obstruction (BOO). This exploratory study aimed to assess whether UTI burden is associated with the presence of BOO in women with chronic LUTS following MUS. Secondarily, UTI patterns before and after urethral sling excision were descriptively evaluated.
METHODS: A retrospective chart review was conducted examining women with a history of MUS and persistent LUTS for at least six months at a single tertiary care center. Obstruction was assessed using urodynamic studies according to Blaivas criteria or fluoroscopic evidence. UTIs were defined using a combination of culture-positive results and documented symptomatic episodes. Associations between UTI burden and obstruction were evaluated using exploratory regression analyses, and symptom outcomes were assessed before and after sling lysis.
RESULTS: Among 95 patients, 58 (61%) demonstrated urodynamic evidence of obstruction. Across the entire cohort, the median number of UTIs over a two-year period was zero. The proportion of patients with at least one UTI did not differ significantly between obstructed and non-obstructed groups (Fisher's exact test, p=0.80). On exploratory multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, menopausal status, and diabetes, the association between pre-lysis UTI burden and obstruction was not statistically significant (odds ratio [OR] 1.08, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.90-1.29, p=0.42). Fifty-seven patients underwent sling lysis. In obstructed patients undergoing lysis, UTI frequency did not change significantly postoperatively (p=0.29), although many patients reported subjective improvement in storage and voiding symptoms.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cohort of women with chronic LUTS following MUS, UTI burden was not observed to be associated with the presence of BOO. While sling excision was associated with subjective symptom improvement, changes in UTI frequency were not statistically significant. These findings suggest that UTI history alone may have limited utility as a clinical marker of obstruction and highlight the need for larger, prospective studies with standardized outcome measures.

articles.title: Progesterone Receptor Antagonists for Labor Induction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Pellot IR, Darché RL, Pires PW et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate mifepristone, a progesterone receptor antagonist, for labor induction and cesarean delivery and related measures of maternal and neonatal safety.
DATA SOURCES: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials was conducted in accordance with PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses) 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251236886). MEDLINE, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov , and Scopus were searched through October 2025.
METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies included randomized trials evaluating mifepristone for labor induction in singleton pregnancies at 37 weeks or more of gestation. Studies involving pregnancy termination, intrauterine fetal death, preterm induction, or concomitant cervical ripening interventions in which the effects of mifepristone could not be isolated were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. The primary outcome was cesarean delivery. Secondary outcomes included induction-to-delivery interval, time to labor onset, Bishop score, need for prostaglandin or oxytocin, postpartum hemorrhage, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, and 5-minute Apgar score less than 7. Data were pooled with a random-effects model.
TABULATION, INTEGRATION, AND RESULTS: The primary analysis included all 15 eligible randomized controlled trials across mifepristone dosing regimens (n=1,063) and control conditions (n=811). Mifepristone was associated with 33% reduced odds of cesarean delivery (33.1% vs 41.9%, odds ratio 0.67, 95% CI, 0.54-0.82) compared with the control method of induction. Mifepristone was associated with higher Bishop scores at 24 hours, shorter induction-to-delivery intervals, and less prostaglandin and oxytocin use compared with control methods. Findings were similar in sensitivity analysis limited to placebo-controlled and high-quality trials (cesarean delivery odds ratio 0.58, 95% CI, 0.40-0.83). No differences were observed in postpartum hemorrhage, NICU admission, or low Apgar score, although most studies did not report these outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Use of mifepristone for labor induction was associated with reduced odds of cesarean delivery, as well as improved cervical ripening and labor induction efficiency. No evidence of short-term maternal or neonatal risk was found, although robust data were limited. Findings support the role of…

articles.title: Association Between Dynamic Changes in the Sling-Pubis Gap and Urinary Symptoms After Tension-Free Vaginal Tape Surgery: Protocol for a Prospective Observational Pilot Study.
articles.authors: Degirmenci Y, Efe Sayın C, Hasenburg A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is one of the most common pelvic floor disorders in women and is frequently treated surgically using midurethral sling procedures. Despite the high success rates of these procedures, postoperative voiding dysfunction remains a clinically relevant complication that may negatively affect patient satisfaction and quality of life. The underlying mechanisms are multifactorial and not completely understood. In particular, the interaction among sling position, urethral mobility, and pelvic floor dynamics during increases in intra-abdominal pressure may influence postoperative urinary function. Dynamic transperineal ultrasound has emerged as a valuable imaging modality for evaluating sling position and urethral mobility; however, the relationship between dynamic sonographic sling parameters and postoperative urinary symptoms has not yet been sufficiently clarified.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to investigate the association between dynamic sonographic sling parameters and postoperative changes in patient-reported lower urinary tract symptoms following retropubic tension-free vaginal tape surgery.
METHODS: This prospective, noninterventional observational pilot study will be conducted at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, University Medical Center Mainz, Germany. Female patients scheduled for retropubic tension-free vaginal tape surgery for SUI will be recruited consecutively. Preoperative assessment will include clinical examination, completion of the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) questionnaire, and standardized transperineal ultrasound imaging at rest and during the Valsalva maneuver. Postoperative follow-up will be performed 3 months after surgery and will include repeat ultrasound examination and IPSS assessment. Sonographic parameters will include urethral mobility, sling-pubis gap, tape-urethra distance, and sling morphology. The primary outcome will be the correlation between changes in the sling-pubis gap during the Valsalva maneuver and changes in IPSS scores. Secondary outcomes will include associations among clinical variables, sonographic findings, and postoperative voiding symptoms.
RESULTS: Ethics approval for this study has been obtained from the Ethics Committee of the State Medical Association of Rhineland-Palatinate (reference number 2025-18448). At the time of manuscript submission, participant recruitment had not yet begun and was scheduled to begin in August 2026. The target…

articles.title: Low-Carbohydrate Diets, Nutritional Adequacy, Glycemia, and Perinatal Outcomes in Women With Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Secondary Analysis of the DiGest Trial.
articles.authors: Ahmad E, Dib S, Jones D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The optimal dietary carbohydrate intake for pregnant women is disputed internationally. Many authorities recommend a minimum of 175 g/day of carbohydrates primarily to support maternal brain glucose requirements and normal fetal brain development. We assessed whether low (<175 g/day) or very low (<120 g/day) carbohydrate intake was associated with altered nutrient intake, glycemia, or pregnancy outcomes in women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Women recruited to the Dietary Intervention in Gestational Diabetes Trial (DiGest) completed masked continuous glucose monitoring and a 24-h dietary recall at baseline before random assignment to receive either a standard- (2,000 kcal/day) or reduced-energy diet (1,200 kcal/day) from ∼29-36 weeks' gestation.
RESULTS: At baseline, 215 women completed a dietary assessment, of whom 66 (30.7%), 74 (34.4%), and 75 (34.9%) reported standard (≥175 g/day), low (120-175 g/day), and very low carbohydrate intake (<120 g/day), respectively. Women consuming fewer carbohydrates consumed less energy, less dietary fiber, and fewer vitamins (B and E) and minerals but proportionally more protein and fat. Consumption of <120 g/day carbohydrates as assessed at baseline before the intervention was associated with a lower time above range (TAR) >120 mg/dL (-6.8% [95% CI -13.4% to -0.2%]; P = 0.044) and lower birth weight (-9.6 [95% CI -18.7 to -0.6] centiles; P = 0.037), but no difference in large- or small-for-gestational-age birth weight was observed. Low carbohydrate intake as a proportion of total energy intake (<35%) without energy restriction was associated with reduced TAR but not with a difference in birth weight.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower carbohydrate intake at baseline was associated with modestly improved glycemia before random assignment in women with GDM, but vigilance to maintain adequate intake of micronutrients and fiber is required.

articles.title: Immune-related DNA methylation signatures, age prediction, and cross-tissue assessment via biologically informed neural networks.
articles.authors: Cheng X, Wu C, Yang X et al.
articles.abstract: Immune-related DNA methylation patterns may provide interpretable markers of biological ageing and disease relevance. This exploratory study integrated four Illumina HumanMethylation450 and MethylationEPIC datasets comprising paediatric peripheral-blood leukocytes (GSE36054; 192 retained after quality control), infant buccal cells (n = 542), neuronal nuclei (n = 58), and peripheral blood from a polybrominated-biphenyl exposure cohort (n = 659). The paediatric peripheral-blood dataset served as the primary modelling cohort, with infant buccal cells providing an independent early-life cross-tissue reference. Processing included cohort-specific quality control and normalisation, batch adjustment, empirical-Bayes differential methylation analysis, pathway enrichment, repeated 10-fold cross-validation, biologically informed neural-network modelling, feature attribution, cross-tissue assessment, gene-ablation analysis, disease mapping, and two-sample Mendelian randomisation. IL6, CXCR4, CDK11 and CREBBP showed the strongest coherent methylation signals and stable predictive contributions, whereas BCLAF1 contributed less consistently. These loci mapped to cytokine-receptor interaction, chemokine signalling, G2/M checkpoint regulation, histone acetylation, and apoptosis-related pathways. The neural network achieved a cross-validated mean absolute error of 1.87 years and R2 of 0.781; removing the polybrominated-biphenyl-associated feature filter yielded comparable performance (MAE 1.91 years; R2 = 0.772). Prioritised features also showed cross-tissue consistency in infant buccal cells. Mendelian randomisation identified genetically supported associations of IL6 methylation with preterm birth and lower mean birth weight and of CXCR4 methylation with preterm birth after multiplicity correction. These associations do not establish that methylation itself causes the outcomes. The findings prioritise immune-related methylation features across paediatric blood and infant buccal contexts within an interpretable framework for age-related methylation and outcome-oriented molecular investigation.

articles.title: Maternal Diabetes during Pregnancy and Risk of Childhood Psoriasis in Offspring: A National Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Weissmann S, Amitai N, Honig E et al.
articles.abstract: Objective Maternal diabetes during pregnancy is associated with long-term metabolic and immune-related outcomes in offspring. While psoriasis is strongly linked to metabolic comorbidities later in life, the impact of in utero exposure to maternal diabetes on psoriasis risk in offspring remains unknown. We investigated whether maternal diabetes during pregnancy is associated with the development of childhood psoriasis in offspring. Research Design and Methods We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using electronic health record data from Clalit Health Services, Israel's largest health maintenance organization. The cohort included 215,280 singleton live births between 2010 and 2023, with follow-up through 2024. Maternal diabetes during pregnancy was identified using ICD-10 codes and categorized as gestational diabetes, type 1 diabetes, or type 2 diabetes. The primary outcome was childhood psoriasis in offspring. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis adjusted for maternal, pregnancy, and offspring characteristics were used to estimate associations. Results Overall, 5.4% of offspring were born to mothers with diabetes during pregnancy. During follow-up, 1,557 children (0.7%) were diagnosed with psoriasis. Psoriasis prevalence did not differ between offspring exposed and unexposed to maternal diabetes (0.7% vs. 0.7%). No associations were observed by diabetes subtype, treatment modality, or degree of glycemic control. In adjusted analyses, maternal diabetes was not associated with childhood psoriasis in offspring (HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.90-1.54; p = 0.246). Conclusions Maternal diabetes during pregnancy was not associated with increased childhood psoriasis risk in offspring. Our findings do not support a substantial role for prenatal metabolic dysregulation in childhood psoriasis development.

articles.title: Making long-acting HIV PrEP routine in college health: durable systems, not dedicated heroes.
articles.journal: Journal of American college health : J of ACH
articles.authors: Broker P
articles.abstract: For many U.S. students, college health is the practical home of primary care and their most direct point of access to HIV prevention. In this commentary I argue that HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), including long-acting cabotegravir and lenacapavir, should be offered as routine preventive care in college health rather than as a specialty service. Nearly all responding student health services in national benchmarking data offer STI and HIV testing and contraception, while far fewer offer PrEP or prompt clinicians to educate patients on PrEP. That gap, the June 2025 approval of lenacapavir, and a quality improvement initiative that raised PrEP counseling from 3.0% to 97% point to a capacity-based framework of on-site, hybrid, and closed-loop referral models. The minimum standard is not identical infrastructure but a reliable pathway from routine offer to receipt of the chosen regimen. Clinics need durable systems rather than dedicated heroes.

articles.title: Oxidative Stress in Female Reproductive Health and Infertility: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, Therapeutic Interventions.
articles.authors: Takalani NB, Lebelo SL
articles.abstract: Infertility is defined by the World Health Organization as the inability to achieve pregnancy after one year of regular, unprotected sexual intercourse. Female infertility can result from problems with ovulation, hormone imbalances, endometriosis, blocked fallopian tubes, and poor egg quality. One factor linked to these conditions is oxidative stress, which occurs when harmful molecules in the body exceed its natural antioxidant defences. This imbalance may damage reproductive cells and tissues, affecting hormone function, embryo quality, implantation, and pregnancy outcomes. Oxidative stress has been associated with several reproductive disorders, including polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), previously called polycystic ovary syndrome, and endometriosis. As a result, there is growing interest in natural approaches that may help protect reproductive health. Some medicinal plants contain natural antioxidants that may reduce oxidative stress and protect reproductive cells from damage. This review examines the impact of oxidative stress on female reproductive health and explores the potential role of medicinal plants in supporting fertility and reproductive well-being.

articles.title: Testosterone as part of hormone replacement therapy in menopausal women: what do we know so far? A narrative review.
articles.authors: Mishra I, Robinson L
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: Testosterone is an essential endogenous hormone in women, exerting physiological actions in reproductive and non-reproductive tissues. Despite the increased demand for the use of testosterone for an array of menopausal symptoms beyond sexual functions, there is a lack of robust evidence on its impact on cardiovascular and musculoskeletal health and cognition. The aim of this review is to provide an overview of evidence-based indications of testosterone as part of menopausal hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in women and highlight the uncertainties, evidence gaps, and future research priorities. This narrative review synthesised current evidence on the physiological role of testosterone, indications for testosterone as part of HRT, clinical efficacy, formulation and prescribing, and safety profile. Testosterone declines across the adult female lifespan until the late sixth decade, and the menopausal transition itself has no meaningful independent impact on testosterone concentrations. Transdermal preparations maintaining testosterone levels in the physiological range are generally safe, with potential side effects of acne and hair growth. The existing high-quality evidence, including national and international guidelines, recommends that hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in postmenopausal women is the only evidence-based indication for use; the evidence does not support use for any other symptom, nor for disease prevention.
LAY SUMMARY: Testosterone, widely known as the male hormone, is also produced naturally in women and plays an important role throughout their lifespan. There has been a growing use of testosterone for a range of symptoms in menopausal women, including low sexual desire, low mood, fatigue, poor memory, and heart and bone health. This review brings together the current evidence and guidelines on testosterone as part of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in menopausal women, including its impact on reproductive and non-reproductive tissues; when it is indicated to be prescribed and in what forms; and safety and gaps in existing evidence. We found that there is high-quality evidence to support the use of testosterone for low sexual desire where conventional HRT has not helped. Transdermal preparations are recommended with no serious side effects at testosterone levels normally found in women. There is insufficient evidence to support its use for brain, heart, and bone health. This represents an area of focus for future…

articles.title: Nutritional supplements in the treatment of endometriosis-associated symptoms: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Seven M, Galla L, Gstoettner M et al.
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: Dietary supplements and antioxidant therapies are frequently used by women with endometriosis to improve symptoms; however, their clinical effectiveness remains unclear. This systematic review evaluated the effects of dietary supplements on pain, quality of life (QoL), fertility outcomes, and lesion progression in women with endometriosis. MEDLINE via PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The eligibility criteria included women with diagnosed endometriosis receiving dietary supplements compared with placebo, no treatment, or standard care. Findings were narratively synthesized, and risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Twenty-four RCTs, involving 2,019 participants, were included. Pain findings were heterogeneous. Improvements across multiple pain domains were reported with nanomicellar curcumin, used either alone or as an adjunct to dienogest, selenium added to dienogest, Proscur, and garlic; vitamin and melatonin findings were mixed, while omega-3 fatty acids, conventional curcumin, and resveratrol showed no clear benefit. QoL outcomes were similarly heterogeneous: nanocurcumin plus dienogest, Proscur, and postoperative multinutrient therapy improved overall or disease-specific QoL, whereas most other interventions showed no between-group benefit. Fertility outcomes were limited to intermediate markers of reproductive success, which improved in some studies but did not lead to higher pregnancy rates. Evidence on lesion progression was limited; adjunctive nanocurcumin and selenium reduced endometrioma size, while postoperative multinutrient supplementation did not reduce recurrence. Dietary supplements may improve selected symptom-related outcomes, but effects were intervention-specific and evidence remains insufficient to support their routine use as standalone treatments. Further adequately powered trials are needed.
LAY SUMMARY: Endometriosis is a condition where tissue similar to the lining of the uterus (endometrium) grows outside the uterus, which can cause severe chronic pelvic pain, limit quality of life, and lead to infertility. In addition to standard medical treatment (painkillers or hormones), many patients with endometriosis use additional supplements, such as vitamins or antioxidants, to alleviate symptoms, but it is unclear how well these approaches work. In this study, we reviewed 24 clinical trials involving 2,019 women with endometriosis to evaluate the effects of…

articles.title: Evaluation of the Hologic Aptima® Vaginitis and Seegene Allplex™ assays for microbiological diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis and Candida vaginitis in women in France, relative to Nugent score and culture.
articles.authors: Martaresche C, Scherrer F
articles.abstract: Introduction. Molecular assays such as the Hologic Aptima® Vaginitis Panel and Seegene Allplex™ Vaginitis assay offer improved sensitivity and multiplex detection for the diagnosis of vaginitis compared with the non-molecular standard of care.Gap Statement. Evidence comparing the relative performance of Aptima versus Seegene is limited, as is knowledge of Aptima's compatibility with non-proprietary swabs.Aim. This prospective study assessed the diagnostic performance of the Aptima BV (bacterial vaginosis) and Aptima CV/TV assays (Candida vaginitis/Trichomonas vaginitis) alongside the Seegene Allplex assay in symptomatic women (≥18 years) presenting for vaginitis testing in primary care in France.Methodology. Two vaginal swabs were taken per patient: one Aptima Multitest Swab and one non-proprietary Σ-TRANSWAB liquid Amies collection swab. Aptima swab data were used solely to confirm performance of the Aptima assays under current test conditions, while all primary assay comparisons were performed using Σ-TRANSWAB samples. These comparisons were performed for each assay relative to Nugent score (for BV) or culture (for CV), as well as Aptima relative to Seegene.Results. In total, 500 women underwent vaginitis testing between July and August 2024.
