When using non-proprietary Σ-TRANSWAB collection methods, sensitivity and specificity values for the Aptima BV assay were 96.7 and 89.7% relative to Nugent score, and 89.9 and 90.6% for Seegene Allplex relative to Nugent score. Among 'intermediate BV' samples (n=66), agreement between Seegene Allplex and Nugent score was 1.5%. Sensitivity and specificity values for the detection of CV were 88.6 and 90.8% for the Aptima CV/TV assay, and 90.2 and 93.7% for Seegene Allplex. Assay detection of TV could not be validated due to an insufficient number of TV-positive samples (n=1). These findings were consistent with Aptima's performance when using proprietary collection methods.Conclusion. Overall, the Aptima Vaginitis Panel demonstrated comparably high diagnostic performance to Seegene Allplex for the detection of BV and CV when using a non-proprietary sample collection method. TV prevalence was too low in this cohort to permit meaningful assay evaluation for this pathogen.

articles.title: Multiple Dimensions of Social Vulnerability and Cervical Cancer Screening Uptake.
articles.authors: Haury J, Chanier JB, Renevier B et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Despite organized screening programs, persistent social inequalities undermine cervical cancer screening effectiveness in high-income countries, disproportionately affecting the most socially vulnerable women.
OBJECTIVES: To identify distinct social vulnerability profiles among pregnant women and examine their associations with cervical cancer screening adherence and intraepithelial lesion detection.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study assessed all pregnant women 25 years or older who delivered at Centre Hospitalier Intercommunal André-Grégoire, a single tertiary care maternity unit in France, between May 1, 2019, and May 1, 2025.
EXPOSURES: Social vulnerability was assessed across 15 indicators spanning administrative, psychological, and violence-related domains. Multiple component analysis and hierarchical clustering on principal components identified 6 distinct vulnerability profiles. Multiple logistic regression examined associations between profiles and cervical screening inadequacy (no cervical sample within the last 3 years, including those never screened) and squamous intraepithelial lesion detection, adjusting for maternal age and body mass index.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Cervical screening inadequacy (primary outcome) and low- and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion detection (secondary outcome).
RESULTS: Among 18 253 women (median [IQR] age, 32.3 [29.1-36.0] years; median [IQR] body mass index, 25.9 [22.7-29.4]), 10 248 (56.1%) were up to date with screening. Six vulnerability profiles were identified. Compared with the low-vulnerability reference profile, all profiles showed increased odds of screening inadequacy: substance use and psychological vulnerability (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.33; 95% CI, 1.20-1.48), migrant or linguistic barrier (AOR, 3.40; 95% CI, 3.16-3.66), psychological violence (AOR, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.75-2.32), sexual violence (AOR, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.74-2.48), and physical violence (AOR, 2.54; 95% CI, 2.19-2.95). Violence-exposed and substance use profiles also had significantly higher proportions of women with a detected intraepithelial lesion despite reduced screening participation.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of pregnant women, distinct social vulnerability profiles were differentially associated with cervical cancer screening inadequacy; women with migration-related barriers experienced the greatest disadvantage, and violence-exposed women showed both…

articles.title: The neolignan Miliusin B inhibits cell migration and promotes apoptotic cell death in cervical cancer cell line HeLa.
articles.authors: Srisuphan R, Rayanil KO, Pengnam S et al.
articles.abstract: Previously, we reported the discovery, chemical characterization, and preliminary anticancer activity of Miliusin B (MB), a natural neolignan from Miliusa sessilis, demonstrating cytotoxicity and selectivity against the human cervical cancer cell line HeLa. In the present study, we further investigated the underlying anticancer mechanisms of MB. Consistent with our earlier findings, MB exhibited sub-micromolar cytotoxicity toward HeLa cells with >60-fold selectivity relative to non-cancerous controls. Mechanistic analyses revealed that cytotoxic concentrations of MB (5 µM) induced G2/M cell-cycle arrest and activated apoptotic pathways, as evidenced by caspase-9, caspase-3 and PARP cleavage. In addition, MB significantly impaired HeLa cell migration at sub-toxic concentrations (≤ 0.5 µM). Its efficacy was further validated using a three-dimensional spheroid model, where MB suppressed spheroid growth at 0.5 and 5 µM. Finally, combinatorial assays with standard cisplatin (Cis)-based cervical cancer chemotherapeutics (Cis monotherapy and Cis doublet regimens) demonstrated that MB enhanced the anti-proliferative effects of all treatments tested. Collectively, these findings highlight MB as a promising selective cytotoxic and anti-migratory candidate for further development as a potential therapeutic agent against cervical cancer.

articles.title: Robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for uterus transplantation: a systematic review of surgical techniques, donor safety, and recipient outcomes.
articles.authors: Baradwan S, Latifah HM, Hafedh B et al.
articles.abstract: Uterus transplantation (UTx) has emerged as a promising treatment for women with absolute uterine factor infertility (AUFI), enabling pregnancy and live birth with their own genetic offspring. Living-donor uterus procurement remains the most technically demanding component of the procedure. Robotic-assisted donor hysterectomy has been introduced to improve surgical precision, reduce donor morbidity, and preserve graft quality, while recipient implantation is performed via laparotomy. This systematic review evaluated current evidence on robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for UTx, focusing on surgical techniques, donor safety, recipient outcomes, and reproductive success. Databases and trial registries were searched from inception through June 2026. Six studies reporting 29 unique robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomies across five countries met the inclusion criteria. All procedures used the da Vinci Xi robotic platform. Operative time and estimated blood loss decreased with increasing surgical experience, while major donor complications (Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher) were less frequent in later series. Among cases with reported follow-up, no graft loss was observed; restoration of menstruation, embryo transfer, clinical pregnancy, and live birth were achieved, including ten live births in the largest programme. Robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for uterus transplantation appears technically feasible and has been associated with viable grafts and successful pregnancies in highly selected cases. However, major donor complications, including ureteric injury requiring reimplantation and bilateral oophorectomy, were observed, and the true incidence of donor morbidity remains uncertain. Current evidence remains limited to small observational studies, and these findings support careful evaluation within structured, multidisciplinary programmes and international registries rather than widespread expansion.

articles.title: Effectiveness of prenatal predictors for congenital diaphragmatic hernia on survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation requirement: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Rogers E, Le Vance J, Naidu S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is associated with high mortality and morbidity. Antenatal counselling enables parents to prepare for the postnatal outcomes and relies on effective prognostic tools. Ultrasound (USS) predictors including observed/expected lung head ratio (o/e LHR) and liver position, are used independently, or combined into severity classifications. The aim was to evaluate the association between USS predictors, and severity classifications with survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) requirement in prenatally diagnosed CDH at Birmingham Women's and Children's Hospital (BWC).
METHODS: CDH patients from BWC with dates of birth between 1st December 2013-1st December 2023 were retrospectively collected. Study inclusion required o/e LHR measurement between 22- and 32-weeks gestational age (GA.) Comparisons between groups was assessed by Fisher exact test and Mann-Whitney U test. Logistic regression was performed to determine prognostic ability, with area under curve (AUC) calculated.
RESULTS: 91 eligible patients were identified, which included 82 left-sided, and 9 right-sided CDH. Overall, 55% survived to discharge and 13% required ECMO. In the left CDH cohort, 57% of infants survived to discharge, and 15% required ECMO. O/e LHR, liver position and the combined predictive model including o/e LHR and liver position were predictive of survival to discharge with good prognostic ability (AUC 0.769, AUC 0.703, and AUC 0.823, respectively). O/e LHR, liver position, and the combined predictive model were not predictive of ECMO requirement. In the right CDH patients, 33% survived to discharge, O/e LHR and liver position were not predictive of survival to discharge.
CONCLUSION: O/e LHR, liver position and the combination of these predictors, predicted survival to discharge in prenatally diagnosed left CDH with the combined model, the most predictive particularly in the isolated left CDH sub-group. Further analysis into effective predictors for ECMO requirement, and for right and complex left CDH is required.

articles.title: Roles and Biological Effects of Polysaccharides in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Ding N, Sun C, Wang H et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) represents a prevalent and clinically significant reproductive-endocrine disorder among women of childbearing age. While dietary interventions, regular physical activity, and targeted lifestyle modifications have been validated to confer therapeutic benefits for PCOS management, polysaccharides key bioactive components of higher plants with extensive distribution throughout the plant and animal kingdoms exhibit distinct pleiotropic bioactivities, including anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, hypoglycemic, lipid-lowering, and anti-obesogenic properties. In the context of PCOS treatment, these natural macromolecules hold considerable promise for alleviating clinical manifestations, ameliorating insulin resistance and obesity, attenuating inflammatory responses, and restoring sex hormone homeostasis. Cumulative evidence from preclinical and clinical studies has demonstrated that polysaccharides can improve menstrual irregularities, reduce body weight, lower blood glucose and serum testosterone levels, and suppress aberrant inflammation. The present review systematically summarizes the multifaceted effects of diverse polysaccharide compounds on PCOS, aiming to provide insights into their potential as complementary therapeutic agents for this complex disorder.

articles.title: Understanding Past and Present Surgical Registries for Patients with Uterovaginal Prolapse and Planning the Development of a Global Registry.
articles.authors: Collins S, Yurteri-Kaplan L, Vereeck S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Registries following patients who undergo surgery for uterovaginal pelvic organ prolapse provide real-world postoperative evidence. We aimed to identify characteristics of successful registries that could be used to develop a sustainable global registry for these patients.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review of the literature to identify existing and past registries on the surgical management of primary uterovaginal pelvic organ prolapse. Once identified, key characteristics of the registries were collected, and consensus statements about future efforts to develop a global registry were created. These statements were evaluated through a modified Delphi process.
RESULTS: One hundred and eleven articles were identified and reviewed, published from 17 registries. Consensus was achieved for the following three statements: surgeons treating patients for uterovaginal pelvic organ prolapse should standardize baseline, surgical, and postoperative objective and subjective data to facilitate the development of a universal registry; urogynecological surgeons and researchers should seek to minimize cost and maximize feasibility by automating data collection through emerging technologies; urogynecological surgeons and researchers should seek the input of key stakeholders to iteratively improve the registry and ensure that it remains evidence-based and current.
CONCLUSIONS: Understanding past and present surgical registries prepares us for the multifaceted efforts that will be required to develop a sustainable, global registry for the surgical management of uterovaginal pelvic organ prolapse.

articles.title: Prophylactic Midurethral Slings at the Time of Pelvic Organ Prolapse Repair.
articles.authors: Gurbuz E, Chidawanyika T, Uyanik E et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Prophylactic midurethral sling (MUS) placement can prevent de novo stress urinary incontinence (SUI) after pelvic organ prolapse (POP) repair, but the concern about additional MUS-related adverse events remains.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to compare postoperative outcomes between women with and without preoperative SUI after undergoing concomitant POP repair and MUS placement.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included women undergoing POP repair with concurrent MUS placement between 2017 and 2023. Patients in the prophylactic group did not have preoperative SUI, whereas those in the nonprophylactic group did. The primary outcome was postoperative SUI. Secondary outcomes included recurrent urinary tract infection (UTI), voiding difficulty, overactive bladder symptoms, pelvic pain, and mesh complications. Multivariate logistic regression was used to adjust for potential confounders.
RESULTS: Of 1,132 women, there were 409 (36.1%) prophylactic and 723 (63.9%) nonprophylactic MUS procedures. Women in the prophylactic group were significantly older, predominantly postmenopausal, of lower body mass index, and more commonly had stage 3 POP and underwent sacrocolpopexy. Median follow-up was 12 months. Postoperative SUI occurred less frequently in the prophylactic group (1.7% vs 5.8%; P=0.001). Women with a prophylactic MUS were nearly 3 times less likely to have postoperative SUI (adjusted odds ratio, 0.31; 95% CI, 0.14-0.72). Postoperative recurrent UTIs were less common in the prophylactic group (1.5% vs 4.4%; P=0.008), whereas other adverse events were comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Women without preoperative SUI had lower rates of postoperative SUI after concomitant POP repair and MUS placement, with similar rates of adverse events.

articles.title: Effects of the GnRH agonist leuprorelin on liver volume in premenopausal women with severe polycystic liver disease.
articles.authors: Wijbenga IG, Duijzer R, Geertsema P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic liver disease (PLD) is characterized by multiple liver cysts, sometimes leading to severe liver enlargement, with associated physical and psychosocial complaints. Treatment options are limited. Female gender is a risk factor for PLD; estrogen supplementation increases liver size in women with PLD, whereas the polycystic liver decreases after menopause. Estrogens may therefore be a target for therapy.
METHODS: In this prospective, open-label study, premenopausal women aged 18-45 years with severe PLD were randomized 1:1 to a direct start of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist leuprorelin (n=6) or to standard care with delayed start of leuprorelin 18 months after randomization (n=8). The gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist (11.25 mg injections once every 3 mo) leads to a reduction in estrogens and progesterone, and consequently to medically induced menopause. The primary outcome was liver growth rate at 18 months. Secondary outcomes comprised quality of life, menopausal side effects, and adverse events. An interim analysis was performed when all participants had reached month 18, as notable side effects were expressed.
RESULTS: In the group with direct start of leuprorelin, liver volume still increased in half of the participants, with the median liver growth rate not significantly different from the standard care group (4.04 [-4.62 to 6.84] vs. 11.0 [0.70-13.2] %/year, respectively, p=0.15). Importantly, PLD-related quality of life did not improve with treatment, whereas menopausal side effects were severe, leading one participant to stop treatment early. The total number of adverse events in the direct versus standard care group was 38 versus 9, respectively (p<0.001). Because of these results, the study was terminated early.
CONCLUSIONS: leuprorelin treatment did not reverse liver volume, while menopausal side effects and adverse events were substantial.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcome Following Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation and Potential Emerging Etiologies.
articles.authors: Haïssaguerre M, Benali K, de Groot N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unexplained cardiac death and cardiac arrest associated with idiopathic ventricular fibrillation (IVF) are heterogeneous pathologies responsible for significant mortality in young people.
OBJECTIVES: This retrospective multicenter cohort study evaluated the natural history of a large cohort of IVF survivors including recurrence burden, emerging etiologies, and long-term management.
METHODS: This study included IVF patients from 46 tertiary centers and followed for at least 5 years. Patients over the age of 15 years who had documented ventricular fibrillation and extensive negative investigations supporting the diagnosis of IVF were included. Patients were followed in each center with their outcome being established on data collection from subsequent clinical records, new investigations, genetic results, and implanted defibrillator recordings. Recurrent arrhythmias and mortality were assessed. Diagnoses were graded as definite (direct evidence) or probable (indirect criteria).
RESULTS: A total of 825 patients (37% women; age 35.7 ± 12 years) were followed for a median duration of 120 months (Q1-Q3: 78-180 months). Death occurred in 27 patients (3.3%) from cardiac (n = 10; 1.2%), noncardiac (n = 9; 1.1%), and unknown (n = 8; 1%) causes, and few patients (4.5%) developed overt cardiomyopathy. Overall arrhythmia recurrence increased steadily over 2 decades, reaching 52.7% of patients, with a median time to first recurrence of 20 months (Q1-Q3: 5-48 months) and a similar incidence in men and women. Emergent etiologies occurred in 68.8% of the total population, and were associated with new information during recurrences, structural changes, genetic results, and mapping procedures. They included reclassified inherited arrhythmia conditions in 73 (8.8%), focal sources in 272 (33.0%), and definite or probable microstructural myocardial alterations (MiCMs) with normal imaging in 223 (27.0%), while no diagnosis was identified in 257 (31.2%). Compared with MiCM, focal IVF included more women, occurred more frequently at rest/sleep, and was associated with narrow QRS complexes (90.1 ± 12 milliseconds vs 104.8 ± 16 milliseconds; P < 0.001). Quinidine appeared effective in preventing focal IVF (68.3%) whereas beta-blockers appeared effective (49.3%) in MiCM-IVF. Catheter ablation was performed in 181 patients with no recurrence observed in 75.7%.
CONCLUSIONS: This multicenter long-term cohort study of IVF survivors shows low cardiac mortality, a persistent…

articles.title: Bothersome VMS associated with menopause: a survey of the impact on women and their partners in the United States.
articles.authors: Kingsberg SA, Ajmera M, Shiozawa A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the impact of vasomotor symptoms (VMS) on women going through menopause and their partners, and the anticipated gaps in these perceptions.
METHODS: Noninterventional, online surveys (May-June 2024) of women with VMS in the United States and their partners. Surveys were similar, but not identical, to allow comparisons of perspectives. No personally identifiable information was collected.
RESULTS: The survey was completed by 253 matched women and partner pairs. Mean age for women was 50.7 and partners 52.2 years. Similar numbers of women (40.7%, n=103) and partners (46.3%, n=117) reported that the woman had severe VMS. Women were more likely to seek treatment for any condition; 73.5% (n=186) of women and 58.5% (n=148) of partners reported high likelihood of seeking treatment. However, 78.7% (n=199) of women reported never receiving VMS treatment. Fewer women (48.6%, n=123) than partners (67.2%, n=170) reported that the partner encouraged the woman to understand their symptoms and pursue VMS treatment. More than half of women (59.3%; n=131) and partners (50.5%; n=113) reported a ≥2-point decrease in sexual satisfaction when comparing before VMS to the present.
CONCLUSIONS: VMS have the potential to reduce relationship satisfaction for women and for their partners. Although women and partners were generally aligned on the daily life impact of VMS, there were problems with communication and gaps in perception. Furthermore, most women had never received treatment for VMS. This suggests an unmet need for educational programs and highlights the importance of enhancing communication between women experiencing VMS and their health care professionals.

articles.title: Natural, clean, yet still allergenic: contact allergen burden in vulvar soothing products.
articles.authors: McAleer L, Negris O, Mauskar MM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the prevalence of contact allergens in over-the-counter nonhormonal vulvar soothing products and determine whether common marketing claims identify products with lower allergen burden.
METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of externally applied vulvar soothing products sold through major US retailers was performed. Ingredients were compared with the North American Contact Dermatitis Group 80-allergen series. Product characteristics, marketing descriptors, and allergen burden were analyzed using descriptive and comparative statistics.
RESULTS: Among 65 products, 78% contained at least one allergen, and 49% contained botanical-derived allergens. Fragrance ingredients were the most common allergens (39%), followed by sodium benzoate (25%), phenoxyethanol (12%), and propylene glycol (9%). Marketing descriptors, including "natural," "hypoallergenic," and "fragrance-free," were not associated with lower allergen burden. Twenty-eight percent of "fragrance-free" products contained botanical scent allergens, and all "hypoallergenic" products contained at least one allergen. Ointments had lower allergen burden than other vehicles (P = 0.02), while product price was not associated with allergen burden.
CONCLUSIONS: Most nonhormonal vulvar soothing products contain common contact allergens despite marketing suggesting improved tolerability. These findings support ingredient-based counseling by Menopause Society Certified Practitioners and other menopause health care professionals when recommending over-the-counter vulvar products to minimize contact allergen exposure and contact dermatitis risk.

articles.title: Lifestyle factors associated with hot flash frequency and daily interference: highlighting the role of sleep quality, diet quality and physical activity.
articles.authors: Ranatunga VS, Sutarsa N, Vargas N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine associations of lifestyle and demographic factors with hot flash frequency (HFF) and hot flash-related daily interference (HFRDI) in a multicultural Australian convenience sample. The study fills an evidence gap by investigating how lifestyle factors interact with ethnicity and self-reported menopausal status in Australia's diverse population, an area with limited prior research.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey conducted in 2024-2025 included a convenience sample of women who self-identified as being in perimenopause and postmenopause (mean age: 56.1±6.6 y). All demographic, menopause, lifestyle, medication-use, and symptom information was self-reported through the online questionnaire. Demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, menopause status, and symptom outcomes were self-reported. Diet quality, physical activity, and sleep were assessed using an adapted Global Diet Quality Score, an International Physical Activity Questionnaire-based measure, and a modified Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, respectively. Menopause status was self-reported, and duration in that status was recorded; Stages of Reproductive Aging Workshop (STRAW) +10 informed the terminology but was not used to assign specific reproductive-aging substages. Outcomes included HFF and HFRDI. Ordinal logistic models estimated adjusted associations controlling for age, menopause status/duration, and ethnicity.
RESULTS: Sleep quality was the strongest correlate of HFF and HFRDI. For HFF, each one-category worsening in sleep quality was associated with higher odds of being in a higher frequency category (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=2.44; P =0.001); older age was inversely associated (aOR=0.42; P =0.002). For HFRDI, poorer sleep was strongly associated with greater interference (aOR=4.93; P <0.001). Ethnicity was not associated with frequency ( P =0.687) but was associated with daily interference (aOR=2.66; P =0.037). Diet quality showed a nonsignificant inverse association for daily interference ( P =0.077). Physical activity showed a small, nonsignificant tendency toward higher frequency ( P =0.135).
CONCLUSION: Findings suggest the importance of routine sleep quality for symptom burden and may inform lifestyle-focused approaches to symptom management.

articles.title: Levator ani muscle enthesis-related pain in patients with bladder pain syndrome: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Lim HC, Wang PH, Lin KC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome is a chronic pelvic pain condition with heterogenous mechanisms. Levator ani muscle (LAM) enthesis-related pain has been proposed as a musculoskeletal contributor to bladder pain symptoms. This study investigated whether LAM enthesis-related pain is independent of cystoscopic glomerulation in patients presenting with bladder pain symptoms.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 231 patients with painful bladder symptoms who underwent cystoscopy between January 2019 and September 2024. Patients were stratified according to the presence or absence of cystoscopic glomerulations. Demographic characteristics, lower urinary tract symptoms, and pelvic pain phenotypes were compared between groups. Logistic regression was used to assess associations between cystoscopic glomerulation and LAM pain subtypes.
RESULTS: Age, height, body weight, body mass index, and lower urinary tract symptoms did not differ significantly between groups. Glomerulations were not significantly associated with LAM pain (P = 0.168) or enthesis-related pain (P = 0.372). In logistic regression analysis, glomerulations were not associated with overall LAM pain (odds ratio 0.71; 95% confidence interval 0.37-1.35; P = 0.292) or LAM enthesis-related pain (odds ratio 0.98; 95% confidence interval 0.51-1.87; P = 0.940).
CONCLUSIONS: LAM enthesis-related pain was not significantly associated with cystoscopic glomerulation in this cohort. These findings suggest that LAM enthesis-related pain may represent a possible musculoskeletal phenotype among patients with bladder pain syndrome; however, this hypothesis requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Task-Dependent Synergy between FTIR and Raman Spectroscopy for Sperm Quality Prediction.
articles.authors: Campanella B, Birindelli L, Legnaioli S et al.
articles.abstract: Male infertility affects approximately 15% of couples worldwide, contributing to 40-50% of infertility cases in Western countries. Standard semen analysis remains the cornerstone of fertility assessment, yet conventional parameters (concentration, motility, morphology) have limited predictive value for fertilization success. Vibrational spectroscopy, particularly Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) and Raman spectroscopy, offers rapid, nondestructive chemical fingerprinting of biological samples. However, optimal strategies for integrating multimodal spectroscopic data remain unclear, and the value of fusion may depend on the biological end point. This study systematically compares FTIR and Raman spectroscopy, both independently and through multiple fusion strategies, for predicting rectilinear progressive sperm motility (binary classification) and normal morphology (continuous regression) in human seminal plasma. We determine whether complementary information exists, when fusion provides value, and which strategy optimally leverages multimodal data. Building on Raman-derived Multivariate Curve Resolution-Alternating Least Squares (MCR-ALS) concentration profiles, we further develop a clinical classifier based on four seminal plasma biomarkers (human serum albumin, glutathione S-transferase, transferrin, lysophosphatidylcholine), validated by leave-one-patient-out cross-validation and Firth's penalized logistic regression to address near-complete separation in this small-sample setting (n = 30). Our findings reveal technique-specific advantages: Raman spectroscopy substantially outperforms FTIR for binary motility classification, with feature-level fusion matching but not exceeding Raman's performance, indicating limited complementarity. Conversely, FTIR alone achieves superior predictive accuracy for continuous morphological outcomes. The clinical classifier based on MCR-ALS-derived biomarkers achieved AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) = 0.855, accuracy = 86.7%, and BER (Balanced Error Rate) = 0.136, with model significance confirmed by permutation testing. Elevated human serum albumin and lysophosphatidylcholine emerged as the strongest negative predictors of high motility, consistent with seminal tract inflammation and sperm-cytotoxic phospholipid accumulation, while transferrin showed a positive association in line with its role in iron availability for sperm function. These results demonstrate that optimal spectroscopic approaches depend on the biological…

articles.title: Cytology and hrHPV Testing in HPV-Vaccinated Women Entering Cervical Screening: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Cruickshank ME, Pan J, Cuschieri K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the predictive performance of cytology and high-risk HPV (hrHPV) testing in young HPV-vaccinated women participating in the cervical screening programme in Scotland.
DESIGN: Prospective observational study.
SETTING: Routine cervical screening services in three Scottish Health Boards between 2011 and 2015.
POPULATION: Women born between 1991 and 1995 attending routine cervical screening who were eligible for HPV immunisation, including catch-up vaccination cohorts.
METHODS: Residual liquid-based cytology samples were tested for hrHPV using Hybrid Capture 2. Women with high-grade cytology, hrHPV-positive and BNA/mild dyskaryosis, and a subset of hrHPV-positive women with negative cytology from one participating region were invited for colposcopy. Colposcopy and histology outcomes were obtained from the National Colposcopy Clinical Information Audit System (NCCIAS). Positive and negative predictive values (PPV, NPV) for CIN2+ were estimated within the study referral framework, and hrHPV persistence across repeat testing was examined.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: PPV and NPV for CIN2+ within the colposcopy referral pathway and patterns of hrHPV persistence in a selected group who attended for colposcopy.
RESULTS: From 10 000 co-tested residual samples, hrHPV positivity was 86% in borderline/mild cytology and 27% in cytology-negative samples. Among 1352 women who attended for colposcopy, 184 CIN2+ cases were identified. Within the selective referral framework, hrHPV testing demonstrated a PPV for CIN2+ of 14.3% (95% CI: 12.5-16.4) and an NPV of 98.9% (95% CI: 94.0-99.9), while high-grade cytology demonstrated a PPV of 71.7% (95% CI: 59.2-81.5) and an NPV of 89.2% (95% CI: 87.4-90.8). Among 1007 women with repeat testing, hrHPV persistence declined with increasing inter-test intervals, with greater clearance observed over longer follow-up periods.
CONCLUSIONS: In this early HPV-vaccinated cohort screened within the historical Scottish programme from age 20 years, hrHPV testing retained a high negative predictive value but a low positive predictive value for CIN2+, reflecting the low prevalence of disease in vaccinated populations. These estimates reflect outcomes within a selective colposcopy referral framework and should not be interpreted as population-level screening accuracy measures. The findings support the role of cytology triage alongside hrHPV testing while highlighting the need for further evaluation of screening strategies in highly…

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of ERAP1 Genetic Variants and Haplotypes in Cervical Cancer: Insights From TCGA-CESC and a Brazilian Patient Cohort.
articles.authors: Dian AL, Cunha APA, Melo CPS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the association between genetic variants and haplotypes of ERAP1 and clinical outcomes in cervical cancer patients, utilizing data from the TCGA-CESC and a cohort of Brazilian patients.
METHODS: ERAP1 variants and haplotypes were evaluated in two distinct cohorts: whole-exome sequencing (WES) data from 173 cervical cancer cases in the TCGA-CESC dataset, and Sanger sequencing data from 52 Brazilian cervical cancer patients. The TCGA-CESC data were employed for in silico analysis to identify significant ERAP1 variants and haplotypes, which were subsequently evaluated in Brazilian cervical cancer samples. The Tumor IMmune Estimation Resource (TIMER) tool was used to assess the association between ERAP1 expression and immune cell infiltration.
RESULTS: Haplotype analysis of ERAP1 in the TCGA-CESC dataset revealed that H005 (rs26653-rs2287987-rs30187-rs10050860-rs17482078-rs27044) and H023 (rs26653-rs27895-rs30187-rs27044) haplotypes were significantly associated with poorer survival outcomes. Homozygosity for H005 and the presence of H023 were strongly associated with both overall survival (OS) (HR = 9.591, p = 0.00384; HR = 10.183, p = 0.02862, respectively) and disease-specific survival (DSS) (HR = 12.851, p = 0.00162; HR = 15.183, p = 0.01191, respectively). TCGA-CESC data showed that homozygosity for rs2287987 (p.Met349Val) was associated with an increased risk of death in both overall survival (OS) (HR = 11.043, p = 0.00376) and disease-specific survival (DSS) (HR = 13.833, p = 0.00255), whereas rs30187 (p.Lys528Arg) demonstrated a protective effect for DSS, reducing mortality risk in both heterozygous (HR = 0.374, p = 0.04055) and homozygous (HR = 0.346, p = 0.03845) forms. However, although these variants were individually associated with survival outcomes in the dataset, this association was not retained in the multivariate analysis, suggesting that these variants may not have an independent prognostic effect. Similarly, no associations were found for these variants in the Brazilian cervical cancer cohort, suggesting that the impact of these variants on the prognosis of cervical cancer patients may be primarily influenced by the combination of variants. Furthermore, ERAP1 expression levels were positively correlated with CD8+ T cell infiltration (correlation coefficient = 0.264, p = 0.00000960), which was associated with improved survival outcomes (HR = 0.006, p = 0.049).
CONCLUSION: ERAP1 haplotype H005…

articles.title: Androgen driven organoids for the male urogenital system.
articles.authors: Liu A, Yang L, Yan X et al.
articles.abstract: Androgen signalling plays a central role in the development and function of the male urogenital system, including the adrenal gland, prostate, and testis. Disruption of the androgen axis underlies diseases ranging from infertility to castration-resistant prostate cancer, yet current models fail to fully display its multi-organ and hormone-driven complexity. Organoid systems provide a promising platform to model androgen-responsive tissues while preserving three-dimensional structure and cellular heterogeneity, with the ability for long-term culture and cryopreservation. Recent advances have enabled the generation of prostate, testicular, and adrenocortical organoids, offering new opportunities to study androgen receptor signalling, steroidogenesis, and lineage plasticity. Here, we review androgen-driven organoids across the male urogenital axis and discuss emerging strategies to recapitulate endocrine crosstalk. Despite these advances, current models remain reductionist and lack systemic integration. Future efforts toward multi-organ platforms and engineered microenvironments may enable the elucidation of the role of androgen signalling in physiological conditions and disease development.

articles.title: Impact of lateral internal sphincterotomy on quality of life and postoperative faecal incontinence in chronic anal fissure: An observational before and after study.
articles.journal: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
articles.authors: Capre-Pereira J, Pérez-Imbachí HF, Gempeler A et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate the impact of lateral internal sphincterotomy on symptom resolution and quality of life, overall and related to faecal incontinence, in patients with chronic anal fissure.
METHODS: An analytical observational before- and after study was conducted in adults with chronic anal fissure who underwent lateral internal sphincterotomy between 2020 and 2024. Quality of life changes were assessed using the EQ-5D-5L and VAS Score. In patients with preoperative faecal incontinence, changes were evaluated using the Faecal Incontinence Quality of Life Scale (FIQLS). FIQLS and VAS scores were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and EQ-5D-5L changes were analysed using the Paretian Classification of Health Change,Probability of Superiority and Health Profile Matrix.
RESULTS: A total of 332 patients were analysed, 52.1% male (173/332), with a median age of 43 years (IQR 34-55). According to the Paretian Classification of Health Change, 85.6% (279/326) showed an overall improvement in quality of life. All EQ-5D-5L domains demonstrated improvement after the procedure, with the greatest impact observed in the pain/discomfort domain (96.9%, 281/290). These findings were supported by probability of superiority values (mobility = 0.53; self-care = 0.54; usual activities = 0.64; pain/discomfort = 0.92; anxiety/depression = 0.58) and were reflected in the Health Profile Matrix. Preoperative faecal incontinence was present in 7.8% (26/332), with no significant changes in quality of life according to FIQLS.
CONCLUSION: Lateral internal sphincterotomy improved overall quality of life in patients with chronic anal fissure without worsening faecal incontinence related quality of life and was associated with symptom resolution.

articles.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Bupropion for Smoking Cessation During Pregnancy: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Habib GR, Ramanathan P, Garas G et al.
articles.abstract: Smoking during pregnancy is associated with adverse maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes. Although behavioral counseling remains first-line treatment, pharmacotherapy may be considered when counseling alone is insufficient. This scoping review mapped the available evidence on the safety and effectiveness of bupropion for smoking cessation during pregnancy. The review was conducted according to Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, the Cochrane Library, PsycINFO, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched without date restrictions for English-language studies evaluating bupropion for smoking cessation during pregnancy. Two reviewers independently screened records, and the review team extracted data on smoking cessation, maternal safety, and fetal or neonatal outcomes. Of 599 records identified, 13 sources of evidence met the inclusion criteria. Maternal and fetal safety findings were generally reassuring, with no consistent increase in maternal adverse events, major congenital malformations, preterm birth, impaired fetal growth, or serious neonatal morbidity. Evidence for smoking cessation effectiveness was mixed. Some studies reported improved short-term abstinence, reduced cigarette consumption or tobacco exposure, and improvement in craving or withdrawal symptoms, whereas other randomized trials found no significant improvement in sustained abstinence compared with placebo or counseling. Interpretation was limited by small samples, few bupropion-exposed pregnancies, heterogeneous designs and outcomes, and restrictive trial eligibility criteria. Current evidence is more reassuring regarding maternal, fetal, and neonatal safety than it is conclusive regarding smoking cessation effectiveness. Larger, adequately powered studies involving more representative pregnant populations are needed to clarify efficacy and detect uncommon adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Burnout in Gastrointestinal Endoscopy.
articles.authors: Conti CB, O'Reilly SM, Martinez-Moreno B et al.
articles.abstract: Objectives Burnout is underinvestigated in endoscopy. Given the increasing complexity of endoscopic practice, understanding burnout is crucial to addressing the problem and finding possible risk and protective factors. Methods A survey with 38 questions was internationally distributed via professional networks and social media. The survey investigated demographic data, professional experience, mentorship, work-life balance, and burnout. Burnout' three symptoms were: feeling exhausted, feeling negative, and feeling emotionally drained. Individuals with all three symptoms were defined as burnout, whereas those having at least one symptom were defined as at risk of burnout. Univariate and multivariate statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS 30.0. Results Totally, 553 endoscopists from 48 countries responded (51% male). Overall, 31% of the endoscopists were classified as having burnout, whereas 42% were considered at risk. At multivariable analysis, the delay of planning to have a family due to career was independently associated with burnout, OR: 2.48 [1.59-2.88]. Protective factors against burnout were: working in Asia 0.59 [0.38-0.93] and having a supportive mentor 0.50 [0.30-0.82]. Conclusion One out of every three endoscopists who responded to the questionnaire possessed features of burnout and one out of every two is at risk of developing it. Delay in family planning was associated with burnout, whereas working in Asia and having a supportive mentor were protective. This results may allow targeting of supportive programs to reduce burnout.

articles.title: Knowledge Graphs for Cervical Cancer Across the Care Continuum: From Vaccination and Screening to Personalized Therapy.
articles.authors: Leng J, Wei W, Wen X et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related death among women worldwide, with a disproportionately high burden in low- and middle-income countries. Infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) is the central etiological factor. Although HPV vaccination and standardized screening can substantially reduce incidence and mortality, major bottlenecks persist in real-world settings, including inadequate coverage, loss to follow-up, data silos, and limited interpretability of algorithms. Knowledge graphs (KGs), characterized by their core "entity-relation" structure, can integrate electronic medical records, HPV genotyping, pathology/imaging, multi-omics, and public health data within a unified semantic framework, and provide traceable evidence chains and reasoning pathways to support clinical decision-making. KGs may become an important enabler. This review summarizes the potential mechanisms and application paradigms of KGs along the full continuum of cervical cancer prevention and care, including primary prevention (vaccination strategies and health education), screening and diagnosis (multimodal data integration, explainable AI, and clinical decision support systems, CDSS), as well as therapeutic decision-making and follow-up management (molecular subtyping, drug associations, and recurrence monitoring. We further highlight key challenges such as ontology standardization, cross-institutional interoperability, dynamic knowledge updating, and reliability of automated knowledge extraction. Future work should focus on establishing reusable, engineering-oriented pathways for the synergy of "KG + large language models (LLMs)/multimodal AI", the development of explainability evaluation metrics, privacy-compliant frameworks, and deployable solutions for primary care settings, in order to accelerate progress toward the global cervical cancer elimination goal.

articles.title: Trends, Risk Factors, and Future Burden of Female Breast Cancer in China and Other G20 Countries, 1990-2050: A Comparative Global Burden of Disease 2023 Analysis.
articles.authors: Dong X, Kang X, Wu Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study analyzes the burden of female breast cancer in China and other G20 countries from 1990 to 2023, characterizes its trends and risk factors, and projects the burden to 2050.
METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates, we evaluated age-standardized rates of incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), the mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR), and trends (estimated annual percentage change, EAPC); applied Das Gupta decomposition, sociodemographic index (SDI) gradient, attributable-risk, and socioeconomic-inequality analyses, with stratification by premenopausal (20-54 years) and postmenopausal (≥55 years) age groups; and used autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models to forecast to 2050.
RESULTS: In 2023, China's age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) was 31.6 per 100,000, the second lowest among G20 members (range: India 29.4 to France 114.6), yet China recorded the largest absolute burden (342,725 cases and 76,589 deaths). Between 1990 and 2023, China's age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR) declined far more rapidly than in the rest of the G20 (EAPC -1.92 vs -0.23), whereas its ASIR rose only modestly (EAPC 0.40 vs 1.05); China's MIR fell to the eighth lowest by 2023. Across members, SDI correlated positively with ASIR (r = 0.74) but inversely with MIR (r = -0.84). Decomposition attributed China's rising deaths chiefly to population aging, partly offset by declining age-specific rates. Rates in the postmenopausal age group exceeded those in the premenopausal age group in all 19 members. By 2050, China's ASIR is projected to remain broadly stable, while absolute cases rise by approximately 131%.
CONCLUSIONS: Across the G20, female breast-cancer burden is undergoing an epidemiological transition: absolute burden is rising as populations grow and age, while age-standardized mortality is declining in most members, with marked heterogeneity across the G20. The burden is shifting toward older women in the postmenopausal age group, while the mortality-to-incidence ratio remains higher in lower-SDI members. These patterns argue for G20-coordinated, equity-focused prevention and survival care.

articles.title: DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel reprograms the immuno-oxidative microenvironment to support stem cell-based cartilage repair in osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Yu H, Hu Z, Tan Q et al.
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease, and stem cell therapy is often limited by a hostile joint microenvironment. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and damage-associated cell-free DNA (cfDNA) cooperatively drive innate immune activation, inflammatory macrophage polarization, and chondrogenic instability, forming an immuno-oxidative barrier to cartilage repair. Here, we developed a bioactive DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel (MNKB/HA) to remodel this niche and enhance BMSC-mediated cartilage repair. MNKB/HA integrates Mn3O4 nanozymes with Kartogenin (KGN)-engineered bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) in an injectable hyaluronic acid matrix. Mn3O4 exhibited SOD- and CAT-like activities, scavenging O2·-, H2O2, and ·OH, while efficiently adsorbing cfDNA and CpG-ODN to suppress TLR9/MyD88 signaling and M1 polarization and promote M2 polarization. In vitro, 10 μg/mL Mn3O4 was cytocompatible, protected BMSCs and chondrocytes from H2O2-induced apoptosis, and reshaped inflammatory secretion, with IL-10 increased 8.3-fold and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β reduced. KGN stabilized the chondrogenic phenotype (SOX9, COL Ⅱ, ACAN), while its combination with Mn3O4 synergistically enhanced chondrogenic stability under oxidative/inflammatory stress. In rat OA, intra-articular MNKB/HA reduced OARSI scores, restored COL II and ACAN, decreased MMP13, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and attenuated synovitis and osteophytes. MNKB/HA also reduced synovial cfDNA, weakened TLR9 signaling, promoted M2 polarization, and showed intra-articular retention for at least 10 days without notable systemic toxicity. Thus, MNKB/HA remodels the immuno-oxidative niche through synergistic ROS scavenging and cfDNA adsorption, providing a strategy for stem cell-mediated cartilage repair in OA.

articles.title: Screening for asthma among women referred for fertility treatment using a symptom questionnaire and fractional exhaled nitric oxide.
articles.authors: Miller ON, Hansen AV, Tidemandsen C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Asthma, a highly prevalent disorder among women of reproductive age, is associated with infertility and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Well-controlled asthma likely improves fertility and pregnancy outcomes, yet asthma is underdiagnosed. Therefore, we evaluated the value of the 'Life Quality Test (LQT)' from the American College of Asthma, Allergy and Immunology and fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) as a screening tool for current asthma among women referred for fertility treatment, as they may benefit from further assessment.
METHODS: A cross-sectional observational study was set up within the PRO-ART study. Women referred for fertility treatment at four Danish hospitals completed the LQT-survey. Those with affirmative responses were invited for a screening visit with spirometry, bronchial provocation, and FeNO measurement. Asthma diagnosis was based on bronchial provocation. Associations between asthma, FeNO, and LQT-scores were assessed using logistic regression. A grid-search algorithm identified thresholds for an effective screening tool.
RESULTS: Of 188 women screened, 119 (63.3%) had asthma, of whom 47 (39.4%) had no previous asthma diagnosis. FeNO alone was weakly predictive (OR 1.04, p = 0.036), while LQT-scores were stronger predictors for asthma (OR 1.40, p < 0.001). Combined, FeNO and LQT-scores revealed good predictive value (AUC = 0.82). A screening algorithm with combined criteria of LQT ≥ 7, FeNO ≥ 25 ppb, or 5 ≤ LQT < 7 with FeNO 12-25 ppb achieved 87.9% sensitivity and 55.4% specificity.
CONCLUSION: Undiagnosed asthma is common among women referred for fertility treatment. Combining FeNO and LQT-score provides a feasible, non-invasive screening method for probable asthma, warranting validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Diagnostic Utility of FNAC in Cutaneous Adnexal Tumors: A Cytohistomorphological Correlation in 21 Cases.
articles.authors: Shukla P, Singh S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skin adnexal tumors (SATs) are uncommon neoplasms showing differentiation toward hair follicles, sebaceous glands, or sweat glands. Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) offers a rapid, minimally invasive diagnostic approach, though histopathology remains the gold standard.
AIM: To correlate cytological features with histopathological findings in SATs.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A prospective study was conducted over 18 months (July 2022-December 2023) in the Department of Pathology of a tertiary health care center. Twenty-one cases with both FNAC and histopathology were included. FNAC smears were stained with hematoxylin & eosin, Papanicolaou, and May-Grünwald-Giemsa. Biopsy specimens were processed and examined histologically. Special stains and immunohistochemistry were used when necessary. Cytohistological correlation was classified as complete, partial, or absent.
RESULTS: Of 517 skin biopsies, 29 were diagnosed as SATs on histopathology. The FNAC correlation was available in 21 cases only, and so these cases were included in the study. Nineteen were benign (90.5%), and two were malignant (9.5%). The group in their 20s was the most commonly affected (33%). Males outnumbered females (2:1). The head and neck region was the most common site. A complete correlation was observed in 42.8% of cases, partial correlation in 23.8%, and no correlation in 33.4%. Inadequate smears and overlapping morphology contributed to diagnostic discrepancies.
CONCLUSION: FNAC, although limited in some cases, is valuable in differentiating benign from malignant cutaneous nodules. A clinico-cytohistological approach improves diagnostic accuracy and guides appropriate management.

articles.title: Two-Dimensional Plot of the Image Analysis of Ovarian Tumor Peritoneal Cytology Specimens to Distinguish Malignant from Negative Cases.
articles.authors: Konno M, Kobayashi S, Shibanuma R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE AND METHODS: Computer-assisted image analysis (CAIA) was used to analyze Papanicolaou-stained peritoneal cytology specimens from 142 patients with ovarian tumors. A two-dimensional plot was then created with the area of the cell/cell cluster on the x-axis and the maximum value of the connected nuclear area within that cell/cell cluster on the y-axis, after which the patterns were classified.
RESULTS: Ovarian cancer positive cases displayed a predominantly vertical pattern (V-type) or a diagonal pattern (D-type) cell/cell cluster plots, whereas the majority of the negative cases showed a small cluster pattern (S-type) or a horizontal pattern (H-type). In suspicious cases, almost equal frequencies of V-, D-, and S-types were observed. We found that V- and D-type patterns in negative cases were attributed to the presence of clusters of mesothelial cells, lymphocytes, and histiocytes. However, the amount of cell clusters in the area where positive cells were distributed (positivity rate) was significantly lower in both negative and suspicious cases than in positive cases. Evaluating the plot pattern and positivity rate together allowed us to reliably distinguish between malignant and negative cases.
CONCLUSION: Although previous CAIA of cytological specimens has fundamentally focused on nuclear area, morphology, and color evaluation, our method of combining cell/cell cluster area and the connected nuclear area in two dimensions reflects a part of the algorithm used by humans in cytological diagnosis and can become a promising analytical method in the near future. This study highlights the importance of actively incorporating diagnostic indicators used by humans into CAIA.

articles.title: Macrophages and immunometabolism in diminished ovarian reserve: pathological features and therapeutic implications.
articles.authors: Li B, Zhang J, Wu Q et al.
articles.abstract: Diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) is a prevalent reproductive endocrine disorder that significantly impairs female fertility. While traditional research has emphasized intrinsic oocyte defects, growing evidence highlights the ovarian immune microenvironment-specifically macrophages-as a critical regulator of follicular fate and reserve maintenance. Nevertheless, the mechanisms by which macrophage dysfunction drives DOR remain incompletely understood, and the interplay between chronic inflammation and macrophage metabolic reprogramming has yet to be systematically elucidated. This narrative review synthesizes literature from immunology, metabolism, and reproductive medicine, framing current evidence as established findings, putative mechanisms, and emerging hypotheses. The key findings are threefold: 1) macrophage polarization imbalance, which is marked by sustained M1 activation and impaired M2 function, constitutes a core pathological feature of DOR; 2) this imbalance is driven by metabolic reprogramming-specifically, metabolic inflexibility in M1 (persistent glycolytic commitment) and suppressed oxidative phosphorylation in M2-which links inflammaging to ovarian fibrosis and follicular depletion; and 3) pharmacological modulation of macrophage immunometabolism (e.g., AMPK/PPARγ activators, LXR agonists, and itaconate) and engineered delivery platforms (e.g., exosomes and targeted nanocarriers) hold preclinical promise. This review establishes an "immunometabolic axis" framework that integrates macrophage polarization, metabolic dysregulation, and ovarian reserve loss, advancing the understanding of DOR pathogenesis and informing precision interventions.

articles.title: Endometrial cancer molecular classification: research advances and clinical application.
articles.authors: Liu Y, Li Y, Zhang L
articles.abstract: As research in molecular biology continues to advance, the classification of endometrial cancer has gradually shifted from traditional histology toward risk stratification based on the integration of molecular subtyping with clinicopathologic factors. Molecular subtyping has not only transformed our understanding of the biological heterogeneity of endometrial cancer but also provided new evidence for prognostic assessment and treatment selection. However, the maturity of clinical evidence and the translational therapeutic value vary across molecular subtypes. This review systematically summarizes the molecular characteristics and clinical significance of the POLE ultramutated(POLE-mut)subtype, mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) subtype, p53 abnormal (p53-abn) subtype, and no specific molecular profile (NSMP) subtype, with a focus on evaluating whether different molecular features can be further translated from risk stratification into specific treatment decisions. Centering on key issues such as de-escalated therapy for the POLE-mut subtype, the predictive value of immunotherapy for the dMMR subtype, intensified therapy for the p53-abn subtype, and further risk stratification of the NSMP subtype, this review analyzes the clinical basis and limitations of existing evidence and further discusses the challenges that tumors with multiple molecular features pose for classification and treatment decision making. Building on this, the paper compares how major international guidelines integrate molecular information with clinical and pathologic factors and analyzes real world implementation barriers such as testing standardization, result interpretation, and healthcare accessibility. Finally, it outlines the potential value of emerging technologies, including liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence, and multiomics, in dynamic risk assessment and precision therapy. This review aims to trace the continuum of evidence from molecular discovery to clinical action, clarifying which clinical decisions can be supported by existing molecular markers and identifying questions that current evidence cannot yet answer, thereby providing guidance for the precise application and clinical translation of molecular subtyping in endometrial cancer.

articles.title: The cGAS-STING pathway in ovarian cancer: from genomic instability to immunotherapeutic vulnerability.
articles.authors: Chen HH, Ni FX, Huang DH et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, a status largely attributable to late-stage diagnosis and inevitable chemoresistance. The cGAS-STING pathway, a cornerstone of innate immune surveillance, has emerged as a critical nexus linking genomic instability to antitumor immunity-a connection of particular relevance in ovarian cancer, where chromosomal instability is a defining hallmark. This review synthesizes current understanding of the cGAS-STING pathway in ovarian cancer, spanning molecular mechanisms to translational opportunities. We delineate the dualistic nature of STING signaling, which orchestrate robust T cell-mediated antitumor immunity under certain conditions yet paradoxically foster immunosuppression and tumor progression in others. Particular emphasis is placed on the intricate interplay between DNA damage repair deficiencies-especially in BRCA1/2 and homologous recombination-and STING-dependent immune activation, which forms the mechanistic basis for the immunomodulatory effects of PARP inhibitors. We critically examine the TME, where CAFs and myeloid cells integrate STING signals to either potentiate or constrain antitumor immunity. The landscape of STING-modulating therapeutic strategies is surveyed, encompassing direct agonists, nanoparticle-based delivery platforms, and rational combinations with immune checkpoint blockade and DNA-damaging agents. Finally, we identify key unresolved questions, including the need for predictive biomarkers, strategies to overcome resistance, and the challenge of balancing therapeutic efficacy against potential toxicities. By integrating recent discoveries with established paradigms and explicitly addressing the "double-edged sword" duality of STING signaling, the stromal response, and a proposed roadmap for biomarker-guided therapeutic development, this review aims to provide a framework that distinguishes itself from prior comprehensive reviews by integrating recent discoveries with established paradigms and explicitly addressing the 'double-edged sword' duality of STING signaling, the stromal response, and a proposed roadmap for biomarker-guided therapeutic development.

articles.title: Recurrent implantation failure: a registry-corroborated, age-stratified definition and pragmatic five-tiered management algorithm.
articles.authors: Elzeiny H, Quaas AM, Bielfeld AP et al.
articles.abstract: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) remains a significant challenge in reproductive medicine, imposing substantial emotional, clinical, and financial burden on affected couples. RIF is generally defined as failure to achieve pregnancy after multiple transfers of good-quality embryos, yet progress in the field has been constrained by the absence of a universally accepted definition and by the inherent complexity of investigating the embryo-endometrial interface. Recent evidence has prompted a reappraisal of the factors contributing to RIF, distinguishing it from the mechanistically distinct entity of embryo-intrinsic failure (recurrent embryo arrest and poor embryo development). This narrative review synthesises epidemiological data, evaluates the evidence base for available diagnostic modalities, and appraises current management strategies, including the controversies surrounding adjunctive treatments. We propose a registry-corroborated, age-stratified definition of RIF - the ABCDE framework - and a five-tiered, clinically applicable management algorithm that integrates the available evidence with expert recommendation to guide clinicians within a shared decision-making framework. Future directions include prospective multicentre validation, incorporation of artificial intelligence for risk prediction, and development of novel therapeutic approaches targeting the embryo-endometrial interface.

articles.title: Prevalence and spectrum of variants in homologous recombination repair genes in ovarian cancer in Latin America: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Vargas-Castellanos E, Santiago-Tovar N, Murcia-Soriano L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian cancer is a major cause of gynecologic cancer mortality worldwide, with disproportionately poor outcomes in Latin America (LATAM). Variants in homologous recombination repair genes, especially BRCA1/2, are predictive biomarkers for platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibitors. However, data on the prevalence and spectrum of homologous recombination repair variants in LATAM populations remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize the prevalence and spectrum of pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants in homologous recombination repair pathway genes among LATAM ovarian cancer patients and highlight clinical and research implications.
STUDY DESIGN: The review protocol was developed in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) and was registered in the international prospective register of systematic reviews (PROSPERO; registration number CRD420251019706). We systematically searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, LILACS, Cochrane, and Epistemonikos through April 2025. Eligible studies included LATAM ovarian cancer patients tested with multigene panels covering homologous recombination repair genes beyond BRCA1/2. Data extraction followed 2025 ACMG/AMP guidelines, and study quality was assessed with the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Pooled prevalence was estimated using random- and common-effects meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Eight studies published between 2017 and 2023, including 442 patients with ovarian cancer from Brazil, Argentina, Mexico, Chile, and Colombia, were included in the systematic review. Following variant curation and reclassification, 7 studies comprising 433 patients and 96 pathogenic/likely pathogenic homologous recombination repair variant carriers were retained for prevalence analysis, yielding a crude prevalence of 22.2%. Pathogenic variants predominated (91.7%), with BRCA1 (55.2%) and BRCA2 (40.6%) accounting for ∼96% of carriers. Non-BRCA homologous recombination repair variants (CHEK2, BARD1, and RAD51D) accounted for 4.2%. The pooled prevalence of germline pathogenic/likely pathogenic homologous recombination repair variants was 17% (95% CI, 9%-26%; I²=56.2%), increasing to 20% (95% CI, 16%-23%; I²=0%) after sensitivity analysis excluding 2 micro-cohorts. Five recurrent variants were identified across multiple cohorts and countries. No study evaluated somatic homologous recombination repair variants or homologous recombination deficiency…

articles.title: Endocrine determinants of MASLD: mechanisms and therapeutic targets.
articles.authors: Chaturvedi R, Mathew A, Pradhan A et al.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately 30% of adults worldwide, yet is still framed largely as a hepatological disorder despite being driven substantially by endocrine and metabolic dysfunction. This review proposes a unified endocrine framework organised around seven hormonal axes, presenting each in terms of molecular pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and therapeutic implications. Insulin resistance is the central driver, coupling chronic caloric excess to hepatic de novo lipogenesis through selective hepatic insulin resistance, although genetic variants in PNPLA3 and TM6SF2 can uncouple steatosis from metabolic risk. Adipose tissue dysfunction contributes through adipocyte senescence, adipokine imbalance, and inflammatory adipose-liver signalling. Reduced hepatic thyroid hormone sensitivity, even in euthyroid individuals, predicts steatosis and fibrosis and underpins the first approved liver-directed therapy. Gonadal steroids exert sexually dimorphic effects, with testosterone deficiency, menopausal oestrogen loss, and polycystic ovary syndrome representing distinct risk states. Glucocorticoid dysregulation is stage-dependent, shifting from enhanced hepatic cortisol clearance in steatosis to local amplification in steatohepatitis. The gut-liver-endocrine axis, encompassing incretin, bile acid, and fibroblast growth factor signalling, has proved the most therapeutically tractable. Reduced GH/IGF-1 signalling, whether from pituitary disease or obesity-induced functional suppression, promotes both steatosis and fibrogenesis. Biological sex and life-course influences spanning developmental programming and ageing further modify these determinants. Two agents, resmetirom and semaglutide, now have US FDA accelerated approval for noncirrhotic MASH with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis, supporting the principle that correcting axis-specific endocrine dysfunction can produce measurable hepatic benefit; however, both approvals are accelerated and await confirmatory outcome data, while others remain investigational. An endocrine framework offers both a coherent account of pathogenesis and a rational basis for biomarker-guided, phenotype-targeted therapy.

articles.title: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals in male reproductive health: exposure risks, reproductive toxicity and emerging perspectives.
articles.authors: Ma D, Yang Q, Guo J et al.
articles.abstract: Male reproductive health represents a growing global health challenge, and increasing evidence highlights the contribution of environmental exposures to declining male reproductive function. Endocrine-disrupting chemicals are widespread environmental contaminants that interfere with endocrine regulation and have been associated with impaired semen quality, hormonal imbalance and testicular dysfunction. Here, we summarize current advances in understanding EDC-induced male reproductive toxicity, focusing on major chemical classes, including bisphenols, phthalates, pesticides, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and heavy metals. We discuss the interconnected mechanisms underlying reproductive impairment, including disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, altered steroidogenesis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, blood-testis barrier disruption, immune dysregulation and epigenetic reprogramming. Importantly, emerging evidence from developmental origins of health and disease perspectives indicates that exposure during critical developmental windows may establish persistent molecular alterations, influencing reproductive outcomes across the life course. In addition, the metabolic effects of certain EDCs, including obesity and metabolic dysfunction, may further exacerbate male reproductive impairment. Given that human exposure occurs predominantly in the form of complex chemical mixtures, future research should integrate exposomics, multi-omics approaches and longitudinal cohorts to clarify causal relationships and identify susceptible populations. Such advances will be essential for developing precision environmental health strategies to preserve male reproductive function.

articles.title: Multimodal biomarkers for early detection and immunotherapy assessment in hepatocellular carcinoma: integrating liquid biopsy, AI-based imaging and tumor immune profiling.
articles.authors: Zhao Y, Chen X, Zhao H
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) commonly develops in chronically diseased liver and remains challenging because of late detection, heterogeneity, recurrence and limited hepatic reserve. Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based combinations improve outcomes in advanced HCC, but durable responses occur in only a subset of patients. This structured narrative review evaluates biomarkers by intended use: surveillance and early detection, pretreatment prognostic stratification, treatment selection, on-treatment monitoring, neoadjuvant response assessment and postoperative minimal residual disease (MRD) detection. Serum alpha-fetoprotein and clinical scores are accessible but largely reflect tumor burden, inflammation or liver function. Cell-free DNA methylation and fragmentomics provide early-detection and tissue-of-origin signals, while circulating tumor DNA tracks molecular burden and clonal evolution. Tissue and spatial profiling clarify immune responsiveness and resistance, whereas radiomics and deep learning noninvasively assess whole-tumor and peritumoral heterogeneity. These modalities are complementary but require distinct evidence standards. Most early-detection studies use case-control or enriched cohorts, and most immunotherapy associations are retrospective, prognostic or monitoring-related. No biomarker yet supports routine selection among ICI regimens. Unlike modality-specific summaries, this review aligns each biomarker with a defined clinical decision and evidentiary category and proposes a longitudinal framework integrating baseline blood, imaging and tissue features with on-treatment dynamics, preoperative reassessment and postoperative molecular surveillance. Clinical translation requires standardized assays, representative multicenter cohorts, locked external validation and biomarker-guided trials demonstrating value beyond established criteria.

articles.title: Interpretable machine learning prioritizes transcriptomic features associated with ferroptosis-mitochondrial permeability transition net activity states in cervical cancer.
articles.authors: Zhang H, Zhu Y, Shao W et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cervical carcinogenesis involves oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and altered non-apoptotic cell-death programs. Ferroptosis and mitochondrial permeability transition (MPT)-driven necrosis may share upstream stress-related transcriptional signals, but their joint pathway-state features in cervical cancer remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We constructed a directionality-aware net pathway activity framework using evidence-audited ferroptosis-promoting, ferroptosis-inhibitory, MPT-promoting, and MPT-inhibitory gene sets in 304 TCGA-CESC primary tumors. The score was benchmarked against ssGSEA, GSVA, and PLAGE and evaluated in controlled simulations. For feature prioritization, score-defining genes were excluded from predictors and Elastic Net feature selection, XGBoost tuning, and model fitting were performed strictly within repeated nested cross-validation. Outer-test SHAP, model-sensitivity analysis, and a 200-permutation complete-pipeline test were used for interpretation and robustness assessment. External validation used GSE138080, GSE63514, GSE223804, and GSE151666.
RESULTS: CombinedNet showed moderate-to-high concordance with ssGSEA, GSVA, and PLAGE (Spearman rho = 0.735, 0.882, and 0.943, respectively), while 1,300 controlled simulations showed strong recovery of the latent promoter-minus-inhibitor balance across scenarios and effect sizes (mean rho = 0.944; mean sign-recovery accuracy = 0.902; mean standardized RMSE = 0.305). The leakage-resistant repeated nested-CV model yielded AUC = 0.780 (95% CI 0.766-0.795); a matched complete-pipeline permutation test gave empirical p = 0.005. Stability-weighted SHAP and perturbation prioritized CKMT1B and KLK13, whereas GNA13, PANX2, and all five sterol genes were not selected in any of 25 outer-fold models. The sterol genes retained modest score correlations but showed no model sensitivity. Across three lesion-progression cohorts, no pathway score remained associated with stage after FDR correction; in the cancer-only GSE151666 RNA-seq cohort, CombinedNet also showed no FIGO-stage trend.
CONCLUSION: This study supports directionality-aware transcriptomic scoring and a leakage-resistant feature-prioritization framework, but does not support GNA13/PANX2 or cholesterol-biosynthesis signals as stable model drivers or the composite score as a validated lesion-stage biomarker. The findings remain hypothesis-generating and require…

articles.title: Severity and Determinants of Anemia Among Adolescent Girls in Africa: A Multicountry and Multilevel Analysis of 25 Countries.
articles.authors: Ejigu BA, Begashaw GB, Tiruneh FN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anemia remains a major public health concern in Africa, with substantial health and developmental consequences. Adolescents, particularly girls, are at increased risk due to rapid growth, menstruation, and inadequate dietary intake. Identifying the severity and determinants of anemia among adolescent girls in Africa is crucial for developing appropriate interventions, yet evidence remains scarce.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the severity and determinants of anemia among adolescent girls in Africa using nationally representative data.
METHODS: Data were obtained from the most recent Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) of 25 African countries, including 41,662 adolescent girls aged 15-19 years. The severity of anemia was determined using descriptive statistics based on proportions. Anemia severity was modeled as a four-level ordinal outcome (none, mild, moderate, and severe) using survey-weighted multilevel ordinal (proportional-odds) logistic regression with a random intercept at the cluster level. Chi-square tests assessed initial associations, and adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported from the final model.
RESULTS: The overall magnitude of anemia among adolescent girls was 42.3% (95% CI: 41.96-44.20). In the multivariable analysis, factors significantly associated with lower odds of anemia included primary education (AOR = 0.84; 95% CI: 0.75-0.94), secondary and above education (AOR = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.75-0.98), rich and richer wealth status (AOR = 0.77; 95% CI: 0.65-0.91), employment (0.86; 95% CI: 0.78-0.94), hormonal contraceptive use (AOR = 0.44; 95% CI: 0.38-0.51), parity (0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.95), and normal and overweight/obese nutritional status (AOR = 0.84; 95% CI:0.73-0.97 and AOR = 0.75; 95% CI: 0.62-0.91), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Anemia affects a substantial proportion of adolescent girls in Africa and is influenced by educational, economic, reproductive, and nutritional factors. Interventions should focus on keeping girls in school, encouraging employment opportunities, and maintaining healthy bodyweight. Addressing these determinants is vital for improving adolescent girls' health and achieving sustainable development goals.

articles.title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus among 15,224 gynecological outpatients in Xuzhou, China, during 2023-2025.
articles.authors: Chai S, Hu L, Fan W et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated HPV prevalence and genotype distribution among gynecological outpatients at the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University, aiming to inform region-specific cervical cancer prevention strategies.
METHODS: We determined the HPV subtypes by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and analyzed the HPV prevalence, genotype distribution in 15,224 gynecological outpatients by age group and year.
RESULTS: Among the 15,224 outpatients, 4,884 (32.08%) tested positive for HPV, with single high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) infection being the predominant pattern (16.48%).
