The top five HR-HPV genotypes were HPV52 (5.58%), 16 (4.93%), 58 (4.49%), 53 (3.54%), and 56 (2.51%). The top three low-risk HPV (LR-HPV) genotypes were HPV42 (3.30%), 81 (2.16%), and 43 (1.76%). From 2023 to 2025, the overall HPV prevalence among this study population exhibited a significant increasing trend, rising from 27.57 to 36.63% (p(linear by linear) < 0.001). Overall HPV prevalence differed significantly across age groups (p < 0.001), exhibiting a bimodal distribution, with the highest rate in the ≤24 years group (42.30%), followed by the 55-64 years group (37.29%) and the ≥65 years group (36.43%), and the lowest in the 25-34 years group (29.05%). Across age groups, the top five HR-HPV genotypes varied slightly but consistently included HPV52, 16, 58, 53, and 56. For LR-HPV infections, the top three genotypes were HPV6, 42, and 11 in the ≤24 years group, whereas HPV42, 81, and 43 ranked as the top three in all other age groups.
CONCLUSION: The prevalence of HPV infection among women attending gynecological outpatient clinics of the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University is relatively high and has demonstrated an increasing trend over the study period. Adolescents and middle-aged and older women exhibit higher HPV prevalence. The predominant genotypes are HR-HPV52, 16, 58, 53, and 56, as well as LR-HPV42, 81, and 43. In addition to strengthening universal health education, the observed age-specific distribution suggests that young women and middle-aged and older women may be important target groups for future prevention strategies. Furthermore, the high prevalence of non-vaccine-covered genotypes (HPV53, 56, 42, 81, and 43) warrants continued surveillance and further investigation of their clinical significance, although these implications should be considered preliminary.

articles.title: Unsaturated fatty acids as immunometabolic modulators in high-risk pregnancies: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and translational perspectives.
articles.authors: Olinto da Fonseca E, Carvalho de Faria J, Santos RP et al.
articles.abstract: High-risk pregnancies (HRPs) are characterized by the convergence of metabolic dysfunction, chronic low-grade inflammation, and placental maladaptation, leading to increased maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. Emerging evidence indicates that these conditions are driven by a tightly integrated immunometabolic axis, in which metabolic stress activates innate immune pathways, amplifying systemic and placental inflammation. Unsaturated fatty acids (UFAs), including monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), have gained attention as key modulators of this axis. Omega-3 PUFAs, such as eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), influence membrane composition, lipid mediator synthesis, and intracellular signaling pathways involved in inflammation and metabolism. At the cellular level, these fatty acids attenuate pro-inflammatory signaling through nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), modulate inflammasome activation, improve mitochondrial function, and promote the production of specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs), thereby facilitating the resolution of inflammation. Clinical evidence from observational studies, randomized controlled trials, and meta-analyses supports the role for omega-3 supplementation in reducing the risk of preterm birth, particularly among women with low baseline DHA status. However, findings for other outcomes, including preeclampsia and gestational diabetes, remain heterogeneous, likely reflecting variability in study design, baseline nutritional status, dosage, and timing of intervention. Although several studies support a beneficial role of omega-3 supplementation, the overall clinical evidence remains heterogeneous. While reductions in preterm birth are consistently observed, findings for other outcomes, such as preeclampsia and gestational diabetes, are inconsistent across randomized controlled trials. Differences in study design, baseline nutritional status, timing, dosage, and adherence likely contribute to these discrepancies. Importantly, several well-conducted trials have reported null effects, highlighting the need for cautious interpretation and more targeted approaches. This review synthesizes current evidence on the immunometabolic mechanisms underlying HRPs and highlights UFAs as biologically plausible and clinically relevant modulators. It focuses on the importance of precision nutrition approaches that incorporate baseline nutritional assessment and biomarker-guided stratification…

articles.title: AKNA serves as a prognostic biomarker and restrains endometrial cancer progression via STING activation and macrophage reprogramming.
articles.authors: Tu Y, Xu L, Tian C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: AKNA, an AT-hook transcription factor, plays a critical role in cancer development. However, its prognostic value and biological function in endometrial cancer (EC) remain unclear.
METHODS: To systematically investigate AKNA in EC, we integrated multi-omics data (The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx), and single-cell transcriptomics), dual independent clinical cohorts (TCGA-UCEC dataset and two institutional cohorts), and in vitro/in vivo experimental models. Immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR and Western blotting were used for expression validation. Functional assays, including lentiviral-mediated AKNA knockdown/overexpression, CCK-8, scratch-wound, Transwell, flow cytometry, and colony formation assays were conducted to assess the effects of AKNA modulation on proliferation, migration, invasion, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, chemosensitivity and macrophage polarization. Mechanistically, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) sequencing (ChIP-seq), ChIP-qPCR, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were employed to define the transcriptional regulation of stimulator of interferon genes (STING) by AKNA. A prognostic nomogram integrating AKNA expression with clinicopathological features was developed and externally validated in independent cohorts.
RESULTS: AKNA was significantly downregulated in EC tissues compared with normal endometrium, which was associated with advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage, aggressive histological subtypes, and poor prognosis. AKNA knockdown promoted EC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, while enhancing M2 macrophage polarization and reducing sensitivity to paclitaxel and potentially compromising anti-tumor innate immunity. Conversely, AKNA overexpression or STING activation by cyclic GMP-AMP reversed these malignant phenotypes. Mechanistically, AKNA directly bound to the STING promoter and transcriptionally activated STING, thereby inducing TANK-binding kinase 1 and interferon regulatory factor 3 phosphorylation. The nomogram combining AKNA with clinicopathological features demonstrated high accuracy in predicting EC recurrence and outperformed single-variable models in both training and validation cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: AKNA deficiency promotes EC progression by transcriptionally suppressing STING and driving M2 macrophage polarization. AKNA serves as a robust prognostic biomarker and predictive indicator for…

articles.title: Connecting gut microbiome composition to symptom severity and host genetics in endometriosis.
articles.authors: Nardone GG, Rosso LE, Santin A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis (EM) is a multifactorial, estrogen-dependent inflammatory disease characterized by high clinical variability. Growing evidence is highlighting the role of gut microbiome dysbiosis in EM pathophysiology; however, associations between microbiome, symptom severity, and host genetics remain poorly characterized. Extra-oral taste receptor genes (TGs), expressed in both the gastrointestinal and female reproductive systems, may represent novel mediators of gut-reproductive tract axis crosstalk.
METHODS: A total of 50 women with surgically confirmed EM were deeply clinically characterized, including the evaluation of EM-symptoms and their severity. Microbiome profiles were obtained by 16S rRNA gene sequencing of rectal swabs. Genetic variants within four TGs (TAS2R3, TAS2R4, TAS2R5, and TAS2R14) were assessed using SNP-array genotyping. Microbiome composition was investigated through the evaluation of alpha and beta diversity, as well as enterotype classification analyses. Associations between EM-related features, bacterial taxa and TG-SNPs were investigated using regression models.
RESULTS: Three distinct gut microbiome community types were identified, dominated by Bacteroides, Prevotella, and Escherichia-Shigella. While microbiome composition did not differ significantly across EM stages, beta diversity was associated with dysmenorrhea (R2 = 0.13) and disease stage (R2 = 0.12). Regarding TGs, SNPs within TAS2R14 gene showed significant associations with alpha and beta diversity indices. Reduced abundance of short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa, including members of the Lachnospiraceae and Ruminococcaceae families, was associated with dysmenorrhea, whereas increased abundance of Prevotella and Mobiluncus with dysuria and infertility, respectively. Finally, an increased premenstrual pain severity was associated with a reduced relative abundance of taxa within the order Burkholderiales (β = -2.265) and the family Sutterellaceae (β = -1.563); high postmenstrual pain severity was associated with a lower abundance of Bifidobacteriales (β = -4.932) and Bifidobacteriaceae (β = -4.134).
CONCLUSION: This case-only study elucidated the complex relationship between gut microbiome composition, EM-related symptoms, and host genetic variation. In particular, extra-oral taste receptor genes emerged as novel risk factors to host-microbiome interactions, supporting their potential role in the microbiota-endometriosis axis and opening new perspectives…

articles.title: Platform-based manufacturing of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes derived from different solid tumor types.
articles.authors: Lievense J, Tas L, van Zon M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In adoptive cell therapy with tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), TILs are isolated and expanded ex vivo from an autologous tumor lesion. TIL therapy, comprising preparative lymphodepleting chemotherapy, TIL infusion, and post-infusion supportive interleukin-2 (IL-2) administration, has demonstrated efficacy in patients with metastatic melanoma. Interest in extending TIL therapy to other solid tumors is growing, and a tumor-agnostic manufacturing platform would allow first-in-human trials to be launched rapidly in these indications.
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated whether a manufacturing process and control strategy developed for metastatic melanoma-derived TILs could be adapted into a tumor-agnostic platform for the generation of TILs from different solid tumor types, referred to as NTU101.
METHODS: The feasibility of generating TILs from endometrial carcinoma (ENDC, n=9), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC, n=9), and penile cancer (PENC, n=10) lesions was assessed during process development (PD) runs using predefined quality criteria. Throughout PD runs, flow cytometry was used to characterize cells. When available, autologous tumor digest was used to assess the tumor-reactive potential of TILs. Based on PD experience, adjusted quality criteria were applied to manufacture one full-scale GMP NTU101-drug product (DP) per tumor type.
RESULTS: Overall, 89% (n=25/28) of PD NTU101-DPs manufactured met the predefined quality criteria, containing at least 0.5×10^9 and 90% viable CD45+CD3+ cells, less than 1.0% of cellular impurities (viable CD45- and CD19+ cells), and a potency of more than 1.0×10^3 pg/mL IFN-γ secretion upon CD3/CD28-polymer stimulation. Across the tumor types, PD NTU101-DPs had comparable T-cell subset and differentiation state compositions. In vitro tumor-reactive potential was detected in 82% of tested NTU101-DPs (ENDC: 71%, n=5/7; NSCLC: 80%, n= 4/5; and PENC: 100%, n=5/5), although the level of reactivity will need to be confirmed with a more in-depth assay. One GMP NTU101-DP was then manufactured from each tumor type, and all three met NTU101's quality criteria.
CONCLUSION: The NTU101 platform produced comparable NTU101-DPs from three solid tumor types beyond melanoma, with in vitro tumor-reactive potential for some batches. This platform can be applied in TIL therapy clinical trials to generate ENDC-, NSCLC-, and PENC-derived TILs, and possibly other solid tumor types.

articles.title: Management of Hypertension in Pregnancy: Policy Options for Health Care Service Decision-Makers.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular and thoracic research
articles.authors: Mirghafourvand M, Doshmangir L, Alizadeh-Dibazari Z
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypertensive disorders are a major cause of maternal mortality, and early detection can reduce risks for mothers and infants. Implementing evidence based, context appropriate strategies may improve outcomes. This study aimed to propose policy options to strengthen monitoring and management of hypertension in pregnancy.
METHODS: The study consisted of two phases. First, a scoping review synthesized global strategies for improving hypertension management during pregnancy. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, SID, and Google Scholar without time limits, restricted to English and Persian studies. Based on the findings, policy options were developed. In the second phase, 13 experts evaluated these options across five criteria-population benefit, cost/economics, ethics/equity, feasibility, and constituency acceptance-using a five point Likert scale. The top options were further analyzed for advantages, disadvantages, and implementation needs.
RESULTS: From 2,253 identified records, 14 studies informed five policy options: (a) an educational video package on hypertension and preventive self‑care; (b) a maternal mobile application for hypertension management; (c) remote self‑monitoring of blood pressure; (d) a smart multimodal management system; and (e) ambulatory monitoring with Holter devices. Experts ranked the educational video package highest overall and highest for cost/economic, ethics/equity, and feasibility, the mobile application highest for constituency acceptance, and remote blood pressure monitoring highest for population benefit.
CONCLUSION: Integrating global evidence with expert input yielded three priority policy options: educational video‑based training, a maternal hypertension management app, and remote self‑monitoring of blood pressure. These strategies emphasize empowerment and improved self‑management for pregnant women.

articles.title: Pregnancy outcome documentation in low-resource settings: a multi-country study.
articles.authors: Hucko A, Prauseová J, Parker EPK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As the maternal vaccine portfolio expands, reliable documentation of adverse events of special interest (AESI) is critical for safety surveillance in low- and middle-income countries (LMIC). However, such documentation is often not easily available, even prior to introduction of new vaccines, and background rates are therefore lacking.
METHODS: Nested within a retrospective multisite analysis of routine maternal health data from six LMICs (Bangladesh, The Gambia, Nepal, Nigeria, Tanzania, and Uganda) from 2019 to 2022, we extracted aggregated monthly counts of vaccination-relevant pregnancy AESI- preterm birth, stillbirth, congenital malformations, neonatal death, and maternal death- and assessed their availability, completeness, and consistency using descriptive analyses. Outcome rates were compared with published country-specific background estimates.
FINDINGS: Among 123,867 pregnancies across 27 clinics (totaling 1277 clinic-months) in six LMICs, substantial limitations in pregnancy outcome recording were identified. AESI recording was predominantly paper-based (clinic registers in 92.6% of clinics, maternal-held documents in 51.9%); with use of digital systems in only 14.8% of clinics. Congenital malformations and preterm subcategories were absent in seven of 27 clinics (25.9%). Documentation completeness ranged from 65.2% to 68.9% for preterm birth categories to 96.8% to 98.4% for mortality outcomes (stillbirths, neonatal and maternal deaths). Considerable inter-clinic variability was noted, and observed rates diverged substantially from national background estimates for several pregnancy outcomes.
INTERPRETATION: Substantial gaps in documentation of routine clinical data across LMIC underscore the need for linked, standardized, and digital maternal and neonatal outcome documentation to support the safe introduction and surveillance of vaccines administered during pregnancy.

articles.title: Integrated pituitary adaptations to the low estrogen state.
articles.authors: Miles TK, Odle AK, Herdman AK et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Estrogen's broad trophic effects on anterior pituitary function are not fully understood. The compound 4-vinyl cyclohexene diepoxide (VCD) induces early ovarian failure and reduced E2 production, which may differentially affect anterior pituitary cells. We recently identified transcriptomic changes in pituitary gonadotropes at the single-cell level in females treated with VCD for 20 days, which were acyclic, with low serum estradiol (E2) levels and 8-12-fold increases in gonadotropins 138 days later.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We tested vehicle-control and VCD-treated female mice in metabolic cages and assayed serum hormone levels by EIA, and pituitary cell transcripts by qRT-PCR and single-cell RNA-seq.
RESULTS: VCD-treated mice showed normal metabolic health. Compared with controls, VCD-treated females exhibited a 5-fold elevation in serum pituitary thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels and near-normal thyroid hormone levels. Pituitary Tshb mRNA levels were reduced, and pituitary Gh, Prl, and Pomc mRNA levels were unchanged. Serum growth hormone (GH) levels were higher in VCD-treated mice than in controls 62 days after the start of treatment (perimenopause) and then reduced to control levels after 118-138 days. Ingenuity Pathway Analyses (IPA) of upregulated differentially expressed gene (DEG) transcripts predicted activation of G protein-mediated signaling pathways in one scRNA-seq somatotrope subcluster and in the thyrotrope and lactotrope clusters. In contrast, downregulated DEGs in corticotropes and the remaining two somatotrope clusters predicted downregulation of critical signaling pathways.
DISCUSSION: The unchanged pituitary Gh, Prl, and Pomc mRNA levels correlated with unchanged serum levels. The interim rise in serum GH 62 days after treatment agrees with reports of perimenopausal responses due to estrogen spikes. Reduced pituitary Tshb correlates with the recently reported reduced expression in gonadotropes. IPA analysis of upregulated DEGs in thyrotrope clusters predicted the activation of canonical signaling pathways that support elevated serum TSH levels. The near-normal thyroid hormone levels suggest subclinical hypothyroidism in menopausal women. Downregulated DEGs in corticotropes and in two somatotrope subclusters predicted compromised stress and metabolic responses. Finally, reduced multihormone gene expression suggested compromised plasticity in a low-estrogen environment. These different responses to a sustained…

articles.title: Treatment decisions, not patient demographics, predict a positive pregnancy test after autologous IVF: a retrospective cohort study from northern India.
articles.authors: Kamath R, Rodrigues G, Singh S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infertility affects about one in six people worldwide over a lifetime, and in vitro fertilisation (IVF) is the mainstay of treatment for many of them. In India most IVF is delivered in private clinics and paid for out of pocket. The question is which factors determine whether an IVF cycle produces a pregnancy: the characteristics a patient arrives with, or the treatment decisions made once she is there.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 288 women who underwent IVF at a private fertility centre in Faridabad, Haryana, between April 2023 and October 2024. One record was analysed per woman, taken from her most recent cycle. The outcome was a positive serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG) test, the last outcome routinely documented at the centre. Donor-oocyte (recipient) cycles were analysed separately from autologous cycles, because success in a donor cycle depends on the donor rather than on the patient. Categorical associations were tested using Fisher's exact test. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable binomial logistic regression.
RESULTS: Seventy-seven cycles (26.7%) used donor oocytes and 211 (73.3%) were autologous. The positive beta-hCG rate was 70.6% in autologous cycles and 54.5% in donor cycles (p = 0.016). Within autologous cycles, two treatment decisions were associated with the outcome: intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) versus conventional IVF (76.0% versus 46.2%, p < 0.001) and frozen versus fresh embryo transfer (74.9% versus 51.3%, p = 0.006). No demographic characteristic was associated with the outcome. After adjustment (N = 210), conventional IVF carried lower odds than ICSI (adjusted odds ratio 0.16, 95% CI 0.06-0.42, p < 0.001) and frozen transfer higher odds than fresh (adjusted odds ratio 2.80, 95% CI 1.30-6.04, p = 0.009). Oocyte yield was marginally associated (adjusted odds ratio 1.11 per oocyte, 95% CI 1.00-1.22, p = 0.041). In absolute terms, ICSI corresponded to 32.5 percentage points and frozen transfer to 18.5 percentage points. Age was not associated with the outcome, although autologous cycles spanned only 22-42 years and the study was underpowered to detect age effects.
CONCLUSION: In autologous cycles at this centre, treatment decisions rather than patient demographics predicted a positive pregnancy test. The cohort was socioeconomically narrow and drawn from a single private centre. The absence of demographic effects should therefore not be read as…

articles.title: A Review of Guidelines for the Use of Tranexamic Acid in the Management of Postpartum Hemorrhage and Assessment of Associated Maternal Outcomes.
articles.authors: Shekhawat K, Ahuja A, Parekh R et al.
articles.abstract: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) remains a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality worldwide, requiring rapid recognition and coordinated hemostatic intervention. Tranexamic acid (trans-4-aminomethylcyclohexane-1-carboxylic acid; TXA), an antifibrinolytic agent that inhibits plasminogen-mediated fibrin degradation, has emerged as an important component of PPH management. Despite growing evidence supporting TXA, recommendations on its timing and placement within PPH treatment algorithms vary across major international guidelines. This narrative review examines the pharmacology, clinical indications, safety profile, and therapeutic role of TXA in PPH. It evaluates evidence supporting TXA in obstetric and non-obstetric hemorrhage, compares its role with other hemostatic therapies, and critically examines recommendations from major international and national organizations. It pays particular attention to differences in how these guidelines position TXA within PPH treatment pathways and integrate it with other first-response interventions. This review also considers uncertainties around prophylactic use, alternative hemostatic therapies, and variation in guideline implementation. Greater consistency in evidence-based recommendations may clarify TXA's role in contemporary PPH management while allowing flexibility for differences in healthcare settings and resources.

articles.title: Early prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus using deep learning applied to routinely collected clinical data.
articles.authors: Cubillos G, Monckeberg M, Illanes SE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in early pregnancy enables timely, targeted interventions to reduce risks for both the mother and fetus. We aimed to improve early GDM prediction and clinical risk stratification using a novel deep learning (DL) approach that transforms tabular clinical data into images using a genetic algorithm.
METHODS: A dataset of 1,611 pregnancies was used. The dataset contained routinely collected early-pregnancy data, including clinical measurements, blood tests, and medical history. A novel method to transform tabular data into images was applied to enable the use of deep learning models for GDM prediction. A genetic algorithm optimized the spatial arrangement of variables during image generation by determining their spatial positions. Interpretability was assessed using gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) to identify variables the model preferentially attended to for positive and negative predictions.
RESULTS: Multiple model configurations were evaluated by varying the spatial arrangement of variables within the transformation. Prioritizing high sensitivity, one model achieved an accuracy of 0.86, sensitivity of 0.82, specificity of 0.87, and an AUC-ROC of 0.83. Another model achieved an accuracy of 0.79, sensitivity of 0.92, specificity of 0.77, and an AUC-ROC of 0.85. Compared with previously published machine learning models using the same dataset, our approach demonstrated improved performance. Our best models increased specificity by an average of 13.93 percentage points compared with traditional ML models at matched sensitivity levels, thereby reducing false-positive classifications that may lead to additional clinical evaluation. Grad-CAM analysis revealed that attention patterns of the model aligned with established clinical risk factors for GDM, with first trimester fasting glycemia and parity preferentially attended for positive predictions and maternal weight for negative predictions.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that transforming tabular clinical data into image representations, optimized using a genetic algorithm, improves early GDM prediction. Representing tabular variables as images enables more effective application of DL models, which have demonstrated enhanced pattern recognition in image-based tasks compared with traditional machine learning methods. Performance improvements over state-of-the-art approaches were achieved. Accurate DL models can be developed…

articles.title: Dietary inflammatory index and gestational diabetes mellitus in a multicenter cross sectional study in Suzhou.
articles.authors: Wang C, Yang Y, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence linking dietary inflammatory potential with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) has been inconsistent. We examined this association in a multicenter cross-sectional study.
METHODS: Women attending three tertiary hospitals in Suzhou, China, from February to November 2025 completed a food-frequency questionnaire at 24 to 28 gestational weeks, recalling the preceding three months. A 26-parameter Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) was calculated, and GDM was defined from 75-g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) values. Logistic regression adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, obstetric, behavioral, and hospital covariates.
RESULTS: The primary analysis included 1,071 women after removal of 23 exact duplicate records; 225 (21.0%) had GDM. Mean age was 29.28 years (SD 4.17), prepregnancy body mass index was 22.42 kg/m² (SD 3.28), and DII was 0.71 (SD 1.13). Each one-SD higher DII was associated with higher adjusted GDM odds (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.06 to 1.51; P = 0.011). The adjusted quartile trend was not significant (P = 0.162), and there was no evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.888). Among 803 women completing the questionnaire one to three days before OGTT, the estimate was attenuated and imprecise (OR 1.20, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.48).
CONCLUSION: Higher continuous DII was associated with GDM, but quartile and sensitivity analyses limited the consistency of the findings. Overlapping exposure and outcome windows and measurement limitations precluded causal or predictive interpretation.

articles.title: Long-term clinical outcomes in females with precocious puberty treated with gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogues.
articles.authors: Khawaja N, Karaki K, Ruba'i MK et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate long-term anthropometric, metabolic, reproductive, and bone mineral density (BMD) outcomes in girls with central precocious puberty (CPP) treated with Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone analogues (GnRHa).
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort with cross-sectional follow-up assessment, 82 of 265 eligible females (30.9%) with central precocious puberty or central hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis activation who had received GnRHa participated in long-term evaluation. Anthropometric outcomes, insulin sensitivity indices (HOMA-IR and QUICKI), hormonal profile, BMD, and reproductive outcomes including polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) were assessed. Analyses used available cases for each outcome; missing values were not imputed.
RESULTS: The mean age at final evaluation was 17.61 ± 4.3 years, and mean GnRHa treatment duration was 3.14 ± 1.9 years. Mean height at final follow-up was 159.85 ± 6.5 cm; the mean difference from baseline predicted adult height was 1.98 cm (95% CI, -0.37 to 4.34; P = 0.097). The distribution of BMI categories did not change significantly from baseline to final follow-up. Mean HOMA-IR and QUICKI were 3.76 ± 1.82 and 0.319 ± 0.025, respectively; among adults, 14/28 (50.0%) met each prespecified adult-derived threshold for reduced insulin sensitivity. PCOS was identified in 15/67 participants (22.4%). Mean lumbar and femoral BMD Z-scores were -0.25 ± 1.23 and -0.55 ± 1.03, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Among participants who completed long-term follow-up, attained height was comparable at the group level with predicted adult and mid-parental height, and mean BMD Z-scores were within age- and sex-referenced ranges. PCOS and PCOS-related features were observed, while insulin sensitivity indices were associated with adiposity. Because only 30.9% of eligible patients participated and there was no untreated comparison group, these findings describe the evaluated cohort and should not be interpreted as causal effects of GnRHa treatment.

articles.title: Effect of meso-and micro-level quality improvement interventions to improve intrapartum care and birth outcome in Nepal- stepped wedge cluster randomized trial.
articles.authors: Gurung R, Basnet O, Paudel P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-quality intrapartum care benefits from implementation of quality improvement (QI) interventions. However, scale-up of meso- and micro-level QI interventions to improve health facility performance have shown mixed results in Nepal.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effect of such interventions to intrapartum care and intrapartum mortality (intrapartum stillbirth and first day neonatal death) in public health facilities of Nepal.
STUDY DESIGN: A stepped-wedge cluster randomized design was applied to implement the SUSTAIN package, comprising meso- and micro-level QI interventions in 8 hospitals across all provinces of Nepal over a 21-month period. Each hospital had a 2-month window to introduce QI interventions in their governance and clinical processes. Women with gestational age ≥22 weeks were included with research teams established in each hospital to monitor mortality and health workers' performance. For each outcome, hospital-specific incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated by comparing event rates in the intervention period with those in the control period.
RESULTS: The study enrolled, 55,325 and 53,578 women were enrolled in the control and intervention periods, respectively. The SUSTAIN package resulted in a statistically non-significant reduction (16%) in intrapartum mortality at the hospital level (IRR 0.84 (95% CI: 0.66, 1.08)), while at the individual level there was also statistically non-significant lower odd (37%) of mortality (aOR: 0.63 (0.38, 1.04), P<.0001)). Improvement in intrapartum care were consistent in most of care indicators with adherence to hand-washing increased by 2.36 fold (IRR 2.36 (95% CI: 1.03, 5.39)), fetal heart-rate monitoring increased by 1.55 fold (IRR 1.55 (95% CI: 1.10, 2.17)), delayed cord clamping increased non-significantly by1.14 fold (IRR 1.14 (95% CI: 0.96, 1.35)), immediate skin-to-skin contact increased by 9.92 fold (IRR 9.92 (95% CI: 3.21, 30.64)), early breastfeeding increased by 4.09 fold (IRR 4.09 (95% CI: 2.07, 8.11)), and bag-and-mask within 1 minute increased by 3.30 fold (IRR 3.30 (95% CI: 2.02, 5.40).
CONCLUSION: A synergistic and multi-faceted QI package implementation can improve intrapartum care with a statistically non-significant reduction in intrapartum mortality even during the COVID-19 pandemic.
TRIAL: https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN16741720.

articles.title: Prospective evaluation of donor-derived cell-free DNA for noninvasive detection of acute rejection in an Asian heart transplant population.
articles.journal: Transplant international : official journal of the European Society for Organ Transplantation
articles.authors: Zheng S, Liu S, Zhu Z et al.
articles.abstract: Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) is the gold standard for diagnosing post-heart transplant acute rejection (AR) but is invasive. Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) is a promising noninvasive biomarker, yet thresholds for Asian recipients remain undefined. This prospective study enrolled 80 patients, with 299 dd-cfDNA specimens analyzed via a novel Chinese-developed next-generation sequencing assay targeting 48 Indel sites. A reference cohort (n = 42) established post-transplant dd-cfDNA kinetics, while a biopsy cohort (n = 41, 18 acute cellular rejection [ACR], 9 antibody-mediated rejection [AMR], 14 no rejection [NR]) paired with EMB evaluated diagnostic performance. dd-cfDNA peaked at week 1, with a stable trend emerging from week 4 and stable levels reached by week 8. AR patients had significantly higher dd-cfDNA levels than NR patients (0.87% vs. 0.23%, P < 0.001). The optimal composite AR threshold was 0.33% (AUC = 0.874, sensitivity 81.0%, specificity 85.7%). dd-cfDNA decreased post-therapy (P = 0.011) and showed an inverse association with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (P = 0.004). This study provides initial evidence for an assay- and cohort-specific dd-cfDNA threshold (0.33%) for AR detection in Chinese recipients. Given the modest NPV (75.0%), this threshold is better suited for a "rule-in" strategy, and low values should not be used in isolation to defer biopsy. External validation in multicenter cohorts is required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: Scaling HPV Self-Sampling in Low-Resource Settings: From Evidence to Sustainable Implementation.
articles.authors: Inturrisi F, Serrano B, de Sanjosé S
articles.abstract: Profound global inequities in cervical cancer burden persist, with nearly 90% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). High-performance human papillomavirus (HPV) testing is the recommended primary screening method, but its scale-up remains constrained by resource and infrastructure limitations. HPV self-sampling optimizes health system resources by eliminating universal speculum examinations during primary screening, yet a critical implementation gap remains regarding how programs transition from pilot projects to routine national practice. To examine this transition, a literature search was conducted through May 2026, focusing on implementation of cervical screening using vaginal self-sampling and molecular DNA amplification techniques within resource-limited settings. While policy endorsement in LMICs expanded from 10 countries in 2020 to 29 in 2026-with 23 recommending self-sampling for all women-real-world implementation lags significantly, as reflected in an estimated five-year HPV-based screening coverage of only 2% in LMICs in 2022. Selected country case studies illustrate diverse delivery models and varying stages of implementation scale, ranging from localized research projects and regional campaigns to scaled national programs: community health worker home visits increased screening uptake four-fold in Argentina, digital health platforms and electronic registries are supporting national scale-up in Malaysia and Rwanda, and single-day near-point-of-care projects achieved very high follow-up rates in remote Amazonian populations. Beyond these country experiences, the review evaluates key considerations along the clinical care cascade, highlighting the importance of triage and treatment capacity, active tracing strategies to minimize loss to follow-up, and supply chain management. Ultimately, self-sampling serves as a promising equity strategy whose success relies on sustained political, financial, and structural commitment across the full clinical pathway.

articles.title: Retrospective evaluation of first-trimester miscarriage following euploid embryo transfer.
articles.journal: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi
articles.authors: Chan CCW, Higo S, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study investigated the possible causes of first-trimester miscarriages after euploid embryo transfer from both genetic and maternal perspectives.
METHODS: Data were retrospectively collected from seven in-vitro fertilisation centres and two preimplantation genetic testing laboratories in Hong Kong. The study included patients who underwent preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) between 2015 and 2024, followed by frozen-thawed single euploid embryo transfer resulting in confirmed clinical pregnancies that ended in miscarriage before 12 weeks of gestation. Baseline demographic data and, when available, genetic results for the products of gestation (POG) were reviewed.
RESULTS: In total, 1792 PGT-A cycles and 884 embryo transfers were performed. Sixty-five transfers resulted in clinical pregnancies that ended in miscarriage before 12 weeks of gestation. Genetic testing was conducted on 14 POG samples in this study. In one case, the PGT-A and POG results were discordant; mosaic trisomy 8 was detected only in the POG. No consistent pattern in maternal demographic factors was evident.
CONCLUSION: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy appears effective; the majority of firsttrimester miscarriages after euploid embryo transfers are unlikely to be explained by discordant PGT-A results. Despite its high accuracy, PGT-A cannot detect all forms of chromosomal mosaicism and therefore cannot completely prevent miscarriage. Reviews of clinical and medical histories, along with cytogenetic testing of POG after a miscarriage following euploid embryo transfer in selected cases, may provide additional insights into possible contributing factors and future management options. The underlying cause may remain unexplained in many cases.

articles.title: Association between atherogenic index of plasma at 11-20 weeks of gestation and gestational diabetes risk: A prospective cohort study in China.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Kong M, Zhong C, Gao Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent studies have linked insulin resistance and the onset of type 2 diabetes mellitus to the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP). This integrated lipid marker reflects cardiovascular risk and atherogenic dyslipidemia. However, its relationship with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is not completely understood. This study aimed to evaluate the association between AIP measured at 11-20 weeks of gestation and the subsequent risk of GDM and to identify the optimal AIP threshold for GDM prediction.
METHODS: A total of 2068 women with singleton pregnancies were included in this prospective cohort study from the Tongji Maternal and Child Health Cohort. AIP was calculated from fasting triglycerides and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) measurements obtained at 11-20 weeks of gestation, before GDM diagnosis by 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24-28 weeks of gestation. Subgroup analysis, restricted cubic spline models, and multivariable logistic regression were used to assess the relationship between GDM and AIP. The predictive performance of AIP alone and in combination with maternal age, pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) was compared via receiver operating characteristic curve analysis.
RESULTS: Gestational diabetes mellitus was diagnosed in 252 participants (12.3%). Women in the highest AIP quartile demonstrated a substantially higher risk than those in the lowest quartile (adjusted odds ratio 2.56; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.63-4.01; P < 0.001), and higher AIP levels were associated with a progressively higher risk of GDM. AIP and GDM risk were found to be significantly positively correlated (P for overall association <0.001), with no statistically significant evidence of nonlinearity (P for nonlinearity = 0.700), as assessed by restricted cubic spline analysis. Based on the maximum Youden index, an AIP value equal to 0.091 was determined to be the ideal cut-off for GDM prediction. A multivariable model incorporating AIP, pre-pregnancy BMI, maternal age, and LDL-C showed improved discriminative ability compared with AIP alone (area under the curve 0.69; 95% CI 0.66-0.73).
CONCLUSION: Elevated AIP levels at 11-20 weeks of gestation were independently associated with an increased risk of GDM. Importantly, the inclusion of AIP alongside established maternal risk factors enhanced predictive accuracy. The findings of this study indicate that AIP might serve as a useful adjunctive…

articles.title: Occult serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma and high-grade serous carcinoma at risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy in BRCA1/2 carriers: A Czech two-center cohort.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Zikan Dubova O, Dostalek L, Emingr M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy is the standard intervention for prevention of tubo-ovarian carcinoma in women with pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants, yet the optimal timing remains clinically challenging, particularly for BRCA2 carriers.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 329 clinically asymptomatic BRCA1/2 carriers who underwent prophylactic gynecologic surgery with sectioning and extensively examining the fimbria (SEE-FIM) protocol histopathologic assessment at two Czech tertiary centers between November 2014 and September 2024. The primary outcome was occult malignant or premalignant pathology, defined as serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) or invasive high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC). The cohort included 211 BRCA1 and 118 BRCA2 carriers.
RESULTS: Overall, 10 occult lesions were detected (3.0%, 95% confidence interval 1.7-5.5): five STIC lesions (1.5%) and five occult HGSCs (1.5%). Among BRCA1 carriers, eight lesions were identified (3.8%), including all five STIC lesions and three HGSCs. Among BRCA2 carriers, two occult HGSCs were detected (1.7%), both after the age of 55 years, and no STIC was found. The difference in any occult lesion between BRCA1 and BRCA2 carriers was not statistically significant (p = 0.504), but lesion numbers were small. Occult HGSC occurred at an older age than did STIC (median 55.0 vs. 43.0 years; p = 0.012). In exploratory analyses, a family history of breast cancer and ever smoking were associated with occult lesions, including in a reduced multivariable model, but these findings require cautious interpretation because of the sparse number of events.
CONCLUSIONS: These data support meticulous pathologic evaluation and individualized counseling. The absence of early BRCA2-associated occult lesions should be considered hypothesis generating and should not be interpreted as evidence for delaying risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy beyond current recommendations.

articles.title: Characterizing Heat Health Hazards and Receptivity of Cooling Interventions Among Indoor Lumber Mill Workers in Southern Thailand.
articles.authors: Thepaksorn P, Hom Thepaksorn EK, Bach A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness and feasibility of two workplace cooling strategies and identify priorities for future mixed-methods research and practical solutions.
METHODS: A pilot randomized crossover field trial was conducted among 12 sawmill workers in southern Thailand under three conditions: no cooling (CON), a phase change cooling vest (VEST), and a combined cooling oasis (OASIS: hydration, fans, water dousing, cooling towels). Core temperature and heart rate were continuously monitored. Worker perceptions were explored through post-intervention focus group discussions.
RESULTS: Compared with CON, OASIS reduced core temperature (-0.24°C; 95% CI: 0.23, 0.25) and heart rate (-7 bpm; 95% CI: 6, 9), while VEST reduced core temperature (-0.17°C; 95% CI: 0.17, 0.18) and heart rate (-5 bpm; 95% CI: 4, 6). Despite greater physiological benefits from OASIS, most workers preferred VEST due to ease of use and caused minimal disruption to workflow. OASIS was perceived as effective but interruptive.
CONCLUSIONS: Combined cooling strategies can reduce heat strain in indoor industrial settings; however, the adoption of interventions is strongly influenced by practicality and economic considerations. Hybrid approaches and structural improvements are recommended. A full mixed-methods study is needed to evaluate effectiveness, productivity, and cost-effectiveness to inform scalable occupational heat policies.

articles.title: Evaluating the diagnostic value of PLR and related hematologic parameters combined with CA-125 for endometriomas.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Su P, Huang Y, Kang F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disease, with inflammation relating to pathogenesis and staging. We compared inflammatory indices and clinical characteristics between patients with ovarian endometriomas and those with benign ovarian tumors to evaluate their diagnostic value and identify affordable blood markers for diagnosis and staging.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center case-control study included 645 patients having laparoscopic surgery between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2024: 372 with endometriosis and 273 controls with benign ovarian teratomas. Blood parameters and clinical characteristics were compared with Mann-Whitney U and t-tests. Independent risk factors for endometrioma and staging were evaluated using binary logistic regression. Predictive efficacy was assessed via receiver operating characteristic curves. Relationships between cancer antigen 125 (CA-125) and hematologic parameters were determined with correlation analyses.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with endometrioma had higher platelet-to-lymphocyte (PLR), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte (NLR) × CA-125, and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios (MLR) × CA-125, PLR × CA-125, and CA-125. Patients with endometrioma had more pelvic pain, larger cysts, and fewer pregnancies than controls. Higher CA-125 and visual analog scale (VAS) scores occurred with endometriomas. Patients with stage IV had higher platelet counts, NLR × CA-125, MLR × CA-125, PLR × CA-125, and CA-125 levels than Stage III. Preoperative bilateral endometriomas and elevated CA-125 were independent risk factors for Stage IV. CA-125 was positively correlated with PLR, cyst diameter, cyst area, VAS score, and bilateral endometriomas.
CONCLUSION: The staging system is important for assessing endometrial lesions, although it may not reflect the level of inflammatory activity. For patients with dysmenorrhea or pelvic pain, elevated CA-125 demonstrated superior diagnostic value for ovarian endometrioma compared with PLR × CA-125, and could serve as a simple, cost-effective, and efficient assessment tools, providing information regarding endometriosis to inform clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Placental histopathology and angiogenic biomarkers in two phenotypes of pre-eclampsia, early and late onset-a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Ajjaguttu SR, Gorle S, Nanda N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The placenta plays a central role in the development of pre-eclampsia (PE). It has been identified with two distinct types as early and late onset pre-eclampsia (EOPE and LOPE) with distinct pathophysiological profiles. This study aimed to compare angiogenic biomarkers, uterine artery Doppler indices and placental histopathology between EOPE and LOPE.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care center involving 300 women (150 EOPE and 150 LOPE). Uterine artery Doppler, maternal serum biomarkers (soluble fms like tyrosine kinase [sFlt-1], placental growth factor [PlGF], sFlt-1/PlGF ratio) were measured within 2 weeks of delivery. Placentas were examined post-delivery and reported as per Amsterdam Placental Workshop Group Consensus.
RESULTS: The mean uterine artery pulsatility index (PI) was higher in EOPE compared to LOPE. Median sFlt-1 and sFlt-PlGF ratios were elevated in EOPE while the PlGF values were significantly higher in LOPE. Histopathologic analysis revealed perivillous fibrin deposition, increased syncytial knots, and multiple infarctions as predominant lesions in EOPE. In LOPE, infarctions and calcifications were more common. In EOPE, all placental lesions correlated with PlGF, sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, and uterine artery PI. In LOPE, only infarctions and syncytial knots showed correlation with sFlt-1 and sFlt-1/PlGF ratio.
CONCLUSION: EOPE is characterized by pronounced angiogenic imbalance, impaired uteroplacental perfusion, and severe placental pathology in terms of maternal vascular malperfusions. LOPE presents with milder biochemical and Doppler changes, with placental lesions suggestive of aging rather than maternal vascular malperfusions.

articles.title: Exercise in pregnant elite athletes: Physiological considerations, risks, and benefits.
articles.authors: Madera I, Bhargava V, Patel J et al.
articles.abstract: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) recommends engagement in moderate exercise throughout pregnancy, including aerobic and strengthening activities, which has been shown to offer numerous benefits during pregnancy. However, the intersection of pregnancy and athletics presents a unique set of challenges. ACOG guidelines on exercise during pregnancy primarily target recreational exercisers. Tailored recommendations are needed for pregnant elite athletes. This study examines both how pregnancy affects physiology and the risks/benefits of high-intensity exercise. Two independent reviews were conducted, using MESH search terms including "pregnant athletes," "female elite athlete," "maternal health," "exercise pregnancy." From 56 total studies, 40 studies with clinical data on over 4163 women, including elite athletes, were included in the review. Regular exercise during pregnancy can improve cardiovascular fitness and fetal vascular function while reducing risks of gestational diabetes, hypertensive disorders, delivering a large-for-gestational-age infant, and excessive weight gain. High-intensity activities can compromise fetal blood flow. Endurance athletes may safely maintain their training regimens during pregnancy, whereas those in high-altitude or contact sports require adjustments. Routine, non-intense exercise during pregnancy offers significant maternal and fetal health benefits. Future work should establish individualized recommendations supporting pregnant elite athlete health.

articles.title: Oral gonadotropin-releasing hormone antagonists versus injectable cetrorelix for luteinizing hormone surge prevention in donor in vitro fertilization cycles: A retrospective cohort study of efficacy, embryology, and stimulation dynamics.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Mondal R, Nandi M
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the effectiveness of oral gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonists (elagolix and relugolix) compared to injectable cetrorelix in preventing premature luteinizing hormone (LH) surge and luteinization during controlled ovarian stimulation in donor in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles and assesses their impact on oocyte maturity, embryo development, and stimulation efficiency.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary fertility center including 173 donor cycles allocated into three groups: cetrorelix (n = 60), relugolix (n = 55), and elagolix (n = 58). All donors met standardized inclusion criteria and underwent stimulation with recombinant gonadotropins. GnRH antagonist regimens were initiated when follicles reached ≥14 mm. Primary outcome was the composite rate of premature LH surge and/or luteinization. Secondary outcomes included mature oocyte yield (MII), fertilization and blastocyst development, gonadotropin usage, stimulation duration, and drug-related adverse events. Multivariable regression models adjusted for donor age, body mass index, antral follicle count, antral follicle count, and calendar time.
RESULTS: Observed composite endocrine escape rates were low and numerically similar across groups (3.3-3.6%), although the study was substantially underpowered for this rare endpoint. However, suspected premature ovulation/empty follicle syndrome was observed only in the elagolix group (6.9% vs. 0%, P = 0.017); this finding is based on four events and should be interpreted as exploratory. MII yield and MII rate were significantly lower in both oral antagonist groups compared to cetrorelix (P < 0.001). Oral groups required higher gonadotropin doses and longer stimulation. No cases of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome occurred. Adherence was high across groups; adverse events were more frequent with elagolix (12.1%).
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory retrospective donor IVF cohort, observed endocrine escape rates were low across oral and injectable antagonist groups, but the study was underpowered to establish equivalence or non-inferiority. Oral antagonist use was associated with lower MII oocyte yield, greater stimulation burden, and fewer usable blastocysts. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered prospective trials.

articles.title: Burnout and second victim phenomenon in obstetrics: Psychological impact of maternal and perinatal adverse events, medico-legal stress, workplace violence, and organizational culture.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Chandra R, Kumari S
articles.abstract: Obstetrics is among the most psychologically demanding fields in medicine. Clinicians must safeguard the lives of both mother and fetus while managing unpredictable emergencies, life-threatening complications, and considerable medico-legal scrutiny. Repeated exposure to maternal and perinatal adverse events leaves obstetricians particularly vulnerable to burnout and the second victim phenomenon. This review examines the occupational stressors driving burnout in obstetrics, with particular attention to the second victim phenomenon, moral injury, medico-legal pressure, workplace violence, and the organizational factors that shape clinician well-being. A narrative review of English-language literature in PubMed and PubMed Central was conducted for studies published up to June 2026, using pre-specified search terms combined with reference-list screening of key publications; formal risk-of-bias assessment and protocol registration were not undertaken, consistent with a narrative rather than systematic review design. Burnout affects an estimated 40%-75% of obstetricians and gynecologists, and nearly 45% will experience the second victim phenomenon during their career, with 19% reporting an episode in the past year. Adverse obstetric events commonly provoke guilt, anxiety, sleep disturbance, and post-traumatic stress symptoms, compounded by long hours, litigation, workplace violence, moral injury, and dual responsibility for mother and fetus. These pressures drive defensive practice, reduced job satisfaction, medical errors, and workforce attrition. Structured peer-support programs, debriefing, Just Culture principles, and organizational wellness initiatives show promising, although largely observational, evidence of benefit. Burnout and second victim experiences are significant occupational hazards in obstetrics. Evidence-based organizational support is essential for clinician well-being, workforce retention, and the safety and quality of maternity care, although higher-quality, obstetric-specific intervention research is needed.

articles.title: Challenging gender-based & obstetric violence: Medical students' evolving perspectives in OBGYN care.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Romero-Padrón MA, Herrera-Padilla LF, Cepeda XC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Medical students undergo professional socialization during clinical rotations, which shapes their perceptions and responses to patient care. Obstetric and gender-based violence are pervasive issues in obstetrics and gynecology, where hierarchical dynamics may normalize unethical practices. Our study aimed to explore the perceptions, observations, learning experiences, and beliefs of students regarding gender-based and obstetric violence during their obstetrics and gynecology rotation in Mexico.
METHODS: We used a mixed-methods design, incorporating a pre- and post-rotation questionnaire with Likert-scale and open-ended questions. Our questionnaire assessed perceptions of respectful treatment, violence, self-competence, and emotional reactions. We applied the Wilcoxon test to evaluate statistical differences, and qualitative responses underwent open coding for thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Of 100 students who completed both timepoints, familiarity with obstetric violence increased from 93% to 100%. Reports of encountering patients affected by violence rose significantly (24% to 85%, P < 0.001). Students observed increased instances of psychological abuse, medical malpractice, and violations of bioethical principles. Self-confidence in managing victims of sexual violence improved (1.85 vs. 3.09, P < 0.001), but students consistently reported sadness and anger when witnessing abuse. Perceptions of respectful treatment by healthcare staff, particularly nursing personnel, decreased significantly.
CONCLUSIONS: The obstetrics and gynecology rotation significantly heightened the medical students' awareness of obstetric and gender-based violence, improved self-competence in managing affected patients, and revealed persistent emotional distress. Findings highlight the need for improved medical education emphasizing ethical role modeling, emotional support, and strategies to address the persistence of violent and unethical practices in clinical environments.

articles.title: Persisting challenges for antioxidants use in treatment of male infertility.
articles.authors: Eldamnhoury EM, El-Sakka AI
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Oxidative stress {OS} has emerged as a major etiological factor to male infertility and is present in significant proportion of subfertile patients classified as male oxidative stress infertility. This review aimed to critically evaluate the current challenges associated with the use of antioxidants in the management of male infertility.
AREAS COVERED: This manuscript was conducted using review of literature addressing oxidative stress, antioxidant therapy, diagnostic biomarkers, sperm DNA damage, assisted reproductive technologies {ART}, and clinical outcomes in male infertility. Review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify relevant studies published from January 2000 to March 2026, with emphasis on systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials and clinical guidelines. The evidence was critically evaluated across several major challenges that were identified and analyzed, including oxidative stress assessment, antioxidant mechanisms, diagnostic standardization, patient selection, treatment protocols, reductive stress, bioavailability, outcome measures, long-term safety, ART interactions, and publication bias. Major barriers that contribute to the inconsistency in the outcome of antioxidants use include the absence of standardized diagnostic criteria for oxidative stress, lack of consensus regarding antioxidant formulations and dosages, heterogeneity among clinical trials, and the risk of reductive stress resulting from excessive supplementation.
EXPERT OPINION: Despite the biological rationale supporting antioxidant therapy in male infertility, substantial challenges continue to limit its evidence-based clinical application. Future research should prioritize standardized diagnostic approaches, biomarker-guided patient selection, optimization of dosage and treatment duration, and assessment of clinically relevant reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: Aging-related morphological changes in the obturator internus and levator ani.
articles.authors: Muro S, Tsuchiya J, Ibara T et al.
articles.abstract: Pelvic floor dysfunction is a common condition in adult women. In addition to the levator ani, the obturator internus, a lateral pelvic wall muscle, has been suggested to be anatomically and mechanically associated with pelvic floor morphology. Here, we quantitatively characterized age-related morphological changes in the obturator internus and levator ani using geometric morphometric analysis. We hypothesized a significant association between principal components accounting for major shape variation and age. This cross-sectional study included 27 adult women aged 25-83 years with gynecological conditions but without pelvic floor disorders based on clinical assessment and imaging findings. Standardized pelvic magnetic resonance imaging scans were obtained between April 2024 and July 2024 at a single tertiary care center. Elliptic Fourier analysis was applied to the segmented obturator internus contours; a landmark-based method was used to evaluate the combined shape of the obturator internus and levator ani. Principal component analysis and linear regression were performed to assess associations with age. Procrustes analysis of variance was used to evaluate the overall shape-age relationships. Elliptic Fourier analysis revealed that increasing age was significantly associated with relative narrowing of the superior portion, an inferior morphological shift of the medial surface groove, and increased prominence of the medial eminence of the obturator internus. A landmark-based analysis revealed similar age-related shape changes, including inferiorly directed shape changes of the groove, verticalization of the levator ani, and widening of the levator hiatus. Procrustes analysis revealed a significant relationship between age and overall shape variation. Aging was associated with coordinated age-related morphological remodeling of the obturator internus and levator ani.

articles.title: Scaffold-Hydrogel Synergy with OPC-Crosslinked dUECM and VEGF-Nanocomposite Hydrogel Achieves Dual "Structural-Vascular" Regeneration in Rats.
articles.authors: Wang X, Gu Q, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Absolute uterine factor infertility (AUFI) remains untreatable with current assisted reproduction techniques. Although decellularized uterine extracellular matrix (dUECM) holds promise for uterine reconstruction, its clinical translation is limited by rapid degradation and poor angiogenic capacity. Herein, a dual-component system was developed by combining oligomeric proanthocyanidin (OPC)-crosslinked dUECM with an injectable VEGF-loaded nanocomposite hydrogel. The OPC-dUECM scaffold (1 mg/mL OPC solution) restored native-like tensile strength, reduced collagenase-induced degradation to 52%, and facilitated cellular infiltration. The VEGF-EPL-HP nanocomposite hydrogel was fabricated by encapsulating VEGF (350 ng/mL) in ε-polylysine/heparin-poloxamer (EPL-HP) nanoparticles dispersed within a thermosensitive hydrogel. The hydrogel exhibited a gelation temperature of 23.2°C, provided sustained VEGF release over 7 days, and showed negligible hemolytic toxicity. In vitro, this hydrogel significantly enhanced the migration and tube formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells. At 90 days post-surgery in a rat uterine defect model, the combined OPC-dUECM + VEGF-EPL-HP group achieved full endometrial and myometrial regeneration, accompanied by elevated microvessel density, attenuated inflammation, and negligible fibrotic lesions. Collectively, this study validated a synergistic scaffold-hydrogel platform enabling concurrent structural reconstruction and vascularization of the injured uterus, offering a clinically translatable strategy for AUFI patients.

articles.title: EZH2 in Ovarian Cancer: Mechanistic Dependencies, Therapeutic Platforms and Translational Combinations.
articles.authors: Tong A, Lin X, Yang L
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecologic malignancy because most patients present with advanced disease and ultimately relapse despite surgery, platinum- based chemotherapy, and modern maintenance strategies. Enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2), the catalytic core of polycomb repressive complex 2, has emerged as a context-dependent epigenetic regulator that links chromatin repression to cellular plasticity, repair-state adaptation, stemness, metabolism, and immune remodeling. This review aims to define the clinical relevance of context-dependent EZH2 states in ovarian cancer and compare the therapeutic logic, evidence maturity, and limitations of available EZH2-targeting platforms.
METHODS: We conducted a focused narrative synthesis of ovarian-cancer-relevant preclinical studies, medicinal-chemistry reports, and clinical evidence, supplemented by targeted PubMed searches and ClinicalTrials.gov checks during revision. Evidence was interpreted in light of biologic context, therapeutic platform, combination rationale, and the degree of ovarian-specific clinical support.
RESULTS: Current evidence supports a role for EZH2 in ovarian tumor progression through canonical polycomb repressive complex 2-dependent mechanisms and, in selected contexts, non-canonical functions. Therapeutic development now includes catalytic inhibitors, dual EZH1/2 inhibitors, EEDdirected inhibitors, degraders, and RNA-based strategies. In ovarian cancer, the strongest mechanistic rationale currently supports combinations with platinum chemotherapy and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibition, whereas immune-oriented and broader cotargeting strategies remain promising but less mature.
DISCUSSION: The key translational question is not simply whether EZH2 can be pharmacologically engaged, but which form of EZH2 dependency is present, in which biologic context, and with which partner therapy. Catalytic inhibition alone may underperform when adaptive redundancy, polycomb complex architecture, or non-canonical protein function sustain tumor fitness.
CONCLUSION: EZH2 should be viewed not as a uniformly validated ovarian-cancer target, but as a context-dependent vulnerability whose most defensible near-term clinical positioning is biomarkerinformed combination development rather than unselected monotherapy.

articles.title: Silence and Sorrow: A Qualitative Exploration of the Hidden Role of Communication Failures in Perinatal Care.
articles.authors: Rent S, Nussbaum L, Bassett E et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Perinatal mortality remains high in low- and middle-income countries, with Tanzania bearing one of the greatest burdens. The Three Delays framework is often used to analyze preventable perinatal deaths and includes care seeking, reaching care, and receiving definitive care. This study explores Tanzanian mothers' experiences of perinatal loss, focusing on delays and gaps in care.
METHODS: This study was conducted at Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Center (KCMC) in Moshi, Tanzania. Fifty women who experienced stillbirth or neonatal death completed intake surveys about their perinatal loss experience. Of these, 40 completed semi-structured in-depth interviews 8 weeks post-loss. Interviews explored barriers in care seeking, access, delivery, and communication. Survey data were analyzed with descriptive statistics. Interview data were thematically coded using a directed content analysis combining a priori codes from the three delays framework and inductive coding.
RESULTS: Participants perceived delays in seeking care (50%), receiving care at initial facilities (27.5%), referral processes (12.5%), and care at KCMC (17.5%). Nearly half (45%) reported inadequate communication from healthcare providers. Three key themes emerged: (1) women perceived delays in care at all points along their care trajectory (2) gaps in communication impacted medical care for women and newborns, and hindered healing after perinatal loss; and (3) women emphasized the need for emotional support and compassionate communication following loss.
DISCUSSION: While structural, process, and financial barriers persist, informational and relational communication gaps represent an under-addressed challenge across the perinatal loss care pathway. Rather than being viewed in isolation, efforts to strengthen communication should be integrated into broader health system strategies aimed at reducing delays, improving access to timely and quality care, and supporting families after stillbirth or neonatal death. Strengthening communication within health systems, both as an informational and relational process, has the potential to enhance care experiences, build trust, and support emotional healing after perinatal loss.

articles.title: Behavioral Health Conditions, Maternal Factors and Severe Maternal Morbidity in Michigan: A Statewide Analysis of Birth Hospitalizations.
articles.authors: Stone M, Smith F, Nechuta S
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal mortality continues to rise in the United States and continued monitoring of the burden and risk factors for severe maternal morbidity (SMM) is crucial. Studies have shown that maternal substance use disorders (SUDs) and mental health disorders (i.e., behavioral health disorders (BHDs)) are important risk factors for maternal mortality, but less is known for SMM. We examined maternal characteristics and BHDs in association with SMM in Michigan (MI).
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional pooled analysis using data from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project State Inpatient Database (2019-2023) for birth hospitalizations for females aged ≥ 15 years in MI (n = 495,074). Using the CDC's SMM definition, SMM prevalence was determined using ICD-10-CM diagnosis and procedure codes. We examined maternal characteristics and individual BHDs in association with SMM using multivariable logistic regression to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: We identified 4563 SMM events. The rate per 10,000 births increased from 78.4 (2019) to 100.1 (2023). Maternal characteristics associated with SMM included lowest zip code-level income (aOR:1.16, 95% CI: 1.12-1.40) and Black race/ethnicity (aOR:1.75, 95% CI: 1.57-1.86). Results for maternal characteristics varied by SMM type. Several BHDs, including SUDs, were associated with increased SMM. For example, the aORs (95% CI) for depression and anxiety-related disorders with SMM were 1.47(1.34-1.62) and 1.60(1.47-1.75), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: We found an increase in SMM in MI and identified key risk factors, including social and mental health-related factors, which inform identification of those at risk for SMM to support targeting of resources and prevention efforts.

articles.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Quinolin-2-One-Indole Schiff Base Hybrids as Potential EGFR-Targeted Anticancer Agents Against Breast and Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Dessai PG, Bhandurge P, Nazareth C et al.
articles.abstract: A series of new quinolin-2-one-indole Schiff base hybrids was designed, synthesized, and tested as potential anticancer agents targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor. The designed compounds were synthesized via a multistep synthetic route comprising phenylhydrazone formation, Fischer indole cyclization, Vilsmeier-Haack formylation, and subsequent Schiff base condensation. Structural elucidation was performed using IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and mass spectral analysis. In silico studies demonstrated that the synthesized compounds exhibited strong binding affinities to both wild-type (PDB ID: 1M17) and mutant EGFR (PDB ID: 4ZAU), as evidenced by favorable docking scores, with PYd2 showing the strongest interaction. Molecular dynamics simulations over 100 ns further confirmed that the PYd2-EGFR complexes remained stable, maintaining consistent protein-ligand contacts and exhibiting stable RMSD and RMSF values throughout the simulation period. Predicted ADME-toxicity profiles demonstrated favorable drug-like properties, oral absorption, and acceptable toxicity profiles for most synthesized derivatives. In vitro anticancer evaluation against MDA-MB-231 and SK-OV-3 cell lines identified PYd2 as the most potent analog. ELISA-based studies demonstrated significant inhibition of EGFR expression and phosphorylation, while DAPI staining revealed characteristic apoptotic nuclear changes in treated cells. Overall, PYd2 showed favorable predicted EGFR binding and antiproliferative activity against both cancer cell lines.

articles.title: Advancing assisted reproductive technology in Africa: a narrative review on the promising role of molecular biology and molecular techniques.
articles.authors: Kyei F, Napo C, Nabawo C et al.
articles.abstract: Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) has significantly improved fertility outcomes globally, yet its full potential remains underutilized. In Africa, persistent barriers including high costs, limited access, inadequate infrastructure, lack of awareness, and sociocultural and ethical concerns impedes its utility. This review explores the promising role of molecular biology and advanced molecular techniques in overcoming these challenges and advancing ART on the continent. Techniques such as preimplantation genetic testing (PGT), non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT), CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, mitochondrial replacement therapy (MRT), and single-cell RNA sequencing offer opportunities to enhance embryo selection, minimize genetic and epigenetic risks, and improve pregnancy success rates. Furthermore, innovations like biomarker discovery, liquid biopsy, and genomic screening can personalize treatment strategies and improve reproductive outcomes. We also provide a narrative on the progress made in expanding ART services, improving affordability through low-cost protocols, and building local expertise through training and collaborations. While challenges persist, especially in regulation and access to ART, the integration of molecular innovations in a phased manner has the potential to transform ART if implemented within appropriate infrastructural, ethical, and policy frameworks. This review underscores the need for sustained investment, policy reform, and interdisciplinary collaboration to bridge existing gaps and ensure that ART technologies are accessible, safe, and effective for all individuals and couples affected by infertility in the region.

articles.title: The lived experiences of reproductive-aged women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a qualitative study.
articles.authors: Ward KJ, Benzley AK, King Stone KL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PCOS is a complex health condition that affects up to 20% females of reproductive age worldwide, and approximately 5 million U.S. females of reproductive aged females. Despite the prevalence of the condition, research on the lived experiences of women with PCOS is limited, particularly in the United States.
METHODS: This study employed a phenomenological qualitative design to explore the lived experiences of individuals diagnosed with PCOS. We conducted semi-structured interviews via web conferencing with 39 females 18-45 years of age, residing in the U.S. with PCOS. Transcribed interviews were analyzed using the Framework Method.
RESULTS: We identified ten primary themes in the data 1) Critical shift point, 2) Education, 3) Future Experience, 4) Gaslighting (or blame), 5) Medical Experience, 6) Present Emotional Experience, 7) Social Impacts, 8) Treatment, 9) Well-documented Physical Symptoms, and 10) Not Well-Documented Symptoms and an additional 37 sub-themes. Overall, the experiences of living with PCOS were generally negative, especially in relation to gaslighting or blame, medical experience, symptoms - both well documented and not well documented, present emotional experience, social impacts, and treatment. Additionally, many participants reported a critical shift point that led to them seeking a diagnosis and treatment for their condition, and a lack of education in relation to PCOS.
CONCLUSIONS: Women with PCOS experience a wide-ranging physical, mental, and relational impacts. Awareness of the impact of PCOS is needed to reduce gaps in provider knowledge, social disconnect, fear of judgment, and mental health concerns. Further research is needed to understand the impact of PCOS on the lived experience of post-menopausal women, and to develop improved education for both providers and those in the social circle of women with PCOS.

articles.title: AI-powered risk prediction models for preventable maternal mortality in rural settings: a systematic review.
articles.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
articles.authors: Aifuobhokhan J, Ogunjinmi A, Agbarakwe CA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal mortality remains disproportionately high in low- and middle-income countries, particularly in rural settings with limited access to skilled obstetric care. Artificial intelligence and machine learning models offer promise for early risk prediction, yet their methodological rigour, applicability, and deployment feasibility in resource-constrained rural contexts remain inadequately synthesised. This systematic review evaluated AI-powered risk prediction models for preventable maternal mortality, with an emphasis on their suitability for rural and low-resource settings.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online for studies published from January 2015 to August 2025.
