Studies employing AI or machine learning to predict maternal mortality or severe maternal outcomes were included. The Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST) assessed methodological quality across four domains: participants, predictors, outcomes, and analysis. Data extraction captured study characteristics, model architectures, performance metrics, validation strategies, and rural implementation considerations. This review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251174343) and reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies met inclusion criteria, predominantly from sub-Saharan Africa (n = 12) and South Asia (n = 8). Dataset sizes ranged from 402 to over 31 million records from national surveys (n = 14), hospital registries (n = 9), and Internet of Things monitoring systems (n = 5). Random Forest (n = 14), ensemble methods (n = 11), and neural networks (n = 11) were most frequently employed. Reported area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values ranged from 0.70 to 0.95 (median 0.84), with sensitivity 70-92% and specificity 65-85%. PROBAST assessment revealed low risk of bias for participants (24/28), predictors (25/28), and outcomes (24/28), but substantial concerns in the analysis domain (14/28 low risk, 8/28 high risk). Key limitations included reliance on synthetic oversampling without external validation, inadequate reporting of calibration, and small sample sizes in IoT studies. Only 11 studies (39%) conducted external validation. Common predictors were maternal age, blood pressure, gestational age, parity, and antenatal care attendance. Rural implementation barriers included limited connectivity, data…

articles.title: Longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and their association with cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity risk in postmenopausal women: evidence from the CHARLS study.
articles.authors: Xu J, Liu R, Zhang M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and the risk of cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity (CRMM) in a population of postmenopausal women.
METHODS: A total of 2,859 postmenopausal women from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) were included, with 4 repeated measurements of night sleep duration collected from 2011 to 2018. Group-based trajectory modeling was adopted to identify distinct sleep duration trajectory patterns. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations between sleep trajectories and incident CRMM ascertained between 2018 and 2020. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses were further conducted to validate the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: Three sleep duration trajectory patterns were identified: normal-stable (33.9% of the cohort), normal-fluctuating decline (52.0%), and short-rapid decline (14.1%). During a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome (incident CRMM) occurred in 108 participants (3.8%). Compared with normal-stable group, those in normal-fluctuating decline and short-rapid decline groups had an increased risk of CRMM (ORs of 2.30 [95%CI, 1.35-3.91] and 3.75 [95%CI, 1.99-7.07], respectively) after adjustment for multiple covariates. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these associations, which were independent of key baseline characteristics and missing data.
CONCLUSION: In postmenopausal women, short and declining sleep duration trajectories are strong, independent risk factors for CRMM. Public health and clinical interventions should prioritize maintaining stable, adequate sleep to mitigate multimorbidity risk in this population.

articles.title: A risk assessment model for gestational diabetes mellitus integrating maternal demographics and hematological indices in Thai women.
articles.authors: Sai-Ong T, Waeyeng D, Khamphaya T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Universal screening for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) is the gold standard, but it can be difficult and expensive in resource-limited settings. Many current prediction models rely on specialized tests that are not available in primary care. This study aimed to create a cost-effective risk assessment model using common maternal demographic and blood test data to help identify GDM risk in Thai pregnant women.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study with 200 pregnant women (24-28 weeks of gestation) at a secondary care hospital in Southern Thailand. We analyzed routine antenatal data, including complete blood count and other lab results. A risk-scoring system was built using multivariate logistic regression. We then tested the model's performance using Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis to determine the optimal cut-off point.
RESULTS: Six independent predictors were found maternal age over 35 years, systolic blood pressure above 130 mmHg, glycosuria, hemoglobin at least 11 g/dL, platelets at least 260.50 × 103/µL, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) of 2.89 or higher. The combined risk model performed better (AUC = 0.804; 95% CI: 0.74-0.87) than single-marker models. With a risk score cut-off of 2.5 (indicating three or more risk factors), the model had a sensitivity of 71.4% and a specificity of 78.1%.
CONCLUSION: The new risk assessment model, which uses basic demographic and routine blood test data, offers a reliable and affordable way to screen for GDM. This method enables early risk identification and helps healthcare providers use resources more efficiently, potentially reducing unnecessary tests in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: CDS2 Drives Tumor Progression in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer via the PI3K/AKT Pathway.
articles.authors: Cao L, Chen Y, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) frequently disseminates within the lipid-rich peritoneal cavity, where tumor progression is accompanied by metabolic adaptations involving lipid utilization and mitochondrial function. Although these metabolic alterations are increasingly recognized as important features of EOC progression and peritoneal metastasis, the molecular factors linking mitochondrial-lipid metabolic remodeling with aggressive tumor behavior remain incompletely characterized. We therefore integrated mitochondrial- and lipid metabolism-related transcriptomic analyses to identify candidate regulators and further investigated the clinical and biological features associated with CDS2.
RESULTS: Seven key genes associated with mitochondrial and lipid metabolism were identified in EOC through comprehensive bioinformatic analyses and were used to construct the MALRS prognostic model. Further integration of FIGO stage, histologic grade, and MALRS scores yielded a nomogram whose calibration plots showed good agreement between predicted and observed 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival probabilities. Subsequent screening of these candidate genes in chemotherapy-resistant datasets identified CDP-diacylglycerol synthase 2 (CDS2) as the most consistently upregulated candidate gene. Clinical validation confirmed that CDS2 was significantly overexpressed in tumor tissues and was associated with advanced disease stage, and survival analysis showed that higher CDS2 expression was associated with shorter progression-free survival (PFS) in stage III/IV patients. Functional characterization demonstrated that CDS2 overexpression promoted both lipid droplet accumulation and migratory capacity in ovarian cancer cells. Pathway analysis identified significant enrichment of PI3K/AKT signaling, and experimental validation confirmed CDS2-mediated hyperactivation of PI3K/AKT phosphorylation. Computational immune-deconvolution analyses further identified exploratory associations between CDS2 expression, estimated T-cell abundance, and immune-checkpoint transcripts.
CONCLUSION: CDS2 is a lipid metabolism-associated candidate biomarker linked to aggressive clinicopathological features in EOC. Our findings associate CDS2 with disease progression, PI3K/AKT-related signaling, and immune-related transcriptomic features, supporting its further evaluation as a candidate prognostic marker.

articles.title: Impact of the 25-Hour Religious Fast of "Yom Kippur" on Pregnancy Outcomes in Low-Risk Singleton Pregnancies in Israel: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.authors: Waysbort S, Bas Lando M, Zivotofsky A et al.
articles.abstract: Evidence regarding the impact of prolonged religious fasting during pregnancy is limited and inconsistent. We aimed to examine the effects of Yom Kippur fasting, a complete 25-h religious fast, on pregnancy outcomes, with a primary focus on preterm delivery, in low-risk singleton pregnancies in Jerusalem, Israel. We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study of Jewish women aged 18-45 years with uncomplicated singleton pregnancies delivered in our maternity wards between 2006 and 2021. Data were extracted from electronic medical records. A preliminary survey estimated the prevalence of fasting during Yom Kippur at 92% (80% complete, 12% partial). Deliveries occurring on Yom Kippur and up to two days afterward were compared with deliveries on the corresponding days one week prior. The primary outcome was preterm delivery (< 37 weeks). Secondary outcomes included preterm birth <34, <32, and <28 weeks, other maternal and neonatal outcomes, and biochemical markers of maternal dehydration including urine ketones, blood urea nitrogen, hemoglobin, and hematocrit. During the study period, 5832 deliveries occurred across study and control days. After exclusions, 3943 deliveries (67.6%) were analyzed: 697 occurred on Yom Kippur, 1485 within one day and 2080 within two days following, and 1863 occurred on the three corresponding days the week before. Preterm delivery rates were comparable across groups (< 37 weeks: 2.2%, 1.9%, 2.2%, and 2.2% in groups 1, 2, 3, and control, respectively). Multivariate analysis revealed no significant differences in gestational age at delivery or preterm birth rates at various thresholds. Study group women exhibited higher hematocrit and urine ketone levels, without clinically significant adverse maternal and neonatal effects. Labor duration was shorter in fasting women, who also presented with greater cervical dilation, underwent fewer vaginal examinations, had lower epidural use, and reduced chorioamnionitis rates. However, the rate of shoulder dystocia was higher among fasting women. The 25-h Yom Kippur religious fast does not appear to increase the risk of preterm delivery or other adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes in low-risk singleton pregnancies. The observed association with shorter labor may reflect dehydration-related changes in maternal physiology. Further studies are warranted to assess the impact of prolonged fasting in high-risk pregnancies.

articles.title: CBX4 and NOX4 Expression Are Associated With Chemoradiotherapy Response and Overall Survival in Locally Advanced Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Pang X, Qin X, Que L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tissue biomarkers may improve risk stratification in locally advanced cervical cancer before definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). We evaluated pretreatment expression of chromobox 4 (CBX4), NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4), specificity protein 1 (SP1), and copper transporter 1 (CTR1) in relation to CCRT response and overall survival.
METHODS: In this retrospective 1:1 matched case-control study, pretreatment biopsies from 40 patients with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma (20 CCRT-resistant, 20 CCRT-sensitive) were quantified by AI-assisted digital pathology using H-scores. A parsimonious CBX4 + NOX4 logistic model was evaluated by apparent ROC, leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV), repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and bootstrap optimism correction. Overall survival analyses were exploratory.
RESULTS: CBX4 and NOX4 expression was lower in CCRT-resistant tumors (median H-score: CBX4, 40.47 vs. 79.62; NOX4, 7.00 vs. 53.93; both p < 0.001), whereas SP1 and CTR1 did not differ. Apparent AUCs were 0.840 for CBX4 and 0.843 for NOX4. The two-marker model had an apparent AUC of 0.903, LOOCV AUC 0.845, repeated 5-fold CV AUC 0.854 ± 0.022, and bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.883. High CBX4 and NOX4 expression was associated with better 5-year overall survival; in joint Cox models, hazard ratios per 1-SD increase were 0.31 (95% CI 0.13-0.74) for CBX4 and 0.48 (0.26-0.90) for NOX4. No histochemically detectable copper deposits were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower pretreatment CBX4 and NOX4 expression was associated with a CCRT-resistant phenotype and poorer overall survival in this small, response-enriched cohort. Internal resampling suggested discrimination, but same-dataset marker selection may introduce residual optimism and does not establish generalizability. Independent validation in a consecutively recruited cohort is required before clinical application. No mechanisms involving DNA repair, ROS, or chemoradiotherapy sensitivity were established.

articles.title: Low-dose histrelin for ovulation induction in mares: a partially randomized crossover pilot study.
articles.authors: de Barros Fogagnoli L, Jose KCA, Weckl R et al.
articles.abstract: This partially randomized crossover pilot study evaluated reduced doses of histrelin for ovulation induction in mares and compared intramuscular (IM) administration with pharmacopuncture at the Bai-hui and Yan-chi acupoints. Eleven mares were enrolled, of which nine completed all eight protocols and were included in the analyses. The protocols comprised 250 µg histrelin IM (standard dose), 75 µg IM, 25 µg IM, no intervention, saline at Bai-hui, saline at Yan-chi, 25 µg histrelin at Bai-hui, and 25 µg histrelin at Yan-chi. Ovulation was assessed by transrectal ultrasonography at scheduled examinations until detected, with ovulation within 48 h as the primary outcome. Ovulations first detected at 24 h were excluded from the primary analysis. Ovulation within 48 h occurred in 88.9% (8/9) of observations with 250 µg IM, 87.5% (7/8) with 75 µg IM, 87.5% (7/8) with 25 µg IM, 37.5% (3/8) with no intervention, 50.0% (3/6) with saline at Bai-hui, 100% (9/9) with 25 µg histrelin at Bai-hui, 12.5% (1/8) with saline at Yan-chi, and 87.5% (7/8) with 25 µg histrelin at Yan-chi. Exact 95% confidence intervals were wide, reflecting the small sample size. Exploratory pairwise comparisons with the no-intervention protocol were performed without adjustment for multiple comparisons and should be interpreted cautiously. The findings provide preliminary evidence that reduced histrelin doses, including 25 µg, may induce ovulation within 48 h in mares. However, this study did not demonstrate an advantage of pharmacopuncture over IM administration of the same reduced dose. Larger, fully randomized studies are required to confirm the efficacy of reduced-dose histrelin and determine whether administration at specific acupoints provides any additional effect.

articles.title: Impact of intrapartum ultrasound on mode of delivery guidance and adverse pregnancy outcomes in primigravidae undergoing vaginal trial labor.
articles.authors: Chen X, Li W, Li H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to analyze the impact of intrapartum ultrasound on mode of delivery guidance and the occurrence of adverse pregnancy outcomes in primigravidae undergoing a vaginal trial of labor.
METHODS: A total of 200 primigravidae admitted to our hospital from January 2021 to December 2022 were included as the subjects of this study. They were randomly divided into a control group and a study group, with 100 cases in each group. The control group underwent the vaginal finger test, while the study group underwent a combination of the vaginal finger test and intrapartum ultrasound. The consistency between the vaginal finger test and intrapartum ultrasound in determining fetal position was evaluated in the study group, and the mode of delivery and pregnancy outcomes were compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: The consistency of fetal occiput position between ultrasound and vaginal finger examination in the study group was 54.5% for occiput anterior position, 46.1% for occiput posterior position, and 31.4% for occiput transverse position, with an overall consistency of 46.5%. There was no significant difference in the cesarean section rate between the two groups. The rate of vaginal delivery in the control group was significantly lower than that in the study group, while the rate of perineal laceration was significantly higher in the control group. There were no significant differences in adverse outcomes for mothers and newborns between the two groups. The Angle of Progression (AOP) during natural vaginal delivery was significantly higher than that in other delivery modes, while AOP in cesarean section was significantly lower than that in other delivery modes. The head-perineum distance (HPD) during natural vaginal delivery was significantly lower than that in other delivery modes, while HPD in cesarean section was significantly higher than that in other delivery modes.
CONCLUSION: Intrapartum ultrasound serves as an important adjunct in a vaginal trial of labor for primigravidae, aiding healthcare providers in accurately determining fetal head position, reducing the rate of perineal laceration, and increasing the rate of vaginal delivery. Notably, there are significant differences in ultrasound findings between women undergoing natural vaginal delivery and those with other delivery modes.

articles.title: Are prophylactic antibiotics routinely necessary in laparoscopic adnexal surgery? A multicenter cohort study.
articles.authors: Miyata H, Kobayashi E, Yasuda M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The benefit of routine prophylactic antibiotics for clean laparoscopic adnexal surgery remains unclear. We evaluated whether pre-incision cefazolin reduces the incidence of 30-day surgical site infections (SSIs), and we identified perioperative risk factors for SSIs.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using clinical data from Osaka University and six affiliated hospitals. Among 1,865 patients who underwent laparoscopic adnexal surgery for benign conditions, 1,678 were included after specified exclusions. Patients received either pre-incision cefazolin (n = 1,415) or no prophylaxis (n = 263) according to institutional policy. The primary outcome was the incidence of SSI during the 30-day postoperative interval, classified according to CDC criteria. The association between prophylaxis and SSI was evaluated using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Propensity scores were estimated using age, body mass index, diabetes mellitus, endometriosis, and previous abdominal surgery. Risk factors for SSI were assessed using multivariable logistic regression analysis. Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed by repeating the same IPTW procedure within specified subgroups, and procedure-specific supplementary analyses were performed for ovarian cystectomy.
RESULTS: SSI occurred in 1.1% of patients in both groups: 16/1,415 in the cefazolin group and 3/263 in the non-antibiotic group. In IPTW-adjusted analyses, the incidence of SSI did not differ between groups (1.1% vs. 1.2%; p = 0.915). In multivariable analysis, operative time ≥120 min was associated with SSI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.54, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.41-8.85). In supplementary analyses restricted to an ovarian cystectomy subgroup, uterine manipulator use was associated with SSI (aOR 4.03, 95% CI 1.26-12.90).
CONCLUSION: Routine prophylactic cefazolin was not associated with a significantly lower incidence of 30-day SSI after clean laparoscopic adnexal surgery. Given few SSI events and the potential for residual confounding, our findings support further evaluation of a selective rather than routine approach to prophylactic antibiotic use.

articles.title: Endogenous replication stress creates a unique therapeutic window for ALC1 targeting.
articles.authors: Aubuchon LN, Wong DH, Greenberg SF et al.
articles.abstract: Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) are approved for homologous recombination-deficient (HRD) high-grade serous ovarian cancers. However, their durable benefit is severely limited by resistance and hematologic toxicity. PARPi are also largely ineffective in homologous recombination-proficient tumors, especially CCNE1-amplified cancers, which remain therapeutically intractable. We show that loss of the chromatin remodeler Amplified in Liver Cancer 1 (ALC1) markedly sensitizes serous ovarian cancer cells, xenografts, and patient-derived models to PARPi across both HRD and CCNE1-amplified contexts. Unlike other PARPi sensitizers, ALC1 depletion circumvents clinically relevant PARPi resistance while sparing BRCA wild-type and heterozygous nonmalignant cells, revealing an unusually wide therapeutic index. Mechanistically, this selectivity is dictated by intrinsic replication-stress burden, which renders cancer cells uniquely dependent on ALC1-mediated stress tolerance. Accordingly, collective data from cell line and patient samples reveal endogenous phospho-T21 RPA2 as a predictive biomarker of PARPi responsiveness following ALC1 targeting. These findings establish ALC1 targeting as a mechanistically grounded, biomarker-guided strategy to safely expand PARPi efficacy and support the clinical advancement of ALC1 inhibitors currently in Phase I trials.

articles.title: Organization of the first national workshop for families in Switzerland concerned with hereditary cancer syndromes.
articles.authors: Glick S, Aceti M, Barton CM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although Patient and Public Involvement (PPI) workshops with families affected by hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes can benefit both affected individuals and their support networks, PPI workshops are rarely being organized. This article presents the planning and implementation of a one-day PPI workshop for families affected by Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer (HBOC) or Lynch Syndrome (LS) in Switzerland.
WORKSHOP DESIGN & IMPLEMENTATION: The event was funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation and planned over a 12-month period. The program included expert sessions presented by clinicians and researchers; moderated, small-group participatory exchanges exploring patients' and families' unmet health, psychosocial and educational needs; and interactions with patient advocates. Participant satisfaction surveys were analyzed using descriptive statistics.
RESULTS: One hundred and five adults attended the workshop in Bern in May 2025, with representation from the three major linguistic regions of Switzerland. Almost 75% of participants reported a personal genetic predisposition to cancer. Most respondents were very satisfied or satisfied with the workshop (92%), and nearly all (96%) found the presentations engaging, with the topic of immunotherapy as an emerging treatment rated highest. The participatory exchange sessions were the most valued component of the workshop overall (97% positive feedback).
CONCLUSIONS: We provide proof of concept for the feasibility and positive impact of organizing a national workshop for families affected by HBOC and LS. The participatory nature of the workshop allowed affected individuals and their support networks to communicate unmet needs related to their personal experiences and suggest future avenues for research.

articles.title: Early apical release versus conventional (non-early apical release) holmium laser enucleation of the prostate: a systematic review and meta-analysis of postoperative urinary incontinence and functional outcomes.
articles.authors: Mansour I, Shaheen M, Elkenany AJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite proven safety, efficacy, and durability of Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP), postoperative transient stress urine incontinence (SUI) was a concern for years. A technical modification of the original HoLEP, namely early apical release (EAR) has been suggested to reduce postoperative SUI. This study aimed to collate available evidence on the impact of EAR on the post HoLEP SUI and functional outcomes in comparison to conventional (non-EAR) HoLEP.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive literature search was performed until February 2026. The Search focused on studies comparing EAR with conventional HoLEP. The primary outcome was the impact of each technique on SUI. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Cochrane Risk of Bias-2 tool. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using random-effects models. Analyses were performed using RevMan 5.3.
RESULTS: Five studies with 2821 patients were analyzed. EAR showed a lower risk of early SUI at 4-6 weeks (RR0.47, 95%CI 0.37-0.60; I² = 0.0%). At mid-term follow-up, 3-4 months, EAR was associated with lower risk of SUI (RR 0.44, 95%CI 0.28-0.69; I² = 0%). At 6-12 months, there were no significant differences in urinary incontinence. EAR had fewer intraoperative and late postoperative complications. However, EAR showed more early postoperative complications, mainly Clavien-Dindo grade I-II. Despite this, hospital stay was similar between both groups. Functional outcomes, including IPSS, quality of life, Qmax, and PVR, were comparable between groups throughout follow-up. Lastly, Operative time, enucleation time, morcellation time, and catheter duration were also comparable.
CONCLUSION: EAR reduces early SUI while maintaining comparable functional outcomes compared to conventional HoLEP. These findings indicate EAR is an effective continence-optimizing modification during HoLEP.

articles.title: Gastrointestinal and Urological Tract Injuries During Cesarean Delivery: A Surgical Review With National Epidemiologic Data.
articles.authors: Zeineddin A, Olivencia-Delgado MN, Nasef KE et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCesarean delivery is the most common major surgical procedure performed worldwide, accounting for approximately one-third of US deliveries. Gastrointestinal (GI) and urological (URO) tract injuries are uncommon but disproportionately morbid complications. Increasing complexity, particularly repeat cesarean and placenta accreta spectrum (PAS), and uneven on-site subspecialty coverage have expanded the role of general surgeons as intraoperative consultants for these injuries, especially outside large tertiary centers.MethodsWe analyzed the National Inpatient Sample (NIS, 2005-2019) to characterize the contemporary epidemiology, predictors, and outcomes of GI/URO injuries during cesarean delivery, complemented by a literature review focused on intraoperative recognition and management principles most relevant to the consulting general surgeon.ResultsAmong 3 816 895 cesarean deliveries, 8891 involved a documented GI/URO injury requiring surgical intervention (≈233 per 100 000). Bladder injuries predominated (78.2%), followed by bowel repair (13.3%), bowel resection (7.8%), and ureteral injuries (1.3%). Injuries were associated with markedly higher ICU admission (3.4% vs 0.2%), respiratory failure (1.7% vs 0.1%), in-hospital mortality (0.22% vs 0.01%), and resource utilization. Prior cesarean delivery was the strongest predictor of URO injury (OR 2.92; 95% CI 2.71-3.13).ConclusionsGI/URO injuries during cesarean delivery are uncommon but highly morbid, and the operative complexity that produces them is rising. With variable on-site subspecialty coverage, the general surgeon is frequently the first operative consultant. Familiarity with intraoperative principles, prevention strategies in high-risk cases, structured recognition, and initial repair or damage-control temporization should be considered a core competency for surgeons covering trauma, rural, or emergency general surgery call.

articles.title: The importance of CSF distribution for target values and risk profiling for idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus shunt surgery.
articles.authors: Warntjes M, Georgiopoulos C, Saridakis N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus is characterized by gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary incontinence. Symptom improvement can be achieved by shunt surgery, especially regarding gait difficulties. This study investigated whether CSF volumetry can define postoperative target values associated with clinical improvement and, secondly, predict potential non-response or overdrainage complications.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Forty-seven patients with iNPH were prospectively followed for three years after shunt surgery. Quantitative MRI was performed at baseline and at 3, 12, and 36 months postoperatively. Automatic segmentation yielded ventricular volume, subarachnoid CSF volume, ratio of ventricular and total CSF volume and ratio of total brain volume and intracranial volume. Clinical outcome was assessed using the Hellström iNPH scale. Patients were classified as responders and non-responders and further subdivided with and without overdrainage complications.
RESULTS: Eighty-seven percent of patients were classified as responders. Responders demonstrated a 26% reduction in ventricular volume(139 ml at baseline and 102 ml at three years) accompanied by a >60% improvement in iNPH score. The ventricular/total CSF ratio decreased from 0.34 to 0.25. Non-responders exhibited low ratios already at baseline, due to a significantly higher subarachnoid CSF volume. Overdrainage-related postural headaches were associated withlow subarachnoid CSF volume, younger age, higher baseline iNPH score, and higher BPV/ICV ratio. Aggregate z-scores combining multiple baseline metrics improved discrimination between responders, non-responders, and patients at risk for overdrainage.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline volumetry may provide target values and risk stratification for shunt surgery in iNPH. Responders showed a reduction of ventricular volume to ∼100 ml and ventricle/total CSF ratio to ∼0.25. High subarachnoid CSF volumes at baseline, however, was associated with poor response, while low subarachnoid CSF volume indicated an increased risk of postural headache. Quantitative CSF segmentation may improve patient selection and postoperative management in iNPH.

articles.title: Identification and Validation of Biomarkers Associated With Mitochondrial Dynamics in Preeclampsia.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Liu X, Liu M, Chen C et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Despite studies highlighting mitochondrial dynamics in preeclampsia (PE), the regulatory mechanisms of mitochondrial dynamics-related genes (MD-RGs) in PE remain unclear. This study aims to explore these mechanisms.
METHODS: PE-related datasets (GSE10588 and GSE98224) and 23 MD-RGs were used. Differential expression, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, machine learning (ML), gene expression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were conducted to screen for PE biomarkers. A nomogram was established to predict PE occurrence. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and immunoinfiltration analysis were subsequently performed.
RESULTS: Reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was used to measure biomarker expression, identifying GLUL, GPX3, and KCND2 as PE biomarkers. GPX3 and KCND2 were upregulated, whereas GLUL was downregulated in PE. These biomarkers had area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.7-0.9 in the datasets, and the integrated nomogram reached 0.973, indicating precision in PE prediction. GSEA revealed that ribosome and E. coli coenriched KCND2 and GLUL. Immunoinfiltration analysis revealed that Tregs were significantly correlated with KCND2 and GLUL among differential immune cells in PE patients versus controls. Finally, expression validation revealed that GLUL was significantly upregulated and expressed in the control group, whereas GPX3 and KCND2 were highly expressed in PE patients, with KCND2 reaching significant levels, which is consistent with the bioinformatics analysis.
CONCLUSION: In total, 3 mitochondrial dynamics-related biomarkers (GLUL, GPX3, and KCND2) were identified, and the biomarker-based nomogram was used to predict the onset risk of PE patients. The mining of these biomarkers contributed to an in-depth understanding of the pathogenesis of MD-RGs in PE.

articles.title: Laparoscopic Versus Laparotomy for Cytoreductive Surgery in Advanced Ovarian Cancer: A Prospective Cohort Study Comparing Surgical Outcomes, Postoperative Complications, Quality of Life, and Survival.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Yang G, Yang J, Chen Y
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare surgical outcomes, postoperative complications, quality of life, and survival between laparoscopic surgery and laparotomy for cytoreductive surgery in patients with advanced ovarian cancer.
METHODS: This cohort study included 60 patients with FIGO Stage III-IV advanced ovarian cancer, allocated to the control group or the study group. Quality of life was measured. Overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and progression-free survival (PFS) were analyzed.
RESULTS: Laparoscopic surgery significantly reduced operative time, blood loss, time to bowel recovery, and chemotherapy initiation. It also resulted in higher lymph node yield and optimal cytoreduction rate. Postoperative complication rates, including hypokalemia, hypoproteinemia, wound infection, and venous thrombosis, were significantly lower in the laparoscopic group. Quality of life improved significantly post-treatment in the laparoscopic group. Five-year OS rates were 75.0% vs. 51.9% (p = 0.055), DFS rates were 75.0% vs. 51.9% (p = 0.057), and PFS rates were 75.0% vs. 51.9% (p = 0.072) for laparoscopic and laparotomy groups, respectively. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed trends favoring the laparoscopic group, with OS approaching statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: Laparoscopic cytoreductive surgery in advanced ovarian cancer improves perioperative outcomes, reduces complications, and enhances postoperative recovery while maintaining comparable long-term survival outcomes to laparotomy.

articles.title: Identification of Risk-Related Prenatal Medication Exposure Profiles for Childhood Asthma Using the Bayesian Profile Regression: A Cohort Study Using the POMME Cohort.
articles.authors: Russo S, Bénévent J, Beau AB
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify prenatal medication exposure profiles associated with childhood asthma.
METHODS: This population-based cohort study used data from the POMME (PrescriptiOn Médicaments Mères Enfants) cohort, including 18 851 children born in the Haute-Garonne area (France) in 2010 and 2015, and followed until 2023. Prenatal exposure was defined as medications dispensed to mothers during pregnancy, classified by Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical subclasses, assessed separately for each trimester as none, one dispensing, or at least two dispensings. Childhood asthma from Age 4 years onward was identified using an algorithm based on dispensing of asthma medications. Bayesian profile regression was applied to simultaneously cluster children according to prenatal medication exposure profiles and asthma occurrence. High-risk profiles were characterised by predominant medication classes, timing of exposure and maternal and infant characteristics.
RESULTS: Seventeen prenatal medication exposure profiles were identified. Six profiles were associated with a higher average risk of childhood asthma compared with the overall population risk (15.2%). High-risk profiles were characterised by repeated exposure throughout pregnancy to medications for acid-related disorders, thyroid hormones, antibiotics, asthma medications and antihistamines, as well as by combinations involving antibiotics, nasal medications and cold medicines in late pregnancy. Mothers in high-risk profiles more frequently presented chronic conditions and pregnancy-related complications.
CONCLUSION: This exploratory study identified prenatal medication exposure profiles associated with childhood asthma using a semi-supervised Bayesian approach. This method highlights combinations and critical windows that may warrant further investigation and supports Bayesian profile regression as a useful tool for signal detection in perinatal pharmacoepidemiology.

articles.title: Second-Generation Synthesis of the Male Contraceptive YCT-529.
articles.authors: Gantasala N, Cheryala N, Georg GI
articles.abstract: We report a practical synthesis of the nonhormonal male contraceptive YCT-529. The method features key transformations: Grignard-mediated acetylation, the α-methylenation of a methyl ketone, and pyrrole formation via the Stetter and Paal-Knorr reaction sequence. It avoids iridium and palladium catalysts, overcoming the major limitations of an earlier synthesis. The current scalable synthesis proceeds in 6 steps from bromochromene 4 in 51% overall yield and does not require chromatographic purification.

articles.title: Early β-hCG Trajectories After Single-Dose Methotrexate Treatment and Their Predictive Value for Treatment Failure in Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Zhang J, Ma Y
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify distinct early beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) trajectories following single-dose methotrexate (MTX) treatment for tubal ectopic pregnancy and to evaluate their associations with treatment outcomes and potential value for Day-7 posttreatment risk stratification.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included hemodynamically stable patients with confirmed tubal ectopic pregnancy treated with single-dose MTX. Among 828 patients in the all-clinical cohort, 373 had quantitative β-hCG measurements at Day 0, Day 4, and Day 7 and were included in trajectory modeling. Group-based trajectory modeling was applied to log-transformed β-hCG values. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations with overall treatment failure and clinical treatment failure, while exploratory Day-7 risk-stratification analyses assessed model discrimination, calibration, and net benefit.
RESULTS: Overall treatment failure occurred in 94 of 373 patients (25.2%), and clinical treatment failure occurred in 45 patients. A three-class quadratic model identified a rapid decline class (56.3%), delayed decline class (28.2%), and persistent elevation/slow decline class (15.5%). Compared with the rapid decline class, the persistent elevation/slow decline class was associated with higher odds of overall treatment failure (adjusted OR [aOR] = 85.42, 95% CI: 25.64-284.55) and clinical treatment failure (aOR = 52.65, 95% CI: 11.22-246.88), although estimates for clinical failure were imprecise. In the exploratory Day-7 model for overall treatment failure, the apparent AUC increased from 0.775 for the base clinical model to 0.862 after adding trajectory class (p < 0.001). Trajectory classes also showed heterogeneity in clinical failure within conventional Day 4-Day 7 β-hCG response categories.
CONCLUSION: Early β-hCG trajectories were associated with treatment outcomes after single-dose MTX and may complement conventional Day-7 posttreatment reassessment. Their clinical utility requires prospective multicenter external validation before routine use.

articles.title: LSD1 exerts crucial functions to drive the progression of meiotic prophase I during spermatogenesis.
articles.journal: Journal of genetics and genomics = Yi chuan xue bao
articles.authors: Zhu T, Qin S, Dong Y et al.
articles.abstract: Epigenetic modifications are critical determinants governing the proper initiation and progression of gametogenesis. Accumulating evidence has indicated that epigenetic dysregulation underlies the pathogenesis of infertility. However, detailed information on the individual powerful roles of these epigenetic enzymes in facilitating programmed meiosis remains elusive. This study indicates that lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) plays critical roles during meiotic prophase I in mouse spermatogenesis. Germ cell-specific deletion of the Lsd1 gene in male mice caused meiotic arrest at the pachytene stage, ultimately leading to infertility. In primary spermatocytes of Lsd1-deficient mice, compromised homologous chromosome synapsis and DNA double-strand break repair activated the DNA damage checkpoint pathway, triggering spermatocyte apoptosis. Mechanistically, LSD1 directly binds to the promoters of meiotic genes, including Prdm9 and Rpa2, to regulate their expression during meiosis. PRDM9 and RPA2 are upregulated upon LSD1 loss and are essential for homologous recombination and DNA double-strand break repair. The promoters of Prdm9 and Rpa2 are also occupied by H3K4me2, whose levels increase upon LSD1 loss. Collectively, this study highlights the crucial role of LSD1 in orchestrating meiotic genes, possibly through its demethylase activity during spermatogenesis, and may help explain the pathology of non-obstructive azoospermia in humans.

articles.title: Prenatal maternal phosphatidylcholine and children's behavior and cognition through 4 years of age: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Hunter SK, Hoffman MC, Law AJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The increasing popularity of choline supplements may prompt patients to seek advice on safe, effective doses during prenatal visits. The rationale for prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements stems from the fetal developmental role of the α7-nicotinic cholinergic receptor gene CHRNA7, which is associated with schizophrenia, attention deficit disorder, and autism spectrum disorder. Fetal brain developmental problems, including those linked to CHRNA7, convey a risk for these mental illnesses. Choline derived from maternal phosphatidylcholine intake activates fetal α7-nicotinic receptors, which facilitate brain neurosynaptic development, observed after birth as robust inhibition of cerebral neurophysiological responses to repeated stimuli. A previous study found that maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine, compared with placebo, significantly improved newborns' neurophysiology and thereby decreased the children's attention and social withdrawal problems at 40 months of age.
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine, compared with placebo, in a larger randomized clinical trial supports fetal brain development to decrease childhood attention and social behavioral problems and to increase cognitive performance.
STUDY DESIGN: A clinical trial at the University of Colorado Hospital Prenatal Clinics and affiliated community hospitals randomized 206 women to 9000 mg phosphatidylcholine (the form of choline occurring naturally in food) or placebo from 16 weeks' gestation through delivery. From 18 months to 4 years of age, 142 children were assessed by their parents using the Child Behavior Checklist for ages 1.5-5 years. The 2 primary outcomes were withdrawn and attention problems. A secondary outcome was the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence-Fourth Edition Full Scale Intelligence Quotient. Cerebral neurophysiological inhibition, assessed soon after birth, confirmed the effects of phosphatidylcholine on fetal developmental.
RESULTS: Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements compared with placebo resulted in fewer children with multiple or pervasive withdrawn problems and increased Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence-Fourth Edition Full Scale Intelligence Quotient (mean difference, 7.78; 95% confidence interval, 1.88-13.7) (P=.010). Attention problems did not decrease significantly (P=.051). In exploratory analyses, 11 children had Child Behavior Checklist autism spectrum T-scores in the clinical…

articles.title: Association of Bisphenol A exposure on hormone-associated benign and malignant disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Soleman SR, Desrini S, Setiya DFJ et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bisphenol A (BPA) and its analogs have garnered considerable public and scientific attention due to their endocrine-disrupting properties in humans. This systematic review aims to address the question of whether exposure to Bisphenol A is associated with the risk of hormone-associated benign and malignant disorders.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted from inception to February 2024 to identify eligible human case-control studies investigating exposure to BPA and its analogs. The study selection and data extraction processes were performed independently and in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. All analyses were conducted using Review Manager (RevMan) software, version 5.4.
RESULTS: Following the removal of duplicate records, 661 eligible articles were identified, with 44 studies ultimately included in the final analysis. Bisphenol A was the most frequently investigated contaminant, whereas its analogs were only reported in one study. Most studies reported PCOS, breast cancers, benign and malignant endometrial disorders and only one study reported prostate cancer. The result indicate that BPA exposure is associated with PCOS (SMD=1.19; CI95: 0.70-1.67), benign endometrial disorders (SMD=0.94; CI95: 0.15, 1.73), breast cancer (SMD=0.68; CI95: 0.44-0.92). Nevertheless, these associations demonstrate considerable heterogeneity.
CONCLUSION: Bisphenol A exposure is associated with the risk endocrine-related benign and malignant disorders, such as PCOS, breast cancer, and benign endometrial disorders. Nevertheless, the interpretation of these findings is limited by substantial heterogeneity, largely attributable to small sample sizes in case and control groups.

articles.title: Strategy-Based Comparison of Fresh Double Embryo Transfer Versus Sequential Single Embryo Transfers in Women With Adequate Blastocyst Availability.
articles.authors: Weng TH, Lee CC, Lee KS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the cumulative reproductive outcomes of two embryo transfer strategies in women with adequate blastocyst availability: immediate fresh double embryo transfer (DET) and a sequential strategy consisting of fresh single embryo transfer (SET) followed by frozen-thawed SET derived from the same retrieval cohort.
DESIGN: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Taipei MacKay Memorial Hospital using clinical data from January 2017 to December 2023.
SETTING: A single tertiary reproductive center.
SUBJECTS: Women younger than 40 years with normal ovarian reserve and ≥ two good-quality blastocysts obtained from a single stimulation cycle.
EXPOSURE: Patients underwent either fresh DET or sequential SET that included a second transfer within three years.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Cumulative clinical pregnancy rate (CCPR) and cumulative live birth rate (CLBR) per retrieval cycle.
RESULTS: A total of 256 patients were included: 135 in the sequential SET group (33.39 ± 3.13 years) and 121 in the fresh DET group (35.41 ± 2.87 years). The CCPR was significantly higher in the sequential SET group than in the fresh DET group (86.7% vs.61.2%; RR: 1.42, 95% CI: 1.21-1.66), as was the CLBR (63.7% vs.51.2%; RR: 1.24, 95% CI: 1.00-1.54). Although the initial pregnancy rate was lower in the group who would have sequential SET than fresh DET (41.4% vs.61.2%), cumulative pregnancy outcomes improved substantially after the second transfer in the SET cohort. The miscarriage rate did not differ significantly between the sequential SET and fresh DET groups (24.7% vs. 14.9%; RR: 1.67, 95% CI: 0.89-3.13), whereas the twin pregnancy rate was markedly lower (0% vs.14.9%, p < 0.001) in the sequential SET group. Based on pooled neonatal data irrespective of plurality, mean gestational age (38.47 vs.37.41 weeks, p = 0.69) and mean birth weight (3065 vs.2773 g, p = 0.09) were comparable between groups. Preterm births per oocyte retrieval cycle were significantly less frequent following sequential SET than fresh DET (2 vs.16, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with favorable embryo availability, sequential SET demonstrated higher cumulative reproductive outcomes within a strategy-based framework than fresh DET. These findings reflect differences in embryo utilization pathways rather than in isolated transfer efficacy; they should be interpreted in the context of treatment continuation and cohort selection.

articles.title: The Effect of Male Partner Smoking on Cumulative Live Birth after In vitro Fertilization (IVF): a Large Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Verwoerd G, West R, Cai J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the cumulative live birth rates after one oocyte retrieval among smoke-free couples and couples where only the male partner smoked cigarettes (after using fresh and frozen embryos).
DESIGN: Prospective cohort study SUBJECTS: : 1,388 couples undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatment (one oocyte retrieval each) between 1 August 2019 to 10 June 2021 at a tertiary level hospital IVF center in Kunming, China. Follow-up data were collected for up to three years and nine months after embryo transfer and four years after recruitment of the first couple.
EXPOSURE: Cigarette smoking among male partners MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: : Cumulative live birth and early pregnancy loss rates RESULTS: : After adjusting for woman's age, man's age, woman's BMI, man's BMI, woman's educational level, man's educational level, duration of infertility, primary versus secondary infertility, insemination method and baseline infertility cause variables, the relative risk (RR) for achieving a cumulative live birth for couples where the male partner consumed < 20 cigarettes per day was not significantly different from smoke-free couples (RR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.84 - 1.02) but 19.0% lower for couples where the male partner consumed ≥ 20 cigarettes per day (RR = 0.81, 95% CI 0.71 - 0.93). The adverse effect of male partner smoking was significant before achieving a fetal heartbeat in both groups of smokers, but more obvious in heavy smokers (RR = 0.89, 95% CI 0.81 - 0.98 and 0.78, 95% CI 0.68 - 0.89). Once a fetal heartbeat had been established, there was no evidence of any further impact on cumulative live birth rate.
CONCLUSION: Couples who need IVF treatment should be counselled that male partner smoking could reduce their chances of having a baby.

articles.title: Health-Related Quality of Life, Mood, and Sexual Function in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS): Assessing the Impact of Combined Oral Contraceptive Pills and Metformin Therapy (characters with spaces: 175, limit 125).
articles.authors: Satish S, Ewy J, Coutifaris C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To study the effects of combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs), metformin, and their combination on health-related quality of life, depression, anxiety, and sexual function in women with hyperandrogenic polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) and elevated BMI.
DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a double-blind, double-dummy, parallel, randomized controlled trial (COMET-PCOS).
SUBJECTS: 240 women aged 21-40 years with hyperandrogenic PMOS and BMI ≥25 kg/m2, randomized to COCP, metformin, or COCP+metformin; analyses were subset to subjects with a response at both baseline and end of study.
INTERVENTION: Six months of COCP (20μg ethinyl estradiol/0.15 mg desogestrel), metformin XR 2000 mg/day, or combination therapy.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Changes from baseline to study end in modified PCOS Health Related Quality of Life (mPCOSQ) domains, Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI Y-1 and Y-2), Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) and Female Sexual Distress Scale (FSDS).
RESULTS: Compared to baseline, mPCOSQ scores improved across all domains in the combination group (n=60, p<0.01), COCP group (n=56, p<0.01, except menstrual health and acne domains), and metformin group (n=51, p<0.05, except body hair and weight domains). Depressive symptoms and depression prevalence were unchanged in the COCP and combined group but improved in the metformin group (p<0.001). State anxiety improved in the metformin and combined groups (p<0.01); trait anxiety improved across all groups (p<0.05). FSFI scores were lower in the COCP group for the desire (p<0.001) and arousal (p=0.03) domains with no difference in total score (p=0.07); however, sexual distress decreased in both the COCP (p=0.03) and metformin groups (p=0.03). There were no significant changes in the prevalence of sexual dysfunction in any group.
CONCLUSION: Although COCPs and metformin are commonly used to manage PMOS, limited data exist on their impact on mental and sexual health. Our study demonstrates favorable or neutral effects of these therapies on mental health and quality of life in women with hyperandrogenic PMOS and elevated BMI. Metformin improved depressive symptoms and anxiety, while COCPs produced modest reductions in sexual desire without increasing sexual distress or dysfunction. These findings provide clinically relevant data for counseling women with PMOS, a group at high risk for mental health disorders.

articles.title: Fertility, pregnancy, and women's health in bronchiectasis: a multicenter study and ELF-EMBARC patient survey.
articles.authors: Boehm-Cohen L, Pollock J, Kompatsiari E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchiectasis in women of reproductive age is increasingly recognized, yet data on fertility and pregnancy outcomes remain limited.
RESEARCH QUESTION: What are fertility characteristics, pregnancy outcomes, and patient-reported reproductive health experiences in women with bronchiectasis?
STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study across EMBARC-affiliated centers including women with bronchiectasis and pregnancy between 2012 and 2023. Clinical, pulmonary, obstetric, and neonatal data were collected. In parallel, an international patient survey assessed fertility, pregnancy, and hormonal influences on disease. Statistical analyses included comparative and correlation testing.
RESULTS: Eighty-three women contributed data from 121 pregnancies and 123 neonates. Mean age at conception was 29.5 years. Assisted reproductive technologies were used in 32.1% of pregnancies, more frequently in primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) than other etiologies (48.5% vs. 8.7%, P=0.004). Lung function remained stable during and after pregnancy. Exacerbations occurred in 58.6% of pregnancies. Mean gestational age was 38 weeks and mean birth weight was 2.99 kg. Pre-pregnancy FEV1 correlated with birth weight (ρ=0.42, P=0.001) and gestational age (ρ=0.25, P=0.042). Neonatal outcomes were generally favorable. Survey data (n=629) demonstrated an early onset of menopause in women with bronchiectasis diagnosed before age 50 years compared to after 50 years. Women with PCD reported difficulties conceiving more often than women with early onset bronchiectasis without PCD.
INTERPRETATION: Pregnancy in women with bronchiectasis is frequently complicated by exacerbations and low neonatal birth weight. Subfertility is primarily driven by PCD, while non-PCD bronchiectasis shows rates similar to the general population. Pre-pregnancy lung function is associated with neonatal outcomes, supporting the importance of pulmonary optimization and multidisciplinary care before and during pregnancy.

articles.title: "Mirabegron as a protective agent in testosterone-induced prostate and seminal vesicle toxicity: Insights into PCNA and TLR-4 pathways".
articles.authors: Abdel-Hameed SS, El-Daly M, Matouk AI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Testosterone is an androgenic hormone and one of the anabolic steroids used in the management of conditions related to hypogonadism as well as to enhance performance in bodybuilders. Prolonged use of testosterone has been linked to adverse outcomes on male reproductive organs. Mirabegron, a β3- adrenergic receptor agonist, is used to alleviate symptoms of overactive bladder and recently, it has shown substantial antioxidant and antinflammmatory effects.
AIM: This study was designed to investigate the potential protective effects of mirabegron against testosterone induced-toxicity on prostate and seminal vesicle tissues via modulating oxidative stress, inflammation and androgenic activities.
METHODS: Male Wistar rats (200-250 g) were divided into three groups (n = 8); control; received vehicle, testosterone; received testosterone enanthate (3 mg/kg, S.C.), and testosterone + mirabegron; received testosterone (3 mg/kg, S.C.) and mirabegron (10 mg/kg, P.O.) concurrently. Treatments and vehicle were administrated daily for 4 weeks.
RESULTS: Mirabegron attenuated the testosterone-induced changes on serum levels of testosterone, FSH and LH as well as reduced prostatic 5α-reductase 1 (5AR1) (0.9433 ± 0.09597 ng/mg) levels. Mirabegron improved the testosterone-induced histopathological alterations of the prostate and seminal vesicle tissues. Further, it reduced prostatic TGF-β1 level (42.93 ± 3.593 pg/mg) and increased GSH content in both prostatic and seminal vesicle tissues ((25.59 ± 0.8877 and 31.70 ± 0.895 µmol/mg; respectively. Additionally, mirabegron prophylactic treatment suppressed testosterone-induced increase of oxidative stress, inflammatory and proliferative mediators, including MDA, total nitrite, iNOS, TLR4, IL-1β, PCNA, and procaspase-3.
CONCLUSION: Mirabegron mitigated the damage on prostate and seminal vesicle tissues induced by testosterone through its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities.

articles.title: Functional and Surgical Outcomes of Nerve-Sparing Approaches in Deep Infiltrating Endometriosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Aloslani J, Alnwman J, Alsahli H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the surgical safety and functional outcomes of nerve-sparing surgery in the management of deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE).
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and LILACS were searched from January 2000 to August 2025 for studies evaluating nerve-sparing surgery in women with surgically confirmed DIE.
METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included women with surgically confirmed DIE who underwent nerve-sparing procedures. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Pooled estimates with 95% confidence intervals were calculated, and statistical heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic.
TABULATION, INTEGRATION AND RESULTS: Sixteen studies involving 1623 women were included. The pooled conversion rate to open surgery was 0.3%, while intraoperative and postoperative complication rates were 1.5% and 9.8%, respectively. Urinary voiding dysfunction occurred in 6.9% of patients, and Low Anterior Resection Syndrome occurred in 10.2%. The pooled postoperative Female Sexual Function Index score was 22.3. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across several functional outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Nerve-sparing surgery for DIE appears feasible and is associated with acceptable surgical and functional outcomes. However, the current evidence is limited, and substantial heterogeneity precludes conclusions regarding equivalence or superiority compared with conventional surgery. Further well-designed prospective and comparative studies are needed.

articles.title: Acetaminophen Use in Pregnancy: Evidence, Controversies, and Clinical Counseling.
articles.authors: Higgs AJ, Seif KE
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aimed to review the current evidence regarding acetaminophen use in pregnancy, evaluate reported associations with adverse neurodevelopmental and reproductive outcomes, and provide an evidence-based framework for clinical counseling and decision-making. A narrative review of the literature was performed, emphasizing large observational cohort studies, sibling-comparison analyses, pharmacokinetic data, and recent systematic reviews evaluating prenatal acetaminophen exposure and maternal-fetal outcomes. Acetaminophen is the most commonly used analgesic and antipyretic in pregnancy, with 50 to 65% of pregnant individuals reporting use. Although observational studies have reported associations between prenatal acetaminophen exposure and adverse neurodevelopmental and reproductive outcomes, including attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, autism spectrum disorder, and cryptorchidism, these findings remain inconsistent and are subject to substantial confounding, particularly by indication. Large, methodologically rigorous studies incorporating sibling-controlled analyses have demonstrated attenuation or disappearance of these associations, suggesting that underlying maternal conditions may account for the observed risks. Pharmacokinetic studies demonstrate placental transfer of acetaminophen, although fetal metabolism differs because of limited glucuronidation capacity. Current pharmacologic evidence does not support a causal relationship between standard maternal acetaminophen use and premature fetal ductus arteriosus closure. Current evidence does not support a causal relationship between typical prenatal acetaminophen exposure and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. Given the known risks of untreated maternal pain and fever, acetaminophen should remain the preferred first-line analgesic and antipyretic during pregnancy when clinically indicated. Patients should receive balanced, evidence-based counseling that acknowledges observational findings while emphasizing the limitations of current data. Use at the lowest effective dose for the shortest necessary duration remains appropriate clinical guidance.
KEY POINTS: · Early associations weaken in sibling studies.. · Current evidence does not support causality.. · Acetaminophen remains first-line medication in pregnancy..

articles.title: Sustained induction of PMOS-like phenotype in mice exposed to letrozole in drinking water.
articles.authors: Stevenson KA, Kerbus R, Anderson GM et al.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; formerly polycystic ovary syndrome) is the most common endocrinopathy affecting women of reproductive age, characterized by ovarian dysfunction and hyperandrogenism, with metabolic disturbances including insulin resistance and obesity also present for 50% of PMOS patients. Effective preclinical models are crucial for evaluating therapeutic interventions. However, current mouse models of hyperandrogenemia induced by aromatase inhibition typically rely on subcutaneous letrozole implants, which require surgical procedures and struggle to sustain PMOS-like phenotypes over an extended period necessary for thorough drug assessment. We hypothesized that an oral letrozole administration would provide extended maintenance of syndrome-like features. Female mice received letrozole either via subcutaneous implant (~1.67 mg/kg/day for 70 days) or orally in drinking water (~1 mg/kg/day for up to 130 days). Estrous cyclicity was monitored by vaginal cytology. Hormonal, metabolic, and histological assessments were performed. While a subcutaneous letrozole implant only sustained hyperandrogenic, metabolic and reproductive phenotypes for ~50 days, oral letrozole administration sustained complete anovulation for at least 100 days, maintaining a persistent diestrus stage. The oral letrozole treatment produced comprehensive PMOS-like features, including significantly elevated testosterone levels, increased luteinizing hormone concentration, pulse frequency and amplitude, enhanced hypothalamic androgen receptor expression, decreased hypothalamic progesterone receptor expression, cystic-like ovarian morphology, increased body weight, impaired insulin sensitivity, and elevated adiposity during the entire time of the treatment period (18 weeks), compared to the placebo treatment. Uterine weight was not decreased, suggesting normal circulating estrogen concentrations. These findings demonstrate that oral letrozole delivery offers a more accessible method of administration, resulting in a sustained induction of PMOS-like phenotypes. This approach effectively maintains both reproductive and metabolic features essential for comprehensive evaluation, thereby enhancing the model's utility for investigating therapeutic interventions in PMOS.

articles.title: Oropouche virus infection in pregnant women in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Brasil P, Nielsen-Saines K, Ferreira H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although adverse maternal and infant outcomes have been reported following Oropouche virus infection, the frequencies of these outcomes have not been compared with those in uninfected pregnancies. We followed up pregnant women from areas with Oropouche virus transmission in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil, to evaluate potential adverse maternal and infant outcomes following Oropouche virus exposure.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study across the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, we included pregnant women receiving prenatal care in municipalities with or at high risk of Oropouche virus outbreaks. Inclusion criteria were: ongoing risk of Oropouche virus infection at the time of prenatal visit; prenatal care at one of the participating sites; and willingness and ability to consent to and participate in the study. Exclusion criteria included infection with other arboviruses and fetal chromosomal abnormalities. Maternal blood, urine, and saliva were collected and tested for Oropouche virus by RT-PCR at enrolment and pregnancy endpoints. IgG and IgM serologies from maternal blood, placental tissue PCR, and immunohistochemistry were done. Confirmed infections were defined by: positive Oropouche virus PCR in blood, urine, saliva, or placenta; positive Oropouche virus placental immunohistochemistry; or Oropouche virus-specific IgM or IgG seroconversion. Possible infection was defined as one positive IgM result without a positive PCR. Negative results ruled out infection. Adverse maternal outcomes (reported by study investigators following up participants at study sites) were maternal death or disability, fetal loss, or haemorrhage; adverse infant outcomes were neonatal death or malformations. Relative risks adjusted for maternal age, other congenital infections, and use of tobacco, alcohol, and drugs during pregnancy for adverse maternal and infant outcomes were calculated.
FINDINGS: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Oct 8, 2025, 544 participants were enrolled: 130 (24%) with confirmed, 143 (26%) with possible, and 271 (50%) with no Oropouche virus infection. The median cycle threshold value of RT-PCR was 29·7 (IQR 25·8-34·9). Among the 130 women with confirmed infection, 104 (80%) developed detectable IgG antibodies. Symptoms were present in 80 (62%) women with confirmed infection, not necessarily associated with adverse outcomes (adjusted relative risk [aRR] 0∙84 [95% credible interval 0∙51-1∙21]). By the end of follow-up, the pregnancies of 119 women…

articles.title: Understanding Colorectal Cancer Screening Gaps Among Adults Aged 45-49.
articles.authors: Myers S, Ueland T, Davis ES et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The United States Preventative Task Force recommends initiating colorectal cancer (CRC) screening at age 45, but screening rates among 45-49 y-olds has been lower than older age groups. Reasons for low screening rates among younger individuals are not clear.
METHODS: Using Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 2022 to 2024, we investigated factors associated with CRC screening among adults aged 45-49; stratified analyses were conducted among the insured and uninsured. Among screened individuals, associations with undergoing endoscopy versus another screening modality were studied. We characterized preventative care behaviors including seeking primary care, time since last checkup, and completion of other age-appropriate cancer screening.
RESULTS: Of 50,132 individuals, 21,566 (42.6%) underwent CRC screening. Those with primary care physicians had higher odds of screening (odds ratio = 1.71; 95% confidence interval = 1.47-1.98, ref: no primary care physician), but increasing time since one's last visit was associated with decreasing odds of screening at all time intervals (5+ y ago: odds ratio = 0.29; 95% confidence interval = 0.23-0.38, ref: <1 y). Lower income, rural residence, no insurance, and lower educational attainment were associated with lower odds of screening. CRC screening was completed in only 41.3% of women who had mammograms and 48% who were screened for cervical cancer.
CONCLUSIONS: Uptake of CRC screening lags in adults aged 45-49, with differences in socioeconomic factors and preventative care utilization. A majority of eligible but unscreened individuals accessed other age-appropriate cancer screening tests, directing focus to patient- and provider-specific factors as potential targets for intervention.

articles.title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes as early indicators of long-term maternal atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Batista PG, Huntermann R, Montenegro MV et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) - including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), preterm birth, and fetal growth deviations - are emerging female-specific cardiovascular risk factors, but their association with long-term maternal atrial fibrillation (AF) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between APOs and subsequent AF.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central, and Scopus. We included population-based cohort studies comparing women with and without APOs and reporting incident maternal AF during follow-up. Time-to-event associations were synthesized, pooling hazard ratios (HRs) and corresponding 95 % confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: 12 population-based cohort studies including over 11 million women were analyzed. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy were associated with higher long-term risk of AF (HR 1.50; 95 % CI 1.38-1.62), as was preeclampsia (HR 1.45; 95 % CI 1.23-1.71). Preterm birth was also associated with increased AF risk (HR 1.29; 95 % CI 1.13-1.48). Delivery of a large for gestational age infant was associated with higher AF risk (HR 1.23; 95 % CI 1.13-1.34), whereas small for gestational age delivery showed an inverse association (HR 0.88; 95 % CI 0.80-0.97). For GDM, the association was more uncertain, with wide CIs and effect estimates suggesting an increased risk (HR 1.20; 95 % CI 0.84-1.72).
CONCLUSION: Hypertensive and vascular pregnancy complications are associated with elevated long-term maternal AF risk. Associations for gestational diabetes and fetal growth phenotypes were heterogeneous and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings support APOs as markers of later arrhythmic vulnerability.

articles.title: Detection of female genital tract abnormalities in antenatally detected fetal unilateral renal agenesis: Original retrospective case series with review of literature.
articles.authors: Resta C, Ntalianis KM, Cloke B et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In females, unilateral renal agenesis is associated with genital tract abnormalities, which can cause complications in childhood and beyond. However, its prevalence and characteristics are not consistently integrated into antenatal counselling.
METHODS: An original retrospective case series study (2005-2024) at Guy's and St Thomas' Hospital identified fetuses with isolated antenatally diagnosed unilateral renal agenesis from an Astraia database, with standardized 6-week postnatal imaging.
RESULTS: 110 cases of renal agenesis were identified. Of these, fifteen cases (n = 15) were excluded due to bilateral renal agenesis and five due to additional extra-renal abnormalities (n = 5). Outcome data was unavailable for 13 cases. Of the remaining 77 cases, 44 were males and 33 females. Of female fetuses,7 were diagnosed as pelvic kidneys postnatally, with no additional abnormalities present. From the remaining 26 cases with true unilateral renal agenesis, 5 (19%) were found to have associated genital tract abnormalities, which included uterovaginal fistula (n = 2) and Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome with a bicornuate uterus (n = 3) identified at the six-week postnatal scan.
CONCLUSION: Among female infants with isolated unilateral renal agenesis, 19% had associated genital tract malformations, underscoring the need for antenatal counselling and multidisciplinary approach beginning in the prenatal period.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of colposcopy-directed biopsy compared with LEEP histology: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Kowoll K, Hachenberg J, Stalp JL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colposcopy-directed biopsy is widely used in the diagnosis of cervical dysplasia, but its accuracy is variable. Reliable detection of clinically significant lesions (CIN2+) is essential for appropriate treatment. This study assessed its diagnostic performance using histology after LEEP as the reference standard and explored factors associated with discrepancies.
METHODS: 423 procedures were analyzed. Histological findings from colposcopy-directed biopsy were compared with the histology of the subsequent LEEP specimen. Diagnostic performance for CIN2+ was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and accuracy; agreement was assessed using weighted Cohen's kappa. Subgroup analyses considered transformation zone (TZ) type, age, and menopausal status. Multivariable logistic regression assessed predictors of histopathological underestimation.
RESULTS: Biopsy showed 97.0% sensitivity, 20.0% specificity, and 80.6% accuracy for CIN2+ detection. Exact histological agreement occured in 61.7% of procedures (κ = 0.31). Histopathological underestimation occurred in 12.3% and overestimation in 26.0%, indicating a tendency toward overestimation. Exact agreement decreased from 75.8% in TZ1 to 48.0% in TZ3 and from 65.2% in premenopausal to 48.4% in postmenopausal patients. Complete-case multivariable analysis included 227 procedures and 23 underestimation events. Compared with TZ1, TZ2 and TZ3 were independently associated with higher odds of underestimation other included covariates were not.
CONCLUSION: Colposcopy-directed biopsy shows high sensitivity but limited specificity for CIN2+ detection, with notable diagnostic discrepancies. Histological concordance was lower in patients with TZ 3 and in postmenopausal women, while TZ was independently associated with underestimation. These findings highlight the importance of considering anatomical and patient-related factors when interpreting biopsy results and planning clinical management.

articles.title: Sperm telomere length: A potential reflection of genomic integrity and environmental influences on male fertility.
articles.authors: Ghasemnejad-Berenji H, Parvin A, Farasati M et al.
articles.abstract: Infertility affects nearly one in six people worldwide, with male-related factors contributing to approximately half of all cases. Although conventional semen analysis remains central to the assessment of male fertility, it provides limited insight into sperm genomic competence and has only modest value for predicting reproductive outcomes. Sperm telomere length (STL) has therefore gained attention as a potential marker of germ-cell history, genomic integrity, and cumulative exposure to environmental and metabolic stress. Evidence from human studies, however, remains inconsistent. Associations between STL, conventional semen parameters, and assisted reproductive technology (ART) outcomes vary across studies, likely because of differences in study populations, sperm preparation and purification methods, somatic-cell contamination, sample size, confounder adjustment, outcome definitions, and analytical platforms. Among the most widely used methods, quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) provides a relative estimate of mean telomere length based on the telomere-to-single-copy-gene (T/S) ratio in bulk samples, whereas quantitative fluorescence in situ hybridization (qFISH) enables assessment of telomere-signal distributions at the single-cell level. Both approaches offer distinct advantages and limitations, and neither has demonstrated clear clinical superiority. This review integrates current biological, methodological, environmental, and clinical evidence and proposes a cautious mechanistic framework linking oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, telomeric DNA damage, chromatin organization, STL variation, and reproductive outcomes. While STL is biologically plausible as an investigational marker of sperm quality, current evidence is insufficient to support its routine clinical use. Larger, standardized, and well-controlled studies are needed to establish whether STL provides meaningful information beyond existing measures of male fertility.

articles.title: Congenital syphilis as a failure of the maternal-fetal prevention cascade: Clinical implications for pregnant migrant and structurally vulnerable women in high-income settings - an ESCMID study group for infections in Travellers and migrants (ESGITM) perspective.
articles.authors: Meduri AR, Ritacco IA, Capruzzi D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital syphilis remains a preventable but persistent cause of fetal loss, neonatal morbidity, and early-life complications. In high-income settings, its occurrence rarely reflects the absence of diagnostic tools or effective therapy; but more often exposes missed opportunities across antenatal care, sexually transmitted infection prevention, maternal treatment, partner management, and neonatal follow-up. This review investigates congenital syphilis from the viewpoint of the possible failures of the maternal-fetal prevention pathway, with a specific focus on pregnant migrant and structurally vulnerable women.
METHODS: This narrative clinical review synthesizes epidemiological data, international guidelines, surveillance reports, and selects peer-reviewed literature on maternal and congenital syphilis, antenatal screening, vertical transmission, penicillin treatment, neonatal assessment, migrant health, and structural barriers to care. Relevant sources available up to june 2026 have been identified through targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, institutional websites, and guideline repositories, including those of WHO, CDC, ECDC, USPSTF, and BASHH.
RESULTS: Congenital syphilis may result from inadequacies at multiple points: delayed antenatal access, missed or late screening, incomplete or non-stage-appropriate treatment, untreated partners, reinfection, poor documentation, and inadequate neonatal follow-up. Pregnant migrant women and structurally vulnerable women may face additional barriers, including language difficulties, administrative insecurity, unstable housing, stigma, unsafe partner disclosure, mobility, and fragmented care across the various emergency centres, sexual health, obstetric, and neonatal services.
