Prevention should therefore prioritize reducing missed opportunities through early and repeated screening when indicated, same-visit testing when follow-up is uncertain, rapid linkage between antenatal and STI services, quantitative non-treponemal testing, penicillin-based stage-appropriate treatment, safe partner management, and clear maternal-neonatal documentation.
CONCLUSIONS: Congenital syphilis should be considered a sentinel event revealing failings in antenatal care, STI prevention, migrant health access, and continuity of care. For pregnant migrant and structurally vulnerable women, prevention requires integrated, accessible, and safely coordinated maternal-neonatal pathways.

articles.title: Tebuconazole-induced ferroptosis impairs human trophoblast function via GPX4: A multi-omics study on unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss.
articles.authors: Wang S, Che H, Ren X et al.
articles.abstract: Tebuconazole (TEB) is a widely used triazole fungicide with suspected endocrine-disrupting and reproductive toxicity. However, its effects on human placental trophoblasts and its association with unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) remain poorly defined. Chorionic villi from 27 women with unexplained RPL and 25 women with normal pregnancies were analyzed by HPLC-MS/MS, and TEB effects were examined in BeWo and HTR-8/SVneo trophoblasts. Villus TEB residues were 1.82-fold higher in the RPL group (mean 0.0356 versus 0.0196 ng/g; P < 0.001), whereas TEB-OH did not differ significantly. In HTR-8/SVneo cells, 48-h TEB exposure reduced estradiol secretion at 20-80 µM and impaired migration at 40-80 µM without a significant loss of CCK-8 viability, and increased intracellular labile Fe2 +. Transcriptome profiling at 80 µM identified 1680 differentially expressed genes (797 up-regulated, 883 down-regulated), and the downregulation of GPX4, TFRC, and SLC40A1 was confirmed by RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Network toxicology identified 72 core targets shared with RPL and fetal growth restriction, and docking predicted GPX4 as a candidate binding target of TEB (Ki= 44.74 µM). Consistent with a ferroptotic mechanism, ferrostatin-1 (2 µM) attenuated TEB-induced lipid peroxidation and Fe2+accumulation and partially restored GPX4, SLC40A1, and TFRC abundance, trophoblast migration, and estradiol secretion. These findings suggest that ferroptosis-related lipid peroxidation contributes to TEB-induced trophoblast dysfunction and links chorionic villus TEB residues to unexplained RPL. Because the effective in vitro concentrations exceed typical human exposure levels, the results provide mechanistic evidence of hazard and warrant further risk assessment.

articles.title: Mortality amongst older patients with delirium superimposed on dementia and malnutrition: A six-year follow-up study.
articles.authors: Enwere P, Yeong K, Lisk R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the association of delirium, superimposed on dementia and malnutrition, with the risk of death after hospital discharge in older adults.
METHODS: This retrospective follow-up study comprised 554 patients aged 61.3-105.3 years (mean 85.5 years, SD 7.6) admitted between 01/04/2019 and 31/01/2020 with acute delirium at a single hospital (United Kingdom). It evaluated the associations between mortality after hospital discharge and the following patient groups: 1) well-nourished without dementia; 2) malnutrition without dementia; 3) well-nourished with delirium superimposed on dementia; and 4) malnutrition with delirium superimposed on dementia. Multivariable logistic and Cox regressions were done, adjusted for age, sex, polypharmacy, anticholinergic burden and comorbidities.
RESULTS: Survivors to discharge (n = 497) were followed for a mean of 6.2 years (74.4 months). The median time from discharge to death was 15.2 months (interquartile range 4.9-33.4). Compared with well-nourished patients without dementia, those with malnutrition and delirium superimposed on dementia had the greatest risks of post-discharge mortality both within one month (odds ratio 6.10, 95% confidence interval 2.4-15.3) and over a 6.2-year period (hazard ratio 1.48, 95% confidence interval 1.13-1.93). The post-discharge median survival time was 26 months for well-nourished patients without dementia, compared with 18 months for patients with malnutrition and without dementia; 16 months for well-nourished patients with delirium superimposed on dementia; and 13 months for those with both malnutrition and delirium superimposed on dementia.
CONCLUSIONS: Older adults with delirium superimposed on dementia and malnutrition have an increased risk of short- and long-term mortality after hospitalisation for delirium. This combination can serve as an indicator for the identification of high-risk patients.

articles.title: Associations of frailty and generalized trust with Ikigai among community-dwelling older adults in Japan: A large population-based cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Sakimoto F, Doi T, Nakakubo S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: "Ikigai" is a Japanese concept of meaning and purpose in life. We examined the associations of frailty and generalized trust with ikigai and their additive interaction.
STUDY DESIGN: This cross-sectional study included 34,545 community-dwelling older adults (mean age 75.4 ± 6.9 years; 52.1% women) who completed postal surveys in five Japanese cities between 2019 and 2023 using the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study for the Next Generation questionnaire. We created 50 imputed datasets for missing data.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: We examined associations with being without ikigai using multivariable logistic regression. We estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) using modified Poisson regression and calculated the relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI). Models included city and other covariates. We also conducted a complete-case analysis.
RESULTS: Overall, 74.9% of participants had ikigai. Frailty (odds ratio [OR] 3.65; 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.26-4.09) and low generalized trust (OR 2.34; 95% CI 2.22-2.47) were each associated with being without ikigai. Participants with both factors had the highest prevalence (PR 3.53; 95% CI 3.30-3.78). However, the RERI was 0.10 (95% CI -0.23 to 0.44), indicating no clear additive interaction. Complete-case findings were similar.
CONCLUSIONS: Frailty and low generalized trust were each associated with being without ikigai, but no clear additive interaction was found. Longitudinal studies are needed because this cross-sectional study cannot establish causality.

articles.title: Postoperative Pelvic Floor Muscle Training for Urinary Incontinence Following Radical Prostatectomy: A Meta-Analysis With Exploratory Subgroup Analysis by Surgical Approach.
articles.authors: Wang X, Ma Y, Zhu Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This meta-analysis evaluated postoperative pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) for urinary incontinence after radical prostatectomy (RP) and explored whether effects differed by surgical approach.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, PEDro, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from January 1, 2005, to January 1, 2025. Random-effects models were used. Short-term ICIQ-SF scores were summarized as standardized mean differences (SMDs; negative values favor PFMT), and long-term continence as odds ratios (ORs), each with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup analyses by surgical approach were exploratory.
RESULTS: Seven RCTs involving 666 participants were included. At 3 months, 3 studies (n = 151) favored PFMT (SMD = -1.22, 95% CI [-2.40, -0.04], P = .04; I² = 90%). A sensitivity analysis excluding de Lira et al. included 2 studies (n = 120) and yielded SMD = -1.81 (95% CI [-2.40, -1.21]; I² = 48%). At 12 months, 4 studies (n = 515) favored PFMT (OR = 7.21, 95% CI [3.99, 13.02], P < .00001; I² = 0%). Interaction tests did not show differences by surgical approach at either 3 months (P = .68) or 12 months (P = .53).
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative PFMT may improve short- and long-term continence recovery after RP. Certainty was very low for the heterogeneous short-term evidence and low for the long-term evidence; differences by surgical approach remain inconclusive.

articles.title: Spatial patterns and multilevel analysis of modern contraceptive utilization among ever sexually active ghanaian women: Evidence from the 2022 Ghana demographic and Health Survey.
articles.authors: Karikari JK, Agyemang S, Abdulai SB et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundModern contraceptive use remains a major public health priority in Ghana, yet geographic inequalities and contextual determinants of utilization among ever sexually active women are not fully understood.ObjectivesThis study aimed to examine the prevalence, spatial distribution, and determinants of modern contraceptive use among ever sexually active Ghanaian women using data from the 2022 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey (GDHS).DesignA cross-sectional study design with multilevel and spatial analysis.MethodsThe study included 10,415 ever sexually active women aged 15-49 years from the 2022 GDHS. Descriptive statistics and Pearson's chi-square tests were performed. Multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression models were fitted to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with modern contraceptive use. Spatial analyses, including Global Moran's I, Local Moran's I, and Getis-Ord Gi* hotspot analysis, were conducted to assess geographic clustering and spatial patterns. Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported.ResultsThe prevalence of modern contraceptive use among women with a history of sexual intercourse was 31.4% (95% CI: 30.1-32.7). Modern contraceptive use demonstrated significant spatial clustering across Ghana (Global Moran's I = 0.218, p = 0.036). Western North emerged as a significant hotspot, whereas Northern and Savannah regions were identified as cold spots of low utilization. Women aged 40-49 years (aOR = 0.55; 95% CI: 0.42-0.73), Muslims (aOR = 0.73; 95% CI: 0.58-0.90), breastfeeding women (aOR = 0.77; 95% CI: 0.63-0.94), and women currently abstaining from sex (aOR = 0.12; 95% CI: 0.09-0.17) had lower odds of using modern contraceptives. Conversely, HIV testing history, recent births, exposure to family planning media messages, and larger household size were associated with higher odds of utilization.ConclusionsModern contraceptive use among ever sexually active Ghanaian women remains relatively low and spatially clustered. Targeted, culturally sensitive, and geographically focused reproductive health interventions are needed to address regional inequalities and improve contraceptive uptake in Ghana.

articles.title: Key Lessons Learned From Implementing a Training Program for Perinatal Patient Safety in a Large Integrated Health Care System.
articles.journal: The Journal of continuing education in the health professions
articles.authors: Nonog JC, Shimer SA, Hand A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In 2020, the Women's and Children's Health team at Kaiser Permanente developed an enterprise-wide continuing professional development system designed to deliver a scalable, mastery-based clinical training focused on perinatal patient safety while fulfilling health care regulatory standards.
METHODS: Using a collaborative design process that relied on interdisciplinary subject matter expert teams, leveraged existing platforms and inexpensive learning software, and incorporated best practices in adult learning, we implemented a complex training program using an innovative learning format and question-level confidence analytics across a large integrated health system. Using the Kirkpatrick Model of Training Evaluation as a framework, we evaluated data from course evaluations including refreshers, quality metrics, and a survey of operational leaders in the Women's and Children's Health service line.
RESULTS: The program demonstrated strong learner engagement and identified clinically relevant knowledge gaps through question-level confidence analytics and showed early indicators of enhanced clinical performance.
DISCUSSION: Key implementation factors for making a large rollout of clinical education more compelling and effective include using interdisciplinary subject matter experts; creating the training in-house; and a flexible review process to make improvements to the content as needed. This work also demonstrates how a mastery-based, interprofessional continuing professional development system using question-level confidence analytics can identify clinical misperceptions and support iterative curriculum refinement at enterprise scale.

articles.title: Prenatal Fetoscopic Intervention for Gastroschisis: A Systematic Review of First Published Human Cases.
articles.authors: Gutfreund MC, Callado GY, Pitta MJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically identify and descriptively summarize the available published human evidence on prenatal fetoscopic intervention for gastroschisis, focusing on reported procedural characteristics, maternal-fetal events, neonatal outcomes, and limitations of the current literature.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidance, with protocol registration in PROSPERO (CRD420261338353). MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies including fetuses with prenatally diagnosed gastroschisis undergoing intrauterine intervention were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data using a standardized form, and assessed reporting quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist for case reports. Given the nature of the available evidence, synthesis was descriptive only.
RESULTS: Of 827 records identified, three single-patient case reports met the inclusion criteria. All described prenatal fetoscopic intervention for gastroschisis in highly specialized centers, with substantial heterogeneity in timing of intervention, uterine access, carbon dioxide insufflation, amniotic fluid management, closure technique, fetal monitoring, and postoperative surveillance. Initial intrauterine bowel reduction was reported in all three cases; however, one fetus developed postoperative bowel re-extrusion within 48 hours, associated with venous Doppler abnormalities, and required delivery followed by EXIT-like repair. All neonates survived, but the absence of comparators, extreme case selection, heterogeneous perioperative management, and likely publication bias preclude any inference regarding efficacy or neonatal benefit.
CONCLUSIONS: Published human evidence on prenatal fetoscopic intervention for gastroschisis is limited to three isolated case reports. These reports describe procedural completion in highly selected cases managed at specialized fetal surgery centers, but they remain insufficient to determine the generalizable feasibility, safety profile, reproducibility, or clinical benefit of this approach compared with contemporary postnatal management. Prenatal repair should therefore remain investigational and should be evaluated within ethically approved prospective protocols with standardized selection criteria, maternal-fetal safety monitoring, operative reporting, and long-term follow-up.

articles.title: Metabolite profiling and pharmacological evaluation of Lablab purpureus seed coat: a rich source of antioxidant, antibacterial and anticancer metabolites.
articles.journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
articles.authors: Hossain MR, Shill R, Hasan MA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer remains a major health concern worldwide, highlighting the need for safer and affordable treatments from natural sources. This study evaluated the antioxidant, antibacterial and anticancer potential of different solvent fractions of Lablab purpureus seed coat using in vitro, in vivo and in silico approaches. Methanol, ethyl acetate, dichloromethane and n-hexane extracts were subjected to phytochemical screening, antioxidant assays, cytotoxicity testing against HeLa cells, antibacterial evaluation, molecular docking and molecular dynamics studies targeting estrogen receptor alpha.
RESULTS: Among the tested extracts, the methanolic fraction showed the strongest antioxidant activity, with half-maximal inhibitory concentration values of 86.83 μg mL-1 and 67.56 μg mL-1 in the 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (i.e. DPPH) and 2,2´-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (i.e. ABTS) assays, respectively. This activity was consistent with its high phenolic and flavonoid contents. In a carbon tetrachloride-induced oxidative stress mouse model, the methanolic extract significantly improved serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase, serum glutamate oxaloacetate transaminase and catalase levels. It also demonstrated strong cytotoxic activity against HeLa cells, reducing cell viability by more than 95%. The n-hexane extract showed notable antibacterial activity, particularly against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, with a zone of inhibition of 32 mm. Gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry analysis of the methanolic crude extract identified 76 compounds, among which N-benzylisatoic anhydride and pallensin showed strong binding affinity toward estrogen receptor alpha, with docking scores comparable to doxorubicin. Pallensin also exhibited favorable electronic properties, whereas molecular dynamics, molecular mechanics/generalized born surface area and principal component analyses confirmed stable ligand-receptor interactions.
CONCLUSION: Overall, the findings indicate that L. purpureus seed coat is a promising source of bioactive compounds with antioxidant, antibacterial and anticancer activities. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Mifepristone Patient Agreement Form and Medication Abortion Knowledge: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.authors: Biggs MA, Ehrenreich K, Kaller S et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: While the US Food and Drug Administration requires medication abortion patients to review and sign a patient agreement form (PAF) under its Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy program, there is limited research examining whether the PAF improves patient knowledge.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether patients are more knowledgeable about medication abortion after reviewing and signing the PAF.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: People receiving mifepristone and misoprostol medications (15 years or older and proficient in English or Spanish) were recruited from 5 facilities in California, Colorado, Illinois, Kansas, and Minnesota (January to October 2025). After receiving standard clinic counseling and the mifepristone medication guide, patients were randomized into 2 study groups and then completed a survey either before (n = 301 control) or after (n = 292 exposed) receiving and signing the PAF. Data were analyzed December 2025 to August 2026.
INTERVENTION: The control group completed the survey before receiving the PAF and any PAF-related counseling. The exposed group received and signed the PAF and any PAF-related counseling and then completed a knowledge survey.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Overall medication abortion knowledge (correct response to 12 items regarding when to seek medical care, effectiveness, administration, potential serious risks, and side effects) and responses to each individual knowledge item.
RESULTS: A total of 593 participants (mean [SD] age, 26.9 [5.8] years; 44 Asian/Pacific Islander [7%], 132 Black [22%], 181 Hispanic [31%], and 159 White [27%] individuals) completed knowledge items (301 control [51%]; 292 exposed [49%]). Across participant characteristics, study groups only differed significantly in reported abortion history. In adjusted analyses, participants answered a mean (95% CI) of 10.37 (10.26-10.48) of 12 knowledge items consistently with the PAF with no study group differences (control: difference, 10.26; exposed: difference, 10.44; adjusted difference, 0.18; 95% CI, -0.04 to 0.39). Nearly everyone knew to contact a "provider" if they "were to have an infection (590 [99%]) or heavy bleeding that soaked through 2 full-size sanitary pads per hour for 2 hours (566 [96%])." The items with answers that were least often concordant with the PAF included how often the treatment does not work (320 [54%]) and taking misoprostol 24 to 48 hours after mifepristone (458 [77%]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The randomized…

articles.title: X-linked novel hemizygous ADGRG2 variants associated with male factor infertility.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Yuan Y, Li Y, Lu W et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To screen for ADGRG2 gene mutations in CFTR-negative patients with male infertility or congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD), and to assess the feasibility and outcomes of intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) for achieving successful pregnancies in this population.
METHODS: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed in 133 infertile men with obstructive azoospermia (OA). Sanger sequencing were conducted on peripheral blood samples collected from nine patients with ADGRG2 variants. The AlphaFold database and PyMOL software were used to predict the 3D structure of the mutant ADGRG2 protein. In vitro assays were conducted to assess the functional impact of the identified ADGRG2 variants. In addition, we also conducted a retrospective analysis of the clinical assisted reproductive information of these patients.
RESULTS: We identified eight ADGRG2 hemizygous pathogenic variants in nine unrelated patients with CBAVD from 133 OA men: one splicing variant (c.1839 + 1G > A), three frameshift variants (c.2956_2957del: p.M986Vfs*2; c.2396dupT: p.L799Ffs*18 and c.895delA: p.I299Ffs*12), two nonsense variants (c.2473C > T: p.R825* and c.2971G > T: p.E991*), and two missense variants (c.510G > C: p.E170D and c.549C > G: p.S183R). All ADGRG2 variants-affected individuals presented with azoospermia or severe oligozoospermia. All of these variants were absent or rare in public databases. 3D protein structure modeling predicted that ADGRG2 variants lead to alterations in the spatial conformation of the protein. In vitro experiments further confirmed that these variants result in the production of truncated proteins or reduced protein levels. Notably, four patients undergoing ICSI treatment achieved successful fertilization and pregnancy.
CONCLUSION: Our findings established ADGRG2 variants cause male infertility and may be the etiology of CBAVD, expanding the associated mutational spectrum and reinforcing the gene's critical role in male fertility, thereby supporting the integration of comprehensive ADGRG2 screening into clinical practice to enhance genetic and reproductive counseling for affected patients.

articles.title: Biological Grafts for the Surgical Management of Uterovaginal Prolapse: A Narrative Overview of the Evolution of Biomaterials.
articles.authors: Alperin M, Moalli P, Acoff E et al.
articles.abstract: Uterovaginal prolapse (U-POP) affects the lives of millions of women worldwide. This narrative review was performed as part of the Global Consensus on controversies and best practices in the surgical management of U-POP. The committee on augmenting and alternative materials for primary U-POP repair addressed three questions: (1) Is there a preferred material for augmentation of primary uterovaginal prolapse repair? (2) What are the critical outcomes for the assessment of augmented repair? and (3) Could novel biomaterials be used preventatively, to avoid the need for surgical intervention for U-POP? We provide a narrative overview of the evolution of biomaterials used in POP repair, from autologous grafts, allografts and xenografts to synthetic mesh and to the engineering and preclinical validation of next-generation smart biomaterials. Each option available today requires a trade-off. Native-tissue repair avoids graft-related complications, but recurrence remains an important problem for some patients. Permanent synthetic implants provide durable structural support, but can cause material-specific complications. Biological grafts have not consistently improved long-term outcomes. New materials are therefore needed that balance mechanical support, tissue integration, and biologic compatibility. We conclude by focusing the attention of the clinical and scientific communities on the scarcity of rigorous comparative trials and on this unmet need in the field of female pelvic medicine.

articles.title: Pelvic Floor Knowledge, Toileting Behaviors, and Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Women with Multiple Sclerosis.
articles.authors: Kiloatar H, Delibay AA, Demir CO et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) are common in women with multiple sclerosis (MS) and may be influenced by neurological involvement as well as behavioral and knowledge-related factors. This study aimed to compare LUTS, pelvic floor health knowledge, and toileting behaviors between women with MS and demographically matched women without MS, examine their associations, and identify predictors of LUTS.
METHODS: This cross-sectional survey included 59 women with MS and 60 demographically matched women without MS. LUTS were assessed using Urogenital Distress Inventory-6 (UDI-6) and Bristol Women's Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Questionnaire (BFLUTS). Pelvic floor health knowledge and toileting behaviors were evaluated using Pelvic Floor Health Knowledge Quiz and Toileting Behavior-Women's Elimination Behaviors Scale, respectively.
RESULTS: Women with MS had higher UDI-6 scores, lower pelvic floor health knowledge, and more negative toileting behaviors compared to women without MS (p < 0.05). After adjustment for potential confounders, group differences remained significant for UDI-6, BFLUTS, and premature voiding (p < 0.05), whereas pelvic floor health knowledge was no longer significant (p > 0.05). In both groups, LUTS severity was positively associated mainly with premature voiding and straining voiding (p < 0.05). The final regression model explained 52.2% of the variance in UDI-6 scores; straining to void, premature voiding, and place preference for voiding were significant predictors.
CONCLUSION: Women with MS had higher LUTS and more negative toileting behaviors, while pelvic floor health knowledge was more closely associated with sociodemographic factors than MS status. These findings underscore the relevance of considering LUTS and toileting behaviors in women with MS.

articles.title: Quantifying the Role of Stage-at-Diagnosis in Racial Disparities in US Cancer Survival: A Population-Based SEER Study for 8 Common Cancers.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.authors: Vayani A, Rutherford M, Booth S
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Black patients with cancer experience worse relative survival, yet it remains unclear how far shifting diagnoses towards earlier stage would reduce mortality.
METHODS: We analysed Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) data (2004-2022) for U.S. Black and White patients aged 15-89 years with eight common cancers, using a 2021-2022 period-analysis window. We estimated age-standardised survival under observed and counterfactual stage distributions in which Black patients had the White stage distribution. We quantified the proportion of the racial survival gap mediated by stage and deaths postponed beyond specified follow-up times.
RESULTS: Among 1,299,386 eligible patients, Black patients were diagnosed at similar or younger ages and had more distant-stage disease for most sites, except rectal cancer in Black women aged < 75 years. At 5 years, stage accounted for large shares of the Black-White disparity in breast, colon, corpus uteri, lung, and oral cavity and pharynx cancers. The mediated proportion was low for rectal cancer in men, pancreatic cancer, and ovarian cancer, with weak evidence for ovarian cancer at age 75 + years and pancreatic cancer in women. The negative indirect effect for rectal cancer in younger women indicated suppression. Deaths postponed varied by follow-up time and cohort size.
CONCLUSIONS: Stage equalisation could yield meaningful short-term mortality reductions for several sites, but stage-focused strategies are not universally beneficial. Equity-oriented policies should pair earlier diagnosis with interventions to improve downstream care pathways.

articles.title: Bioactive components from Sinomenium acutum exhibit anti-inflammatory activity and sensitize cervical cancer cells to paclitaxel.
articles.authors: Wang X, Zhu C, Du X et al.
articles.abstract: Six previously undescribed compounds, together with twelve known compounds, were isolated from Sinomenium acutum. The structures of the unreported compounds were determined by comprehensive spectroscopic data analysis, 13C NMR calculations followed by DP4 + analysis, ECD calculations, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis. Nine compounds exhibited more potent anti-inflammatory activities than the positive control indomethacin. The structure-activity relationship of the isolates with anti-inflammatory effects was elucidated, providing some useful clues for designing and developing structurally novel anti-inflammatory drugs. Furthermore, five compounds reversed the paclitaxel resistance in paclitaxel-resistant cervical cancer cells HeLa/PTX. The combination of compound 4 and paclitaxel promoted cancer cell apoptosis.

articles.title: Oncolytic Vaccinia Virus Armed With CLEC2A Enhances Antitumor Immunity via ROS-Autophagy Feedback Loop and Cytokine Activation.
articles.authors: Su J, Zhai C, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract: Tumors often exhibit immunosuppressive microenvironments (TMEs) and present as immunologically "cold." Oncolytic viruses (OVs), particularly engineered vaccinia viruses (oncoVVs), are an encouraging therapy that directly lyses cancer cells and reprograms the TME. In this study, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of an oncolytic vaccinia virus expressing human C-type lectin domain family 2 member A (oncoVV-CLEC2A) in melanoma and ovarian cancer cells. OncoVV-CLEC2A elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, suppressed Nrf2-mediated antioxidant responses, and triggered autophagy. These changes promoted cytokine production (IL-6, IFN-α/β/γ, TNF-α) via activation of AP-1 and IRF3/7. In a B16-F10 melanoma model, oncoVV-CLEC2A increased serum levels of IFN-γ, accompanied by augmented infiltration of CD8+ T cells and activation of NK cells. Taken together, oncoVV-CLEC2A reshapes the TME by intensifying oxidative stress and autophagic activity, effectively turning "cold" tumors "hot." Notably, the mutual reinforcement between ROS production and autophagy activation not only enhances viral replication but also triggers cytokine-mediated immunity.

articles.title: BMI as a partitioning factor for estradiol and estrone reference intervals in middle-aged men and postmenopausal women.
articles.authors: Kruijt M, de Mutsert R, van Hylckama Vlieg A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Estrogens play a large role in female and male physiology and are routinely determined in the clinical setting. For interpretation, distinct reference intervals (RIs) are applied for men, pre-, and postmenopausal women. Adipose tissue is a potent producer of estrogens and influences the circulating estrogen concentrations, although its impact on estrogen RIs is currently unknown.
METHOD: We determined estradiol and estrone concentrations in 6671 middle-aged participants of a large cohort oversampled for persons with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥27 kg/m2. We investigated partitioning based on sex, age, menopausal status, and BMI by assessing the proportion of subgroups outside each limit of a shared 95% RI (ideally 2.5%) and calculating RIs for justified subgroups according to CLSI EP28-A3c.
RESULTS: As expected, the strongest partitioning factor was sex, followed by menopausal status for women. When using a shared RI for all BMI categories, 4.9% and 5.2% of values in men with obesity and 11.4% and 7.7% of values in postmenopausal women with obesity fell above the RI for estradiol and estrone, respectively. Within postmenopausal women, differences in the upper reference limit were found, being 138, 157, and 210 pmol/L for estradiol and 32, 41, and 74 pmol/L for estrone for normal weight, overweight, and obesity, respectively.
DISCUSSION: Laboratory professionals and clinicians should be aware that BMI affects estrogen concentrations to such an extent that it may influence clinical interpretation. Ideally, their RIs should be stratified by BMI category to reflect the increased estrogen concentrations associated with higher BMI.

articles.title: Selective depletion of AMH-expressing granulosa cells in vivo impairs follicular development and fertility in female mice.
articles.authors: Endo T, Tamemasa M, Hayakawa K et al.
articles.abstract: In brief: We establish an in-vivo mouse model for conditional and selective depletion of anti-Müllerian hormone-expressing granulosa cells and reveal their contribution to follicular development and female fertility. This model provides a useful platform to investigate complex follicular dynamics in vivo. Abstract: In mammals, ovarian follicle development is a highly coordinated process that underlies female fertility. Granulosa cells expressing anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) are widely used as a marker of growing follicles. However, the in-vivo roles of granulosa cells in follicular development and female fertility remain unclear. Here, we analyzed AMH-toxin receptor-mediated cell knockout (AMH-TRECK) transgenic (Tg) mice on a NOG background, in which AMH-expressing granulosa cells are specifically depleted by diphtheria toxin (DT). We first found that, after a single DT injection into postnatal AMH-TRECK Tg females, AMH-expressing granulosa cells in primary and secondary follicles exhibited cleaved caspase-3 signals 1 day later and were depleted 4 days later. Second, after repeated DT injections weekly from 1 to 7 weeks of age in AMH-TRECK Tg females, antral follicles and corpora lutea were rarely observed, and the numbers of primordial, primary, and secondary follicles were decreased. Following pregnant mare serum gonadotropin and human chorionic gonadotropin stimulation, repeated DT-injected Tg females exhibited a reduced number of ovulated oocytes with a low proportion of mature oocytes, resulting in reduced in-vitro fertilization rates and fertility. Furthermore, after a cessation of repeated DT treatment, ovarian weight and follicular development recovered: the numbers of primary, secondary, and antral follicles were recovered, whereas the primordial follicle pool remains reduced. We conclude that selective depletion of AMH-expressing granulosa cells in vivo impairs follicular development and fertility. Our model enables assessment of the in-vivo effects of granulosa cell depletion and may provide a useful platform for future transplantation-based studies to understand complex follicular dynamics.

articles.title: Systemic inflammatory indices for predicting severe placenta accreta spectrum: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Lu X, Lei X, Guo C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) disorders are associated with substantial maternal morbidity, and distinguishing mild from severe forms prenatally remains difficult. Inflammatory indices derived from peripheral blood counts have emerged as promising biomarkers, yet their role in grading PAS severity has been insufficiently investigated. This study aimed to assess the discriminative value of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and other inflammatory indices for differentiating severe from mild PAS within an already diagnosed PAS population in late pregnancy.
METHODS: This retrospective single-centre cohort study included 1,276 patients with histopathologically confirmed PAS. Third-trimester neutrophil, lymphocyte, monocyte, and platelet counts were used to derive neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), SII, and SIRI. Multivariable logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were conducted.
RESULTS: Compared with the mild PAS group (n = 1,060), the severe PAS group (n = 216) showed significantly lower SIRI, SII, NLR, and PLR values (all P < 0.001). SIRI demonstrated moderate discriminative performance (area under the curve = 0.712). DCA suggested its potential clinical usefulness across threshold probabilities.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower third-trimester SIRI, SII, NLR, and PLR values are associated with severe PAS. SIRI shows moderate diagnostic performance and may serve as a cost-effective adjunct to imaging for prenatal risk stratification. Prospective validation is warranted.

articles.title: Impact of prenatal pyrethroid pesticide exposure on neonatal lymphocyte subsets and apoptosis: a birth cohort study.
articles.authors: Qi Z, Zhang L, Xiao X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal pyrethroid pesticides (PYRs) exposure may elevate infection diseases susceptibility of children. However, it is unclear the relationship of PYRs exposure and neonatal immune function. We explored the association of PYRs exposure during three trimesters with neonatal immunity and the roles of lymphocyte apoptosis.
METHODS: Maternal urinary PYRs metabolites (3PBA, 4F3PBA, cis-DBCA) were measured in each trimester. Cord blood lymphocyte subsets and lymphocyte apoptosis rates were assessed by flow cytometry. Multivariate linear regression models were used to examine the associations of trimester-specific and repeated PYRs exposure during pregnancy with neonatal immune function.
RESULTS: High-level cis-DBCA exposure (>75th percentile, 0.78 μg/g) in the third trimester was negatively associated with cord blood CD3+ T cell counts (β = -0.06; 95% CI = -0.12, -0.01) and CD8+ T cell counts (β = -0.09; 95% CI = -0.16, -0.01). Repeated high-level cis-DBCA exposure across two or more trimesters was associated with reduced CD3+ T cell counts (β = -0.09; 95% CI = -0.16, -0.02), CD4+ T cell counts (β = -0.13; 95% CI = -0.22, -0.04), CD8+ T cell counts (β = -0.13; 95% CI = -0.22, -0.04), B cell counts (β = -0.10; 95% CI = -0.20, -0.01), and NK cell counts (β = -0.14; 95% CI = -0.25, -0.03). High-level 3PBA exposure in the first trimester (β = 0.11; 95% CI = 0.01, 0.22) and high-level cis-DBCA exposure in the second trimester (β = 0.16; 95% CI = 0.04, 0.28) were positively associated with cord blood lymphocyte apoptosis rates. Repeated high-level cis-DBCA exposure in two or more trimesters was associated with increased cord blood lymphocyte apoptosis rates (β = 0.19; 95% CI = 0.03, 0.35).
CONCLUSIONS: High-level maternal PYRs exposure during pregnancy may reduce neonatal lymphocyte counts and increase lymphocyte apoptosis. These effects persist throughout gestation, with the third trimester may represent a sensitive window for adverse effects on immune development.

articles.title: FMCerNet: frequency-aware multi-label learning for fine-grained cervical cytology screening.
articles.authors: Zhou L, Cai Q, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Automated cytology screening is essential for early cervical cancer prevention, where gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs) are typically partitioned into tiles for tile-level feature extraction and subsequent WSI-level diagnosis aggregation. However, existing tile-level methods remain constrained by limited input sizes, which frequently obscures sparse and morphologically subtle abnormal cells. Furthermore, these methods commonly formulate tile-level representation learning as a coarse single-label classification task, thereby failing to capture the complex co-occurrence patterns and morphological heterogeneity of cervical cytological abnormalities.
RESULTS: We propose the Frequency-Aware Multi-Label Learning Network (FMCerNet), a tile-level feature extractor equipped with a Large-Field Frequency-Enhanced ViT backbone and a Coarse-to-Fine multi-label classification head. The former incorporates a Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Transform module to efficiently extract frequency-domain features from large-scale tiles, whereas the latter enhances fine-grained tile representation decoding through hierarchical supervision. Experiments on both public and private datasets demonstrate that FMCerNet improves the accuracy of positive screening and fine-grained subtype classification while maintaining high inference speed.
AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: Code at https://github.com/imAzhou/FMCerNet and archived on Zenodo (doi: 10.5281/zenodo.22886105).

articles.title: The mitochondrial-derived peptide MOTS-c improves bioenergetics in aging-associated granulosa cells and oocytes.
articles.authors: Tsui KH, Cheng SH, Lin LT et al.
articles.abstract:
ABSTRACT: Ovarian aging compromises granulosa cell function, mitochondrial homeostasis, metabolism, and oocyte quality. We investigated whether the mitochondrial-derived peptide MOTS-c mitigates these defects using an aging-associated HGL5 granulosa cell model, ex vivo oocytes from young and aged mice, and public granulosa cell transcriptomic datasets. In HGL5 cells, MOTS-c increased mitochondrial mass and ATP-associated fluorescence without increasing cellular or mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, while mass-normalized membrane potential remained unchanged. Seahorse analysis showed increased ATP-linked and maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity, reduced proton leak, and unchanged basal respiration. MOTS-c also remodeled the expression of enzymes involved in glycolysis, lactate-pyruvate handling, and pyruvate-TCA metabolism. Although fission markers were largely unchanged, MOTS-c increased the levels of proteins associated with antioxidant defense, mitochondrial transport, cell junctions, adhesion signaling, and granulosa cell function, including NRF2, phosphorylated AIFM1, RHOT1, KIF5B, ZO-1, E-cadherin, phosphorylated FAK, and AMH. Aged oocytes exhibited reduced polar body extrusion, increased DCFDA fluorescence, and decreased CMXRos intensity. Ex vivo MOTS-c treatment increased post-culture first polar body positivity and mitochondria-associated fluorescence while reducing oxidative stress-associated fluorescence, although outcomes remained below young-reference levels. Reanalysis of human folliculogenesis and nonhuman primate ovarian aging datasets further revealed a young-enriched trend in the MOTS-c-associated metabolic program. These findings suggest that MOTS-c improves metabolic, mitochondrial, and structural features of aging-associated granulosa cells and enhances maturation-associated outcomes in aged oocytes, supporting further investigation of MOTS-c-based strategies for reproductive aging.
LAY SUMMARY: As women age, the quality of their eggs declines, which is a major contributor to age-related infertility. Eggs are supported by neighboring 'helper' cells called granulosa cells, which act like a support crew that supplies the egg with the energy it needs to mature. These helper cells contain mitochondria, tiny energy-generating structures often called the cell's 'powerhouses', and with age these powerhouses become less efficient, leaving eggs with less support than they need. This study tested whether MOTS-c, a small…

articles.title: H3K4me1-Mediated Epigenomic Priming of Chemoresistant Tumor States in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Landais Y, Bertorello J, Puerto MP et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Non-genetic intratumor heterogeneity underlies therapeutic failure in cancer, yet how resistant tumor states are encoded in patients remains unclear. In this study, we show that chemoresistant evolution in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is prefigured by epigenetically primed tumor cell states present before therapy. Using multimodal single-nucleus approaches, we profile transcriptional programs and histone modifications from longitudinal frozen biopsies of 16 patients with HGSOC. Tumors comprise a limited set of functional states that evolve reproducibly under chemotherapy: proliferative and IFN-responsive states are depleted, whereas TNFα-associated and epithelial-mesenchymal transition-associated programs persist or expand. Chromatin profiling reveals that these resistant programs are broadly enriched for histone H3 lysine 4 monomethylation (H3K4me1) prior to treatment, indicating that features of resistance are epigenomically primed. Baseline tumor composition is associated with survival, and fibroblast remodeling accompanies malignant adaptation. Together, these findings identify epigenomic priming as a feature of chemoresistant tumor cell states and provide a scalable framework for anticipating resistance from biopsies.
SIGNIFICANCE: Using a clinically compatible multimodal single-nucleus approach, the authors show that chemoresistant evolution in HGSOC is prefigured by epigenetically primed tumor cell states present before therapy.

articles.title: Baicalein Exerts Cytotoxic Effects Through Cell Cycle Arrest and Mitochondria- Dependent Pathway in Ovarian Cancer Cells: In-Vitro and Computational Evaluation.
articles.authors: Rais J, Jafri A, Singh S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ovarian cancer remains one of the most prevalent and lethal gynecological malignancies globally, necessitating the exploration of novel therapeutic agents. Baicalein, a naturally occurring flavonoid, possesses potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and has recently gained attention for its anticancer potential. This study aimed to elucidate the anticancer efficacy and underlying molecular mechanisms of baicalein in human ovarian carcinoma PA-1 cells through comprehensive in vitro and in silico approaches.
METHODS: PA-1 cells were exposed to increasing concentrations of baicalein, and cytotoxicity was assessed using the MTT assay. Apoptotic induction was evaluated by measuring mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), reactive oxygen species (ROS) induction, and nuclear morphological changes using DAPI, Hoechst/PI, and AO/EB staining. Cell cycle checkpoints were analyzed by flow cytometry. Apoptosis-related genes (p53, Bax, Puma, Noxa, and Bcl-2) expression was quantified using qRT-PCR. In silico molecular docking was performed using PyRx to predict interactions with key apoptotic proteins, while SwissADME was employed to assess pharmacokinetic properties and drug-likeness.
RESULTS: Baicalein significantly reduced PA-1 cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner and induced pronounced morphological changes characteristic of apoptosis. Treatment resulted in elevated ROS production, loss of MMP, nuclear condensation, and S-phase cell cycle arrest. Gene expression analysis demonstrated significant upregulation of pro-apoptotic markers (p53, Bax, Puma, and Noxa) alongside decreased expression of the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl-2. Molecular docking studies revealed favorable binding affinities of baicalein with apoptosis-regulating proteins, and SwissADME analysis confirmed acceptable drug-likeness and pharmacokinetic profiles.
DISCUSSION: These findings showed that baicalein induces apoptosis in ovarian cancer PA-1 cells via a ROSmediated, mitochondria-dependent pathway.
CONCLUSION: This study highlights the potential of baicalein as a promising lead compound for the development of anticancer therapeutics.

articles.title: Eligibility and prescribing of low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia prevention under two international guidelines: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Geçici NA, Demir FN, Sabır YA et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The primary objective was to compare eligibility for low-dose aspirin prophylaxis according to the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) recommendations. Secondary objectives were to evaluate aspirin prescribing among eligible women and preeclampsia outcomes according to guideline eligibility.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1,064 pregnant women with complete clinical data from a tertiary referral hospital in Türkiye. Eligibility was determined according to ACOG and NICE criteria. Agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa and McNemar's test. Aspirin prescribing and preeclampsia outcomes were also evaluated.
RESULTS: According to the ACOG criteria, 311 women (29.23 %, 95 % CI, 26.58-32.03 %) were eligible for aspirin prophylaxis, whereas 130 (12.22 %, 95 % CI, 10.39-14.32 %) met the NICE criteria. The overall agreement between the two guidelines was 82.9 %, with moderate concordance (Cohen's kappa=0.50). McNemar's test demonstrated a significant difference in patient classification (p<0.001). Aspirin was prescribed to only 25.4 % of ACOG-eligible women and 48.5 % of NICE-eligible women. Overall, preeclampsia occurred in 38 of 1,064 women (3.57 %; 95 % CI, 2.61-4.86 %). Among women eligible for aspirin prophylaxis, preeclampsia developed in 23 of 311 women (7.4 %; 95 % CI, 4.98-10.85 %) according to ACOG criteria and in 16 of 130 women (12.3 %; 95 % CI, 7.72-19.06 %) according to NICE criteria.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the ACOG guideline identified substantially more women as eligible for aspirin prophylaxis than the NICE guideline, documented aspirin prescribing remained considerably lower than guideline-defined eligibility, highlighting an implementation gap in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Effects of Aging and Early-Onset Menopause on Intraocular Pressure and Aqueous Humor Conventional Outflow Facility.
articles.authors: Fraticelli-Guzmán NS, Jiang D, Yongphiphatwong B et al.
articles.abstract: Biomechanical parameters play a crucial role in glaucoma development, the world-leading cause of irreversible blindness. Although age is known to affect the tissues' biomechanical properties, early-onset menopause has recently been associated with the risk of developing glaucoma, and the effects of aging relative to early-onset menopause on eyes' biomechanical parameters remain underexplored. This work's goals were to study the effects of aging and early-onset menopause on intraocular pressure (IOP), aqueous humor outflow facility, and ocular compliance. Female Brown Norway rats underwent Sham or surgical menopause (ovariectomy; OVX) at 3-4 months of age and were split into young (5-6 months) or middle-aged groups (9-10 months). We monitored IOP until the established aging time points and performed ex vivo biomechanical measurements via the iPerfusion system. IOP was higher for the middle-aged Sham and OVX animals by 25% and 35%, respectively (p < 0.001), when compared to their respective initial IOPs. Furthermore, middle-aged OVX animals had an 11% higher IOP compared to Sham animals (p = 0.005), and a 20% lower outflow facility (p = 0.031). Ocular compliance decreased with age in the Sham (24.9%, p = 0.011) and OVX (24.5%, p = 0.005) cohorts and by 24.1% independent of cohort (p = 0.0001). Elucidating the effects of age and early-onset menopause on biomechanical parameters that contribute to glaucoma pathology is necessary to move the field forward and help preserve the eyesight of millions of patients.

articles.title: "Treat Him as Another Human, Not as an Animal": Patient and Family Protest or Refusal to "Consent" to Eugenic Sterilization in California Institutions, 1922-1950.
articles.journal: Bulletin of the history of medicine
articles.authors: Dron H
articles.abstract: This examination of sterilization "consent" in California state institutions during the eugenics era (1922-1950) contributes to bioethical and historical scholarship on institutionalization and the limits of consent. Department of Institutions records digitalized by the Sterilization and Social Justice Lab were used to identify 259 cases where relatives or patients refused to "consent" to sterilization, including thirty-five protest letters written by patients or relatives. This analysis addresses the enigma of why administrators exerted considerable bureaucratic labor to document consent from relatives, or occasionally patients, if the law didn't require it, release was conditional on sterilization, and objections were often ignored. It foregrounds the voices of patients and family members responding to requests to sign permission forms. Many family members were estranged and did not want to make sterilization decisions for or take responsibility for an institutionalized person, yet others tried to forestall sterilizations, contest diagnoses, and seek patients' release without sterilization.

articles.title: Defending the Indefensible: Therapeutic Abortion in Nineteenth-Century Brazilian Medical Discourse.
articles.journal: Bulletin of the history of medicine
articles.authors: Dornelas I
articles.abstract: This article analyzes how Brazilian physicians in the nineteenth century framed therapeutic abortion as a lifesaving intervention, arguing for professional authority amid religious and legal constraints. Drawing on medical theses from the Faculdades de Medicina of Rio de Janeiro and Bahia, it explores how doctors defended abortion in cases of obstructed labor, when maternal death was imminent. Physicians appealed to humanitarian urgency, theological reinterpretation, and legal ambiguity to justify their opinions on therapeutic abortion. The article identifies three key sites of contention: opposition from the Catholic Church, medical debates between abortion and cesarean section, and shifting legal frameworks. Much of the debate examined here unfolded under the 1830 Criminal Code, which criminalized abortion without providing explicit protection for therapeutic interventions. Later, the 1890 Penal Code formally recognized therapeutic abortion, but only conditionally, imposing legal liability on physicians in cases of maternal death. This study argues that medical authority over therapeutic abortion emerged through a fragile and contested form of recognition, negotiated within overlapping regimes of law, religion, and medical ethics, and constrained in practice by legal uncertainty and the threat of professional liability.

articles.title: sFlt-1 in Decidua, Placenta, and Maternal Serum in Preeclampsia Subtypes.
articles.authors: Rakner JJ, Jarmund AH, Svoren ÅTR et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Soluble FMS-like tyrosine kinase (sFlt-1) drives maternal symptoms in preeclampsia, serves as a predictive biomarker, and represents a promising therapeutic target. sFlt-1 is expressed in placental and decidual tissue, which together form the maternal-fetal interface. Whether placental and decidual expression of sFlt-1 regulates the maternal serum levels remains unknown. This study aimed to investigate sFlt-1 expression and co-regulation in decidua, placenta, and maternal serum, in normal pregnancies and preeclamptic pregnancies with and without fetal growth restriction.
METHODS: Pregnant women with normal (n=65) or preeclamptic pregnancies with (n=42) or without (n=22) fetal growth restriction were included before cesarean delivery. sFlt-1 expression was quantified in maternal serum and umbilical cord blood (BRAHMS KRYPTOR) and by immunohistochemistry with semi-automated image analysis in decidual and placental tissue.
RESULTS: Decidual and placental sFlt-1 expression was trophoblast-dependent and selectively upregulated in preeclampsia without and with fetal growth restriction, respectively, and maternal serum sFlt-1 was elevated in both preeclampsia subtypes (P<0.001, all comparisons). sFlt-1 expression showed a positive correlation between decidua and placenta but did not correlate with maternal serum levels. Maternal serum sFlt-1 levels diverged: with high levels (>11 500 pg/mL) only in preeclamptic pregnancies (n=21) and low levels (<11 500 pg/mL) in all normal pregnancies (n=28) and 42% (n=15) of preeclamptic pregnancies.
CONCLUSIONS: sFlt-1 expression correlates across the maternal-fetal interface but is not directly reflected in maternal serum. The relationship to preeclampsia subtypes is complex.

articles.title: HPV16 E7-Containing Exosomes May Contribute to PD-L1 Expression in Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes of Cervical Cancer.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Shen G, Luo L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus 16 (HPV16) plays a major role in the development of cervical cancer (CC). Programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) is an important feature of the tumor immune microenvironment and may affect responses to immune checkpoint blockade. However, the relationship between the HPV16 E7 oncoprotein and PD-L1 expression in TILs remains unclear.
AIM: To investigate the presence of HPV16 E7 protein in exosomes from CC tissues and plasma, determine the association between exosomal E7 and PD-L1 expression in TILs, and explore whether E7-rich tumor-derived exosomes contribute to increased PD-L1 expression in TILs.
STUDY DESIGN: This study combined clinical observational analyses and in vitro experiments. Three CC single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, a 30-patient HPV16-positive cohort, and a 104-patient tissue microarray cohort were analyzed. In vitro experiments were conducted to further examine the potential relationship between exosomal E7 and PD-L1 expression in TILs.
METHODS: Blood and pathological samples from 30 patients with HPV16-positive CC, as well as culture fluid from the C33A and SiHa CC cell lines, were collected. Exosomes were isolated, and E7 protein expression was assessed. Bioinformatics analyses of CC single-cell RNA sequencing datasets were performed to evaluate CD274 mRNA expression in TILs. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was used to assess PD-L1 protein expression in TILs in the 30-patient cohort, while multiplex immunofluorescence was used to evaluate E7 and PD-L1 expression in TILs in a 104-patient tissue microarray. Exosome uptake by TILs was assessed using confocal microscopy. TILs were co-cultured with exosomes, and HPV16 E7 and PD-L1 expression was evaluated by quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and western blotting in the TIL blank control, co-culture blank control, co-culture empty vector, and co-culture E7-overexpression groups.
RESULTS: E7 protein was detected in exosomes from the peripheral blood of 28 of 30 patients (93.3%) and in exosomes from SiHa cell culture. PD-L1 was expressed in TILs, with a positive rate of 43.3% (13/30). In the tissue microarray cohort (n = 103; 28 events), higher CD3+PD-L1+/CD3+ expression was associated with poorer survival (HR = 2.97, p = 0.009). CD3+E7+/CD3+ expression showed a borderline association with poorer survival in the dichotomized analysis (HR = 2.15, p = 0.052) but was significantly…

articles.title: Epidemiological Trends and Global Burden of Cervical Cancer: Insights From the 2021 Global Burden of Disease Study.
articles.journal: Physiotherapy research international : the journal for researchers and clinicians in physical therapy
articles.authors: Zhu L, Zhou C, Tong Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Cervical cancer remains a major global health burden, with substantial geographic and sociodemographic inequalities. Although age-standardized rates have declined in many settings, changes in absolute burden, temporal turning points, demographic drivers, development-related national disparities, and non-fatal burden require further characterization. To assess global cervical cancer burden from 1990 to 2021 using GBD 2021 data, with particular emphasis on temporal changes, demographic decomposition, SDI-related national disparities, and non-fatal burden.
METHODS: Annual cervical cancer estimates among females were obtained from GBD 2021 for 1990-2021. Incidence, deaths, DALYs, prevalence, and YLDs were examined globally, across five SDI groups, 21 GBD regions, and 204 countries and territories. Joinpoint regression was used to identify temporal changes in ASIR, ASMR, and ASDR. Changes in absolute burden were decomposed into population growth, population ageing, and epidemiological change. National observed-to-expected (O/E) ratios were estimated from spline-modeled relationships between SDI and age-standardized rates.
RESULTS: Globally, incident cases, deaths, and DALYs increased by 63.0%, 40.3%, and 33.6%, respectively, whereas ASIR, ASMR, and ASDR declined by 15.5%, 32.0%, and 31.4%. Joinpoint analysis identified periods of plateau and rebound within the overall declining trends. Population growth was the largest contributor to increasing absolute burden, while epidemiological change partly offset mortality and DALY increases. SDI was inversely associated with ASIR, ASMR, and ASDR in 2021, but substantial national O/E variation persisted. Prevalent cases increased by 80.9% and YLDs by 76.3%, despite little change in age-standardized prevalence and a modest decline in the age-standardized YLD rate.
DISCUSSION: Despite declining age-standardized mortality and DALY rates, the absolute and non-fatal burden of cervical cancer continues to increase, largely under demographic pressure. Uneven temporal and national patterns highlight the need to complement prevention and treatment efforts with greater attention to survivorship and long-term functional health.

articles.title: Modified LIFT via a Lateral Approach Versus Standard LIFT for Transsphincteric Anal Fistula: A Prospective Randomized Study.
articles.authors: Tok T, Sevim Y
articles.abstract:
AIM: To compare the early clinical outcomes of modified ligation of the intersphincteric fistula tract (LIFT) via a lateral approach with those of standard LIFT in patients with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-confirmed transsphincteric anal fistula.
METHODS: This single-center prospective randomized study included adult patients with transsphincteric anal fistula who were treated between January and May 2024 and were followed through August 2024. Among 96 patients assessed for eligibility, 46 met the eligibility criteria, and 40 consenting patients were randomized at a 1:1 ratio to standard LIFT or modified LIFT via a lateral approach. Follow-up was performed at postoperative weeks 1, 4, 8, and 12. The primary outcome was wound healing time. Secondary outcomes included early recurrence or persistence, postoperative pain assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS), and continence evaluated using the Cleveland Clinic Fecal Incontinence Scale.
RESULTS: A total of 40 patients were analyzed, with 20 patients in each group. Baseline demographic and available clinical characteristics were comparable between the groups. The median wound healing time was significantly shorter in the modified LIFT group than in the standard LIFT group (13 [interquartile range, 10-17] days vs. 29.5 [26-32] days; p < 0.001). No early recurrence or persistence was observed in the modified LIFT group by week 12. In the standard LIFT group, recurrence/persistence was observed in 3 of the 20 patients (15.0%) at week 8 and in 6 of the 20 patients (30.0%) at week 12 (Fisher exact test at week 12; p = 0.020). The median VAS pain scores were low and comparable in the standard LIFT versus modified LIFT groups at week 1 (0.90 vs. 0.95; p = 0.942) and week 4 (0.00 vs. 0.00; p = 0.115). No case of fecal incontinence was noted in either group during follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: In selected patients with transsphincteric anal fistula, compared with standard LIFT, modified LIFT via a lateral approach was associated with faster early wound healing and a lower rate of early recurrence/persistence within 12 weeks, without an observed increase in postoperative pain or fecal incontinence. Larger studies with longer follow-up are warranted before definitive conclusions can be drawn regarding long-term recurrence.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07603635.

articles.title: Diagnostic Value of FAR, CAR, and PNI in Differentiating Benign From Malignant Endometrial Lesions and Assessing High-Risk Pathological Features.
articles.authors: Hu J, Zhang Y, Shao M
articles.abstract:
AIM: Benign endometrial lesions and endometrial cancer often overlap in clinical and ultrasonographic features. This study evaluated the ability of the fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio (FAR), C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR), and prognostic nutritional index (PNI) to differentiate benign endometrial lesions from endometrial cancer and examined their associations with high-risk pathological features.
METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included 374 patients with histopathologically confirmed endometrial lesions, comprising 250 benign lesions and 124 endometrial cancers. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to assess discrimination, and a clinical ultrasound model was constructed. PNI, CAR, and FAR were separately added to the model, followed by bootstrap internal validation. Associations with high-risk pathological features were evaluated using Firth logistic regression adjusted for age, body mass index (BMI), and histologic type.
RESULTS: Patients with endometrial cancer had lower PNI and higher CAR and FAR levels. The areas under the curve (AUCs) for FAR, PNI, and CAR were 0.820, 0.793, and 0.781, respectively. The clinical ultrasound model had an AUC of 0.863, which increased to 0.918 after adding FAR and remained 0.903 after bootstrap correction. After correction for multiple comparisons, lower PNI and higher FAR were associated with deep myometrial invasion, lymphovascular space invasion, International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage III-IV, and grade 3 tumors, whereas CAR showed no statistically significant associations.
CONCLUSIONS: FAR showed the highest observed discriminatory performance among PNI and CAR and provided incremental information beyond the clinical ultrasound model. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

articles.title: Effect of Adjunctive Mifepristone Pre-treatment on Operative Efficiency and Postoperative Recovery in Cesarean Scar Pregnancy Undergoing Curettage After Uterine Artery Embolization.
articles.authors: Lv J, Pan J, Weng X et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aims to evaluate whether short-course mifepristone pre-treatment improves procedural efficiency and early recovery after uterine artery embolization (UAE), followed by dilation and curettage (D&C) for cesarean scar pregnancy.
METHODS: This retrospective study recruited 108 patients with cesarean scar pregnancy who underwent dilation and D&C between January 2020 and July 2023. Patients were divided into 2 groups according to the pre-treatment approach. The control group (n = 65) received pre-treatment with UAE alone, while the study group (n = 43) received pre-treatment with mifepristone in addition to the treatment used in the control group. The two groups were compared for operative metrics, early recovery, and postoperative adverse events. Serum β-human chorionic gonadotrophin (β-hCG) levels were evaluated upon admission and again on postoperative day 1. Patients were followed for one year to assess pregnancy-related outcomes, and the findings were compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: In the study group, the surgery duration was shorter, and the intraoperative blood loss was lower than in the control group (p < 0.05). The length of hospital stay was comparable between the two groups (p > 0.05). Similarly, the incidences of repeat D&C, massive hemorrhage, and re-embolization of the uterine artery were also comparable between groups (p > 0.05). There were no cases of conversion to laparotomy or hysterectomy in either group. At the time of admission, the β-hCG levels in the study group were not significantly different from those in the control group. However, on the first day after the procedure, the β-hCG levels in the study group were lower than those in the control group, but the difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.051). The study group had a shorter duration of vaginal bleeding and achieved normal menstrual function earlier than the control group (p < 0.05). The menstrual cycle was comparable between the two groups (p > 0.05). The incidences of fever, gastrointestinal symptoms, abnormal liver function, and intrauterine adhesions were also comparable between the two groups (p > 0.05). Follow-up analysis showed no significant differences between the two groups in subsequent pregnancy or recurrence of cesarean scar pregnancy (p > 0.05). Time to pregnancy was descriptively reported only among patients who achieved pregnancy and was not statistically compared because of the small number of events.
CONCLUSIONS:…

articles.title: Patient experience with early pregnancy loss in the primary care setting: a qualitative study.
articles.authors: Harriett LE, Maristany S, Sanchez L et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This qualitative study describes patient perspectives on early pregnancy loss (EPL), the medical term for miscarriage, care in one federally qualified health centre (FQHC) that initiated provision of a mifepristone plus misoprostol regimen.
BACKGROUND: EPL is a common pregnancy complication that can generally be treated by primary care providers (PCPs), yet many PCPs report barriers to providing the most effective medication regimen: mifepristone plus misoprostol. Limited data exist on patient experiences with EPL in the primary care setting.
METHODS: Researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with a sample of patients who received EPL care from one Illinois FQHC between 2021 and 2022. Interview transcripts were coded and analysed to identify themes regarding how primary care can address patients' needs when experiencing pregnancy loss.
RESULTS: Participants (n = 16) expressed satisfaction with EPL management at the FQHC, specifically that the option of medication management eased concerns about potential complications and provided clear expectations of the passage of the pregnancy. Medication management became a more accessible option for patients after the clinic began stocking mifepristone. Participant suggestions to improve EPL management in primary care included stronger and/or more timely analgesia, increased education, and mental health support. Participants identified barriers to EPL care including difficulty scheduling visits and perceived lack of urgency when triaged by clinic staff.
CONCLUSION: Patients report comfort with and interest in the option of medication management for EPL in the community-based primary care setting. Barriers in primary care clinic infrastructure and logistics must be considered and optimized to provide timely and safe EPL care.

articles.title: Masculine Attitudes and Vasectomy Uptake in the United States.
articles.authors: Brewer M, Murdock R
articles.abstract: Vasectomy has potential to disrupt normative gendered expectations around contraception that place an unequal burden of pregnancy prevention on women and their bodies. Despite this, and evidence linking masculine ideals with men's health behaviours, studies rarely consider how masculinity shapes men's contraceptive practices, including their use of male contraception. We examine how masculine attitudes relate to vasectomy use among a national sample of contracepting men in the United States. Drawing on male respondents from the 2011-2019 National Survey of Family Growth aged 25 to 44 (N = 5899), we find that vasectomy is more common among men who agree that men have greater sexual needs than women. However, this difference is mostly explained by men's number of biological children, which strongly predicts vasectomy uptake. This suggests that men may hold traditional masculine attitudes while disrupting the gendered division of contraceptive labour via vasectomy. We also find that vasectomy status does not differ based on attitudes about men going to the doctor for preventive health care or showing pain. This study has implications for advancing research on the determinants of vasectomy use and men's role in contraception.

articles.title: Clinical, Cytological, and Virological Factors Associated with Histological Severity and Recurrence in Vaginal Intraepithelial Neoplasia: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
articles.authors: Della Corte L, Palumbo M, Foreste V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VAIN) is a rare HPV-related condition with heterogeneous behavior and a relevant recurrence risk. Factors associated with severity and recurrence remain incompletely defined.
OBJECTIVE: To explore clinical, cytological, virological, and colposcopic features associated with high-grade VAIN and recurrence.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 42 women with histologically confirmed VAIN at a tertiary center between January 2020 and January 2026. All underwent vaginal cytology, high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotyping, colposcopy, and biopsy. Histology was classified as VAIN1 or VAIN2-3. Recurrence was defined as a histologically confirmed lesion after treatment and documented disease-free assessment. Associations were assessed using bivariate and exact analyses.
RESULTS: VAIN2-3 was diagnosed in 31 women (73.8%). Among HR-HPV-positive women, HPV16-related infection was more frequent in VAIN2-3 than VAIN1 (65.4% vs 18.2%; OR 8.50, 95% CI 1.27-91.56; p = 0.013). Cytology was associated with histological grade (p = 0.024); all women with HSIL/ASC-H had VAIN2-3, although sensitivity was limited. Over a median follow-up of 24 months, eight women (19.0%) recurred after a median of 11.5 months. HPV16-related infection was more frequent with recurrence (75.0% vs 38.2%; OR 4.85, 95% CI 0.70-54.01; p = 0.112), but the evidence was not definitive. HPV16-only infection showed borderline evidence of association (p = 0.050), while no clear outcome pattern emerged for multiple-genotype infection. No other significant associations with recurrence were observed.
CONCLUSION: HPV16-related infection was associated with high-grade histology among HR-HPV-positive women, while its prognostic relevance for recurrence remains uncertain. The limited sensitivity of cytology underscores the value of multimodal assessment. These exploratory signals warrant prospective validation.

articles.title: Folate receptor alpha expression in uterine serous carcinoma: a single-institution analysis.
articles.authors: Batra S, Huang T, Skala S et al.
articles.abstract: Uterine serous carcinoma (USC) is an aggressive histologic subtype of endometrial cancer for which limited targeted therapeutic options exist. Folate receptor alpha (FOLRα) is an established therapeutic target in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, but its expression patterns in USC remain poorly characterized. We sought to evaluate the prevalence and distribution of FOLRα expression in USC and assess the applicability of ovarian cancer-derived FOLRα thresholds to this histology. We conducted a retrospective review of patients with pathologically confirmed USC treated at a single institution from 2017 to 2024. FOLRα expression was assessed using the VENTANA FOLR1 (FOLR1-2.1) RxDx assay. Positivity was defined as ≥75% of tumor cells demonstrating moderate-to-strong membranous staining (PS2+ scoring). Seventy-three patients were included. Median age was 71 years; 53% had uterine-confined disease at presentation. In our cohort, nine tumors (12.3%) met the high-expression threshold for FOLRα positivity. An additional 13 tumors (17.8%) demonstrated intermediate expression, while 69.9% showed <50% staining. FOLRα expression in USC is variable, and only a minority of tumors met the high-expression threshold used for mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV) eligibility in ovarian cancer. However, nearly one-third demonstrated medium-to-high expression, suggesting that FOLRα targeting may not be fully captured by ovarian cancer-derived biomarker cutoffs in this disease process. These descriptive, hypothesis-generating findings support further evaluation of FOLRα-directed strategies, including combination approaches, in prospective studies of USC.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Vitex Extract on Menopausal Symptoms and Quality of Life in Postmenopausal Women: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Reddy PA, Aluri S, Ca A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postmenopausal women often experience vasomotor and hormonal symptoms due to a decline in estradiol levels, which affects their quality of life (QOL). Botanical extracts like Vitexextract, known for their estrogen- and progesterone-like actions, may offer a safe and effective approach for alleviating postmenopausal symptoms and improving overall quality of life.
METHODS: The current study was a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, monocenter clinical study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Vitex extract in postmenopausal women aged 40-65 years. Sixty eligible participants were randomized to either the Vitex extract or placebo group equally and instructed to take one capsule daily after breakfast for 60 days. The primary endpoints included changes in the Blatt-Kupperman Index (BKI), Menopause-Specific Quality of Life Questionnaire (MENQOL), Menopause Rating Scale (MRS), and overall QOL scores. The study was prospectively registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2025/03/082025).
RESULTS: After 60 days, Vitex extract supplementation led to clinically and statistically significant improvements compared with placebo in all primary outcomes. Notable reductions were observed in BKI, MENQOL, and MRS scores, reflecting better control of vasomotor, psychosocial, physical, and sexual symptoms. Improvements were also seen in the reduction in joint and muscle pain, stress levels, and serum cortisol. Hormonal regulation of luteinizing hormone (LH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), estradiol, and thyroid function, along with reduced rheumatoid factor, indicated anti-inflammatory and endocrine benefits. No adverse effects or lab abnormalities were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center study, Vitex extract appeared effective and was well tolerated, suggesting its potential as a safe, non-hormonal option for relieving menopausal symptoms and improving quality of life in postmenopausal women. However, these findings should be confirmed in larger, multi-center trials before broader clinical recommendations can be made.

articles.title: Hypothesis-Generating Single-Cell Analysis of the Endometrial Cancer Immune Microenvironment With Complementary Multiomics Evidence.
articles.authors: Ouyang X, Guo X, Yang X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial cancer (EC) has a heterogeneous immune microenvironment, and response-associated biology remains incompletely characterized. We used the retained EC single-cell dataset to describe immune-cell states and complemented it with TCGA-UCEC, independent gut microbiome cohorts, and RL95-2 proof-of-concept experiments. All responder versus nonresponder scRNA-seq comparisons are descriptive and hypothesis generating because only one sample was available per clinical response group.
