METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from EC patients undergoing anti-PD-1 immunotherapy (GEO: GSE251923; one responder, GSM7990051, and one nonresponder, GSM7990052; 17,546 cells retained after quality control) were analyzed using Scanpy, Leiden clustering, and over-representation analysis with GO biological process, KEGG, and MSigDB Hallmark gene sets using Enrichr with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Bulk RNA-seq from TCGA-UCEC (554 tumor and 35 normal samples) was used for complementary transcriptomic analysis. Gut microbiome 16S rRNA datasets (SRA: PRJNA897842 and PRJNA833670) were analyzed as independent cohorts, and RL95-2 qRT-PCR experiments were interpreted as proof-of-concept.
RESULTS: Ten major cell populations were identified in the EC immune microenvironment. In this single responder/nonresponder sample pair, the nonresponder sample showed patterns consistent with higher M2-associated macrophage marker expression, increased T-cell checkpoint/exhaustion marker expression, and lower cytotoxic activity scores. These observations are descriptive and cannot establish patient-level significance. TCGA-UCEC analyses and the independent microbiome and RL95-2 experiments provide complementary, hypothesis-generating evidence; no unverified classifier-performance estimate is reported.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a hypothesis-generating description of immune patterns in one EC responder and one nonresponder sample, complemented by TCGA-UCEC, independent microbiome datasets, and RL95-2 proof-of-concept experiments. The findings nominate candidate immune, hormonal, and microbiome-associated pathways for further investigation but do not establish patient-level response differences, causality, or clinically validated biomarkers.

articles.title: Acute macular neuroretinopathy: is the name still appropriate?
articles.journal: Medical hypothesis, discovery & innovation ophthalmology journal
articles.authors: Mambretti M, Casalino G
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute macular neuroretinopathy (AMN) is a rare but increasingly reported retinal disorder that predominantly affects young women and is characterized by acute-onset paracentral scotomas and distinctive parafoveal macular lesions. Following its first report in 1975 as an inner retinal disease, a considerable body of work has been produced, expanding on its clinical presentation and systemic associations. Aim of this review is to synthesize the current understanding of AMN, including existing controversies on nomenclature.
METHODS: A literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE for English-language articles published up to 31 July 2025. Search terms included "acute macular neuroretinopathy" and "acute macular outer retinopathy". Additional relevant sources were identified through manual screening of reference lists and targeted updating of the literature through 28 August 2025. Relevant articles were selected for inclusion in this narrative review based on the authors' judgment of relevance to the review aims.
RESULTS: Multiple cases of AMN in association with a variety of ocular and systemic conditions have been reported. Reported associations include viral illnesses such as influenza, Dengue fever, oral contraceptive use, vasoconstrictive agents, non-ocular trauma, and vaccination. An increased incidence of AMN was reported at a single center during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. Advances in multimodal retinal imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography, have led to a more precise localization and insight into the pathogenesis of the disease in the outer retinal layers. These findings have prompted some authors to suggest renaming the condition acute macular outer retinopathy (AMOR) to better reflect the anatomical involvement.
CONCLUSIONS: AMN appears to primarily affect the outer retinal layers, with current evidence suggesting a role for underlying vascular impairment in its pathogenesis. Although "AMOR" may offer a more anatomically precise description, AMN remains widely used in the academic literature and continues to be both appropriate and accepted. Further research is needed to elucidate the underlying pathophysiology, precisely localize the site of vascular impairment, and explore potential therapeutic strategies. In this context, consistent terminology is essential, and the continued use of the acronym "AMN" is supported by both clinical and historical considerations.

articles.title: Effect of a Subanesthetic Dose of Esketamine on Postoperative Sleep Disturbance After Oocyte Retrieval Under Intravenous Anesthesia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Ma Q, Li H, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) is a common complication after oocyte retrieval under intravenous anesthesia. This study aimed to evaluate whether a subanesthetic dose of esketamine reduces the incidence of PSD.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial included 196 women undergoing oocyte retrieval under intravenous anesthesia. Participants were randomly assigned to the esketamine or control group. During anesthesia induction, the esketamine group received an intravenous bolus of esketamine 0.2 mg/kg, whereas the control group received an equivalent volume of normal saline. The primary analysis was conducted according to the intention-to-treat principle, with missing outcome data handled using multiple imputation; 189 participants (95 in the control group and 94 in the esketamine group) were included in the per-protocol sensitivity analysis. The primary outcome was the incidence of PSD on postoperative day (POD) 3, defined using a composite criterion of an Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS) score ≥6 or a numerical rating scale (NRS) score ≥6. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of PSD on POD 1, postoperative pain scores, postoperative anxiety and depression scores, and patient satisfaction with the anesthetic technique.
RESULTS: In the intention-to-treat analysis with multiple imputation, the estimated incidence of PSD on POD 3 was lower in the esketamine group than in the control group (13.06% vs 24.90%; risk difference, -11.84 percentage points [95% CI, -22.98 to -0.69]; relative risk [RR], 0.52 [95% CI, 0.28-0.99]; P = 0.047). The per-protocol (PP) sensitivity analysis yielded similar results (12.8% vs 24.2%; RR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.28-0.99]; P = 0.043). PSD on POD 1 did not differ between the groups. No between-group differences in postoperative anxiety or depression scores were noted. Postoperative pain scores at 30 minutes were significantly lower in the esketamine group (P < 0.001). Dreaming was more frequent in the esketamine group (21.4% vs 11.2%; P = 0.048), and the time to full alertness (12 [10-14] vs 11 [9-13] minutes; P = 0.002) and postanesthesia care unit (PACU) stay (34 [30-37] vs 31 [29-34] minutes; P = 0.005) were modestly longer.
CONCLUSION: A single subanesthetic dose of esketamine was associated with a lower incidence of short-term PSD on POD 3 in women undergoing oocyte retrieval under intravenous anesthesia. Larger multicenter studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Long-term prophylaxis for hereditary angioedema: Navigating the switch between therapies.
articles.authors: Banerji A, Bernstein JA, Bouillet L et al.
articles.abstract: Long-term prophylactic treatments (LTPs) are a major component of disease management for patients with hereditary angioedema (HAE). Patients with HAE experience considerable disease burden, as the frequent, unpredictable, and potentially life-threatening nature of HAE attacks negatively impacts patients' quality of life. LTPs aim to mitigate HAE symptoms by reducing HAE attack frequency and severity, leading to improved disease management and quality of life. As the treatment landscape has recently expanded with the addition of approved LTPs (namely, garadacimab and donidalorsen in 2025), the decision to switch between therapies is becoming increasingly common in clinical practice, and physicians and patients must carefully navigate these treatment transitions to minimize the risk of breakthrough HAE attacks and other safety concerns. Across clinical studies, treatment switching was reported for a variety of reasons, including suboptimal efficacy or frequent breakthrough attacks, safety and adverse events, family planning, treatment burden (including the LTP dosing frequency and route of administration), and drug costs and access. As these treatment options have unique mechanisms of action, durations of effect, and drug clearance rates, clinicians must carefully evaluate approaches for patients to safely switch between therapies while aiming to minimize the risk of breakthrough attacks due to lapses in prophylaxis. This review summarizes the current clinical data available in patients who have switched between first-line LTPs (namely, C1 inhibitor, lanadelumab, and berotralstat), recently approved LTPs garadacimab and donidalorsen, and second-line LTPs (androgens and antifibrinolytics) and it aims to inform health care providers as they navigate this complex treatment landscape. Clinical data available that directly evaluate or compare switching strategies between LTPs are limited, highlighting the need for further prospective studies to better characterize treatment outcomes and guide switching treatments for patients with HAE.

articles.title: LncRNA Arsa-DT is required for spermatogenesis and male fertility by regulating G2/M progression.
articles.authors: Choi H, Kim JE, Kim JY et al.
articles.abstract: Male infertility is a major reproductive health burden worldwide, yet its molecular etiology remains largely unknown. The testis expresses numerous long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), although their involvement in the pathophysiology of male infertility remains unexplored. Here, we identified Arsa-DT, a testis-predominant divergent lncRNA of Arsa, and demonstrated its essential role in maintaining male fertility. Loss of Arsa-DT leads to subfertility, characterized by reduced sperm production, increased sperm abnormalities, and decreased serum testosterone levels. Notably, Arsa-DT deficiency alters the testosterone-to-estradiol ratio through upregulation of aromatase expression. Specifically expressed in the nuclei of spermatogonia and spermatocytes, Arsa-DT regulates spermatogenesis in the seminiferous tubules. Mechanistically, Arsa-DT regulates G2/M phase progression and chromosome segregation in male germ cells. Collectively, our findings identify Arsa-DT, a testis-predominant lncRNA, as a regulator of spermatogenesis by controlling G2/M phase progression of male germ cells. This study provides mechanistic insights into the pathogenesis of male infertility.

articles.title: Caregiver-implemented standardized-to-individualized behavior-analytic toilet-training package for preschoolers with autism.
articles.authors: Osos JA, Higbee TS, Mendoza MR et al.
articles.abstract: Children with autism often face challenges with incontinence and may benefit from more structured toilet training relative to neurotypical children. In the current study, we evaluated a standardized-to-individualized behavior-analytic toilet-training package with caregivers as the interventionists. We used telehealth to train caregivers remotely to support their implementation of the procedures and obtain additional data on implementation and outcomes. Four preschool-aged children with autism and their caregivers participated. Three of four participants met mastery criteria with a standardized toilet-training package and one participant required a contingent progressive sit schedule. Intervention components were successfully faded, and all participants maintained performance after 4 weeks. The findings demonstrate that clinic-based toilet-training procedures can be implemented at home by caregivers with telehealth support. This approach to toilet training provides families with an alternative to clinic-based treatment and could increase access to treatment among those residing in rural or underserved areas.

articles.title: Integrated molecular and histopathological analysis reveals genotype-phenotype correlations and diagnostic challenges in endometrial stromal sarcoma.
articles.authors: Cai Y, Chen L, Li K et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial stromal sarcomas (ESSs) comprise a heterogeneous group of uterine mesenchymal tumors characterized by diverse morphological features and recurrent molecular alterations. Although molecular classification has substantially improved ESS diagnosis, the relationship between specific genetic alterations and morphological phenotypes remains incompletely understood. We performed an integrated molecular and histopathological analysis of ESS to investigate genotype-phenotype correlations and refine tumor classification. A total of 61 patients with histologically suspected ESSs were initially enrolled, and 51 successfully underwent targeted RNA sequencing, followed by comprehensive morphological reassessment, immunohistochemical evaluation, molecular validation, and clinicopathological correlation. Molecularly confirmed ESSs demonstrated distinct genotype-associated morphological patterns. PHF1-rearranged low-grade ESSs showed a strong association with hypocellular growth and prominent collagenized stroma. Quantitative cellularity analysis further demonstrated significantly lower tumor cellularity in PHF1-rearranged low-grade ESSs compared with JAZF1::SUZ12-rearranged tumors (p < 0.001). High-grade ESSs with YWHAE::NUTM2 and BCOR::ZC3H7B alterations showed higher mitotic activity than low-grade ESSs and demonstrated tongue-like infiltration patterns in both primary and metastatic lesions, indicating that this growth pattern, traditionally emphasized in low-grade ESSs, may represent a broader morphological feature of ESSs. Molecular reassessment led to the reclassification of 10 cases (19.6%, 10/51), identifying tumors with alternative molecular alterations that were initially diagnosed as ESSs based on morphology alone. Among these cases, a uterine sarcoma harboring a novel GATA6::SRF fusion exhibited a low-grade ESS-like morphological phenotype but lacked the characteristic molecular alterations of conventional ESSs, suggesting a potential molecularly defined uterine sarcoma subtype requiring further investigation. Our findings demonstrate that integrated molecular and histopathological analysis extends beyond diagnostic refinement by revealing genotype-phenotype relationships, expanding the molecular spectrum of ESSs and ESS-like uterine sarcomas, and providing new insights into the biological heterogeneity of these rare tumors. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

articles.title: Phenotyping Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome: Clinical and Mechanistic Evidence, Candidate Biomarkers, and Implications for Management.
articles.authors: Qiao P, Tian Z, He Z
articles.abstract: Interstitial cystitis and bladder pain syndrome are clinically overlapping conditions that should be distinguished according to Hunner lesion status. IC with Hunner lesions is a distinct inflammatory bladder disease characterized by urothelial denudation, lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, adaptive immune activation, and progressive structural impairment. The intensity and distribution of these inflammatory and structural abnormalities may vary among patients with IC, but the underlying pathological pattern is comparatively coherent. BPS without Hunner lesions is substantially more heterogeneous. Urothelial barrier dysfunction, mast cell and sensory nerve signaling, pelvic floor dysfunction, peripheral sensitization, and central or nociplastic pain mechanisms may contribute to symptoms in different combinations. Candidate urine and blood-based biomarkers, including cytokines, chemokines, neurotrophic factors, immune cell indices, and multiomics signatures, may support phenotyping, assessment of disease activity, or prediction of treatment response. However, most remain exploratory because their intended clinical use, analytical standardization, diagnostic thresholds, and external validity have not been established. This narrative review compares the clinical and histopathological features of IC and BPS, evaluates the evidence for proposed immune and neuroregulatory mechanisms, examines the translational status of candidate biomarkers, and discusses disease-specific and phenotype-guided management. These findings support a primary distinction between IC and BPS. Additional phenotyping is useful after this distinction to characterize heterogeneity within BPS and clinically relevant coexisting mechanisms.

articles.title: Conservative and Nonsurgical Management of Pelvic Organ Prolapse.
articles.authors: Hong CX, LaCross J
articles.abstract: Pelvic organ prolapse is a common condition for which treatment should be guided by symptom burden, functional impairment, and patient goals. Conservative management represents first-line therapy and includes expectant management, lifestyle and behavioral modification, pelvic floor physiotherapy, and vaginal pessary treatment. This review summarizes contemporary evidence supporting these approaches, including pelvic floor muscle training, constipation and activity management, and pessary fitting, maintenance, and outcomes. We additionally highlight recent advances in pelvic floor rehabilitation, pessary biomechanics, patient self-management, and patient-specific pessary technologies that may further individualize prolapse care.

articles.title: Sex differences in the association of uric acid to HDL-cholesterol ratio (UHR) with subclinical cardiovascular damage.
articles.authors: Rubino M, Palummo A, Massimino M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global mortality, with risk increasing significantly in women post-menopause. Identifying accessible biomarkers for subclinical risk stratification is a clinical priority. The uric acid to HDL-cholesterol ratio (UHR) has emerged as a composite marker reflecting metabolic burden and reduced vascular protection. This study investigates the independent association between UHR and subclinical organ damage, exploring sex-specific differences.
METHODS: We analyzed 1,198 Caucasian subjects. Subclinical cardiovascular damage was evaluated via carotid intima-media thickness (c-IMT) and left ventricular mass index (LVMI). Multivariate linear regression and formal interaction analyses were employed to assess the independent association of UHR with organ damage, adjusting for traditional cardiometabolic risk factors.
RESULTS: UHR correlated significantly with adiposity, insulin resistance, blood pressure, and lipid profiles. In the total population, UHR was independently associated with both c-IMT (β = 0.093, p = 0.003) and LVMI (β = 0.194, p < 0.0001). A significant sex-UHR interaction was observed for LVMI (p = 0.024). Sex-stratified analyses revealed that UHR was linked to LVMI in women, particularly those postmenopausal, but not in males. In postmenopausal women, UHR remained an independent determinant of LVMI (β = 0.164, p = 0.033).
CONCLUSIONS: UHR is independently associated with subclinical cardiovascular damage, displaying a sex-specific relationship with myocardial remodeling after menopause. As an inexpensive and easily accessible biomarker, UHR may represent a practical tool to combat clinical inertia and improve the early selection of postmenopausal women warranting targeted diagnostic workups.

articles.title: Fertility-care readiness among healthcare students and workers in Al-Baha, Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Albanghali MA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Saudi Arabia has experienced a marked fertility decline alongside health-system reforms under Vision 2030, yet evidence on healthcare workforce readiness for fertility and reproductive health (RH) counselling remains limited at the provincial level. Most Saudi studies have examined community demand, married women in primary care, or specialist groups in major urban centres. Demand-side evidence from Al-Baha indicates limited exposure to family-planning counselling and greater reliance on media than healthcare providers for RH information, highlighting the need to assess provider-side readiness in transitional provinces.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from December 2024 to February 2025 among healthcare students enrolled at Al-Baha University and active healthcare workers employed by Al-Baha Health Cluster across Public Health, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, and Laboratory Medicine. A 23-item instrument assessed four domains: Knowledge and Education, Access and Practice, Beliefs/Attitudes/Cultural Norms, and Lifestyle and Health Status.
RESULTS: Among 577 respondents, the mean age was 25.7 ± 9.0 years and 406 (70.4%) were students. Only 75 (13.0%) had attended a fertility/RH workshop, 126 (21.8%) reported full familiarity with international RH guidelines, and 209 (36.2%) were very confident in cross-cultural counselling. In multivariable analysis, high counselling confidence was associated with workshop attendance (adjusted OR [aOR] 10.78; 95% CI 4.92-23.62), cultural-value alignment with family planning (aOR 6.10; 95% CI 3.28-11.35), city residence (aOR 3.21; 95% CI 2.04-5.06), and above-median knowledge (aOR 1.71; 95% CI 1.05-2.79). Healthcare worker status showed a negative adjusted association (aOR 0.37; 95% CI 0.17-0.81), requiring cautious interpretation.
CONCLUSION: Fertility-care readiness in Al-Baha was uneven and was associated mainly with modifiable factors, notably workshop attendance, cultural-value alignment with family planning, and knowledge level, as well as the contextual factor of urban residence, rather than professional role alone. Structured fertility/RH training, culturally responsive counselling education, and capacity building beyond urban centres may strengthen workforce readiness for RH counselling.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Development and validation of a risk prediction model for preterm birth in women concurrent with Hepatitis B virus carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.authors: Gui Z, Fan X, Zang T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm birth is a major adverse neonatal outcome that has been associated with maternal hepatitis B virus carrier status. Co-occurrence of hepatitis B virus carrier status carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus is associated with an increased risk of preterm birth compared with hepatitis B virus carrier status alone. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a clinically applicable multivariable prediction model incorporating both clinical risk factors and maternal blood biomarkers to estimate preterm birth risk among women with concurrent hepatitis B virus carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed using clinical data and maternal blood biomarkers from 882 pregnant women with hepatitis B virus carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus who delivered at Women's Hospital, in Zhejiang Province, China, from January 2015 to December 2024. Following data preprocessing, participants were randomly allocated to training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. Variable selection was performed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were subsequently conducted to assess the associations of clinical variables and maternal blood biomarkers with preterm birth in women with concurrent hepatitis B virus carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus. A nomogram was developed to facilitate clinical application. Model discrimination and calibration were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis and calibration plots, respectively, while clinical utility was assessed through decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 847 women with hepatitis B virus carrier status and gestational diabetes mellitus were included in this study, of whom 187 (22%) experienced preterm birth. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified pre-pregnancy body mass index, diastolic blood pressure, systolic blood pressure, alanine aminotransferase, placenta previa, white blood cell count, and maternal blood biomarkers-including total protein, total bile acid, total thyroxine, mode of membrane rupture, and prothrombin time-as independent predictors of preterm birth. These variables were incorporated into a nomogram, which demonstrated good calibration and discrimination. The area under the curve was 0.854 (95% CI: 0.823-0.881) in the training set and 0.754 (95% CI: 0.697-0.806) in the…

articles.title: The relationship between C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index and incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity in postmenopausal women: insights from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS).
articles.authors: Wang L, Luo C, Shao Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM), defined as the coexistence of at least two cardiometabolic diseases, is an increasing public health burden. Postmenopausal women may be particularly vulnerable because menopause-related metabolic and inflammatory changes can intensify cardiometabolic risk. However, simple tools for early CMM risk prediction in this population remain limited. The C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) integrates inflammatory status and insulin resistance, but its association with incident CMM in postmenopausal women has not been fully evaluated. We therefore investigated the relationship between CTI and new-onset CMM and assessed its predictive performance and potential clinical utility when combined with other clinical variables.
METHODS: Data were obtained from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). The study included 2972 postmenopausal women (aged ≥45 years) without CMM at baseline, with a mean follow-up duration of 103.53 months. The association between CTI and the risk of CMM was assessed using a multivariate Cox regression model. The dose-response relationship was examined through restricted cubic splines (RCS), and the cumulative incidence of CMM across different CTI level groups was compared using the Kaplan-Meier curve. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses, which included repeated validation with the third wave as the baseline, reanalysis after excluding missing values, and stratification by age and menopausal age, were conducted to confirm the robustness of the findings. The predictive performance and incremental value of CTI were evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, net reclassification improvement index (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement index (IDI). Additionally, a nomogram was constructed based on variables selected through LASSO regression.
RESULTS: A total of 395 participants (13.3%) developed new-onset CMM during follow-up. Multivariate Cox regression analysis indicated that for each 1-unit increase in CTI, the risk of CMM rose by 95% (HR=1.95, 95%CI: 1.66-2.30). In comparison to the lowest quartile group of CTI, the highest quartile group had a higher risk of CMM (HR=3.91, 95%CI: 2.62-5.82, P for trend <0.001). RCS analysis suggested a positive linear association between CTI and the risk of CMM (P-overall <0.001, P-nonlinear = 0.577). The Kaplan-Meier curve showed a higher cumulative incidence of CMM in the high CTI group…

articles.title: Family Planning Data and Measurement in the Era of Changing Global Development Architecture.
articles.authors: Farid S, Wolfe A, MacQuarrie K et al.
articles.abstract: Decades of progress in global sexual and reproductive health programming and data availability are threatened as over 80 percent of donor funding for family planning (FP) comes from governments that have announced significant cuts to official development assistance. This commentary examines how FP2030 is adapting its measurement framework and annual reporting given uncertainty around the future of household surveys, such as the Demographic and Health Survey, and the loss of technical resources. FP2030 will pivot from reporting on 22 indicators to a "minimum set" of 15 priority indicators. FP2030's Performance Monitoring and Evidence Working Group (PME WG), a group of FP measurement experts, arrived at these recommendations through a series of consensus-building working meetings. The 15 indicators leverage existing mathematical models and health management information systems (HMIS). Moreover, this commentary provides a complementary set of indicators that should be prioritized if new data collection opportunities arise. Ultimately, while FP2030 and the PME WG believe that models and HMIS data will become more essential, these tools cannot fully replace household surveys. Continued investment in FP data availability remains critical to ensuring the community can review data that protects the rights and needs of individuals.

articles.title: Screening for beta thalassemia trait in a heterogeneous university-based population in Delhi-NCR, India.
articles.authors: Choudhury O, Saraswathy KN, Lal A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thalassemia is a major monogenic blood disorder, with India bearing a substantial burden. Although carrier screening is the most effective preventive strategy, inconsistent criteria, borderline HbA2 values, diverse mutations, and limited HbE detection hinder effectiveness. This study determines the prevalence of molecularly confirmed beta thalassemia trait (BTT) and HbE detected through a large-scale screening approach among young adults in Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) and develops a potential scalable model for university-based carrier detection.
METHODS: We recruited 4886 young adults aged 18-35 years from universities in Delhi-NCR. All blood samples underwent CBC and HPLC analysis, with selected samples subjected to genetic analysis using ARMS-PCR and Sanger sequencing.
RESULTS: The prevalence of molecularly confirmed BTT and HbE trait detected through the study screening approach was 1.6% and 0.4%, respectively. Overall, 2% showed elevated HbA2 with low MCV and MCH, while 5.1% of carriers had borderline HbA2. Five common beta thalassemia mutations accounted for 84.8% of cases. Nearly 21% of samples with HbA2 4-9% showed no mutations on genetic testing. HbA2 4-9% plus low MCV and MCH showed the highest PPV, with 92% sensitivity and 88% specificity. No significant differences in BTT distribution were observed by region, religion, or social category.
CONCLUSIONS: Large-scale screening for BTT among young adults in university-based settings may facilitate early carrier identification. HbA2 levels of 4-9% combined with low MCV and MCH appear to be an effective first-tier screening criterion, while further criteria are needed to identify and prioritize individuals with borderline HbA2 levels (3.2-3.9%) for molecular confirmation. Future studies should focus on developing and validating robust, context-appropriate population-level screening protocols for BTT in India.

articles.title: The use of nonsteroid anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID) after artificial insemination in high milk yielding cows.
articles.authors: Tsiligianni SA, Saratsi A, Tsiligianni T
articles.abstract: Reproductive performance is markedly reduced during high milk production. In this study, we used a combination of meloxicam, a non-steroid anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), known to inhibit the synthesis of prostaglandins, with or without GnRH, a hormone commonly used to induce ovulation or luteinization in cattle. The effects of meloxicam (0.5 mg/kg BW) alone or in combination with GnRH (100 µg of gonadoreline) were evaluated in cows with medium (MMY, n = 59, 30-40 L milk at the 10-day interval before and after AI) and high (HMY, n = 57, > 40 L) milk production from 90 to 120 days in milk. Cows (n = 46) received ovsynch with double PGF2α at day 7 and 8 after the 1st GnRH; 24 of these cows received GnRH at day 7 after AI and NSAID at day 15 after AI (meta-ovsynch, OS+GnRH+NSAID), the rest (n = 22) was the control group (OS). Furthermore, cows (n = 70) at natural estrous were divided randomly into 3 AI groups: (1) AI (n = 24), cows received only AI, (2) AI+NSAID (n = 24) cows received NSAID 15 d after AI and (3) AI+GnRH+NSAID (n = 22) cows received GnRH 7 d after AI and NSAID 15 d after AI. Pregnancy diagnosis was performed by PAG 28 d after AI. Z0.5 criterion was used to compare the conception rates (CR). Between ovsynch groups no significant difference was observed. Among AI groups, the CR was higher (P = 0.012) in the AI+GnRH+NSAID (72.73%) than in the AI group (41.67%). Furthermore, in HMY cows, significantly higher CR was recorded in the AI+GnRH+NSAID (70%) compared to the AI+NSAID (25%) or the AI (42.86%) groups; in MMY cows, CR was higher (P < 0.05) in the AI+NSAID (83.33%) and AI+GnRH+NSAID (75%) compared to the AI group (40%) It seems that different protocols could be used depending on the milk yield at AI.

articles.title: Reproductive and litter performance following artificial insemination using semen transported in conventional and temperature-monitored carriers: a field evaluation in rural smallholder pig farms.
articles.authors: Pearodwong P, Nitiwararak K, Junsuri T et al.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the association between semen transportation method and reproductive and litter performance following artificial insemination (AI) in rural smallholder pig farms. A total of 191 inseminated Landrace × Yorkshire crossbred females (40 gilts and 151 sows) from 23 farms in Nan Province, Thailand, were included. Females were classified according to semen transportation method as either conventional carrier (n = 96) or temperature-monitored carrier (n = 95). Associations between transportation method, distance group, season, female category, and their interactions and reproductive performance, litter traits, and birth weight characteristics were evaluated. Transportation method was not significantly associated with conception, pregnancy, or farrowing rates (P > 0.05). However, the temperature-monitored carrier was associated with higher numbers of piglets born alive (10.95 ± 0.71 vs. 9.03 ± 0.60; P = 0.029) and total born piglets per litter (12.26 ± 0.63 vs. 10.84 ± 0.60; P = 0.039) compared with the conventional carrier. Significant interactions between transportation method and distance group were observed for born alive (P = 0.007) and total born piglets (P = 0.029). Litter size remained relatively constant across distance groups in the temperature-monitored carrier group, whereas litter size was observed at greater transportation distance in the conventional carrier group. In conclusion, the use of a temperature-monitored carrier was associated with higher numbers of born alive and total born piglets per litter but was not associated with fertility rates under practical smallholder farming conditions. The association between transportation distance and litter performance varied between semen transportation methods under practical conditions in rural smallholder pig farms.

articles.title: Gestational age-specific nomograms for fetal eyeball depth and intraocular measurements using 3-D ultrasound.
articles.authors: Odeh M, Nasra R, Leibovitz Z et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To establish gestational age-specific nomograms for fetal eyeball anteroposterior (AP) diameter and intraocular measurements (lens AP diameter, vitreous body AP diameter).
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted and included singleton pregnancies without prenatal or postnatal structural abnormalities. Three-dimensional ultrasound volumes of the fetal face acquired between 12 and 41 weeks' gestation were analyzed using multiplanar reformatting to obtain a standardized axial orbital plane. Right and left eyeball, lens, and vitreous body AP diameters were measured. Gestational age-specific reference ranges were generated using percentile distributions. Quadratic regression was used to assess associations with gestational age and biparietal diameter.
RESULTS: Of 608 volumes screened, 588 were included. Complete assessment of all parameters was available in 577 (98.1%). All ocular and intraocular measurements increased with gestational age (all p < 0.001). Quadratic regression demonstrated associations between gestational age and eyeball AP diameter (right R2 = 0.80; left R2 = 0.79), lens AP diameter (right R2 = 0.44; left R2 = 0.42), and vitreous body AP diameter (right R2 = 0.80; left R2 = 0.81). Similar associations were observed with biparietal diameter (all p < 0.001). Gestational age-specific nomograms and percentile tables are presented.
CONCLUSIONS: Gestational age-specific nomograms for fetal eyeball depth and intraocular measurements are provided and may support objective prenatal assessment of fetal ocular growth.

articles.title: The impact of obesity and overweight on maternal and fetal health with conservative preconception interventions: a structured narrative review.
articles.authors: Mateusz S, Aleksandra H, Katarzyna F et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Overweight and obesity before pregnancy are associated with adverse maternal, pregnancy-related, and longer-term health outcomes. This review aimed to summarize recent evidence on preconception overweight and obesity and to synthesize findings on conservative preconception or interpregnancy interventions, including lifestyle, dietary, behavioral, weight-management, and supplementation-based strategies.
METHODS: A structured narrative review with a predefined database search was conducted. PubMed and Embase were searched for studies published between January 2019 and December 2023 using the search string (("obesity" OR "overweight") AND "preconception"). Due to heterogeneity in study design, populations, interventions, comparators, outcomes, and follow-up durations, findings were synthesized narratively rather than quantitatively. Thirteen studies were included: 11 intervention studies and 2 observational cohort studies retained as contextual evidence.
RESULTS: Observational evidence associated higher preconception BMI with adverse pregnancy-related outcomes, including labor induction, cesarean delivery, preterm birth, neonatal care admission, stillbirth, and post-delivery dysglycemia. Conservative interventions showed heterogeneous effects. Preconception weight loss was associated with selected fertility-related and glucose-related benefits in some studies, including shorter time to pregnancy after a very-low-energy diet intervention and lower odds of recurrent gestational diabetes mellitus when meaningful weight loss was achieved. Supplementation-based interventions showed inconsistent findings across BMI subgroups. Safety-related outcomes varied between studies, and long-term follow-up suggested that sustained benefits may depend on successful weight loss and maintenance of behavioral change.
CONCLUSIONS: Conservative preconception interventions may provide selected benefits for women with overweight or obesity, particularly when clinically meaningful weight loss is achieved. However, current evidence remains heterogeneous and does not define a single optimal intervention model, timing, or universal weight-loss target.

articles.title: Short-term obstetrical and neonatal complications in women with endometriosis.
articles.authors: Leybovitz-Haleluya N, Gutvirtz G, Bendet A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endometriosis is a chronic gynecological condition that affects women in their reproductive age and could potentially lead to reproductive difficulties. Despite extensive research into the impact of endometriosis on fertility and reproductive health, its association with obstetric complications and short-term neonatal outcomes is still an area of limited understanding with conflicting evidence in published studies. We conducted this study to explore a potential effect of endometriosis on obstetric and neonatal outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective population-based cohort study was conducted comparing obstetric and perinatal complications in women with and without endometriosis. We evaluated all singleton deliveries that occurred between 1991 and 2021 at a tertiary medical center. Fetuses with chromosomal abnormalities or congenital malformations were excluded. Generalized estimation equation (GEE) models were used to control for maternal recurrence in the cohort and for confounding variables.
RESULTS: During the study period, 232,476 deliveries met our inclusion criteria, 0.1% (n = 224) of whom had documented endometriosis. In the univariate analysis, women with endometriosis were significantly older, had higher rates of infertility and diabetes mellitus, and were more likely to undergo cesarean delivery. They also had higher rates of preterm birth and low birthweight infants, whereas perinatal mortality rates were comparable between the groups. In the GEE models, after controlling for maternal age, gravidity, and fertility treatments, the association for most of the aforementioned variables was no longer statistically significant. However, women with endometriosis were found to have a significant independent higher risk for cesarean delivery (adjusted OR 2.14 (1.62-2.83, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Among the obstetrical and perinatal complications investigated in this study, endometriosis was found to be an independent risk factor for cesarean delivery, while all other pregnancy outcomes were comparable to women without endometriosis.

articles.title: Genome-Wide NIPT With Fetal-Fraction Enrichment and BinDel: Clinical Cohort Evaluation of Microdeletion and -Duplication Detection.
articles.authors: Vaiküll K, Paluoja P, Mölder S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the analytical and clinical performance of fetal fraction (FF) enriched genome-wide noninvasive prenatal testing (GW-NIPT) for the detection of clinically relevant copy number variants (CNVs) down to 1 Mb.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 10,501 singleton pregnancies tested with FF enrichment-based GW-NIPT between August 2023 and July 2025. CNV analysis was performed using BinDel and WisecondorX.
RESULTS: FF enrichment increased the mean FF to 24% (2.4-fold increase). Clinically relevant CNVs, including microdeletions and microduplications, were detected down to approximately 1 Mb. Performance was robust across all maternal body mass index (BMI) categories. The retest rate was 0.95%, resulting in a final no-call rate of 0.03% with no BMI-attributable failures. The workflow demonstrated high observed sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value for common aneuploidies, rare autosomal trisomies, sex chromosome aneuploidies and subchromosomal CNVs.
CONCLUSIONS: FF enrichment enhances the analytical resolution of first-trimester GW-NIPT, extending detection of subchromosomal CNVs to approximately 1 Mb across diverse patient populations, although detection at the lower end of this range remains fetal-fraction dependent. This approach broadens the scope of prenatal screening while maintaining low test failure rates. All positive findings require confirmatory diagnostic testing and appropriate genetic counseling.
